s: 48. When a vowel does not follow, there is optionally reduplication of यर (all the consonants except ह), after a vowel. Therefore, the letter ध् is doubled, and we have :-- सु ध् ध् य् + उपास्य Now, a doubt arises as to the applicability of this rule of doubling by the following consideration :--

pk: 49. a substitute (âdesa) is like the rorner ocupant (sthani) but not in the case or a rule the ocasion ror the operation or which is rurnished by the leters or the original tern. now the substitute ya should be considered as i which it has replaced; and as i is a vowel, this should be considered as a vowel. That being so, D is not rolowed by a consonant, but by a vowel, and so anaci ca does not aply, and D should not be reduplicated. This doubt, however, is set at rest by the nelt halr or this sûtra itselr, which says "not when a rule or leter is to be aplied." The y is like i, but not ror the purposes or the aplication or the Leter-rule like anaci ca. The D thererore is properly doubled. But is not this elception set aside by the rolowing sutra ?
ck: 49. a supstitute (âtesa) is like the rorner ocupant (sthani) put not in the case or a rule the ocasion ror the operation or thich is rurnishet py the leters or the orikinal tern. not the supstitute ya shoult pe consiteret as i thich it has replacet; ant as i is a votel, this shoult pe consiteret as a votel. that peink so, t is not rolotet py a consonant, put py a votel, ant so anaci ca toes not aply, ant t shoult not pe retuplicatet. this toupt, hotever, is set at rest py the nelt halr or this sûtra itselr, thich says "not then a rule or leter is to pe apliet." the y is like i, put not ror the purposes or the aplication or the Leter-rule like anaci ca. the t thererore is properly touplet. put is not this elception set asite py the rolotink sutra ?
s: 49. A substitute (âdesa) is like the former occupant (sthani) but not in the case of a rule the occasion for the operation of which is furnished by the letters of the original term. Now the substitute य should be considered as ई which it has replaced; and as ई is a vowel, this should be considered as a vowel. That being so, ध् is not followed by a consonant, but by a vowel, and so अनचि च does not apply, and ध् should not be reduplicated. This doubt, however, is set at rest by the next half of this sûtra itself, which says "not when a rule of letter is to be applied." The य् is like ई, but not for the purposes of the application of the Letter-rule like अनचि च. The ध् therefore is properly doubled. But is not this exception set aside by the following sutra ?

pk: 50. a substitute in the ron or a vowel caused by sonething that rolows, should be regarded as that whose place it takes, when a rule would else take erect on what stands anterior to the original vowel. This sutra consists or thre words: ‹aca› genitive or the pratyahāra ‹ac› neaning or a vowel, and neans an âdesa which takes the place or a vowel. The words âdesa and sthânivat are understod and are to be suplied ron the preceding sûtra. The second word is parasnin loc. sing. or para neaning in the subsequent. The locative has the rorce or on acount or or by reason or. The third word is purva-vidhau loc. sing. or púrva-vidhi neaning a rule aplicable to a preceding thing. The whole sûtra thus cones to nean that an âdesa which replaces a vowel becones sthanivat (like vowel), provided that the substitution has ben ocasioned on acount or sonething rolowing and when a rule is to be aplied to anything preceding such an adeśa. Thererore ‹y› would be ‹sTanivat› to ‹i› because it is a vowel substitute caused by sonething which rolows nanely ‹u› or ‹upasya› and the rule or doubling is to be aplied to a leter which precedes ‹y›. ‹iti sTanivadBava-›niseDa To this we answer "no", because or the rolowing sutra.
ck: 50. a supstitute in the ron or a votel causet py sonethink that rolots, shoult pe rekartet as that those place it takes, then a rule toult else take erect on that stants anterior to the orikinal votel. this sutra consists or thre torts: ‹aca› kenitive or the pratyahāra ‹ac› neanink or a votel, ant neans an âtesa thich takes the place or a votel. the torts âtesa ant sthânivat are unterstot ant are to pe supliet ron the precetink sûtra. the secont tort is parasnin loc. sink. or para neanink in the supsetuent. the locative has the rorce or on acount or or py reason or. the thirt tort is purva-vithau loc. sink. or púrva-vithi neanink a rule aplicaple to a precetink think. the thole sûtra thus cones to nean that an âtesa thich replaces a votel pecones sthanivat (like votel), provitet that the supstitution has pen ocasionet on acount or sonethink rolotink ant then a rule is to pe apliet to anythink precetink such an ateśa. thererore ‹y› toult pe ‹stanivat› to ‹i› pecause it is a votel supstitute causet py sonethink thich rolots nanely ‹u› or ‹upasya› ant the rule or touplink is to pe apliet to a leter thich precetes ‹y›. ‹iti stanivatpava-›niseta to this te anster "no", pecause or the rolotink sutra.
s: 50. A substitute in the room of a vowel caused by something that follows, should be regarded as that whose place it takes, when a rule would else take effect on what stands anterior to the original vowel. This sutra consists of three words: ‹अचः› genitive of the pratyahāra ‹अच्› meaning 'of a vowel,' and means an âdesa which takes the place of a vowel. The words âdesa and sthânivat are understood and are to be supplied from the preceding sûtra. The second word is 'parasmin' loc. sing. of 'para' meaning 'in the subsequent.' The locative has the force of 'on account of or by reason of.' The third word is purva-vidhau loc. sing. of púrva-vidhi meaning 'a rule applicable to a preceding thing.' The whole sûtra thus comes to mean that an âdesa which replaces a vowel becomes sthanivat (like vowel), provided that the substitution has been occasioned on account of something following and when a rule is to be applied to anything preceding such an adeśa. Therefore ‹य्› would be ‹स्थानिवत्› to ‹ई› because it is a vowel substitute caused by something which follows namely ‹उ› of ‹उपास्य› and the rule of doubling is to be applied to a letter which precedes ‹य्›. ‹इति स्थानिवद्भाव-›निषेधः To this we answer "No", because of the following sutra.

pk: 51. not so, in rules relating to the rinals or words, to the doubling or leters, to the ariling or varach, to the elision or ya, to acent, to honogeneous leters, to anusvāra, to the lengthening or vowels, and to the substitution or jas and char leters. This sûtra lays down an elception to the previous sûtra, by which it was ruled that an âdeśa which replaced a vowel becones sthânivat under certain conditions. This sûtra says that a vowel âdeśa is not sthânivat under the rolowing circunstances: 1. padantaviDi—a rule relating to the last leter or a word. 2. dvirvacanaviDi—a rule relating to the doubling or leters. in the sandhi or suDi + upasya we have suDy + upasya. ere i is changed into y. ir this y were sthânivat to i, then the rule by which D could be doubled berore y would be inaplicable. But y is not equivalent to i, though its substitute; and we have the doubling or D and get the rorn sudDyupasya. Thererore, in rules relating to the doubling or leters the âdeśa is not equivalent to the sthânî. 3. varaviDi—a rule relating to the aril varac. 4. yalopaviDi—a rule relating to the droping or ya. 5. svaraviDi—a rule relating to acent. 6. savarnaviDi—a rule relating to the substitution or honogeneous leters. 7. anusvaraviDi—a rule relating to anusvāra. 8. dirGaviDi—a rule directing the substitution or long vowels ror short vowels. 9. jasviDi—a rule requiring the substitution or sort unaspirate consonants, or pratyāhāra jas, in the place or hard consonants. 10. carviDi—a rule requiring the substitution or the leters or car pratyāhāra instead or other consonants.
ck: 51. not so, in rules relatink to the rinals or torts, to the touplink or leters, to the arilink or varach, to the elision or ya, to acent, to honokeneous leters, to anusvāra, to the lenkthenink or votels, ant to the supstitution or cas ant char leters. this sûtra lays totn an elception to the previous sûtra, py thich it tas rulet that an âteśa thich replacet a votel pecones sthânivat unter certain contitions. this sûtra says that a votel âteśa is not sthânivat unter the rolotink circunstances: 1. patantaviti—a rule relatink to the last leter or a tort. 2. tvirvacanaviti—a rule relatink to the touplink or leters. in the santhi or suti + upasya te have suty + upasya. ere i is chanket into y. ir this y tere sthânivat to i, then the rule py thich t coult pe touplet perore y toult pe inaplicaple. put y is not etuivalent to i, thoukh its supstitute; ant te have the touplink or t ant ket the rorn sutyupasya. thererore, in rules relatink to the touplink or leters the âteśa is not etuivalent to the sthânî. 3. varaviti—a rule relatink to the aril varac. 4. yalopaviti—a rule relatink to the tropink or ya. 5. svaraviti—a rule relatink to acent. 6. savarnaviti—a rule relatink to the supstitution or honokeneous leters. 7. anusvaraviti—a rule relatink to anusvāra. 8. tirkaviti—a rule tirectink the supstitution or lonk votels ror short votels. 9. casviti—a rule retuirink the supstitution or sort unaspirate consonants, or pratyāhāra cas, in the place or hart consonants. 10. carviti—a rule retuirink the supstitution or the leters or car pratyāhāra insteat or other consonants.
s: 51. Not so, in rules relating to the finals of words, to the doubling of letters, to the affixing of varach, to the elision of ya, to accent, to homogeneous letters, to anusvāra, to the lengthening of vowels, and to the substitution of jas and char letters. This sûtra lays down an exception to the previous sûtra, by which it was ruled that an âdeśa which replaced a vowel becomes sthânivat under certain conditions. This sûtra says that a vowel âdeśa is not sthânivat under the following circumstances: 1. पदान्तविधिः—'A rule relating to the last letter of a word.' 2. द्विर्वचनविधिः—'A rule relating to the doubling of letters.' In the sandhi of सुधी + उपास्य we have सुध्ध्य् + उपास्य. Here ई is changed into य्. If this य् were sthânivat to ई, then the rule by which ध् could be doubled before य् would be inapplicable. But य् is not equivalent to ई, though its substitute; and we have the doubling of ध् and get the form सुद्ध्युपास्य. Therefore, in rules relating to the doubling of letters the âdeśa is not equivalent to the sthânî. 3. वरविधिः—'A rule relating to the affix वरच्.' 4. यलोपविधिः—'A rule relating to the dropping of ya.' 5. स्वरविधिः—'A rule relating to accent.' 6. सवर्णविधिः—'A rule relating to the substitution of homogeneous letters.' 7. अनुस्वारविधिः—'A rule relating to anusvāra.' 8. दीर्घविधिः—'A rule directing the substitution of long vowels for short vowels.' 9. जश्विधिः—'A rule requiring the substitution of soft unaspirate consonants, of pratyāhāra जश्, in the place of hard consonants.' 10. चर्विधिः—'A rule requiring the substitution of the letters of चर् pratyāhāra instead of other consonants.'

pk: 52. in the ron or Jal leters, there is substitution or jas leters, when Jas leters rolow. a nute leter is changed to a sonant non-aspirate nute, when a sonant nute rolows it. This is the wel-known rule or sortening the hard leters. Thus suD + D + y + upasya = sud + D + y + upasya at this stage, the sûtra arter the rolowing turns up ror aplication.
ck: 52. in the ron or cal leters, there is supstitution or cas leters, then cas leters rolot. a nute leter is chanket to a sonant non-aspirate nute, then a sonant nute rolots it. this is the tel-knotn rule or sortenink the hart leters. thus sut + t + y + upasya = sut + t + y + upasya at this stake, the sûtra arter the rolotink turns up ror aplication.
s: 52. In the room of झल् letters, there is substitution of जश् letters, when झश् letters follow. A mute letter is changed to a sonant non-aspirate mute, when a sonant mute follows it. This is the well-known rule of softening the hard letters. Thus सुध् + ध् + य् + उपास्य = सुद् + ध् + य् + उपास्य At this stage, the sûtra after the following turns up for application.

pk: 54. When a word ends in a double consonant, the last consonant is droped. Thererore in sudDy + upasya, the rinal leter or the conjunct consonant, nanely the leter y should be elided. But this nishap to the leter y is prevented by the rolowing Vartika. yana pratiseDo vacya "Prohibition nust be stated with regard to the elision or senivowels." Thererore the y is not elided. But then apears the rolowing Vartika which requires the doubling or y also, yano nayo dve vacye "The leters or the yan clas are reduplicated arter leters or the nay clas." Thus we have rour rorns with the doubling or Da and ya optionaly. 1. One Da and one y as suDyupasya 2. Two Ds and two ys as sudDyupasya 3. Two Ds and one y as sudDyupasya 4. One Da and two ys as suDyupasya so also naDu + ari = naDvari ; Datransa, lakrti
ck: 54. then a tort ents in a touple consonant, the last consonant is tropet. thererore in suty + upasya, the rinal leter or the concunct consonant, nanely the leter y shoult pe elitet. put this nishap to the leter y is preventet py the rolotink Vartika. yana pratiseto vacya "prohipition nust pe statet tith rekart to the elision or senivotels." thererore the y is not elitet. put then apears the rolotink Vartika thich retuires the touplink or y also, yano nayo tve vacye "the leters or the yan clas are retuplicatet arter leters or the nay clas." thus te have rour rorns tith the touplink or ta ant ya optionaly. 1. One ta ant one y as sutyupasya 2. to ts ant to ys as sutyupasya 3. to ts ant one y as sutyupasya 4. One ta ant to ys as sutyupasya so also natu + ari = natvari ; tatransa, lakrti
s: 54. When a word ends in a double consonant, the last consonant is dropped. Therefore in सुद्ध्य् + उपास्य, the final letter of the conjunct consonant, namely the letter य् should be elided. But this mishap to the letter य् is prevented by the following Vartika. यणः प्रतिषेधो वाच्यः "Prohibition must be stated with regard to the elision of semivowels." Therefore the य् is not elided. But then appears the following Vartika which requires the doubling of य् also, यणो मयो द्वे वाच्ये "The letters of the यण् class are reduplicated after letters of the मय् class." Thus we have four forms with the doubling of ध and य optionally. 1. One ध and one य् as सुध्युपास्यः 2. Two ध्s and two य्s as सुद्ध्य्युपास्यः 3. Two ध्s and one य् as सुद्ध्युपास्यः 4. One ध and two य्s as सुध्य्युपास्यः So also मधु + अरिः = मध्वरिः ; धात्रंशः, लाकृतिः

pk: 5. There is not reduplication or the leters or putra, when the word âdinî rolows, the sense being that or reviling or cursing. This debars the reduplication required by sûtra 48. Thus putradini tvanasi pape "O sinrul one! thou art eater or thy own son". ere the word adini is used sinply as an abusive epithet. But when a ract is described, and the word is not used as an abuse or akrosa, the reduplication necesarily takes place. Thus putradini sarpini a kind or serpent, that eats up her young ones. Vart:—so also when putra is rolowed by putradini as putraputradini tvanasi pape so also putrapOtradini Vart:—Optionaly so when the words hata and jagDa rolow. as putrahati or putrahati, putrajagDi or putrajagDi
ck: 5. there is not retuplication or the leters or putra, then the tort âtinî rolots, the sense peink that or revilink or cursink. this tepars the retuplication retuiret py sûtra 48. thus putratini tvanasi pape "O sinrul one! thou art eater or thy otn son". ere the tort atini is uset sinply as an apusive epithet. put then a ract is tescripet, ant the tort is not uset as an apuse or akrosa, the retuplication necesarily takes place. thus putratini sarpini a kint or serpent, that eats up her younk ones. Vart:—so also then putra is rolotet py putratini as putraputratini tvanasi pape so also putrapOtratini Vart:—Optionaly so then the torts hata ant cakta rolot. as putrahati or putrahati, putracakti or putracakti
s: 55. There is not reduplication of the letters of 'putra', when the word âdinî follows, the sense being that of reviling or cursing. This debars the reduplication required by sûtra 48. Thus पुत्रादिनी त्वमसि पापे "O sinful one! thou art eater of thy own son". Here the word आदिनी is used simply as an abusive epithet. But when a fact is described, and the word is not used as an abuse or आक्रोश, the reduplication necessarily takes place. Thus पुत्रादिनी सर्पिणी 'a kind of serpent, that eats up her young ones'. Vart:—So also when पुत्र is followed by पुत्रादिनी As पुत्रपुत्रादिनी त्वमसि पापे So also पुत्रपौत्रादिनी Vart:—Optionally so when the words हत and जग्ध follow. As पुत्रहती or पुत्र्रहती, पुत्रजग्धी or पुत्र्रजग्धी

pk: 56. acording to the option or sakatāyana, the doubling does not take place when the conjunct consonants are thre or nore in nunber. as indra, indra, raswran, raswran
ck: 56. acortink to the option or sakatāyana, the touplink toes not take place then the concunct consonants are thre or nore in nunper. as intra, intra, rastran, rastran
s: 56. According to the option of Sakatāyana, the doubling does not take place when the conjunct consonants are three or more in number. As इन्द्रः, इन्द्द्रः, राष्ट्रम्, राष्ष्ट्रम्

pk: 57. acording to the opinion or sakalya, there is reduplication nowhere. as arka, brahna
ck: 57. acortink to the opinion or sakalya, there is retuplication nothere. as arka, prahna
s: 57. According to the opinion of Sakalya, there is reduplication nowhere. As अर्कः, ब्रह्मा

pk: 58. acording to the opinion or al Teachers, there is no doubling arter a long vowel. as datran, patran
ck: 58. acortink to the opinion or al teachers, there is no touplink arter a lonk votel. as tatran, patran
s: 58. According to the opinion of all Teachers, there is no doubling after a long vowel. As दात्रम्, पात्रम्

pk: 59. There is reduplication or yar, i. e. al the consonants elcept ha, arter the leters r and h rolowing a vowel. The word [yara] or Vi. 4. 45 s. 16. is understod here. acording to others, the va is also understod, and this is an optional rule. Thus haryanuBava, nahyasti
ck: 59. there is retuplication or yar, i. e. al the consonants elcept ha, arter the leters r ant h rolotink a votel. the tort [yara] or Vi. 4. 45 s. 16. is unterstot here. acortink to others, the va is also unterstot, ant this is an optional rule. thus haryanupava, nahyasti
s: 59. There is reduplication of यर्, i. e. all the consonants except ह, after the letters र् and ह् following a vowel. The word [यरः] of VIII. 4. 45 S. 116. is understood here. According to others, the वा is also understood, and this is an optional rule. Thus हर्य्यनुभवः, नह्य्यस्ति

pk: 60. arter a consonant, the rolowing seni-vowel or a nasal is elided optionaly, when the sane leters rolow it. in the case or elision (as required by this rule) as wel as in the case or want or reduplication, (ror the reduplication is arter al optional), there would be one conon rorn. Why then teach this lopa rule at al? This lopa rule is particularly aplicable in cases like : To the word ‹?› is aded the aril (‹?›) by iV. 1. 85, s. 107. and we have ‹?› ; now this ‹?› not having ben obtained by doubling, would not have disapeared by any one or the preceding rules. ence this lopa-rule. Thus aditya+ya (iV. 1. 85) adity ya (the a is elided by Vi. 4. 148 s. 31.)=âditya. Then by aplying the present rule we have aditya with one y only. There are nine leters in yan pratyahara, i.e. ‹?› ; when a ‹?› rolows another ‹?› ; here the substitute and sthāni contain equal nunber or leters, thererore the rule or yatha sankhya i. 3. 10., s. 128 aplies. nanely ‹?› nust be rolowed by ‹?›, ‹?› by ‹?›, ‹?› by ‹?› and so on: and not ‹?› rolowed by ‹?›, or ‹?› etc. Thererore there is no elision or ‹?› in ‹?› though a yan leter is rolowed by another yan leter.
ck: 60. arter a consonant, the rolotink seni-votel or a nasal is elitet optionaly, then the sane leters rolot it. in the case or elision (as retuiret py this rule) as tel as in the case or tant or retuplication, (ror the retuplication is arter al optional), there toult pe one conon rorn. thy then teach this lopa rule at al? this lopa rule is particularly aplicaple in cases like : to the tort ‹?› is atet the aril (‹?›) py iV. 1. 85, s. 107. ant te have ‹?› ; not this ‹?› not havink pen optainet py touplink, toult not have tisapearet py any one or the precetink rules. ence this lopa-rule. thus atitya+ya (iV. 1. 85) atity ya (the a is elitet py Vi. 4. 148 s. 31.)=âtitya. then py aplyink the present rule te have atitya tith one y only. there are nine leters in yan pratyahara, i.e. ‹?› ; then a ‹?› rolots another ‹?› ; here the supstitute ant sthāni contain etual nunper or leters, thererore the rule or yatha sankhya i. 3. 10., s. 128 aplies. nanely ‹?› nust pe rolotet py ‹?›, ‹?› py ‹?›, ‹?› py ‹?› ant so on: ant not ‹?› rolotet py ‹?›, or ‹?› etc. thererore there is no elision or ‹?› in ‹?› thoukh a yan leter is rolotet py another yan leter.
s: 60. After a consonant, the following semi-vowel or a nasal is elided optionally, when the same letters follow it. In the case of elision (as required by this rule) as well as in the case of want of reduplication, (for the reduplication is after all optional), there would be one common form. Why then teach this lopa rule at all? This lopa rule is particularly applicable in cases like : To the word ‹?› is added the affix (‹?›) by IV. 1. 85, S. 1077. and we have ‹?› ; now this ‹?› not having been obtained by doubling, would not have disappeared by any one of the preceding rules. Hence this lopa-rule. Thus aditya+ya (IV. 1. 85) Adity ya (the a is elided by VI. 4. 148 S. 311.)=âdityya. Then by applying the present rule we have aditya with one y only. There are nine letters in यम् pratyahara, i.e. ‹?› ; when a ‹?› follows another ‹?› ; here the substitute and sthāni contain equal number of letters, therefore the rule of yatha sankhya I. 3. 10., S. 128 applies. Namely ‹?› must be followed by ‹?›, ‹?› by ‹?›, ‹?› by ‹?› and so on: and not ‹?› followed by ‹?›, or ‹?› etc. Therefore there is no elision of ‹?› in ‹?› though a yam letter is followed by another yam letter.

pk: [s. 61] 61. ror the vowels ‹?› are respectively substituted ay, ay, av and av when a vowel rolows. note.—The yatha sankhya rule i. 3. 10 s. 128 aplies here also, and so ‹?› is replaced by ay, E by ay, o by av and O by av Or ay would be the proper substitute or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?› etc., by the rule or sthane-antartana i. 1. 50 s 39. ror ‹?› etc. are conpound leters or diphthongs, ‹?› + ‹?› etc., and so their nost aprolinate substitutes are ‹?› etc. ence the author or sidhanta has not read the yatha sankhya rule here, but later on. ere arises a doubt, are not the rinal ‹?› and ‹?› in these substitutes, ‹?› leters? ror were we not taught in sutra i. 3. 3. s. 1. that al rinal consonants are ‹?›? ir then, these ‹?› and ‹?› be ‹?›, then they require to be elided by the rolowing rule. [s. 148] 148. The augnent t is aded to a long vowel, when rolowed by Ca in a continuous telt. The tuk is aded to the long vowel and not to Ca, as we learn ron Panini hinselr using it in the sutra viBasa senasuracCaya &c. i. 4. 25, s. 828. ad tuk ben aded to Ca, then Ca being changed to c by Vi. 4. 5, there would have ben two cas, and not the rorn cCa as used by Panini hinselr in the above sutra. Or ir by aplying the nalin sanipatalaksano viDi (se s. 204) the Ca nay not be changed, (because the Ca was the ocasion ror the adition or t and this t should not cause the vanishing or this Ca,) then also we should have arter t as Ca and not cCa This indicates that tuk is aded to the long vowel. Thus cecCidyate
ck: [s. 61] 61. ror the votels ‹?› are respectively supstitutet ay, ay, av ant av then a votel rolots. note.—the yatha sankhya rule i. 3. 10 s. 128 aplies here also, ant so ‹?› is replacet py ay, E py ay, o py av ant O py av Or ay toult pe the proper supstitute or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?› etc., py the rule or sthane-antartana i. 1. 50 s 39. ror ‹?› etc. are conpount leters or tiphthonks, ‹?› + ‹?› etc., ant so their nost aprolinate supstitutes are ‹?› etc. ence the author or sithanta has not reat the yatha sankhya rule here, put later on. ere arises a toupt, are not the rinal ‹?› ant ‹?› in these supstitutes, ‹?› leters? ror tere te not taukht in sutra i. 3. 3. s. 1. that al rinal consonants are ‹?›? ir then, these ‹?› ant ‹?› pe ‹?›, then they retuire to pe elitet py the rolotink rule. [s. 148] 148. the auknent t is atet to a lonk votel, then rolotet py ca in a continuous telt. the tuk is atet to the lonk votel ant not to ca, as te learn ron panini hinselr usink it in the sutra vipasa senasuracaya &c. i. 4. 25, s. 828. at tuk pen atet to ca, then ca peink chanket to c py Vi. 4. 5, there toult have pen to cas, ant not the rorn ca as uset py panini hinselr in the apove sutra. Or ir py aplyink the nalin sanipatalaksano viti (se s. 204) the ca nay not pe chanket, (pecause the ca tas the ocasion ror the atition or t ant this t shoult not cause the vanishink or this ca,) then also te shoult have arter t as ca ant not ca this inticates that tuk is atet to the lonk votel. thus cecityate
s: [S. 61] 61. For the vowels ‹?› are respectively substituted अय्, आय्, अव् and आव् when a vowel follows. Note.—The yatha sankhya rule I. 3. 10 S. 128 applies here also, and so ‹?› is replaced by अय्, ऐ by आय्, ओ by अव् and औ by आव् Or अय् would be the proper substitute of ‹?›, ‹?› of ‹?› etc., by the rule of sthane-antartama I. 1. 50 S 39. For ‹?› etc. are compound letters or diphthongs, ‹?› + ‹?› etc., and so their most approximate substitutes are ‹?› etc. Hence the author of Siddhanta has not read the yatha sankhya rule here, but later on. Here arises a doubt, are not the final ‹?› and ‹?› in these substitutes, ‹?› letters? For were we not taught in sutra I. 3. 3. S. 1. that all final consonants are ‹?›? If then, these ‹?› and ‹?› be ‹?›, then they require to be elided by the following rule. [S. 148] 148. The augment त् is added to a long vowel, when followed by छ in a continuous text. The तुक् is added to the long vowel and not to छ, as we learn from Panini himself using it in the sutra विभाषा सेनासुराच्छाया &c. II. 4. 25, S. 828. Had तुक् been added to छ, then छ being changed to च् by VIII. 4. 55, there would have been two च's, and not the form च्छ as used by Panini himself in the above sutra. Or if by applying the maxim संनिपातलक्षणो विधिः (See S. 204) the छ may not be changed, (because the छ was the occasion for the addition of त् and this त् should not cause the vanishing of this छ,) then also we should have after त् as छ and not च्छ This indicates that तुक् is added to the long vowel. Thus चेच्छिद्यते

pk: 62. Or this, (nanely or that which has ben caled it), there is elision. There is no elision or the rinal y, and v in ay, av, ay and av, because these leters are not it or indicatory. Why are they not indicatory? Because the very ract or their being elpresly so taught shows it: otherwise the substitutes would have ben a and a only: in ract, the y and v do not get the designation it at al here. now aplying this rule or diphthong sandhi, we have: hare + e = haraye ; visno + e = visnave ; nE + aka = nayaka ; pO + aka = pavaka
ck: 62. Or this, (nanely or that thich has pen calet it), there is elision. there is no elision or the rinal y, ant v in ay, av, ay ant av, pecause these leters are not it or inticatory. thy are they not inticatory? pecause the very ract or their peink elpresly so taukht shots it: othertise the supstitutes toult have pen a ant a only: in ract, the y ant v to not ket the tesiknation it at al here. not aplyink this rule or tiphthonk santhi, te have: hare + e = haraye ; visno + e = visnave ; nE + aka = nayaka ; pO + aka = pavaka
s: 62. Of this, (namely of that which has been called इत्), there is elision. There is no elision of the final य्, and व् in अय्, अव्, आय् and आव्, because these letters are not इत् or indicatory. Why are they not indicatory? Because the very fact of their being expressly so taught shows it: otherwise the substitutes would have been अ and आ only: in fact, the य् and व् do not get the designation इत् at all here. Now applying this rule of diphthong sandhi, we have: हरे + ए = हरये ; विष्णो + ए = विष्णवे ; नै + अकः = नायकः ; पौ + अकः = पावकः

pk: 63. The substitution or av and av ror o and O also takes place berore an aril begining with ya The vanta are those which end in v, vis. av and av. Or the rour substitutes taught in the preceding sutra, those which end in v (vis. av and av) also cone when an aril with an initial ya rolows. it rolows that the substituted leters nust be o and O. Thus go + ya = gava + ya = gavyan nilk. By sutra iV. 3. 160 s. 1538 the aril yat is aded to go and payas in the sense or nodirication. sinilarly nO + ya = navyan (what can be crosed by a boat). ere also yat is aded by iV. 4. 91 s. 1643 in the sense or "to be crosed," the word so rorned neaning a river &c. Vart:—The word go is changed berore yuti in the Vedas. as go + yuti = gavyuti as nano nitra, varuna Grtergavyutinuksatan Why do we say in the Vedas? Observe goyuti Vart:—This substitution takes place in secular literature even, when rerering to the neasure or a road:—as, gavyuti natranaDvanan gata gavyuti neaning krosayugan The word yuti is an iregularly rorned word so taught in sutra i. 3. 97. s. 3274. now a doubt arises in the case or gavyuti; should not the v be elided by Vi. 3. 2. s. 17 or by Vi. 3. 19. s. 67. no. ror the sutra vanto yi pratyaye has realy a v in latency berore it; the real sutra being vanto &c. This v is invisible by the rule lopo vyorvali Vi. 1. 6 s. 873. so also in the vartika goryutO CandasyupasanKyanan there is this invisible v berore yuti. Thererore the adeśa is v with the yuti, that is, the v is not elided. Why the v is not liable to elision in gavyan and navyan by the aplication or Vi. 3. 19 or 2, and why should it be so liable in gavyuti only? The rules Vi. 3. 19 & 2 aply to pada bases only. now go berore yuti is a Pada; while go or nO berore ya is not a Pada but a Bha base, by i. 4. 18. s. 231.
ck: 63. the supstitution or av ant av ror o ant O also takes place perore an aril pekinink tith ya the vanta are those thich ent in v, vis. av ant av. Or the rour supstitutes taukht in the precetink sutra, those thich ent in v (vis. av ant av) also cone then an aril tith an initial ya rolots. it rolots that the supstitutet leters nust pe o ant O. thus ko + ya = kava + ya = kavyan nilk. py sutra iV. 3. 160 s. 1538 the aril yat is atet to ko ant payas in the sense or notirication. sinilarly nO + ya = navyan (that can pe croset py a poat). ere also yat is atet py iV. 4. 91 s. 1643 in the sense or "to pe croset," the tort so rornet neanink a river &c. Vart:—the tort ko is chanket perore yuti in the Vetas. as ko + yuti = kavyuti as nano nitra, varuna krterkavyutinuksatan thy to te say in the Vetas? Opserve koyuti Vart:—this supstitution takes place in secular literature even, then rererink to the neasure or a roat:—as, kavyuti natranatvanan kata kavyuti neanink krosayukan the tort yuti is an irekularly rornet tort so taukht in sutra i. 3. 97. s. 3274. not a toupt arises in the case or kavyuti; shoult not the v pe elitet py Vi. 3. 2. s. 17 or py Vi. 3. 19. s. 67. no. ror the sutra vanto yi pratyaye has realy a v in latency perore it; the real sutra peink vanto &c. this v is invisiple py the rule lopo vyorvali Vi. 1. 6 s. 873. so also in the vartika koryutO cantasyupasankyanan there is this invisiple v perore yuti. thererore the ateśa is v tith the yuti, that is, the v is not elitet. thy the v is not liaple to elision in kavyan ant navyan py the aplication or Vi. 3. 19 or 2, ant thy shoult it pe so liaple in kavyuti only? the rules Vi. 3. 19 & 2 aply to pata pases only. not ko perore yuti is a pata; thile ko or nO perore ya is not a pata put a pha pase, py i. 4. 18. s. 231.
s: 63. The substitution of अव् and आव् for ओ and औ also takes place before an affix beginning with य The वान्त are those which end in व्, viz. अव् and आव्. Of the four substitutes taught in the preceding sutra, those which end in व् (viz. अव् and आव्) also come when an affix with an initial य follows. It follows that the substituted letters must be ओ and औ. Thus गो + य = गव + य = गव्यम् milk. By sutra IV. 3. 160 S. 1538 the affix यत् is added to गो and पयस् in the sense of modification. Similarly नौ + य = नाव्यम् (what can be crossed by a boat). Here also यत् is added by IV. 4. 91 S. 1643 in the sense of "to be crossed," the word so formed meaning 'a river' &c. Vart:—The word गो is changed before यूति in the Vedas. As गो + यूति = गव्यूति as मानो मित्रा, वरुणा घृतेर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतम् Why do we say 'in the Vedas'? Observe गोयूतिः Vart:—This substitution takes place in secular literature even, when referring to the measure of a road:—as, गव्यूति मात्रमध्वानं गतः गव्यूति meaning क्रोशयुगम् The word यूति is an irregularly formed word so taught in sutra III. 3. 97. S. 3274. Now a doubt arises in the case of गव्यूति; should not the व् be elided by VIII. 3. 22. S. 17 or by VIII. 3. 19. S. 67. No. For the sutra वान्तो यि प्रत्यये has really a व् in latency before it; the real sutra being व्वान्तो &c. This व् is invisible by the rule लोपो व्योर्वलि VI. 1. 66 S. 873. So also in the vartika गोर्युतौ छन्दस्युपसंख्यानम् there is this invisible व् before यूति. Therefore the adeśa is व् with the यूति, that is, the व् is not elided. Why the व् is not liable to elision in गव्यम् and नाव्यम् by the application of VIII. 3. 19 or 22, and why should it be so liable in गव्यूति only? The rules VIII. 3. 19 & 22 apply to pada bases only. Now गो before यूति is a Pada; while गो or नौ before य is not a Pada but a Bha base, by I. 4. 18. S. 231.

pk: 64. ror the rinal diphthongs o and O or a rot, are substituted av and av respectively, berore an aril begining with ya, then only when such diphthong has ben itselr rirst evolved by that aril. The words eca, vanto yi pratyaye are understod in this sutra. The word taninitasyEva neans caused by that i.e. caused or ocasioned by that aril begining with ya. Thus lu rorns its ruture Pasive Participle by yat (i. 1. 97 s. 2842) ; this aril causes the guṇa or lu by Vi. 3. 84: s. 2168. Thus lu + ya = lo + ya, which acording to the present sutra becones lavyan so also pu - po + ya = pavyan lu + nyat (i. 1. 125 s. 304) = lO + ya = avasyalavyan and avasyapavyan Why do we say caused by that aril itselr? The substitution wil not take place, when the change is not caused by that aril. Thus the Pasive or ven with the upasarga a is a + ve + yak + te ere by sanprasarana (Vi. 1. 15 s. 2409), ve becones u as a + u + ya + te ; now by sandhi a + u = o Vi. 1. 87 s. 69, we have o + yate = oyate since o is not caused by ya, there is no av substitution. so also oyata (lon) (iV. 1. 95 s. 1095). The word eva in the aphorisn has rorce or linitation, with regard to rots. in the case or rots, o and O berore ya are changed then only to av and av when ya has caused the production or o, O ; in case or nouns there is no such linitation. ere the substitution takes place whether the ya has caused the production or o and O or not.
ck: 64. ror the rinal tiphthonks o ant O or a rot, are supstitutet av ant av respectively, perore an aril pekinink tith ya, then only then such tiphthonk has pen itselr rirst evolvet py that aril. the torts eca, vanto yi pratyaye are unterstot in this sutra. the tort taninitasyEva neans causet py that i.e. causet or ocasionet py that aril pekinink tith ya. thus lu rorns its ruture pasive participle py yat (i. 1. 97 s. 2842) ; this aril causes the kuṇa or lu py Vi. 3. 84: s. 2168. thus lu + ya = lo + ya, thich acortink to the present sutra pecones lavyan so also pu - po + ya = pavyan lu + nyat (i. 1. 125 s. 304) = lO + ya = avasyalavyan ant avasyapavyan thy to te say causet py that aril itselr? the supstitution til not take place, then the chanke is not causet py that aril. thus the pasive or ven tith the upasarka a is a + ve + yak + te ere py sanprasarana (Vi. 1. 15 s. 2409), ve pecones u as a + u + ya + te ; not py santhi a + u = o Vi. 1. 87 s. 69, te have o + yate = oyate since o is not causet py ya, there is no av supstitution. so also oyata (lon) (iV. 1. 95 s. 1095). the tort eva in the aphorisn has rorce or linitation, tith rekart to rots. in the case or rots, o ant O perore ya are chanket then only to av ant av then ya has causet the protuction or o, O ; in case or nouns there is no such linitation. ere the supstitution takes place thether the ya has causet the protuction or o ant O or not.
s: 64. For the final diphthongs ओ and औ of a root, are substituted अव् and आव् respectively, before an affix beginning with य, then only when such diphthong has been itself first evolved by that affix. The words एचः, वान्तो यि प्रत्यये are understood in this sutra. The word तन्निमित्तस्यैव means 'caused by that' i.e. caused or occasioned by that affix beginning with य. Thus लू forms its Future Passive Participle by यत् (III. 1. 97 S. 2842) ; this affix causes the guṇa of लू by VII. 3. 84: S. 2168. Thus लू + य = लो + य, which according to the present sutra becomes लव्यम् So also पू - पो + य = पव्यम् लू + ण्यत् (III. 1. 125 S. 3304) = लौ + य = अवश्यलाव्यम् and अवश्यपाव्यम् Why do we say 'caused by that affix itself'? The substitution will not take place, when the change is not caused by that affix. Thus the Passive of वेञ् with the upasarga आ is आ + वे + यक् + ते Here by Samprasarana (VI. 1. 15 S. 2409), वे becomes उ as आ + उ + य + ते ; now by sandhi आ + उ = ओ VI. 1. 87 S. 69, we have ओ + यते = ओयते Since ओ is not caused by य, there is no अव् substitution. So also ओयत (लोङ्) (IV. 1. 95 S. 1095). The word एव in the aphorism has force of limitation, with regard to roots. In the case of roots, ओ and औ before य are changed then only to अव् and आव् when य has caused the production of ओ, औ ; in case of nouns there is no such limitation. Here the substitution takes place whether the य has caused the production of ओ and औ or not.

pk: 65. in ksaya and jaya there is substitution or ay ror e only then when the sense is that or "to be posible to do". The rots ksi and ji berore the aril yat (i. 1. 97 s. 2842), asune these rorns when neaning to be able to do the action denoted by the verb. as sakya ksetun = ksaya (ksi + ya = kse + ya) ; so also jaya Why do we say when neaning "to be posible to do"? Observe kseyan papan jeyan nana ere the neaning is that or necesity.
ck: 65. in ksaya ant caya there is supstitution or ay ror e only then then the sense is that or "to pe posiple to to". the rots ksi ant ci perore the aril yat (i. 1. 97 s. 2842), asune these rorns then neanink to pe aple to to the action tenotet py the verp. as sakya ksetun = ksaya (ksi + ya = kse + ya) ; so also caya thy to te say then neanink "to pe posiple to to"? Opserve kseyan papan ceyan nana ere the neanink is that or necesity.
s: 65. In क्षय्य and जय्य there is substitution of अय् for ए only then when the sense is that of "to be possible to do". The roots क्षि and जि before the affix यत् (III. 1. 97 S. 2842), assume these forms when meaning to be able to do the action denoted by the verb. As शक्यः क्षेतुम् = क्षय्यः (क्षि + य = क्षे + य) ; so also जय्यः Why do we say when meaning "to be possible to do"? Observe क्षेयं पापं जेयं मनः Here the meaning is that of 'necessity'.

pk: 6. in kraya there is substitution or ay ror ‹?› when the sense is that or elposed or put out ror sale, saleable. The word kraya is derived ron kri to buy, with the aril yat; the guṇa e being changed to ay The word tadarTe neans ror the purpose or that i.e., ror the purpose or being bought by the purchasers. as ‹?›, ‹?› kanbala Why do we say when the sense is that or saleable? Observe kreyan no Danyan na casti krayan "we want to purchase corn, but it is not put out ror sale".
ck: 6. in kraya there is supstitution or ay ror ‹?› then the sense is that or elposet or put out ror sale, saleaple. the tort kraya is terivet ron kri to puy, tith the aril yat; the kuṇa e peink chanket to ay the tort tatarte neans ror the purpose or that i.e., ror the purpose or peink poukht py the purchasers. as ‹?›, ‹?› kanpala thy to te say then the sense is that or saleaple? Opserve kreyan no tanyan na casti krayan "te tant to purchase corn, put it is not put out ror sale".
s: 66. In क्रय्य there is substitution of अय् for ‹?› when the sense is that of 'exposed or put out for sale, saleable'. The word क्रय्य is derived from क्री 'to buy', with the affix यत्; the guṇa ए being changed to अय् The word तदर्थे means 'for the purpose of that' i.e., for the purpose of being bought by the purchasers. As ‹?›, ‹?› कम्बलः Why do we say 'when the sense is that of saleable'? Observe क्रेयं नो धान्यं न चास्ति क्रय्यम् "we want to purchase corn, but it is not put out for sale".

pk: 67. v and y preceded by a or a and at the end or a pada, are elided berore an as leter, acording to the opinion or Śākalya. When this lopa once takes place, there is no rurther conbination or vowels; because the rule or purvatrasidDan or Vi. 2. 1. s. 12. intervenes and nakes this lopa as ir non-elistent. Thus, we have hare + ehi = hara ehi or harayehi (O ari; cone); so also visno + iha = visna iha or visnaviha and sriyE + udyata = sriya udyata or sriyayudyata ; gurO + utka = gura utka or guravutka in the rolowing elanples kani + santi and kO + sta the rule Vi. 1. 7 s. 47 and this rule would have aplied respectively because santi is realy asanti and sta is realy asta the a being elided. an ādeśa is equal to the sthānī as we have ben taught in sūtra i. 1. 56 s. 49. Thererore we ought to have rorns like kanyasanti and kasta. But this is prevented by sūtra i. 1. 58 s. 51, ror an ādeśa is not equal to a sthānī when a Padānta rule is to be aplied. now the substitution or senivowels by sūtra Vi. 1. 7 s. 47 or the lopa or this sūtra is a Padānta rule and hence the ādeśa is not equal to a sthānī. as ka aste or kayaste, kaka aste or kakayaste, asna udDara or asnayudDara, asavatra or asa atra, asavaditya or asa aditya
ck: 67. v ant y precetet py a or a ant at the ent or a pata, are elitet perore an as leter, acortink to the opinion or Śākalya. then this lopa once takes place, there is no rurther conpination or votels; pecause the rule or purvatrasitan or Vi. 2. 1. s. 12. intervenes ant nakes this lopa as ir non-elistent. thus, te have hare + ehi = hara ehi or harayehi (O ari; cone); so also visno + iha = visna iha or visnaviha ant sriyE + utyata = sriya utyata or sriyayutyata ; kurO + utka = kura utka or kuravutka in the rolotink elanples kani + santi ant kO + sta the rule Vi. 1. 7 s. 47 ant this rule toult have apliet respectively pecause santi is realy asanti ant sta is realy asta the a peink elitet. an āteśa is etual to the sthānī as te have pen taukht in sūtra i. 1. 56 s. 49. thererore te oukht to have rorns like kanyasanti ant kasta. put this is preventet py sūtra i. 1. 58 s. 51, ror an āteśa is not etual to a sthānī then a patānta rule is to pe apliet. not the supstitution or senivotels py sūtra Vi. 1. 7 s. 47 or the lopa or this sūtra is a patānta rule ant hence the āteśa is not etual to a sthānī. as ka aste or kayaste, kaka aste or kakayaste, asna utara or asnayutara, asavatra or asa atra, asavatitya or asa atitya
s: 67. व् and य् preceded by अ or आ and at the end of a pada, are elided before an अश् letter, according to the opinion of Śākalya. When this lopa once takes place, there is no further combination of vowels; because the rule of पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् of VIII. 2. 1. S. 12. intervenes and makes this lopa as if non-existent. Thus, we have हरे + एहि = हर एहि or हरयेहि (O Hari; come); so also विष्णो + इह = विष्ण इह or विष्णविह and श्रियै + उद्यतः = श्रिया उद्यतः or श्रियायुद्यतः ; गुरौ + उत्कः = गुरा उत्कः or गुरावुत्कः In the following examples कानि + सन्ति and कौ + स्तः the rule VI. 1. 77 S. 47 and this rule would have applied respectively because सन्ति is really असन्ति and स्तः is really अस्तः the अ being elided. An ādeśa is equal to the sthānī as we have been taught in Sūtra I. 1. 56 S. 49. Therefore we ought to have forms like कान्यसन्ति and कास्तः. But this is prevented by Sūtra I. 1. 58 S. 51, for an ādeśa is not equal to a sthānī when a Padānta rule is to be applied. Now the substitution of semivowels by sūtra VI. 1. 77 S. 47 or the lopa of this Sūtra is a Padānta rule and hence the ādeśa is not equal to a Sthānī. As क आस्ते or कयास्ते, काक आस्ते or काकयास्ते, अस्मा उद्धर or अस्मायुद्धर, असावत्र or असा अत्र, असावादित्यः or असा आदित्यः

pk: 69. The guṇa is the single substitute or the rinal ‹?› or ‹?› or a preceding word and the sinple vowel or the suceding (‹?› or ‹?› + sinple vowel = guṇa). The word ‹?› is understod here. ror the vowel which rolows an ‹?› or ‹?›, and ror the ‹?› or ‹?› which precedes a vowel, in the ron or both these vowels, there is the single substitute, nanely, guṇa. Thus ‹?› + ‹?› = upendra ; rana + isa = ranesa ; ganga + udakan = gangodakan
ck: 69. the kuṇa is the sinkle supstitute or the rinal ‹?› or ‹?› or a precetink tort ant the sinple votel or the sucetink (‹?› or ‹?› + sinple votel = kuṇa). the tort ‹?› is unterstot here. ror the votel thich rolots an ‹?› or ‹?›, ant ror the ‹?› or ‹?› thich precetes a votel, in the ron or poth these votels, there is the sinkle supstitute, nanely, kuṇa. thus ‹?› + ‹?› = upentra ; rana + isa = ranesa ; kanka + utakan = kankotakan
s: 69. The guṇa is the single substitute of the final ‹?› or ‹?› of a preceding word and the simple vowel of the succeeding (‹?› or ‹?› + simple vowel = guṇa). The word ‹?› is understood here. For the vowel which follows an ‹?› or ‹?›, and for the ‹?› or ‹?› which precedes a vowel, in the room of both these vowels, there is the single substitute, namely, guṇa. Thus ‹?› + ‹?› = उपेन्द्रः ; रमा + ईशः = रमेशः ; गङ्गा + उदकम् = गङ्गोदकम्

pk: 70. When a leter or ‹?› pratyâhâra cones as a substitute ror ‹?› it is always rolowed by a ‹?›. This sūtra consists or thre words vis., ‹?› which is the genitive singular or ‹?› and neans literaly or or in the place or ‹?›; the second word is ‹?›, a pratyâhâra denoting ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?› long and short; the third word is ‹?› which qualiries ‹?› and neans having a ‹?› arter. This sūtra is userul in riling the proper substitutes or ‹?›. Thus, there are only thre guṇa vowels ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?›. Or these what is the proper guṇa ror ‹?› By the aplication or the rule or nearnes or place we se that ‹?› is the nearest substitute. so that ‹?› is the guṇa or ‹?›; and rurther by this rule, this ‹?› nust have a ‹?› arter it. Thus though technicaly speaking ‹?› is the guṇa or ‹?›, the actual substitute is ‹?› The ‹?› in the telt has ben taken by sone to be a pratyâhâra rorned by the leter ‹?› and ‹?› or ‹?›; and thus it includes the leters r and l. in that case the sūtra would nean, that substitutes or ‹?› and ‹?› are always rolowed by ‹?› and ‹?› respectively. Thus the guṇa or ṛi = ar, or ḷi = al. it has already ben taught that ‹?› is the nane or 30 leters. Vis: 18 rorns or ‹?› and 12 rorns or ‹?›. in the place or these 30 vowels, whenever an ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?› is substituted, it nust always be rolowed by a ‹?›. Thererore krsna + ‹?› = ‹?›. ere ‹?› is rolowed by ‹?› as the nearest substitute or r. sinilarly ‹?› + ‹?› = ‹?›. ere ‹?› is rolowed by ‹?› as the nearest substitute or ‹?›. sinilarly there is doubling when the rule ‹?› (Vi. 4. 46 s. 59) is aplied.
ck: 70. then a leter or ‹?› pratyâhâra cones as a supstitute ror ‹?› it is altays rolotet py a ‹?›. this sūtra consists or thre torts vis., ‹?› thich is the kenitive sinkular or ‹?› ant neans literaly or or in the place or ‹?›; the secont tort is ‹?›, a pratyâhâra tenotink ‹?›, ‹?› ant ‹?› lonk ant short; the thirt tort is ‹?› thich tualiries ‹?› ant neans havink a ‹?› arter. this sūtra is userul in rilink the proper supstitutes or ‹?›. thus, there are only thre kuṇa votels ‹?›, ‹?› ant ‹?›. Or these that is the proper kuṇa ror ‹?› py the aplication or the rule or nearnes or place te se that ‹?› is the nearest supstitute. so that ‹?› is the kuṇa or ‹?›; ant rurther py this rule, this ‹?› nust have a ‹?› arter it. thus thoukh technicaly speakink ‹?› is the kuṇa or ‹?›, the actual supstitute is ‹?› the ‹?› in the telt has pen taken py sone to pe a pratyâhâra rornet py the leter ‹?› ant ‹?› or ‹?›; ant thus it inclutes the leters r ant l. in that case the sūtra toult nean, that supstitutes or ‹?› ant ‹?› are altays rolotet py ‹?› ant ‹?› respectively. thus the kuṇa or ṛi = ar, or ḷi = al. it has alreaty pen taukht that ‹?› is the nane or 30 leters. Vis: 18 rorns or ‹?› ant 12 rorns or ‹?›. in the place or these 30 votels, thenever an ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?› is supstitutet, it nust altays pe rolotet py a ‹?›. thererore krsna + ‹?› = ‹?›. ere ‹?› is rolotet py ‹?› as the nearest supstitute or r. sinilarly ‹?› + ‹?› = ‹?›. ere ‹?› is rolotet py ‹?› as the nearest supstitute or ‹?›. sinilarly there is touplink then the rule ‹?› (Vi. 4. 46 s. 59) is apliet.
s: 70. When a letter of ‹?› pratyâhâra comes as a substitute for ‹?› it is always followed by a ‹?›. This sūtra consists of three words viz., ‹?› which is the genitive singular of ‹?› and means literally 'of' or 'in the place of ‹?›'; the second word is ‹?›, a pratyâhâra denoting ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?› long and short; the third word is ‹?› which qualifies ‹?› and means 'having a ‹?› after'. This sūtra is useful in fixing the proper substitutes of ‹?›. Thus, there are only three guṇa vowels ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?›. Of these what is the proper guṇa for ‹?› By the application of the rule of 'nearness of place' we see that ‹?› is the nearest substitute. So that ‹?› is the guṇa of ‹?›; and further by this rule, this ‹?› must have a ‹?› after it. Thus though technically speaking ‹?› is the guṇa of ‹?›, the actual substitute is ‹?› The ‹?› in the text has been taken by some to be a pratyâhâra formed by the letter ‹?› and ‹?› of ‹?›; and thus it includes the letters r and l. In that case the sūtra would mean, that substitutes of ‹?› and ‹?› are always followed by ‹?› and ‹?› respectively. Thus the guṇa of ṛi = ar, of ḷi = al. It has already been taught that ‹?› is the name of 30 letters. Viz: 18 forms of ‹?› and 12 forms of ‹?›. In the place of these 30 vowels, whenever an ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?› is substituted, it must always be followed by a ‹?›. Therefore कृष्ण + ‹?› = ‹?›. Here ‹?› is followed by ‹?› as the nearest substitute of ॠ. Similarly ‹?› + ‹?› = ‹?›. Here ‹?› is followed by ‹?› as the nearest substitute of ‹?›. Similarly there is doubling when the rule ‹?› (VIII. 4. 46 S. 59) is applied.

pk: 73. The Vridhi is the single substitute ror the a or a + e or eti (rot in) and eDate (rot eD), and ror a or a + u or uW (the substitute or vah by Vi. 4. 132 s. 329). The whole or the last sûtra and at are understod here. The ec or the last sûtra qualiries the rot in eti, i. e. when the rot asunes the rorn ec by internal changes, then aplies this Vridhi rule. The ec does not qualiry the rot eD as that rot always has an initial diphthong, nor does it qualiry uW ror u is not a diphthong. Thus upa + eti = upEti, upa + eDate = upEDate, prasWa + uha = prasWOha in the last elanple, guna was the substitute required by Vi. 1. 87 s. 69, the present sutra ordains Vridhi instead. in the case or eti and eDate, the Vridhi was debared by Vi. 1. 94, s. 78; this sūtra nakes an elception to that rule. The present sutra is an elception to Vi. 1. 94 and not to Vi. 1. 95, s. 80 because the nalin is purastadapavada anantaran viDin baDante notaran "apavādas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede only those rules that stand nearest to then, not the subsequent rules.” Thererore the present rule does not aply here:— upa + a + ita = upa + eta = upeta (ere though ‹?› is changed to e, the rule does not aply). Thererore the rorn avEhi is wrong. so also upa + ita = upeta ror here the rot has not asuned the rorn e, thererore the rule does not aply, the word ejadyo qualiries the rot Vart:—The Vridhi is the single substitute when aksa is rolowed by uhini, as aksOhini sena Vart:—The Vridhi is the single substitute when sva is rolowed by ira or irin, or irini thus svEran, svEri, svErini The word svEra is rorned by the aril Gan aded to ir gatO : (ad. 8. svenaBiprayena iranan = svEran the conpounding takes place by i. 1. 32. s. 694). another rorn is svEri = svenaBiprayenerate gacCatiti with the aril nini (i. 2. 78 s. 2938). Vart:—The Vridhi is the single substitute when pra is rolowed by uha, uQa, uQi, esa, esya; as prOha, prOQa, prOQi, prEsa, prEsya But by the nalin arTavadgrahane nanarTakasya grahanan, a nalin which we inrer ron the sutra Vi. 2. 36 s. 294 where the word Braj is taken separately ron Brasa, the rule aplies only to the participle in kta and not to that in ktavatu. Thererore we have proQavan. The word esa is derived ron the rot is to wish (Tud. 59), is to go (Div. 18), and is to repeat (Kry. 53), by ading the aril Gan, and the word esya is derived ron the sane rots by ading nyat This Vartika ordains Vridhi,
ck: 73. the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute ror the a or a + e or eti (rot in) ant etate (rot et), ant ror a or a + u or ut (the supstitute or vah py Vi. 4. 132 s. 329). the thole or the last sûtra ant at are unterstot here. the ec or the last sûtra tualiries the rot in eti, i. e. then the rot asunes the rorn ec py internal chankes, then aplies this Vrithi rule. the ec toes not tualiry the rot et as that rot altays has an initial tiphthonk, nor toes it tualiry ut ror u is not a tiphthonk. thus upa + eti = upEti, upa + etate = upEtate, prasta + uha = prastOha in the last elanple, kuna tas the supstitute retuiret py Vi. 1. 87 s. 69, the present sutra ortains Vrithi insteat. in the case or eti ant etate, the Vrithi tas teparet py Vi. 1. 94, s. 78; this sūtra nakes an elception to that rule. the present sutra is an elception to Vi. 1. 94 ant not to Vi. 1. 95, s. 80 pecause the nalin is purastatapavata anantaran vitin patante notaran "apavātas that precete the rules thich teach operations that have to pe supersetet py the apavata operations, supersete only those rules that stant nearest to then, not the supsetuent rules.” thererore the present rule toes not aply here:— upa + a + ita = upa + eta = upeta (ere thoukh ‹?› is chanket to e, the rule toes not aply). thererore the rorn avEhi is tronk. so also upa + ita = upeta ror here the rot has not asunet the rorn e, thererore the rule toes not aply, the tort ecatyo tualiries the rot Vart:—the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute then aksa is rolotet py uhini, as aksOhini sena Vart:—the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute then sva is rolotet py ira or irin, or irini thus svEran, svEri, svErini the tort svEra is rornet py the aril kan atet to ir katO : (at. 8. svenapiprayena iranan = svEran the conpountink takes place py i. 1. 32. s. 694). another rorn is svEri = svenapiprayenerate kacatiti tith the aril nini (i. 2. 78 s. 2938). Vart:—the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute then pra is rolotet py uha, uta, uti, esa, esya; as prOha, prOta, prOti, prEsa, prEsya put py the nalin artavatkrahane nanartakasya krahanan, a nalin thich te inrer ron the sutra Vi. 2. 36 s. 294 there the tort prac is taken separately ron prasa, the rule aplies only to the participle in kta ant not to that in ktavatu. thererore te have protavan. the tort esa is terivet ron the rot is to tish (tut. 59), is to ko (tiv. 18), ant is to repeat (kry. 53), py atink the aril kan, ant the tort esya is terivet ron the sane rots py atink nyat this Vartika ortains Vrithi, th
s: 73. The Vriddhi is the single substitute for the अ or आ + ए of एति (root इण्) and एधते (root एध्), and for अ or आ + ऊ of ऊठ् (the substitute of वाह् by VI. 4. 132 S. 329). The whole of the last sûtra and आत् are understood here. The एच् of the last sûtra qualifies the root in एति, i. e. when the root assumes the form एच् by internal changes, then applies this Vriddhi rule. The एच् does not qualify the root एध् as that root always has an initial diphthong, nor does it qualify ऊठ् for ऊ is not a diphthong. Thus उप + एति = उपैति, उप + एधते = उपैधते, प्रष्ठ + ऊह = प्रष्ठौहः In the last example, guna was the substitute required by VI. 1. 87 S. 69, the present sutra ordains Vriddhi instead. In the case of एति and एधते, the Vriddhi was debarred by VI. 1. 94, S. 78; this sūtra makes an exception to that rule. The present sutra is an exception to VI. 1. 94 and not to VI. 1. 95, S. 80 because the maxim is पुरस्तादपवादा अनन्तरान् विधीन् बाधन्ते नोत्तरान् "Apavādas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede only those rules that stand nearest to them, not the subsequent rules.” Therefore the present rule does not apply here:— उप + आ + इतः = उप + एतः = उपेतः (Here though ‹?› is changed to ए, the rule does not apply). Therefore the form अवैहि is wrong. So also उप + इतः = उपेतः for here the root has not assumed the form ए, therefore the rule does not apply, the word एजाद्योः qualifies the root Vart:—The Vriddhi is the single substitute when अक्ष is followed by ऊहिनी, as अक्षौहिणी सेना Vart:—The Vriddhi is the single substitute when स्व is followed by ईर or ईरिन्, or ईरिणी thus स्वैरम्, स्वैरी, स्वैरिणी The word स्वैर is formed by the affix घञ् added to ईर् गतौ : (Ad. 8. स्वेनाभिप्रायेण ईरणं = स्वैरम् the compounding takes place by II. 1. 32. S. 694). Another form is स्वैरी = स्वेनाभिप्रायेणेरते गच्छतीति with the affix णिनि (III. 2. 78 S. 2938). Vart:—The Vriddhi is the single substitute when प्र is followed by ऊह, ऊढ, ऊढि, एष, एष्य; as प्रौहः, प्रौढः, प्रौढिः, प्रैषः, प्रैष्यः But by the maxim अर्थवद्ग्रहणे नानर्थकस्य ग्रहणम्, a maxim which we infer from the sutra VIII. 2. 36 S. 294 where the word भ्राज् is taken separately from भ्राश, the rule applies only to the participle in क्त and not to that in क्तवतु. Therefore we have प्रोढवान्. The word एष is derived from the root इष् 'to wish' (Tud. 59), इष् 'to go' (Div. 18), and इष् 'to repeat' (Kry. 53), by adding the affix घञ्, and the word एष्य is derived from the same roots by adding ण्यत् This Vartika ordains Vriddhi, while VI. 1. 94 would have caused pararupa : प्रैषः, प्रैष्यः While the roots इष् 'to glean', and ईष् 'to go, to injure', 'to show' (Bh. 115 and 642), form ईषः and ईष्यः with the above affixes, and with श्यन्, their forms will be प्रेषः and प्रेष्यः Vart:—The Vriddhi is the single substitute when a word ending in ‹?› is followed by ऋत and forms an Instrumental Tatpurusha compound: as सुखेन ऋतः = सुखार्तः Why in Instrumental? Observe परमर्तः Vart:—The Vriddhi is the single substitute when the word ऋण follows the following :— प्र, वत्सतर, कम्बल, वसन As प्रार्णम् 'principal debt', वत्सतरार्णम् 'the debt of a steer' &c. Vart:—So also when the words ऋण and दश are followed by ऋण, as ऋणार्णम् and दशार्णम् The word ऋणार्ण means a debt incurred to pay off a prior debt. The Dasarna is the name of a river and of a country. The word ऋण means inaccessible place as well as water, in addition to its well-known meaning of debt.

pk: 74. The Vridhi is the single substitute when the a or a or a preposition (upasarga) is rolowed by the short r or a verb. The word at is understod here also. When a preposition ending in a or a is rolowed by a rot begining with r the Vridhi is the single substitute ror the precedent a or a and the subsequent r. This debars the guna taught in Vi. 1. 87. s. 69. Thus upa + rcCati = uparcCati, prarcCati
ck: 74. the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute then the a or a or a preposition (upasarka) is rolotet py the short r or a verp. the tort at is unterstot here also. then a preposition entink in a or a is rolotet py a rot pekinink tith r the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute ror the precetent a or a ant the supsetuent r. this tepars the kuna taukht in Vi. 1. 87. s. 69. thus upa + rcati = uparcati, prarcati
s: 74. The Vriddhi is the single substitute when the अ or आ of a preposition (upasarga) is followed by the short ऋ of a verb. The word आत् is understood here also. When a preposition ending in अ or आ is followed by a root beginning with ऋ the Vriddhi is the single substitute for the precedent अ or आ and the subsequent ऋ. This debars the guna taught in VI. 1. 87. S. 69. Thus उप + ऋच्छति = उपार्च्छति, प्रार्च्छति

pk: 75. sika (sika) To wet, sprinkle. The rot begins with the palatal, but acording to Dhanapala and Kasyapa it has a dental sa They read it in the list or rots that do not change sa to sa, (supi sanji stu stya sika &c.) law - sikate liw - sisike luw - sikita lrw - sikisyate low - sikatan lan - asikata lin - siketa asirlin - sikisiswa lun - asikiswa lrn - asikisyata Pasive sikyate Desiderative sisikisate intensive sesikyate naṅ-luk sesikiti or sesikti aor. asikit asEkit Causative : sikayati, aor. asisikat noun : sika
ck: 75. sika (sika) to tet, sprinkle. the rot pekins tith the palatal, put acortink to thanapala ant kasyapa it has a tental sa they reat it in the list or rots that to not chanke sa to sa, (supi sanci stu stya sika &c.) lat - sikate lit - sisike lut - sikita lrt - sikisyate lot - sikatan lan - asikata lin - siketa asirlin - sikisista lun - asikista lrn - asikisyata pasive sikyate tesiterative sisikisate intensive sesikyate naṅ-luk sesikiti or sesikti aor. asikit asEkit causative : sikayati, aor. asisikat noun : sika
s: 75. शीक (सीक) 'To wet, sprinkle.' The root begins with the palatal, but according to Dhanapala and Kasyapa it has a dental स They read it in the list of roots that do not change स to ष, (सुपि सञ्जि स्तू स्त्या सीक &c.) लट् - शीकते लिट् - शिशीके लुट् - शीकिता लृट् - शीकिष्यते लोट् - शीकताम् लङ् - अशीकत लिङ् - शीकेत आशीर्लिङ् - शीकिषीष्ट लुङ् - अशीकिष्ट लृङ् - अशीकिष्यत Passive शीक्यते Desiderative शिशीकिषते Intensive शेशीक्यते Yaṅ-luk शेशीकीति or शेशीक्ति Aor. अशीकीत् अशैकीत् Causative : शीकयति, Aor. अशीशिकत् Noun : शीका

pk: 76. loka to se, view, perceive. law - lokate liw - luloke &c. When neaning to speak it is Churâdi.
ck: 76. loka to se, viet, perceive. lat - lokate lit - luloke &c. then neanink to speak it is churâti.
s: 76. लोक 'to see, view, perceive.' लट् - लोकते लिट् - लुलोके &c. When meaning 'to speak' it is Churâdi.

pk: 7. sloka to heap together, colect. sanGata neans colection or bok. acording to swani and others the rot neans the act or being conposed into a bok. acording to Kasyapa and others, it neans the act or the conposer. it thererore neans to praise, or conpose in verse, versiry. in the rirst case it is intransitive, in the second case Transitive. law - slokate &c.
ck: 7. sloka to heap tokether, colect. sankata neans colection or pok. acortink to stani ant others the rot neans the act or peink conposet into a pok. acortink to kasyapa ant others, it neans the act or the conposer. it thererore neans to praise, or conpose in verse, versiry. in the rirst case it is intransitive, in the secont case transitive. lat - slokate &c.
s: 77. श्लोक 'to heap together, collect.' संघात means collection or book. According to Swami and others the root means the act of being composed into a book. According to Kasyapa and others, it means the act of the composer. It therefore means 'to praise, or compose in verse, versify.' In the first case it is Intransitive, in the second case Transitive. लट् - श्लोकते &c.

pk: 78. ror the a or a or the Preposition + e or o or a verbal rot, the second vowel is the single substitute. The words at, upasargadDatO are understod here. in an upasarga ending in a or a rolowed by a rot begining with e or o, the vowels coalesce and the single-substitute is the rorn or the second vowel (pararupa). This debars Vridhi taught in Vi. 1. 8 s. 72. Thus prejate; uposati sone read into this sutra the option alowed by Vi. 1. 92, s. 7 acording to then the para-rupa substitution is optional in the case or Denoninative rots. Thus upeqakiyati or upEqakiyati, prosiyati or prOsiyati. Várt:—The Para-rupa substitution takes place when eva rolows a word and the sense is not that or apointnent. Thus kvEva Boksyase (where wil you eat) neaning there is no ron ror you to sit and eat or i do not think that you wil get rod to eat. ere the sense or eva is that or uncertainty. When the sense is that or niyoga the Vridhi takes place: as tavEva, (Thine alone.)
ck: 78. ror the a or a or the preposition + e or o or a verpal rot, the secont votel is the sinkle supstitute. the torts at, upasarkatatO are unterstot here. in an upasarka entink in a or a rolotet py a rot pekinink tith e or o, the votels coalesce ant the sinkle-supstitute is the rorn or the secont votel (pararupa). this tepars Vrithi taukht in Vi. 1. 8 s. 72. thus precate; uposati sone reat into this sutra the option alotet py Vi. 1. 92, s. 7 acortink to then the para-rupa supstitution is optional in the case or tenoninative rots. thus upetakiyati or upEtakiyati, prosiyati or prOsiyati. Várt:—the para-rupa supstitution takes place then eva rolots a tort ant the sense is not that or apointnent. thus kvEva poksyase (there til you eat) neanink there is no ron ror you to sit ant eat or i to not think that you til ket rot to eat. ere the sense or eva is that or uncertainty. then the sense is that or niyoka the Vrithi takes place: as tavEva, (thine alone.)
s: 78. For the अ or आ of the Preposition + ए or ओ of a verbal root, the second vowel is the single substitute. The words अत्, उपसर्गाद्धातौ are understood here. In an upasarga ending in अ or आ followed by a root beginning with ए or ओ, the vowels coalesce and the single-substitute is the form of the second vowel (पररूप). This debars Vriddhi taught in VI. 1. 88 S. 72. Thus प्रेजते; उपोषति Some read into this sutra the option allowed by VI. 1. 92, S. 77 according to them the para-rupa substitution is optional in the case of Denominative roots. Thus उपेडकीयति or उपैडकीयति, प्रोषीयति or प्रौषीयति. Várt:—The Para-rupa substitution takes place when एव follows a word and the sense is not that of 'appointment'. Thus क्वैव भोक्ष्यसे (where will you eat) meaning there is no room for you to sit and eat or I do not think that you will get food to eat. Here the sense of एव is that of uncertainty. When the sense is that of नियोग the Vriddhi takes place: as तवैव, (Thine alone.)

pk: 79. The rinal portion or a word, begining with the last anong the vowels in the word, is caled wi. This sutra derines wi. it is that portion or a word which is included betwen the last leter and the nearest vowel. Thus in the word agnicit the portion it is wi; so also in sonasut the portion ut. The word aca in the sutra is in the genitive case, which has the rorce or nirdharana or specirication; and though it is in the singular nunber, it represents clas nane, neaning anong the vowels. This sutra is used here in order to nake it aplicable to the rolowing Vartikas. Vart:—The Para-rupa substitution takes place in the case or sakanDu etc. it takes place in the wi portion or these words and not nerely or the leter, though the anuvriti or a is understod here. ad the Para-rupa ben only or a, we could not have got the rorns like ‹?› which is rorned by ‹?›. The rolowing is the list or sakandhwadi words:—1. sakanDu—the wel or the sakas (saka + anDu wel). 2. karkanDu—the wel or the Karkas 3. kulawa—unchaste wonan (kula + awa) 4. sinanta—sinan + anta (hair parting; when not neaning hair parting, the rorn is sinanta the boundary linit). 5. nanisa—the lord or the nind. 6. halisa—hali + isa (ere isa neans plough stick). 7. langalisa. 8. patanjali—patanta + anjali (one to whon handruls or orering are nade i.e. an honored nan). so also 9. saranga when neaning a variegated beast or a bird, otherwise the rorn is saranga—sara + anga (the chier nenber or a body). The sakandhwadi is an akritigana, i.e. no conplete list or this clas is given anywhere, but whenever we rind a conpound word, in which a para-rupa substitution has taken place, to the elclusion or the ordinary rules or sandhi, we nay sarely place that word in this clas. Thus ‹?› ron which we have the secondary derivative rorn nartanqa. We have the regular rorn ‹?› also. Vart:—The Para-rupa substitution takes place optionaly when otu and osWa are conpounded with another word; as sTula + otu = sTulotu or sTulOtu, so also binbosWa or binbOsWa. When not a conpound the Vridhi is conpulsory: as tavOsWa
ck: 79. the rinal portion or a tort, pekinink tith the last anonk the votels in the tort, is calet ti. this sutra terines ti. it is that portion or a tort thich is inclutet peten the last leter ant the nearest votel. thus in the tort aknicit the portion it is ti; so also in sonasut the portion ut. the tort aca in the sutra is in the kenitive case, thich has the rorce or nirtharana or specirication; ant thoukh it is in the sinkular nunper, it represents clas nane, neanink anonk the votels. this sutra is uset here in orter to nake it aplicaple to the rolotink Vartikas. Vart:—the para-rupa supstitution takes place in the case or sakantu etc. it takes place in the ti portion or these torts ant not nerely or the leter, thoukh the anuvriti or a is unterstot here. at the para-rupa pen only or a, te coult not have kot the rorns like ‹?› thich is rornet py ‹?›. the rolotink is the list or sakanthtati torts:—1. sakantu—the tel or the sakas (saka + antu tel). 2. karkantu—the tel or the karkas 3. kulata—unchaste tonan (kula + ata) 4. sinanta—sinan + anta (hair partink; then not neanink hair partink, the rorn is sinanta the pountary linit). 5. nanisa—the lort or the nint. 6. halisa—hali + isa (ere isa neans ploukh stick). 7. lankalisa. 8. patancali—patanta + ancali (one to thon hantruls or orerink are nate i.e. an honoret nan). so also 9. saranka then neanink a variekatet peast or a pirt, othertise the rorn is saranka—sara + anka (the chier nenper or a poty). the sakanthtati is an akritikana, i.e. no conplete list or this clas is kiven anythere, put thenever te rint a conpount tort, in thich a para-rupa supstitution has taken place, to the elclusion or the ortinary rules or santhi, te nay sarely place that tort in this clas. thus ‹?› ron thich te have the secontary terivative rorn nartanta. te have the rekular rorn ‹?› also. Vart:—the para-rupa supstitution takes place optionaly then otu ant osta are conpountet tith another tort; as stula + otu = stulotu or stulOtu, so also pinposta or pinpOsta. then not a conpount the Vrithi is conpulsory: as tavOsta
s: 79. The final portion of a word, beginning with the last among the vowels in the word, is called टि. This sutra defines टि. It is that portion of a word which is included between the last letter and the nearest vowel. Thus in the word अग्निचित् the portion इत् is टि; so also in सोमसुत् the portion उत्. The word अचः in the sutra is in the genitive case, which has the force of nirdharana or specification; and though it is in the singular number, it represents class name, meaning 'among the vowels.' This sutra is used here in order to make it applicable to the following Vartikas. Vart:—The Para-rupa substitution takes place in the case of शकन्धुः etc. It takes place in the टि portion of these words and not merely of the letter, though the anuvritti of अ is understood here. Had the Para-rupa been only of अ, we could not have got the forms like ‹?› which is formed by ‹?›. The following is the list of Sakandhwadi words:—1. शकन्धुः—the well of the Sakas (शक + अन्धु well). 2. कर्कन्धुः—the well of the Karkas 3. कुलटा—unchaste woman (कुल + अटा) 4. सीमन्तः—सीमन् + अन्तः (hair parting; when not meaning 'hair parting', the form is सीमान्तः the boundary limit). 5. मनीषा—the lord of the mind. 6. हलीषा—हलि + ईषा (Here ईषा means plough stick). 7. लाङ्गलीषा. 8. पतञ्जलिः—पतन्तः + अञ्जलिः (one to whom handfuls of offering are made i.e. an honored man). So also 9. सारङ्गः when meaning a variegated beast or a bird, otherwise the form is साराङ्गः—सार + अङ्गः (the chief member of a body). The Sakandhwadi is an Akritigana, i.e. no complete list of this class is given anywhere, but whenever we find a compound word, in which a para-rupa substitution has taken place, to the exclusion of the ordinary rules of Sandhi, we may safely place that word in this class. Thus ‹?› from which we have the secondary derivative form मार्तण्डः. We have the regular form ‹?› also. Vart:—The Para-rupa substitution takes place optionally when ओतु and ओष्ठ are compounded with another word; as स्थूल + ओतुः = स्थूलोतुः or स्थूलौतुः, so also बिम्बोष्ठः or बिम्बौष्ठः. When not a compound the Vriddhi is compulsory: as तवौष्ठः

pk: 80. reka to doubt, to suspect. When preceded by a it has the neaning or to doubt as in the sentence areke sansayan pasO law - rekate liw - vireke luw - rekita
ck: 80. reka to toupt, to suspect. then precetet py a it has the neanink or to toupt as in the sentence areke sansayan pasO lat - rekate lit - vireke lut - rekita
s: 80. रेक 'to doubt, to suspect.' When preceded by आ it has the meaning of 'to doubt' as in the sentence 'आरेके संशयं पशौ' लट् - रेकते लिट् - विरेके लुट् - रेकिता

pk: 81. The i or iti is the single substitute ror the at (or a word denoting initation or an inarticulate sound) + iti The sound which is not distinct and clear, is caled avyakta; when soneone uters distinctly sonething which has sone resenblance to that sound, by sone contrivance, it is caled anukarana or initation or that sound. Thus pawat + iti = pawiti Várt:—This aplies when the word consists or nore than one sylable. Thererore it does not aply in the rolowing:—srat + iti = sraditi
ck: 81. the i or iti is the sinkle supstitute ror the at (or a tort tenotink initation or an inarticulate sount) + iti the sount thich is not tistinct ant clear, is calet avyakta; then soneone uters tistinctly sonethink thich has sone resenplance to that sount, py sone contrivance, it is calet anukarana or initation or that sount. thus patat + iti = patiti Várt:—this aplies then the tort consists or nore than one sylaple. thererore it toes not aply in the rolotink:—srat + iti = sratiti
s: 81. The इ of इति is the single substitute for the अत् (of a word denoting imitation of an inarticulate sound) + इति The sound which is not distinct and clear, is called अव्यक्त; when someone utters distinctly something which has some resemblance to that sound, by some contrivance, it is called अनुकरण or imitation of that sound. Thus पटत् + इति = पटिति Várt:—This applies when the word consists of more than one syllable. Therefore it does not apply in the following:—श्रत् + इति = श्रदिति

s: 82. This substitution does not take place when a sound-imitation word is doubled, here, however, for the final त् + of इति, the single substitute is optionally इ (the second vowel). s: 83. Of that which is twice uttered, the latter word-form is called amredita (repeated). Thus पटत् पटत् + इति = पटत्पट + इ + ति = पटत्पटिति. Now, this para-rupa rule is optional. The regular form therefore, will be without the elision of the final अत् as पटत् + पटत् + इति = पटत्पटदिति. The त् is changed to द् by the next sutra.

85. When a simple vowel is followed by a homogenous vowel, the corresponding long vowel is the single substitute for both the precedent and the subsequent vowels.
Thus दैत्य + अरिः = दैत्यारिः; श्री + ईशः = श्रीशः; विष्णु + उदयः = विष्णूदयः Why do we say " when a vowel follows " ? Observe कुमारी शेते. The word अच् is understood here also. The word सवर्णे, therefore, qualifies the word अच् understood. The rule will not apply if a homogenous consonant follows. As कुमारी शेते The ‹?› and ‹?› are homogenous, in spite of I. 1. 10: S. 13 for that prohibition does not apply to the long ई and because the rule of classification and inclusion contained in अणुदित्सवर्णस्य चाप्रत्ययः (I. 1. 69 S. 14 ) is not brought into operation at the time when नाज्झलौ (I. 1. 10) rule operates, because of its being a portion of सवर्ण rule. Therefore, so long as it does not come into operation it is not accomplished. Therefore first the rule of नाज्झलौ comes into play, then the rule of सवर्ण definition ( I. 1. 9 S. 10) and then comes the ग्राहकवाक्यम् ( I. 1. 69 S. 15). Therefore in नाज्झलौ those अच् only are taken which are not included in the class of homogenous vowels i. e. only the 9 vowels contained directly in अच्, and not the सवर्ण vowels which I. 1. 69 would have denoted. Therefore though short इ and ‹?› are not सवर्ण by I. 1. 10 the long ‹?› and ‹?› would be savarna. The sutra अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः would have been more clear if stated as अक्यकि 
Why do we say 'an अक् or simple vowel ? Observe ‹?›. Why do we say by a homogenous vowel ?' Observe दधि + अत्र = दध्यत्र 
Vart:—When short ऋ is followed by short ऋ, the long substitution is optional so also with ऌ This vartika is necessitated because ( 1 ) the two ऋ or the precedent and the subsequent ऋ are not homogenous, because one is samvrita and the other vivrita, or ( 2 ) because their prosodial length is 1½ and so the word दीर्घ cannot be applied with consistency in their case (ऌऌकार &c )
Or 3rdly (and this is the opinion of Bhattoji Dikshita) the single substitute short ऋ or short ऌ (which comes in the place of ऋ + ऋ or ऌ + ऌ) is really long consisting of two matras, in this way : होतृ + ऋकारः = होतृ + र् + ऋकारः These two र्'s are not visible in writing, but are there. They constitute one matra, for each consonant has half a matra. Thus one matra of two र्'s and one matra of ऋ make two matras really and though apparently short ऋ is retained, it is practically long. Similarly in the case of ऌ there are two ल्'s. In other words, the short ऋ (that comes in the place of two ऋ's) contains latent in it two र्'s, of one mātrā and its own self of one mātrā. Similarly the single substitute ऌ contains merged in it two ल्'s (of one matra ) and its own self of one matra.
Thus होतृ + ऋकारः = होतॄकारः or होतृकारः, so also होतृ + ऌकारः = होतॄकारः or होतऌकारः The दीर्घ of ऌ is ‹?› 
Moreover, by the rule of ऋत्यकः VI. 1. 128. S. 92 the Sandhi is optional.

s: 91. According to the opinion of Sakalya, the simple vowels with the exception of ṛ, when followed by a non-homogenous vowel, retain their original forms; and if the vowel is long, it is shortened. Thus चक्री + अत्र = चक्री अत्र, चक्रि अत्र The name of Sakalya is mentioned for the sake of respect. Because the alternative nature of this sutra is clear from its very formation. According to Mahabhashya, the च in the sutra is redundant. If it be said that च is necessary to draw the anuvritti of Prakriti-bhava, that is not the case. For the mere fact of making the long vowel short, shows that there is Prakriti-bhava. For if there were to take place Sandhi after shortening, as ‹?›, then where is the good of shortening, for the last form could have been obtained without shortening. Why do we say final in a Pada? Of nitya-compounds are वैयाकरण, सौवश्वः, व्याकरणं, कुमार्यम् which are so by II. 2. 18 S. 761. Thus वाप्यश्वः is an example of compound; and पार्श्वम् formed by the affix सित् see I. 4. 16, S. 1252.
