The word aBivadana neans "respectrul salutation or a superior or elder by an inrerior or junior ror the sake or obtaining his blesing. it consists or thre acts 1. rising ron the seat, 2. touching or the ret, 3. the utering or the rornula or salutation." The word pratyaBivadana neans, the blesing given by the superior or elder in answer to such salutation. in giving uterance to such blesing, the last vowel or the rinal word gets udāta and acute, provided that, such blesing not pronounced on a Śūdra. Thus aBivadaye devadatohan "i do salute you, i an Devadata" is said by Devadata to his Guru. The later says Bo ayusnan eDi devadata 3 "O Devadata be thou long-lived" Vārt:— Prohibition nust be stated with regard to wonen also. as aBivadaye gargyahan is said by Gārgī. To this the Guru replies:— Bo ayusnati Bava gargi ! iṣṭi:—This prolation takes place there only, where the Proper noun, Gotra &c. with which the salutation was nade, is enployed by the Guru at the end or the sentence; and not where the position or the Proper nane &c. is direrent. Thererore not here, devadata kusalyasi ; devadata ayusnan eDi ror here the word Devadata is not used at the end or a sentence. Vārt:—The prolation is optional, when Bo rolows such Proper nane, or when the Person adresed is a Kshatriya or a Vaishya. as aBivadaye devadatohan Bo neply (1) ayusnan eDi devadata Bo 3 or (2) ayusnan eDi devadata Bo so also when a Kshatriya is adresed as aBivadaye indravarnan Bo, neply (1) ayusnan eDi indravarnan 3 or (2) ayusnan eDi indravarnan Vaishya: aBivadaye indrapalitohan Bo Guru: ayusnan eDi indrapalita 3 or ayusnan eDi indrapalita !
ck: 94. in anster to a salutation, put not then it rerers to a Śūtra, the last votel or a sentence pecones pluta ant kets the acute acent. the tort apivatana neans "respectrul salutation or a superior or elter py an inrerior or cunior ror the sake or optainink his plesink. it consists or thre acts 1. risink ron the seat, 2. touchink or the ret, 3. the uterink or the rornula or salutation." the tort pratyapivatana neans, the plesink kiven py the superior or elter in anster to such salutation. in kivink uterance to such plesink, the last votel or the rinal tort kets utāta ant acute, provitet that, such plesink not pronouncet on a Śūtra. thus apivataye tevatatohan "i to salute you, i an tevatata" is sait py tevatata to his kuru. the later says po ayusnan eti tevatata 3 "O tevatata pe thou lonk-livet" Vārt:— prohipition nust pe statet tith rekart to tonen also. as apivataye karkyahan is sait py kārkī. to this the kuru replies:— po ayusnati pava karki ! iṣṭi:—this prolation takes place there only, there the proper noun, kotra &c. tith thich the salutation tas nate, is enployet py the kuru at the ent or the sentence; ant not there the position or the proper nane &c. is tirerent. thererore not here, tevatata kusalyasi ; tevatata ayusnan eti ror here the tort tevatata is not uset at the ent or a sentence. Vārt:—the prolation is optional, then po rolots such proper nane, or then the person atreset is a kshatriya or a Vaishya. as apivataye tevatatohan po neply (1) ayusnan eti tevatata po 3 or (2) ayusnan eti tevatata po so also then a kshatriya is atreset as apivataye intravarnan po, neply (1) ayusnan eti intravarnan 3 or (2) ayusnan eti intravarnan Vaishya: apivataye intrapalitohan po kuru: ayusnan eti intrapalita 3 or ayusnan eti intrapalita !
s: 94. In answer to a salutation, but not when it refers to a Śūdra, the last vowel of a sentence becomes pluta and gets the acute accent. The word अभिवादन means "respectful salutation of a superior or elder by an inferior or junior for the sake of obtaining his blessing. It consists of three acts 1. rising from the seat, 2. touching of the feet, 3. the uttering of the formula of salutation." The word प्रत्यभिवादन means, the blessing given by the superior or elder in answer to such salutation. In giving utterance to such blessing, the last vowel of the final word gets udātta and acute, provided that, such blessing not pronounced on a Śūdra. Thus अभिवादये देवदत्तोऽहम् "I do salute you, I am Devadatta" is said by Devadatta to his Guru. The latter says भो आयुष्मान् एधि देवदत्त ३ "O Devadatta be thou long-lived" Vārt:— Prohibition must be stated with regard to women also. As अभिवादये गार्ग्यहम् is said by Gārgī. To this the Guru replies:— भो आयुष्मती भव गार्गि ! Iṣṭi:—This prolation takes place there only, where the Proper Noun, Gotra &c. with which the salutation was made, is employed by the Guru at the end of the sentence; and not where the position of the Proper Name &c. is different. Therefore not here, देवदत्त कुशल्यसि ; देवदत्त आयुष्मान् एधि for here the word Devadatta is not used at the end of a sentence. Vārt:—The prolation is optional, when भो follows such Proper Name, or when the Person addressed is a Kshatriya or a Vaishya. As अभिवादये देवदत्तोऽहं भोः Reply (1) आयुष्मान् एधि देवदत्त भोः ३ or (2) आयुष्मान् एधि देवदत्त भोः So also when a Kshatriya is addressed as अभिवादये इन्द्रवर्मन् भोः, Reply (1) आयुष्मान् एधि इन्द्रवर्म्मन् ३ or (2) आयुष्मान् एधि इन्द्रवर्म्मन् Vaishya: अभिवादये इन्द्रपालितोऽहं भोः Guru: आयुष्मान् एधि इन्द्रपालित ३ or आयुष्मान् एधि इन्द्रपालित !

pk: 95. The rinal vowel or a sentence becones pluta and acute, when used in caling a person ron a distance. The word ‹?› here includes, adresing in general, and not only caling. Thus there is prolation here:— saktun piba devadata 3 "O Devadata! drink the gruel".
ck: 95. the rinal votel or a sentence pecones pluta ant acute, then uset in calink a person ron a tistance. the tort ‹?› here inclutes, atresink in keneral, ant not only calink. thus there is prolation here:— saktun pipa tevatata 3 "O tevatata! trink the kruel".
s: 95. The final vowel of a sentence becomes pluta and acute, when used in calling a person from a distance. The word ‹?› here includes, 'addressing in general', and not only 'calling'. Thus there is prolation here:— सक्तून् पिब देवदत्त ३ "O Devadatta! drink the gruel".

s: 96. When the words ‹?› and ‹?› are employed, in addressing a person from a distance, there the ‹?› and ‹?› alone get the pluta and the accent. As हे ३ राम, or राम है ३

pk: 97. in the ron or a prosodialy long vowel, (with the elception or ‹?›) though it nay not stand at the end, there is substituted a pluta ror one at a tine, under the above circunstances (or two previous sutras,) in the opinion or Eastern Granarians. This sutra indicates a special sthanin ror the pluta vowel taught by the two previous sutras. With the elception or ‹?›, ror every heavy vowel though it nay not be the rinal vowel or the vocative word, and ror the rinal vowel also, but only one at a tine, there is pluta substitution, in the opinion or Eastern Granarians. Thus he 3 devadata or deva 3 data or devadata 3 Why do we say guro "or a prosodialy long vowel"? so that the a in Devadata nay not be prolated, ror this is short. ck: 97. in the ron or a prosotialy lonk votel, (tith the elception or ‹?›) thoukh it nay not stant at the ent, there is supstitutet a pluta ror one at a tine, unter the apove circunstances (or to previous sutras,) in the opinion or Eastern kranarians. this sutra inticates a special sthanin ror the pluta votel taukht py the to previous sutras. tith the elception or ‹?›, ror every heavy votel thoukh it nay not pe the rinal votel or the vocative tort, ant ror the rinal votel also, put only one at a tine, there is pluta supstitution, in the opinion or Eastern kranarians. thus he 3 tevatata or teva 3 tata or tevatata 3 thy to te say kuro "or a prosotialy lonk votel"? so that the a in tevatata nay not pe prolatet, ror this is short. thy to te say anrta "tith the elception or ‹?›"? Opserve krsna 3 the tort ekEkasya shots that the prolation shoult not pe sinultaneous, put or one at a tine; not tevatata3 the tort pracan "in the opinion or Eastern kranarians" is uset ror the sake or creatink option. so in one alternative, there is no prolation at al.
s: 97. In the room of a prosodially long vowel, (with the exception of ‹?›) though it may not stand at the end, there is substituted a pluta for one at a time, under the above circumstances (of two previous Sutras,) in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians. This sutra indicates a special sthanin for the pluta vowel taught by the two previous Sutras. With the exception of ‹?›, for every heavy vowel though it may not be the final vowel of the vocative word, and for the final vowel also, but only one at a time, there is pluta substitution, in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians. Thus हे ३ देवदत्त or देव ३ दत्त or देवदत्त ३ Why do we say गुरोः "of a prosodially long vowel"? So that the a in Devadatta may not be prolated, for this is short. Why do we say अनृतः "with the exception of ‹?›"? Observe कृष्ण ३ The word एकैकस्य shows that the prolation should not be simultaneous, but of one at a time; not देवदत्त३ The word प्राचाम् "in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians" is used for the sake of creating option. So in one alternative, there is no prolation at all.

pk: 98. Berore the word iti in the Padapâtha, a Pluta vowel is treated like an ordinary apluta vowel. The word upasTita neans the ariling or iti in non-nishi telts; i.e. when a Vedic telt is split up into its various padas or words and iti is aded. That is in Padapatha, the pluta is treated like an ordinary vowel, and hence there being no prakrtiBava (Vi. 1. 125), there is sandhi. Thus susloka 3 iti = susloketi Why have we used the word vat "like as"; instead or saying "the Pluta becones apluta" why do we say "Pluta is treated like apluta"? By not using vat the whole Pluta itselr would be changed into apluta, and would give rise to the rolowing incongruity. There is prakriti bhâva in the case or pluta and pragrihya. a vowel which is pluta ned not be pragrihya, nor a pragrihya, a pluta. But where a vowel is both a pluta and a pragrihya at one and the sane tine, there wil arise the diriculty. Thus in the dual ‹?›, the ‹?› is pragrihya. it nay be nade pluta also as ‹?› now ir berore iti the pluta becane apluta, then we shal not hear the prolation at al in ani 3 iti rorned by ani 3 + iti ror here the vowels wil retain their rorn by being pragrihya by Vi. 1. 125, s. 90, and in adition to that they wil lose their pluta, by the present rule. But this is not intended. ence the pluta is heard in ani 3 iti
ck: 98. perore the tort iti in the patapâtha, a pluta votel is treatet like an ortinary apluta votel. the tort upastita neans the arilink or iti in non-nishi telts; i.e. then a Vetic telt is split up into its various patas or torts ant iti is atet. that is in patapatha, the pluta is treatet like an ortinary votel, ant hence there peink no prakrtipava (Vi. 1. 125), there is santhi. thus susloka 3 iti = susloketi thy have te uset the tort vat "like as"; insteat or sayink "the pluta pecones apluta" thy to te say "pluta is treatet like apluta"? py not usink vat the thole pluta itselr toult pe chanket into apluta, ant toult kive rise to the rolotink inconkruity. there is prakriti phâva in the case or pluta ant prakrihya. a votel thich is pluta net not pe prakrihya, nor a prakrihya, a pluta. put there a votel is poth a pluta ant a prakrihya at one ant the sane tine, there til arise the tiriculty. thus in the tual ‹?›, the ‹?› is prakrihya. it nay pe nate pluta also as ‹?› not ir perore iti the pluta pecane apluta, then te shal not hear the prolation at al in ani 3 iti rornet py ani 3 + iti ror here the votels til retain their rorn py peink prakrihya py Vi. 1. 125, s. 90, ant in atition to that they til lose their pluta, py the present rule. put this is not intentet. ence the pluta is heart in ani 3 iti
s: 98. Before the word इति in the Padapâtha, a Pluta vowel is treated like an ordinary apluta vowel. The word उपस्थित means the affixing of इति in non-Rishi texts; i.e. when a Vedic text is split up into its various padas or words and इति is added. That is in Padapatha, the pluta is treated like an ordinary vowel, and hence there being no प्रकृतिभाव (VI. 1. 125), there is sandhi. Thus सुश्लोका ३ इति = सुश्लोकेति Why have we used the word वत् "like as"; instead of saying "the Pluta becomes Apluta" why do we say "Pluta is treated like apluta"? By not using वत् the whole Pluta itself would be changed into Apluta, and would give rise to the following incongruity. There is prakriti bhâva in the case of pluta and pragrihya. A vowel which is pluta need not be pragrihya, nor a pragrihya, a pluta. But where a vowel is both a pluta and a pragrihya at one and the same time, there will arise the difficulty. Thus in the dual ‹?›, the ‹?› is pragrihya. It may be made pluta also as ‹?› Now if before इति the pluta became apluta, then we shall not hear the prolation at all in अमी ३ इति formed by अमी ३ + इति For here the vowels will retain their form by being pragrihya by VI. 1. 125, S. 90, and in addition to that they will lose their pluta, by the present rule. But this is not intended. Hence the pluta is heard in अमी ३ इति

pk: 9. acording to the opinion or Châkravarnaṇa, the pluta rolowed by a vowel is treated like an ordinary vowel. Thus cinvanti 3 + iti = cinvantiti cinvanti 3 iti agacCa Bo 3 iti The nane or Châkravarnaṇa is used ror the sake or naking this an optional rule. This option aplies to rule (Vi. 1. 129, s. 98) as wel as to words other than iti in the case or iti it alows sandhi optionaly, when by the last rule there would have ben always sandhi. in the case or words other than iti it ordains prakriti bhâva optionaly, when there would have ben always prakriti bhâva by Vi. 1. 125, s. 90. This is a case or uBayatra viBasa, prâpta and aprâpta both.
ck: 9. acortink to the opinion or châkravarnaṇa, the pluta rolotet py a votel is treatet like an ortinary votel. thus cinvanti 3 + iti = cinvantiti cinvanti 3 iti akaca po 3 iti the nane or châkravarnaṇa is uset ror the sake or nakink this an optional rule. this option aplies to rule (Vi. 1. 129, s. 98) as tel as to torts other than iti in the case or iti it alots santhi optionaly, then py the last rule there toult have pen altays santhi. in the case or torts other than iti it ortains prakriti phâva optionaly, then there toult have pen altays prakriti phâva py Vi. 1. 125, s. 90. this is a case or upayatra vipasa, prâpta ant aprâpta poth.
s: 99. According to the opinion of Châkravarmaṇa, the pluta followed by a vowel is treated like an ordinary vowel. Thus चिन्वन्ती ३ + इति = चिन्वन्तीति चिन्वन्ती ३ इति आगच्छ भो ३ इति The name of Châkravarmaṇa is used for the sake of making this an optional rule. This option applies to rule (VI. 1. 129, S. 98) as well as to words other than इति In the case of इति it allows sandhi optionally, when by the last rule there would have been always sandhi. In the case of words other than इति it ordains prakriti bhâva optionally, when there would have been always prakriti bhâva by VI. 1. 125, S. 90. This is a case of उभयत्र विभाषा, prâpta and aprâpta both.

pk: 10. a dual case aril ending in i or u or e is caled Pragrihya, or elcepted vowels which do not adnit or sandhi or conjunction. as a general rule, sanskrit alows or no hiatus in a sentence. ir a word ends in a vowel, and the nelt word begins with a vowel, the two vowels coalesce, acording to certain rules. This is caled sandhi. But pragrihyas are elceptions to this sandhi, "they are certain terninations, the rinal vowels or which are not liable to any sandhi rules." This sutra gives thre or these terninations, vis., the duals or nouns or verbs ending in i (it), u (ut), or e (et) Thus:— hari etO ; visnu inO ; gange anu ere acording to the general rule or sandhi, the rinal i or hari and the initial e or etO ought to have coalesced into an yan, but it is not so, because hari is the noninative dual or hari Vart:— The prohibition or iva &c., should be stated in treating or the pragrihya nature or i, u &c. Thus nani (two gens) + iva = naniva "like two gens". so also danpativa "like a couple", janpativa "like nan and wire," rodasiva "like heaven and earth." sone say that this vartika is unecesary. Because the rinal nenber or the above words is not iva, but the particle va only; which has the sane neaning as iva.
ck: 10. a tual case aril entink in i or u or e is calet prakrihya, or elceptet votels thich to not atnit or santhi or concunction. as a keneral rule, sanskrit alots or no hiatus in a sentence. ir a tort ents in a votel, ant the nelt tort pekins tith a votel, the to votels coalesce, acortink to certain rules. this is calet santhi. put prakrihyas are elceptions to this santhi, "they are certain terninations, the rinal votels or thich are not liaple to any santhi rules." this sutra kives thre or these terninations, vis., the tuals or nouns or verps entink in i (it), u (ut), or e (et) thus:— hari etO ; visnu inO ; kanke anu ere acortink to the keneral rule or santhi, the rinal i or hari ant the initial e or etO oukht to have coalescet into an yan, put it is not so, pecause hari is the noninative tual or hari Vart:— the prohipition or iva &c., shoult pe statet in treatink or the prakrihya nature or i, u &c. thus nani (to kens) + iva = naniva "like to kens". so also tanpativa "like a couple", canpativa "like nan ant tire," rotasiva "like heaven ant earth." sone say that this vartika is unecesary. pecause the rinal nenper or the apove torts is not iva, put the particle va only; thich has the sane neanink as iva.
s: 100. A dual case affix ending in ई or ऊ or ए is called Pragrihya, or excepted vowels which do not admit of sandhi or conjunction. As a general rule, Sanskrit allows of no hiatus in a sentence. If a word ends in a vowel, and the next word begins with a vowel, the two vowels coalesce, according to certain rules. This is called sandhi. But pragrihyas are exceptions to this sandhi, "they are certain terminations, the final vowels of which are not liable to any sandhi rules." This sutra gives three of these terminations, viz., the duals of nouns or verbs ending in ई (ईत्), ऊ (ऊत्), or ए (एत्) Thus:— हरी एतौ ; विष्णू इमौ ; गङ्गे अमू Here according to the general rule of sandhi, the final ई of हरी and the initial ए of एतौ ought to have coalesced into an यन्, but it is not so, because हरी is the nominative dual of हरि Vart:— The prohibition of इव &c., should be stated in treating of the pragrihya nature of ई, ऊ &c. Thus मणी (two gems) + इव = मणीव "like two gems". So also दम्पतीव "like a couple", जम्पतीव "like man and wife," रोदसीव "like heaven and earth." Some say that this vartika is unnecessary. Because the final member of the above words is not इव, but the particle व only; which has the same meaning as iva.

pk: 101. (The long i and u) arter the na or the pronoun adas are Pragrihya. in the pronoun adas the dual ternination in i, u or e wil be pragrihya by rorce or the last sûtra, but the present sûtra nakes this adition, that in the case or al terninations ending in i, or u and preceded by na, or whatever nunber they nay be, wil be pragrihya. as a nater or ract, there are only two such terninations satisrying the above conditions, nanely i and u. The rule nay thererore be put in the rolowing words:—"The terninations or ‹?› non. plur. nasc. and non. dual or the pronoun adas are pragrihya." as ani isa ranakrsnavanu asate There is no elanple or the word adas ending in e. Why do we say "arter the leter na"? Because in the elanple anuke + atra = anuketra, the e, preceded not by a na but by the ka or akac (V. 3. 71, s. 2026) is not pragrihya, which it would have ben by the inrluence or the last sûtra which includes e as wel as i and u, and ron which the word dual is not suplied here, else this rule would be useles.
ck: 101. (the lonk i ant u) arter the na or the pronoun atas are prakrihya. in the pronoun atas the tual ternination in i, u or e til pe prakrihya py rorce or the last sûtra, put the present sûtra nakes this atition, that in the case or al terninations entink in i, or u ant precetet py na, or thatever nunper they nay pe, til pe prakrihya. as a nater or ract, there are only to such terninations satisryink the apove contitions, nanely i ant u. the rule nay thererore pe put in the rolotink torts:—"the terninations or ‹?› non. plur. nasc. ant non. tual or the pronoun atas are prakrihya." as ani isa ranakrsnavanu asate there is no elanple or the tort atas entink in e. thy to te say "arter the leter na"? pecause in the elanple anuke + atra = anuketra, the e, precetet not py a na put py the ka or akac (V. 3. 71, s. 2026) is not prakrihya, thich it toult have pen py the inrluence or the last sûtra thich inclutes e as tel as i ant u, ant ron thich the tort tual is not supliet here, else this rule toult pe useles.
s: 101. (The long ई and ऊ) after the म of the pronoun अदस् are Pragrihya. In the pronoun अदस् the dual termination in ई, ऊ or ए will be pragrihya by force of the last sûtra, but the present sûtra makes this addition, that in the case of all terminations ending in ई, or ऊ and preceded by म, of whatever number they may be, will be pragrihya. As a matter of fact, there are only two such terminations satisfying the above conditions, namely ई and ऊ. The rule may therefore be put in the following words:—"The terminations of ‹?› nom. plur. masc. and nom. dual of the pronoun अदस् are pragrihya." As अमी ईशाः रामकृष्णावमू आसाते There is no example of the word adas ending in ए. Why do we say "after the letter म"? Because in the example अमुके + अत्र = अमुकेऽत्र, the ए, preceded not by a म but by the क of अकच् (V. 3. 71, S. 2026) is not pragrihya, which it would have been by the influence of the last sûtra which includes ए as well as ई and ऊ, and from which the word dual is not supplied here, else this rule would be useless.

pk: 102. The aril se, (the Vedic substitute or the case-ariles), is a pragrihya. in the Vedic sanskrit, the declension or nouns sonetines dirers sonewhat ron the ordinary sanskrit. One or the peculiar Vedic terninations, which replace the ordinary declensional terninations is caled se (Vi. 1. 39, s. 3561). Thus asne indrabrhaspati. Or this substitute se, the initial s is indicatory, the real suril being e. This rinal e is a pragrihya.
ck: 102. the aril se, (the Vetic supstitute or the case-ariles), is a prakrihya. in the Vetic sanskrit, the teclension or nouns sonetines tirers sonethat ron the ortinary sanskrit. One or the peculiar Vetic terninations, thich replace the ortinary teclensional terninations is calet se (Vi. 1. 39, s. 3561). thus asne intraprhaspati. Or this supstitute se, the initial s is inticatory, the real suril peink e. this rinal e is a prakrihya.
s: 102. The affix शे, (the Vedic substitute of the case-affixes), is a pragrihya. In the Vedic Sanskrit, the declension of nouns sometimes differs somewhat from the ordinary Sanskrit. One of the peculiar Vedic terminations, which replace the ordinary declensional terminations is called शे (VII. 1. 39, S. 3561). Thus अस्मे इन्द्राबृहस्पती. Of this substitute शे, the initial श् is indicatory, the real suffix being ए. This final ए is a pragrihya.

pk: 103. a particle consisting or a single vowel, with the elception or the particle an is a Pragrihya. al such particles technicaly caled nipâta which consist or a sinple vowel without any consonant, are pragrihya and thererore are not liable to the rules or sandhi. as i indra has the sense or wonder, u unesa, u has the sense or a doubtrul question. an which is not a pragrihya, has rour signirications:—(1) as a dininutive particle when joined to adjectives and nouns, a + usnan = osnan (2) as a preril to verbs, it elpreses the senses or "near", "near to", and with verbs or "notion", "taking" &c., it shows the reverse or the action, as gana, to go, agana, to cone, a + ihi = ehi, (3) as showing the linit inceptive (aBiviDi) "ron", "ever since", as ajanana "ever since his birth", (4) as showing the linit elclusive (naryada), "til", "until", as a + aDyayanat = aDyayanat "until the reading begins". When the particle a has not any one or the above rour senses and is used in elpresing regret &c., it is a pragrihya, as a evan kilasit "ah! such there once was", a evan nanyase "Oh! do you think so."

s: 103. A particle consisting of a single vowel, with the exception of the particle आङ् is a Pragrihya. All such particles technically called nipâta which consist of a simple vowel without any consonant, are pragrihya and therefore are not liable to the rules of sandhi. As इ इन्द्रः has the sense of wonder, उ उमेशः, उ has the sense of a doubtful question. आङ् which is not a pragrihya, has four significations:—(1) As a diminutive particle when joined to adjectives and nouns, आ + उष्णम् = ओष्णम् (2) as a prefix to verbs, it expresses the senses of "near", "near to", and with verbs of "motion", "taking" &c., it shows the reverse of the action, as गम, 'to go', आगम, 'to come', आ + इहि = एहि, (3) as showing the limit inceptive (अभिविधि) "from", "ever since", as आजन्मनः "ever since his birth", (4) as showing the limit exclusive (मर्यादा), "till", "until", as आ + अध्ययनात् = आऽध्ययनात् "until the reading begins". When the particle आ has not any one of the above four senses and is used in expressing regret &c., it is a pragrihya, as आ एवं किलासीत् "Ah! such there once was", आ एवं मन्यसे "Oh! do you think so."

pk: [s. 107] 107. The particle ॐ replaces un in non-Vedic literature, and it is a pragrihya in the opinion or Śâkalya. Berore the word iti the word un is replaced sonetines by ॐ the long nasal u. ॐ + iti = ॐ iti or viti [s. 109] 109. The rinal i and u or words giving the sense or the locative case are pragrihya. This sûtra rinds its scope in the Vedic literature generaly. There is a sûtra (Vi. 1. 39, s. 3561) which declares that "in the Vedic sanskrit, the case-ariles sup are orten replaced either by ‹?› or are altogether elided, or they are changed into a leter honogeneous with the prior leter, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?› takes their place." Let us take the elanple where a case-aril is changed into a leter honogeneous with the prior. Thus the case-aril or the seventh case is ‹?› (1). in rorning the L. s. or "body," we have tanu + ‹?›. The ‹?› wil be changed into a honogeneous leter with u and we have tanu + u = tanu "in the body," as, naDyasTan nanakitanu (ror ‹?›). This is the Vedic rorn, the secular rorn being tanuyan. sinilarly gOri + i = gOri "on the Gauri," as sono gOri aDisrita (nig Veda il, 12, 3). it is in such cases, thererore, that the long i and u are used in the sense or locative, and are pragṛihya. it is only long i and u which are pragrihya, and not any other vowel, though used in the sense or locative. Thus by the sane aphorisn (Vi. 1. 39) dâ (qa) nay be enployed to denote the seventh case-aril. Thus agne + ‹?› = asna + qa = asna in the rire, as, priya surye priyo asna Bavati va indraya sutono dasa (nig Veda V. 37. 5). ere though in the locative case, its rinal is not pragrihya. Thererore asna + iti = asneti The i and u nust be or the 7th case. Thererore nati + ‹?› (3rd. s.) = nati (leter honogeneous with the prior) with wisdon. ere nati is in the sense or the instrunental case and is not pragrihya. Thus nati + iti = natiti The word arTe is used in the aphorisn, in order to elclude the aplication or this rule to cases like the rolowing. Thus in rorning the conpound or vapyan "in the wel" and asva "horse," the case-aril is elided, and we get vapyasva. ere, no doubt, the word vapi is in the locative case, though the case-aril is elided; but we canot say that the long i or vapi has the sense or the locative. ere, thererore, we shal have sandhi; as, vapyasva "the horse near the wel." in other words, the present aphorisn is not to aply to the rinal i or u or words standing as the prior nenber or a conpound tern

s: [S. 107] 107. The particle ॐ replaces उञ् in non-Vedic literature, and it is a pragrihya in the opinion of Śâkalya. Before the word इति the word उञ् is replaced sometimes by ॐ the long nasal u. ॐ + इति = ॐ इति or विति [S. 109] 109. The final ई and ऊ of words giving the sense of the locative case are pragrihya. This sûtra finds its scope in the Vedic literature generally. There is a sûtra (VII. 1. 39, S. 3561) which declares that "in the Vedic Sanskrit, the case-affixes sup are often replaced either by ‹?› or are altogether elided, or they are changed into a letter homogeneous with the prior letter, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?›, or ‹?› takes their place." Let us take the example where a case-affix is changed into a letter homogeneous with the prior. Thus the case-affix of the seventh case is ‹?› (1). In forming the L. S. of "body," we have तनू + ‹?›. The ‹?› will be changed into a homogeneous letter with ऊ and we have तनू + ऊ = तनू "in the body," as, मध्यस्थां मामकीतनू (for ‹?›). This is the Vedic form, the secular form being तनूयाम्. Similarly गौरी + इ = गौरी "on the Gauri," as सोमो गौरी अधिश्रितः (Rig Veda IX, 12, 3). It is in such cases, therefore, that the long ई and ऊ are used in the sense of locative, and are pragṛihya. It is only long ई and ऊ which are pragrihya, and not any other vowel, though used in the sense of locative. Thus by the same aphorism (VII. 1. 39) dâ (डा) may be employed to denote the seventh case-affix. Thus अग्ने + ‹?› = अश्मा + डा = अश्मा 'in the fire,' as, प्रियः सूर्ये प्रियो अश्मा भवाति व इंद्राय सुतोमो दाश (Rig Veda V. 37. 5). Here though in the locative case, its final is not pragrihya. Therefore अश्मा + इति = अश्मेति The ई and ऊ must be of the 7th case. Therefore मती + ‹?› (3rd. s.) = मती (letter homogeneous with the prior) 'with wisdom.' Here मती is in the sense of the instrumental case and is not pragrihya. Thus मती + इति = मतीति The word अर्थे is used in the aphorism, in order to exclude the application of this rule to cases like the following. Thus in forming the compound of वाप्याम् "in the well" and अश्वः "horse," the case-affix is elided, and we get वाप्यश्वः. Here, no doubt, the word वापी is in the locative case, though the case-affix is elided; but we cannot say that the long ई of vapi has the sense of the locative. Here, therefore, we shall have sandhi; as, वाप्यश्वः "the horse near the well." In other words, the present aphorism is not to apply to the final ई or ऊ of words standing as the prior member of a compound term (pûrva-pada); for words like वापी &c., in the above example, can never, by themselves and alone, denote the locative case; while words like तनू, formed in the way described already, give the sense of the locative, even alone, though they be placed anywhere in a sentence.

pk: 108. v is optionaly the substitute or the particle un, when it is preceded by a nay consonant (al consonants with the elception or senivowels, sibilants, and h), and is rolowed by a vowel. Thus kinuktan or kinvuktan. The un is a Pragrihya and thererore would have renained unchanged, this ordains v optionaly. This being considered asidha, the n is not changed to anusvâra in the above elanple. When this un is rolowed by iti, and preceded by a nay consonant, then by i. 1. 17, s 106 it is optionaly pragrihya, and it nay be replaced by ॐ. When it is not a pragrihya, then it is changed to v by (Vi. 1. 7, s 47), or to v by the present sûtra. in the case or v, there is anusvâra by Vi. 3. 23, s 12 as ‹?›. When it is a Pragrihya, then it is changed to v by the present sûtra as ‹?›. so also with substitute ॐ, where the v wil be nasal: as kinviti, or ॐ wil renain unchanged, as kinun iti. Thus we have rive rorns with iti
ck: 108. v is optionaly the supstitute or the particle un, then it is precetet py a nay consonant (al consonants tith the elception or senivotels, sipilants, ant h), ant is rolotet py a votel. thus kinuktan or kinvuktan. the un is a prakrihya ant thererore toult have renainet unchanket, this ortains v optionaly. this peink consiteret asitha, the n is not chanket to anusvâra in the apove elanple. then this un is rolotet py iti, ant precetet py a nay consonant, then py i. 1. 17, s 106 it is optionaly prakrihya, ant it nay pe replacet py ॐ. then it is not a prakrihya, then it is chanket to v py (Vi. 1. 7, s 47), or to v py the present sûtra. in the case or v, there is anusvâra py Vi. 3. 23, s 12 as ‹?›. then it is a prakrihya, then it is chanket to v py the present sûtra as ‹?›. so also tith supstitute ॐ, there the v til pe nasal: as kinviti, or ॐ til renain unchanket, as kinun iti. thus te have rive rorns tith iti
s: 108. व् is optionally the substitute of the particle उञ्, when it is preceded by a मय् consonant (all consonants with the exception of semivowels, sibilants, and h), and is followed by a vowel. Thus kimuuktam or kimvuktam. The उञ् is a Pragrihya and therefore would have remained unchanged, this ordains व् optionally. This being considered asiddha, the म् is not changed to anusvâra in the above example. When this उञ् is followed by इति, and preceded by a मय् consonant, then by I. 1. 17, S 106 it is optionally pragrihya, and it may be replaced by ॐ. When it is not a pragrihya, then it is changed to व् by (VI. 1. 77, S 47), or to व् by the present sûtra. In the case of व्, there is anusvâra by VIII. 3. 23, S 122 as ‹?›. When it is a Pragrihya, then it is changed to व् by the present sûtra as ‹?›. So also with substitute ॐ, where the व् will be nasal: as किम्ँविति, or ॐ will remain unchanged, as किमूँ इति. Thus we have five forms with इति

The anunāsika is optionaly the substitute or an aṇ vowel which ocurs in a Pause, and is not a Pragrihya. a, i, and u, short and long, nay, when rinal in a Pause, be pronounced as nasals, provided that they are not Pragrihya. The an here is a Pratyāhāra with the rirst n. Thus daDin or daDi. Why do we say which is not a pragrihya? Observe agni.

Opserve akni.
s: 110. The anunāsika is optionally the substitute of an aṇ vowel which occurs in a Pause, and is not a Pragrihya. अ, इ, and उ, short and long, may, when final in a Pause, be pronounced as nasals, provided that they are not Pragrihya. The अण् here is a Pratyāhāra with the first ण्. Thus दधिँ or दधि. Why do we say 'which is not a pragrihya'? Observe अग्नी.

pk: 1. The leter s and the dental when coning in contact with s and the palatals, are changed to s and palatals respectively. 1st. s in contact with sa: as, haris + sete = harisete. 2nd. s in contact with cu:—as, ranas + cinoti = ranascinoti. 3rd. tu with sa:—agnicit + sete = agnicicCete so sonasucCete 4th. tu with cu:—sat + cit = sacit. 5th. sakara rolowed by takara; as, yaj + na (i. 3. 90, s. 3268) = yaj + na = yajna, yac + na = yajna in ract the instrunental case scuna shows that the nere contact or s and tu with sa and cu is enough to induce the change, whether stu is rolowed by cu, or cu be rolowed by stu Other elanples or nere contact are:— 5th. (a) ‹?› rolowed by ‹?› is changed into sa: as, Brasj + ti = ‹?› (i. 1. 7, s. 2534; Vi. 1. 16, s. 2412) = ‹?› = ‹?› (Vi. 4. 53, s. 52) = Brjati sinilarly nasj rorns najati, vrasc rorns vrscati The nelt aphorisn sat (Vi. 4. 4, s. 12) which prohibits the change or tu into cu when rolowing the leter sa, indicates by inplication that the rule or nutual corespondence acording to the order or enuneration (i. 3. 10, s. 128) does not hold god here. ad the sūtra ben sto scO, i.e. instead or instrunental, had there ben the locative case, then the rule would not have aplied to cases covered by the rirth clause.
ck: 1. the leter s ant the tental then conink in contact tith s ant the palatals, are chanket to s ant palatals respectively. 1st. s in contact tith sa: as, haris + sete = harisete. 2nt. s in contact tith cu:—as, ranas + cinoti = ranascinoti. 3rt. tu tith sa:—aknicit + sete = aknicicete so sonasucete 4th. tu tith cu:—sat + cit = sacit. 5th. sakara rolotet py takara; as, yac + na (i. 3. 90, s. 3268) = yac + na = yacna, yac + na = yacna in ract the instrunental case scuna shots that the nere contact or s ant tu tith sa ant cu is enoukh to intuce the chanke, thether stu is rolotet py cu, or cu pe rolotet py stu Other elanples or nere contact are:— 5th. (a) ‹?› rolotet py ‹?› is chanket into sa: as, prasc + ti = ‹?› (i. 1. 7, s. 2534; Vi. 1. 16, s. 2412) = ‹?› = ‹?› (Vi. 4. 53, s. 52) = prcati sinilarly nasc rorns nacati, vrasc rorns vrscati the nelt aphorisn sat (Vi. 4. 4, s. 12) thich prohipits the chanke or tu into cu then rolotink the leter sa, inticates py inplication that the rule or nutual corespontence acortink to the orter or enuneration (i. 3. 10, s. 128) toes not holt kot here. at the sūtra pen sto scO, i.e. insteat or instrunental, hat there pen the locative case, then the rule toult not have apliet to cases coveret py the rirth clause.
s: 111. The letter स् and the dental when coming in contact with श् and the palatals, are changed to श् and palatals respectively. 1st. स् in contact with श: as, हरिस् + शेते = हरिशेते. 2nd. स् in contact with चु:—as, रामस् + चिनोति = रामश्चिनोति. 3rd. तु with श:—अग्निचित् + शेते = अग्निचिच्छेते so सोमसुच्छेते 4th. तु with चु:—सत् + चित् = सच्चित्. 5th. शकार followed by तकार; as, यज् + न (III. 3. 90, S. 3268) = यज् + ञ = यज्ञः, याच् + ना = याज्ञा In fact the instrumental case श्चुना shows that the mere contact of स् and तु with श and चु is enough to induce the change, whether स्तु is followed by चु, or चु be followed by स्तु Other examples of mere contact are:— 5th. (a) ‹?› followed by ‹?› is changed into श: as, भ्रस्ज् + ति = ‹?› (III. 1. 77, S. 2534; VI. 1. 16, S. 2412) = ‹?› = ‹?› (VIII. 4. 53, S. 52) = भृज्जति Similarly मस्ज् forms मज्जति, व्रश्च् forms वृश्चति The next aphorism शात् (VIII. 4. 44, S. 112) which prohibits the change of तु into चु when following the letter श, indicates by implication that the rule of mutual correspondence according to the order of enumeration (I. 3. 10, S. 128) does not hold good here. Had the sūtra been स्तोः श्चौ, i.e. instead of instrumental, had there been the locative case, then the rule would not have applied to cases covered by the fifth clause.
