s: 112. In the room of तु there is not a palatal substitute, when श precedes. The words न and स्तोः are understood here. This is an exception to the last rule. Thus विश् + न (III. 3. 90, S. 3268) = विश् + न (VI. 4. 19, S. 2561) = विश्नः Similarly प्रश्नः

pk: 13. The leters s and dentals in contact with s and cerebrals, are changed into s and cerebrals respectively. The word sto is to be read into the sûtra. ere also there is absence or nutual corespondence acording to the order or enuneration. (1) s with s, as, ranas + sasWa = ranasasWa (2) s with w, as, ranas + wikate = ranaswikate (3) t with s, as, pes + ta = peswa (4) t with w, as, tat + wika = tawika cakrin + QOkase = cakrinQOkase
ck: 13. the leters s ant tentals in contact tith s ant cereprals, are chanket into s ant cereprals respectively. the tort sto is to pe reat into the sûtra. ere also there is apsence or nutual corespontence acortink to the orter or enuneration. (1) s tith s, as, ranas + sasta = ranasasta (2) s tith t, as, ranas + tikate = ranastikate (3) t tith s, as, pes + ta = pesta (4) t tith t, as, tat + tika = tatika cakrin + tOkase = cakrintOkase
s: 113. The letters स् and dentals in contact with ष् and cerebrals, are changed into ष् and cerebrals respectively. The word स्तोः is to be read into the sûtra. Here also there is absence of mutual correspondence according to the order of enumeration. (1) स् with ष्, as, रामस् + षष्ठः = रामष्षष्ठः (2) स् with ट्, as, रामस् + टीकते = रामष्टीकते (3) त् with ष्, as, पेष् + ता = पेष्टा (4) त् with ट्, as, तत् + टीका = तट्टीका चक्रिन् + ढौकसे = चक्रिण्ढौकसे

pk: 14. arter wu rinal in a Pada, the change or a dental (stu) to a cerebral (swu), does not take place, elcept in the case or the aril nan Thus saw + santa = sawsanta saw + te = sawte Why do we say padantat rinal in a Pada? Observe iq + te = iwe Why do we say wo arter wu? Observe sarpis + tanan = sarpiswanan Why do we say anan elcept in the case or the aril nān? Observe saw + nan = sanan This elception is very inadequate. ence the rolowing Vārtika: it should be stated rather that navati and nagari as wel as nan are not prevented ron undergoing the cerebral change. as, sanan or sil, sanavati ninety-sil, sanagarya sil cities.
ck: 14. arter tu rinal in a pata, the chanke or a tental (stu) to a cerepral (stu), toes not take place, elcept in the case or the aril nan thus sat + santa = satsanta sat + te = sate thy to te say patantat rinal in a pata? Opserve it + te = ite thy to te say to arter tu? Opserve sarpis + tanan = sarpistanan thy to te say anan elcept in the case or the aril nān? Opserve sat + nan = sanan this elception is very inatetuate. ence the rolotink Vārtika: it shoult pe statet rather that navati ant nakari as tel as nan are not preventet ron unterkoink the cerepral chanke. as, sanan or sil, sanavati ninety-sil, sanakarya sil cities.
s: 114. After टु final in a Pada, the change of a dental (स्तु) to a cerebral (ष्टु), does not take place, except in the case of the affix नाम् Thus षट् + सन्तः = षट्सन्तः षट् + ते = षट्ते Why do we say पदान्तात् 'final in a Pada'? Observe ईड् + ते = ईट्टे Why do we say टोः 'after टु'? Observe सर्पिष् + तमम् = सर्पिष्टमम् Why do we say अनाम् 'except in the case of the affix nām'? Observe षट् + नाम् = षण्णाम् This exception is very inadequate. Hence the following Vārtika: it should be stated rather that नवति and नगरी as well as नाम् are not prevented from undergoing the cerebral change. As, षण्णाम् 'of six', षण्णवतिः ninety-six, षण्णगर्यः six cities.

pk: 15. in the ron or a dental (tu), there is not a cerebral substitute, when sa rolows. The word na is to be read into the aphorisn. as, san + sasWa = sansasWa ere the sûtra Jalan jasonte (s. 84) should be read again, by which a sort consonant is substituted ror the hard. Thus vak + isa = vagisa ; cit + rupan = cidrupan
ck: 15. in the ron or a tental (tu), there is not a cerepral supstitute, then sa rolots. the tort na is to pe reat into the aphorisn. as, san + sasta = sansasta ere the sûtra calan casonte (s. 84) shoult pe reat akain, py thich a sort consonant is supstitutet ror the hart. thus vak + isa = vakisa ; cit + rupan = citrupan
s: 115. In the room of a dental (तु), there is not a cerebral substitute, when ष follows. The word न is to be read into the aphorism. As, सन् + षष्ठः = सन्षष्ठः Here the Sûtra झलां जशोऽन्ते (S. 84) should be read again, by which a soft consonant is substituted for the hard. Thus वाक् + ईशः = वागीशः ; चित् + रूपम् = चिद्रूपम्

pk: 16. in the ron or a yara leter ( every consonant elcept ha ) rinal in a Pada, when a nasal rolows, there is optionaly a nasal substitute. The word padanta is understod here. Thus etat + nurari = etanurari or etadnurari This rule does not aply to r as catur + nuKa = caturnuKa Why do we say rinal in a Pada? Observe, ved + ni = vedni ere there is no option. so also ‹?› Vart:—When it is a pratyaya or aril that rolows the nasalisation is obligatory in the secular language. Thus tat + natran = tanatran, sinilarly cinayan it is, however, only berore the ariles naya and natra that the change is obligatory, and not berore every aril begining with a nasal. ow do you elplain the rorn kakudnanta in the sentence nadodagra kakudnanta? Because the da is used in yavadi clas (ror a list or the words belonging to this clas, se Ganapatha Vi. 2. 9).
ck: 16. in the ron or a yara leter ( every consonant elcept ha ) rinal in a pata, then a nasal rolots, there is optionaly a nasal supstitute. the tort patanta is unterstot here. thus etat + nurari = etanurari or etatnurari this rule toes not aply to r as catur + nuka = caturnuka thy to te say rinal in a pata? Opserve, vet + ni = vetni ere there is no option. so also ‹?› Vart:—then it is a pratyaya or aril that rolots the nasalisation is oplikatory in the secular lankuake. thus tat + natran = tanatran, sinilarly cinayan it is, hotever, only perore the ariles naya ant natra that the chanke is oplikatory, ant not perore every aril pekinink tith a nasal. ot to you elplain the rorn kakutnanta in the sentence natotakra kakutnanta? pecause the ta is uset in yavati clas (ror a list or the torts pelonkink to this clas, se kanapatha Vi. 2. 9).
s: 116. In the room of a यर letter ( every consonant except ह ) final in a Pada, when a Nasal follows, there is optionally a Nasal substitute. The word पदान्त is understood here. Thus एतत् + मुरारिः = एतन्मुरारिः or एतद्मुरारिः This rule does not apply to र् as चतुर् + मुखः = चतुर्मुखः Why do we say 'final in a Pada'? Observe, वेद् + मि = वेद्मि Here there is no option. So also ‹?› Vart:—When it is a pratyaya or affix that follows the nasalisation is obligatory in the secular language. Thus तत् + मात्रम् = तन्मात्रम्, similarly चिन्मयम् It is, however, only before the affixes मय and मात्र that the change is obligatory, and not before every affix beginning with a nasal. How do you explain the form ककुद्मन्तः in the sentence 'मदोदग्राः ककुद्मन्तः'? Because the द is used in यवादि class (For a list of the words belonging to this class, see Ganapatha VIII. 2. 9).

pk: 17. in the ron or tu (a dental) when the leter la rolows, one honogeneous with the later is substituted. Thus tat + laya = talaya ; vidvan + liKati = vidvanliKati ere t has ben changed to pure l, while the dento-nasal n is changed to a nasal lan.
ck: 17. in the ron or tu (a tental) then the leter la rolots, one honokeneous tith the later is supstitutet. thus tat + laya = talaya ; vitvan + likati = vitvanlikati ere t has pen chanket to pure l, thile the tento-nasal n is chanket to a nasal lan.
s: 117. In the room of तु (a dental) when the letter ल follows, one homogeneous with the latter is substituted. Thus तत् + लयः = तल्लयः ; विद्वान् + लिखति = विद्वाँल्लिखति Here त् has been changed to pure ल्, while the dento-nasal न् is changed to a nasal लँ.

pk: 18. arter ud, in the ron or the sa or sthā and stanbha, the substitute is a leter belonging to the clas or the prior (i. e. a dental is substituted ror this sa ) as ud + sTata = ud + Tata = ud + Tata ( Vi. 4. 65 s. 120 ) = ut + Tata (Vi. 4. 5 s. 121 ) = utTata, utTatun, utTatavyan so also with stanBa, as, utanBita, utanBitun &c. (se i. 1. 67 s. 41 and 54. s. 4 ) ere the aghosha (surd) and nahāprāṇa sa is changed to Ta which is also aghosha and nahāprāṇa. This then is optionaly elided by Jaro Jari (s. 71 ). But in the alternative when there is no lopa the T is heard in pronunciation. By the rule Kari ca ( s. 121 ), the T is not changed to car leter, because the rule or car is not aplicable to T; ror this T is considered as non-elistent ror the purposes or car rules.
ck: 18. arter ut, in the ron or the sa or sthā ant stanpha, the supstitute is a leter pelonkink to the clas or the prior (i. e. a tental is supstitutet ror this sa ) as ut + stata = ut + tata = ut + tata ( Vi. 4. 65 s. 120 ) = ut + tata (Vi. 4. 5 s. 121 ) = utata, utatun, utatavyan so also tith stanpa, as, utanpita, utanpitun &c. (se i. 1. 67 s. 41 ant 54. s. 4 ) ere the akhosha (surt) ant nahāprāṇa sa is chanket to ta thich is also akhosha ant nahāprāṇa. this then is optionaly elitet py caro cari (s. 71 ). put in the alternative then there is no lopa the t is heart in pronunciation. py the rule kari ca ( s. 121 ), the t is not chanket to car leter, pecause the rule or car is not aplicaple to t; ror this t is consiteret as non-elistent ror the purposes or car rules.
s: 118. After उद्, in the room of the स of sthā and stambha, the substitute is a letter belonging to the class of the prior (i. e. a dental is substituted for this स ) As उद् + स्थाता = उद् + थ्थाता = उद् + थाता ( VIII. 4. 65 S. 120 ) = उत् + थाता (VIII. 4. 55 S. 121 ) = उत्थाता, उत्थातुम्, उत्थातव्यम् So also with स्तम्भ, as, उत्तम्भिता, उत्तम्भितुम् &c. (See I. 1. 67 S. 41 and 54. S. 44 ) Here the Aghosha (Surd) and Mahāprāṇa स is changed to थ which is also Aghosha and Mahāprāṇa. This then is optionally elided by झरो झरि (S. 71 ). But in the alternative when there is no lopa the थ् is heard in pronunciation. By the rule खरि च ( S. 121 ), the थ् is not changed to चर् letter, because the rule of चर् is not applicable to थ्; for this थ् is considered as non-existent for the purposes of चर् rules.

pk: 19. in the ron or the leter ha, arter Jay (a sonant nute) there is optionaly a leter honogeneous with the prior. The pratyāhāra Jay includes al nutes. But practicaly sonant nutes are only taken here. The substitute or h wil be G by the rule or nearnes or place or uterance, because h is a ghosha (sonant), nahāprāṇa (aspirated) and saṁvṛta (contracted) and so is also G. Thus vak + hari = vagGari or vaghari
ck: 19. in the ron or the leter ha, arter cay (a sonant nute) there is optionaly a leter honokeneous tith the prior. the pratyāhāra cay inclutes al nutes. put practicaly sonant nutes are only taken here. the supstitute or h til pe k py the rule or nearnes or place or uterance, pecause h is a khosha (sonant), nahāprāṇa (aspiratet) ant saṁvṛta (contractet) ant so is also k. thus vak + hari = vakari or vakhari
s: 119. In the room of the letter ह, after झय् (a sonant Mute) there is optionally a letter homogeneous with the prior. The pratyāhāra झय् includes all Mutes. But practically sonant Mutes are only taken here. The substitute of ह् will be घ् by the rule of nearness of place of utterance, because ह् is a ghosha (sonant), Mahāprāṇa (aspirated) and Saṁvṛta (contracted) and so is also घ्. Thus वाक् + हरिः = वाग्घरिः or वाग्हरिः

pk: 120. in the ron or a s preceded by a surd nute, there is optionaly the leter Ca when a vowel or ha, ya, va or ra rolows such a s Though Jay neans al nutes, the rule, however, aplies to surd nutes. The words Jay and anyatarasyan are to be read into the sûtra. Thus tat + siva = tad + siva (s. 84) = tad + Civa = tac + Civa = tacCiva. at this stage aplies the nelt sûtra.
ck: 120. in the ron or a s precetet py a surt nute, there is optionaly the leter ca then a votel or ha, ya, va or ra rolots such a s thoukh cay neans al nutes, the rule, hotever, aplies to surt nutes. the torts cay ant anyatarasyan are to pe reat into the sûtra. thus tat + siva = tat + siva (s. 84) = tat + civa = tac + civa = taciva. at this stake aplies the nelt sûtra.
s: 120. In the room of a श् preceded by a surd Mute, there is optionally the letter छ when a vowel or ह, य, व or र follows such a श् Though झय् means all Mutes, the rule, however, applies to surd mutes. The words झय् and अन्यतरस्याम् are to be read into the sûtra. Thus तत् + शिव = तद् + शिव (S. 84) = तद् + छिव = तच् + छिव = तच्छिव. At this stage applies the next Sûtra.

pk: 121. in the ron or Jal, there is the substitute car when Kar rolows. a sonant non-aspirate nute is the substitute or a nute, when a surd nute or a sibilant rolows. The words Jalan and cara are suplied ron the last sūtra. Thererore j is changed to c and we have the rorn tacCiva or tadsiva Vartika:—it should rather be stated when a leter or an pratyāhāra rolows. The sūtra only gives aw leters, the Vartika ads the leters la, and the nasals. Thus tat + slokena = tacClokena, tadslokena. Why do we say when a leter or an pratyāhāra rolows? Observe ‹?›.
ck: 121. in the ron or cal, there is the supstitute car then kar rolots. a sonant non-aspirate nute is the supstitute or a nute, then a surt nute or a sipilant rolots. the torts calan ant cara are supliet ron the last sūtra. thererore c is chanket to c ant te have the rorn taciva or tatsiva Vartika:—it shoult rather pe statet then a leter or an pratyāhāra rolots. the sūtra only kives at leters, the Vartika ats the leters la, ant the nasals. thus tat + slokena = taclokena, tatslokena. thy to te say then a leter or an pratyāhāra rolots? Opserve ‹?›.
s: 121. In the room of झल्, there is the substitute चर् when खर् follows. A sonant non-aspirate mute is the substitute of a mute, when a surd mute or a sibilant follows. The words झलाम् and चरः are supplied from the last sūtra. Therefore ज् is changed to च् and we have the form तच्छिवः or तद्शिवः Vartika:—It should rather be stated when a letter of अम् pratyāhāra follows. The sūtra only gives अट् letters, the Vartika adds the letters ल, and the nasals. Thus तत् + श्लोकेन = तच्छ्लोकेन, तद्श्लोकेन. Why do we say when a letter of अम् pratyāhāra follows? Observe ‹?›.

pk: 12. The anusvāra is substituted ror n, at the end or a word, berore a consonant. Thus harin vande The word hali is understod in this sūtra. The n nust be at the end or a pada which we get ron sūtra alontyasya (s. 42 ) ; thererore not here : ganyate.
ck: 12. the anusvāra is supstitutet ror n, at the ent or a tort, perore a consonant. thus harin vante the tort hali is unterstot in this sūtra. the n nust pe at the ent or a pata thich te ket ron sūtra alontyasya (s. 42 ) ; thererore not here : kanyate.
s: 122. The Anusvāra is substituted for म्, at the end of a word, before a consonant. Thus हरिं वन्दे The word हलि is understood in this sūtra. The म् must be at the end of a pada which we get from sūtra अलोऽन्त्यस्य (S. 42 ) ; therefore not here : गम्यते.

pk: 123. The anusvāra is substituted ror the n and n, not rinal in a pada, berore al consonants, with the elception or nasals and seni-vowels. Thus yasansi, akransyate Why do we say berore a Jal consonant ? se nanyate. note:—Why do we say not rinal in a Pada? Observe rajan pahi.
ck: 123. the anusvāra is supstitutet ror the n ant n, not rinal in a pata, perore al consonants, tith the elception or nasals ant seni-votels. thus yasansi, akransyate thy to te say perore a cal consonant ? se nanyate. note:—thy to te say not rinal in a pata? Opserve racan pahi.
s: 123. The Anusvāra is substituted for the न् and म्, not final in a pada, before all consonants, with the exception of Nasals and semi-vowels. Thus यशांसि, आक्रंस्यते Why do we say before a झल् consonant ? See मन्यते. Note:—Why do we say 'not final in a Pada'? Observe राजन् पाहि.

pk: 124. in the ron or anusvāra, when yay rolows, a leter honogeneous with the later is substituted. Thus ankita, ancita, kunWita, santa, sunPita. These are thus rorned:— To the causal churādi rot anki (neaning pada and lakshaṇa), we ad the participial aril kta. Thus anki + kta. The causal sign is elided by the sūtra ‹?› (Vi. 4. 52. s. 3057). Then by the present rule, we have ‹?›. The i here is the iw augnent. Or it nay be ron the rot aki (neaning lakshaṇa) where the augnent nun becones anusvāra by Vi. 3. 24, s. 123, and then this n becones n. ancita cones ron the rot ancu (neaning pūjā), with the aril kta. The n is not elided by Vi. 4. 30 s. 424. kunWita is rorned ron the rot kusWi (neaning pratighāta). The augnent nun is aded to the rot berore the sew participial aril. This is changed into n. santa is rorned ron the rot san (neaning upaśana) with the aril kta (se Vi. 2. 27. s. 3068). The a or san is lengthened by Vi. 4. 15. s. 26. The n is changed to n by the present rule. sunPita is rorned ron the rot sunBu (neaning grantha) with the aril kta. in kurvanti, the na is not changed into na, though required by Vi. 4. 3. s. 197. Because the ‹?› is asidha, and thererore by the prior rule Vi. 3. 24. s. 123, the n is rirst changed into anusvāra (Vi. 2. 1. s. 12). That anusvāra is again changed into na by the present rule, na being honogeneous with t. This change again being asidDa as ir it had never taken place (Vi. 2. 1. s. 12), the na is never substituted ror na
ck: 124. in the ron or anusvāra, then yay rolots, a leter honokeneous tith the later is supstitutet. thus ankita, ancita, kuntita, santa, sunpita. these are thus rornet:— to the causal churāti rot anki (neanink pata ant lakshaṇa), te at the participial aril kta. thus anki + kta. the causal sikn is elitet py the sūtra ‹?› (Vi. 4. 52. s. 3057). then py the present rule, te have ‹?›. the i here is the it auknent. Or it nay pe ron the rot aki (neanink lakshaṇa) there the auknent nun pecones anusvāra py Vi. 3. 24, s. 123, ant then this n pecones n. ancita cones ron the rot ancu (neanink pūcā), tith the aril kta. the n is not elitet py Vi. 4. 30 s. 424. kuntita is rornet ron the rot kusti (neanink pratikhāta). the auknent nun is atet to the rot perore the set participial aril. this is chanket into n. santa is rornet ron the rot san (neanink upaśana) tith the aril kta (se Vi. 2. 27. s. 3068). the a or san is lenkthenet py Vi. 4. 15. s. 26. the n is chanket to n py the present rule. sunpita is rornet ron the rot sunpu (neanink krantha) tith the aril kta. in kurvanti, the na is not chanket into na, thoukh retuiret py Vi. 4. 3. s. 197. pecause the ‹?› is asitha, ant thererore py the prior rule Vi. 3. 24. s. 123, the n is rirst chanket into anusvāra (Vi. 2. 1. s. 12). that anusvāra is akain chanket into na py the present rule, na peink honokeneous tith t. this chanke akain peink asita as ir it hat never taken place (Vi. 2. 1. s. 12), the na is never supstitutet ror na
s: 124. In the room of anusvāra, when यय् follows, a letter homogeneous with the latter is substituted. Thus अङ्कितः, अञ्चितः, कुण्ठितः, शान्तः, शुम्फितः. These are thus formed:— To the causal churādi root अङ्कि (meaning pada and lakshaṇa), we add the participial affix क्त. Thus अङ्कि + क्त. The causal sign is elided by the sūtra ‹?› (VI. 4. 52. S. 3057). Then by the present rule, we have ‹?›. The इ here is the इट् augment. Or it may be from the root अकि (meaning lakshaṇa) where the augment नुम् becomes anusvāra by VIII. 3. 24, S. 123, and then this न् becomes ङ्. अञ्चितः comes from the root अञ्चु (meaning pūjā), with the affix क्त. The न् is not elided by VI. 4. 30 S. 424. कुण्ठितः is formed from the root कुष्ठि (meaning pratighāta). The augment नुम् is added to the root before the सेट् participial affix. This is changed into ण्. शान्तः is formed from the root शम् (meaning upaśama) with the affix क्त (See VII. 2. 27. S. 3068). The अ of शम् is lengthened by VI. 4. 15. S. 2666. The म् is changed to न् by the present rule. शुम्फितः is formed from the root शुम्भू (meaning grantha) with the affix क्त. In कुर्वन्ति, the न is not changed into ण, though required by VIII. 4. 3. S. 197. Because the ‹?› is asiddha, and therefore by the prior rule VIII. 3. 24. S. 123, the न् is first changed into anusvāra (VIII. 2. 1. S. 12). That anusvāra is again changed into न by the present rule, न being homogeneous with त्. This change again being असिद्ध as if it had never taken place (VIII. 2. 1. S. 12), the ण is never substituted for न

pk: 125. in the ron or anusvāra rinal in a Pada, the substitution or a leter honogeneous with the later is optional. Thus tvankarosi or tvan karosi; sanyanta or sanyanta; sanvatsara or sanvatsara; yanlokan or yan lokan. ere the anusvāra has becone nasal y v l in the other alternative.
ck: 125. in the ron or anusvāra rinal in a pata, the supstitution or a leter honokeneous tith the later is optional. thus tvankarosi or tvan karosi; sanyanta or sanyanta; sanvatsara or sanvatsara; yanlokan or yan lokan. ere the anusvāra has pecone nasal y v l in the other alternative.
s: 125. In the room of anusvāra final in a Pada, the substitution of a letter homogeneous with the latter is optional. Thus त्वङ्करोषि or त्वं करोषि; संय्यन्ता or संयन्ता; संव्वत्सरः or संवत्सरः; यँल्लोकम् or यं लोकम्. Here the anusvāra has become nasal य् व् ल् in the other alternative.

pk: 126. na is substituted ror the n or san, berore the word raj ending with the aril kvip Thus sanraw The substitution or na ror na is ror the sake or preventing the anusvāra change (Vi. 3. 24. s. 123.). Why do we say berore kvip? se sanvraw (Vi. 4. 40. s. 2986. Vart). Why do we say or san? Observe viBraw (Vi. 2. 36. s. 294). Why do we say ending with kvip? Observe sanrajita, sanrajitun, sanrajitavyan The kvip is aded by i. 2. 61 s. 2975; the j is changed to s by Vi. 2. 36, s. 294, which is changed to w at the end or a word, in sanraw sanrajyan is rorned by syan aril, as it belongs to Brāhnaṇādi clas.
ck: 126. na is supstitutet ror the n or san, perore the tort rac entink tith the aril kvip thus sanrat the supstitution or na ror na is ror the sake or preventink the anusvāra chanke (Vi. 3. 24. s. 123.). thy to te say perore kvip? se sanvrat (Vi. 4. 40. s. 2986. Vart). thy to te say or san? Opserve viprat (Vi. 2. 36. s. 294). thy to te say entink tith kvip? Opserve sanracita, sanracitun, sanracitavyan the kvip is atet py i. 2. 61 s. 2975; the c is chanket to s py Vi. 2. 36, s. 294, thich is chanket to t at the ent or a tort, in sanrat sanracyan is rornet py syan aril, as it pelonks to prāhnaṇāti clas.
s: 126. म is substituted for the म् of सम्, before the word राज् ending with the affix क्विप् Thus सम्राट् The substitution of म for म is for the sake of preventing the anusvāra change (VIII. 3. 24. S. 123.). Why do we say 'before क्विप्'? See संव्राट् (VI. 4. 40. S. 2986. Vart). Why do we say 'of सम्'? Observe विभ्राट् (VIII. 2. 36. S. 294). Why do we say 'ending with क्विप्'? Observe संराजिता, संराजितुम्, संराजितव्यम् The क्विप् is added by III. 2. 61 S. 2975; the ज् is changed to ष् by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294, which is changed to ट् at the end of a word, in सम्राट् साम्राज्यम् is formed by ष्यञ् affix, as it belongs to Brāhmaṇādi class.

pk: 127. na is optionaly substituted ror n berore that ha which itselr is rolowed by a na The n nay be changed to anusvāra or renain unchanged berore a word begining with ‹?›. Thus ror kin hnalayati, what does he cause to shake? Vārt:—Berore ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?›, the preceding ‹?› nay be changed to ya, va or la respectively. now, by this Vārtika, thre leters y, v, l, are ordained in the ron or ‹?›. But the rule does not say which leter is to be substituted ror which leter. To renove this doubt the rolowing interpretation sūtra should be renenbered:—
ck: 127. na is optionaly supstitutet ror n perore that ha thich itselr is rolotet py a na the n nay pe chanket to anusvāra or renain unchanket perore a tort pekinink tith ‹?›. thus ror kin hnalayati, that toes he cause to shake? Vārt:—perore ‹?›, ‹?› ant ‹?›, the precetink ‹?› nay pe chanket to ya, va or la respectively. not, py this Vārtika, thre leters y, v, l, are ortainet in the ron or ‹?›. put the rule toes not say thich leter is to pe supstitutet ror thich leter. to renove this toupt the rolotink interpretation sūtra shoult pe renenperet:—
s: 127. म is optionally substituted for म् before that ह which itself is followed by a म The म् may be changed to anusvāra or remain unchanged before a word beginning with ‹?›. Thus for किम् ह्मलयति, 'what does he cause to shake'? Vārt:—Before ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?›, the preceding ‹?› may be changed to य, व or ल respectively. Now, by this Vārtika, three letters य्, व्, ल्, are ordained in the room of ‹?›. But the rule does not say which letter is to be substituted for which letter. To remove this doubt the following interpretation sūtra should be remembered:—

pk: 128. When a rule involves the case or equal nunbers or substitutes and or things ror which these are to be substituted, their nutual corespondence or asignent or each to each, is acording to the order or enuneration. Thererore as under the rorner rule, the leters to be substituted are thre in nunber and the substitutes are also thre in nunber, thererore aplying the present rule, y would be replaced by yan्; v by van् and l by lan्. Thus we have kin hyalayati or kin hyalayati; kin hvalayati or kin hvalayati; kin hladayati or kin hladayati.
ck: 128. then a rule involves the case or etual nunpers or supstitutes ant or thinks ror thich these are to pe supstitutet, their nutual corespontence or asiknent or each to each, is acortink to the orter or enuneration. thererore as unter the rorner rule, the leters to pe supstitutet are thre in nunper ant the supstitutes are also thre in nunper, thererore aplyink the present rule, y toult pe replacet py yan्; v py van् ant l py lan्. thus te have kin hyalayati or kin hyalayati; kin hvalayati or kin hvalayati; kin hlatayati or kin hlatayati.
s: 128. When a rule involves the case of equal numbers of substitutes and of things for which these are to be substituted, their mutual correspondence or assignment of each to each, is according to the order of enumeration. Therefore as under the former rule, the letters to be substituted are three in number and the substitutes are also three in number, therefore applying the present rule, य् would be replaced by यँ्; व् by वँ् and ल् by लँ्. Thus we have किम् ह्यलयति or किं ह्यलयति; किम् ह्वलयति or किं ह्वलयति; किम् ह्लादयति or किं ह्लादयति.

pk: 129. n is optionaly substituted ror n, when it is rolowed by ha which has a n arter it. n becones n berore a word begining with h; as kinhute or kin hute.
ck: 129. n is optionaly supstitutet ror n, then it is rolotet py ha thich has a n arter it. n pecones n perore a tort pekinink tith h; as kinhute or kin hute.
s: 129. न् is optionally substituted for म्, when it is followed by ह which has a न् after it. म् becomes न् before a word beginning with ह्; as किन्हुते or किं हुते.

pk: 130. The augnent kuk is aded to a rinal n, and the augnent wuk to a rinal n, berore a sibilant, optionaly. The kuk and wuk augnents being considered as asidha, there is no change, i.e. sort leters are not substituted ror the hard. Berore giving the elanples or this sūtra, the rolowing Vārtika nust be aplied, in order to get the proper rorns. Vārtika :— acording to the option or Āchārya Pauṣkarasādi, the leters or car pratyāhāra are replaced by the second leters or their clas, when rolowed by a sibilant (a leter or sar pratyāhāra). Thus pranKasasWa or prankasasWa or pransasWa; suganWsasWa or suganwsasWa or sugansasWa.
ck: 130. the auknent kuk is atet to a rinal n, ant the auknent tuk to a rinal n, perore a sipilant, optionaly. the kuk ant tuk auknents peink consiteret as asitha, there is no chanke, i.e. sort leters are not supstitutet ror the hart. perore kivink the elanples or this sūtra, the rolotink Vārtika nust pe apliet, in orter to ket the proper rorns. Vārtika :— acortink to the option or Āchārya pauṣkarasāti, the leters or car pratyāhāra are replacet py the secont leters or their clas, then rolotet py a sipilant (a leter or sar pratyāhāra). thus prankasasta or prankasasta or pransasta; sukantsasta or sukantsasta or sukansasta.
s: 130. The augment कुक् is added to a final ङ्, and the augment टुक् to a final ण्, before a sibilant, optionally. The कुक् and टुक् augments being considered as asiddha, there is no change, i.e. soft letters are not substituted for the hard. Before giving the examples of this sūtra, the following Vārtika must be applied, in order to get the proper forms. Vārtika :— According to the option of Āchārya Pauṣkarasādi, the letters of चर् pratyāhāra are replaced by the second letters of their class, when followed by a sibilant (a letter of शर् pratyāhāra). Thus प्राङ्खषष्ठः or प्राङ्कषष्ठः or प्राङ्षष्ठः; सुगण्ठ्षष्ठः or सुगण्ट्षष्ठः or सुगण्षष्ठः.

pk: 131. arter a word ending in q there nay optionaly be aded the augnent Duw to a word begining with s Thus sawtsanta or sawsanta. The word na is to be construed as ablative singular, and not Genitive singular or q, because or the nalin uBayanirdese pancaninirdeso baliyan
ck: 131. arter a tort entink in t there nay optionaly pe atet the auknent tut to a tort pekinink tith s thus satsanta or satsanta. the tort na is to pe construet as aplative sinkular, ant not kenitive sinkular or t, pecause or the nalin upayanirtese pancaninirteso paliyan
s: 131. After a word ending in ड् there may optionally be added the augment धुट् to a word beginning with स् Thus षट्त्सन्तः or षट्सन्तः. The word ङः is to be construed as Ablative singular, and not Genitive singular of ड्, because of the maxim उभयनिर्देशे पञ्चमीनिर्देशो बलीयान्

pk: 132. arter a word ending in n, Duw is optionaly the augnent to a word begining with s Thus santsa or sansa
ck: 132. arter a tort entink in n, tut is optionaly the auknent to a tort pekinink tith s thus santsa or sansa
s: 132. After a word ending in न्, धुट् is optionally the augment to a word beginning with स् Thus सन्त्सः or सन्सः

pk: 13. The augnent tuk nay optionaly be aded to a word ending in n, when a word begining with sa rolows. By rule Vi. 4. 63. s. 120. there is an optional Ca. By the rule Jaro Jari savarne Vi. 4. 65. s. 71. there is elision or the ‹?› in the other alternative. Thus sanCsanBu or sanCanBu or sancCanBu or sasanBu.
ck: 13. the auknent tuk nay optionaly pe atet to a tort entink in n, then a tort pekinink tith sa rolots. py rule Vi. 4. 63. s. 120. there is an optional ca. py the rule caro cari savarne Vi. 4. 65. s. 71. there is elision or the ‹?› in the other alternative. thus sancsanpu or sancanpu or sancanpu or sasanpu.
s: 133. The augment तुक् may optionally be added to a word ending in न्, when a word beginning with श follows. By rule VIII. 4. 63. S. 120. there is an optional छ. By the rule झरो झरि सवर्णे VIII. 4. 65. S. 71. there is elision of the ‹?› in the other alternative. Thus सञ्छ्शम्भुः or सञ्छम्भुः or सञ्च्छम्भुः or सशम्भुः.

pk: 134. arter a word ending in n, n or n which is preceded by a light vowel, the sane consonant n, n or n is aded invariably at the begining or the nelt word, which conences with a vowel. The word ‹?› is in the ablative singular here; and qualiries ‹?› and itselr qualiries the word ‹?› understod, and thus there is tadanta-vidhi. Though the word (Vi. 1. 16 s. 40) is in the Genitive singular, yet it should be converted here into ablative singular, because or its conection with ‹?› is in the Locative singular, but should be construed as Genitive singular here; it is elhibited in the 7th case ror the sake or brevity, and or the subsequent sûtras. nan is a pratyâhâra neaning na, na and na; and so also nanuw is a pratyâhâra containing the thre augnents nuw, nuw and nuw in other words ‹?› is augnent arter ‹?›, arter ‹?› and arter ‹?›; or that these leters are doubled practicaly. Thus nuw is the augnent arter a word ending in na, as pratyanatna nuw is the augnent arter a word ending in na, as ‹?› nuw is the augnent arter a word ending in na, as suganisa
ck: 134. arter a tort entink in n, n or n thich is precetet py a likht votel, the sane consonant n, n or n is atet invariaply at the pekinink or the nelt tort, thich conences tith a votel. the tort ‹?› is in the aplative sinkular here; ant tualiries ‹?› ant itselr tualiries the tort ‹?› unterstot, ant thus there is tatanta-vithi. thoukh the tort (Vi. 1. 16 s. 40) is in the kenitive sinkular, yet it shoult pe convertet here into aplative sinkular, pecause or its conection tith ‹?› is in the Locative sinkular, put shoult pe construet as kenitive sinkular here; it is elhipitet in the 7th case ror the sake or previty, ant or the supsetuent sûtras. nan is a pratyâhâra neanink na, na ant na; ant so also nanut is a pratyâhâra containink the thre auknents nut, nut ant nut in other torts ‹?› is auknent arter ‹?›, arter ‹?› ant arter ‹?›; or that these leters are touplet practicaly. thus nut is the auknent arter a tort entink in na, as pratyanatna nut is the auknent arter a tort entink in na, as ‹?› nut is the auknent arter a tort entink in na, as sukanisa
s: 134. After a word ending in ङ्, ण् or न् which is preceded by a light vowel, the same consonant ङ्, ण् or न् is added invariably at the beginning of the next word, which commences with a vowel. The word ‹?› is in the Ablative singular here; and qualifies ‹?› and itself qualifies the word ‹?› understood, and thus there is tadanta-vidhi. Though the word (VIII. 1. 16 S. 40) is in the Genitive singular, yet it should be converted here into Ablative singular, because of its connection with ‹?› is in the Locative singular, but should be construed as Genitive singular here; it is exhibited in the 7th case for the sake of brevity, and of the subsequent sûtras. ङम् is a pratyâhâra meaning ङ, ण and न; and so also ङमुट् is a pratyâhâra containing the three augments ङुट्, णुट् and नुट् In other words ‹?› is augment after ‹?›, after ‹?› and after ‹?›; or that these letters are doubled practically. Thus ङुट् is the augment after a word ending in ङ, as प्रत्यङ्ङात्मा णुट् is the augment after a word ending in ण, as ‹?› नुट् is the augment after a word ending in न, as सुगण्णीशः

pk: 135. ru is substituted ror the n or san (and thereby ‹?› or ‹?› is substituted ror ‹?›) when the augnent suw rolows, in a sanhitâ.
ck: 135. ru is supstitutet ror the n or san (ant therepy ‹?› or ‹?› is supstitutet ror ‹?›) then the auknent sut rolots, in a sanhitâ.
s: 135. रु is substituted for the म् of सम् (and thereby ‹?› or ‹?› is substituted for ‹?›) when the augment सुट् follows, in a samhitâ.

pk: 136. in the rolowing sutras upto Vi. 3. 12, this is always to be suplied — "But here a nasal vowel nay optionaly be substituted ror the preceding vowel arter which ru has ben ordained." This is an adhikâra sutra. ror the leter which stands berore that leter ror which ru has ben substituted, there is substituted a nasal vowel, in this division or Granar, where ru is the subject or discusion. Thus sutra Vi. 3. 5, s. 135 says "in the place or the rinal n or san, there is ru when augnent suw rolows." The vowel a or san becones nasal; as ‹?›, ‹?›
ck: 136. in the rolotink sutras upto Vi. 3. 12, this is altays to pe supliet — "put here a nasal votel nay optionaly pe supstitutet ror the precetink votel arter thich ru has pen ortainet." this is an athikâra sutra. ror the leter thich stants perore that leter ror thich ru has pen supstitutet, there is supstitutet a nasal votel, in this tivision or kranar, there ru is the supcect or tiscusion. thus sutra Vi. 3. 5, s. 135 says "in the place or the rinal n or san, there is ru then auknent sut rolots." the votel a or san pecones nasal; as ‹?›, ‹?›
s: 136. In the following sutras upto VIII. 3. 12, this is always to be supplied — "But here a nasal vowel may optionally be substituted for the preceding vowel after which रु has been ordained." This is an adhikâra sutra. For the letter which stands before that letter for which रु has been substituted, there is substituted a nasal vowel, in this division of Grammar, where रु is the subject of discussion. Thus sutra VIII. 3. 5, S. 135 says "In the place of the final म् of सम्, there is रु when augment सुट् follows." The vowel अ of सम् becomes nasal; as ‹?›, ‹?›

pk: 137. arter what precedes, ir we onit to substitute the nasal, then anusvâra shal be the augnent. The substitution or nasal is optional by Vi. 3. 2. s. 136. When nasal is not substituted, we ad an anusvâra to such vowel. The word anya should be read into the sûtra to conplete the sense, i. e. anunasikat anyo yo varna "a leter other than a nasal", i. e. a leter ror which nasal has not ben ordained, and which stands berore ru Thus Vi. 3. 5. s. 135 teaches substitution or the n or san, an anusvâra would be aded. as sanskarta, sanskartavyan sone say "the word para in the sûtra neans anya, and so we ned not suply the word anya ron outside". They say anunasikat para = anunasikadanya; i. e. the anusvâra takes place in that alternative when there is no nasal. That anusvâra is an augnent and not a substitute. it is an augnent to the vowel which precedes ru By the rule Karavasanayorvisarjaniya the ru is changed into Visarga and by the nelt rule this Visarga is changed into s.
ck: 137. arter that precetes, ir te onit to supstitute the nasal, then anusvâra shal pe the auknent. the supstitution or nasal is optional py Vi. 3. 2. s. 136. then nasal is not supstitutet, te at an anusvâra to such votel. the tort anya shoult pe reat into the sûtra to conplete the sense, i. e. anunasikat anyo yo varna "a leter other than a nasal", i. e. a leter ror thich nasal has not pen ortainet, ant thich stants perore ru thus Vi. 3. 5. s. 135 teaches supstitution or the n or san, an anusvâra toult pe atet. as sanskarta, sanskartavyan sone say "the tort para in the sûtra neans anya, ant so te net not suply the tort anya ron outsite". they say anunasikat para = anunasikatanya; i. e. the anusvâra takes place in that alternative then there is no nasal. that anusvâra is an auknent ant not a supstitute. it is an auknent to the votel thich precetes ru py the rule karavasanayorvisarcaniya the ru is chanket into Visarka ant py the nelt rule this Visarka is chanket into s.
s: 137. After what precedes, if we omit to substitute the nasal, then anusvâra shall be the augment. The substitution of nasal is optional by VIII. 3. 2. S. 136. When nasal is not substituted, we add an anusvâra to such vowel. The word अन्यः should be read into the sûtra to complete the sense, i. e. अनुनासिकात् अन्यो यो वर्णः "a letter other than a nasal", i. e. a letter for which nasal has not been ordained, and which stands before रु Thus VIII. 3. 5. S. 135 teaches substitution of the म् of सम्, an anusvâra would be added. As संस्कर्त्ता, संस्कर्त्तव्यम् Some say "the word पर in the sûtra means अन्य, and so we need not supply the word अन्यः from outside". They say अनुनासिकात् परः = अनुनासिकादन्यः; i. e. the anusvâra takes place in that alternative when there is no nasal. That anusvâra is an augment and not a substitute. It is an augment to the vowel which precedes रु By the rule खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः the रु is changed into Visarga and by the next rule this Visarga is changed into स्.

pk: 138. s is the substitute or a visarga, when a hard consonant (Kara) rolows. The word Kara is understod here. There is Visarga also by the rule va sari Vi. 3. 36, s. 157. Then we have the rolowing Vârtika which ordains s always, and never visarga. Vârt:—ror the rinals or san, pun and kan there is always substituted s. Thus aplying the previous rour rules we have san + karta = san + r + karta (Vi. 1. 137 s. 250) = s + ‹?› + suw + karta (Vi. 3. 2. s. 136) = sanskarta or sanskarta acording to nahâbhâshya, there is elision or s arter san. Thus there wil be 108 rorns or this word sanskarta Thus sanskarta and sanskarta with the elision or s Then with two s, as sanskarta, sanskarta Then we aply Vi. 4. 47 s. 48 to this later, and have thre s, as ‹?›, or ‹?› The anusvâra is considered to be a vowel (ac) ror this purpose. ron the thre nasal rorns sanskarta, sanskarta and ‹?›, we get thre nore by doubling the ka by the vârtika sara Kaya The thre rorns having anusvâra, wil also double their anusvâra in adition to k doubling. Thus we have 12 rorns in anusvâra and sil in nasal, altogether 18 rorns. Then the ta wil be doubled and trebled and thus with one ta, two ta and thre ta, we have 3 × 18 = 54 rorns. This wil be doubled (2 × 54 = 108) when an is nasalised.
ck: 138. s is the supstitute or a visarka, then a hart consonant (kara) rolots. the tort kara is unterstot here. there is Visarka also py the rule va sari Vi. 3. 36, s. 157. then te have the rolotink Vârtika thich ortains s altays, ant never visarka. Vârt:—ror the rinals or san, pun ant kan there is altays supstitutet s. thus aplyink the previous rour rules te have san + karta = san + r + karta (Vi. 1. 137 s. 250) = s + ‹?› + sut + karta (Vi. 3. 2. s. 136) = sanskarta or sanskarta acortink to nahâphâshya, there is elision or s arter san. thus there til pe 108 rorns or this tort sanskarta thus sanskarta ant sanskarta tith the elision or s then tith to s, as sanskarta, sanskarta then te aply Vi. 4. 47 s. 48 to this later, ant have thre s, as ‹?›, or ‹?› the anusvâra is consiteret to pe a votel (ac) ror this purpose. ron the thre nasal rorns sanskarta, sanskarta ant ‹?›, te ket thre nore py touplink the ka py the vârtika sara kaya the thre rorns havink anusvâra, til also touple their anusvâra in atition to k touplink. thus te have 12 rorns in anusvâra ant sil in nasal, altokether 18 rorns. then the ta til pe touplet ant treplet ant thus tith one ta, to ta ant thre ta, te have 3 × 18 = 54 rorns. this til pe touplet (2 × 54 = 108) then an is nasaliset.
s: 138. स् is the substitute of a visarga, when a hard consonant (खर) follows. The word खर is understood here. There is Visarga also by the rule वा शरि VIII. 3. 36, S. 157. Then we have the following Vârtika which ordains स् always, and never visarga. Vârt:—For the finals of सम्, पुम् and कान् there is always substituted स्. Thus applying the previous four rules we have सम् + कर्ता = सम् + र् + कर्ता (VI. 1. 137 S. 2550) = स् + ‹?› + सुट् + कर्ता (VIII. 3. 2. S. 136) = संस्कर्ता or सँस्कर्ता According to Mahâbhâshya, there is elision of स् after सम्. Thus there will be 108 forms of this word संस्कर्त्ता Thus संस्कर्त्ता and सँस्कर्त्ता with the elision of स् Then with two स्, as संस्कर्त्ता, सँस्कर्त्ता Then we apply VIII. 4. 47 S. 48 to this latter, and have three स्, as ‹?›, or ‹?› The anusvâra is considered to be a vowel (अच्) for this purpose. From the three nasal forms संस्कर्ता, संस्स्कर्ता and ‹?›, we get three more by doubling the क by the vârttika शरः खयः The three forms having anusvâra, will also double their anusvâra in addition to क् doubling. Thus we have 12 forms in anusvâra and six in nasal, altogether 18 forms. Then the त will be doubled and trebled and thus with one त, two त and three त, we have 3 × 18 = 54 forms. This will be doubled (2 × 54 = 108) when अण् is nasalised.

pk: 139. ru is substituted ror the na or pun, (whereby the u is changed to un or un) berore a surd nute (Kay) which is rolowed by a vowel, senivowel or a nasal (an pratyâhâra). The word puns is rorned by the unâdi aril qunasun aded to the rot pun There are two views or unâdi rorned words: one considers then as derivative words, the other regards then as non-derivative or ruQi words. ir the word puns be taken as a derivative word (vyutpati paksha) then the elception "apratyaye" or the sûtra Vi. 3. 41. s. 15 would aply, and ‹?› would not be changed to ‹?› by Vi. 3. 41. s. 15. To prevent both these incongruities, the Vârtika sanpukananiti sa (se the preceding sûtra) always ordains s and never ‹?› Thus pun + kokila = pur + kokila = ‹?› (Vi. 3. 41. s. 15) = punskokila or punskokila (Vi. 3. 2 & 4 s. 135 & 136). sinilarly punsputra or punsputra Why do we say berore a surd nute? Observe pundasa, pungava (V. 4. 92. s. 729). Why do we say rolowed by a vowel or senivowel or nasal? Observe punksira, punksura Vârtika:—not so when Kyan rolows pun, in those cases where Kyan is substituted ror caks (i. 4. 54 s. 2476). as punKyanan Kyana is rorned by ading lyuw to caks (i. 3. 15 s. 3290).
ck: 139. ru is supstitutet ror the na or pun, (therepy the u is chanket to un or un) perore a surt nute (kay) thich is rolotet py a votel, senivotel or a nasal (an pratyâhâra). the tort puns is rornet py the unâti aril tunasun atet to the rot pun there are to viets or unâti rornet torts: one consiters then as terivative torts, the other rekarts then as non-terivative or ruti torts. ir the tort puns pe taken as a terivative tort (vyutpati paksha) then the elception "apratyaye" or the sûtra Vi. 3. 41. s. 15 toult aply, ant ‹?› toult not pe chanket to ‹?› py Vi. 3. 41. s. 15. to prevent poth these inconkruities, the Vârtika sanpukananiti sa (se the precetink sûtra) altays ortains s ant never ‹?› thus pun + kokila = pur + kokila = ‹?› (Vi. 3. 41. s. 15) = punskokila or punskokila (Vi. 3. 2 & 4 s. 135 & 136). sinilarly punsputra or punsputra thy to te say perore a surt nute? s: 139. रु is substituted for the म of पुम्, (whereby the उ is changed to उँ or उं) before a surd mute (खय्) which is followed by a vowel, semivowel or a nasal (अम् pratyâhâra). The word पुंस् is formed by the Unâdi affix डुमसुन् added to the root पुञ् There are two views of Unâdi formed words: one considers them as derivative words, the other regards them as non-derivative or रूढि words. If the word पुंस् be taken as a derivative word (vyutpatti paksha) then the exception "apratyaye" of the sûtra VIII. 3. 41. S. 155 would apply, and ‹?› would not be changed to ‹?› by VIII. 3. 41. S. 155. To prevent both these incongruities, the Vârtika संपूकानामिति सः (see the preceding sûtra) always ordains स् and never ‹?› Thus पुम् + कोकिलः = पुर् + कोकिलः = ‹?› (VIII. 3. 41. S. 155) = पुंस्कोकिलः or पुँस्कोकिलः (VIII. 3. 2 & 4 S. 135 & 136). Similarly पुंस्पुत्रः or पुँस्पुत्रः Why do we say 'before a surd mute'? Observe पुंदासः, पुंगवः (V. 4. 92. S. 729). Why do we say 'followed by a vowel or semivowel or nasal'? Observe पुंक्षीरः, पुंक्षुरः Vârttika:—Not so when ख्यञ् follows पुम्, in those cases where ख्याञ् is substituted for चक्ष् (II. 4. 54 S. 2476). As पुंख्यानम् ख्यान is formed by adding ल्युट् to चक्ष् (III. 3. 115 S. 3290).

pk: 140. ru is substituted ror the rinal n or a word, with the elception or the n or prasan, berore a Cav leter (Ca, Wa, Ta, ca, wa, ta), which is rolowed by an an leter (vowel, senivowel and nasal). The word anpare is to be read into this sûtra. The word aprasan in the sûtra is in the noninative case, but it has the rorce or Genitive. sarngin + CinDi = sarngir + CinDi (Vi. 3. 7. s. 140) = sarngi + CinDi (Vi. 3. 15 s. 76) = sarngis + CinDi (Vi. 3. 34 s. 138) = sarngis + CinDi (Vi. 4. 40 s. 301) = sarngisCinDi or sarnginsCinDi (Vi. 3. 2-4 s. 136, s. 137). sinilarly cakrinstrayasva, cakrinstrayasva Why do we say or a Pada ? Observe hanti ere the ‹?› or Can is not changed to ‹?› berore ti, because it is not rinal in a pada. Why do we say with the elception or the ‹?› or prasan? Observe prasan tanoti, prasan cinoti Why do we say when an rolows Cav? se Bavan tsaruka tsaru is sword, he who is delterous in it is caled tsaruka (kan V. 2. 64, s. 1864).
ck: 140. ru is supstitutet ror the rinal n or a tort, tith the elception or the n or prasan, perore a cav leter (ca, ta, ta, ca, ta, ta), thich is rolotet py an an leter (votel, senivotel ant nasal). the tort anpare is to pe reat into this sûtra. the tort aprasan in the sûtra is in the noninative case, put it has the rorce or kenitive. sarnkin + cinti = sarnkir + cinti (Vi. 3. 7. s. 140) = sarnki + cinti (Vi. 3. 15 s. 76) = sarnkis + cinti (Vi. 3. 34 s. 138) = sarnkis + cinti (Vi. 4. 40 s. 301) = sarnkiscinti or sarnkinscinti (Vi. 3. 2-4 s. 136, s. 137). sinilarly cakrinstrayasva, cakrinstrayasva thy to te say or a pata ? Opserve hanti ere the ‹?› or can is not chanket to ‹?› perore ti, pecause it is not rinal in a pata. thy to te say tith the elception or the ‹?› or prasan? Opserve prasan tanoti, prasan cinoti thy to te say then an rolots cav? se pavan tsaruka tsaru is stort, he tho is telterous in it is calet tsaruka (kan V. 2. 64, s. 1864).
s: 140. रु is substituted for the final न् of a word, with the exception of the न् of प्रशान्, before a छव् letter (छ, ठ, थ, च, ट, त), which is followed by an अम् letter (vowel, semivowel and nasal). The word अम्परे is to be read into this sûtra. The word अप्रशान् in the sûtra is in the Nominative case, but it has the force of Genitive. शार्ङ्गिन् + छिन्धि = शार्ङ्गिर् + छिन्धि (VIII. 3. 7. S. 140) = शार्ङ्गिः + छिन्धि (VIII. 3. 15 S. 76) = शार्ङ्गिस् + छिन्धि (VIII. 3. 34 S. 138) = शार्ङ्गिश् + छिन्धि (VIII. 4. 40 S. 3301) = शार्ङ्गिश्छिन्धि or शार्ङ्गिँश्छिन्धि (VIII. 3. 2-4 S. 136, S. 137). Similarly चक्रिंस्त्रायस्व, चक्रिँस्त्रायस्व Why do we say of a Pada ? Observe हन्ति Here the ‹?› of छन् is not changed to ‹?› before ति, because it is not final in a pada. Why do we say 'with the exception of the ‹?› of प्रशान्'? Observe प्रशान् तनोति, प्रशान् चिनोति Why do we say when अम् follows छव्? See भवान् त्सरुकः त्सरु is sword, he who is dexterous in it is called त्सरुक (कन् V. 2. 64, S. 1864).

pk: 141. ru is optionaly substituted ror the ‹?› or nrn berore ‹?›. Thus nrn + pahi = ‹?› + pahi, ‹?› + pahi (Vi. 3. 15, s. 176). at this stage aplies the rolowing sutra.
ck: 141. ru is optionaly supstitutet ror the ‹?› or nrn perore ‹?›. thus nrn + pahi = ‹?› + pahi, ‹?› + pahi (Vi. 3. 15, s. 176). at this stake aplies the rolotink sutra.
s: 141. रु is optionally substituted for the ‹?› of नॄन् before ‹?›. Thus नॄन् + पाहि = ‹?› + पाहि, ‹?› + पाहि (VIII. 3. 15, S. 176). At this stage applies the following sutra.

By the nalin yena naprapte &c. this sutra debars the sutra Vi. 3. 34, s. 138 which ordains ror the visarga. But it does not debar Vi. 3. 35, s. 150. Thererore we have the visarga in vasa ksOnan &c. s: 142. ‹?› and ‹?› are optionally substituted for the visarga, when followed by a hard guttural or a hard labial. The word च 'and' in the sutra indicates that the visarga also comes. By the maxim येन नाप्राप्ते &c. this sutra debars the sutra VIII. 3. 34, S. 138 which ordains for the visarga. But it does not debar VIII. 3. 35, S. 150. Therefore we have the visarga in वासः क्षौमम् &c. Thus we get ‹?› पाहि or ‹?› पाहि or ‹?› पाहि or ‹?› पाहि or नॄन्पाहि

pk: 143. ru is substituted ror the n or kan when it is rolowed by another kan which is an anredita. ere by the vartika, under s. 138, the ru is changed to s Or the nelt sutra aplies :—
ck: 143. ru is supstitutet ror the n or kan then it is rolotet py another kan thich is an anretita. ere py the vartika, unter s. 138, the ru is chanket to s Or the nelt sutra aplies :—
s: 143. रु is substituted for the न् of कान् when it is followed by another कान् which is an amredita. Here by the vartika, under S. 138, the रु is changed to स् Or the next sutra applies :—

pk: 14. sa or sa is substituted ror the visarga, berore a hard gutural and labial in the words kaska and the rest. This is an apavada to sutra Vi. 3. 37, s. 142. sa is substituted arter i or u, and s everywhere else. Thus kaska, 2. kutaskuta (with a or kuta agata), 3. Bratusputra (Vi. 3. 23, s. 981), 4. sunaskarna (Vi. 3. 21, s. 979), 5. sadyaskala, 6. sadyaskri (ron kri to buy with the aril kvip, because it belongs to sanpadadi clas), 7. sadyaska (ron sadyaskri in the sense or tatraBava kratu), 8. kanskan (the ru is by Vi. 3. 12, s. 143), 9. sarpiskunqika, 10. catuskapalan, 1. Danuskapalan, 12. barhispalan, 13. yajuspatran no conplete list or this clas is given anywhere. it is an akritigana. Thus kanskan or kanskan

s: 144. स or ष is substituted for the visarga, before a hard guttural and labial in the words कस्क and the rest. This is an Apavada to Sutra VIII. 3. 37, S. 142. ष is substituted after इ or उ, and स् everywhere else. Thus कस्कः, 2. कुतस्कुतः (with अ of कुत आगतः), 3. भ्रातुष्पुत्रः (VI. 3. 23, S. 981), 4. शुनस्कर्णः (VI. 3. 21, S. 979), 5. सद्यस्कालः, 6. सद्यस्क्री (from क्री 'to buy' with the affix क्विप्, because it belongs to Sampadadi class), 7. साद्यस्कः (from सद्यस्क्री in the sense of तत्रभवः क्रतुः), 8. कांस्कान् (the रु is by VIII. 3. 12, S. 143), 9. सर्पिष्कुण्डिका, 10. चतुष्कपालम्, 11. धनुष्कपालम्, 12. बर्हिष्पालम्, 13. यजुष्पात्रम् No complete list of this class is given anywhere. It is an Akritigana. Thus कांस्कान् or काँस्कान्

pk: 145. in the sutras or Panini begining with this up to Vi. 1. 157 inclusive, the words sanhitayan in an unbroken rlow or spech, should be suplied.
