Whatever we shal say in the sutras preceding that, nust be understod to aply to words which are in sanhita, that is, which are pronounced together with an uninterupted voice.
ck: 145. in the sutras or panini pekinink tith this up to Vi. 1. 157 inclusive, the torts sanhitayan in an unproken rlot or spech, shoult pe supliet. this is an athikara or kovernink sutra, elertink its inrluence up to Vi. 1. 158. thatever te shal say in the sutras precetink that, nust pe unterstot to aply to torts thich are in sanhita, that is, thich are pronouncet tokether tith an uninteruptet voice.
s: 145. In the sutras of Panini beginning with this up to VI. 1. 157 inclusive, the words संहितायाम् 'in an unbroken flow of speech,' should be supplied. This is an adhikara or governing sutra, exerting its influence up to VI. 1. 158. Whatever we shall say in the sutras preceding that, must be understood to apply to words which are in संहिता, that is, which are pronounced together with an uninterrupted voice.

pk: 146. The augnent t is aded to a preceding short vowel also when a Ca rolows in an uninterupted spech. To a short vowel rolowed by Ca, is aded the augnent t in sanhita. ere we nust renenber the rule purvatrasidDan (Vi. 2. 1, s. 12) to get the proper rorn. Thus sva + Caya = svat + Caya. ere apear two rules, (1) Vi. 4. 40, s. 1 requiring the t to be changed to c; (2) Vi. 2. 39, s. 84 requiring the t to be changed to d. By the nalin purvatrasidDan the c change wil be considered as non-erective ror the purposes or jastva change. Thererore we aply this second rule rirst and get svad + Caya (Vi. 2. 39, s. 84). ere apear again two rules (1) Vi. 4. 5, s. 121 by which d is required to be changed into a car leter, and (2) Vi. 4. 40, s. 1 by which d is required to be changed to j. The later takes erect, the rorner being considered as asidha, and we get svaj + Caya, and then j is changed to c — svac + Caya (Vi. 4. 5, s. 121). ere apears the rule Vi. 2. 30, s. 378 requiring c to be changed to k. But c was obtained by Vi. 4. 5 a rule subsequent to Vi. 2. 30 and thererore it is considered as asidha, and so c is not changed to k Thus we have svacCaya, sivacCaya
ck: 146. the auknent t is atet to a precetink short votel also then a ca rolots in an uninteruptet spech. to a short votel rolotet py ca, is atet the auknent t in sanhita. ere te nust renenper the rule purvatrasitan (Vi. 2. 1, s. 12) to ket the proper rorn. thus sva + caya = svat + caya. ere apear to rules, (1) Vi. 4. 40, s. 1 retuirink the t to pe chanket to c; (2) Vi. 2. 39, s. 84 retuirink the t to pe chanket to t. py the nalin purvatrasitan the c chanke til pe consiteret as non-erective ror the purposes or castva chanke. thererore te aply this secont rule rirst ant ket svat + caya (Vi. 2. 39, s. 84). ere apear akain to rules (1) Vi. 4. 5, s. 121 py thich t is retuiret to pe chanket into a car leter, ant (2) Vi. 4. 40, s. 1 py thich t is retuiret to pe chanket to c. the later takes erect, the rorner peink consiteret as asitha, ant te ket svac + caya, ant then c is chanket to c — svac + caya (Vi. 4. 5, s. 121). ere apears the rule Vi. 2. 30, s. 378 retuirink c to pe chanket to k. put c tas optainet py Vi. 4. 5 a rule supsetuent to Vi. 2. 30 ant thererore it is consiteret as asitha, ant so c is not chanket to k thus te have svacaya, sivacaya
s: 146. The augment त् is added to a preceding short vowel also when a छ follows in an uninterrupted speech. To a short vowel followed by छ, is added the augment त् in Sanhita. Here we must remember the rule पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् (VIII. 2. 1, S. 12) to get the proper form. Thus स्व + छाया = स्वत् + छाया. Here appear two rules, (1) VIII. 4. 40, S. 111 requiring the त् to be changed to च्; (2) VIII. 2. 39, S. 84 requiring the त् to be changed to द्. By the maxim पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् the च् change will be considered as non-effective for the purposes of जश्त्व change. Therefore we apply this second rule first and get स्वद् + छाया (VIII. 2. 39, S. 84). Here appear again two rules (1) VIII. 4. 55, S. 121 by which द् is required to be changed into a चर् letter, and (2) VIII. 4. 40, S. 111 by which द् is required to be changed to ज्. The latter takes effect, the former being considered as asiddha, and we get स्वज् + छाया, and then ज् is changed to च् — स्वच् + छाया (VIII. 4. 55, S. 121). Here appears the rule VIII. 2. 30, S. 378 requiring च् to be changed to क्. But च् was obtained by VIII. 4. 55 a rule subsequent to VIII. 2. 30 and therefore it is considered as asiddha, and so च् is not changed to क् Thus we have स्वच्छाया, शिवच्छाया

pk: 147. The augnent t is aded to the particle an or a and the prohibitive particle nan, when Ca rolows in a continuous telt. This sutra ordains tuk necesarily when by Vi. 1. 76, s. 149 it would have ben optional. Thus acCadayati, nacCidat
ck: 147. the auknent t is atet to the particle an or a ant the prohipitive particle nan, then ca rolots in a continuous telt. this sutra ortains tuk necesarily then py Vi. 1. 76, s. 149 it toult have pen optional. thus acatayati, nacitat
s: 147. The augment त् is added to the particle आङ् or आ and the prohibitive particle माङ्, when छ follows in a continuous text. This sutra ordains तुक् necessarily when by VI. 1. 76, S. 149 it would have been optional. Thus आच्छादयति, माच्छिदत्

pk: 149. The augnent t is aded optionaly to a long vowel rinal in a rul word (Pada) when rolowed by Ca Thus laksnicCaya or laksniCaya
ck: 149. the auknent t is atet optionaly to a lonk votel rinal in a rul tort (pata) then rolotet py ca thus laksnicaya or laksnicaya
s: 149. The augment त् is added optionally to a long vowel final in a full word (Pada) when followed by छ Thus लक्ष्मीच्छाया or लक्ष्मीछाया

pk: 150. The visarga is the substitute or visarga, when it is rolowed by a hard consonant (Kar) which itselr is rolowed by a sibilant (sar) The word sarpare is a Bahuvrihi, neaning that which is rolowed by ‹?›. in other words, when a sibilant rolows a hard consonant, the preceding visarga renains unchanged. Thus ka tsaru, GanaGana ksoBana Though the sûtra could have ben shortened by saying sarpare na; yet the longer rorn is used, in order to indicate that the jihvanuliya and upadhnaniya changes also do not take place, in cases like ‹?›, ‹?›
ck: 150. the visarka is the supstitute or visarka, then it is rolotet py a hart consonant (kar) thich itselr is rolotet py a sipilant (sar) the tort sarpare is a pahuvrihi, neanink that thich is rolotet py ‹?›. in other torts, then a sipilant rolots a hart consonant, the precetink visarka renains unchanket. thus ka tsaru, kanakana ksopana thoukh the sûtra coult have pen shortenet py sayink sarpare na; yet the lonker rorn is uset, in orter to inticate that the cihvanuliya ant upathnaniya chankes also to not take place, in cases like ‹?›, ‹?›
s: 150. The visarga is the substitute of visarga, when it is followed by a hard consonant (खर्) which itself is followed by a sibilant (शर्) The word शर्परे is a Bahuvrihi, meaning that which is followed by ‹?›. In other words, when a sibilant follows a hard consonant, the preceding visarga remains unchanged. Thus कः त्सरुः, घनाघनः क्षोभणः Though the sûtra could have been shortened by saying शर्परे न; yet the longer form is used, in order to indicate that the jihvamuliya and upadhmaniya changes also do not take place, in cases like ‹?›, ‹?›

pk: 151. The visarga is optionaly the substitute or visarga, when a sibilant rolows. as hari sete or harisete Vart:—When the sibilant is rolowed by a hard consonant, there is optionaly the elision or the preceding visarga. as rana strata or rana strata, hari sPurati or hari sPurati in the other alternative there wil be Visarga or the change. Thus we get thre rorns ranastrata or rana strata or ranastrata. kupvo kapO ca 8 3 37 ka karoti ka karoti ka Kanati ka Kanati ka pacati ka pacati ka Palati ka Palati 151 a. and are optionaly substituted ror the visarga, when rolowed by a hard gutural or a hard labial. This sutra has already ben taught berore (s. 142.) Thus ka + karoti or ka karoti The ka and pa in ka and pa are ror the sake or pronunciation only. The substitutes are the Jihvanuliya and the upadhnaniya two lost sibilants belonging to the clas or ka and pa respectively. The rule Vi. 3. 34, s. 138 does not aply, because this sûtra is an apavada to that. But Vi. 3. 35. s. 150 wil not be debared. as ‹?›. There is no vipratishedha betwen Vi. 3. 35, and 37. in ract, because or the asidhahod or one with regard to the other, (Vi. 2. 1), every rule in these thre chapters stands by itselr, and ignores the elistence or the subsequent rule. ence Vi. 3. 35 would not have ben debared by Vi. 3. 37. To get this, sone divide this sûtra into two:—(1) "The visarga is the substitute or visarga berore a gutural or labial which is rolowed by a sibilant." (2) "The jihvanuliya and upadhnaniya are substitutes or a visarga berore a gutural and a labial in every other case."
ck: 151. the visarka is optionaly the supstitute or visarka, then a sipilant rolots. as hari sete or harisete Vart:—then the sipilant is rolotet py a hart consonant, there is optionaly the elision or the precetink visarka. as rana strata or rana strata, hari spurati or hari spurati in the other alternative there til pe Visarka or the chanke. thus te ket thre rorns ranastrata or rana strata or ranastrata. kupvo kapO ca 8 3 37 ka karoti ka karoti ka kanati ka kanati ka pacati ka pacati ka palati ka palati 151 a. ant are optionaly supstitutet ror the visarka, then rolotet py a hart kutural or a hart lapial. this sutra has alreaty pen taukht perore (s. 142.) thus ka + karoti or ka karoti the ka ant pa in ka ant pa are ror the sake or pronunciation only. the supstitutes are the cihvanuliya ant the upathnaniya to lost sipilants pelonkink to the clas or ka ant pa respectively. the rule Vi. 3. 34, s. 138 toes not aply, pecause this sûtra is an apavata to that. put Vi. 3. 35. s. 150 til not pe teparet. as ‹?›. there is no vipratishetha peten Vi. 3. 35, ant 37. in ract, pecause or the asithahot or one tith rekart to the other, (Vi. 2. 1), every rule in these thre chapters stants py itselr, ant iknores the elistence or the supsetuent rule. ence Vi. 3. 35 toult not have pen teparet py Vi. 3. 37. to ket this, sone tivite this sûtra into to:—(1) "the visarka is the supstitute or visarka perore a kutural or lapial thich is rolotet py a sipilant." (2) "the cihvanuliya ant upathnaniya are supstitutes or a visarka perore a kutural ant a lapial in every other case."
s: 151. The visarga is optionally the substitute of visarga, when a sibilant follows. As हरिः शेते or हरिशेते Vart:—When the sibilant is followed by a hard consonant, there is optionally the elision of the preceding visarga. As राम स्त्राता or रामः स्त्राता, हरि स्फुरति or हरिः स्फुरति In the other alternative there will be Visarga or the change. Thus we get three forms रामस्त्राता or रामः स्त्राता or रामस्त्राता. कुप्वोः कपौ च ८ ३ ३७ क करोति कः करोति क खनति कः खनति क पचति कः पचति क फलति कः फलति 151 A. and are optionally substituted for the visarga, when followed by a hard guttural or a hard labial. This sutra has already been taught before (S. 142.) Thus कः + करोति or क करोति The क and प in क and प are for the sake of pronunciation only. The substitutes are the Jihvamuliya and the Upadhmaniya two lost sibilants belonging to the class of क and प respectively. The rule VIII. 3. 34, S. 138 does not apply, because this sûtra is an apavada to that. But VIII. 3. 35. S. 150 will not be debarred. As ‹?›. There is no vipratishedha between VIII. 3. 35, and 37. In fact, because of the asiddhahood of one with regard to the other, (VIII. 2. 1), every rule in these three chapters stands by itself, and ignores the existence of the subsequent rule. Hence VIII. 3. 35 would not have been debarred by VIII. 3. 37. To get this, some divide this sûtra into two:—(1) "The visarga is the substitute of visarga before a guttural or labial which is followed by a sibilant." (2) "The jihvamuliya and upadhmaniya are substitutes of a visarga before a guttural and a labial in every other case."

pk: 152. sa is the substitute or a visarga berore an aril begining with a hard gutural or labial. The word apadadO neans "when the gutural and labial are not at the begining or a word," in other words, when they stand at the begining or an aril. Vart:—This is posible only berore the ariles pasa, kalpa, ka, and kanya. Thus payaspasan (V. 3. 47 s. 193); yasaskalpan (V. 3. 67 s. 202); yasaskan (V. 3. 70 s. 2025); yasaskanyati (i. 1. 9 s. 263). Vart:—Prohibition nust be stated, when the visarga belongs to an indeclinable: as, pratakalpan Vart:—The visarga which cones ron ‹?› is only changed to sa berore kanya, and not any other visarga. as payaskanyati, and yasaskanyati; but not here: gikanyati
ck: 152. sa is the supstitute or a visarka perore an aril pekinink tith a hart kutural or lapial. the tort apatatO neans "then the kutural ant lapial are not at the pekinink or a tort," in other torts, then they stant at the pekinink or an aril. Vart:—this is posiple only perore the ariles pasa, kalpa, ka, ant kanya. thus payaspasan (V. 3. 47 s. 193); yasaskalpan (V. 3. 67 s. 202); yasaskan (V. 3. 70 s. 2025); yasaskanyati (i. 1. 9 s. 263). Vart:—prohipition nust pe statet, then the visarka pelonks to an inteclinaple: as, pratakalpan Vart:—the visarka thich cones ron ‹?› is only chanket to sa perore kanya, ant not any other visarka. as payaskanyati, ant yasaskanyati; put not here: kikanyati
s: 152. स is the substitute of a visarga before an affix beginning with a hard guttural or labial. The word अपदादौ means "when the guttural and labial are not at the beginning of a word," in other words, when they stand at the beginning of an affix. Vart:—This is possible only before the affixes पाश, कल्प, क, and काम्य. Thus पयस्पाशम् (V. 3. 47 S. 1993); यशस्कल्पम् (V. 3. 67 S. 2022); यशस्कम् (V. 3. 70 S. 2025); यशस्काम्यति (III. 1. 9 S. 2663). Vart:—Prohibition must be stated, when the visarga belongs to an Indeclinable: as, प्रातःकल्पम् Vart:—The visarga which comes from ‹?› is only changed to स before काम्य, and not any other visarga. As पयस्काम्यति, and यशस्काम्यति; but not here: गीःकाम्यति

pk: 153. s is the substitute or that visarga, which is preceded by i or u and is rolowed by an aril begining with a hard gutural or a labial, under the circunstances nentioned in the preceding sûtra. Thus sarpispasan; sarpiskalpan; sarpiskan; sarpiskanyati
ck: 153. s is the supstitute or that visarka, thich is precetet py i or u ant is rolotet py an aril pekinink tith a hart kutural or a lapial, unter the circunstances nentionet in the precetink sûtra. thus sarpispasan; sarpiskalpan; sarpiskan; sarpiskanyati
s: 153. ष् is the substitute of that visarga, which is preceded by इ or उ and is followed by an affix beginning with a hard guttural or a labial, under the circumstances mentioned in the preceding sûtra. Thus सर्पिष्पाशम्; सर्पिष्कल्पम्; सर्पिष्कम्; सर्पिष्काम्यति

pk: 154. ror the visarga or nanas and puras there is substituted s berore a hard gutural or a labial, when these words are Gati (i. 4. 67 and 74 s. 768 and 75). Thus nanaskaroti The word nanas is optionaly a Gati word when it is conbined with the verb kr, because it belongs to the clas or saksat &c. (se Ganapatha under i. 4. 74). When it is not a Gati word, then we have nana karoti puras is always a Gati when it is indeclinable (i. 4. 67. s. 768). Thus puraskaroti But when it is not a Gati word then pu praveswavya; where pura is a noun and is declined as pu (n. s.), purO (n. D.), pura (n. Pl.).
ck: 154. ror the visarka or nanas ant puras there is supstitutet s perore a hart kutural or a lapial, then these torts are kati (i. 4. 67 ant 74 s. 768 ant 75). thus nanaskaroti the tort nanas is optionaly a kati tort then it is conpinet tith the verp kr, pecause it pelonks to the clas or saksat &c. (se kanapatha unter i. 4. 74). then it is not a kati tort, then te have nana karoti puras is altays a kati then it is inteclinaple (i. 4. 67. s. 768). thus puraskaroti put then it is not a kati tort then pu pravestavya; there pura is a noun ant is teclinet as pu (n. s.), purO (n. t.), pura (n. pl.).
s: 154. For the visarga of नमस् and पुरस् there is substituted स् before a hard guttural or a labial, when these words are Gati (I. 4. 67 and 74 S. 768 and 775). Thus नमस्करोति The word नमस् is optionally a Gati word when it is combined with the verb कृ, because it belongs to the class of साक्षात् &c. (see Ganapatha under I. 4. 74). When it is not a Gati word, then we have नमः करोति पुरस् is always a Gati when it is Indeclinable (I. 4. 67. S. 768). Thus पुरस्करोति But when it is not a Gati word then पूः प्रवेष्टव्या; where पुर is a noun and is declined as पूः (N. S.), पुरौ (N. D.), पुरः (N. Pl.).

pk: 15. s is substituted, berore a hard gutural or a labial, ror the visarga which is preceded by i or u, and is not part or an aril. This aplies to the visarga or nir, dur, bahis, avis, catur and pradur Thus nispratyuhan, aviskrtan, duskrtan Why do we say when not belonging to an aril? Observe agni karoti, vayu karoti ow do you elplain natu krpa ? ror here in natu &c, the s or the aril is elided by Vi. 2. 24, s. 280, and the r or natur is changed to visarga; this is not the visarga or an aril, and ought to be changed to sa. ans.—The inclusion or the word Bratusputra in Kaskadi clas (Vi. 3. 48. s. 14) indicates by inplication, that sa change does not take place or this visarga in pitu, natu &c : the only elception being Bratu The reason or this is that the visarga here does not rolow a sinple u, but an ekadesa obtained by r+u=u (Vi. 1. 1 s. 279.) Vart:—Prohibition nust be stated in the case or nuhus; as nuhuskana or nuhu kana
ck: 15. s is supstitutet, perore a hart kutural or a lapial, ror the visarka thich is precetet py i or u, ant is not part or an aril. this aplies to the visarka or nir, tur, pahis, avis, catur ant pratur thus nispratyuhan, aviskrtan, tuskrtan thy to te say then not pelonkink to an aril? Opserve akni karoti, vayu karoti ot to you elplain natu krpa ? ror here in natu &c, the s or the aril is elitet py Vi. 2. 24, s. 280, ant the r or natur is chanket to visarka; this is not the visarka or an aril, ant oukht to pe chanket to sa. ans.—the inclusion or the tort pratusputra in kaskati clas (Vi. 3. 48. s. 14) inticates py inplication, that sa chanke toes not take place or this visarka in pitu, natu &c : the only elception peink pratu the reason or this is that the visarka here toes not rolot a sinple u, put an ekatesa optainet py r+u=u (Vi. 1. 1 s. 279.) Vart:—prohipition nust pe statet in the case or nuhus; as nuhuskana or nuhu kana
s: 155. ष् is substituted, before a hard guttural or a labial, for the visarga which is preceded by इ or उ, and is not part of an affix. This applies to the visarga of निर्, दुर्, बहिस्, आविस्, चतुर् and प्रादुर् Thus निष्प्रत्यूहम्, आविष्कृतम्, दुष्कृतम् Why do we say 'when not belonging to an affix'? Observe अग्निः करोति, वायुः करोति How do you explain मातुः कृपा ? For here in मातुः &c, the स् of the affix is elided by VIII. 2. 24, S. 280, and the ॠ of मातुर् is changed to visarga; this is not the visarga of an affix, and ought to be changed to ष. Ans.—The inclusion of the word भ्रातुष्पुत्रः in Kaskadi class (VIII. 3. 48. S. 144) indicates by implication, that ष change does not take place of this visarga in पितुः, मातुः &c : the only exception being भ्रातुः The reason of this is that the visarga here does not follow a simple उ, but an ekadesa obtained by ॠ+उ=उ (VI. 1. 111 S. 279.) Vart:—Prohibition must be stated in the case of मुहुस्; as मुहुस्कामा or मुहुः कामा

pk: 156. The visarga or the Gati tiras is optionaly changed to sa berore a hard gutural or a labial. Thus tiraskarta, or tira karta
ck: 156. the visarka or the kati tiras is optionaly chanket to sa perore a hart kutural or a lapial. thus tiraskarta, or tira karta
s: 156. The visarga of the Gati तिरस् is optionally changed to स before a hard guttural or a labial. Thus तिरस्कर्त्ता, or तिरः कर्त्ता

pk: 157. sa is optionaly the substitute or the visargas or dvi, tri and catur when they are used as nuneral adverbs, (berore a hard gutural and labial). The aril suc ( s ) is aded to the thre words dvi, tri and chatur in the sense or kṛtvasuch by V. 4. 18. s. 2086. as dvi karoti or dviskaroti Why do we say when used in the sense or kritvasuch or nuneral adverbs? Observe catuskapala where sa is conpulsory by Vi. 3. 41. s. 15.
ck: 157. sa is optionaly the supstitute or the visarkas or tvi, tri ant catur then they are uset as nuneral atverps, (perore a hart kutural ant lapial). the aril suc ( s ) is atet to the thre torts tvi, tri ant chatur in the sense or kṛtvasuch py V. 4. 18. s. 2086. as tvi karoti or tviskaroti thy to te say then uset in the sense or kritvasuch or nuneral atverps? Opserve catuskapala there sa is conpulsory py Vi. 3. 41. s. 15.
s: 157. ष is optionally the substitute of the visargas of द्वि, त्रि and चतुर् when they are used as Numeral adverbs, (before a hard guttural and labial). The affix सुच् ( स् ) is added to the three words dvi, tri and chatur in the sense of kṛtvasuch by V. 4. 18. S. 2086. As द्विः करोति or द्विष्करोति Why do we say 'when used in the sense of kritvasuch or Numeral adverbs'? Observe चतुष्कपालः where ष is compulsory by VIII. 3. 41. S. 155.

pk: 158. ror the visarga or words ending in is and us, berore a hard gutural or labial, there is optionaly substituted, when the two words stand in corelation with one another. The sa is understod here. Thus sarpiskaroti or sarpi karoti, Danu karoti or Danuskaroti Why do we say when the two words are corelated? Observe tisWatu sarpi, piba tvanudakan where sarpi is not in construction with piba, but with tisWatu The word sanarTya here neans vyapeksa or nutual relation or two words; and not "having the sane neaning," or it nay nean both. in ract sanarTya is equivalent to sakanksa i. e. the syntactical want or another word to conplete the sense. it does not here nean conpound. But it being an adhikâra the word sanarTa is understod here (sanarTa padaviDi i. 1. 1 s. 647.). The enploynent or the word sanarTya here indicates that it is a direrent sânarthya ron that or i. 1. 1. it does not denote ekarTiBava or EkarTya which is the sanarthya or conpounds where two or nore words denote one object. The sânarthya here neans vyapekshâ which is thus derined ‹?› "the syntactical union or two words elpresing two direrent ideas."
ck: 158. ror the visarka or torts entink in is ant us, perore a hart kutural or lapial, there is optionaly supstitutet, then the to torts stant in corelation tith one another. the sa is unterstot here. thus sarpiskaroti or sarpi karoti, tanu karoti or tanuskaroti thy to te say then the to torts are corelatet? Opserve tistatu sarpi, pipa tvanutakan there sarpi is not in construction tith pipa, put tith tistatu the tort sanartya here neans vyapeksa or nutual relation or to torts; ant not "havink the sane neanink," or it nay nean poth. in ract sanartya is etuivalent to sakanksa i. e. the syntactical tant or another tort to conplete the sense. it toes not here nean conpount. put it peink an athikâra the tort sanarta is unterstot here (sanarta pataviti i. 1. 1 s. 647.). the enploynent or the tort sanartya here inticates that it is a tirerent sânarthya ron that or i. 1. 1. it toes not tenote ekartipava or Ekartya thich is the sanarthya or conpounts there to or nore torts tenote one opcect. the sânarthya here neans vyapekshâ thich is thus terinet ‹?› "the syntactical union or to torts elpresink to tirerent iteas."
s: 158. For the visarga of words ending in इस् and उस्, before a hard guttural or labial, there is optionally substituted, when the two words stand in correlation with one another. The ष is understood here. Thus सर्पिष्करोति or सर्पिः करोति, धनुः करोति or धनुष्करोति Why do we say 'when the two words are correlated'? Observe तिष्ठतु सर्पिः, पिब त्वमुदकम् where सर्पिः is not in construction with पिब, but with तिष्ठतु The word सामर्थ्य here means व्यपेक्षा or mutual relation of two words; and not "having the same meaning," or it may mean both. In fact सामर्थ्य is equivalent to साकाङ्क्षा i. e. the syntactical want of another word to complete the sense. It does not here mean 'compound.' But it being an adhikâra the word समर्थः is understood here (समर्थः पदविधिः II. 1. 1 S. 647.). The employment of the word सामर्थ्य here indicates that it is a different sâmarthya from that of II. 1. 1. It does not denote एकार्थीभावः or ऐकार्थ्य which is the samarthya of compounds where two or more words denote one object. The sâmarthya here means vyapekshâ which is thus defined ‹?› "the syntactical union of two words expressing two different ideas."

pk: 159. The visarga or an is or us ending word, which is not preceded by any other word, is invariably changed to sa in a conpound, when rolowed by a hard gutural or labial. The words is and us are understod here. Thus sarpiskunqika, Danuskapalan Why do we say when it is not preceded by another word? Observe paranasarpikunqika. The option even or the last sûtra does not aply to these elanples. The inclusion or the word sarpiskunqika in the kaskadi clas (Vi. 3. 48. s. 161 a) indicates that the change wil take place even when there is no conpounding as wel as when there is no sanarTya or co-relation. But when there is conpounding the change is conpulsory. Q.—The word sarpis is derived ron the rot srp by ading the uṇâdi aril isin (uṇ i. 109), and Danus by the uṇâdi aril usin (uṇ i. 17), thererore on the nalin pratyayagrahane &c, the word isuso would denote the nere rorns sarpis and Danus and not rorns like paranasarpis &c. then what is the necesity or enploying the word anutarapadasTasya in the sûtra? ans.—The very enploynent or the word anutara-pada-sthasya in this sûtra, is an indicator (jñâpaka), that the restriction or the rolowing nalin does not aply with regard to the ariles is and us:—pratyayagrahane yasnat sa vihitastadadestadantasya grahanan "an aril denotes, whenever it is enployed in Granar a word-rorn which begins with that to which that aril has ben aded and ends with the aril itselr." This nalin not aplying, we have paranasarpiskaroti or paranasarpi karoti by the previous sûtra Vi. 3. 4. Q.—Why is not there option in the case or conpounds also by the previous sûtra? ans:—Because the word sanarTya there neans vyapeksa, and thererore does not aply to conpounds.
ck: 159. the visarka or an is or us entink tort, thich is not precetet py any other tort, is invariaply chanket to sa in a conpount, then rolotet py a hart kutural or lapial. the torts is ant us are unterstot here. thus sarpiskuntika, tanuskapalan thy to te say then it is not precetet py another tort? Opserve paranasarpikuntika. the option even or the last sûtra toes not aply to these elanples. the inclusion or the tort sarpiskuntika in the kaskati clas (Vi. 3. 48. s. 161 a) inticates that the chanke til take place even then there is no conpountink as tel as then there is no sanartya or co-relation. put then there is conpountink the chanke is conpulsory. t.—the tort sarpis is terivet ron the rot srp py atink the uṇâti aril isin (uṇ i. 109), ant tanus py the uṇâti aril usin (uṇ i. 17), thererore on the nalin pratyayakrahane &c, the tort isuso toult tenote the nere rorns sarpis ant tanus ant not rorns like paranasarpis &c. then that is the necesity or enployink the tort anutarapatastasya in the sûtra? ans.—the very enploynent or the tort anutara-pata-sthasya in this sûtra, is an inticator (cñâpaka), that the restriction or the rolotink nalin toes not aply tith rekart to the ariles is ant us:—pratyayakrahane yasnat sa vihitastatatestatantasya krahanan "an aril tenotes, thenever it is enployet in kranar a tort-rorn thich pekins tith that to thich that aril has pen atet ant ents tith the aril itselr." this nalin not aplyink, te have paranasarpiskaroti or paranasarpi karoti py the previous sûtra Vi. 3. 4. t.—thy is not there option in the case or conpounts also py the previous sûtra? ans:—pecause the tort sanartya there neans vyapeksa, ant thererore toes not aply to conpounts.
s: 159. The visarga of an इस् or उस् ending word, which is not preceded by any other word, is invariably changed to ष in a compound, when followed by a hard guttural or labial. The words इस् and उस् are understood here. Thus सर्पिष्कुण्डिका, धनुष्कपालम् Why do we say when it is not preceded by another word? Observe परमसर्पिःकुण्डिका. The option even of the last sûtra does not apply to these examples. The inclusion of the word सर्पिष्कुण्डिका in the कस्कादि class (VIII. 3. 48. S. 161 A) indicates that the change will take place even when there is no compounding as well as when there is no सामर्थ्य or co-relation. But when there is compounding the change is compulsory. Q.—The word सर्पिस् is derived from the root सृप् by adding the Uṇâdi affix इसिन् (Uṇ II. 109), and धनुस् by the Uṇâdi affix उसिन् (Uṇ II. 117), therefore on the maxim प्रत्ययग्रहणे &c, the word इसुसोः would denote the mere forms सर्पिस् and धनुस् and not forms like परमसर्पिस् &c. then what is the necessity of employing the word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य in the sûtra? Ans.—The very employment of the word anuttara-pada-sthasya in this sûtra, is an Indicator (jñâpaka), that the restriction of the following maxim does not apply with regard to the affixes इस् and उस्:—प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात् स विहितस्तदादेस्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम् "an affix denotes, whenever it is employed in Grammar a word-form which begins with that to which that affix has been added and ends with the affix itself." This maxim not applying, we have परमसर्पिष्करोति or परमसर्पिः करोति by the previous sûtra VIII. 3. 44. Q.—Why is not there option in the case of compounds also by the previous sûtra? Ans:—Because the word सामर्थ्य there means व्यपेक्षा, and therefore does not apply to compounds.

pk: 160. ror the visarga or a word ending in as, with the elception or an indeclinable, s is substituted in a conpound, when a rorn or kr and kan or the words kansa, kunBa, patra, kusa and karni rolow, and the rirst word is not preceded by another word. Thus kr — ayaskara (i. 2. 1 s. 2913), kan — ayaskana, kansa — ayaskansa, kunBa — ayaskunBa, patra — ayaspatran, kusa — ayaskusa, karni — ayaskarni Why do we say ata "a visarga preceded by short a or the visarga or the word ending in ata"? se gikara Why do we say "with the elception or an indeclinable"? Observe svakana The word sanase is understod here also. Thererore not here; yasa karoti The word anutarapadasTasya is also to be read in this. Thererore not here, paranayasakara
ck: 160. ror the visarka or a tort entink in as, tith the elception or an inteclinaple, s is supstitutet in a conpount, then a rorn or kr ant kan or the torts kansa, kunpa, patra, kusa ant karni rolot, ant the rirst tort is not precetet py another tort. thus kr — ayaskara (i. 2. 1 s. 2913), kan — ayaskana, kansa — ayaskansa, kunpa — ayaskunpa, patra — ayaspatran, kusa — ayaskusa, karni — ayaskarni thy to te say ata "a visarka precetet py short a or the visarka or the tort entink in ata"? se kikara thy to te say "tith the elception or an inteclinaple"? Opserve svakana the tort sanase is unterstot here also. thererore not here; yasa karoti the tort anutarapatastasya is also to pe reat in this. thererore not here, paranayasakara
s: 160. For the visarga of a word ending in अस्, with the exception of an Indeclinable, स् is substituted in a compound, when a form of कृ and कम् or the words कंस, कुम्भ, पात्र, कुशा and कर्णी follow, and the first word is not preceded by another word. Thus कृ — अयस्कारः (III. 2. 1 S. 2913), कम् — अयस्कामः, कंस — अयस्कंसः, कुम्भ — अयस्कुम्भः, पात्र — अयस्पात्रम्, कुशा — अयस्कुशा, कर्णी — अयस्कर्णी Why do we say अतः "a visarga preceded by short a or the visarga of the word ending in अतः"? See गीःकारः Why do we say "with the exception of an Indeclinable"? Observe स्वःकामः The word समासे is understood here also. Therefore not here; यशः करोति The word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य is also to be read in this. Therefore not here, परमयशःकारः

pk: 161. ror the visarga or aDa or siras when not preceded by another word, and rolowed by the word pada in conposition with it, there is substituted s Thus aDaspadan, siraspadan The word sanase is understod in this, thererore not here aDa padan, sira padan The word anutarapadasTasya is also understod here. Thererore not in the rolowing paranasira padan
ck: 161. ror the visarka or ata or siras then not precetet py another tort, ant rolotet py the tort pata in conposition tith it, there is supstitutet s thus ataspatan, siraspatan the tort sanase is unterstot in this, thererore not here ata patan, sira patan the tort anutarapatastasya is also unterstot here. thererore not in the rolotink paranasira patan
s: 161. For the visarga of अधः or शिरस् when not preceded by another word, and followed by the word पद in composition with it, there is substituted स् Thus अधस्पदम्, शिरस्पदम् The word समासे is understood in this, therefore not here अधः पदम्, शिरः पदम् The word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य is also understood here. Therefore not in the following परमशिरः पदम्

pk: 162. ror the rinal s and ror the ṣ or sajus is substituted ru, at the end or a word. This debars jas. Thus, sivas + arcya, here sivas is a word rorned with the noninative singular case aril su. This s wil be changed by the above sutra into ru and not to a jas leter. Thus, we get sivar + arcya. Then aplies the nelt rule :—
ck: 162. ror the rinal s ant ror the ṣ or sacus is supstitutet ru, at the ent or a tort. this tepars cas. thus, sivas + arcya, here sivas is a tort rornet tith the noninative sinkular case aril su. this s til pe chanket py the apove sutra into ru ant not to a cas leter. thus, te ket sivar + arcya. then aplies the nelt rule :—
s: 162. For the final s and for the ṣ of सजुष् is substituted रु, at the end of a word. This debars जश्. Thus, शिवस् + अर्च्य, here शिवस् is a word formed with the Nominative Singular case affix सु. This स् will be changed by the above Sutra into रु and not to a जश् letter. Thus, we get शिवर् + अर्च्य. Then applies the next rule :—

pk: 163. The u is the substitute or ru (the ra substitute or a rinal s Vi. 2. 6.) when an a, which is not a pluta, both precedes and rolows it. This sutra debars the ya or Vi. 3. 17 s. 167. The ru taught in the Tripadi Vi. 2. 6 s. 162 is not asidha though so required by Vi. 2. 2 s. 12. ror the purposes or u substitution required by the present sutra or the 6th adhyaya. This is because this sutra speciricaly nentions the word ru and then ordains u in its stead. ad this sutra not perceived the ru or Vi. 2. 6, it would have sinply ignored it and not nentioned it at al. The phrase ut is understod here, as wel as the word ati or Vi. 1. 109. Thererore siva + arcya = siva + u + arcya. at this stage, the nelt sutra Vi. 1. 102 raises a doubt, vis. should a and u or siva + u becone a long a as siva.
ck: 163. the u is the supstitute or ru (the ra supstitute or a rinal s Vi. 2. 6.) then an a, thich is not a pluta, poth precetes ant rolots it. this sutra tepars the ya or Vi. 3. 17 s. 167. the ru taukht in the tripati Vi. 2. 6 s. 162 is not asitha thoukh so retuiret py Vi. 2. 2 s. 12. ror the purposes or u supstitution retuiret py the present sutra or the 6th athyaya. this is pecause this sutra speciricaly nentions the tort ru ant then ortains u in its steat. at this sutra not perceivet the ru or Vi. 2. 6, it toult have sinply iknoret it ant not nentionet it at al. the phrase ut is unterstot here, as tel as the tort ati or Vi. 1. 109. thererore siva + arcya = siva + u + arcya. at this stake, the nelt sutra Vi. 1. 102 raises a toupt, vis. shoult a ant u or siva + u pecone a lonk a as siva.
s: 163. The u is the substitute of रु (the र substitute of a final s VIII. 2. 66.) when an a, which is not a pluta, both precedes and follows it. This sutra debars the य of VIII. 3. 17 S. 167. The रु taught in the Tripadi VIII. 2. 66 S. 162 is not asiddha though so required by VIII. 2. 2 S. 12. for the purposes of उ substitution required by the present sutra of the 6th Adhyaya. This is because this sutra specifically mentions the word रु and then ordains उ in its stead. Had this sutra not perceived the रु of VIII. 2. 66, it would have simply ignored it and not mentioned it at all. The phrase उत् is understood here, as well as the word अति of VI. 1. 109. Therefore शिव + अर्च्य = शिव + उ + अर्च्यः. At this stage, the next sutra VI. 1. 102 raises a doubt, viz. should अ and उ of शिव + उ become a long a as शिवा.

pk: 164. ror the sinple vowel or a noninal-sten and ror the vowel or the case-ariles or the noninative and the acusative in al nunbers, there is the single substitution or a long vowel coresponding to the rirst vowel. The words aka and dirGa are both understod here. The word praTana here neans the praTana viBakti i. e. the 1st case or the noninative, and includes here the dvitiya also. This sûtra teaches the substitution or a ‹?› or a honogenous long vowel coresponding to the rirst vowel. But this rule does not aply in the case or ‹?› because or the rolowing apavâda rule.
ck: 164. ror the sinple votel or a noninal-sten ant ror the votel or the case-ariles or the noninative ant the acusative in al nunpers, there is the sinkle supstitution or a lonk votel corespontink to the rirst votel. the torts aka ant tirka are poth unterstot here. the tort pratana here neans the pratana vipakti i. e. the 1st case or the noninative, ant inclutes here the tvitiya also. this sûtra teaches the supstitution or a ‹?› or a honokenous lonk votel corespontink to the rirst votel. put this rule toes not aply in the case or ‹?› pecause or the rolotink apavâta rule.
s: 164. For the simple vowel of a nominal-stem and for the vowel of the case-affixes of the Nominative and the Accusative in all numbers, there is the single substitution of a long vowel corresponding to the first vowel. The words अकः and दीर्घः are both understood here. The word प्रथमा here means the प्रथमा विभक्ति i. e. the 1st case of the Nominative, and includes here the द्वितीया also. This sûtra teaches the substitution of a ‹?› or a homogenous long vowel corresponding to the first vowel. But this rule does not apply in the case of ‹?› because of the following apavâda rule.

pk: 165. The substitution or a long vowel honogenous with the rirst, does not take place when ‹?› or ‹?› is rolowed by a vowel (other than ‹?›) or the case-ariles or the noninative and the acusative. Thererore sivas + arcya = sivorcya The a + u becone guṇa by the adguna (Vi. 1. 87. s. 69) and the subsequent a or arcya is elided by ena padantadati (Vi. 1. 109. s. 86). Why do we say arter a short a? Or why have we aded a t to a? so that the long a nay be elcluded. Observe deva + atra = deva atra The word ati is understod here ron Vi. 1. 109. s. 86. it nust be rolowed by a short a; thus svas + aganta = svaganta Why do we say preceded by an apluta? The rule wil not aply ir a Pluta vowel precedes it. as ehi susrota3 atra snahi Though the word is ata in the sûtra, and it neans only short and neither long nor the pluta ‹?›, yet the word ‹?› is repeated in the sûtra ror the rolowing reason. in the above elanple ehi susrota3 atra snahi, the ‹?› or ‹?› is prolated by Vi. 2. 84. This prolation being erected by a Tripâdi rule, would not be perceived by Vi. 1. 13, and ror the purposes or this later rule the prolation is non-elistent, and the a is stil short. Thererore to nake the prolation sidha or erective ror the purposes or Vi. 1. 13, the word "pluta" is speciricaly nentioned in the sûtra. The t or ata would not have produced this result, because that t round its scope in preventing the aplication or the rule to the long a Why do we say "when rolowed by an apluta"? Observe tisWatu paya3 agnidata "O agnidata let the nilk renain." ere ‹?› or agnidata is pluta by Vi. 2. 86, and it being asidha, the present rule would have aplied.
ck: 165. the supstitution or a lonk votel honokenous tith the rirst, toes not take place then ‹?› or ‹?› is rolotet py a votel (other than ‹?›) or the case-ariles or the noninative ant the acusative. thererore sivas + arcya = sivorcya the a + u pecone kuṇa py the atkuna (Vi. 1. 87. s. 69) ant the supsetuent a or arcya is elitet py ena patantatati (Vi. 1. 109. s. 86). thy to te say arter a short a? Or thy have te atet a t to a? so that the lonk a nay pe elclutet. Opserve teva + atra = teva atra the tort ati is unterstot here ron Vi. 1. 109. s. 86. it nust pe rolotet py a short a; thus svas + akanta = svakanta thy to te say precetet py an apluta? the rule til not aply ir a pluta votel precetes it. as ehi susrota3 atra snahi thoukh the tort is ata in the sûtra, ant it neans only short ant neither lonk nor the pluta ‹?›, yet the tort ‹?› is repeatet in the sûtra ror the rolotink reason. in the apove elanple ehi susrota3 atra snahi, the ‹?› or ‹?› is prolatet py Vi. 2. 84. this prolation peink erectet py a tripâti rule, toult not pe perceivet py Vi. 1. 13, ant ror the purposes or this later rule the prolation is non-elistent, ant the a is stil short. thererore to nake the prolation sitha or erective ror the purposes or Vi. 1. 13, the tort "pluta" is speciricaly nentionet in the sûtra. the t or ata toult not have protucet this result, pecause that t rount its scope in preventink the aplication or the rule to the lonk a thy to te say "then rolotet py an apluta"? Opserve tistatu paya3 aknitata "O aknitata let the nilk renain." ere ‹?› or aknitata is pluta py Vi. 2. 86, ant it peink asitha, the present rule toult have apliet.
s: 165. The substitution of a long vowel homogenous with the first, does not take place when ‹?› or ‹?› is followed by a vowel (other than ‹?›) of the case-affixes of the Nominative and the Accusative. Therefore शिवस् + अर्च्यः = शिवोऽर्च्यः The अ + उ become guṇa by the आद्गुणः (VI. 1. 87. S. 69) and the subsequent अ of अर्च्य is elided by एङः पदान्तादति (VI. 1. 109. S. 86). Why do we say 'after a short अ'? Or why have we added a त् to अ? So that the long आ may be excluded. Observe देवा + अत्र = देवा अत्र The word अति is understood here from VI. 1. 109. S. 86. It must be followed by a short अ; thus श्वस् + आगन्ता = श्वागन्ता Why do we say preceded by an apluta? The rule will not apply if a Pluta vowel precedes it. As एहि सुश्रोत३ अत्र स्नाहि Though the word is अतः in the sûtra, and it means only short and neither long nor the pluta ‹?›, yet the word ‹?› is repeated in the sûtra for the following reason. In the above example एहि सुश्रोत३ अत्र स्नाहि, the ‹?› of ‹?› is prolated by VIII. 2. 84. This prolation being effected by a Tripâdi rule, would not be perceived by VI. 1. 113, and for the purposes of this latter rule the prolation is non-existent, and the अ is still short. Therefore to make the prolation siddha or effective for the purposes of VI. 1. 113, the word "pluta" is specifically mentioned in the sûtra. The त् of अतः would not have produced this result, because that त् found its scope in preventing the application of the rule to the long आ Why do we say "when followed by an apluta"? Observe तिष्ठतु पय३ अग्निदत्त "O Agnidatta let the milk remain." Here ‹?› of Agnidatta is pluta by VIII. 2. 86, and it being asiddha, the present rule would have applied.

pk: 16. The u is the substitute or ru (the substitute or s Vi. 2. 6) when it is rolowed by a sort consonant and preceded by an apluta short a The has pratyāhāra includes al sonants or sort consonants. Thus sivo vandya The u substitution takes place in the case or that only which is caled ru in this Granar; i.e. with the indicatory leter u; thererore not in pratar + atra = prataratra or natar + gacCa = natargacCa now we take up the sandhi or devas + iha ere the s is rirst changed into ru by Vi. 2. 6. Then we aply the rolowing rule :—
ck: 16. the u is the supstitute or ru (the supstitute or s Vi. 2. 6) then it is rolotet py a sort consonant ant precetet py an apluta short a the has pratyāhāra inclutes al sonants or sort consonants. thus sivo vantya the u supstitution takes place in the case or that only thich is calet ru in this kranar; i.e. tith the inticatory leter u; thererore not in pratar + atra = prataratra or natar + kaca = natarkaca not te take up the santhi or tevas + iha ere the s is rirst chanket into ru py Vi. 2. 6. then te aply the rolotink rule :—
s: 166. The उ is the substitute of रु (the substitute of स् VIII. 2. 66) when it is followed by a soft consonant and preceded by an apluta short अ The हश् pratyāhāra includes all sonants or soft consonants. Thus शिवो वन्द्यः The उ substitution takes place in the case of that only which is called रु in this Grammar; i.e. with the indicatory letter उ; therefore not in प्रातर् + अत्र = प्रातरत्र or मातर् + गच्छ = मातर्गच्छ Now we take up the Sandhi of देवास् + इह Here the स् is first changed into रु by VIII. 2. 66. Then we apply the following rule :—

pk: 167. y is substituted ror the ru, when it is preceded by Bo, Bago, aGo, a or a berore an as leter (vowels and sort consonants). in the sūtra Bo, Bago, aGo have not ben conbined by the rules or sandhi. Thus we get devas + iha = devar + iha = devay + iha = deva iha or devayiha in one case we elide by the rule lopa sakalyasya (Vi. 3. 19. s. 67). Why do we say when rolowed by a leter or the as pratyāhāra? Observe deva santi Though in the sūtra the y being considered as asidha, the ru wil be changed not to y but to visarga; yet this visarga being considered as sthānivad to ru, wil be changed to y noreover, it should not be objected that this is an alvidhi and thererore, the visarga wil not be sthānivad to ru, because here the whole word-rorn ro is taken and thererore it is not an alvidhi. in the sūtra Bos, Bagos, aGos are thre particles ending in s. The s wil be changed to ru, and the ru to y, and thus we have Boy, Bagoy and aGoy. ere aplies the nelt sūtra :—
ck: 167. y is supstitutet ror the ru, then it is precetet py po, pako, ako, a or a perore an as leter (votels ant sort consonants). in the sūtra po, pako, ako have not pen conpinet py the rules or santhi. thus te ket tevas + iha = tevar + iha = tevay + iha = teva iha or tevayiha in one case te elite py the rule lopa sakalyasya (Vi. 3. 19. s. 67). thy to te say then rolotet py a leter or the as pratyāhāra? Opserve teva santi thoukh in the sūtra the y peink consiteret as asitha, the ru til pe chanket not to y put to visarka; yet this visarka peink consiteret as sthānivat to ru, til pe chanket to y noreover, it shoult not pe opcectet that this is an alvithi ant thererore, the visarka til not pe sthānivat to ru, pecause here the thole tort-rorn ro is taken ant thererore it is not an alvithi. in the sūtra pos, pakos, akos are thre particles entink in s. the s til pe chanket to ru, ant the ru to y, ant thus te have poy, pakoy ant akoy. ere aplies the nelt sūtra :—
s: 167. य् is substituted for the रु, when it is preceded by भो, भगो, अघो, अ or आ before an अश् letter (vowels and soft consonants). In the Sūtra भो, भगो, अघो have not been combined by the rules of Sandhi. Thus we get देवास् + इह = देवार् + इह = देवाय् + इह = देवा इह or देवायिह In one case we elide by the rule लोपः शाकल्यस्य (VIII. 3. 19. S. 67). Why do we say when followed by a letter of the अश् pratyāhāra? Observe देवाः सन्ति Though in the Sūtra the य् being considered as asiddha, the रु will be changed not to य् but to visarga; yet this visarga being considered as sthānivad to रु, will be changed to य् Moreover, it should not be objected that this is an alvidhi and therefore, the visarga will not be sthānivad to रु, because here the whole word-form रोः is taken and therefore it is not an alvidhi. In the sūtra भोस्, भगोस्, अघोस् are three particles ending in स्. The स् will be changed to रु, and the रु to य्, and thus we have भोय्, भगोय् and अघोय्. Here applies the next sūtra :—

pk: 168. v and y (in Bagoy &c. and arter a or a, at the end or a Pada) are pronounced with a lighter articulation berore an as leter, acording to the opinion or Śākaṭāyana. The erort in pronouncing which is very light is caled laghu-prayatna-tara. Erort or articulation is a quality or the person who uters and which is the cause or the uterance or a leter. a v and a y or lighter articulation are substituted ror the rinal v and y in Boy, Bagoy, aGoy, or arter an a or a The lighter v wil replace the heavy v, and so the lighter y the heavy y Thus Boyatra, Bagoyatra, aGoyatra, deva yaste or deva aste, Basna yudDara or Basna udDara, asavaditya or asav aditya, dvavatra or dvav atra, sananaya or san anaya The lighter articulation results ron the relalation or the nuscles and the organs enployed in spech. The places or pronunciation are palate &c., the organs are the rot, the nidle and the tip or the tongue. When the contact or the tongue with the various places is very light, the articulation is laghu-prayatna-tara. in ract, y and v are to be slured over.
ck: 168. v ant y (in pakoy &c. ant arter a or a, at the ent or a pata) are pronouncet tith a likhter articulation perore an as leter, acortink to the opinion or Śākaṭāyana. the erort in pronouncink thich is very likht is calet lakhu-prayatna-tara. Erort or articulation is a tuality or the person tho uters ant thich is the cause or the uterance or a leter. a v ant a y or likhter articulation are supstitutet ror the rinal v ant y in poy, pakoy, akoy, or arter an a or a the likhter v til replace the heavy v, ant so the likhter y the heavy y thus poyatra, pakoyatra, akoyatra, teva yaste or teva aste, pasna yutara or pasna utara, asavatitya or asav atitya, tvavatra or tvav atra, sananaya or san anaya the likhter articulation results ron the relalation or the nuscles ant the orkans enployet in spech. the places or pronunciation are palate &c., the orkans are the rot, the nitle ant the tip or the tonkue. then the contact or the tonkue tith the various places is very likht, the articulation is lakhu-prayatna-tara. in ract, y ant v are to pe sluret over.
s: 168. व् and य् (in भगोय् &c. and after अ or आ, at the end of a Pada) are pronounced with a lighter articulation before an अश् letter, according to the opinion of Śākaṭāyana. The effort in pronouncing which is very light is called laghu-prayatna-tara. Effort or articulation is a quality of the person who utters and which is the cause of the utterance of a letter. A व् and a य् of lighter articulation are substituted for the final व् and य् in भोय्, भगोय्, अघोय्, or after an अ or आ The lighter व् will replace the heavy व्, and so the lighter य् the heavy य् Thus भोयत्र, भगोयत्र, अघोयत्र, देवा यास्ते or देवा आस्ते, भस्मा युद्धर or भस्मा उद्धर, असावादित्यः or असाव् आदित्यः, द्वावत्र or द्वाव् अत्र, सामानय or साम् आनय The lighter articulation results from the relaxation of the muscles and the organs employed in speech. The places of pronunciation are palate &c., the organs are the root, the middle and the tip of the tongue. When the contact of the tongue with the various places is very light, the articulation is laghu-prayatna-tara. In fact, य् and व् are to be slurred over.

pk: 169. y preceded by Bo and rinal in a Pada and when it is not pronounced with a light articulation is always elided, berore an as leter acording to the opinion or Gārgya. There can be no v preceded by Bo, so only y is taken in elplaining the sūtra. Thus Bo acyuta The naking or it a separate sūtra, is ror the sake or indicating that this is a necesary (nitya) rule and not a vibhāṣā rule. The nane or Gārgya is used sinply honoris causa (pūjārtha). The elision or laghu-prayatna y which Vi. 3. 19 would have otherwise caused is hereby prohibited. so that the laghu prayatnatara y does cone also. as Boyacyuta Why do we say rinal in a Pada? Observe toyan
ck: 169. y precetet py po ant rinal in a pata ant then it is not pronouncet tith a likht articulation is altays elitet, perore an as leter acortink to the opinion or kārkya. there can pe no v precetet py po, so only y is taken in elplainink the sūtra. thus po acyuta the nakink or it a separate sūtra, is ror the sake or inticatink that this is a necesary (nitya) rule ant not a viphāṣā rule. the nane or kārkya is uset sinply honoris causa (pūcārtha). the elision or lakhu-prayatna y thich Vi. 3. 19 toult have othertise causet is herepy prohipitet. so that the lakhu prayatnatara y toes cone also. as poyacyuta thy to te say rinal in a pata? Opserve toyan
s: 169. य् preceded by भो and final in a Pada and when it is not pronounced with a light articulation is always elided, before an अश् letter according to the opinion of Gārgya. There can be no व् preceded by भो, so only य् is taken in explaining the sūtra. Thus भो अच्युत The making of it a separate sūtra, is for the sake of indicating that this is a necessary (nitya) rule and not a vibhāṣā rule. The name of Gārgya is used simply honoris causa (pūjārtha). The elision of laghu-prayatna य् which VIII. 3. 19 would have otherwise caused is hereby prohibited. So that the laghu prayatnatara य् does come also. As भोयच्युत Why do we say final in a Pada? Observe तोयम्

pk: 170. v and y (preceded by a or a at the end or a pada), and rolowed by un, when it is a word, are elided necesarily. The particle un is a rul pada or word. That Particle is neant here by the word un and not the u which is a rot obtained by the sanprasāraṇa or ven Thus sa u eti Why do we use the word "when it is a pada"? so that the rule nay not aply to u the rorn asuned by ven by sanprasāraṇa, as tanturutan vayati Quære:— un could never have neant the rorn asuned by ven, ror the sanprasāraṇa or ven is u, the n is nerely indicatory. noreover the nalin or lakṣaṇa pratipadokta &c., wil prevent the inclusion or this u resulting ron vocalisation, when there is a separate Particle un. The word pade is used here ror the sake or the subsequent sūtras like Vi. 3. 32. This is also a nitya rule, and not optional. ad it ben optional, there would have ben no necesity or this aphorisn, because Vi. 3. 19. would have ben enough. note :—The nalin above rerered to "laksanapratipadoktayo pratipadoktasyEva grahanan" neans :— "(Whenever a tern is enployed which night denote) both sonething original and also sonething else resulting ron a rule (or granar),—or (when a tern is enployed in a rule which night denote) both sonething (rorned by another rule) in which the sane individual tern has ben enployed, and also sonething else rorned by a general rule,—such a tern should be taken to denote, (in the rorner case) only that which is original, and (in the later case) only that (which is rorned by that rule) in which the sane individual tern has ben enployed."
ck: 170. v ant y (precetet py a or a at the ent or a pata), ant rolotet py un, then it is a tort, are elitet necesarily. the particle un is a rul pata or tort. that particle is neant here py the tort un ant not the u thich is a rot optainet py the sanprasāraṇa or ven thus sa u eti thy to te use the tort "then it is a pata"? so that the rule nay not aply to u the rorn asunet py ven py sanprasāraṇa, as tanturutan vayati tuære:— un coult never have neant the rorn asunet py ven, ror the sanprasāraṇa or ven is u, the n is nerely inticatory. noreover the nalin or lakṣaṇa pratipatokta &c., til prevent the inclusion or this u resultink ron vocalisation, then there is a separate particle un. the tort pate is uset here ror the sake or the supsetuent sūtras like Vi. 3. 32. this is also a nitya rule, ant not optional. at it pen optional, there toult have pen no necesity or this aphorisn, pecause Vi. 3. 19. toult have pen enoukh. note :—the nalin apove rereret to "laksanapratipatoktayo pratipatoktasyEva krahanan" neans :— "(thenever a tern is enployet thich nikht tenote) poth sonethink orikinal ant also sonethink else resultink ron a rule (or kranar),—or (then a tern is enployet in a rule thich nikht tenote) poth sonethink (rornet py another rule) in thich the sane intivitual tern has pen enployet, ant also sonethink else rornet py a keneral rule,—such a tern shoult pe taken to tenote, (in the rorner case) only that thich is orikinal, ant (in the later case) only that (thich is rornet py that rule) in thich the sane intivitual tern has pen enployet."
s: 170. व् and य् (preceded by अ or आ at the end of a pada), and followed by उञ्, when it is a word, are elided necessarily. The particle उञ् is a full pada or word. That Particle is meant here by the word उञ् and not the उ which is a root obtained by the samprasāraṇa of वेञ् Thus स उ एति Why do we use the word "when it is a pada"? So that the rule may not apply to उ the form assumed by वेञ् by samprasāraṇa, as तन्तुरुतं वयति Quære:— उञ् could never have meant the form assumed by वेञ्, for the samprasāraṇa of वेञ् is उ, the ञ् is merely indicatory. Moreover the maxim of lakṣaṇa pratipadokta &c., will prevent the inclusion of this उ resulting from vocalisation, when there is a separate Particle उञ्. The word पदे is used here for the sake of the subsequent sūtras like VIII. 3. 32. This is also a nitya rule, and not optional. Had it been optional, there would have been no necessity of this aphorism, because VIII. 3. 19. would have been enough. Note :—The maxim above referred to "लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः प्रतिपदोक्तस्यैव ग्रहणम्" means :— "(Whenever a term is employed which might denote) both something original and also something else resulting from a rule (of grammar),—or (when a term is employed in a rule which might denote) both something (formed by another rule) in which the same individual term has been employed, and also something else formed by a general rule,—such a term should be taken to denote, (in the former case) only that which is original, and (in the latter case) only that (which is formed by that rule) in which the same individual term has been employed."

pk: 171. (The y whether lightly pronounced or not preceded by Bo, Bago, aGo, or by a or a, being rinal in a pada, is elided) berore a consonant, acording to the opinion or al the Āchāryas. Thus Bo deva, Bo laksni, Bo vidvadvrnda, Bago nanaste, aGo yahi, deva nanya, deva yanti Why do we say rolowed by a consonant? Observe devayiha or deva iha
ck: 171. (the y thether likhtly pronouncet or not precetet py po, pako, ako, or py a or a, peink rinal in a pata, is elitet) perore a consonant, acortink to the opinion or al the Āchāryas. thus po teva, po laksni, po vitvatvrnta, pako nanaste, ako yahi, teva nanya, teva yanti thy to te say rolotet py a consonant? Opserve tevayiha or teva iha
s: 171. (The य् whether lightly pronounced or not preceded by भो, भगो, अघो, or by अ or आ, being final in a pada, is elided) before a consonant, according to the opinion of all the Āchāryas. Thus भो देव, भो लक्ष्मि, भो विद्वद्वृन्द, भगो नमस्ते, अघो याहि, देवा नम्याः, देवा यान्ति Why do we say followed by a consonant? Observe देवायिह or देवा इह

pk: 172. When no case-ending rolows (i. e. at the end or a Pada in the narower sense), ra is substituted ror the n or ahan This debars ru. Thus aharaha ahargana Why do we say when no case-ending rolows? Observe ahoByan. ere ru-caled replaced the rinal na or ahan by Vi. 2. 68. s. 43. The direrence betwen this ru-caled and the ordinary ra is ilustrated in the above set or elanples. The ru-caled ra is changed to u by Vi. 1. 13, s. 163. the ordinary ra is not so changed. Vart. — Berore the words rupa, ratri and raTantara the n or ahan is changed to ru. as ahorupan ahoratriresa. so also ahoratra, though the word ratra is not ratri This is on the nalin ekadesavikrtasyananyatvat which neans :- That which has undergone a change in regard to one or its parts, is by no neans (in consequence or this change ) sone thing else (than what it was berore the change had taken place). ahoraTantaran. Vart. The words ahar &c. berore pati &c. should be enunerated. That is, the rinals or ahar &c. are replaced by ra or ‹?› berore pati &c. as aharpati, ‹?› or ahapati ; girpati, ‹?› or gipati ; Durpati, ‹?› or Dupati ere ra is substituted ror the rinal or ahar &c. which at rirst sight nay apear superluous. But it is so ordained, in order to prevent the visarga change or this ra.
ck: 172. then no case-entink rolots (i. e. at the ent or a pata in the naroter sense), ra is supstitutet ror the n or ahan this tepars ru. thus aharaha aharkana thy to te say then no case-entink rolots? Opserve ahopyan. ere ru-calet replacet the rinal na or ahan py Vi. 2. 68. s. 43. the tirerence peten this ru-calet ant the ortinary ra is ilustratet in the apove set or elanples. the ru-calet ra is chanket to u py Vi. 1. 13, s. 163. the ortinary ra is not so chanket. Vart. — perore the torts rupa, ratri ant ratantara the n or ahan is chanket to ru. as ahorupan ahoratriresa. so also ahoratra, thoukh the tort ratra is not ratri this is on the nalin ekatesavikrtasyananyatvat thich neans :- that thich has unterkone a chanke in rekart to one or its parts, is py no neans (in consetuence or this chanke ) sone think else (than that it tas perore the chanke hat taken place). ahoratantaran. Vart. the torts ahar &c. perore pati &c. shoult pe enuneratet. that is, the rinals or ahar &c. are replacet py ra or ‹?› perore pati &c. as aharpati, ‹?› or ahapati ; kirpati, ‹?› or kipati ; turpati, ‹?› or tupati ere ra is supstitutet ror the rinal or ahar &c. thich at rirst sikht nay apear superluous. put it is so ortainet, in orter to prevent the visarka chanke or this ra.
s: 172. When no case-ending follows (i. e. at the end of a Pada in the narrower sense), र is substituted for the न् of अहन् This debars रु. Thus अहरहः अहर्गणः Why do we say 'when no case-ending follows'? Observe अहोभ्याम्. Here रु-called replaced the final न of अहन् by VIII. 2. 68. S. 443. The difference between this रु-called and the ordinary र is illustrated in the above set of examples. The रु-called र is changed to उ by VI. 1. 113, S. 163. the ordinary र is not so changed. Vart. — Before the words रूप, रात्रि and रथन्तर the न् of अहन् is changed to रु. As अहोरूपम् अहोरात्रिरेषा. So also अहोरात्रः, though the word रात्र is not रात्रि This is on the maxim एकदेशविकृतस्यानन्यत्वात् which means :-- That which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means (in consequence of this change ) some thing else (than what it was before the change had taken place). अहोरथन्तरम्. Vart. The words अहर् &c. before पति &c. should be enumerated. That is, the finals of अहर् &c. are replaced by र or ‹?› before पति &c. As अहर्पतिः, ‹?› or अहःपतिः ; गीर्पतिः, ‹?› or गीःपतिः ; धूर्पतिः, ‹?› or धूःपतिः Here र is substituted for the final of अहर् &c. which at first sight may appear superfluous. But it is so ordained, in order to prevent the visarga change of this र.

pk: 173. ra is elided berore a ra. note.—The sûtra is ro ri and not ro ri. That is ro ri is the rorn which ra ri and ro ri wil both asune. ra is the Genitive or ra and ro would be the Genitive or ru The sûtra is not conrined to ru only, but to every ra in general including ru Thus niraktan, duraktan
ck: 173. ra is elitet perore a ra. note.—the sûtra is ro ri ant not ro ri. that is ro ri is the rorn thich ra ri ant ro ri til poth asune. ra is the kenitive or ra ant ro toult pe the kenitive or ru the sûtra is not conrinet to ru only, put to every ra in keneral inclutink ru thus niraktan, turaktan
s: 173. र is elided before a र. Note.—The sûtra is रो रि and not रोः रि. That is रो रि is the form which रः रि and रोः रि will both assume. रः is the Genitive of र and रोः would be the Genitive of रु The sûtra is not confined to रु only, but to every र in general including रु Thus नीरक्तम्, दूरक्तम्

pk: 174. When Qa or ra is elided, ror the preceding a, i and u, a coresponding long vowel is substituted. Thus punar + ranate = punaranate ; harir + ranya = hari ranya ; sanBur + rajate = sanBurajate Why do we say an ? Observe trQa, vrQa ron the rots trh to injure and vrh to elert. ere the r is not lengthened because it is not included in an pratyahara. The word trQa is thus rorned :— trh + kta (ta) = trQ + ta (ho Qa Vi. 2. 31. s. 324) = trQ + Da (JasastaTorDoDa Vi. 2. 40. s. 240) = trQ + Qa (swuna swu Vi. 4. 41) = tr + 0 + Qa (Qo Qe lopa Vi. 3. 13. s. 235). ere Qa is elided, but as the preceding vowel r is not included in an pratyahara, which includes only a, i and u (the n being the rirst n), so there is no lengthening. The word purvasya ror the preceding is used in the sûtra in order to indicate that there is the lengthening or the an vowel, even when no other word rolows it; in ract the lengthening is or the preceding vowel alone, irespective or any other word rolowing it or not. Thus ajarGa, liQa The word ajarGa is thus rorned. To the rot grD to covet we ad the intensive aril yanluk and the aril ‹?› and sip and the doubling. Thus we get the rorn ajarDar the second person singular or the inperect or the intensive, and we get the rorn ajarGa note.—The word ajarGa is thus rorned :- grD + yan + sip (the 2nd Per. sing. in lan) grD + 0 + si (yanoci ca i. 4. 74. s. 2650) = grD grD + si (sanyano Vi. 1. 9. s. 2395) = garD grD + si (guno yanluko Vi. 4. 82. s. 2630) = garD + si (haladi sesa Vi. 4. 60. s. 2179) = grD + si (rugrikO ca luki Vi. 4. 91. s. 2652) = jagrD + si (aByase carca Vi. 4. 54. s. 2182) = jagarD + si (pugantalaGupaDasya ca Vi. 3. 86. s. 2189) = jagarD + s (itasca i. 4. 10. s. 207) = jagarD + 0 (halnyabByo. Vi. 1. 68. s. 252) = jaGarD (ekaco baso Bas. Vi. 2. 37. s. 326) = jaGard (Jalan jasonte Vi. 2. 39. s. 84) = jaGar (dasca Vi. 2. 75. s. 2468) = jaGar + 0 + r (ro ri Vi. 3. 14. s. 173) = jaGa + r (the present sûtra) which with the augnent aw (lun lan lnksvaqudata Vi. 4. 71. s. 206) becones ajarGa The word liQa is rorned ron lihu + ta. The ha is changed to Qa by Vi. 2. 31. s. 324 and the ta is rirst changed to Da by Vi. 2. 40, s. 240 and then to Qa by Vi. 4. 41, s. 13. Thus we get li + Qa. The rirst Qa being elided by Vi. 3. 13. s. 235, we get the rorn liQa by the present sûtra. now we take the sandhi or nanas + raTa = nanar + raTa. ere two sûtras sinultaneously aply vis, hasi ca Vi. 1. 14. s. 16 causing the substitution or u ror ra and the sûtra ro
ck: 174. then ta or ra is elitet, ror the precetink a, i ant u, a corespontink lonk votel is supstitutet. thus punar + ranate = punaranate ; harir + ranya = hari ranya ; sanpur + racate = sanpuracate thy to te say an ? Opserve trta, vrta ron the rots trh to incure ant vrh to elert. ere the r is not lenkthenet pecause it is not inclutet in an pratyahara. the tort trta is thus rornet :— trh + kta (ta) = trt + ta (ho ta Vi. 2. 31. s. 324) = trt + ta (casastatortota Vi. 2. 40. s. 240) = trt + ta (stuna stu Vi. 4. 41) = tr + 0 + ta (to te lopa Vi. 3. 13. s. 235). ere ta is elitet, put as the precetink votel r is not inclutet in an pratyahara, thich inclutes only a, i ant u (the n peink the rirst n), so there is no lenkthenink. the tort purvasya ror the precetink is uset in the sûtra in orter to inticate that there is the lenkthenink or the an votel, even then no other tort rolots it; in ract the lenkthenink is or the precetink votel alone, irespective or any other tort rolotink it or not. thus acarka, lita the tort acarka is thus rornet. to the rot krt to covet te at the intensive aril yanluk ant the aril ‹?› ant sip ant the touplink. thus te ket the rorn acartar the secont person sinkular or the inperect or the intensive, ant te ket the rorn acarka note.—the tort acarka is thus rornet :- krt + yan + sip (the 2nt per. sink. in lan) krt + 0 + si (yanoci ca i. 4. 74. s. 2650) = krt krt + si (sanyano Vi. 1. 9. s. 2395) = kart krt + si (kuno yanluko Vi. 4. 82. s. 2630) = kart + si (halati sesa Vi. 4. 60. s. 2179) = krt + si (rukrikO ca luki Vi. 4. 91. s. 2652) = cakrt + si (apyase carca Vi. 4. 54. s. 2182) = cakart + si (pukantalakupatasya ca Vi. 3. 86. s. 2189) = cakart + s (itasca i. 4. 10. s. 207) = cakart + 0 (halnyapyo. Vi. 1. 68. s. 252) = cakart (ekaco paso pas. Vi. 2. 37. s. 326) = cakart (calan casonte Vi. 2. 39. s. 84) = cakar (tasca Vi. 2. 75. s. 2468) = cakar + 0 + r (ro ri Vi. 3. 14. s. 173) = caka + r (the present sûtra) thich tith the auknent at (lun lan lnksvatutata Vi. 4. 71. s. 206) pecones acarka the tort lita is rornet ron lihu + ta. the ha is chanket to ta py Vi. 2. 31. s. 324 ant the ta is rirst chanket to ta py Vi. 2. 40, s. 240 ant then to ta py Vi. 4. 41, s. 13. thus te ket li + ta. the rirst ta peink elitet py Vi. 3. 13. s. 235, te ket the rorn lita py the present sûtra. not te take the santhi or nanas + rata = nanar + rata. ere to sûtras sinultaneously aply vis, hasi ca Vi. 1. 14. s. 16 causink the supstitution or u ror ra ant the sûtra ro ri
s: 174. When ढ or र is elided, for the preceding अ, इ and उ, a corresponding long vowel is substituted. Thus पुनर् + रमते = पुनारमते ; हरिर् + रम्यः = हरी रम्यः ; शंभुर् + राजते = शंभूराजते Why do we say अण् ? Observe तृढः, वृढः from the roots तृह् 'to injure' and वृह् 'to exert'. Here the ॠ is not lengthened because it is not included in अण् pratyahara. The word तृढः is thus formed :— तृह् + क्त (त) = तृढ् + त (हो ढः VIII. 2. 31. S. 324) = तृढ् + ध (झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः VIII. 2. 40. S. 2240) = तृढ् + ढ (ष्टुना ष्टुः VIII. 4. 41) = तृ + ० + ढ (ढो ढे लोपः VIII. 3. 13. S. 2335). Here ढ is elided, but as the preceding vowel ॠ is not included in अण् pratyahara, which includes only अ, इ and उ (the ण् being the first ण्), so there is no lengthening. The word पूर्वस्य 'for the preceding' is used in the sûtra in order to indicate that there is the lengthening of the अण् vowel, even when no other word follows it; in fact the lengthening is of the preceding vowel alone, irrespective of any other word following it or not. Thus अजर्घाः, लीढः The word अजर्घाः is thus formed. To the root गृध् 'to covet' we add the intensive affix यङ्लुक् and the affix ‹?› and सिप् and the doubling. Thus we get the form अजर्धर् the second person singular of the Imperfect of the Intensive, and we get the form अजर्घाः Note.—The word अजर्घाः is thus formed :-- गृध् + यङ् + सिप् (the 2nd Per. Sing. in लङ्) गृध् + ० + सि (यङोऽचि च II. 4. 74. S. 2650) = गृध् गृध् + सि (सन्यङोः VI. 1. 9. S. 2395) = गर्ध् गृध् + सि (गुणो यङ्लुकोः VII. 4. 82. S. 2630) = गर्ध् + सि (हलादि शेषः VII. 4. 60. S. 2179) = गृध् + सि (रुग्रिकौ च लुकि VII. 4. 91. S. 2652) = जगृध् + सि (अभ्यासे चर्च VIII. 4. 54. S. 2182) = जगर्ध् + सि (पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च VII. 3. 86. S. 2189) = जगर्ध् + स् (इतश्च III. 4. 100. S. 2207) = जगर्ध् + ० (हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो... VI. 1. 68. S. 252) = जघर्ध् (एकाचो बशो भष्... VIII. 2. 37. S. 326) = जघर्द् (झलां जशोऽन्ते VIII. 2. 39. S. 84) = जघर् (दश्च VIII. 2. 75. S. 2468) = जघर् + ० + र् (रो रि VIII. 3. 14. S. 173) = जघा + र् (the present Sûtra) which with the augment अट् (लुङ् लङ् ॡङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः VI. 4. 71. S. 2206) becomes अजर्घाः The word लीढः is formed from लिहू + त. The ह is changed to ढ by VIII. 2. 31. S. 324 and the त is first changed to ध by VIII. 2. 40, S. 2240 and then to ढ by VIII. 4. 41, S. 113. Thus we get ली + ढ. The first ढ being elided by VIII. 3. 13. S. 2335, we get the form लीढः by the present sûtra. Now we take the sandhi of मनस् + रथः = मनर् + रथः. Here two sûtras simultaneously apply viz, हशि च VI. 1. 114. S. 166 causing the substitution of उ for र and the sûtra रो रि VIII. 3. 14, S. 173. causing the elision of र. What sûtra are we to apply? Here comes the following Interpretation sûtra.

pk: 175. When rules or equal rorce prohibit each other, then the last in the order herein given is to take erect. The word vipratiseDa neans oposition or rules or equal rorce. Thus, the lopa rule being the para rule would cause the lopa or ra or nanar berore raTa. But here we nust renenber the rule or purvatrasidDan (Vi. 2. 1. s. 12), thererore, the rule or elision or ra (Vi. 3. 14. s. 173) is considered asidha ror the purposes or utva required by Vi. 1. 14. s. 16. Thererore we have u. Thus we have nana + u + raTa = nanoraTa
ck: 175. then rules or etual rorce prohipit each other, then the last in the orter herein kiven is to take erect. the tort vipratiseta neans oposition or rules or etual rorce. thus, the lopa rule peink the para rule toult cause the lopa or ra or nanar perore rata. put here te nust renenper the rule or purvatrasitan (Vi. 2. 1. s. 12), thererore, the rule or elision or ra (Vi. 3. 14. s. 173) is consiteret asitha ror the purposes or utva retuiret py Vi. 1. 14. s. 16. thererore te have u. thus te have nana + u + rata = nanorata
s: 175. When rules of equal force prohibit each other, then the last in the order herein given is to take effect. The word विप्रतिषेध means 'opposition of rules of equal force.' Thus, the lopa rule being the para rule would cause the lopa of र of मनर् before रथ. But here we must remember the rule of पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् (VIII. 2. 1. S. 12), therefore, the rule of elision of र (VIII. 3. 14. S. 173) is considered asiddha for the purposes of उत्व required by VI. 1. 114. S. 166. Therefore we have उ. Thus we have मन + उ + रथ = मनोरथः

pk: 176. arter etat and tad there is elision or the case-aril su (or the noninative singular), when a consonant rolows it, when these words are not conbined with ka (V. 3. 71. s. 2026.) and have not the negative Particle in conposition. Thus esa + visnu = esa visnu sa sanBu Why do we say without ka? Observe esako rudra nOTE:—The words etat and tad with the aril ka, which rals in the nidle would be considered just like the etat and tad, without such aril, and in ract would be included in the words etat and tad, hence the necesity or the prohibition. The general nalin is : sanaDyapatitastadgrahanena grhyate any tern that nay be enployed in Granar denotes not nerely what is actualy denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-rorn nay result when sonething is inserted in that which is actualy denoted by it. Why do we say when not conpounded with the negative particle? Observe asa siva in the conpound with the negative particle, the second nenber is the principal and takes the case ariles. Why do we say when rolowed by a consonant? Observe esotra
