s: 176. After एतत् and तद् there is elision of the case-affix सु (of the nominative singular), when a consonant follows it, when these words are not combined with क (V. 3. 71. S. 2026.) and have not the Negative Particle in composition. Thus एषः + विष्णुः = एष विष्णुः स शंभुः Why do we say 'without क'? Observe एषको रुद्रः NOTE:—The words एतत् and तद् with the affix क, which falls in the middle would be considered just like the एतत् and तद्, without such affix, and in fact would be included in the words एतत् and तद्, hence the necessity of the prohibition. The general maxim is : सन्मध्यपतितस्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यते 'any term that may be employed in Grammar denotes not merely what is actually denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-form may result when something is inserted in that which is actually denoted by it.' Why do we say 'when not compounded with the negative particle'? Observe असः शिवः In the compound with the negative particle, the second member is the principal and takes the case affixes. Why do we say 'when followed by a consonant'? Observe एषोऽत्र

pk: 17. The case-aril or he, is elided berore a vowel, ir by such elision the netre or the rot becones conplete. Thus senanavidi praBrti ya isise ( nig. i. 24. 1.) sa inan Bavati ( prapnuhi, avate prapyarTasya lowi rupan ) praBrtin (prakarsena Brtan stuti) ya ( he brhaspate yastvan ) isise ( sarvasya jagata isvaro Bavasi ) " acept ( O Brihaspati ! ) this god burden ( or our praise ) e who rulest, ” acording to Vanana the author or Kasika, this rule is conrined to Vedic netres only. acording to others, the rule is aplied to al slokas without any such distinction. in elplaining this sûtra we have used the word satyeva " only then " in order to linit its scope ; and this we get by the rorce or the word bahulan in the sûtra Vi. 1. 13. s. 3526. which inediately precedes it in the order or ashtadhyáyí. Thererore there is no elision here, because the verse is conpleted without elision. sohana janasudDanan ( naghuvansa ) we canot say sa ahan or sahanu &c. sedu raja ksayati carsaninan ( nig i 32. 15 ) sOsaDiraBiruDyase ( nig Vi. 43. 9 ). The case-ending being elided, the sandhi takes place. Why do we say when by such elision the netre or the line is conpleted ? Observe sa it kseti sa evanuktya The word aci in the sûtra is ror the sake or distinctnes : ror the purposes or netre would not have ben served by eliding the aril berore a consonant, ror then the sylables would renain the sane. it is by sandhi that a sylable is lesened ; and sandhi would take place only with a vowel. acording to Kasika the Pâda nust rerer to a Pada or the nig-Veda only. Others elplain the word pada as a rot or a sloka also, and acording to then this rule is not conrined to Vedic netres only. Thus we have :- sEsa dasaraTi rana, sEsa raja yuDisWira, sEsakarno nahatyagi sEsa Bino nahabala
ck: 17. the case-aril or he, is elitet perore a votel, ir py such elision the netre or the rot pecones conplete. thus senanaviti praprti ya isise ( nik. i. 24. 1.) sa inan pavati ( prapnuhi, avate prapyartasya loti rupan ) praprtin (prakarsena prtan stuti) ya ( he prhaspate yastvan ) isise ( sarvasya cakata isvaro pavasi ) " acept ( O prihaspati ! ) this kot purten ( or our praise ) e tho rulest, ” acortink to Vanana the author or kasika, this rule is conrinet to Vetic netres only. acortink to others, the rule is apliet to al slokas tithout any such tistinction. in elplainink this sûtra te have uset the tort satyeva " only then " in orter to linit its scope ; ant this te ket py the rorce or the tort pahulan in the sûtra Vi. 1. 13. s. 3526. thich inetiately precetes it in the orter or ashtathyáyí. thererore there is no elision here, pecause the verse is conpletet tithout elision. sohana canasutanan ( nakhuvansa ) te canot say sa ahan or sahanu &c. setu raca ksayati carsaninan ( nik i 32. 15 ) sOsatirapirutyase ( nik Vi. 43. 9 ). the case-entink peink elitet, the santhi takes place. thy to te say then py such elision the netre or the line is conpletet ? Opserve sa it kseti sa evanuktya the tort aci in the sûtra is ror the sake or tistinctnes : ror the purposes or netre toult not have pen servet py elitink the aril perore a consonant, ror then the sylaples toult renain the sane. it is py santhi that a sylaple is lesenet ; ant santhi toult take place only tith a votel. acortink to kasika the pâta nust rerer to a pata or the nik-Veta only. Others elplain the tort pata as a rot or a sloka also, ant acortink to then this rule is not conrinet to Vetic netres only. thus te have :- sEsa tasarati rana, sEsa raca yutistira, sEsakarno nahatyaki sEsa pino nahapala
s: 177. The case-affix of 'he,' is elided before a vowel, if by such elision the metre of the foot becomes complete. Thus सेमामाविद्दि प्रभृति य ईशिषे ( Rig. II. 24. 1.) सः इमाम् भवति ( प्राप्नुहि, अवतेः प्राप्यर्थस्य लोटि रूपं ) प्रभृतिम् (प्रकर्षेण भृतां स्तुति) यः ( हे बृहस्पते यस्त्वं ) ईशिषे ( सर्वस्य जगत ईश्वरो भवसि ) " accept ( O Brihaspati ! ) this good burden ( of our praise ) He who rulest, ” According to Vamana the author of Kasika, this rule is confined to Vedic metres only. According to others, the rule is applied to all Slokas without any such distinction. In explaining this sûtra we have used the word सत्येव " only then " in order to limit its scope ; and this we get by the force of the word बहुलं in the sûtra VI. 1. 133. S. 3526. which immediately precedes it in the order of Ashtadhyáyí. Therefore there is no elision here, because the verse is completed without elision. सोऽहमा जन्मशुद्धानाम् ( Raghuvansa ) we cannot say स अहम् or साहमू &c. सेदु राजा क्षयति चर्षणीनाम् ( Rig I 32. 15 ) सौषधिरभिरुध्यसे ( Rig VIII. 43. 9 ). The case-ending being elided, the Sandhi takes place. Why do we say 'when by such elision the metre of the line is completed' ? Observe स इत् क्षेति स एवमुक्त्या The word अचि in the sûtra is for the sake of distinctness : for the purposes of metre would not have been served by eliding the affix before a consonant, for then the syllables would remain the same. It is by sandhi that a syllable is lessened ; and sandhi would take place only with a vowel. According to Kasika the Pâda must refer to a Pada of the Rig-Veda only. Others explain the word पाद as 'a foot of a sloka ' also, and according to them this rule is not confined to Vedic metres only. Thus we have :- सैष दाशरथी रामः, सैष राजा युधिष्ठिरः, सैषकर्णो महात्यागी सैष भीमो महाबलः

pk: 178. a signiricant rorn or a word, not being a verbal rot (dhâtu), or an aril (pratyaya) or a word ending in an aril, is caled a prâtipadika or crude-rorn or noninal base. This derines the word "prâtipadika" or crude-rorn. The pratipadika is the internediate stage in the developnent or a rul word (pada), ron the undirerentiated base caled the dhâtu or rot. it is that part or a word which is capable or receiving the case-terninations. The word arTavat neans having signirication. With the elception or verbal rots and ariles, a word-rorn having a signiricance or neaning is caled prâtipadika.
ck: 178. a sikniricant rorn or a tort, not peink a verpal rot (thâtu), or an aril (pratyaya) or a tort entink in an aril, is calet a prâtipatika or crute-rorn or noninal pase. this terines the tort "prâtipatika" or crute-rorn. the pratipatika is the internetiate stake in the tevelopnent or a rul tort (pata), ron the untirerentiatet pase calet the thâtu or rot. it is that part or a tort thich is capaple or receivink the case-terninations. the tort artavat neans havink siknirication. tith the elception or verpal rots ant ariles, a tort-rorn havink a sikniricance or neanink is calet prâtipatika.
s: 178. A significant form of a word, not being a verbal root (dhâtu), or an affix (pratyaya) or a word ending in an affix, is called a prâtipadika or crude-form or Nominal base. This defines the word "prâtipadika" or crude-form. The pratipadika is the intermediate stage in the development of a full word (pada), from the undifferentiated base called the dhâtu or root. It is that part of a word which is capable of receiving the case-terminations. The word अर्थवत् means having signification. With the exception of verbal roots and affixes, a word-form having a significance or meaning is called prâtipadika.

s: 182. (From this point forward as far as the end of Book Fifth, whatever we shall treat of, should be understood to come), after what ends with feminine affixes ‹?› or ‹?›, or after a crude-form. This is an 'adhikara' aphorism pure and simple. It simply consists of terms which other aphorisms, in order to complete their sense, are under the necessity of borrowing. In other words, this sûtra points out the base to which the affixes beginning with ‹?› treated of in the next sûtra, and ending with ‹?› (V. 4. 151), are to be applied. The sutra consists of three words. The term ‹?› is a common name for the three affixes ‹?›, ‹?›, and ‹?› The term ‹?› is the common name for the three affixes ‹?› and ‹?›. These are feminine affixes and are taught from sûtra 4 to 65 of the Fourth chapter. The word ‹?› means 'crudeform' and has been defined in sûtra I. 2. 45, 46, i. e. that which is possessed of a meaning, not being a root or an affix; or what ends with a Kṛt or a Taddhita affix. The word ‹?› is a Samâhâra-dvandva or Collective aggregate of these three words. Paribhâshâ:—Why have we employed the word 'ṅy-âp' in the aphorism? Is not the word prâtipadika wide enough to include the words ending with the feminine affixes, by virtue of the paribhâshâ—“A prâtipadika denotes, whenever it is employed in grammar, also such a crude-form as is derived from it by the addition of an affix denoting gender”? Ans:—The words ङी and आप् are specifically used in the sûtra in order to indicate that the Taddhita affixes should be added, after the words have taken the Feminine affixes and not before. Note:—The Kâśikâ gives the following answer to the above question. Not so. The paribhâshâ you quote applies to that case where there is a rule relating to an individual word-form given in the Sûtra itself. In other words, “this paribhâshâ is applicable when a word is employed in grammar which either denotes prâtipadikas generally (as the word 'prâtipadika' does in this sûtra) or denotes a particular prâtipadika, (such as the words युवा खलति, पलित, वलिन, and जरति in II. 1. 67)” That is, in II. 1. 67, the masculine form yuva, also includes the feminine: but not so everywhere. Moreover the words ङी, आप् have been employed in the Sûtra, in order to make the taddhita affixes applicable to feminine words ending in long ई (ङी) or long आ (आप्). Thus the feminine of 'काल' and 'हरिण' is, 'काली' and 'हरिणी', the feminine of 'खट्वा' and 'माला' is 'खट्वा' and 'माला' After these words we can apply the taddhita affix 'तरप्' as 'कालितरा,' 'हरिणितरा' 'खट्वतरा,' and 'मालतरा' Now, had we not used that word 'ṅy-âp' in the Sûtra, and wished to express the same idea as is done, say, by the word 'kâlitara,' we could not have got this form at all. The word काल takes ङीष् by IV. 1. 42; to which when तरप् is added, the vowel is shortened by VI. 3. 43; and we shall get the form कालितरा Why do you then say that the taddhita affixes could not be applied, but for the words ṅy-âp? A. To this we answer, that by the rule of vipratishedha, the taddhita would have debarred the feminine. Thus when feminine alone is meant and not comparison, we shall have काली; and when comparison alone is meant and not feminine, we shall have कालतर; but when both feminine and comparison are meant, then would arise the difficulty; and according to the general maxim, the taddhita would have debarred the feminine. But by using the word ṅy-âp, it is shown that first the feminine affixes are to be added, and then the comparison making affixes. The objector says:—The inclusion of ङी and आप् in this sûtra is useless, for the following reason:—all bases ending with the Feminine affixes can be considered as Prâtipadikas, on the strength of the maxim Prâtipadika grahaṇe liṅga-viśishṭasya &c. For example, श्वश्रूः “mother-in-law,” derived from the masculine श्वशुर with the affix ऊङ् (see Vârttika under IV. 1. 68. S. 523. श्वशुरस्योकाराकारलोपश्च). Here the word श्वश्रू must be a prâtipadika, otherwise no case affix can be add

s: 183. (After what ends with the feminine terminations or ‹?›, or after a crude-form, the following affixes are employed):— 1st. Singular: su (s), Dual: au, Plural: jas (as); 2nd. Singular: am, Dual: auṭ (au), Plural: śas (as); 3rd. Singular: ṭâ (â), Dual: bhyâm, Plural: bhis; 4th. Singular: ṅe (e), Dual: bhyâm, Plural: bhyas; 5th. Singular: ṅasi (as), Dual: bhyâm, Plural: bhyas; 6th. Singular: ṅas (as), Dual: os, Plural: âm; 7th. Singular: ṅi (i), Dual: os, Plural: sup (su). In the above affixes, letters like ‹?› in ‹?› and ‹?› are 'anubandhas' employed either for the sake of facility of pronunciation, or as distinguishing marks. The final प् is employed for the sake of forming the pratyâhâra सुप्, which is the collective name for the above 21 case-affixes. The letters ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, and ‹?› are ‹?› or servile letters.

pk: 184. The triads or conjugational ariles and case-ariles are also caled vibhakti or inrlective ariles. The word viBakti neans a conplete triad. Thus saptani viBakti neans the thre ariles or the seventh case, i. e., the locative singular, dual, and plural. so ‹?› neans the third person, singular, dual, and plural.
ck: 184. the triats or concukational ariles ant case-ariles are also calet viphakti or inrlective ariles. the tort vipakti neans a conplete triat. thus saptani vipakti neans the thre ariles or the seventh case, i. e., the locative sinkular, tual, ant plural. so ‹?› neans the thirt person, sinkular, tual, ant plural.
s: 184. The triads of conjugational affixes and case-affixes are also called vibhakti or Inflective affixes. The word विभक्ति means a complete triad. Thus सप्तमी विभक्ति means the three affixes of the seventh case, i. e., the locative singular, dual, and plural. So ‹?› means the third person, singular, dual, and plural.

pk: 187. in elpresing nulteity, a Plural case aril is enployed. Declension or nasculines ending in a now we take up the declension or the word ending in short a. in non. sing. the aril su is aded. Thus rana + su = ran + s = rana in rorning the Dual, the rolowing aplies.
ck: 187. in elpresink nulteity, a plural case aril is enployet. teclension or nasculines entink in a not te take up the teclension or the tort entink in short a. in non. sink. the aril su is atet. thus rana + su = ran + s = rana in rornink the tual, the rolotink aplies.
s: 187. In expressing multeity, a Plural case affix is employed. Declension of Masculines ending in a Now we take up the declension of the word ending in short a. In Nom. Sing. the affix सु is added. Thus राम + सु = राम् + स् = रामः In forming the Dual, the following applies.

pk: 18. Or the words having the sane rorn, and al in the sane one case-ternination, the last one is only retained. This is a very inportant sûtra, and deals with what is technicaly caled Ekasesha (or retention or one). When there are two or nore words or the sane rorn, and the sane case ternination, standing together, one is retained and the rest are droped. Thus rana + rana = rana The word ranO is rorned by ading the aril O to rana and by superseding Vi. 1. 102. s. 164 by Vi. 1. 104 s. 165 and aplying Vi. 1. 8 s. 72, we get the vridhi. in rorning the non. Pl. we ad jas. Thus rana + jas. The j is indicatory by the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 18. Or the torts havink the sane rorn, ant al in the sane one case-ternination, the last one is only retainet. this is a very inportant sûtra, ant teals tith that is technicaly calet Ekasesha (or retention or one). then there are to or nore torts or the sane rorn, ant the sane case ternination, stantink tokether, one is retainet ant the rest are tropet. thus rana + rana = rana the tort ranO is rornet py atink the aril O to rana ant py supersetink Vi. 1. 102. s. 164 py Vi. 1. 104 s. 165 ant aplyink Vi. 1. 8 s. 72, te ket the vrithi. in rornink the non. pl. te at cas. thus rana + cas. the c is inticatory py the rolotink sûtra.
s: 188. Of the words having the same form, and all in the same one case-termination, the last one is only retained. This is a very important sûtra, and deals with what is technically called Ekasesha (or retention of one). When there are two or more words of the same form, and the same case termination, standing together, one is retained and the rest are dropped. Thus राम + राम = राम The word रामौ is formed by adding the affix औ to राम and by superseding VI. 1. 102. S. 164 by VI. 1. 104 S. 165 and applying VI. 1. 88 S. 72, we get the vriddhi. In forming the Nom. Pl. we add जस्. Thus राम + जस्. The ज् is indicatory by the following sûtra.

pk: 189. The initial palatals and linguals or an aril are indicatory. Thus the j or jas would becone it. so the aril is realy as. But is not the rinal s or as also it by the sûtra halantyan i. 3. 3. s. 1.? no, because or the rolowing elceptions:—
ck: 189. the initial palatals ant linkuals or an aril are inticatory. thus the c or cas toult pecone it. so the aril is realy as. put is not the rinal s or as also it py the sûtra halantyan i. 3. 3. s. 1.? no, pecause or the rolotink elceptions:—
s: 189. The initial palatals and linguals of an affix are indicatory. Thus the ज् of जस् would become इत्. So the affix is really अस्. But is not the final स् of अस् also इत् by the sûtra हलन्त्यम् I. 3. 3. S. 1.? No, because of the following exceptions:—

pk: 190. The rinal dental consonants, and the rinal s and n are not it, in ariles caled vibhakti or inrlective ariles. Thererore the s or jas is not it. Thus rana + as. at this stage the rolowing rule apears which requires the a + a to be changed to a by pararupanekadesa —
ck: 190. the rinal tental consonants, ant the rinal s ant n are not it, in ariles calet viphakti or inrlective ariles. thererore the s or cas is not it. thus rana + as. at this stake the rolotink rule apears thich retuires the a + a to pe chanket to a py pararupanekatesa —
s: 190. The final dental consonants, and the final स् and म् are not इत्, in affixes called vibhakti or inflective affixes. Therefore the स् of जस् is not इत्. Thus राम + अस्. At this stage the following rule appears which requires the अ + अ to be changed to अ by पररूपमेकादेशः —

pk: 191. also when the short a, not being rinal in a Pada, is rolowed by a Guṇa leter, then in the ron or both the precedent and the subsequent — the single substitute is the rorn or the subsequent i. e. the Guṇa. But this ekadeśa rule is superseded by the subsequent rule praTanayo purvasavarna Vi. 1. 102. s. 164, which requires the lengthening or the preceding vowel; while the present sûtra ato gune debars the inediately suceding sûtra aka savarne dirGa Vi. 1. 101. s. 85. by the nalin:— Paribhâshâ:—apavâdas that precede (the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavâda-operations), supersede (only) those rules that stand nearest to then, not the subsequent (rules). Thererore the nearest rule Vi. 1. 101. s. 85 is superseded by the present sûtra and not the subsequent rule Vi. 1. 102. s. 164. Thus rana + as = rana. The Vocative case is like the noninative; the only direrence is in the singular. The Vocative singular is caled sanbudhi by the rolowing:
ck: 191. also then the short a, not peink rinal in a pata, is rolotet py a kuṇa leter, then in the ron or poth the precetent ant the supsetuent — the sinkle supstitute is the rorn or the supsetuent i. e. the kuṇa. put this ekateśa rule is supersetet py the supsetuent rule pratanayo purvasavarna Vi. 1. 102. s. 164, thich retuires the lenkthenink or the precetink votel; thile the present sûtra ato kune tepars the inetiately sucetink sûtra aka savarne tirka Vi. 1. 101. s. 85. py the nalin:— pariphâshâ:—apavâtas that precete (the rules thich teach operations that have to pe supersetet py the apavâta-operations), supersete (only) those rules that stant nearest to then, not the supsetuent (rules). thererore the nearest rule Vi. 1. 101. s. 85 is supersetet py the present sûtra ant not the supsetuent rule Vi. 1. 102. s. 164. thus rana + as = rana. the Vocative case is like the noninative; the only tirerence is in the sinkular. the Vocative sinkular is calet sanputhi py the rolotink:
s: 191. Also when the short a, not being final in a Pada, is followed by a Guṇa letter, then in the room of both the precedent and the subsequent — the single substitute is the form of the subsequent i. e. the Guṇa. But this ekadeśa rule is superseded by the subsequent rule प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः VI. 1. 102. S. 164, which requires the lengthening of the preceding vowel; while the present sûtra अतो गुणे debars the immediately succeeding sûtra अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः VI. 1. 101. S. 85. by the maxim:— Paribhâshâ:—Apavâdas that precede (the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the Apavâda-operations), supersede (only) those rules that stand nearest to them, not the subsequent (rules). Therefore the nearest rule VI. 1. 101. S. 85 is superseded by the present sûtra and not the subsequent rule VI. 1. 102. S. 164. Thus राम + अस् = रामाः. The Vocative case is like the nominative; the only difference is in the singular. The Vocative singular is called Sambuddhi by the following:

pk: 192. in the sense or vocative, the singular nunber or the rirst case-aril is caled sanbudhi. Thus the vocative singular or rana is rana + su ere the rolowing sûtra aplies.
ck: 192. in the sense or vocative, the sinkular nunper or the rirst case-aril is calet sanputhi. thus the vocative sinkular or rana is rana + su ere the rolotink sûtra aplies.
s: 192. In the sense of vocative, the singular number of the first case-affix is called Sambuddhi. Thus the vocative singular of राम is राम + सु Here the following sûtra applies.

pk: 193. The consonant or the noninative-aril (su and its substitute an) is elided in the Vocative singular, arter a noninal-sten ending in e or o or a short vowel. The elision here being taught with regard to the base which is a sanbudDi and which is qualiried by having e or o or a short vowel ror its rinal, it does not aply to he kataratkula ! in kataratkula there is not the elision or the t or the aril ad, the substitute or an; ror the aril there is ad (Vi. 1. 25). This aril being ‹?› causes the elision or the rinal or katara (Vi. 4. 143), and we have katar + at, here we have not a prâtipadika which ends in a short vowel, but in a consonant, hence t is not elided. se also Vi. 1. 25. The word en is used in the sûtra in order to indicate that the guṇa substitution required by hrasvasya guna Vi. 3. 108, is stronger than lopa. Thererore in he hare, the aril is not elided, rirst, and then guṇa substituted ror i, but rirst there is guṇa substitution and then the aril is elided, sinilarly visno. ror the guṇa substitution is stronger than elision, because it is a rule subsequent in order, the elision being Vi. 1. 69, the Guṇa being Vi. 3. 108; and because Guṇa is a nitya rule. Thererore when it is guṇated to e, there being no short vowel lert, the elision or su would not have taken place had the word en ben not used in the sûtra. now the acusative singular is rorned thus: rana + an. ere aplies the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 193. the consonant or the noninative-aril (su ant its supstitute an) is elitet in the Vocative sinkular, arter a noninal-sten entink in e or o or a short votel. the elision here peink taukht tith rekart to the pase thich is a sanputi ant thich is tualiriet py havink e or o or a short votel ror its rinal, it toes not aply to he kataratkula ! in kataratkula there is not the elision or the t or the aril at, the supstitute or an; ror the aril there is at (Vi. 1. 25). this aril peink ‹?› causes the elision or the rinal or katara (Vi. 4. 143), ant te have katar + at, here te have not a prâtipatika thich ents in a short votel, put in a consonant, hence t is not elitet. se also Vi. 1. 25. the tort en is uset in the sûtra in orter to inticate that the kuṇa supstitution retuiret py hrasvasya kuna Vi. 3. 108, is stronker than lopa. thererore in he hare, the aril is not elitet, rirst, ant then kuṇa supstitutet ror i, put rirst there is kuṇa supstitution ant then the aril is elitet, sinilarly visno. ror the kuṇa supstitution is stronker than elision, pecause it is a rule supsetuent in orter, the elision peink Vi. 1. 69, the kuṇa peink Vi. 3. 108; ant pecause kuṇa is a nitya rule. thererore then it is kuṇatet to e, there peink no short votel lert, the elision or su toult not have taken place hat the tort en pen not uset in the sûtra. not the acusative sinkular is rornet thus: rana + an. ere aplies the rolotink sûtra.
s: 193. The consonant of the nominative-affix (सु and its substitute अम्) is elided in the Vocative singular, after a nominal-stem ending in ए or ओ or a short vowel. The elision here being taught with regard to the base which is a संबुद्धि and which is qualified by having ए or ओ or a short vowel for its final, it does not apply to हे कतरत्कुल ! In कतरत्कुल there is not the elision of the त् of the affix अद्द्, the substitute of अम्; for the affix there is अद्द् (VII. 1. 25). This affix being ‹?› causes the elision of the final of कतर (VI. 4. 143), and we have कतर् + अत्, here we have not a prâtipadika which ends in a short vowel, but in a consonant, hence त् is not elided. See also VII. 1. 25. The word एङ् is used in the sûtra in order to indicate that the guṇa substitution required by ह्रस्वस्य गुणः VII. 3. 108, is stronger than lopa. Therefore in हे हरे, the affix is not elided, first, and then guṇa substituted for इ, but first there is guṇa substitution and then the affix is elided, similarly विष्णो. For the guṇa substitution is stronger than elision, because it is a rule subsequent in order, the elision being VI. 1. 69, the Guṇa being VII. 3. 108; and because Guṇa is a nitya rule. Therefore when it is guṇated to ए, there being no short vowel left, the elision of सु would not have taken place had the word एङ् been not used in the sûtra. Now the accusative singular is formed thus: राम + अम्. Here applies the following sûtra.

pk: 194. There is the single substitution or the rirst vowel, when a sinple vowel is rolowed by the short vowel or the case-ending an The word ak is understod here. Thus rana + an = ranan. so also acusative dual ranO as berore. now the acusative plural is rorned thus:— rana + sas ere aplies the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 194. there is the sinkle supstitution or the rirst votel, then a sinple votel is rolotet py the short votel or the case-entink an the tort ak is unterstot here. thus rana + an = ranan. so also acusative tual ranO as perore. not the acusative plural is rornet thus:— rana + sas ere aplies the rolotink sûtra.
s: 194. There is the single substitution of the first vowel, when a simple vowel is followed by the short vowel of the case-ending अम् The word अक् is understood here. Thus राम + अम् = रामम्. So also accusative dual रामौ as before. Now the accusative plural is formed thus:— राम + शस् Here applies the following sûtra.

pk: 195. The initial l and s, and the guturals or al ariles, elcept Tadhita, are indicatory. The initial l, s, k, K, g, G, n or ariles are indicatory, elcept in Tadhita ariles. Thererore s being it, the aril is as. Thus rana + as. at this stage aplies the rolowing sûtra:—
ck: 195. the initial l ant s, ant the kuturals or al ariles, elcept tathita, are inticatory. the initial l, s, k, k, k, k, n or ariles are inticatory, elcept in tathita ariles. thererore s peink it, the aril is as. thus rana + as. at this stake aplies the rolotink sûtra:—
s: 195. The initial ल् and श्, and the gutturals of all affixes, except Taddhita, are indicatory. The initial ल्, श्, क्, ख्, ग्, घ्, ङ् of affixes are indicatory, except in Taddhita affixes. Therefore श् being इत्, the affix is अस्. Thus राम + अस्. At this stage applies the following sûtra:—

pk: 196. īj a To go, to censure, blane. law—ijate liw—ijancakre luw—ijita Pasive ijyate Des. ijijisate Caus. ijayati aor. na BavanEjijat The rot ij is shortened rirst to i berore the aril can, and then reduplicated. se Vi. 4. 1. s. 2314.

s: 196. īj a To go, to censure, blame. लट्—ईजते लिट्—ईजाञ्चक्रे लुट्—ईजिता Passive ईज्यते Des. ईजिजिषते Caus. ईजयति Aor. मा भवानैजिजत् The root ईज् is shortened first to इ before the affix चङ्, and then reduplicated. See VII. 4. 1. S. 2314.

pk: 201. arter a sten ending in a, are substituted ina ror the instrunental ending wa ; at ror the ablative ending nasi, and sya ror the Genitive ending nas Thus ranena the na being changed to na
ck: 201. arter a sten entink in a, are supstitutet ina ror the instrunental entink ta ; at ror the aplative entink nasi, ant sya ror the kenitive entink nas thus ranena the na peink chanket to na
s: 201. After a stem ending in अ, are substituted इन for the Instrumental ending टा ; आत् for the Ablative ending ङसि, and स्य for the Genitive ending ङस् Thus रामेण the न being changed to ण

pk: 202. Berore a case-ending begining with yan (literaly a consonant or yan Pratyahara), the rinal a or a noninal sten is also lengthened. The whole or the phrase ato dirGo yani is understod here (Vi. 3. 101 / s. 2170). Thus rana + Byan = ranaByan
ck: 202. perore a case-entink pekinink tith yan (literaly a consonant or yan pratyahara), the rinal a or a noninal sten is also lenkthenet. the thole or the phrase ato tirko yani is unterstot here (Vi. 3. 101 / s. 2170). thus rana + pyan = ranapyan
s: 202. Before a case-ending beginning with यञ् (literally a consonant of यञ् Pratyahara), the final अ of a Nominal stem is also lengthened. The whole of the phrase अतो दीर्घो यञि is understood here (VII. 3. 101 / S. 2170). Thus राम + भ्याम् = रामाभ्याम्

pk: 203. arter a noninal sten ending in a, Es is substituted ror the case-ending Bis The adesa Es consists or nore than one leter and thererore replaces the whole or Bis, by the rule anekalsit sarvasya i. 1. 5. s. 45. Thus rana + Es = ranE
ck: 203. arter a noninal sten entink in a, Es is supstitutet ror the case-entink pis the atesa Es consists or nore than one leter ant thererore replaces the thole or pis, py the rule anekalsit sarvasya i. 1. 5. s. 45. thus rana + Es = ranE
s: 203. After a nominal stem ending in अ, ऐस् is substituted for the case-ending भिस् The adesa ऐस् consists of more than one letter and therefore replaces the whole of भिस्, by the rule अनेकाल्शित् सर्वस्य I. 1. 55. S. 45. Thus राम + ऐस् = रामैः

pk: 204. arter a sten ending in a, there is substituted ya ror the Dative ending ne Thus rana + e = rana + ya = ranaya. ere the ya being taken to be sthânivat to ne gets also the designation or sup and thererore the a or rana is lengthened berore ya by the rule Vi. 3. 102, s. 202. The nalin sanipatalaksano viDi raninitan tadviGatasya "that which is taught in a rule the aplication or which is ocasioned by the conbination or two things, does not becone the cause or the destruction or that conbination" does not aply here. Thus ya is substituted here, because the preceding word ends in a short a, thus this short a ocasioned the elistence or ya, thererore this ya canot ocasion the destruction or a But that however it does, ror it is on acount or this ya, that the preceding a is replaced by a. The anitya nature or this nalin is indicated by Panini hinselr, by rorning the dative or kaswa in sutra i. 1. 14 &c. The ne: is the anonalous Genitive case or the Dative ending; this aril is elhibited without any vibhakti in Vi. 1. 28 s. 382. The ne: should not be taken as the Genitive singular or the aril ni or the Locative singular. so also ranaByan as berore. The dative plural is rorned thus rana + Byas. ere aplies the rolowing sutra :—
ck: 204. arter a sten entink in a, there is supstitutet ya ror the tative entink ne thus rana + e = rana + ya = ranaya. ere the ya peink taken to pe sthânivat to ne kets also the tesiknation or sup ant thererore the a or rana is lenkthenet perore ya py the rule Vi. 3. 102, s. 202. the nalin sanipatalaksano viti raninitan tatvikatasya "that thich is taukht in a rule the aplication or thich is ocasionet py the conpination or to thinks, toes not pecone the cause or the testruction or that conpination" toes not aply here. thus ya is supstitutet here, pecause the precetink tort ents in a short a, thus this short a ocasionet the elistence or ya, thererore this ya canot ocasion the testruction or a put that hotever it toes, ror it is on acount or this ya, that the precetink a is replacet py a. the anitya nature or this nalin is inticatet py panini hinselr, py rornink the tative or kasta in sutra i. 1. 14 &c. the ne: is the anonalous kenitive case or the tative entink; this aril is elhipitet tithout any viphakti in Vi. 1. 28 s. 382. the ne: shoult not pe taken as the kenitive sinkular or the aril ni or the Locative sinkular. so also ranapyan as perore. the tative plural is rornet thus rana + pyas. ere aplies the rolotink sutra :—
s: 204. After a stem ending in अ, there is substituted य for the Dative ending ङे Thus राम + ए = राम + य = रामाय. Here the य being taken to be sthânivat to ङे gets also the designation of सुप् and therefore the अ of राम is lengthened before य by the rule VII. 3. 102, S. 202. The maxim संनिपातलक्षणो विधि रनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य "that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination" does not apply here. Thus य is substituted here, because the preceding word ends in a short अ, thus this short अ occasioned the existence of य, therefore this य cannot occasion the destruction of अ But that however it does, for it is on account of this य, that the preceding अ is replaced by आ. The anitya nature of this maxim is indicated by Panini himself, by forming the dative of कष्ट in Sutra III. 1. 14 &c. The ङे: is the anomalous Genitive case of the Dative ending; this affix is exhibited without any vibhakti in VII. 1. 28 S. 382. The ङे: should not be taken as the Genitive singular of the affix ङि of the Locative singular. So also रामाभ्याम् as before. The dative plural is formed thus राम + भ्यस्. Here applies the following Sutra :—

pk: 205. Berore a case-ending begining with Jal (lit. a consonant), in the Plural, e is substituted ror the rinal a or a noninal sten. as raneBya Why in the Plural ? Observe rana ; ranasya Why berore a case-aril begining with a consonant? Observe rananan (the lengthening here is by Vi. 4. 3. s. 30). Why a case-aril? Observe pacaDvan, and not pacaDyan now, we rorn the ablative singular rana + nasi = rana + at (by Vi. 1. 12. s. 201). ere the t or the aril should be changed to d by Jalan jasonte and wil then optionaly be changed to t by the rolowing sutra.
ck: 205. perore a case-entink pekinink tith cal (lit. a consonant), in the plural, e is supstitutet ror the rinal a or a noninal sten. as ranepya thy in the plural ? Opserve rana ; ranasya thy perore a case-aril pekinink tith a consonant? Opserve rananan (the lenkthenink here is py Vi. 4. 3. s. 30). thy a case-aril? Opserve pacatvan, ant not pacatyan not, te rorn the aplative sinkular rana + nasi = rana + at (py Vi. 1. 12. s. 201). ere the t or the aril shoult pe chanket to t py calan casonte ant til then optionaly pe chanket to t py the rolotink sutra.
s: 205. Before a case-ending beginning with झल् (lit. a consonant), in the Plural, ए is substituted for the final अ of a Nominal stem. As रामेभ्यः Why in the Plural ? Observe रामः ; रामस्य Why before a case-affix beginning with a consonant? Observe रामाणाम् (the lengthening here is by VI. 4. 3. S. 300). Why a case-affix? Observe पचध्वम्, and not पचध्यम् Now, we form the Ablative Singular राम + ङसि = राम + आत् (by VII. 1. 12. S. 201). Here the त् of the affix should be changed to द् by झलां जशोऽन्ते and will then optionally be changed to त् by the following Sutra.

pk: 206. The car is optionaly the substitute or a Jal that ocurs in a Pause. The word Jalan is understod in the sutra. a sonant or a surd non-aspirate nay stand as rinal in a Pause; but not an aspirate consonant. By Vi. 2. 39, s. 84, a non-aspirate sonant can only stand in a rinal position. This ordains that a non-aspirate surd nay also stand as the rinal, when there is Pause. Thus ranat or ranad. The rinal t and d nay be doubled by anaci ca (Vi. 4. 47) we get rour rorns as ranat or ranat or ranad or ranad n. B. This is not aproved by Tatvabodhini, as the neaning or the sûtra is that arter a vowel every consonant elcept h nay be doubled provided that a consonant rolows; ror the word non-vowel does not nean absence or al leters, but rather the absence or vowels only. inrerentialy there nust be a consonant. Bhatoji has taken the negation in anaci in the sense or Prasajya pratishedha; while the proper view is to take it as a Paryudâsa pratishedha. so also ranaByan ; raneBya ; ranasya in ranasya when the sa is doubled, this sa wil not be changed to ta by Kari ca Vi. 4. 5. s. 121, but it wil renain as sa only, because there is direrence betwen ta and sa as regards erort, the ta being alpaprana. ad ta and sa ben the sane, and had ta ben produced by Kari ca, then there would have ben no ned or teaching the substitution or sa by ta in sutras like Vi. 4. 49. s. 2342.
ck: 206. the car is optionaly the supstitute or a cal that ocurs in a pause. the tort calan is unterstot in the sutra. a sonant or a surt non-aspirate nay stant as rinal in a pause; put not an aspirate consonant. py Vi. 2. 39, s. 84, a non-aspirate sonant can only stant in a rinal position. this ortains that a non-aspirate surt nay also stant as the rinal, then there is pause. thus ranat or ranat. the rinal t ant t nay pe touplet py anaci ca (Vi. 4. 47) te ket rour rorns as ranat or ranat or ranat or ranat n. p. this is not aprovet py tatvapothini, as the neanink or the sûtra is that arter a votel every consonant elcept h nay pe touplet provitet that a consonant rolots; ror the tort non-votel toes not nean apsence or al leters, put rather the apsence or votels only. inrerentialy there nust pe a consonant. phatoci has taken the nekation in anaci in the sense or prasacya pratishetha; thile the proper viet is to take it as a paryutâsa pratishetha. so also ranapyan ; ranepya ; ranasya in ranasya then the sa is touplet, this sa til not pe chanket to ta py kari ca Vi. 4. 5. s. 121, put it til renain as sa only, pecause there is tirerence peten ta ant sa as rekarts erort, the ta peink alpaprana. at ta ant sa pen the sane, ant hat ta pen protucet py kari ca, then there toult have pen no net or teachink the supstitution or sa py ta in sutras like Vi. 4. 49. s. 2342.
s: 206. The चर् is optionally the substitute of a झल् that occurs in a Pause. The word झलाम् is understood in the sutra. A sonant or a surd non-aspirate may stand as final in a Pause; but not an aspirate consonant. By VIII. 2. 39, S. 84, a non-aspirate sonant can only stand in a final position. This ordains that a non-aspirate surd may also stand as the final, when there is Pause. Thus रामात् or रामाद्. The final त् and द् may be doubled by अनचि च (VIII. 4. 47) we get four forms as रामात् or रामात्त् or रामाद् or रामाद्द् N. B. This is not approved by Tatvabodhini, as the meaning of the sûtra is that after a vowel every consonant except ह् may be doubled provided that a consonant follows; for the word 'non-vowel' does not mean absence of all letters, but rather the absence of vowels only. Inferentially there must be a consonant. Bhattoji has taken the negation in अनचि in the sense of Prasajya pratishedha; while the proper view is to take it as a Paryudâsa pratishedha. So also रामाभ्याम् ; रामेभ्यः ; रामस्य In रामस्य when the स is doubled, this स will not be changed to त by खरि च VIII. 4. 55. S. 121, but it will remain as स only, because there is difference between त and स as regards effort, the त being अल्पप्राण. Had त and स been the same, and had त been produced by खरि च, then there would have been no need of teaching the substitution of स by त in Sutras like VIII. 4. 49. S. 2342.

pk: 207. Berore the case-ending os, e is substituted ror the rinal or a noninal-sten. as rane + os = ranayo now, we have to rorn the Genitive plural:—rana + an. ere cones the nelt sûtra.
ck: 207. perore the case-entink os, e is supstitutet ror the rinal or a noninal-sten. as rane + os = ranayo not, te have to rorn the kenitive plural:—rana + an. ere cones the nelt sûtra.
s: 207. Before the case-ending ओस्, ए is substituted for the final of a Nominal-stem. As रामे + ओस् = रामयोः Now, we have to form the Genitive plural:—राम + आम्. Here comes the next Sûtra.

pk: 208. The augnent nuw is aded berore the Genitive Plural ending, arter stens ending in a short vowel, arter stens caled nadî (i. 4. 3 &c), and arter the stens ending in the reninine aril ap as rana + n + an at this stage aplies the nelt sûtra.
ck: 208. the auknent nut is atet perore the kenitive plural entink, arter stens entink in a short votel, arter stens calet natî (i. 4. 3 &c), ant arter the stens entink in the reninine aril ap as rana + n + an at this stake aplies the nelt sûtra.
s: 208. The augment नुट् is added before the Genitive Plural ending, after stems ending in a short vowel, after stems called Nadî (I. 4. 3 &c), and after the stems ending in the Feminine affix आप् As राम + न् + आम् At this stage applies the next Sûtra.

pk: 209. The long vowel is substituted ror the rinal or the sten berore the Genitive Plural aril ‹?› (having the augnent nuw). Thus rana + nan = rananan The sutra ‹?› (Vi. 3. 102. s. 202) would also have caused lengthening and being a subsequent one would also have aplied, yet it does not aply here, because or the Paribhasha sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya "(That which is taught in) a rule (the aplication or) which is ocasioned by the conbination (or two things), does not becone the cause or the destruction or that (conbination). But the very ract that this sûtra is enunciated here debars the above Paribhasha. now, we have to rorn the Locative singular ; ‹?› so also ranayo The plural wil be ‹?› (Vi. 3. 103. s 205.) at this stage aplies the rolowing sutra.
ck: 209. the lonk votel is supstitutet ror the rinal or the sten perore the kenitive plural aril ‹?› (havink the auknent nut). thus rana + nan = rananan the sutra ‹?› (Vi. 3. 102. s. 202) toult also have causet lenkthenink ant peink a supsetuent one toult also have apliet, yet it toes not aply here, pecause or the pariphasha sanipatalaksano vitiraninitan tatvikatasya "(that thich is taukht in) a rule (the aplication or) thich is ocasionet py the conpination (or to thinks), toes not pecone the cause or the testruction or that (conpination). put the very ract that this sûtra is enunciatet here tepars the apove pariphasha. not, te have to rorn the Locative sinkular ; ‹?› so also ranayo the plural til pe ‹?› (Vi. 3. 103. s 205.) at this stake aplies the rolotink sutra.
s: 209. The long vowel is substituted for the final of the stem before the Genitive Plural affix ‹?› (having the augment नुट्). Thus राम + नाम् = रामाणाम् The sutra ‹?› (VII. 3. 102. S. 202) would also have caused lengthening and being a subsequent one would also have applied, yet it does not apply here, because of the Paribhasha संनिपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य "(That which is taught in) a rule (the application of) which is occasioned by the combination (of two things), does not become the cause of the destruction of that (combination).' But the very fact that this sûtra is enunciated here debars the above Paribhasha. Now, we have to form the Locative Singular ; ‹?› So also रामयोः The plural will be ‹?› (VII. 3. 103. S 205.) At this stage applies the following sutra.

pk: 212. sa is substituted ror that which is a substitute (or the sa or a rot in Dhatupatha by Vi. 1. 64. s. 264), or which is (the portion or) an aril, under the above nentioned conditions (Vi. 3. 57, 58. s. 21, 424), or being preceded by an in vowel or a gutural. The word cerebral is understod here ron Vi. 3. 5, as wel as sa ron Vi. 3. 56. Thererore, the sa is replaced by sa both being Vivrita and aghosha. Thus ranesu Why do we say when preceded by in vowel or kavarga? Observe ranasya Why do we say a substitute sa or that which is an aril? Observe ‹?›; the sa here is part or the Churadi rot pisa "to go," and is neither a substituted sa nor the sa or an aril. Why do we say not rinal in a Pada? Observe haristatra sinilarly should be declined krsna, nukunda and al other words ending in a DECLEnsiOn Or rana non. singular rana Dual ranO Plural rana Voc. singular he rana ! Dual he ranO ! Plural he rana ! ac. singular ranan Dual ranO Plural ranan ins. singular ranena Dual ranaByan Plural ranE Dative. singular ranaya Dual ranaByan Plural raneBya abl. singular ranat Dual ranaByan Plural raneBya Gen. singular ranasya Dual ranayo Plural rananan Loc. singular rane Dual ranayo Plural ranesu DECLEnsiOn Or PnOnOuns.
ck: 212. sa is supstitutet ror that thich is a supstitute (or the sa or a rot in thatupatha py Vi. 1. 64. s. 264), or thich is (the portion or) an aril, unter the apove nentionet contitions (Vi. 3. 57, 58. s. 21, 424), or peink precetet py an in votel or a kutural. the tort cerepral is unterstot here ron Vi. 3. 5, as tel as sa ron Vi. 3. 56. thererore, the sa is replacet py sa poth peink Vivrita ant akhosha. thus ranesu thy to te say then precetet py in votel or kavarka? Opserve ranasya thy to te say a supstitute sa or that thich is an aril? Opserve ‹?›; the sa here is part or the churati rot pisa "to ko," ant is neither a supstitutet sa nor the sa or an aril. thy to te say not rinal in a pata? Opserve haristatra sinilarly shoult pe teclinet krsna, nukunta ant al other torts entink in a tEcLEnsiOn Or rana non. sinkular rana tual ranO plural rana Voc. sinkular he rana ! tual he ranO ! plural he rana ! ac. sinkular ranan tual ranO plural ranan ins. sinkular ranena tual ranapyan plural ranE tative. sinkular ranaya tual ranapyan plural ranepya apl. sinkular ranat tual ranapyan plural ranepya ken. sinkular ranasya tual ranayo plural rananan Loc. sinkular rane tual ranayo plural ranesu tEcLEnsiOn Or pnOnOuns.
s: 212. ष is substituted for that which is a substitute (of the ष of a root in Dhatupatha by VI. 1. 64. S. 2264), or which is (the portion of) an affix, under the above mentioned conditions (VIII. 3. 57, 58. S. 211, 424), of being preceded by an इण् vowel or a guttural. The word cerebral is understood here from VIII. 3. 55, as well as स from VIII. 3. 56. Therefore, the स is replaced by ष both being Vivrita and Aghosha. Thus रामेषु Why do we say 'when preceded by इण् vowel or कवर्ग'? Observe रामस्य Why do we say 'a substitute स or that which is an affix'? Observe ‹?›; the स here is part of the Churadi root पिस "to go," and is neither a substituted स nor the स of an affix. Why do we say 'not final in a Pada'? Observe हरिस्तत्र Similarly should be declined कृष्ण, मुकुन्द and all other words ending in अ DECLENSION OF राम Nom. Singular रामः Dual रामौ Plural रामाः Voc. Singular हे राम ! Dual हे रामौ ! Plural हे रामाः ! Acc. Singular रामम् Dual रामौ Plural रामान् Ins. Singular रामेण Dual रामाभ्याम् Plural रामैः Dative. Singular रामाय Dual रामाभ्याम् Plural रामेभ्यः Abl. Singular रामात् Dual रामाभ्याम् Plural रामेभ्यः Gen. Singular रामस्य Dual रामयोः Plural रामाणाम् Loc. Singular रामे Dual रामयोः Plural रामेषु DECLENSION OF PRONOUNS.

pk: 213. The words sarva, al, and the rest are caled sarvanâna or pronouns. The words ending in sarva &c. are also sarvanâna. This we inrer ron the sûtra dvandve ca i. 1. 31. s. 24 which prohibits the aplication or the tern sarvanâna to Dvandva conpounds. (That is in al other conpounds elcept Dvandva, the words ending in sarva &c. are sarvanânas. ror sone other elceptions se i. 1. 29. and 30. s. 2 and 23.) Thererore, we have the rorn ‹?› with the aril ‹?› (V. 3. 10 s. 1957.) The word ‹?› ending in sarva gets the nane or sarvanâna and thererore the aril tral is aded to it. sinilarly paranaBavatkan. ere the aril akac is aded by V. 3. 71 s. 2020.
ck: 213. the torts sarva, al, ant the rest are calet sarvanâna or pronouns. the torts entink in sarva &c. are also sarvanâna. this te inrer ron the sûtra tvantve ca i. 1. 31. s. 24 thich prohipits the aplication or the tern sarvanâna to tvantva conpounts. (that is in al other conpounts elcept tvantva, the torts entink in sarva &c. are sarvanânas. ror sone other elceptions se i. 1. 29. ant 30. s. 2 ant 23.) thererore, te have the rorn ‹?› tith the aril ‹?› (V. 3. 10 s. 1957.) the tort ‹?› entink in sarva kets the nane or sarvanâna ant thererore the aril tral is atet to it. sinilarly paranapavatkan. ere the aril akac is atet py V. 3. 71 s. 2020.
s: 213. The words sarva, 'all,' and the rest are called sarvanâma or pronouns. The words ending in sarva &c. are also sarvanâma. This we infer from the Sûtra द्वन्द्वे च I. 1. 31. S. 224 which prohibits the application of the term Sarvanâma to Dvandva compounds. (That is in all other compounds except Dvandva, the words ending in Sarva &c. are sarvanâmas. For some other exceptions see I. 1. 29. and 30. S. 222 and 223.) Therefore, we have the form ‹?› with the affix ‹?› (V. 3. 10 S. 1957.) The word ‹?› ending in sarva gets the name of sarvanâma and therefore the affix tral is added to it. Similarly परमभवत्कान्. Here the affix अकच् is added by V. 3. 71 S. 2020.

pk: 214. arter a prononinal sten ending in a, si (i) is substituted ror the noninative plural (jas). The substitute is long ror the sake or the subsequent sûtra Vi. 1. 19, s. 310 which gives in the dual the rorns like ‹?›. in the case or sarva and words ending in a, it naters litle whether the substitute be short or long ror their sandhi wil always result in e. The substitute si consists or nore than one leter nanely or s and i, and thererore it replaces the whole or the sthani jas (i. 1. 5 s. 45). it is not like the substitute ‹?› &c. or the sûtra Vi. 4. 127. s. 364 which replaces the rinal or ‹?› &c., ror ‹?› is an aril or which ‹?› is an anubandha, and the rolowing Paribhasha aplies to it. Paribhâshâ:—(That which, when destitute or anubandhas, consists or only one leter, nust) not (be considered) to contain nore leters than one when (one or nore) anubandhas are atached to it. But si like qatara and qatana is not put down as an aril in Paninis Granar and thererore their initials sa and qa are not anubandhas. ror the sûtras i. 3. 7 and 8 s. 189 and 195 are aplicable only to Pratyayas. But si is nowhere originaly taught as a Pratyaya. it becones a Pratyaya only then when it replaces the whole or jas and berore such substitution si not being a pratyaya the sa canot be caled it; when it is substituted ror the whole or jas then it becones a pratyaya and then its sa becones an anubandha. note:—The opinion or sekhara is that si is sit ron its very begining because it is liable to elision (lasakvatadDite) and so the whole aril jas is replaced because the substitute is sit Thus sarva + jas = sarva + i = sarve.
ck: 214. arter a prononinal sten entink in a, si (i) is supstitutet ror the noninative plural (cas). the supstitute is lonk ror the sake or the supsetuent sûtra Vi. 1. 19, s. 310 thich kives in the tual the rorns like ‹?›. in the case or sarva ant torts entink in a, it naters litle thether the supstitute pe short or lonk ror their santhi til altays result in e. the supstitute si consists or nore than one leter nanely or s ant i, ant thererore it replaces the thole or the sthani cas (i. 1. 5 s. 45). it is not like the supstitute ‹?› &c. or the sûtra Vi. 4. 127. s. 364 thich replaces the rinal or ‹?› &c., ror ‹?› is an aril or thich ‹?› is an anupantha, ant the rolotink pariphasha aplies to it. pariphâshâ:—(that thich, then testitute or anupanthas, consists or only one leter, nust) not (pe consiteret) to contain nore leters than one then (one or nore) anupanthas are atachet to it. put si like tatara ant tatana is not put totn as an aril in paninis kranar ant thererore their initials sa ant ta are not anupanthas. ror the sûtras i. 3. 7 ant 8 s. 189 ant 195 are aplicaple only to pratyayas. put si is nothere orikinaly taukht as a pratyaya. it pecones a pratyaya only then then it replaces the thole or cas ant perore such supstitution si not peink a pratyaya the sa canot pe calet it; then it is supstitutet ror the thole or cas then it pecones a pratyaya ant then its sa pecones an anupantha. note:—the opinion or sekhara is that si is sit ron its very pekinink pecause it is liaple to elision (lasakvatatite) ant so the thole aril cas is replacet pecause the supstitute is sit thus sarva + cas = sarva + i = sarve.
s: 214. After a pronominal stem ending in अ, शी (ई) is substituted for the nominative plural (जस्). The substitute is long for the sake of the subsequent sûtra VII. 1. 19, S. 310 which gives in the dual the forms like ‹?›. In the case of सर्व and words ending in अ, it matters little whether the substitute be short or long for their sandhi will always result in ए. The substitute शी consists of more than one letter namely of श् and ई, and therefore it replaces the whole of the Sthani जस् (I. 1. 55 S. 45). It is not like the substitute ‹?› &c. of the Sûtra VI. 4. 127. S. 364 which replaces the final of ‹?› &c., for ‹?› is an affix of which ‹?› is an anubandha, and the following Paribhasha applies to it. Paribhâshâ:—(That which, when destitute of Anubandhas, consists of only one letter, must) not (be considered) to contain more letters than one when (one or more) Anubandhas are attached to it. But शी like डतर and डतम is not put down as an affix in Panini's Grammar and therefore their initials श and ड are not Anubandhas. For the Sûtras I. 3. 7 and 8 S. 189 and 195 are applicable only to Pratyayas. But शी is nowhere originally taught as a Pratyaya. It becomes a Pratyaya only then when it replaces the whole of जस् and before such substitution शी not being a pratyaya the श cannot be called इत्; when it is substituted for the whole of जस् then it becomes a pratyaya and then its श becomes an Anubandha. Note:—The opinion of Sekhara is that शी is शित् from its very beginning because it is liable to elision (लशक्वतद्धिते) and so the whole affix जस् is replaced because the substitute is शित् Thus सर्व + जस् = सर्व + ई = सर्वे.

pk: 215. arter a Prononinal sten ending in a, snE is substituted ror the ne or the Dative. Thus sarvasnE
ck: 215. arter a prononinal sten entink in a, snE is supstitutet ror the ne or the tative. thus sarvasnE
s: 215. After a Pronominal stem ending in अ, स्मै is substituted for the ङे of the Dative. Thus सर्वस्मै

pk: 216. arter a Prononinal sten ending in a there is substituted snat ror the ablative ending nasi and snin ror the Locative ending ni Thus sarvasnat
ck: 216. arter a prononinal sten entink in a there is supstitutet snat ror the aplative entink nasi ant snin ror the Locative entink ni thus sarvasnat
s: 216. After a Pronominal stem ending in अ there is substituted स्मात् for the Ablative ending ङसि and स्मिन् for the Locative ending ङि Thus सर्वस्मात्

pk: 217. arter a Prononinal sten ending in a or a, the aril an or the Genitive Plural gets the augnent suw at the begining. The word at or the last sûtra is understod here. Thus sarvesan. (The a is changed to e by Vi. 3. 103. s. 205 and the s is changed to sa) sarvasnin. The rest or the declension or sarva is like rana. note :— But Bavatan or Bavat The an or the sûtra is the Genitive Plural ending an, and not the an or the Locative singular ordained by Vi. 3. 16 s. 270 ; ror that an, takes the augnents aw, yaw or syaw (Vi. 3. 12-14), while the present takes suw. nor the an or the Perect Tense (i. 1. 35 &c.), because that rerers to verb and not to sarvanâna; nor the an or V. 4. 1., ror the sane reason. The word ani is elhibited in the sûtra in the locative case ror the sake or the subsequent sûtra Vi. 1. 53. ror the purposes or the present sûtra, it should be construed, as ir it was in the Genitive case ( ana sarvanana suw ), because sarvanana being in the ablative case, the augnent wil be aded at the begining or the aril rolowing it, on the nalin adyantO wakitO Other sarvanânas ending in a as visva &c., are sinilarly declined. s: 217. After a Pronominal stem ending in अ or आ, the affix आम् of the Genitive Plural gets the augment सुट् at the beginning. The word आत् of the last sûtra is understood here. Thus सर्वेषाम्. (The अ is changed to ए by VII. 3. 103. S. 205 and the स् is changed to ष) सर्वस्मिन्. The rest of the declension of सर्व is like राम. Note :— But भवताम् of भवत् The आम् of the sûtra is the Genitive Plural ending आम्, and not the आम् of the Locative Singular ordained by VII. 3. 116 S. 270 ; for that आम्, takes the augments आट्, याट् or स्याट् (VII. 3. 112-114), while the present takes सुट्. Nor the आम् of the Perfect Tense (III. 1. 35 &c.), because that refers to verb and not to Sarvanâma; nor the आम् of V. 4. 11., for the same reason. The word आमि is exhibited in the sûtra in the locative case for the sake of the subsequent sûtra VII. 1. 53. For the purposes of the present sûtra, it should be construed, as if it was in the Genitive case ( आमः सर्वनाम्नः सुट् ), because सर्वनाम्नः being in the Ablative case, the augment will be added at the beginning of the affix following it, on the maxim आद्यन्तौ टकितौ Other Sarvanâmas ending in अ as विश्व &c., are similarly declined. The Sarvanâmas are thirty-five in number, namely:— 1 सर्व 'all,' 2 विश्व 'all,' 3 उभ 'two,' 4 उभय 'both,' words formed by the affix 5 डतर such as कतर 'which of two,' words formed by the affix 6 डतम as कतम 'which of many,' 7 अन्य 'other,' 8 अन्यतर 'either,' 9 इतर 'other,' 10 त्वत् 'other,' 11 त्व 'other,' 12 नेम 'half,' 13 सम 'all,' 14 सिम 'whole.' So also 15 पूर्व 'east,' 'prior,' 16 पर 'subsequent,' 17 अवर 'west or posterior,' 18 दक्षिण 'south or right,' 19 उत्तर 'north or inferior,' 'subsequent,' 20 अपर 'other or inferior,' 21 अधर 'west or inferior,' are sarvanâmas when they imply a relation in time or place, as shown above, and not when they are names. So also 22 स्व when it does not mean 'a kinsman or a treasure,' but means 'own.' So also 23 अन्तर when it means 'outer,' or 'an under or lower garment' is a sarvanâma. 24 त्यद् 'he, she, it,' 25 तद् 'he, she, it,' 26 यद् 'who,' 27 एतद् 'this,' 28 इदम् 'it,' 29 अदस् 'that,' 30 एक 'one,' 31 द्वि 'two,' 32 युष्मद् 'you,' 33 अस्मद् 'I,' 34 भवत् 'you,' 35 किम् 'what.' The word उभ 'both' is always used in the dual number; as, उभौ The object of its being inserted in the list of pronominals, (whilst its declension does not differ from that of राम), is its taking the augment अकच् (V. 3. 71. S. 2026) which it could not have taken, if it were not a pronominal; as उभकौ Q. But, could not the same purpose have been served by adding the affix क by sûtra V. 3. 70. S. 2025? Ans. No. For, the affix अकच् being added before the final vowel of उभ leaves the उभ always a dual word on the maxim तन्मध्यपतितस्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यते i. e. “(Any term) that may be employed (in Grammar), denotes (not merely what is actually denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-form may result when) something (is) inserted in that (which is actually denoted by it).” Therefore, अकच् being inserted in उभ does not change its character of always being in the dual, while क being added to it would have destroyed that character. Had it lost its character of being always a dual, then in the case of affix अयच्, it would have required the insertion of अयच् by sûtra V. 2. 44. S. 1845 as it takes it before the affixes त्रल् and तसिल् in उभयतः उभयत्र Therefore Katyayana has said :— Vartika :—The word उभ is used in other places where the sense of dual is not necessary. According to Kaiyata, उभय has no dual number; but according to Haradatta it has. Therefore, before the affix जस् (Nom. Pl.), the substitute अयच् (V. 2. 44. S. 1845) being considered as स्थानिवत् to तयप् which it replaces, the word उभय is considered as ending in तयप् and therefore it would have been optionally a sarvanâma by the sûtra I. 1. 33. S. 226. But the affix अयच् being added irrespective of any विभक्ति is an antaranga rule and therefore, it makes उभय always and not optionally a sarvanâma. Thus उभये, but n

The words purva prior, para arter, avara posterior, dakshina south, utara north, apara other, and adhara inrerior, when they discrininate relative position, not when they are apelatives, are optionaly sarvanâna, berore the aril jas. These seven words have already ben nentioned in the list or sarvananas. They are always sarvanānas, when they have the neaning given to then in the list, i. e., when they inply a relation in tine and space, but when used in any other sense than vyavastha or the riled linit with regards to their own neaning, linit in tine and space, they are not sarvanānas, nor are they so when they are used as apelatives (Thus, when the word daksina neans clever, it is not a sarvanana, as, daksina gayaka clever ninstrels, sinilarly in utara kurava the northern Kurus the word utara is not a prononinal, ror though it declares a direction, it is a Proper noun (like northnen). When these seven words are sarvanâna, they are declined like sarva, elcept in the noninative plural when they nay be declined either as sarvananas, or as ordinary nouns. The option alowed in the case or these words is a prâpta-vibhâshâ.

s: 218. The words purva 'prior,' para 'after,' avara 'posterior,' dakshina 'south,' uttara 'north,' apara 'other,' and adhara 'inferior,' when they discriminate relative position, not when they are appellatives, are optionally sarvanâma, before the affix jas. These seven words have already been mentioned in the list of Sarvanamas. They are always sarvanāmas, when they have the meaning given to them in the list, i. e., when they imply a relation in time and space, but when used in any other sense than vyavastha or the fixed limit with regards to their own meaning, limit in time and space, they are not sarvanāmas, nor are they so when they are used as appellatives (Thus, when the word दक्षिण means 'clever,' it is not a Sarvanama, as, दक्षिणा गायकाः 'clever minstrels,' similarly in उत्तराः कुरवः 'the Northern Kurus' the word उत्तर is not a pronominal, for though it declares a direction, it is a Proper Noun (like Northmen). When these seven words are sarvanâma, they are declined like sarva, except in the nominative plural when they may be declined either as sarvanamas, or as ordinary nouns. The option allowed in the case of these words is a prâpta-vibhâshâ.

Thus sve putra or sva putra ones own sons sve gava or sva gava ones own cows. But when it neans kinsnen or articles or property sva alone is the non. pl. as, sva jnatayo these kinsnen praButa sva

s: 219. The word sva 'own,' when it does not mean a kinsman or property, is optionally a sarvanáma, before the affix जस्. The word स्व when it does not mean a ज्ञाति 'kinsman' or धन 'property' or 'wealth' is always a sarvanāma, in every number and case, as it has been enumerated among the pronominals, except in the nominative plural where it is optionally so. Thus स्वे पुत्राः or स्वाः पुत्राः 'one's own sons' स्वे गावः or स्वा गावः 'one's own cows'. But when it means 'kinsmen' or 'articles of property' स्वाः alone is the nom. pl. pk: 20. The word antara being always a sarvanana, when neaning "outer" or "a lower garnent," is optionaly so berore the aril jas. The word antara when it neans bahiryoga, vis., outer is always sarvanana, so also, when it neans upasanvyana or a lower garnent. Thus antare grha or antara grha outer houses, the residence or Chandal, and other low castes. so antare or antara sawaka the iner garnents, such as peticoats worn under the uper garnents. The word antara when used in the above sense is always sarvanana, but in the noninative plural, it is optionaly so. But, when it is not used in the above senses, it is never a sarvanāna, e. g. granayorantare vasati he lives betwen the two vilages, where the regular locative is antare

s: 220. The word antara being always a sarvanama, when meaning "outer" or "a lower garment," is optionally so before the affix जस्. The word अन्तर when it means बहिर्योग, viz., 'outer' is always sarvanama, so also, when it means उपसंव्यान or 'a lower garment.' Thus अन्तरे गृहाः or अन्तरा गृहाः 'outer houses, the residence of Chandal, and other low castes.' So अन्तरे or अन्तराः शाटकाः 'the inner garments, such as petticoats worn under the upper garments.' The word अन्तर when used in the above sense is always sarvanama, but in the nominative plural, it is optionally so. But, when it is not used in the above senses, it is never a sarvanāma, e. g. ग्रामयोरन्तरे वसति 'he lives between the two villages,' where the regular locative is अन्तरे

s: 221. स्मात् and स्मिन् are optionally substituted for the Ablative and Locative endings, after पूर्व and the eight that follow it. s: 222. The words sarva &c. are not Sarvanāma when they are intended to be employed in a Bahuvrîhi compound. Thus त्वत्कः पिता यस्य त्वत्कपितृकः Similarly, मत्कः पिता यस्य — मत्कपितृकः Here the affix अकच् is added by sutra V. 3. 71 S. 2026 in the sense of contempt or unknown relationship. Here before the taking place of the compound, the name of the sarvanāma is prohibited with regard to the words त्वत्कम् and मत्कम्, otherwise, in ordinary language, the word अकच् would have been used, as it is employed, in the above analytical stage. This अकच् would have been retained even in the compound, as it is retained in the compound अतिभवकान् whose analysis is अतिक्रान्तो भवन्तम्. But the word त्वत् and मत् not being treated as a sarvanama take only the ordinary affix क (V. 3. 70 S. 2025) and not the affix अकच्. Had they been treated as sarvanāma then अकच् would have been inserted before ‹?› by V. 3. 71 S. 2026 giving the forms त्वकत् and मकत् and these forms would have been retained in the compound. But Patanjali has given the forms त्वकत्पितृकः and मकत्पितृकः and has shown the futility of having made this Sūtra at all. According to his opinion, this Sūtra is unnecessary. Therefore, according to the maxim, when the three sages differ, the opinion of the last one is authoritative, we should follow the opinion of Patanjali in this matter. Vartika :— The words सर्व &c. when employed as proper names (संज्ञा) or as a secondary member of a compound (उपसर्जन) are not to be declined as sarvanâma. This we infer by Panini's using such a big word as Sarvanâma, instead of making a short technical name like टि &c. Therefore सर्व &c. are Sarvanamas when they have the meaning of "all &c." as given above in the list, because only those words have been included in the list which have the appropriate meaning of "all" &c, and not words which denote something else, though their form may be "sarva &c." Because in the list such words are only included which have the attributes of the thing defined. Therefore, the rules applicable to these words by the fact of being called sarvanâma or the rules applicable to portions of them by the fact of their being enumerated in this list do not apply. Thus the rules VII. 1. 25. S. 315, VII. 2. 102. S. 265 and VII. 2. 106. S. 381. are rules of an अन्तर्गणकार्य, that is rules which have taken up particular portions of words given in this list. These rules do not apply to words when they are used as संज्ञा and उपसर्जन. Therefore if सर्व be the name of a person, the dative will be सर्वाय, as सर्वाय देहि "give to the person called Sarva." Here the dative is not सर्वस्मै. Similarly when these words are so compounded with others as to lose their original independent character, namely when they are उपसर्जन, they are not treated as sarvanâma, but follow the regular declension, as अतिसर्वाय देहि "give to (him who is) Above-all." Similarly अतिकतरम्. Here there is not the substitution of अद् as required by sûtra VII. 1. 25. S. 315. For कतर would have formed कतरत्, but अतिकतर does not form अतिकतरत् but अतिकतरम् because here कतर is an उपसर्जन and therefore अन्तर्गणकार्य rule VII. 1. 25 S. 315 does not apply. Similarly अतित्यम्. Here VII. 2. 102 S. 265 requiring the substitution of अ for the final of त्यद् and the rule VII. 2. 106. S. 381 requiring the substitution of त् for the non-final do not apply. For though the ordinary form of Nominative Singular of त्यद् is सः, the compound of अति with त्यद् will not be अतिसः in the nominative, but अतितत्.

pk: 23. in the instrunental Deterninative Conpounds the words sarva &c. are not sarvanâna. Thus the word nasapurva is a conpound or nasa and purva — nasenapurva neaning prior by a nonth, where the word nâsa is in the instrunental case. This conpound wil be declined like ordinary words, e. g. its dative wil be nasapurvaya, though the dative or purva, when standing by itselr is purvasnE The sane wil be the case even when there is no conpounding, but the sense is or the instrunental conpound; as nasena purvaya
ck: 23. in the instrunental teterninative conpounts the torts sarva &c. are not sarvanâna. thus the tort nasapurva is a conpount or nasa ant purva — nasenapurva neanink prior py a nonth, there the tort nâsa is in the instrunental case. this conpount til pe teclinet like ortinary torts, e. k. its tative til pe nasapurvaya, thoukh the tative or purva, then stantink py itselr is purvasnE the sane til pe the case even then there is no conpountink, put the sense is or the instrunental conpount; as nasena purvaya
s: 223. In the Instrumental Determinative Compounds the words sarva &c. are not sarvanâma. Thus the word मासपूर्व is a compound of मास and पूर्व — मासेनपूर्व meaning 'prior by a month,' where the word mâsa is in the instrumental case. This compound will be declined like ordinary words, e. g. its dative will be मासपूर्वाय, though the dative of पूर्व, when standing by itself is पूर्वस्मै The same will be the case even when there is no compounding, but the sense is of the Instrumental compound; as मासेन पूर्वाय

pk: 24. and in the Colective Conpound, i. 2. 26 the words sarva etc., are not sarvanâna. Thus ‹?›. This sûtra prohibits the designation sarvanâna with regard to the whole conpound, and not with regard to its various nenbers. The word ‹?› thererore is already a sarvanâna. Then there arises the rolowing diriculty. Why should not ‹?› be aded to ‹?› the rorn ‹?›? We reply, that ‹?› gets ‹?› arter a sarvanâna. ere it is not ordained arter a sarvanâna, but arter a Dvandva conpound which is not a sarvanâna. This prohibition aplies to the conpound as a whole and not to its various nenbers. ir so, why should not the augnent suw cone berore the genitive plural aril (Vi. 1. 52. s. 217) in the case or itara also here, by the rule or tadantaviDi. This is not so because in elplaining that sûtra, we have used the word vihitasya i. e. suw is aded only to that an which is speciricaly ordained arter a sarvanāna and not to every an in general. Thus, the conpound varnasranetara neans, varna the castes, asrana the orders and itara the others. The word itara in this conpound is not to be treated as a sarvanâna, but an ordinary word. Thererore, in the Genitive plural we have varnasranetaranan and not itaresan. so also purvaparanan or the priors and the posteriors.
ck: 24. ant in the colective conpount, i. 2. 26 the torts sarva etc., are not sarvanâna. thus ‹?›. this sûtra prohipits the tesiknation sarvanâna tith rekart to the thole conpount, ant not tith rekart to its various nenpers. the tort ‹?› thererore is alreaty a sarvanâna. then there arises the rolotink tiriculty. thy shoult not ‹?› pe atet to ‹?› the rorn ‹?›? te reply, that ‹?› kets ‹?› arter a sarvanâna. ere it is not ortainet arter a sarvanâna, put arter a tvantva conpount thich is not a sarvanâna. this prohipition aplies to the conpount as a thole ant not to its various nenpers. ir so, thy shoult not the auknent sut cone perore the kenitive plural aril (Vi. 1. 52. s. 217) in the case or itara also here, py the rule or tatantaviti. this is not so pecause in elplainink that sûtra, te have uset the tort vihitasya i. e. sut is atet only to that an thich is speciricaly ortainet arter a sarvanāna ant not to every an in keneral. thus, the conpount varnasranetara neans, varna the castes, asrana the orters ant itara the others. the tort itara in this conpount is not to pe treatet as a sarvanâna, put an ortinary tort. thererore, in the kenitive plural te have varnasranetaranan ant not itaresan. so also purvaparanan or the priors ant the posteriors.
s: 224. And in the Collective Compound, II. 2. 26 the words sarva etc., are not sarvanâma. Thus ‹?›. This sûtra prohibits the designation Sarvanâma with regard to the whole compound, and not with regard to its various members. The word ‹?› therefore is already a Sarvanâma. Then there arises the following difficulty. Why should not ‹?› be added to ‹?› the form ‹?›? We reply, that ‹?› gets ‹?› after a Sarvanâma. Here it is not ordained after a Sarvanâma, but after a Dvandva compound which is not a Sarvanâma. This prohibition applies to the compound as a whole and not to its various members. If so, why should not the augment सुट् come before the genitive plural affix (VII. 1. 52. S. 217) in the case of इतर also here, by the rule of तदन्तविधि. This is not so because in explaining that sûtra, we have used the word विहितस्य i. e. सुट् is added only to that आम् which is specifically ordained after a Sarvanāma and not to every आम् in general. Thus, the compound वर्णाश्रमेतर means, वर्ण 'the castes,' आश्रम 'the orders' and इतर 'the others.' The word इतर in this compound is not to be treated as a sarvanâma, but an ordinary word. Therefore, in the Genitive plural we have वर्णाश्रमेतराणाम् and not इतरेषाम्. So also पूर्वापराणाम् of the priors and the posteriors.

pk: 25. (Their dvandva conpounds) are optionaly sarvanâna, when the noninative plural ternination jas rolows. it declares that berore the ternination jas (which is the ternination or the noninative plural and which in the prononinals is replaced by si), the dvandva conpounds nay be treated either as sarvanānas or as ordinary words. Thus the plural or varnasranetara nay be either varnasranetara or varnasranetare, that is, the word nay take either jas or si. The option alowed in the case or the aplication or the aril jas 1st. pl. to the dvandva conpounds or prononinals, does not eltend to the dvandva conpounds or prononinals which take the aril akac (V. 3. 71). There the sûtra 24 is absolute. Thus, varnasranetaraka. ere akac is not aded but only ka in the plural. This aril (akac) cones berore the last vowel, with what rolows it, or the prononinals and indeclinables.
ck: 25. (their tvantva conpounts) are optionaly sarvanâna, then the noninative plural ternination cas rolots. it teclares that perore the ternination cas (thich is the ternination or the noninative plural ant thich in the prononinals is replacet py si), the tvantva conpounts nay pe treatet either as sarvanānas or as ortinary torts. thus the plural or varnasranetara nay pe either varnasranetara or varnasranetare, that is, the tort nay take either cas or si. the option alotet in the case or the aplication or the aril cas 1st. pl. to the tvantva conpounts or prononinals, toes not eltent to the tvantva conpounts or prononinals thich take the aril akac (V. 3. 71). there the sûtra 24 is apsolute. thus, varnasranetaraka. ere akac is not atet put only ka in the plural. this aril (akac) cones perore the last votel, tith that rolots it, or the prononinals ant inteclinaples.
s: 225. (Their dvandva compounds) are optionally sarvanâma, when the nominative plural termination jas follows. It declares that before the termination जस् (which is the termination of the nominative plural and which in the pronominals is replaced by शी), the dvandva compounds may be treated either as sarvanāmas or as ordinary words. Thus the plural of वर्णाश्रमेतर may be either वर्णाश्रमेतराः or वर्णाश्रमेतरे, that is, the word may take either जस् or शी. The option allowed in the case of the application of the affix जस् 1st. pl. to the dvandva compounds of pronominals, does not extend to the dvandva compounds of pronominals which take the affix अकच् (V. 3. 71). There the sûtra 224 is absolute. Thus, वर्णाश्रमेतरकाः. Here अकच् is not added but only क in the plural. This affix (अकच्) comes before the last vowel, with what follows it, of the pronominals and indeclinables.

pk: 26. and also the words prathana rirst; charana last, as wel as words ending with the aril taya (V. 2. 42); alpa rew, ardha halr, katipaya sone, and nena halr are optionaly sarvanâna, berore the non. pl. ternination. Thus we have praTane or praTana, carane or carana, alpe or alpa, arDe or arDa, katipaye or katipaya, dvitaye or dvitaya, nene or nena The words "optionaly when the aril jas rolows" are understod in this sûtra. By the word taya in the aphorisn, is neant words ending in the aril tayap. The rest are prâtipadikas or crude bases. The word nena has already ben enunerated anong the prononinals, thererore, the option in its case, is what is caled prâpta-vibhâshâ, the result or which wil be that though in the non. pl. it nay be declined like rana the rest or its declension is like sarva, while in the case or prathana &c., the non. pl. nay be like sarva, but the rest or their declension nust be like that or rana. The word ubhaya, has ben rorned by the adition or the aril ayac, and it is already enunerated in the list or prononinals, thererore, by the present sûtra, its non. pl. adnits or two rorns. The aplication or the aril kan or akach nust depend upon the nature or these words, ir prononinals, then akach, otherwise kan. Vârt:— The words rorned by the aril tiya such as, dvitiya and trtiya are optionaly declined as sarvanâna berore the case-ariles having an indicatory na (nit), which are the singular terninations or dative, ablative, genitive and locative, as, dvitiyasnE or dvitiyaya, trtiyasnE or trtiyaya. Paribhâshâ.— (a conbination or leters capable or) elpresing a neaning (denotes), whenever it is enployed (in Granar, that conbination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neaning, but it) does not denote (the sane conbination or leters) void or a neaning. Thererore pawujatiyaya and not pawujatiyasnE. ere the aril is jatiya and not tiya, and in the aril, the portion tiya has no independent neaning or its own. ere ends the declension or sarvanânans. non.
