ck: 26. ant also the torts prathana rirst; charana last, as tel as torts entink tith the aril taya (V. 2. 42); alpa ret, artha halr, katipaya sone, ant nena halr are optionaly sarvanâna, perore the non. pl. ternination. thus te have pratane or pratana, carane or carana, alpe or alpa, arte or arta, katipaye or katipaya, tvitaye or tvitaya, nene or nena the torts "optionaly then the aril cas rolots" are unterstot in this sûtra. py the tort taya in the aphorisn, is neant torts entink in the aril tayap. the rest are prâtipatikas or crute pases. the tort nena has alreaty pen enuneratet anonk the prononinals, thererore, the option in its case, is that is calet prâpta-viphâshâ, the result or thich til pe that thoukh in the non. pl. it nay pe teclinet like rana the rest or its teclension is like sarva, thile in the case or prathana &c., the non. pl. nay pe like sarva, put the rest or their teclension nust pe like that or rana. the tort uphaya, has pen rornet py the atition or the aril ayac, ant it is alreaty enuneratet in the list or prononinals, thererore, py the present sûtra, its non. pl. atnits or to rorns. the aplication or the aril kan or akach nust tepent upon the nature or these torts, ir prononinals, then akach, othertise kan. Vârt:— the torts rornet py the aril tiya such as, tvitiya ant trtiya are optionaly teclinet as sarvanâna perore the case-ariles havink an inticatory na (nit), thich are the sinkular terninations or tative, aplative, kenitive ant locative, as, tvitiyasnE or tvitiyaya, trtiyasnE or trtiyaya. pariphâshâ.— (a conpination or leters capaple or) elpresink a neanink (tenotes), thenever it is enployet (in kranar, that conpination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neanink, put it) toes not tenote (the sane conpination or leters) voit or a neanink. thererore patucatiyaya ant not patucatiyasnE. ere the aril is catiya ant not tiya, ant in the aril, the portion tiya has no intepentent neanink or its otn. ere ents the teclension or sarvanânans. non. Voca. ac. instr. tati. apla. keni. s: 226. And also the words prathama 'first'; charama 'last,' as well as words ending with the affix taya (V. 2. 42); alpa 'few', ardha 'half', katipaya 'some,' and nema 'half' are optionally sarvanâma, before the nom. pl. termination. Thus we have प्रथमे or प्रथमाः, चरमे or चरमाः, अल्पे or अल्पाः, अर्धे or अर्धाः, कतिपये or कतिपयाः, द्वितये or द्वितयाः, नेमे or नेमाः The words "optionally when the affix जस् follows" are understood in this sûtra. By the word तय in the aphorism, is meant words ending in the affix तयप्. The rest are prâtipadikas or crude bases. The word नेम has already been enumerated among the pronominals, therefore, the option in its case, is what is called prâpta-vibhâshâ, the result of which will be that though in the nom. pl. it may be declined like राम the rest of its declension is like sarva, while in the case of prathama &c., the nom. pl. may be like sarva, but the rest of their declension must be like that of राम. The word ubhaya, has been formed by the addition of the affix अयच्, and it is already enumerated in the list of pronominals, therefore, by the present sûtra, its nom. pl. admits of two forms. The application of the affix kan or akach must depend upon the nature of these words, if pronominals, then akach, otherwise kan. Vârt:— The words formed by the affix तीय such as, द्वितीय and तृतीय are optionally declined as sarvanâma before the case-affixes having an indicatory ङ (ङित्), which are the singular terminations of dative, ablative, genitive and locative, as, द्वितीयस्मै or द्वितीयाय, तृतीयस्मै or तृतीयाय. Paribhâshâ.— (A combination of letters capable of) expressing a meaning (denotes), whenever it is employed (in Grammar, that combination of letters in so far as it possesses that meaning, but it) does not denote (the same combination of letters) void of a meaning. Therefore पटुजातीयाय and not पटुजातीयस्मै. Here the affix is जातीय and not तीय, and in the affix, the portion तीय has no independent meaning of its own. Here ends the declension of Sarvanâmans. Nom. pk: 27. jaras nay be substituted ror jara, optionaly berore a case-aril begining with a vowel. By the Paribhasha—(a word or base which ocurs in a rule) in which (the tern) pada or anga is valid, (denotes) both that (word or base by itselr) and (it denotes) also (any word or base) which ends with that (word or base). The substitute jaras wil cone in the case or nirjara also. The substitute jaras consists or nore than one leter and thererore by sûtra i. 1. 5. s. 45, should it not replace the whole or it? no, because or the rolowing Paribhasha;—substitutes take the place or that (or or part or that) which (in a rule) is actualy enunciated. Thererore jaras wil replace the jara portion or nirjara and not the whole. But the rule is "jara is replaced by jaras". There is no jara with long a in nirjara, then why should there be any substitution? But this substitution takes place acording to the Paribhasha:—That which has undergone a change in regard to one or its parts, is by no neans (in consequence or this change) sonething else (than what it was berore the change had taken place). Thererore jara or nirjara is considered the sane as nirjara Thus nirjara + O = nirjaras + O = nirjarasO. The plural wil be nirjarasa The instrunental singular wil be rorned by a as nirjarasa. The substitute vibhakti ending ina or at is debared by jaras and does not take place in the case or nirjara. Thus nirjarasa; nirjarase &c. in the other alternative and also berore the case ariles begining with consonants, the declension or nirjara wil be like rana acording to the Vritikara the ariles ina and at wil cone by the rule or purva-vipratishedha, prohibition in anticipation; and as the sanipatapariBasa is not or universal aplication, the instrunental and ablative singular rorns wil be nirjarasena and nirjarasat and not nirjarasa and nirjarasa. put this supstitution takes place acortink to the pariphasha:—that thich has unterkone a chanke in rekart to one or its parts, is py no neans (in consetuence or this chanke) sonethink else (than that it tas perore the chanke hat taken place). thererore cara or nircara is consiteret the sane as nircara thus nircara + O = nircaras + O = nircarasO. the plural til pe nircarasa the instrunental sinkular til pe rornet py a as nircarasa. the supstitute viphakti entink ina or at is teparet py caras ant toes not take place in the case or nircara. thus nircarasa; nircarase &c. in the other alternative ant also perore the case ariles pekinink tith consonants, the teclension or nircara til pe like rana acortink to the Vritikara the ariles ina ant at til cone py the rule or purva-vipratishetha, prohipition in anticipation; ant as the sanipataparipasa is not or universal aplication, the instrunental ant aplative sinkular rorns til pe nircarasena ant nircarasat ant not nircarasa ant nircarasa. the instrunental plural til pe nircarasE those tho rolot this opinion nake the kenitive sinkular nircarasya put al this is akainst the opinion or the phashyakara. nircara non. sink. nircara tual nircarasO pl. nircarasa Voca. sink. nircara tual nircarasO pl. nircarasa ac. sink. nircarasan tual nircarasO pl. nircarasa instr. sink. nircarasa tual nircarapyan pl. nircarE tati. sink. nircarase tual nircarapyan pl. nircarepya apla. sink. nircarasa tual nircarapyan pl. nircarepya keni. sink. nircarasa tual nircaraso pl. nircarasan Locative sink. nircarasi tual nircaraso pl. nircaresu OptiOnaL rOns sink. nircara nircara nircaran nircarena nircaraya nircarat nir
s: 227. जरस् may be substituted for जरा, optionally before a case-affix beginning with a vowel. By the Paribhasha—(A word or base which occurs in a rule) in which (the term) पद or अङ्ग is valid, (denotes) both that (word or base by itself) and (it denotes) also (any word or base) which ends with that (word or base). The substitute जरस् will come in the case of निर्जर also. The substitute जरस् consists of more than one letter and therefore by sûtra I. 1. 55. S. 45, should it not replace the whole of it? No, because of the following Paribhasha;—Substitutes take the place of that (or of part of that) which (in a rule) is actually enunciated. Therefore जरस् will replace the जरा portion of निर्जर and not the whole. But the rule is "जरा is replaced by जरस्". There is no जरा with long आ in निर्जर, then why should there be any substitution? But this substitution takes place according to the Paribhasha:—That which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means (in consequence of this change) something else (than what it was before the change had taken place). Therefore जर of निर्जर is considered the same as निर्जरा Thus निर्जर + औ = निर्जरस् + औ = निर्जरसौ. The plural will be निर्जरसः The Instrumental singular will be formed by आ as निर्जरसा. The substitute vibhakti ending इन or आत् is debarred by जरस् and does not take place in the case of निर्जर. Thus निर्जरसा; निर्जरसे &c. In the other alternative and also before the case affixes beginning with consonants, the declension of निर्जर will be like राम According to the Vrittikara the affixes इन and आत् will come by the rule of purva-vipratishedha, prohibition in anticipation; and as the सन्निपातपरिभाषा is not of universal application, the Instrumental and Ablative singular forms will be निर्जरसेन and निर्जरसात् and not निर्जरसा and निर्जरसः. The Instrumental Plural will be निर्जरसैः Those who follow this opinion make the Genitive singular निर्जरस्य But all this is against the opinion of the Bhashyakara. निर्जर Nom. pk: 28. in the weak cases (begining with the acusative plural) the rolowing stens are optionaly substituted :— pad ror pada, dat ror danta, nas ror nasika, nas ror nasa, hrd ror hrdaya, nis ror nisa, asan ror asrj, yusan ror yusa, dosan ror dos, yakan ror yakrt, sakan ror sakrt, udan ror udaka and asan ror asya The Kasika gives asan as the substitute ror asana. This is a nistake. Thus pada, padO, pada, padan, padO, pada or padan, pada or padena &c.
ck: 28. in the teak cases (pekinink tith the acusative plural) the rolotink stens are optionaly supstitutet :— pat ror pata, tat ror tanta, nas ror nasika, nas ror nasa, hrt ror hrtaya, nis ror nisa, asan ror asrc, yusan ror yusa, tosan ror tos, yakan ror yakrt, sakan ror sakrt, utan ror utaka ant asan ror asya the kasika kives asan as the supstitute ror asana. this is a nistake. thus pata, patO, pata, patan, patO, pata or patan, pata or patena &c.
s: 228. In the weak cases (beginning with the accusative plural) the following stems are optionally substituted :— पद् for पाद, दत् for दन्त, नस् for नासिका, मास् for मास, हृद् for हृदय, निश् for निशा, असन् for असृज्, यूषन् for यूष, दोषन् for दोस्, यकन् for यकृत्, शकन् for शकृत्, उदन् for उदक and आसन् for आस्य The Kasika gives आसन् as the substitute for आसन. This is a mistake. Thus पादः, पादौ, पादाः, पादम्, पादौ, पदः or पादान्, पदा or पादेन &c.

pk: 230. When the ariles begining with ‹?› (iV. 1. 2) and ending in kap (V. 4. 151.) rolow, not being sarvanânasthâna (i. 1. 43) then that which precedes is caled pada.
ck: 230. then the ariles pekinink tith ‹?› (iV. 1. 2) ant entink in kap (V. 4. 151.) rolot, not peink sarvanânasthâna (i. 1. 43) then that thich precetes is calet pata.
s: 230. When the affixes beginning with ‹?› (IV. 1. 2) and ending in कप् (V. 4. 151.) follow, not being Sarvanâmasthâna (I. 1. 43) then that which precedes is called pada.

pk: 231. and when an aril, with an initial y or an initial vowel, being one or the ariles, begining with ‹?› and ending in ‹?›, rolows, not being sarvanânasthâna, then what precedes, is caled Bha.
ck: 231. ant then an aril, tith an initial y or an initial votel, peink one or the ariles, pekinink tith ‹?› ant entink in ‹?›, rolots, not peink sarvanânasthâna, then that precetes, is calet pha.
s: 231. And when an affix, with an initial य् or an initial vowel, being one of the affixes, beginning with ‹?› and ending in ‹?›, follows, not being Sarvanâmasthâna, then what precedes, is called Bha.

pk: 232. ron this sûtra up to the aphorisn Kadârâh Karnadhâraye (i. 2. 38 s. 751.) only one nane or each thing naned is to be understod. note.—What is that nane then? That which cones last, where the clains are otherwise equal (i. 4. 2. s. 175) and that which, were its clains disalowed, would have no other oportunity or conducing to any result, would be the recognised nane. as a short vowel is caled light by i. 4. 10, s. 31 and it is also caled heavy when it precedes a conjunct consonant (i. 4. 1, s. 32). Thus a short vowel has two nanes light and heavy. But it wil not be caled light when it precedes a conjunct consonant, but wil have only one nane i. e., heavy. Thus in Bid to divide to split, the i is light while the sane leter is heavy in siksa teaching Biksa beging. Thus in the rot ‹?› the ‹?› is heavy and thererore in rorning its aorist we have the rorn atataksat. sinilarly araraksat. The rule Vi. 4. 98 not aplying here, as that rule is aplicable to laghu vowels only. Thererore, in the ariles begining with the acusative Plural and whose initial leter is a vowel, the preceding sten gets the nane or bha only and not that or pada. The result or which is that the hard consonants are not changed into sort. Thus the acusative Plural or ‹?› is pada. The instrunental singular is pada. The ‹?› is not changed to ‹?› by the rule. But berore the ariles begining with consonants, the preceding sten gets the nane or Pada and we have the sortening or the consonants, as padByan &c. sinilarly ac. Pl. nasa, ins. sg. nasa. Berore the aril Byan the sa or nas wil be changed to which wil be changed to a which being elided, we have the rorns naByan, naBi
ck: 232. ron this sûtra up to the aphorisn katârâh karnathâraye (i. 2. 38 s. 751.) only one nane or each think nanet is to pe unterstot. note.—that is that nane then? that thich cones last, there the clains are othertise etual (i. 4. 2. s. 175) ant that thich, tere its clains tisalotet, toult have no other oportunity or contucink to any result, toult pe the recokniset nane. as a short votel is calet likht py i. 4. 10, s. 31 ant it is also calet heavy then it precetes a concunct consonant (i. 4. 1, s. 32). thus a short votel has to nanes likht ant heavy. put it til not pe calet likht then it precetes a concunct consonant, put til have only one nane i. e., heavy. thus in pit to tivite to split, the i is likht thile the sane leter is heavy in siksa teachink piksa pekink. thus in the rot ‹?› the ‹?› is heavy ant thererore in rornink its aorist te have the rorn atataksat. sinilarly araraksat. the rule Vi. 4. 98 not aplyink here, as that rule is aplicaple to lakhu votels only. thererore, in the ariles pekinink tith the acusative plural ant those initial leter is a votel, the precetink sten kets the nane or pha only ant not that or pata. the result or thich is that the hart consonants are not chanket into sort. thus the acusative plural or ‹?› is pata. the instrunental sinkular is pata. the ‹?› is not chanket to ‹?› py the rule. put perore the ariles pekinink tith consonants, the precetink sten kets the nane or pata ant te have the sortenink or the consonants, as patpyan &c. sinilarly ac. pl. nasa, ins. sk. nasa. perore the aril pyan the sa or nas til pe chanket to thich til pe chanket to a thich peink elitet, te have the rorns napyan, napi
s: 232. From this sûtra up to the aphorism Kadârâh Karmadhâraye (II. 2. 38 S. 751.) only one name of each thing named is to be understood. Note.—What is that name then? That which comes last, where the claims are otherwise equal (I. 4. 2. S. 175) and that which, were its claims disallowed, would have no other opportunity of conducing to any result, would be the recognised name. As a short vowel is called 'light' by I. 4. 10, S. 31 and it is also called 'heavy' when it precedes a conjunct consonant (I. 4. 11, S. 32). Thus a short vowel has two names 'light' and 'heavy.' But it will not be called 'light' when it precedes a conjunct consonant, but will have only one name i. e., 'heavy.' Thus in भिद् to divide to split, the इ is 'light' while the same letter is 'heavy' in शिक्ष teaching भिक्ष begging. Thus in the root ‹?› the ‹?› is 'heavy' and therefore in forming its aorist we have the form अततक्षत्. Similarly अररक्षत्. The rule VII. 4. 98 not applying here, as that rule is applicable to laghu vowels only. Therefore, in the affixes beginning with the Accusative Plural and whose initial letter is a vowel, the preceding stem gets the name of bha only and not that of pada. The result of which is that the hard consonants are not changed into soft. Thus the accusative Plural of ‹?› is पदः. The Instrumental singular is पदा. The ‹?› is not changed to ‹?› by the rule. But before the affixes beginning with consonants, the preceding stem gets the name of Pada and we have the softening of the consonants, as पद्भ्याम् &c. Similarly Ac. Pl. मासः, Ins. Sg. मासा. Before the affix भ्याम् the स of मास् will be changed to which will be changed to a which being elided, we have the forms माभ्याम्, माभिः

pk: 234. Or a Bha sten ending in an the a is elided.
ck: 234. Or a pha sten entink in an the a is elitet.
s: 234. Of a Bha stem ending in अन् the अ is elided.

pk: 235. arter r and sa, the n is the substitute or n, when they ocur as conponent leters or the sane word. Thererore the ac. Pl or yusan is rorned by eliding the a and changing the n into n; as yusna; ins. sg. yusna ir we aply the rule or sTanivadBava by sūtra aca parasnin purvaviDO (i. 1. 57 s. 50), and this we can do by elplaining the conpound purva-vidhau purvasnad vidhau neaning "when a rule is to be aplied on acount or or arter sonething which precedes the substitute" and consider the lopa to be sTanivad to a, in that case also the na wil be changed to na by the rule Vi. 4. 2 s. 197, i. e. na is changed to na even when a vowel intervenes. But as a nater or ract, the lopadesa is not sTanivat acording to the rolowing vartika. Vartika:—in the last thre chapters or the 8th Bok or Paninis ashtadhyayi, the rule or sTanivat wil not aply.
ck: 235. arter r ant sa, the n is the supstitute or n, then they ocur as conponent leters or the sane tort. thererore the ac. pl or yusan is rornet py elitink the a ant chankink the n into n; as yusna; ins. sk. yusna ir te aply the rule or stanivatpava py sūtra aca parasnin purvavitO (i. 1. 57 s. 50), ant this te can to py elplainink the conpount purva-vithau purvasnat vithau neanink "then a rule is to pe apliet on acount or or arter sonethink thich precetes the supstitute" ant consiter the lopa to pe stanivat to a, in that case also the na til pe chanket to na py the rule Vi. 4. 2 s. 197, i. e. na is chanket to na even then a votel intervenes. put as a nater or ract, the lopatesa is not stanivat acortink to the rolotink vartika. Vartika:—in the last thre chapters or the 8th pok or paninis ashtathyayi, the rule or stanivat til not aply.
s: 235. After र् and ष, the ण् is the substitute of न्, when they occur as component letters of the same word. Therefore the Ac. Pl of यूषन् is formed by eliding the अ and changing the न् into ण्; as यूष्णः; Ins. Sg. यूष्णा If we apply the rule of स्थानिवद्भाव by sūtra अचः परस्मिन् पूर्वविधौ (I. 1. 57 S. 50), and this we can do by explaining the compound purva-vidhau purvasmad vidhau meaning "when a rule is to be applied on account of or after something which precedes the substitute" and consider the लोप to be स्थानिवद् to अ, in that case also the न will be changed to ण by the rule VIII. 4. 2 S. 197, i. e. न is changed to ण even when a vowel intervenes. But as a matter of fact, the लोपादेश is not स्थानिवत् according to the following vartika. Vartika:—In the last three chapters of the 8th Book of Panini's Ashtadhyayi, the rule of स्थानिवत् will not apply.

pk: 236. The na at the end or a noninal-sten, which is a Pada (i. 4. 17 s. 230.), is elided. The words na and pratipadika in the telt are to be taken in the genitive case; the sign or the genitive being elided here. The elision or na by this sutra being considered asidha ror the purposes or the aplication or the previous sutras, there is not the lengthening or sūtra Vi. 3. 102 s. 202. or the e substitution or Vi. 3. 103. s. 205. or the Es substitution or Vi. 1. 9. s 203. Thererore the rorns are yusaByan and not yusaByan; yusaBi and not yusE; yusaBya and not yuseBya
ck: 236. the na at the ent or a noninal-sten, thich is a pata (i. 4. 17 s. 230.), is elitet. the torts na ant pratipatika in the telt are to pe taken in the kenitive case; the sikn or the kenitive peink elitet here. the elision or na py this sutra peink consiteret asitha ror the purposes or the aplication or the previous sutras, there is not the lenkthenink or sūtra Vi. 3. 102 s. 202. or the e supstitution or Vi. 3. 103. s. 205. or the Es supstitution or Vi. 1. 9. s 203. thererore the rorns are yusapyan ant not yusapyan; yusapi ant not yusE; yusapya ant not yusepya
s: 236. The न at the end of a Nominal-stem, which is a Pada (I. 4. 17 S. 230.), is elided. The words न and प्रातिपदिक in the text are to be taken in the genitive case; the sign of the genitive being elided here. The elision of न by this Sutra being considered asiddha for the purposes of the application of the previous Sutras, there is not the lengthening of sūtra VII. 3. 102 S. 202. or the ए substitution of VII. 3. 103. S. 205. or the ऐस् substitution of VII. 1. 9. S 203. Therefore the forms are यूषभ्याम् and not यूषाभ्याम्; यूषभिः and not यूषैः; यूषभ्यः and not यूषेभ्यः

pk: 237. in a Bha-sten ending in an, the a is optionaly elided berore the Locative ending ni and berore the ending si (i) or the noninative and acusative Dual neuter. as yusni or yusani. in al other cases the word yusan is declined like rana. The word qisyo is a conpound or ni and si and not ‹?› ror the sten is not Bha there. The word padDan in the sūtra Vi. 1. 63 s 28 is used in the sense or prakara i.e. the ariles therein taught are ilustrative only the substitution wil take place even when a sarvananasthana aril rolows. Thererore, where the dual aril O is replaced by si, and it is a sarvananasthāna aril there also that rule Vi. 1. 63 aplies, ror we have in the Bhasya the elanple or kakuBosni. sinilarly also the rolowing are valid :—"padanostriyan" here pad is changed berore the non. sg which is not a weak aril "svantan hrnanasan nana" here hrdaya is changed to hrd in the non. sg. These are ron anara Kosha. and asan yat "They (the Devas) said to the Prana in the nouth" (Brihadaranyaka i. 3. 7) ere asya is changed to asan berore the aril yat asan neans that which is born in the nouth. The word dosan (hand) is used in the neuter gender in the Bhasya or Patanjali. Thererore the rolowing usage is corect :—‹?›, it is also nasculine gender because it is used along with Bujabahu praganqado now, we take up the declension or the word ahan :—
ck: 237. in a pha-sten entink in an, the a is optionaly elitet perore the Locative entink ni ant perore the entink si (i) or the noninative ant acusative tual neuter. as yusni or yusani. in al other cases the tort yusan is teclinet like rana. the tort tisyo is a conpount or ni ant si ant not ‹?› ror the sten is not pha there. the tort patan in the sūtra Vi. 1. 63 s 28 is uset in the sense or prakara i.e. the ariles therein taukht are ilustrative only the supstitution til take place even then a sarvananasthana aril rolots. thererore, there the tual aril O is replacet py si, ant it is a sarvananasthāna aril there also that rule Vi. 1. 63 aplies, ror te have in the phasya the elanple or kakuposni. sinilarly also the rolotink are valit :—"patanostriyan" here pat is chanket perore the non. sk thich is not a teak aril "svantan hrnanasan nana" here hrtaya is chanket to hrt in the non. sk. these are ron anara kosha. ant asan yat "they (the tevas) sait to the prana in the nouth" (prihataranyaka i. 3. 7) ere asya is chanket to asan perore the aril yat asan neans that thich is porn in the nouth. the tort tosan (hant) is uset in the neuter kenter in the phasya or patancali. thererore the rolotink usake is corect :—‹?›, it is also nasculine kenter pecause it is uset alonk tith pucapahu prakantato not, te take up the teclension or the tort ahan :—
s: 237. In a Bha-stem ending in अन्, the अ is optionally elided before the Locative ending ङि and before the ending शी (ई) of the Nominative and Accusative Dual Neuter. As यूष्णि or यूषणि. In all other cases the word यूषन् is declined like राम. The word डिश्योः is a compound of ङि and शी and not ‹?› for the stem is not Bha there. The word पद्धन् in the sūtra VI. 1. 63 S 228 is used in the sense of प्रकार i.e. the affixes therein taught are illustrative only the substitution will take place even when a Sarvanamasthana affix follows. Therefore, where the dual affix औ is replaced by शी, and it is a Sarvanamasthāna affix there also that rule VI. 1. 63 applies, for we have in the Bhasya the example of ककुभोष्णी. Similarly also the following are valid :—"पद्दन्नोऽस्त्रियां" here पद् is changed before the Nom. Sg which is not a weak affix "स्वान्तं हृन्मानसं मम" here हृदय is changed to हृद् in the Nom. Sg. These are from Amara Kosha. and आसन् यत् "They (the Devas) said to the Prana in the mouth" (Brihadaranyaka I. 3. 7) Here आस्य is changed to आसन् before the affix यत् आसन् means that which is born in the mouth. The word दोषन् (hand) is used in the neuter gender in the Bhasya of Patanjali. Therefore the following usage is correct :—‹?›, it is also masculine gender because it is used along with भुजबाहू प्रगण्डदोः Now, we take up the declension of the word अहन् :—

pk: 239. The substitution or a long vowel honogeneous with the rirst, does not take place when a long vowel is rolowed by a noninative or acusative case-aril begining with a vowel (other than ic) or by the non. Pl. aril as The long vowel required by Vi. 1. 102, s. 164. does not take place in the case or words ending in long vowels. Thus noninative singular or visvapa is visvapa; non. Dual visvapa + O = visvapO by the general rule or Vridhi and non. Pl. is visvapa by lengthening the honogeneous leters a and a. in the declension or visvapa the above rorns are regularly obtained. in the case or non. Dual, the lengthening required by Vi. 1. 102. s. 164. is debared by Vi. 1. 104 s. 165 as wel. in the case or non. Pl. visvapa + as (Os) there wil be no harn ir Vi. 1. 102 s. 164 be aplied, ror even that rule wil give the rorn visvapa. Thererore in the case or visvapa the present sutra is not absolutely necesary. But we have given it here ror the sake or logical consistency, ror this sutra aplies to stens ending in long vowels like gOri, the non. Dual and Pl. or which wil be gOryO and gOrya respectively.
ck: 239. the supstitution or a lonk votel honokeneous tith the rirst, toes not take place then a lonk votel is rolotet py a noninative or acusative case-aril pekinink tith a votel (other than ic) or py the non. pl. aril as the lonk votel retuiret py Vi. 1. 102, s. 164. toes not take place in the case or torts entink in lonk votels. thus noninative sinkular or visvapa is visvapa; non. tual visvapa + O = visvapO py the keneral rule or Vrithi ant non. pl. is visvapa py lenkthenink the honokeneous leters a ant a. in the teclension or visvapa the apove rorns are rekularly optainet. in the case or non. tual, the lenkthenink retuiret py Vi. 1. 102. s. 164. is teparet py Vi. 1. 104 s. 165 as tel. in the case or non. pl. visvapa + as (Os) there til pe no harn ir Vi. 1. 102 s. 164 pe apliet, ror even that rule til kive the rorn visvapa. thererore in the case or visvapa the present sutra is not apsolutely necesary. put te have kiven it here ror the sake or lokical consistency, ror this sutra aplies to stens entink in lonk votels like kOri, the non. tual ant pl. or thich til pe kOryO ant kOrya respectively.
s: 239. The substitution of a long vowel homogeneous with the first, does not take place when a long vowel is followed by a nominative or accusative case-affix beginning with a vowel (other than इच्) or by the Nom. Pl. affix अस् The long vowel required by VI. 1. 102, S. 164. does not take place in the case of words ending in long vowels. Thus Nominative Singular of विश्वपा is विश्वपाः; Nom. Dual विश्वपा + औ = विश्वपौ by the general rule of Vriddhi and Nom. Pl. is विश्वपाः by lengthening the homogeneous letters अ and आ. In the declension of विश्वपा the above forms are regularly obtained. In the case of Nom. Dual, the lengthening required by VI. 1. 102. S. 164. is debarred by VI. 1. 104 S. 165 as well. In the case of Nom. Pl. विश्वपा + अस् (औस्) there will be no harm if VI. 1. 102 S. 164 be applied, for even that rule will give the form विश्वपाः. Therefore in the case of विश्वपा the present Sutra is not absolutely necessary. But we have given it here for the sake of logical consistency, for this Sutra applies to stems ending in long vowels like गौरी, the Nom. Dual and Pl. of which will be गौर्यौ and गौर्यः respectively.

pk: 240. The rinal a or a Bha sten, when it ends in a rot, is elided. The lopa wil be or the rinal vowel by i. 1. 52 s. 42. Thererore acu. Pl. wil be visvapa; inst. sing. visvapa, visvapaByan &c. Like visvapa should be declined sanKaDna &c. Why do we say the a or a rot? Observe hahan (the acusative Pl. or haha). its instr. sing. wil be haha + wa = haha by lengthening or honogeneous vowels. its Dat. sing. wil be haha + ne = hahE by Vridhi. its abl. and Geni. sing. wil be haha + nasi or nas = haha by lengthening. its Gen. and Loc. dual wil be haha + os = hahO by Vridhi. its Loc. sing. wil be haha + ni by guna. The rest are like visvapa. By the rule or yoga vibhaga (yogaviBagadiswasidDi) i.e. "ron a rule which we have obtained by taking part or a rule as a separate rule, we nay derive such results as nay be desirable," the present sutra nay be divided into two sutras e.g. (1) ata, the rinal a or a Bha sten is always elided; (2) ato Dato, the rinal a or a Bha sten when it ends in a rot is always elided. Thus are rorned ktva and sna the Genitive singulars or Ktvā and Ś्nā. ror Panini hinselr has declined ktva and sna by the elision or a, se Vi. 1. 37. s. 32 (sanaselanapurvektvo lyap) and i. 1. 83. s. 257. (hala sna sanaJO) ere ends the declension or words ending in long a. visvapa non. Voc. ac. ins. Dat. abl. Gen. Loc. singular visvapa he visvapa visvapan visvapa visvape visvapa visvapa visvapi Dual visvapO he visvapO visvapO visvapaByan visvapaByan visvapaByan visvapo visvapo Plural visvapa he visvapa visvapa visvapaBi visvapaBya visvapaBya visvapan visvapasu haha singular haha he haha hahan haha hahE haha haha hahe Dual hahO he hahO hahO hahaByan hahaByan hahaByan hahO hahO Plural haha he haha hahan hahaBi hahaBya hahaBya hahan hahasu now we take up the declension or the word hari. The non. sing. wil be hari. non. Dual wil be hari + O = hari by lengthening the preceding vowel Vi. 1. 102. s. 164. The Pl. is hari + as ere aplies the rolowing.
ck: 240. the rinal a or a pha sten, then it ents in a rot, is elitet. the lopa til pe or the rinal votel py i. 1. 52 s. 42. thererore acu. pl. til pe visvapa; inst. sink. visvapa, visvapapyan &c. Like visvapa shoult pe teclinet sankatna &c. thy to te say the a or a rot? Opserve hahan (the acusative pl. or haha). its instr. sink. til pe haha + ta = haha py lenkthenink or honokeneous votels. its tat. sink. til pe haha + ne = hahE py Vrithi. its apl. ant keni. sink. til pe haha + nasi or nas = haha py lenkthenink. its ken. ant Loc. tual til pe haha + os = hahO py Vrithi. its Loc. sink. til pe haha + ni py kuna. the rest are like visvapa. py the rule or yoka viphaka (yokavipakatistasiti) i.e. "ron a rule thich te have optainet py takink part or a rule as a separate rule, te nay terive such results as nay pe tesiraple," the present sutra nay pe tivitet into to sutras e.k. (1) ata, the rinal a or a pha sten is altays elitet; (2) ato tato, the rinal a or a pha sten then it ents in a rot is altays elitet. thus are rornet ktva ant sna the kenitive sinkulars or ktvā ant Ś्nā. ror panini hinselr has teclinet ktva ant sna py the elision or a, se Vi. 1. 37. s. 32 (sanaselanapurvektvo lyap) ant i. 1. 83. s. 257. (hala sna sanacO) ere ents the teclension or torts entink in lonk a. visvapa non. Voc. ac. ins. tat. apl. ken. Loc. sinkular visvapa he visvapa visvapan visvapa visvape visvapa visvapa visvapi tual visvapO he visvapO visvapO visvapapyan visvapapyan visvapapyan visvapo visvapo plural visvapa he visvapa visvapa visvapapi visvapapya visvapapya visvapan visvapasu haha sinkular haha he haha hahan haha hahE haha haha hahe tual hahO he hahO hahO hahapyan hahapyan hahapyan hahO hahO plural haha he haha hahan hahapi hahapya hahapya hahan hahasu not te take up the teclension or the tort hari. the non. sink. til pe hari. non. tual til pe hari + O = hari py lenkthenink the precetink votel Vi. 1. 102. s. 164. the pl. is hari + as ere aplies the rolotink.
s: 240. The final आ of a Bha stem, when it ends in a root, is elided. The lopa will be of the final vowel by I. 1. 52 S. 42. Therefore Accu. Pl. will be विश्वपः; Inst. Sing. विश्वपा, विश्वपाभ्याम् &c. Like विश्वपा should be declined शङ्खध्मा &c. Why do we say the आ of a root? Observe हाहान् (the accusative Pl. of हाहा). Its Instr. Sing. will be हाहा + टा = हाहा by lengthening of homogeneous vowels. Its Dat. Sing. will be हाहा + ङे = हाहै by Vriddhi. Its Abl. and Geni. Sing. will be हाहा + ङसि or ङस् = हाहाः by lengthening. Its Gen. and Loc. dual will be हाहा + ओस् = हाहौः by Vriddhi. Its Loc. Sing. will be हाहा + ङि by guna. The rest are like विश्वपा. By the rule of yoga vibhaga (योगविभागादिष्टसिद्धिः) i.e. "From a rule which we have obtained by taking part of a rule as a separate rule, we may derive such results as may be desirable," the present Sutra may be divided into two Sutras e.g. (1) आतः, the final आ of a Bha stem is always elided; (2) आतो धातोः, the final आ of a Bha Stem when it ends in a root is always elided. Thus are formed क्त्वः and श्नः the Genitive Singulars of Ktvā and Ś्nā. For Panini himself has declined क्त्वा and श्ना by the elision of आ, see VII. 1. 37. S. 3332 (समासेलनपूर्वेक्त्वो ल्यप्) and III. 1. 83. S. 2557. (हलः श्नः शानझौ) Here ends the declension of words ending in long आ. विश्वपा Nom. Voc. Acc. Ins. Dat. Abl. Gen. Loc. Singular विश्वपाः हे विश्वपाः विश्वपाम् विश्वपा विश्वपे विश्वपः विश्वपः विश्वपि Dual विश्वपौ हे विश्वपौ विश्वपौ विश्वपाभ्याम् विश्वपाभ्याम् विश्वपाभ्याम् विश्वपोः विश्वपोः Plural विश्वपाः हे विश्वपाः विश्वपः विश्वपाभिः विश्वपाभ्यः विश्वपाभ्यः विश्वपाम् विश्वपासु हाहा Singular हाहाः हे हाहाः हाहाम् हाहा हाहै हाहाः हाहाः हाहे Dual हाहौ हे हाहौ हाहौ हाहाभ्याम् हाहाभ्याम् हाहाभ्याम् हाहौः हाहौः Plural हाहाः हे हाहाः हाहान् हाहाभिः हाहाभ्यः हाहाभ्यः हाहाम् हाहासु Now we take up the declension of the word हरि. The Nom. sing. will be हरिः. Nom. Dual will be हरि + औ = हरी by lengthening the preceding vowel VI. 1. 102. S. 164. The Pl. is हरि + अस् Here applies the following.

pk: 241. Berore the aril as or the non. Pl., guna is substituted ror the rinal short vowel or a noninal sten. Thererore the i or hari is gunated to e. Thus hari + jas = hare + as = haraya. The Vocative sing. wil be hari + su. ere the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 241. perore the aril as or the non. pl., kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal short votel or a noninal sten. thererore the i or hari is kunatet to e. thus hari + cas = hare + as = haraya. the Vocative sink. til pe hari + su. ere the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 241. Before the affix अस् of the Nom. Pl., guna is substituted for the final short vowel of a nominal stem. Therefore the इ of हरि is gunated to ए. Thus हरि + जस् = हरे + अस् = हरयः. The Vocative Sing. will be हरि + सु. Here the following rule applies.

pk: 242. ror short and rinal in a noninal-sten, a guna is substituted in the Vocative singular. Thererore the i or hari is changed to e and the aril su is elided by Vi. 1. 69. s. 193. Thus we get he hare. The ac. rorns are harin, hari, harin. The instr. sing. is hari + wa. ere the rolowing two rules aply.
ck: 242. ror short ant rinal in a noninal-sten, a kuna is supstitutet in the Vocative sinkular. thererore the i or hari is chanket to e ant the aril su is elitet py Vi. 1. 69. s. 193. thus te ket he hare. the ac. rorns are harin, hari, harin. the instr. sink. is hari + ta. ere the rolotink to rules aply.
s: 242. For short and final in a nominal-stem, a guna is substituted in the Vocative Singular. Therefore the इ of हरि is changed to ए and the affix सु is elided by VI. 1. 69. S. 193. Thus we get हे हरे. The Acc. forms are हरिम्, हरी, हरीन्. The Instr. sing. is हरि + टा. Here the following two rules apply.

pk: 243. The rest or the words that end in short i and u are caled ghi with the elception or the word sakhi. Thus hari is a ghi word. Why do we say the rest or the words? Observe nati, ror being a reninine noun does not get the nane or ghi but retains its nane or nadī; ror otherwise its declension wil be nataye, rorned by aplying the rule Vi. 3. 12 s. 268 and Vi. 3. 1 s. 245. But nataye is or course a wrong rorn. Though by the rule i. 4. 1. s. 232 ir the word gets its designation ghi, it can never get the designation nadī and vice versa, and nati which is a nadī word can never be caled ghi, and so even ir the word sesa had not ben used in the sutra, there would not have ben any rear or nati being conrounded with a ghi word, stil sesa is used in the sūtra ror the sake or precision and clearnes. Why do we say short i and u? Observe vataprani. Why do we say with the elception or sakhi? Observe saKa and saKayO. note:—This derines the word ghi. The peculiarity or the declension or ghi words wil be treated later on. The word hrasva is understod in this sutra. The word shesha or the rest inplies the words ending in short i or u which are not the nanes or renales, or ir they are reninine nanes, they are not nadī words. as agni rire. Berore case-ariles having an indicatory n, the ghī nouns gunate their vowel Vi. 3. 1. as agni + ne = agne + e = agnaye "to the rire." so also vayu + ne = vayave "to the wind." But the declension or sakhi in these cases is:—saKya, saKye, saKyu and saKyO.
ck: 243. the rest or the torts that ent in short i ant u are calet khi tith the elception or the tort sakhi. thus hari is a khi tort. thy to te say the rest or the torts? Opserve nati, ror peink a reninine noun toes not ket the nane or khi put retains its nane or natī; ror othertise its teclension til pe nataye, rornet py aplyink the rule Vi. 3. 12 s. 268 ant Vi. 3. 1 s. 245. put nataye is or course a tronk rorn. thoukh py the rule i. 4. 1. s. 232 ir the tort kets its tesiknation khi, it can never ket the tesiknation natī ant vice versa, ant nati thich is a natī tort can never pe calet khi, ant so even ir the tort sesa hat not pen uset in the sutra, there toult not have pen any rear or nati peink conrountet tith a khi tort, stil sesa is uset in the sūtra ror the sake or precision ant clearnes. thy to te say short i ant u? Opserve vataprani. thy to te say tith the elception or sakhi? Opserve saka ant sakayO. note:—this terines the tort khi. the peculiarity or the teclension or khi torts til pe treatet later on. the tort hrasva is unterstot in this sutra. the tort shesha or the rest inplies the torts entink in short i or u thich are not the nanes or renales, or ir they are reninine nanes, they are not natī torts. as akni rire. perore case-ariles havink an inticatory n, the khī nouns kunate their votel Vi. 3. 1. as akni + ne = akne + e = aknaye "to the rire." so also vayu + ne = vayave "to the tint." put the teclension or sakhi in these cases is:—sakya, sakye, sakyu ant sakyO.
s: 243. The rest of the words that end in short इ and उ are called ghi with the exception of the word sakhi. Thus हरि is a ghi word. Why do we say 'the rest of the words'? Observe मति, for being a feminine noun does not get the name of ghi but retains its name of nadī; for otherwise its declension will be मतये, formed by applying the rule VII. 3. 112 S. 268 and VII. 3. 111 S. 245. But मतये is of course a wrong form. Though by the rule I. 4. 1. S. 232 if the word gets its designation ghi, it can never get the designation nadī and vice versa, and मति which is a nadī word can never be called ghi, and so even if the word शेष had not been used in the sutra, there would not have been any fear of मति being confounded with a ghi word, still शेष is used in the sūtra for the sake of precision and clearness. Why do we say short इ and उ? Observe वातप्रमी. Why do we say with the exception of sakhi? Observe सखा and सखायौ. Note:—This defines the word ghi. The peculiarity of the declension of ghi words will be treated later on. The word hrasva is understood in this sutra. The word shesha or 'the rest' implies the words ending in short इ or उ which are not the names of females, or if they are feminine names, they are not nadī words. As अग्नि fire. Before case-affixes having an indicatory ङ्, the ghī nouns gunate their vowel VII. 3. 111. As अग्नि + ङे = अग्ने + ए = अग्नये "to the fire." So also वायु + ङे = वायवे "to the wind." But the declension of sakhi in these cases is:—सख्या, सख्ये, सख्युः and सख्यौ.

pk: 24. na is substituted ror the ending an or the instrunental singular, arter the Ghi stens, when they are not reninine. The word an is the ancient nane or the aril wa. Thus hari + wa = hari + na = harina. Why do we say when they are not reninine? Observe nati + wa = natya.
ck: 24. na is supstitutet ror the entink an or the instrunental sinkular, arter the khi stens, then they are not reninine. the tort an is the ancient nane or the aril ta. thus hari + ta = hari + na = harina. thy to te say then they are not reninine? Opserve nati + ta = natya.
s: 244. ना is substituted for the ending आङ् of the Instrumental singular, after the Ghi stems, when they are not Feminine. The word आङ् is the ancient name of the affix टा. Thus हरि + टा = हरि + ना = हरिणा. Why do we say when they are not feminine? Observe मति + टा = मत्या.

pk: 245. ror the short i and short u or the stens caled Gi (i. 4. 7.) Guna is substituted in the Dative, ablative, Genitive and Locative singular. Why or Gi stens? Observe saKye. Why in the singulars or the Dat., abl., Gen. and Loc. only? Observe hariByan The word case-ending (supi) is understod here also, as the counter-elanples are pawvi &c. The word pawvi is rorned by ading nis to pawu (iV. 1. 4 s. 502). nis is not a case-aril, though it is nit and is aded to pawu which is Gi Thus hari + ne = hare + e = haraye. now we rorn the ablative singular, hari + nasi = hare + as (the i or hari is gunated by the present sutra). at this stage aplies the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 245. ror the short i ant short u or the stens calet ki (i. 4. 7.) kuna is supstitutet in the tative, aplative, kenitive ant Locative sinkular. thy or ki stens? Opserve sakye. thy in the sinkulars or the tat., apl., ken. ant Loc. only? Opserve haripyan the tort case-entink (supi) is unterstot here also, as the counter-elanples are patvi &c. the tort patvi is rornet py atink nis to patu (iV. 1. 4 s. 502). nis is not a case-aril, thoukh it is nit ant is atet to patu thich is ki thus hari + ne = hare + e = haraye. not te rorn the aplative sinkular, hari + nasi = hare + as (the i or hari is kunatet py the present sutra). at this stake aplies the rolotink sûtra.
s: 245. For the short इ and short उ of the stems called घि (I. 4. 7.) Guna is substituted in the Dative, Ablative, Genitive and Locative Singular. Why of घि stems? Observe सख्ये. Why in the Singulars of the Dat., Abl., Gen. and Loc. only? Observe हरिभ्याम् The word case-ending (सुपि) is understood here also, as the counter-examples are पट्वी &c. The word पट्वी is formed by adding ङीष् to पटु (IV. 1. 44 S. 502). ङीष् is not a case-affix, though it is ङित् and is added to पटु which is घि Thus हरि + ङे = हरे + ए = हरये. Now we form the Ablative singular, हरि + ङसि = हरे + अस् (the इ of हरि is gunated by the present Sutra). At this stage applies the following Sûtra.

pk: 246. in the ron or e or o (in the body or a word), + a or the case aril nas or the ablative and Genitive singular, the single substitute is the rorn or the precedent. Thererore hare + as = hare The genitive dual wil be haryo The pl. harinan now, we rorn the Loc. sing. hari + ni = hare + ‹?› (The i is gunated by the preceding sûtra). at this stage aplies the rolowing rule.
ck: 246. in the ron or e or o (in the poty or a tort), + a or the case aril nas or the aplative ant kenitive sinkular, the sinkle supstitute is the rorn or the precetent. thererore hare + as = hare the kenitive tual til pe haryo the pl. harinan not, te rorn the Loc. sink. hari + ni = hare + ‹?› (the i is kunatet py the precetink sûtra). at this stake aplies the rolotink rule.
s: 246. In the room of ए or ओ (in the body of a word), + अ of the case affix ङस् of the Ablative and Genitive Singular, the single substitute is the form of the precedent. Therefore हरे + अस् = हरेः The genitive dual will be हर्योः The pl. हरीणाम् Now, we form the Loc. Sing. हरि + ङि = हरे + ‹?› (The इ is gunated by the preceding sûtra). At this stage applies the following rule.

pk: [s. 247] 247. arter a Ghi (i. 4. 7) sten ending in short i or u, O is substituted ror the ni or the Loc. sg. and a is substituted ror the rinal or such Ghi sten. Thererore hari + ni = hara + O = harO The Loc. du. and pl. wil be haryo and harisu respectively. sripati, agni, ravi, kavi &c. are declined like hari DECLEnsiOn Or hari sing. non. hari, Voc. he hare, ac. harin, ins. harina, Dat. haraye, abl. hare, Gen. hare, Loc. harO Dual. non. hari, Voc. hari, ac. hari, ins. hariByan, Dat. hariByan, abl. hariByan, Gen. haryo, Loc. haryo Plural. non. haraya, Voc. haraya, ac. harin, ins. hariBi, Dat. hariBya, abl. hariBya, Gen. harinan, Loc. harisu now we decline the word saKi There aplies the rolowing rule. [s. 256] 256. arter a sten ending in i or u short, and which is not a nadi or a Ghi, Ot is substituted ror the ni or the Locative singular. as saKyO the rest or the declension or this word is like hari. But the declension or this word, when it rorns the rinal nenber or a conpound, is sonewhat direrent. Thus the word susaKa neaning a god riend, is declined as susaKa, susaKayO, susaKaya. ere the ading or the aril anan (Vi. 1. 93. s. 248) and treating the case ariles as nid as required by Vi. 1. 92. s. 253 are operations which relate to the anga or base and thererore those rules aply not only to the single word saKi but to a conpound word also that ends in saKi. But the conpound word susaKi has not elactly the sane rorn as saKi, thererore the rule i. 4. 7. s. 243 which nakes the speciric nention or the word saKi does not aply to susaKi. Thererore the word susaKi is Gi and its instrunental and Dative wil be susaKina and susaKaye sinilarly in ablative and Genitive singulars the i being gunated by Vi. 3. 1. s. 245 the last rule wil not aply, because here the bases are susaKe + nasi and susaKe + nas. The last and the present rules aply only to that rorn or saKi where the Ki is changed to Ky. in the case or nadi words ‹?› is taught by the previous sûtras; in the case or Gi words Ot preceded by a substitution or ‹?› leters wil be taught in the nelt sutra, so by the rule or elclusion, the present sutra aplies to words other than nadì and ghỉ. Thererore the ablative, Genitive and Locative singular or susaKi wil be susaKe, susaKe and susaKO respectively. sinilarly the conpound word atisaKa neaning one who has thrown away his riend (saKa nasculine) is declined like susaKa But the word paranasaKi when treated as a Bahuvrihi conpound, neaning he whose riend is the suprene
ck: [s. 247] 247. arter a khi (i. 4. 7) sten entink in short i or u, O is supstitutet ror the ni or the Loc. sk. ant a is supstitutet ror the rinal or such khi sten. thererore hari + ni = hara + O = harO the Loc. tu. ant pl. til pe haryo ant harisu respectively. sripati, akni, ravi, kavi &c. are teclinet like hari tEcLEnsiOn Or hari sink. non. hari, Voc. he hare, ac. harin, ins. harina, tat. haraye, apl. hare, ken. hare, Loc. harO tual. non. hari, Voc. hari, ac. hari, ins. haripyan, tat. haripyan, apl. haripyan, ken. haryo, Loc. haryo plural. non. haraya, Voc. haraya, ac. harin, ins. haripi, tat. haripya, apl. haripya, ken. harinan, Loc. harisu not te tecline the tort saki there aplies the rolotink rule. [s. 256] 256. arter a sten entink in i or u short, ant thich is not a nati or a khi, Ot is supstitutet ror the ni or the Locative sinkular. as sakyO the rest or the teclension or this tort is like hari. put the teclension or this tort, then it rorns the rinal nenper or a conpount, is sonethat tirerent. thus the tort susaka neanink a kot rient, is teclinet as susaka, susakayO, susakaya. ere the atink or the aril anan (Vi. 1. 93. s. 248) ant treatink the case ariles as nit as retuiret py Vi. 1. 92. s. 253 are operations thich relate to the anka or pase ant thererore those rules aply not only to the sinkle tort saki put to a conpount tort also that ents in saki. put the conpount tort susaki has not elactly the sane rorn as saki, thererore the rule i. 4. 7. s. 243 thich nakes the speciric nention or the tort saki toes not aply to susaki. thererore the tort susaki is ki ant its instrunental ant tative til pe susakina ant susakaye sinilarly in aplative ant kenitive sinkulars the i peink kunatet py Vi. 3. 1. s. 245 the last rule til not aply, pecause here the pases are susake + nasi ant susake + nas. the last ant the present rules aply only to that rorn or saki there the ki is chanket to ky. in the case or nati torts ‹?› is taukht py the previous sûtras; in the case or ki torts Ot precetet py a supstitution or ‹?› leters til pe taukht in the nelt sutra, so py the rule or elclusion, the present sutra aplies to torts other than natì ant khỉ. thererore the aplative, kenitive ant Locative sinkular or susaki til pe susake, susake ant susakO respectively. sinilarly the conpount tort atisaka neanink one tho has throtn atay his rient (saka nasculine) is teclinet like susaka put the tort paranasaki then treatet as a pahuvrihi conpount, neanink he those rient is the suprene na
s: [S. 247] 247. After a Ghi (I. 4. 7) stem ending in short इ or उ, औ is substituted for the ङि of the Loc. Sg. and अ is substituted for the final of such Ghi stem. Therefore हरि + ङि = हर + औ = हरौ The Loc. du. and pl. will be हर्योः and हरिषु respectively. श्रीपति, अग्नि, रवि, कवि &c. are declined like हरि DECLENSION OF हरि Sing. Nom. हरिः, Voc. हे हरे, Acc. हरिम्, Ins. हरिणा, Dat. हरये, Abl. हरेः, Gen. हरेः, Loc. हरौ Dual. Nom. हरी, Voc. हरी, Acc. हरी, Ins. हरिभ्याम्, Dat. हरिभ्याम्, Abl. हरिभ्याम्, Gen. हर्योः, Loc. हर्योः Plural. Nom. हरयः, Voc. हरयः, Acc. हरीन्, Ins. हरिभिः, Dat. हरिभ्यः, Abl. हरिभ्यः, Gen. हरीणाम्, Loc. हरिषु Now we decline the word सखि There applies the following rule. [S. 256] 256. After a stem ending in इ or उ short, and which is not a Nadi or a Ghi, औत् is substituted for the ङि of the Locative Singular. As सख्यौ the rest of the declension of this word is like हरि. But the declension of this word, when it forms the final member of a compound, is somewhat different. Thus the word सुसखा meaning a good friend, is declined as सुसखा, सुसखायौ, सुसखायः. Here the adding of the affix अनङ् (VII. 1. 93. S. 248) and treating the case affixes as णिद् as required by VII. 1. 92. S. 253 are operations which relate to the अङ्ग or base and therefore those rules apply not only to the single word सखि but to a compound word also that ends in सखि. But the compound word सुसखि has not exactly the same form as सखि, therefore the rule I. 4. 7. S. 243 which makes the specific mention of the word सखि does not apply to सुसखि. Therefore the word सुसखि is घि and its Instrumental and Dative will be सुसखिना and सुसखये Similarly in Ablative and Genitive singulars the इ being gunated by VII. 3. 111. S. 245 the last rule will not apply, because here the bases are सुसखे + ङसि and सुसखे + ङस्. The last and the present rules apply only to that form of सखि where the खि is changed to ख्य्. In the case of नदी words ‹?› is taught by the previous sûtras; in the case of घि words औत् preceded by a substitution of ‹?› letters will be taught in the next sutra, so by the rule of exclusion, the present sutra applies to words other than nadì and ghỉ. Therefore the Ablative, Genitive and Locative Singular of सुसखि will be सुसखेः, सुसखेः and सुसखौ respectively. Similarly the compound word अतिसखा meaning 'one who has thrown away his friend' (सखा masculine) is declined like सुसखा But the word परमसखि when treated as a Bahuvrihi compound, meaning 'he whose friend is the Supreme' may give rise to a difficulty. For, here सखि is merely a secondary word, the real word being the object denoted by the word परमसखि. We therefore cannot treat सखि to be the अङ्ग or base, as we treated it in the case of the word सुसखि. How is this word परमसखि to be declined? It is declined like सुसखा, for though the word सखि here is merely a secondary word and not the base or अङ्ग, yet the rules of अनङ् and णिद्भाव apply to this case also. Thus परमसखा and परमसखायौ &c. Now in the declension of the word अतिसखि when it is a compound meaning 'he who has thrown away his friend' (सखी feminine) the affix टच् does not apply, because the rule which says that the Masculine includes the feminine is not universal. That rule is thus enunciated: प्रातिपदिकग्रहणे लिङ्गविशिष्टस्यापि ग्रहणम् 'A Pratipadika denotes, whenever it is employed (in grammar), also (such a crude form) as is derived from it by the addition of (an affix denoting) gender.' Now applying this Paribhasha to rule V. 4. 91 S. 788 which declares that the affix टच् is added to the words rájan, ahan, and sakhi when at the end of a compound, the Masculine word सखि would include the feminine word सखी also and therefore the form ought to be अतिसखः and not अतिसखिः. This anomaly, however, is prevented by the fact that the above Paribhasha is not universal. The word अतिसखि is declined like हरि and not like the word सखि; and therefore ‹?› do not apply. Because, the word सखी has been shortened to सखि by the rule I. 2. 48, S. 656 and this सखि is,

pk: 248. anan (an) is substituted ror the i or saKi berore su or the noninative singular, (but not in the Vocative singular). Thus saKi + su = saKan + su The anan being a nit augnent, replaces the rinal only, and not the whole (i. 1. 53 s. 43). now aply the rolowing rules.
ck: 248. anan (an) is supstitutet ror the i or saki perore su or the noninative sinkular, (put not in the Vocative sinkular). thus saki + su = sakan + su the anan peink a nit auknent, replaces the rinal only, ant not the thole (i. 1. 53 s. 43). not aply the rolotink rules.
s: 248. अनङ् (अन्) is substituted for the इ of सखि before सु of the Nominative Singular, (but not in the Vocative Singular). Thus सखि + सु = सखन् + सु The अनङ् being a ङित् augment, replaces the final only, and not the whole (I. 1. 53 S. 43). Now apply the following rules.

pk: 249. The leter inediately preceding the last leter or a word is caled the penultinate. Thererore in saKan, the a or Ka is penultinate or upaDa. Being upaDa, the rolowing rule aplies to this a.
ck: 249. the leter inetiately precetink the last leter or a tort is calet the penultinate. thererore in sakan, the a or ka is penultinate or upata. peink upata, the rolotink rule aplies to this a.
s: 249. The letter immediately preceding the last letter of a word is called the penultimate. Therefore in सखन्, the अ of ख is penultimate or उपधा. Being उपधा, the following rule applies to this अ.

pk: 250. in a sten ending in n the preceding vowel is lengthened in strong cases, with the elception or the Vocative singular. Thererore, the a is lengthened and we have saKan + s. now the aril s consists or a single leter and is caled aprkta by the rolowing rule.
ck: 250. in a sten entink in n the precetink votel is lenkthenet in stronk cases, tith the elception or the Vocative sinkular. thererore, the a is lenkthenet ant te have sakan + s. not the aril s consists or a sinkle leter ant is calet aprkta py the rolotink rule.
s: 250. In a stem ending in न् the preceding vowel is lengthened in strong cases, with the exception of the Vocative singular. Therefore, the अ is lengthened and we have सखान् + स्. Now the affix स् consists of a single letter and is called अपृक्त by the following rule.

pk: 252. arter a consonant, there is the elision or the noninative-aril su, and the tense-aril ti and si (when reduced to the rorn or t and s) being consonants; and so also arter the long vowels ni and ap or the reninine (aril ni and ap), there is the elision or the noninative aril su The sutra translated literaly neans — arter a word ending in a consonant, or ni, or ap when a long vowel, the ariles su, ti and si when reduced to a single consonant aril (hal) are elided. But ti and si are elided only arter consonant and hence we have translated it as above. Why do we say "arter a consonant, or a reninine aril ni and ap"? Observe agranani, senani Why do we say "arter a long-voweled reninine aril"? Observe niskOsanbi, atiKawva, where the reninine ariles have ben shortened. Why do we say "when rolowed by ti, and si"? Observe anansit The sip being read along with tip does not include sic, but rerers to sip only. Why do we say when reduced to a single leter? Observe biBarti Why do we say the consonant is elided? Observe biBayancakara ere the aprikta aril a or the Perect is not elided: though it being the substitute or tip is like tip, and ought to have ben elided, had the word hal not ben used in the sutra. Why do we say rirst consonant? Observe raja Why has the elision or s (su), t (tip) and s (sip) ben ordained arter consonants, as they would or thenselves have ben droped by Vi. 2. 23, being the rinals or a conpound consonant? Then the rorns ‹?› could not be evolved. as saKi + su = saKan + s (Vi. 4. 8. s. 250)— and by eliding s by nule Vi. 2. 23, the rorn would have becone saKan and the rinal n could not have ben elided by Vi. 2. 7; ror it is a nalin enunciated in the very opening or the second chapter or the 8th Bok, that in the last thre chapters or that Bok (2nd, 3rd and 4th Chapters), a subsequent rule is as ir it had not taken erect, so rar as any preceding rule is concerned; thererore, the rule Vi. 2. 7 ordaining the elision or n, does not rind scope, since Vi. 2. 23 (ordaining elision or s) is considered as ir it had not taken erect. Thus non. sg. saKa, Voc. sg. he saKe. in rorning the Dual saKi + O the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 252. arter a consonant, there is the elision or the noninative-aril su, ant the tense-aril ti ant si (then retucet to the rorn or t ant s) peink consonants; ant so also arter the lonk votels ni ant ap or the reninine (aril ni ant ap), there is the elision or the noninative aril su the sutra translatet literaly neans — arter a tort entink in a consonant, or ni, or ap then a lonk votel, the ariles su, ti ant si then retucet to a sinkle consonant aril (hal) are elitet. put ti ant si are elitet only arter consonant ant hence te have translatet it as apove. thy to te say "arter a consonant, or a reninine aril ni ant ap"? Opserve akranani, senani thy to te say "arter a lonk-votelet reninine aril"? Opserve niskOsanpi, atikatva, there the reninine ariles have pen shortenet. thy to te say "then rolotet py ti, ant si"? Opserve anansit the sip peink reat alonk tith tip toes not inclute sic, put rerers to sip only. thy to te say then retucet to a sinkle leter? Opserve piparti thy to te say the consonant is elitet? Opserve pipayancakara ere the aprikta aril a or the perect is not elitet: thoukh it peink the supstitute or tip is like tip, ant oukht to have pen elitet, hat the tort hal not pen uset in the sutra. thy to te say rirst consonant? Opserve raca thy has the elision or s (su), t (tip) ant s (sip) pen ortainet arter consonants, as they toult or thenselves have pen tropet py Vi. 2. 23, peink the rinals or a conpount consonant? then the rorns ‹?› coult not pe evolvet. as saki + su = sakan + s (Vi. 4. 8. s. 250)— ant py elitink s py nule Vi. 2. 23, the rorn toult have pecone sakan ant the rinal n coult not have pen elitet py Vi. 2. 7; ror it is a nalin enunciatet in the very openink or the secont chapter or the 8th pok, that in the last thre chapters or that pok (2nt, 3rt ant 4th chapters), a supsetuent rule is as ir it hat not taken erect, so rar as any precetink rule is concernet; thererore, the rule Vi. 2. 7 ortainink the elision or n, toes not rint scope, since Vi. 2. 23 (ortainink elision or s) is consiteret as ir it hat not taken erect. thus non. sk. saka, Voc. sk. he sake. in rornink the tual saki + O the rolotink rules aply.
s: 252. After a consonant, there is the elision of the nominative-affix सु, and the tense-affix ति and सि (when reduced to the form of त् and स्) being consonants; and so also after the long vowels ङी and आप् of the feminine (affix ङी and आप्), there is the elision of the nominative affix सु The sutra translated literally means — After a word ending in a consonant, or ङी, or आप् when a long vowel, the affixes सु, ति and सि when reduced to a single consonant affix (हल्) are elided. But ति and सि are elided only after consonant and hence we have translated it as above. Why do we say "after a consonant, or a feminine affix ङी and आप्"? Observe अग्रामणीः, सेनानीः Why do we say "after a long-vowelled feminine affix"? Observe निष्कौशाम्बिः, अतिखट्वः, where the feminine affixes have been shortened. Why do we say "when followed by ति, and सि"? Observe अनंसीत् The सिप् being read along with तिप् does not include सिच्, but refers to सिप् only. Why do we say 'when reduced to a single letter'? Observe बिभर्ति Why do we say 'the consonant is elided'? Observe बिभयाञ्चकार Here the aprikta affix अ of the Perfect is not elided: though it being the substitute of तिप् is like तिप्, and ought to have been elided, had the word हल् not been used in the sutra. Why do we say 'first consonant'? Observe राजा Why has the elision of स् (सु), त् (तिप्) and स् (सिप्) been ordained after consonants, as they would of themselves have been dropped by VIII. 2. 23, being the finals of a compound consonant? Then the forms ‹?› could not be evolved. As सखि + सु = सखान् + स् (VI. 4. 8. S. 250)— and by eliding स् by Rule VIII. 2. 23, the form would have become सखान् and the final न् could not have been elided by VIII. 2. 7; for it is a maxim enunciated in the very opening of the Second chapter of the 8th Book, that in the last three chapters of that Book (2nd, 3rd and 4th Chapters), a subsequent rule is as if it had not taken effect, so far as any preceding rule is concerned; therefore, the rule VIII. 2. 7 ordaining the elision of न्, does not find scope, since VIII. 2. 23 (ordaining elision of स्) is considered as if it had not taken effect. Thus Nom. Sg. सखा, Voc. Sg. हे सखे. In forming the Dual सखि + औ the following rules apply.

pk: 253. arter saKi, the endings or the strong cases, with the elception or the Vocative singular, are nid That is, they cause Vridhi acording to the rolowing rule :—
ck: 253. arter saki, the entinks or the stronk cases, tith the elception or the Vocative sinkular, are nit that is, they cause Vrithi acortink to the rolotink rule :—
s: 253. After सखि, the endings of the strong cases, with the exception of the Vocative singular, are णिद् That is, they cause Vriddhi according to the following rule :—

pk: 254. Berore the ariles having an indicatory n or n, Vridhi is substituted ror the end-vowel or a sten. Thus saKi + O = saKE + O = saKayO. sinilarly non. Pl. saKaya, ac. sing. saKayan, ac. dual saKayO instrunental sing. wil be rorned by the aril wa and as the word saKi is not a Gi word (se i. 4. 7. s. 243) it does not take na or guna as required by Vi. 3. 120. s. 24 or Vi. 3. 1. s. 245. Thus we have saKi + a = saKya. Dative sing. wil be saKi + ne. in rorning the ablative and Genitive, the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 254. perore the ariles havink an inticatory n or n, Vrithi is supstitutet ror the ent-votel or a sten. thus saki + O = sakE + O = sakayO. sinilarly non. pl. sakaya, ac. sink. sakayan, ac. tual sakayO instrunental sink. til pe rornet py the aril ta ant as the tort saki is not a ki tort (se i. 4. 7. s. 243) it toes not take na or kuna as retuiret py Vi. 3. 120. s. 24 or Vi. 3. 1. s. 245. thus te have saki + a = sakya. tative sink. til pe saki + ne. in rornink the aplative ant kenitive, the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 254. Before the affixes having an indicatory ञ् or ण्, Vriddhi is substituted for the end-vowel of a stem. Thus सखि + औ = सखै + औ = सखायौ. Similarly Nom. Pl. सखायः, Acc. Sing. सखायम्, Acc. dual सखायौ Instrumental Sing. will be formed by the affix टा and as the word सखि is not a घि word (See I. 4. 7. S. 243) it does not take ना or guna as required by VII. 3. 120. S. 244 or VII. 3. 111. S. 245. Thus we have सखि + आ = सख्या. Dative Sing. will be सखि + ङे. In forming the Ablative and Genitive, the following rule applies :—

pk: 25. There is the substitution or u ror a or as or the ablative and Genitive singular, arter saKi and pati, when ror the i or those two stens y is substituted. The phrase nasinaso and ut are understod here also. The Kyatyat neans and includes Ki and ti when the i is changed to ya, and denotes saKi and pati, the i being changed to ya Thus, saKi + as = saKyu as saKyuragacCati, saKyu svan so also patyuragacCati, patyu svan The ilustration or Ki is saKi which is derived ron the Denoninative Verb thus : suKena vartate saKa, saKanicCati = saKa + kyac (i. 1. 8) = saKiya (Vi. 4. 3). now by ading kvip to the Denoninative rot saKiya we get saKi one who wishes ror a riend. The ablative and Genitive singular or this word wil be saKy + as = saKyu also. Or ti we have the rolowing elanple. lunanicCati = luniya, ad kvip = luni, the ablative and Genitive singular or which is also lunyu, the n or luni being the substitute or t or nishtha is considered like ta (Vi. 2. 1). The peculiar elhibition or Kya and tya in the sutra, instead or saying directly saKipatiByan indicates that the rule does not aply to words like atisaKi &c : where we have atisaKe, senapate The word atisaKi is Gi in spite or the prohibition (i. 4. 7), ror that prohibition aplies only to saKi and not to a conpound which ends in it, on the nalin grahanavata pratipadikena tadantaviDirnasti “That which canot posibly be anything but a Pratipadika does (contrary to i. 1. 72) not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itselr”. acording to sone this rule aplies to al Ki and ti, such as suKi one who loves pleasure (suKanicCati = suKiya + kvip), and suti one who wishes a son (sutanicCati = sutiya + kvip). Thus suKyu, sutyu &c.
ck: 25. there is the supstitution or u ror a or as or the aplative ant kenitive sinkular, arter saki ant pati, then ror the i or those to stens y is supstitutet. the phrase nasinaso ant ut are unterstot here also. the kyatyat neans ant inclutes ki ant ti then the i is chanket to ya, ant tenotes saki ant pati, the i peink chanket to ya thus, saki + as = sakyu as sakyurakacati, sakyu svan so also patyurakacati, patyu svan the ilustration or ki is saki thich is terivet ron the tenoninative Verp thus : sukena vartate saka, sakanicati = saka + kyac (i. 1. 8) = sakiya (Vi. 4. 3). not py atink kvip to the tenoninative rot sakiya te ket saki one tho tishes ror a rient. the aplative ant kenitive sinkular or this tort til pe saky + as = sakyu also. Or ti te have the rolotink elanple. lunanicati = luniya, at kvip = luni, the aplative ant kenitive sinkular or thich is also lunyu, the n or luni peink the supstitute or t or nishtha is consiteret like ta (Vi. 2. 1). the peculiar elhipition or kya ant tya in the sutra, insteat or sayink tirectly sakipatipyan inticates that the rule toes not aply to torts like atisaki &c : there te have atisake, senapate the tort atisaki is ki in spite or the prohipition (i. 4. 7), ror that prohipition aplies only to saki ant not to a conpount thich ents in it, on the nalin krahanavata pratipatikena tatantavitirnasti “that thich canot posiply pe anythink put a pratipatika toes (contrary to i. 1. 72) not tenote that thich ents tith it, put it tenotes only itselr”. acortink to sone this rule aplies to al ki ant ti, such as suki one tho loves pleasure (sukanicati = sukiya + kvip), ant suti one tho tishes a son (sutanicati = sutiya + kvip). thus sukyu, sutyu &c.
s: 255. There is the substitution of उ for अ of अस् of the Ablative and Genitive singular, after सखि and पति, when for the इ of those two stems य् is substituted. The phrase ङसिङसोः and उत् are understood here also. The ख्यत्यात् means and includes खि and ति when the इ is changed to य, and denotes सखि and पति, the इ being changed to य Thus, सखि + अस् = सख्युः as सख्युरागच्छति, सख्युः स्वम् So also पत्युरागच्छति, पत्युः स्वम् The illustration of खी is सखी which is derived from the Denominative Verb thus : सुखेन वर्तते सखः, सखमिच्छति = सख + क्यच् (III. 1. 8) = सखीय (VII. 4. 33). Now by adding क्विप् to the Denominative root सखीय we get सखीः 'one who wishes for a friend'. The Ablative and Genitive Singular of this word will be सख्य् + अस् = सख्युः also. Of ती we have the following example. लूनमिच्छति = लूनीय, add क्विप् = लूनी, the Ablative and Genitive singular of which is also लून्युः, the न् of लूनी being the substitute of त् of Nishtha is considered like त (VIII. 2. 1). The peculiar exhibition of ख्य and त्य in the sutra, instead of saying directly सखिपतिभ्याम् indicates that the rule does not apply to words like अतिसखि &c : where we have अतिसखेः, सेनापतेः The word अतिसखि is घि in spite of the prohibition (I. 4. 7), for that prohibition applies only to सखि and not to a compound which ends in it, on the maxim ग्रहणवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्तविधिर्नास्ति “That which cannot possibly be anything but a Pratipadika does (contrary to I. 1. 72) not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itself”. According to some this rule applies to all खी and ती, such as सुखीः 'one who loves pleasure' (सुखमिच्छति = सुखीय + क्विप्), and सुतीः 'one who wishes a son' (सुतमिच्छति = सुतीय + क्विप्). Thus सुख्युः, सुत्युः &c.

pk: 257. The word pati is caled ghi, only when it is in a conpound. The word pati would have ben ghi by the sûtra i. 4. 7. s. 243; the present sûtra is, thererore, a niyana rule, restricting the use or ghi in the case or pati to its ocuring in conposition. The word eva only is used in a restrictive sense. as patya by the lord but Bupatina by the lord or the worlds. so also patye and Bupataye ; patyu and Bupate ; patyO and BupatO &c. When pati is ghi, there is guṇa or the vowel berore the rour nit ariles by Vi. 3. 1. now we take up the declension or the word kati which is always plural. This word is caled sanKya or a nuneral as wel as saw by the rolowing two rules, and thererore, there is sone peculiarity in its declension.
ck: 257. the tort pati is calet khi, only then it is in a conpount. the tort pati toult have pen khi py the sûtra i. 4. 7. s. 243; the present sûtra is, thererore, a niyana rule, restrictink the use or khi in the case or pati to its ocurink in conposition. the tort eva only is uset in a restrictive sense. as patya py the lort put pupatina py the lort or the torlts. so also patye ant pupataye ; patyu ant pupate ; patyO ant pupatO &c. then pati is khi, there is kuṇa or the votel perore the rour nit ariles py Vi. 3. 1. not te take up the teclension or the tort kati thich is altays plural. this tort is calet sankya or a nuneral as tel as sat py the rolotink to rules, ant thererore, there is sone peculiarity in its teclension.
s: 257. The word pati is called ghi, only when it is in a compound. The word pati would have been ghi by the sûtra I. 4. 7. S. 243; the present sûtra is, therefore, a niyama rule, restricting the use of ghi in the case of pati to its occurring in composition. The word eva 'only' is used in a restrictive sense. As पत्या 'by the lord' but भूपतिना 'by the lord of the worlds.' So also पत्ये and भूपतये ; पत्युः and भूपतेः ; पत्यौ and भूपतौ &c. When पति is ghi, there is guṇa of the vowel before the four ङित् affixes by VII. 3. 111. Now we take up the declension of the word कति which is always plural. This word is called संख्या or a numeral as well as षट् by the following two rules, and therefore, there is some peculiarity in its declension.

pk: 258. The words bahu nany, gaṇa clas, and the words ending in the aril vatu (V. 2. 39), and ḍati (V. 2. 41) are caled nunerals (saṅkhyā). The word kati is rorned by the aril qati thererore it is a saṅkhyā.
ck: 258. the torts pahu nany, kaṇa clas, ant the torts entink in the aril vatu (V. 2. 39), ant ḍati (V. 2. 41) are calet nunerals (saṅkhyā). the tort kati is rornet py the aril tati thererore it is a saṅkhyā.
s: 258. The words bahu 'many,' gaṇa 'class,' and the words ending in the affix vatu (V. 2. 39), and ḍati (V. 2. 41) are called numerals (saṅkhyā). The word कति is formed by the affix डति therefore it is a Saṅkhyā.

pk: 259. and the saṅkhyās ending with the aril ḍati are caled shaṭ. Because the word kati is rorned by the aril qati, thererore it is caled saw. The result or being caled saw is that the declensional ariles are elided. The elision or an aril generaly takes place by using one or the thre words as given in the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 259. ant the saṅkhyās entink tith the aril ḍati are calet shaṭ. pecause the tort kati is rornet py the aril tati, thererore it is calet sat. the result or peink calet sat is that the teclensional ariles are elitet. the elision or an aril keneraly takes place py usink one or the thre torts as kiven in the rolotink sûtra.
s: 259. And the saṅkhyās ending with the affix ḍati are called shaṭ. Because the word कति is formed by the affix डति, therefore it is called षट्. The result of being called षट् is that the declensional affixes are elided. The elision of an affix generally takes place by using one of the three words as given in the following Sûtra.

pk: 260. The disapearance or an aril when it is caused by the words luk, ślu or lup are designated by those terns respectively. When an aril is elided by using the tern luk, that disapearance gets the apelation or luk, sinilarly when an aril is elided by using the terns ślu or lup, the disapearance gets the nane or ślu or lup. The noninative and acusative ariles arter the word kati are elided by using the tern luk, as is shown in the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 260. the tisapearance or an aril then it is causet py the torts luk, ślu or lup are tesiknatet py those terns respectively. then an aril is elitet py usink the tern luk, that tisapearance kets the apelation or luk, sinilarly then an aril is elitet py usink the terns ślu or lup, the tisapearance kets the nane or ślu or lup. the noninative ant acusative ariles arter the tort kati are elitet py usink the tern luk, as is shotn in the rolotink sûtra.
s: 260. The disappearance of an affix when it is caused by the words luk, ślu or lup are designated by those terms respectively. When an affix is elided by using the term luk, that disappearance gets the appellation of luk, similarly when an affix is elided by using the terms ślu or lup, the disappearance gets the name of ślu or lup. The nominative and accusative affixes after the word कति are elided by using the term luk, as is shown in the following Sûtra.

pk: 261. The non. and ac. Plural endings are elided arter the nunerals caled saw (i. 1. 24 s. 369). Thererore kati + jas or kati + sas = kati + 0 or kati + 0. now, what is the erect or this sero, does it produce its action on the sten or does it not? naturaly one would have thought, that when an aril is elided, with it nust also vanish al the operations that that aril would have caused on the base. But this is not the case by the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 261. the non. ant ac. plural entinks are elitet arter the nunerals calet sat (i. 1. 24 s. 369). thererore kati + cas or kati + sas = kati + 0 or kati + 0. not, that is the erect or this sero, toes it protuce its action on the sten or toes it not? naturaly one toult have thoukht, that then an aril is elitet, tith it nust also vanish al the operations that that aril toult have causet on the pase. put this is not the case py the rolotink sûtra.
s: 261. The Nom. and Acc. Plural endings are elided after the Numerals called षट् (I. 1. 24 S. 369). Therefore कति + जस् or कति + शस् = कति + ० or कति + ०. Now, what is the effect of this zero, does it produce its action on the stem or does it not? Naturally one would have thought, that when an affix is elided, with it must also vanish all the operations that that affix would have caused on the base. But this is not the case by the following Sûtra.

pk: 263. Or the base (aṅga), whose aril has ben elided by the use or any or the thre words containing lu, the operations dependent on it do not take place, regarding such base. This sûtra is a special elception to the previous aphorisn which was to eltensive. it declares, that when an aril is elided by using the words luk, slu, or lup, then the sign or laksana or the peculiar virtue or the aril also vanishes. Thus there is an inportant direrence in the elision or an aril by rorce or the words lup &c. ; and by the word lopa in one case the virtue or the aril subsists in spite or the elision, in the other it does not. ere the aril is elided by enouncing the word luk, the result is, that the aril canot produce any change which it would otherwise have caused, in the aṅga or inrlective base ; such as guṇa &c. Thus we have kati (non. Pl.); kati (ac. Pl.); katiBi (instr. Pl.); katiBya (Dat. Pl.) ; katiBya (abl. Pl.) ; katinan (Gen. Pl.); katisu (Loc. Pl.). The word asnad (i), yusnad (Thou), and the words caled saw as derined above are alike in the thre genders. Thererore the word kati is nasculine, reninine and neuter. The word tri is always used in the Plural. Thus traya, (non. Pl.); trin (ac. Pl.) ; triBi (instr. Pl.); triBya (Dat. Pl.); triBya (abl. Pl.). But the Genitive Plural is rorned in acordance with the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 263. Or the pase (aṅka), those aril has pen elitet py the use or any or the thre torts containink lu, the operations tepentent on it to not take place, rekartink such pase. this sûtra is a special elception to the previous aphorisn thich tas to eltensive. it teclares, that then an aril is elitet py usink the torts luk, slu, or lup, then the sikn or laksana or the peculiar virtue or the aril also vanishes. thus there is an inportant tirerence in the elision or an aril py rorce or the torts lup &c. ; ant py the tort lopa in one case the virtue or the aril supsists in spite or the elision, in the other it toes not. ere the aril is elitet py enouncink the tort luk, the result is, that the aril canot protuce any chanke thich it toult othertise have causet, in the aṅka or inrlective pase ; such as kuṇa &c. thus te have kati (non. pl.); kati (ac. pl.); katipi (instr. pl.); katipya (tat. pl.) ; katipya (apl. pl.) ; katinan (ken. pl.); katisu (Loc. pl.). the tort asnat (i), yusnat (thou), ant the torts calet sat as terinet apove are alike in the thre kenters. thererore the tort kati is nasculine, reninine ant neuter. the tort tri is altays uset in the plural. thus traya, (non. pl.); trin (ac. pl.) ; tripi (instr. pl.); tripya (tat. pl.); tripya (apl. pl.). put the kenitive plural is rornet in acortance tith the rolotink sûtra.
s: 263. Of the base (aṅga), whose affix has been elided by the use of any of the three words containing लु, the operations dependent on it do not take place, regarding such base. This sûtra is a special exception to the previous aphorism which was too extensive. It declares, that when an affix is elided by using the words लुक्, श्लु, or लुप्, then the 'sign' or लक्षण or the peculiar virtue of the affix also vanishes.
