Thus there is an important difference in the elision of an affix by force of the words लुप् &c. ; and by the word लोप In one case the virtue of the affix subsists in spite of the elision, in the other it does not. Here the affix is elided by enouncing the word 'luk,' the result is, that the affix cannot produce any change which it would otherwise have caused, in the aṅga or inflective base ; such as guṇa &c. Thus we have कति (Nom. Pl.); कति (Acc. Pl.); कतिभिः (Instr. Pl.); कतिभ्यः (Dat. Pl.) ; कतिभ्यः (Abl. Pl.) ; कतीनाम् (Gen. Pl.); कतिषु (Loc. Pl.). The word अस्मद् (I), युष्मद् (Thou), and the words called षट् as defined above are alike in the three genders. Therefore the word कति is masculine, feminine and neuter. The word त्रि is always used in the Plural. Thus त्रयः, (Nom. Pl.); त्रीन् (Acc. Pl.) ; त्रिभिः (Instr. Pl.); त्रिभ्यः (Dat. Pl.); त्रिभ्यः (Abl. Pl.). But the Genitive Plural is formed in accordance with the following sûtra.

pk: 264. traya is substituted ror tri berore the Genitive Plural aril an as trayanan (trinan however apears in the Veda ; as trinanapi sanudranan ). When the word tri rorns the last nenber or a conpound, even then also its declension is as above; as paranatrayanan. But sone say that in those conpounds where tri is not a principal word, but only a secondary nenber or a conpound, there this substitution wil not take place. acording to then the rorn would be priyatrinan. But the proper rorn is priyatrayanan here also. The Locative Plural wil be trisu. now we take up the declension or the word dvi which is always used in the Dual nunber. The rirst rule that aplies to it is the rolowing.
ck: 264. traya is supstitutet ror tri perore the kenitive plural aril an as trayanan (trinan hotever apears in the Veta ; as trinanapi sanutranan ). then the tort tri rorns the last nenper or a conpount, even then also its teclension is as apove; as paranatrayanan. put sone say that in those conpounts there tri is not a principal tort, put only a secontary nenper or a conpount, there this supstitution til not take place. acortink to then the rorn toult pe priyatrinan. put the proper rorn is priyatrayanan here also. the Locative plural til pe trisu. not te take up the teclension or the tort tvi thich is altays uset in the tual nunper. the rirst rule that aplies to it is the rolotink.
s: 264. त्रय is substituted for त्रि before the Genitive Plural affix आम् As त्रयाणाम् (त्रीणाम् however appears in the Veda ; as त्रीणामपि समुद्राणाम् ). When the word त्रि forms the last member of a compound, even then also its declension is as above; as परमत्रयाणाम्. But some say that in those compounds where त्रि is not a principal word, but only a secondary member of a compound, there this substitution will not take place. According to them the form would be प्रियत्रीणाम्. But the proper form is प्रियत्रयाणाम् here also. The Locative Plural will be त्रिषु. Now we take up the declension of the word द्वि which is always used in the Dual Number. The first rule that applies to it is the following.

pk: 265. ror the rinal or tyad and the rest, there is substituted a, when an aril, caled vibhakti, rolows. now the question is what are the tyadadi words. tyadadi words belong to the clas or sarvanana and rorn a sub-division or it and would have ben the rolowing, vis :- tyad, tad, yad, etad, idan, adas, eka, dvi, yusnad, asnad, Bavat and kin but the ishti given below elcludes the last rour words ron the list or tyadadi. ishti :— The tyadadi subdivision begins with the word tyad and ends with the word dvi (inclusive). The word dvi belongs to the clas or tyadadi and thererore its rinal is changed to a berore the ariles, that is the base asunes the rorn or dva. Thus dvO (non. Dual); dvO (ac. Dual); dvaByan (instru., Dative and ablative Duals) dvayo (Genitive and Locative Duals). Why have we said that the tyadadi words do not include the last rour words? Observe the declension or Bavat which is declined as Bavan BavantO Bavanta (non. sing.; Dual and Plural). When tyadadi words are used as sanjna (apelative), or, upasarjana (secondary nenbers or a conpound), then their rinal is not replaced by a. supose the word dvi is the nane or a person, then it wil be declined as dvi (non. sing.) dvi (non. Dual); dvaya (non. Pl.) sinilarly, when the word dvi is an upasarjana as atidvi (he who elcels two), it wil be declined as atidvi (non. sing.), that is like hari. But when dvi is the principal nenber or a conpound the a substitution wil take place; thus paranadvO &c. The word Oquloni is thus declined :— Oquloni (non. sing.) Oquloni (non. Dual), but the non. Pl. wil be Oqulona by the rolowing Vartika. Vartika :— arter the word uqulonan the aril an cones in the Plural nunber denoting the descendant. This Vartika debars the aril in or iV. 1. 96. s. 1096. The acusatives wil be Oqulonin (sing.); Oquloni (Dual); Oqulonan (Plural). ere ends the declension or nasculine words ending in short i. —:0:— nasculine long ī. vatapranirinavitisutrena nana ipratyaya sa ca kit vatan praninite vataprani dirGajasi ca vatapranyO he vataprani ani purva vatapranin vatapranyO vatapranin vatapranya vatapraniByan 3 vatapranye vatapranya 2 vatapranyo 2 vatapranyan varnagrahanatreha nuw nO tu savarnadirGa vataprani vatapranisu evan yayipapyadaya yantyaneneti yayirnarga pati lokaniti papi surya papo kiceti pratyaya kvibante tu vatapranisabdasya ani sasi nO ca visesa vatapranyan vatapranya vatapraniti eranekaca iti vaksyanano yan praDivat bahuvrihO sreyasyo yasya sa bahusreyasi dirGajasi ceti sulopa now
ck: 265. ror the rinal or tyat ant the rest, there is supstitutet a, then an aril, calet viphakti, rolots. not the tuestion is that are the tyatati torts. tyatati torts pelonk to the clas or sarvanana ant rorn a sup-tivision or it ant toult have pen the rolotink, vis :- tyat, tat, yat, etat, itan, atas, eka, tvi, yusnat, asnat, pavat ant kin put the ishti kiven pelot elclutes the last rour torts ron the list or tyatati. ishti :— the tyatati suptivision pekins tith the tort tyat ant ents tith the tort tvi (inclusive). the tort tvi pelonks to the clas or tyatati ant thererore its rinal is chanket to a perore the ariles, that is the pase asunes the rorn or tva. thus tvO (non. tual); tvO (ac. tual); tvapyan (instru., tative ant aplative tuals) tvayo (kenitive ant Locative tuals). thy have te sait that the tyatati torts to not inclute the last rour torts? Opserve the teclension or pavat thich is teclinet as pavan pavantO pavanta (non. sink.; tual ant plural). then tyatati torts are uset as sancna (apelative), or, upasarcana (secontary nenpers or a conpount), then their rinal is not replacet py a. supose the tort tvi is the nane or a person, then it til pe teclinet as tvi (non. sink.) tvi (non. tual); tvaya (non. pl.) sinilarly, then the tort tvi is an upasarcana as atitvi (he tho elcels to), it til pe teclinet as atitvi (non. sink.), that is like hari. put then tvi is the principal nenper or a conpount the a supstitution til take place; thus paranatvO &c. the tort Otuloni is thus teclinet :— Otuloni (non. sink.) Otuloni (non. tual), put the non. pl. til pe Otulona py the rolotink Vartika. Vartika :— arter the tort utulonan the aril an cones in the plural nunper tenotink the tescentant. this Vartika tepars the aril in or iV. 1. 96. s. 1096. the acusatives til pe Otulonin (sink.); Otuloni (tual); Otulonan (plural). ere ents the teclension or nasculine torts entink in short i. —:0:— nasculine lonk ī. vatapranirinavitisutrena nana ipratyaya sa ca kit vatan praninite vataprani tirkacasi ca vatapranyO he vataprani ani purva vatapranin vatapranyO vatapranin vatapranya vatapranipyan 3 vatapranye vatapranya 2 vatapranyo 2 vatapranyan varnakrahanatreha nut nO tu savarnatirka vataprani vatapranisu evan yayipapyataya yantyaneneti yayirnarka pati lokaniti papi surya papo kiceti pratyaya kvipante tu vatapranisaptasya ani sasi nO ca visesa vatapranyan vatapranya vatapraniti eranekaca iti vaksyanano yan prativat pahuvrihO sreyasyo yasya sa pahusreyasi tirkacasi ceti sulopa not te
s: 265. For the final of त्यद् and the rest, there is substituted अ, when an affix, called vibhakti, follows. Now the question is what are the त्यदादि words. त्यदादि words belong to the class of सर्वनाम and form a sub-division of it and would have been the following, viz :- त्यद्, तद्, यद्, एतद्, इदम्, अदस्, एक, द्वि, युष्मद्, अस्मद्, भवत् and किम् but the ishti given below excludes the last four words from the list of त्यदादि. Ishti :— The त्यदादि subdivision begins with the word त्यद् and ends with the word द्वि (inclusive). The word द्वि belongs to the class of त्यदादि and therefore its final is changed to अ before the affixes, that is the base assumes the form of द्व. Thus द्वौ (Nom. Dual); द्वौ (Acc. Dual); द्वाभ्याम् (Instru., Dative and Ablative Duals) द्वयोः (Genitive and Locative Duals). Why have we said that the त्यदादि words do not include the last four words? Observe the declension of भवत् which is declined as भवान् भवन्तौ भवन्तः (Nom. Sing.; Dual and Plural). When त्यदादि words are used as संज्ञा (appellative), or, उपसर्जन (secondary members of a compound), then their final is not replaced by अ. Suppose the word द्वि is the name of a person, then it will be declined as द्विः (Nom. Sing.) द्वी (Nom. Dual); द्वयः (Nom. Pl.) Similarly, when the word द्वि is an उपसर्जन as अतिद्वि (he who excels two), it will be declined as अतिद्विः (Nom. Sing.), that is like हरि. But when द्वि is the principal member of a compound the अ substitution will take place; thus परमद्वौ &c. The word औडुलोमि is thus declined :— औडुलोमिः (Nom. Sing.) औडुलोमी (Nom. Dual), but the Nom. Pl. will be औडुलोमाः by the following Vartika. Vartika :— After the word उडुलोमन् the affix अण् comes in the Plural number denoting the descendant. This Vartika debars the affix इञ् of IV. 1. 96. S. 1096. The Accusatives will be औडुलोमिम् (Sing.); औडुलोमी (Dual); औडुलोमान् (Plural). Here ends the declension of Masculine words ending in short i. —:0:— Masculine long ī. वातप्रमीरिणावितिसूत्रेण माङ ईप्रत्ययः स च कित् वातं प्रमिमीते वातप्रमीः दीर्घाज्जसि च वातप्रम्यौ हे वातप्रमीः अमि पूर्वः वातप्रमीम् वातप्रम्यौ वातप्रमीन् वातप्रम्या वातप्रमीभ्याम् ३ वातप्रम्ये वातप्रम्यः २ वातप्रम्योः २ वातप्रम्याम् वर्णग्रहणात्रेह नुट् ङौ तु सवर्णदीर्घः वातप्रमी वातप्रमीषु एवं ययीपप्यादयः यान्त्यनेनेति ययीर्मार्गः पाति लोकमिति पपीः सूर्यः पापोः किच्चेति प्रत्ययः क्विबन्ते तु वातप्रमीशब्दस्य अमि शसि ङौ च विशेषः वातप्रम्यम् वातप्रम्यः वातप्रमीति एरनेकाच इति वक्ष्यमाणो यण् प्रधीवत् बहुव्रीहौ श्रेयस्यो यस्य स बहुश्रेयसी दीर्घाज्जसि चेति सुलोपः Now we take up the declension of the word वातप्रमी. This word is formed by the Uṇādi affix long ई (See Uṇādi Sūtras Chapter III. 158 and Chapter IV. 1.) added to the root मा to measure, being elided by the rule VI. 4. 64 (Uṇādi Chapter III. 159.) S. 2372. The word literally means 'wind measurer' or 'moving swift as the wind'. It is the name of a kind of an antelope. The affix of it is ई. Therefore वातप्रमा + ई = वातप्रमी. The Nom. Sing. is वातप्रमी. The dual is formed thus : वातप्रमी + औ. Here the rule VI. 1. 102 S. 164 required the substitution of a single long ई in the place of ई + औ. But this is prevented by the rule VI. 1. 105. S. 239. and we get the regular form वातप्रम्यौ. Similarly Nom. Pl. वातप्रम्यः. The Voc. Sing. हे वातप्रमीः. The Acc. Sing. is thus formed :— वातप्रमी + अम्. The single substitution required by VI. 1. 102. S. 164 is set aside by VI. 1. 105. S. 239. But this latter rule is set aside by the Apavada rule VI. 1. 107. (अमि पूर्वः) S. 194 by which there is the single substitution of the first vowel, when a simple vowel is followed by the अम् of the case ending. Therefore the Acc. Sing. is वातप्रमीम्. The Acc. Dual and Pl. are वातप्रम्यौ and वातप्रमीन्. The Inst. Sing. is वातप्रम्या. The Ins. Dual and Pl. are वातप्रमीभ्याम् and वातप्रमीभिः. The Dat. forms are वातप्रम्ये, वातप्रमीभ्याम्, वातप्रमीभ्यः. The Abl. Sing. is वातप्रम्यः. The Genitive Sing. and Dual are वातप्रम्यः and वातप्रम्योः. The Genitive Pl. is वातप्रम्याम्. The augme

pk: 26. Word-rorns ending in long ī and ū, being nanes or renales which are always reninines are caled nadī. The word yu is a conpound or i + u. The word stryākhya neans that which by itselr denotes the nane or a renale. These words nust be always reninine, having no nasculine or the sane rorn, as the word grānaṇī has. as the words kunari Kunārī a virgin yavagu yavāgūḥ rice gruel. Why do we say ending in i and u? Because reninine nouns not ending in these vowels wil not be declined like nadī words. Thus while the Dative or kunari wil be kunaryE, the Dative or duhitr wil be duhitre. Why do we say which are reninine? Because ir they are nanes or nales, they wil not be caled nadī. as granani leader or a vilage; senani leader or an arny; Kalapu a sweper; their Dative being grananye, senanye, Kalapve. Why have we used the word ākhyā nane in the telt? Because the reninine gender nust be denoted by the word itselr and not by any other epithet used along with the word. Thus ir the head-borough or the sweper should be or the renale sel, the Dative singular would stil be grananye and Kalapve striyE. Vartika:— The gender or the word as originaly used should be taken and not the gender or the Conpound word. ere the original word sreyasi is reninine and though the Conpound word bahusreyasi is nasculine stil ror the purposes or geting the designation or nadī the whole word wil be treated as nadī, though sreyasi in this Conpound word is nerely a secondary nenber (upasarjana). Thererore geting the designation or nadī is arected by the rolowing rule in rorning its Vocative.
ck: 26. tort-rorns entink in lonk ī ant ū, peink nanes or renales thich are altays reninines are calet natī. the tort yu is a conpount or i + u. the tort stryākhya neans that thich py itselr tenotes the nane or a renale. these torts nust pe altays reninine, havink no nasculine or the sane rorn, as the tort krānaṇī has. as the torts kunari kunārī a virkin yavaku yavākūḥ rice kruel. thy to te say entink in i ant u? pecause reninine nouns not entink in these votels til not pe teclinet like natī torts. thus thile the tative or kunari til pe kunaryE, the tative or tuhitr til pe tuhitre. thy to te say thich are reninine? pecause ir they are nanes or nales, they til not pe calet natī. as kranani leater or a vilake; senani leater or an arny; kalapu a steper; their tative peink krananye, senanye, kalapve. thy have te uset the tort ākhyā nane in the telt? pecause the reninine kenter nust pe tenotet py the tort itselr ant not py any other epithet uset alonk tith the tort. thus ir the heat-poroukh or the steper shoult pe or the renale sel, the tative sinkular toult stil pe krananye ant kalapve striyE. Vartika:— the kenter or the tort as orikinaly uset shoult pe taken ant not the kenter or the conpount tort. ere the orikinal tort sreyasi is reninine ant thoukh the conpount tort pahusreyasi is nasculine stil ror the purposes or ketink the tesiknation or natī the thole tort til pe treatet as natī, thoukh sreyasi in this conpount tort is nerely a secontary nenper (upasarcana). thererore ketink the tesiknation or natī is arectet py the rolotink rule in rornink its Vocative.
s: 266. Word-forms ending in long ī and ū, being names of females which are always feminines are called Nadī. The word यू is a compound of ई + ऊ. The word stryākhya means that which by itself denotes the name of a female. These words must be always feminine, having no masculine of the same form, as the word grāmaṇī has. As the words कुमारी Kumārī 'a virgin' यवागू yavāgūḥ 'rice gruel.' Why do we say ending in ई and ऊ? Because feminine nouns not ending in these vowels will not be declined like Nadī words. Thus while the Dative of कुमारी will be कुमार्यै, the Dative of दुहितृ will be दुहित्रे. Why do we say 'which are feminine'? Because if they are names of males, they will not be called Nadī. As ग्रामणीः 'leader of a village'; सेनानीः 'leader of an army'; खलपूः 'a sweeper'; their Dative being ग्रामण्ये, सेनान्ये, खलप्वे. Why have we used the word ākhyā 'name' in the text? Because the feminine gender must be denoted by the word itself and not by any other epithet used along with the word. Thus if the head-borough or the sweeper should be of the female sex, the Dative Singular would still be ग्रामण्ये and खलप्वे स्त्रियै. Vartika:— The gender of the word as originally used should be taken and not the gender of the Compound word. Here the original word श्रेयसी is feminine and though the Compound word बहुश्रेयसी is Masculine still for the purposes of getting the designation of Nadī the whole word will be treated as Nadī, though श्रेयसी in this Compound word is merely a secondary member (upasarjana). Therefore getting the designation of Nadī is affected by the following rule in forming its Vocative.

pk: 267. a short vowel is substituted in the Voc. sg. ror the ‹?› or the reninine, in the sense or nother, nother-dear, as wel as ror the long vowel or the words caled nadi. Thus he bahusreyasi. The ac. sing and Dual are bahusreyasin, bahusreyasyO respectively. The ac. Pl. is ‹?›. There is no peculiarity in the instrunental rorns. in rorning the Dative rorns, the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 267. a short votel is supstitutet in the Voc. sk. ror the ‹?› or the reninine, in the sense or nother, nother-tear, as tel as ror the lonk votel or the torts calet nati. thus he pahusreyasi. the ac. sink ant tual are pahusreyasin, pahusreyasyO respectively. the ac. pl. is ‹?›. there is no peculiarity in the instrunental rorns. in rornink the tative rorns, the rolotink rules aply.
s: 267. A short vowel is substituted in the Voc. Sg. for the ‹?› of the feminine, in the sense of 'mother, mother-dear', as well as for the long vowel of the words called Nadi. Thus हे बहुश्रेयसि. The Acc. Sing and Dual are बहुश्रेयसीम्, बहुश्रेयस्यौ respectively. The Acc. Pl. is ‹?›. There is no peculiarity in the Instrumental forms. In forming the Dative forms, the following rules apply.

pk: 268. The augnent aw is aded to the case-endings or the Dat. abl. Gen. and Loc. sg. arter the sten caled nadi. When this aw is aded, there is the single substitution or a Vridhi Vowel by the rolowing rule.
ck: 268. the auknent at is atet to the case-entinks or the tat. apl. ken. ant Loc. sk. arter the sten calet nati. then this at is atet, there is the sinkle supstitution or a Vrithi Votel py the rolotink rule.
s: 268. The augment आट् is added to the case-endings of the Dat. Abl. Gen. and Loc. Sg. after the stem called Nadi. When this आट् is added, there is the single substitution of a Vriddhi Vowel by the following rule.

pk: 269. The Vridhi is the single substitute when the augnent aw is rolowed by any vowel. The aw is the augnent which nit case ariles take arter nadī words (Vi. 3. 12) bahusreyasi + aw + ne = bahusreyasyE (Dative singular). (The aw is the augnent also in the Vedic Tense lew); sinilarly, bahusreyasya. The augnent nuw is aded to the Genitive Plural by Vi. 1. 54. s. 208. as bahusreyasinan. ror the rornation or the Loc. sing. the rolowing rule aplies. note.—The anuvriti or eci ceases; that or aci however, is present. The vowel that is subsequent to the augnent aw, and the aw which is precedent to a vowel—in the ron or these two i.e. the aw and the vowel subsequent and precedent the Vridhi is the single substitute. The augnent aw is aded to the rots begining with a vowel, in the inperect, aorist and Conditional Tenses (Vi. 4. 72 &c). Thus Eksiswa, Eksata, Eksisyata, OBit, OnBit, Onjit ron rots iks darsane (Bhu. 641), unB unPa purane (Tud. 32) and rju Barjave (Tud. 20). note.—The ca and in the sutra shows that the pararupa rule, taught in Vi. 1. 95, 96 when us, ‹?› and ‹?› rolow is superseded, when the preceding vowel is aw Thus ‹?›, ‹?› ‹?›
ck: 269. the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute then the auknent at is rolotet py any votel. the at is the auknent thich nit case ariles take arter natī torts (Vi. 3. 12) pahusreyasi + at + ne = pahusreyasyE (tative sinkular). (the at is the auknent also in the Vetic tense let); sinilarly, pahusreyasya. the auknent nut is atet to the kenitive plural py Vi. 1. 54. s. 208. as pahusreyasinan. ror the rornation or the Loc. sink. the rolotink rule aplies. note.—the anuvriti or eci ceases; that or aci hotever, is present. the votel that is supsetuent to the auknent at, ant the at thich is precetent to a votel—in the ron or these to i.e. the at ant the votel supsetuent ant precetent the Vrithi is the sinkle supstitute. the auknent at is atet to the rots pekinink tith a votel, in the inperect, aorist ant contitional tenses (Vi. 4. 72 &c). thus Eksista, Eksata, Eksisyata, Opit, Onpit, Oncit ron rots iks tarsane (phu. 641), unp unpa purane (tut. 32) ant rcu parcave (tut. 20). note.—the ca ant in the sutra shots that the pararupa rule, taukht in Vi. 1. 95, 96 then us, ‹?› ant ‹?› rolot is supersetet, then the precetink votel is at thus ‹?›, ‹?› ‹?›
s: 269. The Vriddhi is the single substitute when the augment आट् is followed by any vowel. The आट् is the augment which ङित् case affixes take after nadī words (VII. 3. 112) बहुश्रेयसी + आट् + ङे = बहुश्रेयस्यै (Dative Singular). (The आट् is the augment also in the Vedic Tense लेट्); similarly, बहुश्रेयस्याः. The augment नुट् is added to the Genitive Plural by VII. 1. 54. S. 208. As बहुश्रेयसीनाम्. For the formation of the Loc. Sing. the following rule applies. Note.—The anuvritti of एचि ceases; that of अचि however, is present. The vowel that is subsequent to the augment आट्, and the आट् which is precedent to a vowel—in the room of these two i.e. the आट् and the vowel subsequent and precedent the Vriddhi is the single substitute. The augment आट् is added to the roots beginning with a vowel, in the Imperfect, Aorist and Conditional Tenses (VI. 4. 72 &c). Thus ऐक्षिष्ट, ऐक्षत, ऐक्षिष्यत, औभीत्, औम्भीत्, औञ्जीत् from roots ईक्ष् दर्शने (Bhu. 641), उम्भ् उम्फ पूरणे (Tud. 32) and ऋजू भार्जवे (Tud. 20). Note.—The च 'and' in the sutra shows that the पररूप rule, taught in VI. 1. 95, 96 when उस्, ‹?› and ‹?› follow is superseded, when the preceding vowel is आट् Thus ‹?›, ‹?› ‹?›

pk: 270. ror the ending ni or the Loc. sg. there is substituted an, arter a sten caled nadi, arter the reninines in a, and arter ni The augnent nuw is not aded to this an, but only to the an or Genitive Plural; because nuw or the sutra Vi. 1. 54, s. 208 is superseded by the subsequently taught augnent aw or the Vi. 3. 12. s. 268. Thus bahusreyasi + ‹?› = bahusreyasi + ‹?› + ni (Vi. 3. 12. s. 268) bahusreyasi + aw + an = bahusreyasyan The rest or the declensions or bahusreyasi are like those or vataprani The declension or the word atilaksni is as rolows:— non. sing. is atilaksni ere the aril su is not elided as in the last case, because i or laksni is part or the word laksni and is not a reninine aril and thererore the rule halanbyab (Vi. 1. 68. s. 252) does not aply. The rest or the declensions are like those or bahusreyasi note.—The word laksni is rorned by the unadi aril i (unadi sutras i. 160 laksernut, as laks + nuw + i = laksni) now, we take up the declension or the nasculine word kunari This word, though ordinarily reninine, when it is derived ron the Denoninative rot kunari neaning a Brahnan who desires a kunari or acts like a kunari (i. 2. 76. s. 2983) is nasculine, nanely, the Denoninative Verb kunari considered to be rorned by the aril ‹?› (i. 1. 8 or i. 1. 10 s. 2657 or 264) with the aril kvip or i. 2. 76. note.—as kunaryan, kisoryan, gOryan, brahnabanDvan, virabanDvan, Kawvayan, bahurajayan, karisaganDyayan; ni:—grananyan, senanyan The word granani is rorned by kvip aril aded under i. 2. ‹?›. Or the ‹?› is changed to ‹?› by agragrananiByan; and the yan substitute in the Locative is by Vi. 4. 82. Thus kunari + su = kunari su is elided by Vi. 1. 68 s. 252. in rorning the Dual, the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 270. ror the entink ni or the Loc. sk. there is supstitutet an, arter a sten calet nati, arter the reninines in a, ant arter ni the auknent nut is not atet to this an, put only to the an or kenitive plural; pecause nut or the sutra Vi. 1. 54, s. 208 is supersetet py the supsetuently taukht auknent at or the Vi. 3. 12. s. 268. thus pahusreyasi + ‹?› = pahusreyasi + ‹?› + ni (Vi. 3. 12. s. 268) pahusreyasi + at + an = pahusreyasyan the rest or the teclensions or pahusreyasi are like those or vataprani the teclension or the tort atilaksni is as rolots:— non. sink. is atilaksni ere the aril su is not elitet as in the last case, pecause i or laksni is part or the tort laksni ant is not a reninine aril ant thererore the rule halanpyap (Vi. 1. 68. s. 252) toes not aply. the rest or the teclensions are like those or pahusreyasi note.—the tort laksni is rornet py the unati aril i (unati sutras i. 160 laksernut, as laks + nut + i = laksni) not, te take up the teclension or the nasculine tort kunari this tort, thoukh ortinarily reninine, then it is terivet ron the tenoninative rot kunari neanink a prahnan tho tesires a kunari or acts like a kunari (i. 2. 76. s. 2983) is nasculine, nanely, the tenoninative Verp kunari consiteret to pe rornet py the aril ‹?› (i. 1. 8 or i. 1. 10 s. 2657 or 264) tith the aril kvip or i. 2. 76. note.—as kunaryan, kisoryan, kOryan, prahnapantvan, virapantvan, katvayan, pahuracayan, karisakantyayan; ni:—krananyan, senanyan the tort kranani is rornet py kvip aril atet unter i. 2. ‹?›. Or the ‹?› is chanket to ‹?› py akrakrananipyan; ant the yan supstitute in the Locative is py Vi. 4. 82. thus kunari + su = kunari su is elitet py Vi. 1. 68 s. 252. in rornink the tual, the rolotink rules aply.
s: 270. For the ending ङि of the Loc. Sg. there is substituted आम्, after a stem called Nadi, after the Feminines in आ, and after नी The augment नुट् is not added to this आम्, but only to the आम् of Genitive Plural; because नुट् of the Sutra VII. 1. 54, S. 208 is superseded by the subsequently taught augment आट् of the VII. 3. 112. S. 268. Thus बहुश्रेयसी + ‹?› = बहुश्रेयसी + ‹?› + ङि (VII. 3. 112. S. 268) बहुश्रेयसी + आट् + आम् = बहुश्रेयस्याम् The rest of the declensions of बहुश्रेयसी are like those of वातप्रमी The declension of the word अतिलक्ष्मी is as follows:— Nom. Sing. is अतिलक्ष्मीः Here the affix सु is not elided as in the last case, because ई of लक्ष्मी is part of the word लक्ष्मी and is not a feminine affix and therefore the rule 'हलङ्ब्याब्' (VI. 1. 68. S. 252) does not apply. The rest of the declensions are like those of बहुश्रेयसी Note.—The word लक्ष्मी is formed by the Unadi affix ई (Unadi Sutras III. 160 लक्षेर्मुत्, as लक्ष् + मुट् + ई = लक्ष्मी) Now, we take up the declension of the Masculine word कुमारी This word, though ordinarily feminine, when it is derived from the Denominative root कुमारी meaning a Brahman who desires a कुमारी or acts like a कुमारी (III. 2. 76. S. 2983) is Masculine, namely, the Denominative Verb कुमारी considered to be formed by the affix ‹?› (III. 1. 8 or III. 1. 10 S. 2657 or 2664) with the affix क्विप् of III. 2. 76. Note.—As कुमार्याम्, किशोर्याम्, गौर्याम्, ब्रह्मबन्ध्वाम्, वीरबन्ध्वाम्, खट्वायाम्, बहुराजायाम्, कारीषगन्ध्यायाम्; नी:—ग्रामण्याम्, सेनान्याम् The word ग्रामणी is formed by क्विप् affix added under III. 2. ‹?›. Or the ‹?› is changed to ‹?› by अग्रग्रामणीभ्याम्; and the यण् substitute in the Locative is by VI. 4. 82. Thus कुमारी + सु = कुमारी सु is elided by VI. 1. 68 S. 252. In forming the Dual, the following rules apply.

pk: 271. Berore an aril begining with a vowel, there are substituted ror the u or nu, the characteristic or the rots or the rirth clas, ror the rinal i, i, u and u or a rot, as wel as ror the u or Bru, the iyan (ror i or i) and uvan (ror u or u). The substitutes iyan and uvan have indicatory n and thererore they are aplied at the end and by the rule or nearnes or substitutes i replaces i and u replaces u (whether long or short). Thus kunari + O = kunari + O. But this is prevented by the nelt sūtra. note :—sinilarly apnuvanti, raDnuvanti, saknuvanti, ron the rots or the 5th clas. ciksiyatu, luluvatu, luluvu, niyO, niya, luvO, luva and BruvO and ‹?›
ck: 271. perore an aril pekinink tith a votel, there are supstitutet ror the u or nu, the characteristic or the rots or the rirth clas, ror the rinal i, i, u ant u or a rot, as tel as ror the u or pru, the iyan (ror i or i) ant uvan (ror u or u). the supstitutes iyan ant uvan have inticatory n ant thererore they are apliet at the ent ant py the rule or nearnes or supstitutes i replaces i ant u replaces u (thether lonk or short). thus kunari + O = kunari + O. put this is preventet py the nelt sūtra. note :—sinilarly apnuvanti, ratnuvanti, saknuvanti, ron the rots or the 5th clas. ciksiyatu, luluvatu, luluvu, niyO, niya, luvO, luva ant pruvO ant ‹?›
s: 271. Before an affix beginning with a vowel, there are substituted for the उ of नु, the characteristic of the roots of the fifth class, for the final इ, ई, उ and ऊ of a root, as well as for the ऊ of भ्रू, the इयङ् (for इ or ई) and उवङ् (for उ or ऊ). The substitutes इयङ् and उवङ् have indicatory ङ् and therefore they are applied at the end and by the rule of nearness of substitutes इ replaces इ and उ replaces उ (whether long or short). Thus कुमारी + औ = कुमारि + औ. But this is prevented by the next Sūtra. Note :—Similarly आप्नुवन्ति, राध्नुवन्ति, शक्नुवन्ति, from the roots of the 5th class. चिक्षियतुः, लुलुवतुः, लुलुवुः, नियौ, नियः, लुवौ, लुवः and भ्रुवौ and ‹?›

pk: 272. a senivowel is substituted berore an aril begining with a vowel, ror the rinal i or i or a rot, not preceded by a conjunct consonant rorning part or the rot, when the sten is not a nonosylable. Thus instead or iyan we get yan ādeśa, thererore kunari + O = kunaryO; kunari + as = kunarya The Voc. sing is he kunari The ac. sing, Dual and Pl. are kunaryan, kunaryO, kunarya. There are no peculiarities in the instrunental rorns. The Dative sing is kunaryE. The ablative and Genitive singulars are kunarya The Genitive Pl. is kunarinan The Loc. sing. is kunaryan The word praDi is thus declined :— praDi, praDyO, praDya, praDyan, praDya &c. This word is derived ron the rot Dya with the preril pra. The a is changed to i by unadi iV. 15. Thus praDya + kvip = praDi. The short i is lengthened by Vi. 4. 2. s. 259. so we have praDi. The declension or the word uni it is rorned by ading the preril ud to the verb ni. Thererore this long i canot be said to be preceded by a conjunct consonant, ror the conjunct consonant or the sūtra neans the conjunct consonant or the verbal rot and not the conjunct consonant obtained by ading a preril to the sinple rot like ni. Thererore, the present sūtra aplies to uni which is declined as uni, unyO, unya ; he uni ; ac. sing. unyan, Loc. sing. ‹?› in the sane way should be declined the word granani, the non. sing. or which is granani ow do you elplain the rorns durDiya where there is not yan though dur is a Gati, and the word vrscikaBiya where the word vrscika is a Karaka? We reply that the preposition dur is not a Gati with regard to the word Di, because we analyse the word as dusTita Diryesan a Bahuvrihi conpound in which dur is Gati with regard to the word sTita understod. This conpound is rorned by the Vārtika ‹?› &c. (i. 2. 24. s. 830.) by which the subsequent tern sTita is elided arter the Gati word dur. in ract, the word Gati is a relative tern with regard to the verb which a preposition inediately qualiries, and not with regard to any other verb with which it nay be acidentaly in contact. sinilarly vrscikaBi should not be analysed as an ablative conpound (pancani tatpurusa sanasa) rorned by i. 4. 25. s. 58, as vrscikadBiti vrscikaBi; but as vrscikasanbanDini Bi in the rirst case the conpound would nean a person araid or a scorpion; in the other case, which is aplicable here, the rear arising ron a scorpion. in the second case vrscika is not a Karaka with regard to Bi. Thererore the vartika aplies to it.
ck: 272. a senivotel is supstitutet perore an aril pekinink tith a votel, ror the rinal i or i or a rot, not precetet py a concunct consonant rornink part or the rot, then the sten is not a nonosylaple. thus insteat or iyan te ket yan āteśa, thererore kunari + O = kunaryO; kunari + as = kunarya the Voc. sink is he kunari the ac. sink, tual ant pl. are kunaryan, kunaryO, kunarya. there are no peculiarities in the instrunental rorns. the tative sink is kunaryE. the aplative ant kenitive sinkulars are kunarya the kenitive pl. is kunarinan the Loc. sink. is kunaryan the tort prati is thus teclinet :— prati, pratyO, pratya, pratyan, pratya &c. this tort is terivet ron the rot tya tith the preril pra. the a is chanket to i py unati iV. 15. thus pratya + kvip = prati. the short i is lenkthenet py Vi. 4. 2. s. 259. so te have prati. the teclension or the tort uni it is rornet py atink the preril ut to the verp ni. thererore this lonk i canot pe sait to pe precetet py a concunct consonant, ror the concunct consonant or the sūtra neans the concunct consonant or the verpal rot ant not the concunct consonant optainet py atink a preril to the sinple rot like ni. thererore, the present sūtra aplies to uni thich is teclinet as uni, unyO, unya ; he uni ; ac. sink. unyan, Loc. sink. ‹?› in the sane tay shoult pe teclinet the tort kranani, the non. sink. or thich is kranani ot to you elplain the rorns turtiya there there is not yan thoukh tur is a kati, ant the tort vrscikapiya there the tort vrscika is a karaka? te reply that the preposition tur is not a kati tith rekart to the tort ti, pecause te analyse the tort as tustita tiryesan a pahuvrihi conpount in thich tur is kati tith rekart to the tort stita unterstot. this conpount is rornet py the Vārtika ‹?› &c. (i. 2. 24. s. 830.) py thich the supsetuent tern stita is elitet arter the kati tort tur. in ract, the tort kati is a relative tern tith rekart to the verp thich a preposition inetiately tualiries, ant not tith rekart to any other verp tith thich it nay pe acitentaly in contact. sinilarly vrscikapi shoult not pe analyset as an aplative conpount (pancani tatpurusa sanasa) rornet py i. 4. 25. s. 58, as vrscikatpiti vrscikapi; put as vrscikasanpantini pi in the rirst case the conpount toult nean a person arait or a scorpion; in the other case, thich is aplicaple here, the rear arisink ron a scorpion. in the secont case vrscika is not a karaka tith rekart to pi. thererore the vartika aplies to it.
s: 272. A semivowel is substituted before an affix beginning with a vowel, for the final इ or ई of a root, not preceded by a conjunct consonant forming part of the root, when the stem is not a monosyllable. Thus instead of इयङ् we get यण् ādeśa, therefore कुमारी + औ = कुमार्यौ; कुमारी + अस् = कुमार्यः The Voc. Sing is हे कुमारि The Acc. Sing, Dual and Pl. are कुमार्यम्, कुमार्यौ, कुमार्यः. There are no peculiarities in the Instrumental forms. The Dative Sing is कुमार्यै. The Ablative and Genitive Singulars are कुमार्याः The Genitive Pl. is कुमारीणाम् The Loc. Sing. is कुमार्याम् The word प्रधी is thus declined :— प्रधीः, प्रध्यौ, प्रध्यः, प्रध्यम्, प्रध्यः &c. This word is derived from the root ध्या with the prefix प्र. The आ is changed to ई by Unadi IV. 115. Thus प्रध्य + क्विप् = प्रधि. The short इ is lengthened by VI. 4. 2. S. 2559. So we have प्रधीः. The declension of the word उन्नी It is formed by adding the prefix उद् to the verb नी. Therefore this long ई cannot be said to be preceded by a conjunct consonant, for the conjunct consonant of the Sūtra means the conjunct consonant of the verbal root and not the conjunct consonant obtained by adding a prefix to the simple root like नी. Therefore, the present Sūtra applies to उन्नी which is declined as उन्नीः, उन्न्यौ, उन्न्यः ; हे उन्नीः ; Acc. Sing. उन्न्यम्, Loc. Sing. ‹?› In the same way should be declined the word ग्रामणी, the Nom. Sing. of which is ग्रामणीः How do you explain the forms दुर्धियः where there is not यण् though दुर् is a Gati, and the word वृश्चिकभियः where the word वृश्चिक is a Karaka? We reply that the preposition दुर् is not a Gati with regard to the word धी, because we analyse the word as दुःस्थिता धीर्येषां a Bahuvrihi compound in which दुर् is Gati with regard to the word स्थित understood. This compound is formed by the Vārtika ‹?› &c. (II. 2. 24. S. 830.) by which the subsequent term स्थित is elided after the Gati word दुर्. In fact, the word Gati is a relative term with regard to the verb which a preposition immediately qualifies, and not with regard to any other verb with which it may be accidentally in contact. Similarly वृश्चिकभीः should not be analysed as an Ablative compound (पञ्चमी तत्पुरुष समास) formed by I. 4. 25. S. 588, as वृश्चिकाद्भीति वृश्चिकभीः; but as वृश्चिकसम्बन्धिनीः भीः In the first case the compound would mean 'a person afraid of a scorpion'; in the other case, which is applicable here, the fear arising from a scorpion. In the second case वृश्चिक is not a Karaka with regard to भी. Therefore the vartika applies to it.

pk: 273. The seni-vowel substitution does not take place in the case or stens ending in Bu or the word suDi, berore ariles begining with a vowel. Thus pratiBu - pratiBuvO, pratiBuva ; suDi - suDiyO, suDiya now, we take up the elanple or a word rorned ron a Denoninative rot, nanely, the word saKi which is thus rorned saKayan icCati saKiyati (i.e. he who desires a riend). Thus the rot saKiya is a Denoninative rot, to this is aded the aril kvip and the leters ‹?› and ‹?› are both elided. ere the elision or ‹?› being considered as sTanivat there would be yan under the previous sūtra in declining the word. This is prevented by the rolowing. Vârt:—When there is elision berore the aril kvip the elision is not considered as sthanivat. The rules by which the word saKi is rorned are the sane which have ben already rerered to in rorning the word ‹?› as elplained under Vi. 3. 16. s. 270. in declining this word which neans "he who desires a riend" the sane rules are to be aplied which were aplied to the word saKi neaning a riend (se Vi. 1. 68 and Vi. 2. 15. s. 252, 254), because or the nalin ‹?› Thererore we get the noninative rorns saKa ; saKayO ; saKaya, Voc. he saKe : The ac. sing. is saKayan. it is thus rorned saKi + an. ere Vi. 1. 107. s. 194 requires Pûrva-rûpa, that is ‹?›. But that rule is set aside by the subsequent rule Vi. 4. 82. s. 272, requiring yan which would have given the rorn ‹?›. Both these rorns are wrong, ror the last rule even is set aside by the subsequent rule Vi. 1. 92. s. 253. ence the rorn saKayan The ac. Dual is ‹?›. The ac. Pl. is ‹?› + ‹?›, ror the ac. Pl. not being a sarvanânasthâna, there is regular sandhi: saKya. There is no peculiarity in other cases or this word, neaning one who desires a riend. There is another word saKi which is thus rorned saha Kena vartate iti saKa. it is a Bahu-vrîhi conpound rorned by i. 2. 28. s. 848. The ‹?› is changed to ‹?› by Vi. 3. 82. s. 849. in rorning the Denoninative verb ron this saKa, we ad the aril kyac by i. 1. 8. s. 2657. Then, we ad long i by Vi. 4. 3. s. 2658, and thus we get the Denoninative rot. ron this rot, we get the nasculine noun with the aril kvip on the analogy or the previous word. sinilarly are also rorned the words suKi neaning one who desires hapines; and suti neaning one who desires a son. The declension or these words is as rolows:—non. sing. saKi ; suKi ; suti. The dual is saKyO, suKyO, sutyO. The abl. and Gen. singular rorns are saKyu ; suKyu ; sutyu ; by aplying the sūtra Vi. 1.
ck: 273. the seni-votel supstitution toes not take place in the case or stens entink in pu or the tort suti, perore ariles pekinink tith a votel. thus pratipu - pratipuvO, pratipuva ; suti - sutiyO, sutiya not, te take up the elanple or a tort rornet ron a tenoninative rot, nanely, the tort saki thich is thus rornet sakayan icati sakiyati (i.e. he tho tesires a rient). thus the rot sakiya is a tenoninative rot, to this is atet the aril kvip ant the leters ‹?› ant ‹?› are poth elitet. ere the elision or ‹?› peink consiteret as stanivat there toult pe yan unter the previous sūtra in teclinink the tort. this is preventet py the rolotink. Vârt:—then there is elision perore the aril kvip the elision is not consiteret as sthanivat. the rules py thich the tort saki is rornet are the sane thich have pen alreaty rereret to in rornink the tort ‹?› as elplainet unter Vi. 3. 16. s. 270. in teclinink this tort thich neans "he tho tesires a rient" the sane rules are to pe apliet thich tere apliet to the tort saki neanink a rient (se Vi. 1. 68 ant Vi. 2. 15. s. 252, 254), pecause or the nalin ‹?› thererore te ket the noninative rorns saka ; sakayO ; sakaya, Voc. he sake : the ac. sink. is sakayan. it is thus rornet saki + an. ere Vi. 1. 107. s. 194 retuires pûrva-rûpa, that is ‹?›. put that rule is set asite py the supsetuent rule Vi. 4. 82. s. 272, retuirink yan thich toult have kiven the rorn ‹?›. poth these rorns are tronk, ror the last rule even is set asite py the supsetuent rule Vi. 1. 92. s. 253. ence the rorn sakayan the ac. tual is ‹?›. the ac. pl. is ‹?› + ‹?›, ror the ac. pl. not peink a sarvanânasthâna, there is rekular santhi: sakya. there is no peculiarity in other cases or this tort, neanink one tho tesires a rient. there is another tort saki thich is thus rornet saha kena vartate iti saka. it is a pahu-vrîhi conpount rornet py i. 2. 28. s. 848. the ‹?› is chanket to ‹?› py Vi. 3. 82. s. 849. in rornink the tenoninative verp ron this saka, te at the aril kyac py i. 1. 8. s. 2657. then, te at lonk i py Vi. 4. 3. s. 2658, ant thus te ket the tenoninative rot. ron this rot, te ket the nasculine noun tith the aril kvip on the analoky or the previous tort. sinilarly are also rornet the torts suki neanink one tho tesires hapines; ant suti neanink one tho tesires a son. the teclension or these torts is as rolots:—non. sink. saki ; suki ; suti. the tual is sakyO, sukyO, sutyO. the apl. ant ken. sinkular rorns are sakyu ; sukyu ; sutyu ; py aplyink the sūtra Vi. 1. 12.
s: 273. The semi-vowel substitution does not take place in the case of stems ending in भू or the word सुधी, before affixes beginning with a vowel. Thus प्रतिभू -- प्रतिभुवौ, प्रतिभुवः ; सुधी -- सुधियौ, सुधियः Now, we take up the example of a word formed from a Denominative root, namely, the word सखी which is thus formed सखायम् इच्छति सखीयति (i.e. he who desires a friend). Thus the root सखीय is a Denominative root, to this is added the affix क्विप् and the letters ‹?› and ‹?› are both elided. Here the elision of ‹?› being considered as स्थानिवत् there would be यण् under the previous Sūtra in declining the word. This is prevented by the following. Vârt:—When there is elision before the affix क्विप् the elision is not considered as sthanivat. The rules by which the word सखी is formed are the same which have been already referred to in forming the word ‹?› as explained under VII. 3. 116. S. 270. In declining this word which means "he who desires a friend" the same rules are to be applied which were applied to the word सखि meaning a friend (see VI. 1. 68 and VII. 2. 115. S. 252, 254), because of the maxim ‹?› Therefore we get the Nominative forms सखा ; सखायौ ; सखायः, Voc. हे सखे : The Acc. Sing. is सखायम्. It is thus formed सखी + अम्. Here VI. 1. 107. S. 194 requires Pûrva-rûpa, that is ‹?›. But that rule is set aside by the subsequent rule VI. 4. 82. S. 272, requiring यण् which would have given the form ‹?›. Both these forms are wrong, for the last rule even is set aside by the subsequent rule VII. 1. 92. S. 253. Hence the form सखायम् The Acc. Dual is ‹?›. The Acc. Pl. is ‹?› + ‹?›, for the Acc. Pl. not being a Sarvanâmasthâna, there is regular Sandhi: सख्यः. There is no peculiarity in other cases of this word, meaning 'one who desires a friend'. There is another word सखी which is thus formed सह खेन वर्तते इति सखः. It is a Bahu-vrîhi compound formed by II. 2. 28. S. 848. The ‹?› is changed to ‹?› by VI. 3. 82. S. 849. In forming the Denominative verb from this सख, we add the affix क्यच् by III. 1. 8. S. 2657. Then, we add long ई by VII. 4. 33. S. 2658, and thus we get the Denominative root. From this root, we get the masculine noun with the affix क्विप् on the analogy of the previous word. Similarly are also formed the words सुखी meaning 'one who desires happiness'; and सुती meaning 'one who desires a son'. The declension of these words is as follows:—Nom. Sing. सखीः ; सुखीः ; सुतीः. The dual is सख्यौ, सुख्यौ, सुत्यौ. The Abl. and Gen. Singular forms are सख्युः ; सुख्युः ; सुत्युः ; by applying the Sūtra VI. 1. 112. S. 255. Similarly the words लूनीः ; क्षामीः ; प्रस्तीमीः meaning respectively 'one who desires cut off things' e. g. flowers &c.; 'one who desires Vishnu'; and 'one who desires crowd' &c. are to be declined. Note:—The word लून is the past participle of the root लू 'to cut'; the निष्ठा is changed to न by VIII. 2. 44. S. 3018. क्षाम is the past participle of the root क्षै 'to wane', the निष्ठा is changed to म by VIII. 2. 53. S. 3032. Similarly प्रस्तीम is the past participle of the root स्त्या 'to make noise', preceded by the preposition प्र. The निष्ठा is changed to म by VIII. 2. 54. S. 3034. The Samprasâraṇa takes place by VI. 1. 23. The Nom. Sing. forms are लूनीः ; क्षामीः ; प्रस्तीमीः. In other cases their declension is like the word सुखी &c., except the Abl. and Gen. Sing. Here in these cases the words do not really end in खि and ति, and therefore the rule VI. 1. 112. S. 255, is not strictly applicable to them, but as the न of लून and the म of क्षाम and प्रस्तीम are substitutes of त and as these are taught in the Tripâdî, namely the last three chapters of the Ashṭâdhyâyî, therefore the न and म substitutions are considered asiddha for the purposes of the application of the rule contained in the 7¼ adhyâyas. In other words these words are considered as ‹?› ; ‹?› ; ‹?› ; and the rule VI. 1. 112. S. 255 applying to them, we have the Abl. and Genitive Sing. forms as लुन्युः ; क्षाम्युः ; प्रस्तीम्युः But the declension of t

pk: 274. The word kroswu a jackal is treated in the strong cases (with the elception or the Vocative singular) as ir it ended in trc (tr) note:—The word kroswu is declined like kroswr in the strong cases. kroswa kroswarO kroswara, kroswaran, kroswarO But kroswun in weak cases, and he kroswo in the Vocative singular. The acent in the strong cases is also that or the trc aril, i. e. acute on the rinal. The word kroswu is rorned by the aril tun (uṇ. sitanigani &c., i. 69). The word kroswu is treated as kroswr and thererore the rules aplicable to the words ending in r aply to it, vis, the rolowing sūtras.
ck: 274. the tort krostu a cackal is treatet in the stronk cases (tith the elception or the Vocative sinkular) as ir it entet in trc (tr) note:—the tort krostu is teclinet like krostr in the stronk cases. krosta krostarO krostara, krostaran, krostarO put krostun in teak cases, ant he krosto in the Vocative sinkular. the acent in the stronk cases is also that or the trc aril, i. e. acute on the rinal. the tort krostu is rornet py the aril tun (uṇ. sitanikani &c., i. 69). the tort krostu is treatet as krostr ant thererore the rules aplicaple to the torts entink in r aply to it, vis, the rolotink sūtras.
s: 274. The word क्रोष्टु 'a jackal' is treated in the strong cases (with the exception of the Vocative Singular) as if it ended in तृच् (तृ) Note:—The word क्रोष्टु is declined like क्रोष्टृ in the strong cases. क्रोष्टा क्रोष्टारौ क्रोष्टारः, क्रोष्टारम्, क्रोष्टारौ But क्रोष्टून् in weak cases, and हे क्रोष्टो in the Vocative Singular. The accent in the strong cases is also that of the तृच् affix, i. e. acute on the final. The word क्रोष्टु is formed by the affix तुन् (Uṇ. सितनिगमि &c., I. 69). The word क्रोष्टु is treated as क्रोष्टृ and therefore the rules applicable to the words ending in ऋ apply to it, viz, the following Sūtras.

pk: 275. Guṇa is substituted ror the rinal r or a sten, in the Locative singular and in the strong cases. This rule requires kroswr to be changed to kroswar, but this is prevented by the rolowing.
ck: 275. kuṇa is supstitutet ror the rinal r or a sten, in the Locative sinkular ant in the stronk cases. this rule retuires krostr to pe chanket to krostar, put this is preventet py the rolotink.
s: 275. Guṇa is substituted for the final ऋ of a stem, in the Locative singular and in the Strong cases. This rule requires क्रोष्टृ to be changed to क्रोष्टर्, but this is prevented by the following.

pk: 276. anaṅ ( anan ) is substituted ror the rinal or the stens ending in r as wel as ror the rinal or uśanas, purudaṃśas, and anehas, in the noninative singular (but not in the Vocative singular).
ck: 276. anaṅ ( anan ) is supstitutet ror the rinal or the stens entink in r as tel as ror the rinal or uśanas, purutaṃśas, ant anehas, in the noninative sinkular (put not in the Vocative sinkular).
s: 276. Anaṅ ( अनङ् ) is substituted for the final of the stems ending in ऋ as well as for the final of uśanas, purudaṃśas, and anehas, in the Nominative Singular (but not in the Vocative Singular).

pk: 27. in the strong cases, with the elception or the Vocative singular, the penultinate vowel is lengthened in stens rorned by trn and trc ariles, and in ap, svasr, naptr, neswr, tvaswr, ksatr, hotr, potr and prasastr The words naptr &c. in this sūtra are taken to denote niyana, ror ir naptr &c., be taken as derivative words rorned with the aril trn or trc, there was no necesity or their separate nention in this sūtra, because the word trn and trc or the sūtra would have included then. Thererore we say the inclusion or these words shows niyana, or restriction, nanely, other derivative words rorned by the uṇādi ariles trn and trc are not governed by this rule, such as the words pitr, Bratr &c. But the word udgatr is governed by this rule, because we rind udgatara in the nahābhāṣya. Thus we get the rorns kroswa; kroswarO; kroswara; kroswaran; kroswarO; kroswun in the instrunental and other cases, there are double rorns and the rolowing rules aply:—
ck: 27. in the stronk cases, tith the elception or the Vocative sinkular, the penultinate votel is lenkthenet in stens rornet py trn ant trc ariles, ant in ap, svasr, naptr, nestr, tvastr, ksatr, hotr, potr ant prasastr the torts naptr &c. in this sūtra are taken to tenote niyana, ror ir naptr &c., pe taken as terivative torts rornet tith the aril trn or trc, there tas no necesity or their separate nention in this sūtra, pecause the tort trn ant trc or the sūtra toult have inclutet then. thererore te say the inclusion or these torts shots niyana, or restriction, nanely, other terivative torts rornet py the uṇāti ariles trn ant trc are not kovernet py this rule, such as the torts pitr, pratr &c. put the tort utkatr is kovernet py this rule, pecause te rint utkatara in the nahāphāṣya. thus te ket the rorns krosta; krostarO; krostara; krostaran; krostarO; krostun in the instrunental ant other cases, there are touple rorns ant the rolotink rules aply:—
s: 277. In the strong cases, with the exception of the Vocative singular, the penultimate vowel is lengthened in stems formed by तृन् and तृच् affixes, and in अप्, स्वसृ, नप्तृ, नेष्टृ, त्वष्टृ, क्षत्तृ, होतृ, पोतृ and प्रशास्तृ The words नप्तृ &c. in this sūtra are taken to denote Niyama, for if नप्तृ &c., be taken as derivative words formed with the affix तृन् or तृच्, there was no necessity of their separate mention in this sūtra, because the word तृन् and तृच् of the sūtra would have included them. Therefore we say the inclusion of these words shows Niyama, or restriction, namely, other derivative words formed by the Uṇādi affixes तृन् and तृच् are not governed by this rule, such as the words पितृ, भ्रातृ &c. But the word उद्गातृ is governed by this rule, because we find उद्गातारः in the Mahābhāṣya. Thus we get the forms क्रोष्टा; क्रोष्टारौ; क्रोष्टारः; क्रोष्टारम्; क्रोष्टारौ; क्रोष्टून् In the Instrumental and other cases, there are double forms and the following rules apply:—

pk: 278. kroswu nay optionaly be treated as Kroshṭṛ, berore the endings begining with a vowel, in the instrunental and the cases that rolow it. as kroswra or kroswuna, kroswre or kroswave, kroswu or kroswo, kroswro or kroswvo, kroswri or kroswO But kroswun in the acusative Plural, and kroswuByan berore consonant-begining ariles. in rorning the abl. and Genitive, the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 278. krostu nay optionaly pe treatet as kroshṭṛ, perore the entinks pekinink tith a votel, in the instrunental ant the cases that rolot it. as krostra or krostuna, krostre or krostave, krostu or krosto, krostro or krostvo, krostri or krostO put krostun in the acusative plural, ant krostupyan perore consonant-pekinink ariles. in rornink the apl. ant kenitive, the rolotink rules aply.
s: 278. क्रोष्टु may optionally be treated as Kroshṭṛ, before the endings beginning with a vowel, in the Instrumental and the cases that follow it. As क्रोष्ट्रा or क्रोष्टुना, क्रोष्ट्रे or क्रोष्टवे, क्रोष्टुः or क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्ट्रोः or क्रोष्ट्वोः, क्रोष्ट्रि or क्रोष्टौ But क्रोष्टून् in the Accusative Plural, and क्रोष्टुभ्याम् before consonant-beginning affixes. In forming the Abl. and Genitive, the following rules apply.

pk: 279. in the ron or r + a or the case aril nasi / nas or the ablative and Genitive singular, the single substitute is the leter short u note:—Thus r + a = ur (The u nust always be rolowed by r i. 1. 51) though this is not the substitute or r only, but or r + a conjointly on the nalin that a substitute which replaces two, both shown in the genitive case, as rta and akarasya in this sūtra, gets the atributes or every one or these separately as the son C or a rather a and nother B (though both conjointly produce hin) nay be caled indirerently the son or a or the son or B. so the u nay be caled the substitute or r or a The rinal s is then elided by Vi. 2. 24 and we have hotur = hotu Thus hoturagacCati, hotu svan
ck: 279. in the ron or r + a or the case aril nasi / nas or the aplative ant kenitive sinkular, the sinkle supstitute is the leter short u note:—thus r + a = ur (the u nust altays pe rolotet py r i. 1. 51) thoukh this is not the supstitute or r only, put or r + a concointly on the nalin that a supstitute thich replaces to, poth shotn in the kenitive case, as rta ant akarasya in this sūtra, kets the atriputes or every one or these separately as the son c or a rather a ant nother p (thoukh poth concointly protuce hin) nay pe calet intirerently the son or a or the son or p. so the u nay pe calet the supstitute or r or a the rinal s is then elitet py Vi. 2. 24 ant te have hotur = hotu thus hoturakacati, hotu svan
s: 279. In the room of ऋ + अ of the case affix ङसि / ङस् of the Ablative and Genitive singular, the single substitute is the letter short उ Note:—Thus ऋ + अ = उर् (The उ must always be followed by र् I. 1. 51) though this is not the substitute of ऋ only, but of ऋ + अ conjointly on the maxim that a substitute which replaces two, both shown in the genitive case, as ऋतः and अकारस्य in this sūtra, gets the attributes of every one of these separately as the son C of a father A and mother B (though both conjointly produce him) may be called indifferently the son of A or the son of B. So the उ may be called the substitute of ऋ or अ The final स् is then elided by VIII. 2. 24 and we have होतुर् = होतुः Thus होतुरागच्छति, होतुः स्वम्

pk: 280. Or a word ending in a conjunct consonant, only s is elided, ir it cones arter ra; (but any other consonant coning arter ra is not elided). Thus kroswu + as = kroswursa ere the rinal s is elided and the r is changed to visarga. Thus we get kroswu. Berore the Gen. Pl: an, kroswu requires to be treated as kroswr by Vi. 1. 97. s. 278 but this is prevented by the rolowing:— Vārt:—nun, and nuw augnents cone in supersesion or the Tṛj-vadbhāva ordained by the preceding sūtras. Thus the Dative or the neuter noun priyakroswu wil be priyakroswune brahnanaya, priyakroswave vrsalakulaya, and not ‹?› sinilarly with nuw, as kroswunan The Loc. rorns are kroswari or kroswO ; kroswro &c. Berore ariles begining with consonants there is only one rorn. note:—The word kroswu is rorned ron the rot krus to cry or to cal with the aril tun by the uṇādi i. 69. sinilarly the word kroswr is rorned ron the sane rot with the aril trc Both words denote the sane object, i. e. a jackal. But the word kroswu is derective in the rirst rive cases, where kroswr suplies the want. ere ends the declension or nasculine words ending in short u —:o:— huhu huhvO huhva huhun huhvO huhunityadi aticanursabde tu nadikaryavisesa heticanu aticanve aticanva aticanunan aticanvan Kalapu now, we take up the declension or nasculine words ending in long u as huhu (nane or a celestial songster). The non: and ac: rorns are huhu ; huhvO ; huhva huhun huhvO huhun &c. in declining the word aticanu, the nadī rules wil aply, i. e. i. 4. 3. s. 26, 267, 268 &c. The Voc. sing. is thererore, he aticanu The Dat: sing is aticanve ; abl: and Gen. singular aticanva ; Gen. Pl: aticanunan ; Loc. sing aticanvan now we take up the declension or the noun Kalapu The non: sing is Kalapu in rorning the non; Dual the rolowing rule aplies:—

Or a tort entink in a concunct consonant, only s is elitet, ir it cones arter ra; (put any other consonant conink arter ra is not elitet). thus krostu + as = krostursa ere the rinal s is elitet ant the r is chanket to visarka. thus te ket krostu. perore the ken. pl: an, krostu retuires to pe treatet as krostr py Vi. 1. 97. s. 278 put this is preventet py the rolotink:— Vārt:—nun, ant nut auknents cone in supersesion or the tṛc-vatphāva ortainet py the precetink sūtras. thus the tative or the neuter noun priyakrostu til pe priyakrostune prahnanaya, priyakrostave vrsalakulaya, ant not ‹?› sinilarly tith nut, as krostunan the Loc. rorns are krostari or krostO ; krostro &c. perore ariles pekinink tith consonants there is only one rorn. note:—the tort krostu is rornet ron the rot krus to cry or to cal tith the aril tun py the uṇāti i. 69. sinilarly the tort krostr is rornet ron the sane rot tith the aril trc poth torts tenote the sane opcect, i. e. a cackal. put the tort krostu is terective in the rirst rive cases, there krostr suplies the tant. ere ents the teclension or nasculine torts entink in short u —:o:— huhu huhvO huhva huhun huhvO huhunityati aticanursapte tu natikaryavisesa heticanu aticanve aticanva aticanunan aticanvan kalapu not, te take up the teclension or nasculine torts entink in lonk u as huhu (nane or a celestial sonkster). the non: ant ac: rorns are huhu ; huhvO ; huhva huhun huhvO huhun &c. in teclinink the tort aticanu, the natī rules til aply, i. e. i. 4. 3. s. 26, 267, 268 &c. the Voc. sink. is thererore, he aticanu the tat: sink is aticanve ; apl: ant ken. sinkular aticanva ; ken. pl: aticanunan ; Loc. sink aticanvan not te take up the teclension or the noun kalapu the non: sink is kalapu in rornink the non; tual the rolotink rule aplies:—
s: 280. Of a word ending in a conjunct consonant, only स् is elided, if it comes after र; (but any other consonant coming after र is not elided). Thus क्रोष्टु + अस् = क्रोष्टुर्स Here the final स् is elided and the र् is changed to visarga. Thus we get क्रोष्टुः. Before the Gen. Pl: आम्, क्रोष्टु requires to be treated as क्रोष्टृ by VII. 1. 97. S. 278 but this is prevented by the following:— Vārt:—नुम्, and नुट् augments come in supersession of the Tṛj-vadbhāva ordained by the preceding sūtras. Thus the Dative of the Neuter noun प्रियक्रोष्टु will be प्रियक्रोष्टुने ब्राह्मणाय, प्रियक्रोष्टवे वृषलकुलाय, and not ‹?› Similarly with नुट्, as क्रोष्टूनाम् The Loc. forms are क्रोष्टरि or क्रोष्टौ ; क्रोष्ट्रोः &c. Before affixes beginning with consonants there is only one form. Note:—The word क्रोष्टु is formed from the root क्रुश् 'to cry' or 'to call' with the affix तुन् by the Uṇādi I. 69. Similarly the word क्रोष्टृ is formed from the same root with the affix तृच् Both words denote the same object, i. e. 'a jackal'. But the word क्रोष्टु is defective in the first five cases, where क्रोष्टृ supplies the want. Here ends the declension of Masculine words ending in short उ —:o:— हूहूः हूह्वौ हूह्वः हूहूम् हूह्वौ हूहूनित्यादि अतिचमूर्शब्दे तु नदीकार्यविशेषः हेऽतिचमु अतिचम्वे अतिचम्वाः अतिचमूनाम् अतिचम्वाम् खलपूः Now, we take up the declension of Masculine words ending in long ऊ As हूहू (name of a celestial songster). The Nom: and Acc: forms are हूहूः ; हूह्वौ ; हूह्वः हूहूम् हूह्वौ हूहून् &c. In declining the word 'अतिचमू', the Nadī rules will apply, i. e. I. 4. 3. S. 266, 267, 268 &c. The Voc. Sing. is therefore, हे अतिचमु The Dat: Sing is अतिचम्वे ; Abl: and Gen. singular अतिचम्वाः ; Gen. Pl: अतिचमूनाम् ; Loc. Sing अतिचम्वाम् Now we take up the declension of the Noun खलपू The Nom: Sing is खलपूः In forming the Nom; Dual the following rule applies:—

pk: 281. When a case-aril, begining with a vowel rolows, then the senivowel yan is substituted ror the rinal u or u or a sten containing nore than one sylable, ir the sten ends with a verbal rot ending in u or u not preceded by a conjunct consonant rorning part or the rot. as no rots at the end or a sten end in short u, the later is not nentioned in the translation. Thus Kalapu a sweper:—d. KalapvO, pl. Kalapva so also sastrapu and sastrapvO, and sakrlu dual sakrlyO and sakrlya But luluvatu and luluvu berore tense ariles (non-sup) ; lu—luvO, luva (because consisting or one sylable only). Why do we say rorning part or the rot? Observe, ‹?›; ‹?› ere the conjunct consonant is not part or the rot but is part or the preposition ut + lu ulu Why do we say when not preceded by a conjunct consonant? Observe ‹?›: Why do we say that the rirst nenber nust be a Gati or a Karaka ? Observe paranalu, parana luvO : parana luva Why do we say when a case-aril rolows? Observe ‹?› But the declension or the word svaBu is not governed by this rule but by Vi. 4. 85. s. 273. Thus non. rorns are svaBu; svaBuvO, svaBuva so also svayanBu But the declension or the noun varsaBu (the rog) is direrent and is governed by the rolowing rule.
ck: 281. then a case-aril, pekinink tith a votel rolots, then the senivotel yan is supstitutet ror the rinal u or u or a sten containink nore than one sylaple, ir the sten ents tith a verpal rot entink in u or u not precetet py a concunct consonant rornink part or the rot. as no rots at the ent or a sten ent in short u, the later is not nentionet in the translation. thus kalapu a steper:—t. kalapvO, pl. kalapva so also sastrapu ant sastrapvO, ant sakrlu tual sakrlyO ant sakrlya put luluvatu ant luluvu perore tense ariles (non-sup) ; lu—luvO, luva (pecause consistink or one sylaple only). thy to te say rornink part or the rot? Opserve, ‹?›; ‹?› ere the concunct consonant is not part or the rot put is part or the preposition ut + lu ulu thy to te say then not precetet py a concunct consonant? Opserve ‹?›: thy to te say that the rirst nenper nust pe a kati or a karaka ? Opserve paranalu, parana luvO : parana luva thy to te say then a case-aril rolots? Opserve ‹?› put the teclension or the tort svapu is not kovernet py this rule put py Vi. 4. 85. s. 273. thus non. rorns are svapu; svapuvO, svapuva so also svayanpu put the teclension or the noun varsapu (the rok) is tirerent ant is kovernet py the rolotink rule.
s: 281. When a case-affix, beginning with a vowel follows, then the semivowel यण् is substituted for the final उ or ऊ of a stem containing more than one syllable, if the stem ends with a verbal root ending in उ or ऊ not preceded by a conjunct consonant forming part of the root. As no roots at the end of a stem end in short उ, the latter is not mentioned in the translation. Thus खलपू 'a sweeper':—d. खलप्वौ, pl. खलप्वः so also शस्त्रपूः and शस्त्रप्वौ, and सकृल्लूः dual सकृल्ल्यौ and सकृल्ल्यः But लुलुवतुः and लुलुवुः before tense affixes (non-सुप्) ; लू—लुवौ, लुवः (because consisting of one syllable only). Why do we say forming part of the root? Observe, ‹?›; ‹?› Here the conjunct consonant is not part of the root but is part of the preposition उत् + लू उल्लू Why do we say when not preceded by a conjunct consonant? Observe ‹?›: Why do we say that the first member must be a Gati or a Karaka ? Observe परमलू, परम लुवौ : परम लुवः Why do we say when a case-affix follows? Observe ‹?› But the declension of the word स्वभू is not governed by this rule but by VI. 4. 85. S. 273. Thus Nom. forms are स्वभूः; स्वभुवौ, स्वभुवः So also स्वयंभूः But the declension of the Noun वर्षाभू (the frog) is different and is governed by the following rule.

pk: 282. va is substituted ror the u or varsaBu also, when a case-aril begining with a vowel rolows. as varsaBvO varsaBva This is an elception to rule s. 273. The words BanBu, drnBu, janbu, kaPelu, karkanDu, diDisu are unadi rorned words under unâdi sûtras i. 96. Thus drnBu "an author" or "a reciter"; drnBu, drnBvO, drnBun, drnBvO, drnBun. The rest or the declensions is like those or huhu The word drnBu is rorned ron the rot drnBu with the aril u (technicaly kun) But there is another word drnBu (neaning a kind or tre, snake or nonkey) rorned ron the indeclinable word drn to injure and the verb Bu with the aril kvip The declension or this word is governed by the rolowing Vart:—The seni-vowel substitution takes place when drn, kara and punar precede Bu, as drnBvO, drnBva, punarBuvO, punarBuva, karaBvO (karaBvO), karaBva (karaBva) in this vartika, one reading is kara, and another reading is kara, nanely karaBu or karaBu (the neaning or both is the sane, because kara is rorned by the aril an without changing the sense, under sûtra V. 4. 38, s. 2106). The word punarBu nust be taken as a nasculine derivative word, and not the word punarBu which is always reninine. The nouns drnBu and karaBu are declined like svayanBu note:—acording to Eastern Granarians, these two words are declined like varsaBu ere ends the declension or nasculines in long u Declension or nasculines ending in r. s: 282. व is substituted for the ऊ of वर्षाभू also, when a case-affix beginning with a vowel follows. As वर्षाभ्वौ वर्षाभ्वः This is an exception to rule S. 273. The words भम्भू, दृम्भू, जम्बू, कफेलू, कर्कन्धू, दिधिषू are Unadi formed words under Unâdi sûtras I. 96. Thus दृम्भूः "an author" or "a reciter"; दृम्भूः, दृम्भ्वौ, दृम्भूम्, दृम्भ्वौ, दृम्भून्. The rest of the declensions is like those of हूहू The word दृम्भू is formed from the root दृम्भू with the affix ऊ (technically कूँ) But there is another word दृन्भू (meaning a kind of tree, snake or monkey) formed from the indeclinable word दृन् to injure and the verb भू with the affix क्विप् The declension of this word is governed by the following Vart:—The semi-vowel substitution takes place when दृन्, कर and पुनर् precede भू, as दृन्भ्वौ, दृन्भ्वः, पुनर्भूवौ, पुनर्भूवः, काराभ्वौ (कराभ्वौ), काराभ्वः (कराभ्वः) In this vartika, one reading is कर, and another reading is कार, namely करभू or कारभू (the meaning of both is the same, because कार is formed by the affix अण् without changing the sense, under sûtra V. 4. 38, S. 2106). The word पुनर्भू must be taken as a masculine derivative word, and not the word पुनर्भू which is always feminine. The Nouns दृन्भू and काराभू are declined like स्वयंभू Note:—According to Eastern Grammarians, these two words are declined like वर्षाभू Here ends the declension of Masculines in long ऊ Declension of masculines ending in ॠ. धाता हे धातः धातारौ धातारः ऋवर्णान्नस्य णत्वं वाच्यम् * धातॄणामित्यादि एवं नप्त्रादयः उद्गातारौ पिता व्युत्पत्तिपक्षे नप्त्रादिग्रहणस्य नियमार्थत्वान्न दीर्घः पितरौ पितरः पितरम् पितरौ शेषं धातृवत् एवं जामातृभ्रात्रादयः ना नरौ नरः हे नः We take up the declension of the word धातृ. It is governed by the rules already referred to before, namely VII. 3. 110. S. 275; VII. 1. 94. S. 276., VI. 1. 111. S. 279. and VIII. 2. 24. S. 280. Thus धाता; धातारौ; धातारः Voc. हे धातः Vartika:—After words ending in ॠ the dental न is changed to cerebral ण. Therefore Genitive Pl. is धातॄणाम् The declension of नप्तृ &c. mentioned in VI. 4. 11. S. 277. is like धातृ So also that of उद्गातृ But the declension of पितृ is not like this. पितृ is a Unadi formed word, about which there are two views. Some consider Uņâdi affixes as no affixes at all, and therefore Uņâdi words, as रूढि words. Others consider such words as derivative. According to the first view, the declension of पितृ is governed by VII. 3. 110. S. 275, and the ॠ of पितृ is gunated. Thus Nom. Dual and Pl. are पितरौ; पितरः According to the second view, the word पितृ is considered to be formed with the affix तृन् and तृच् added to the root पा 'to protect' by Unadi sûtra II. 94. Then the sûtra VI. 4. 11. S. 277 is read in a restrictive sense, by taking the word नप्तृ as restricting the rule only to नप्तृ &c. and not to पितृ. Therefore, we never have पितारौ but always पितरौ. Thus पिता, पितरौ, पितरः, पितरम्, पितरौ. The rest of the declensions is like those of धातृ. The words जामातृ, भ्रातृ &c. are to be similarly declined. Sing. s: 283. So also नृ before the Genitive Plural नाम् is lengthened optionally. As स्वं नॄणां नृपते, and एवं नृणां नृपते According to some this option is confined to the Vedas, according to others it extends to secular literature also. Here ends the declension of masculines ending in short ॠ Declension of masculines ending in long ॠ कॄतॄ अनयोरनुकरणे प्रकृतिवदनुकरणमिति वैकल्पिक्रातिदेशादित्वे रपरत्वम् कीः किरौ किरः तीः तिरौ तिरः इत्यादि गीर्वत् इत्वाभावपक्षे तु ऋदुशन इति ऋतो ङीति च तपरकरणादनङ्गुणौ न कॄः क्रौ क्रः कॄम् क्रौ कॄन् क्रा क्रे इत्यादि कॄ and तॄ are two roots, when imitative names are formed, we get the nouns कॄ and तॄ These nouns are treated like verbs कॄ and तॄ on the following maxim. Paribhâshâ:—"An imitative name is like original." Therefore the rule VII. 1. 100 S. 2390. read with I. 1. 51. S. 70. applies to these words. Thus we have किर् and तिर् as bases. Therefore the Nom. forms are कीः, किरौ, किरः; तीः, तिरौ, तिरः These are, in fact, declined like the nouns ending in consonant र् as गिर् The above Paribhasha is, however, optional and the ईर् substitution may not take place. In that case, the rules VII. 3. 110 S. 275 and VII. 1. 95. S. 276 requiring the gunation and अनङ् substitution do not apply, because those rules are confined to bases ending in short ॠ as the word ऋत् in those sûtras shows, for the indicatory त् shows that the short ॠ is to be taken (see I. 1. 70 S. 15). Therefore, the declension of these words is कॄः, क्रौ, क्रः, कॄम्, क्रौ, कॄन्, क्रा, क्रे etc. Here ends the declension of masculines ending in long ॠ Declension of Nouns ending in ऌ गम्लृ शक्लृ अनयोरनुकरणेऽनङ् गमा शका गुणविषये तु लपरत्वम् गमलौ गमलः गमलम् गमलौ गम्लॄन् गम्ला गम्ले ङसिङसोस्तु ऋत उदित्युत्त्वे लपरत्वे संयोगान्तस्य लोपः गमल् शकल् इत्यादि We take the declension of nouns गम्लृ and शक्लृ the imitative nouns formed from the roots गम्लृ 'to go' and शक्लृ 'to be able'. In the Nom. Sing. we have anang by VII. 1. 94. S. 276, as गमा, शका. In the other strong cases, we have guna by VII. 3. 110 S. 275, as गमलौ, गमलः, गमलम्, गमलौ, गम्लॄन्, गम्ला, गम्ले In Abl. and Gen. singular, the sûtra VI. 1. 111. S. 279 and I. 1. 51. S. 70 will apply. Therefore, the ‹?› of the affix will be changed to ‹?› followed by र् Thus we have वाम्लू + अस् = ‹?› + स् The स् itself will be elided, because it is a final consonant. Thus, we have ‹?› So also ‹?› &c. Here ends the declension of Nouns ending in ॡ सेः सयौ सयः स्मृतेः स्मृतयौ स्मृतयः Declension of Nouns ending in ए Now, we take up the declension of the word से. This word is thus formed: स + इ; or स + ई = सेः The short इ is the name of Kama (Cupid), as it may be considered to be derived from the word इन् meaning Vishnu with the ड affix meaning the son of इन्. Similarly ई may be considered to be the feminine of इन्, namely the wife of Vishnu. से may therefore mean 'he who is accompanied by Kama' or 'he who is accompanied by Lakshmi'. Therefore, the word is declined as सेः, सयौ, सयः Similarly the word स्मृते which has also two meanings, 'he who remembers Kama (स्मृत + इ)' or 'he who remembers Lakshmi'. The word स्मृत being Nishtha is placed first in this Bahu-vrihi compound by II. 2. 36 S. 899. Thus we get स्मृतेः, स्मृतयौ, स्मृतयः Here ends the declension of Nouns ending in ए Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ओ We take the word गो; to which the following rules apply:—

pk: Declension or nasculine nouns ending in o We take the word go; to which the rolowing rules aply:— 284. The endings or the strong cases are nit arter go That is, these ariles produce al the nit operations: such as Vridhi &c. as, gO, gavO, gava Why have we aded o to the rorn go, and not when it asunes the rorn gu, as in citragu, sabalagu note:—ow do you elplain the rorns he citrago, he sabalagava? This is done on the nalin angavrte punarvrtavaviDiranisWitasya, (when an operation which is taught in the angâdhikâra Vi, 4—Vi. 4. has taken place, and another operation or the angâdhikâra is subsequently aplicable, this later operation is not alowed to take place). ror when Guna once takes place berore the Vocative and the noninative Plural aril by Vi. 3. 108—109, the nit operation or this rule wil not again take place. Or go in the sutra nay be construed as sanbandha-lakshana shashthi (a Genitive denoting a general relation): and the neaning wil be "that sarvanânasthâna aril, denoting singular, dual, plural, which rerers to the neaning or go or cow". While in citragu, the sarvanânasthâna aril does not rerer to cow but to another object, nanely to a person who poseses brindled cows. o in go in this view is ror specirication only.
