s: Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ओ We take the word गो; to which the following rules apply:— 284. The endings of the strong cases are णित् after गो That is, these affixes produce all the णित् operations: such as Vriddhi &c. As, गौः, गावौ, गावः Why have we added ओ to the form गो, and not when it assumes the form गु, as in चित्रगुः, शबलगुः Note:—How do you explain the forms हे चित्रगो, हे शबलगवः? This is done on the maxim अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिरनिष्ठितस्य, (when an operation which is taught in the Angâdhikâra VI, 4—VII. 4. has taken place, and another operation of the Angâdhikâra is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place). For when Guna once takes place before the Vocative and the Nominative Plural affix by VII. 3. 108—109, the णित् operation of this rule will not again take place. Or गो in the sutra may be construed as Sambandha-lakshana Shashthi (a Genitive denoting a general relation): and the meaning will be "that sarvanâmasthâna affix, denoting singular, dual, plural, which refers to the meaning of गो or 'cow'". While in चित्रगु, the sarvanâmasthâna affix does not refer to 'cow' but to another object, namely to a 'person' who possesses brindled cows. ओ in गो in this view is for specification only.

pk: 285. ror o or a noninal sten + an or the acusative case-ending an and sas, the single substitute is a The word ota is a conpound or a + ota Thus go + an = gan, go + sas = ga Thus gan pasya, ga pasya This debars the Vridhi or Vi. 1. 90. so also dyan or dya pasya; as the word dyo is also a noninal sten ending in o The sarvanânasthâna ariles are nit arter this word also (se Vi. 1. 90) which would have caused Vridhi, thererore, this a debars the Vridhi. The word an here neans the aril or the acusative singular, as it is read in conection with the case-aril sas and as the word supi or the last sûtra governs this also. Thererore the verbal Tense-aril an or the inperect is not neant: thus we have acinavan, asunavan gan, gavO, ga; gaya; gave; go etc. Vârtika:—The sûtra Vi. 1. 90 (s. 284) should be read as oto nit, neaning the endings or strong cases are nit arter bases ending in o Vârtika:—and the endings are nit arter those bases only which have vihitavisesana in then. Thus, the noun sudyo is declined as sudyO; sudyavO, sudyava sone read the sûtra as gota so that the rule wil aply to go only. ir the reading gota be taken, then we eltend this rule to sudyo also: as, sudyO, sudyavO, sudyava, by taking go as nerely ilustrative or al words ending in o; and this is done by the leter t in gota, ror the tapara rule aplies to leters, and not to words, so that gota neans and includes words ending in o. The sarva-nânasthâna ariles are nit only arter original bases ending in o and not arter a derivative base ending in o Thererore the sarvanânasthâna aril su or jas coning arter the base Bano, which the noun Banu asunes in the Vocative case is not to be treated as nit, because the o here is derivative. Thererore he Bano, he Banava sinilarly, the word snrto rorned ron snrta + u neaning he who renenbers u or sanBu, is declined as snrto, snrtarvO, snrtarva, snrtaran, snrtarvO, snrtarva etc. ere ends the declension or nouns ending in o
ck: 285. ror o or a noninal sten + an or the acusative case-entink an ant sas, the sinkle supstitute is a the tort ota is a conpount or a + ota thus ko + an = kan, ko + sas = ka thus kan pasya, ka pasya this tepars the Vrithi or Vi. 1. 90. so also tyan or tya pasya; as the tort tyo is also a noninal sten entink in o the sarvanânasthâna ariles are nit arter this tort also (se Vi. 1. 90) thich toult have causet Vrithi, thererore, this a tepars the Vrithi. the tort an here neans the aril or the acusative sinkular, as it is reat in conection tith the case-aril sas ant as the tort supi or the last sûtra koverns this also. thererore the verpal tense-aril an or the inperect is not neant: thus te have acinavan, asunavan kan, kavO, ka; kaya; kave; ko etc. Vârtika:—the sûtra Vi. 1. 90 (s. 284) shoult pe reat as oto nit, neanink the entinks or stronk cases are nit arter pases entink in o Vârtika:—ant the entinks are nit arter those pases only thich have vihitavisesana in then. thus, the noun sutyo is teclinet as sutyO; sutyavO, sutyava sone reat the sûtra as kota so that the rule til aply to ko only. ir the reatink kota pe taken, then te eltent this rule to sutyo also: as, sutyO, sutyavO, sutyava, py takink ko as nerely ilustrative or al torts entink in o; ant this is tone py the leter t in kota, ror the tapara rule aplies to leters, ant not to torts, so that kota neans ant inclutes torts entink in o. the sarva-nânasthâna ariles are nit only arter orikinal pases entink in o ant not arter a terivative pase entink in o thererore the sarvanânasthâna aril su or cas conink arter the pase pano, thich the noun panu asunes in the Vocative case is not to pe treatet as nit, pecause the o here is terivative. thererore he pano, he panava sinilarly, the tort snrto rornet ron snrta + u neanink he tho renenpers u or sanpu, is teclinet as snrto, snrtarvO, snrtarva, snrtaran, snrtarvO, snrtarva etc. ere ents the teclension or nouns entink in o
s: 285. For ओ of a Nominal stem + अम् of the Accusative case-ending अम् and शस्, the single substitute is आ The word ओतः is a compound of आ + ओतः Thus गो + अम् = गाम्, गो + शस् = गाः Thus गां पश्य, गाः पश्य This debars the Vriddhi of VII. 1. 90. So also द्यां or द्याः पश्य; as the word द्यो is also a nominal stem ending in ओ The Sarvanâmasthâna affixes are णित् after this word also (see VII. 1. 90) which would have caused Vriddhi, therefore, this आ debars the Vriddhi. The word अम् here means the affix of the Accusative Singular, as it is read in connection with the case-affix शस् and as the word सुपि of the last sûtra governs this also. Therefore the verbal Tense-affix अम् of the Imperfect is not meant: thus we have अचिनवम्, असुनवम् गाम्, गावौ, गाः; गया; गवे; गोः etc. Vârtika:—The sûtra VII. 1. 90 (S. 284) should be read as ओतो णित्, meaning the endings of strong cases are णित् after bases ending in ओ Vârtika:—And the endings are णित् after those bases only which have विहितविशेषण in them. Thus, the Noun सुद्यो is declined as सुद्यौः; सुद्यावौ, सुद्यावः Some read the sûtra as गोतः so that the rule will apply to गो only. If the reading गोतः be taken, then we extend this rule to सुद्यो also: as, सुद्यौः, सुद्यावौ, सुद्यावः, by taking गो as merely illustrative of all words ending in ओ; and this is done by the letter त् in गोतः, for the तपर rule applies to letters, and not to words, so that गोतः means and includes words ending in ओ. The Sarva-nâmasthâna affixes are णित् only after original bases ending in ओ and not after a derivative base ending in ओ Therefore the Sarvanâmasthâna affix सु or जस् coming after the base भानो, which the Noun भानु assumes in the Vocative case is not to be treated as णित्, because the ओ here is derivative. Therefore हे भानो, हे भानवः Similarly, the word स्मृतो formed from स्मृत + उ meaning 'he who remembers उ or शंभु', is declined as स्मृतोः, स्मृतार्वौ, स्मृतार्वः, स्मृतारम्, स्मृतार्वौ, स्मृतार्वः etc. Here ends the declension of Nouns ending in ओ

pk: Declension or nasculine nouns ending in E. We take the word rE (wealth). 286. Berore a case-ending begining with a consonant, a is substituted ror the rinal or rE Berore ariles begining with vowels, the E or rE is changed to ay by the ordinary rules or sandhi. Thus ra, rayO, raya; rayan, rayO, raya; raya, raByan &c. ere ends the declension or nouns ending in E. -:0:- Declension or nouns ending in O. We take the word glO. it is declined as glO, glavO, glava, glavan, glavO, glava etc. The sûtra Vi. 1. 93. s. 285 aplied only to bases ending in o and not to those which end in O. Because o and O are not savarṇa leters, a ract which we learn ron Panini nentioning then separately in the naheswara sutras e on and E Oc. ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in vowels. -:0:- DECLEnsiOn Or saKi non. ac. ins. s: Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ऐ. We take the word रै (wealth). 286. Before a case-ending beginning with a consonant, आ is substituted for the final of रै Before affixes beginning with vowels, the ऐ of रै is changed to आय् by the ordinary rules of Sandhi. Thus राः, रायौ, रायः; रायम्, रायौ, रायः; राया, राभ्याम् &c. Here ends the declension of Nouns ending in ऐ. -:0:- Declension of Nouns ending in औ. We take the word ग्लौ. It is declined as ग्लौः, ग्लावौ, ग्लावः, ग्लावम्, ग्लावौ, ग्लावः etc. The sûtra VI. 1. 93. S. 285 applied only to bases ending in ओ and not to those which end in औ. Because ओ and औ are not savarṇa letters, a fact which we learn from Panini mentioning them separately in the Maheswara sutras ए ओङ् and ऐ औच्. Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in vowels. -:0:- DECLENSION OF सखि Nom. Acc. Ins. Dat. Abl. Gen. Loc. Voc. pk: now we take up the declension or the word rana. (This word is rorned ron the rot ran to play with the aril a and the reninine aril wap). The non. sing is rana. The aril is elided by Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. in rorning the non and ac. Dual the rolowing rule aplies :— 287. arter a sten ending in the reninine aril ap si is substituted ror the dual endings O or the noninative and acusative. The n in On is ror the purpose or including Ow also. There is, in ract, no such aril as On taught by Panini any where. Thus rana + O = rane The Pl. wil be rana The Vocative sing is rorned acording to the rolowing sutra.
ck: not te take up the teclension or the tort rana. (this tort is rornet ron the rot ran to play tith the aril a ant the reninine aril tap). the non. sink is rana. the aril is elitet py Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. in rornink the non ant ac. tual the rolotink rule aplies :— 287. arter a sten entink in the reninine aril ap si is supstitutet ror the tual entinks O or the noninative ant acusative. the n in On is ror the purpose or inclutink Ot also. there is, in ract, no such aril as On taukht py panini any there. thus rana + O = rane the pl. til pe rana the Vocative sink is rornet acortink to the rolotink sutra.
s: Now we take up the declension of the word रमा. (This word is formed from the root रम् 'to play' with the affix अ and the feminine affix टाप्). The Nom. Sing is रमा. The affix is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. In forming the Nom and Acc. Dual the following rule applies :— 287. After a stem ending in the feminine affix आप् शी is substituted for the dual endings औ of the Nominative and Accusative. The ङ् in औङ् is for the purpose of including औट् also. There is, in fact, no such affix as औङ् taught by Panini any where. Thus रमा + औ = रमे The Pl. will be रमाः The Vocative Sing is formed according to the following Sutra.

pk: 28. e is substituted ror the rinal a or a reninine sten, in the Vocative singular. Thus rana + su = rane + su = rane The aril su is elided by Vi. 1. 69. s. 193. Thus Voc. sing. Dual and Pl are he rane he rane he rana respectively. The ac rorns are ranan rane rana The n is not aded in the ac. Pl. because it is reninine. The rule Vi. 1. 103. s. 196 aplies only to the nasculine nouns. in rorning the instrunental, the rolowing aplies.
ck: 28. e is supstitutet ror the rinal a or a reninine sten, in the Vocative sinkular. thus rana + su = rane + su = rane the aril su is elitet py Vi. 1. 69. s. 193. thus Voc. sink. tual ant pl are he rane he rane he rana respectively. the ac rorns are ranan rane rana the n is not atet in the ac. pl. pecause it is reninine. the rule Vi. 1. 103. s. 196 aplies only to the nasculine nouns. in rornink the instrunental, the rolotink aplies.
s: 288. ए is substituted for the final आ of a Feminine stem, in the Vocative Singular. Thus रमा + सु = रमे + सु = रमे The affix सु is elided by VI. 1. 69. S. 193. Thus Voc. Sing. Dual and Pl are हे रमे हे रमे हे रमाः respectively. The Acc forms are रमाम् रमे रमाः The न् is not added in the Acc. Pl. because it is feminine. The rule VI. 1. 103. S. 196 applies only to the Masculine nouns. In forming the Instrumental, the following applies.

pk: 289. Berore the case-endings os and berore a or . the instrunental, is substituted ror the rinal a or the reninine-aril. an is the nane given to the aril wa, the ins. sing by the ancient granarians. Thus rana + wa = rane + a = ranaya The instr: dual and Pl rorns are ranaByan, ranaBi in rorning the Dative, the rolowing sûtra aplies :—
ck: 289. perore the case-entinks os ant perore a or . the instrunental, is supstitutet ror the rinal a or the reninine-aril. an is the nane kiven to the aril ta, the ins. sink py the ancient kranarians. thus rana + ta = rane + a = ranaya the instr: tual ant pl rorns are ranapyan, ranapi in rornink the tative, the rolotink sûtra aplies :—
s: 289. Before the case-endings ओस् and before आ of ... the Instrumental, is substituted for the final आ of the Feminine-affix. आङ् is the name given to the affix टा, the Ins. Sing by the ancient grammarians. Thus रमा + टा = रमे + आ = रमया The Instr: dual and Pl forms are रमाभ्याम्, रमाभिः In forming the Dative, the following sûtra applies :—

pk: 290. The augnent yaw is aded to the Dat. abl. Gen and Loc. sg. arter a reninine sten ending in ap Thus rana + ne = ranayaw + ne = ranaya + e = ranayE acording to Vi. 1. 8. s. 72. The abl: and Gen: singulars are thus rorned :— rana + nasi = rana + yaw + nasi = ranaya + as = ranaya The Gen: and Loc: dual ranayo is rorned as rolows rana + os = rane + os (Vi. 3. 105. s. 289) = ranayo The Gen: Pl: is rananan (nunw being aded by Vi. 1. 54. s. 208). The Loc. sing ranayan is rorned acording to Vi. 3. 16. s. 270. Thus rana + ni = rana + yaw + an = ranayan The Loc. dual and Pl are ranayo and ranasu The reninine nouns durga &c. are to be sinilarly declined. now we take up the declension or the reninine Pronoun sarva in the rirst thre cases, it is declined like rana in rorning the Dative and other cases the rolowing rules aply :—
ck: 290. the auknent yat is atet to the tat. apl. ken ant Loc. sk. arter a reninine sten entink in ap thus rana + ne = ranayat + ne = ranaya + e = ranayE acortink to Vi. 1. 8. s. 72. the apl: ant ken: sinkulars are thus rornet :— rana + nasi = rana + yat + nasi = ranaya + as = ranaya the ken: ant Loc: tual ranayo is rornet as rolots rana + os = rane + os (Vi. 3. 105. s. 289) = ranayo the ken: pl: is rananan (nunt peink atet py Vi. 1. 54. s. 208). the Loc. sink ranayan is rornet acortink to Vi. 3. 16. s. 270. thus rana + ni = rana + yat + an = ranayan the Loc. tual ant pl are ranayo ant ranasu the reninine nouns turka &c. are to pe sinilarly teclinet. not te take up the teclension or the reninine pronoun sarva in the rirst thre cases, it is teclinet like rana in rornink the tative ant other cases the rolotink rules aply :—
s: 290. The augment याट् is added to the Dat. Abl. Gen and Loc. Sg. after a Feminine stem ending in आप् Thus रमा + ङे = रमायाट् + ङे = रमाया + ए = रमायै according to VI. 1. 88. S. 72. The Abl: and Gen: Singulars are thus formed :— रमा + ङसि = रमा + याट् + ङसि = रमाया + अस् = रमायाः The Gen: and Loc: dual रमयोः is formed as follows रमा + ओस् = रमे + ओस् (VII. 3. 105. S. 289) = रमयोः The Gen: Pl: is रमाणाम् (नुँट् being added by VII. 1. 54. S. 208). The Loc. Sing रमायाम् is formed according to VII. 3. 116. S. 270. Thus रमा + ङि = रमा + याट् + आम् = रमायाम् The Loc. dual and Pl are रमयोः and रमासु The Feminine Nouns दुर्गा &c. are to be similarly declined. Now we take up the declension of the Feminine Pronoun सर्वा In the first three cases, it is declined like रमा In forming the Dative and other cases the following rules apply :—

pk: 291. arter a Prononinal sten ending in long ap or the reninine, the Dat. abl. Gen. and Loc. sg. receive the augnent syaw and the ap or the sten is shortened. as sarvasyE, visvasyE, yasyE, tasyE, kasyE, BavatyE, Bavatya, sarvasya, visvasya, yasya, tasya, kasya, anyasyE, anyasya But where the sten does not end in long ap or the reninine ‹?› This debars the augnent yaw sarva + syaw + ne = sarva + sya + e = sarvasyE Thus Dat: sing is rorned as rolows. sinilarly the abl: and Gen: singular is rorned. suw in Gen: Pl is aded by Vi. 1. 52. s. 217. Though the reninine pronoun sarva is not nentioned in the sarvadi clas, yet the word sarva is caled sarvanana, ror the ekādeśa a or sarva (sarva + ap = sarva) is considered as the rinal or the rirst, and hence the rule Vi. 1. 52. s. 217 wil aply to it. Thus we get the Gen: Pl: sarvasan The Loc: sing is thus rorned sarva + ni = sarva + sya + an = sarvasyan The Loc: Dual and Pl: rorns are sarvayo and sarvasu so also other reninine Pronouns ending in ap like visva &c. are to be declined.
ck: 291. arter a prononinal sten entink in lonk ap or the reninine, the tat. apl. ken. ant Loc. sk. receive the auknent syat ant the ap or the sten is shortenet. as sarvasyE, visvasyE, yasyE, tasyE, kasyE, pavatyE, pavatya, sarvasya, visvasya, yasya, tasya, kasya, anyasyE, anyasya put there the sten toes not ent in lonk ap or the reninine ‹?› this tepars the auknent yat sarva + syat + ne = sarva + sya + e = sarvasyE thus tat: sink is rornet as rolots. sinilarly the apl: ant ken: sinkular is rornet. sut in ken: pl is atet py Vi. 1. 52. s. 217. thoukh the reninine pronoun sarva is not nentionet in the sarvati clas, yet the tort sarva is calet sarvanana, ror the ekāteśa a or sarva (sarva + ap = sarva) is consiteret as the rinal or the rirst, ant hence the rule Vi. 1. 52. s. 217 til aply to it. thus te ket the ken: pl: sarvasan the Loc: sink is thus rornet sarva + ni = sarva + sya + an = sarvasyan the Loc: tual ant pl: rorns are sarvayo ant sarvasu so also other reninine pronouns entink in ap like visva &c. are to pe teclinet.
s: 291. After a Pronominal stem ending in long आप् of the Feminine, the Dat. Abl. Gen. and Loc. Sg. receive the augment स्याट् and the आप् of the stem is shortened. As सर्वस्यै, विश्वस्यै, यस्यै, तस्यै, कस्यै, भवत्यै, भवत्याः, सर्वस्याः, विश्वस्याः, यस्याः, तस्याः, कस्याः, अन्यस्यै, अन्यस्याः But where the stem does not end in long आप् of the Feminine ‹?› This debars the augment याट् सर्वा + स्याट् + ङे = सर्व + स्या + ए = सर्वस्यै Thus Dat: Sing is formed as follows. Similarly the Abl: and Gen: Singular is formed. सुट् in Gen: Pl is added by VII. 1. 52. S. 217. Though the Feminine pronoun सर्वा is not mentioned in the सर्वादि class, yet the word सर्वा is called सर्वनाम, for the ekādeśa आ of सर्वा (सर्व + आप् = सर्वा) is considered as the final of the first, and hence the rule VII. 1. 52. S. 217 will apply to it. Thus we get the Gen: Pl: सर्वासाम् The Loc: Sing is thus formed सर्वा + ङि = सर्व + स्या + आम् = सर्वस्याम् The Loc: Dual and Pl: forms are सर्वयोः and सर्वासु So also other Feminine Pronouns ending in आप् like विश्वा &c. are to be declined.

pk: 292. The sarvanâna words are optionaly declined as such when they ocur in a Bahuvrîhi conpound signirying direction (i. 2. 26. s. 845). Thus utarapurvasyE or utarapurvayE The Bahuvrîhi conpound speciricaly taught in i. 2. 26. s. 845 and not every other bahuvrîhi. Thererore when the word utara or purva are so conpounded as to denote a nad wonan who canot distinguish betwen north and East, there the word (a nad wonan who canot distinguish betwen north and East) though a bahuvrîhi conpound, rorned or pronouns denoting points or conpas, but as the whole conpound does not denote the internediate points or the conpas but is the nane or a person, it is not treated as a sarvanâna. Thererore its Dative sing wil be utarapurvayE and not utarapurvasyE The word bahuvrihi is used in the sûtra only ror the sake or distinctnes, ror the sûtra would have rerered to Bahuvrîhi conpound even without enploying the word bahuvrîhi in it. The word antara is a sarvanāna denoting outer and so it is declined as antarasyE salayE neaning the outer court, but when the word antara denotes a city it is not a sarvanāna and thererore its declension wil be antarayE nagaryE (se Vârtika under sûtra Vi. 1. 52. s. 217). The words dvitiya and trtiya are sinilarly declined elcept in the nit ariles to which the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 292. the sarvanâna torts are optionaly teclinet as such then they ocur in a pahuvrîhi conpount sikniryink tirection (i. 2. 26. s. 845). thus utarapurvasyE or utarapurvayE the pahuvrîhi conpount speciricaly taukht in i. 2. 26. s. 845 ant not every other pahuvrîhi. thererore then the tort utara or purva are so conpountet as to tenote a nat tonan tho canot tistinkuish peten north ant East, there the tort (a nat tonan tho canot tistinkuish peten north ant East) thoukh a pahuvrîhi conpount, rornet or pronouns tenotink points or conpas, put as the thole conpount toes not tenote the internetiate points or the conpas put is the nane or a person, it is not treatet as a sarvanâna. thererore its tative sink til pe utarapurvayE ant not utarapurvasyE the tort pahuvrihi is uset in the sûtra only ror the sake or tistinctnes, ror the sûtra toult have rereret to pahuvrîhi conpount even tithout enployink the tort pahuvrîhi in it. the tort antara is a sarvanāna tenotink outer ant so it is teclinet as antarasyE salayE neanink the outer court, put then the tort antara tenotes a city it is not a sarvanāna ant thererore its teclension til pe antarayE nakaryE (se Vârtika unter sûtra Vi. 1. 52. s. 217). the torts tvitiya ant trtiya are sinilarly teclinet elcept in the nit ariles to thich the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 292. The Sarvanâma words are optionally declined as such when they occur in a Bahuvrîhi compound signifying direction (II. 2. 26. S. 845). Thus उत्तरपूर्वस्यै or उत्तरपूर्वायै The Bahuvrîhi compound specifically taught in II. 2. 26. S. 845 and not every other bahuvrîhi. Therefore when the word उत्तरा or पूर्वा are so compounded as to denote a mad woman who cannot distinguish between North and East, there the word (a mad woman who cannot distinguish between North and East) though a bahuvrîhi compound, formed of pronouns denoting points of compass, but as the whole compound does not denote the intermediate points of the compass but is the Name of a person, it is not treated as a Sarvanâma. Therefore its Dative Sing will be उत्तरपूर्वायै and not उत्तरपूर्वस्यै The word बहुव्रीहि is used in the sûtra only for the sake of distinctness, for the sûtra would have referred to Bahuvrîhi compound even without employing the word bahuvrîhi in it. The word अन्तर is a Sarvanāma denoting 'outer' and so it is declined as अन्तरस्यै शालायै meaning the outer court, but when the word अन्तरा denotes 'a city' it is not a sarvanāma and therefore its declension will be अन्तरायै नगर्यै (See Vârtika under sûtra VII. 1. 52. S. 217). The words द्वितीया and तृतीया are similarly declined except in the ङित् affixes to which the following rule applies.

pk: 293. arter dvitiya and trtiya the Dat. abl. Gen. and Loc. sg. nay optionaly get the augnent syaw berore which the ap is shortened. as dvitiyasyE or dvitiyayE; trtiyasyE or trtiyayE; dvitiyasya or dvitiyaya; trtiyasya or trtiyaya; dvitiyasyan or dvitiyayan; trtiyasyan or trtiyayan The renaining rorns are like those or rana now, we take up the declension or the word anba acording to Vi. 3. 107. s. 267. the Voc. sing is he anba so also he aka, he ala The rinal a or the word ending in sinple qa, la and ka is not shortened. Thus he anbaqe ; he anbale ; he anbike The declension or jara is sonewhat peculiar. Thus non. sg. jara + su = jara ; non. Dual. jara + O = jarasO ; jara is replaced by jaras (Vi. 2. 101. s. 27) berore the sûtra Ona si (Vi. 1. 18. s. 287) could be aplied. in Gen: Pl: jaras substitution takes place berore the augnent nuw could be aded; hence jarasan But the jaras substitution is optional, so when there is no jaras substitution and berore consonantal ariles jara is declined like rana sone rorn the non. Dual as jarasi; their reason is that si wil replace O even where jaras substitution takes place and sanipatapariBasa is not or universal aplication. The Paribhâshâ is as rolows :— sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya i. e. "That which is taught in a rule the aplication or which is ocasioned by the conbination or two things, does not becone the cause or the destruction or that conbination." This is nowhere to be round. Ques. replacing nay be considered as like ‹?› by the rule or ‹?› (i. 1. 56. s. 49), thererore the rive rules nentioned above, nanely, Vi. 1. 18. s. 287, Vi. 3. 105. s. 289, Vi. 3. 13. s. 290; Vi. 3. 14. s. 268; Vi. 3. 16 s. 270, aply to ‹?›. sinilarly those rules would aply also to nas the substitute or nasika; nis the substitute or nisa, prt the substitute or prtana an arny. (se Vi. 1. 64 s. 264). answer. no, ror the sTanivat rule does not aply in cases or analviDi ror the rive rules nentioned above aply only to those reninine rorns which end in long a and not to those rorns which are substitutes or such long ending word. in ract, in the above rules the word ap should be construed as conpounded or a + ap = ap and ni + i = ni; that is those reninine words in a and i which retain their a and i in this state berore the ariles are aded and not those words which do not end in a and i. ror the sane reason, the rorns ‹?› and ‹?› are not to be governed by these rules ror they end in short ‹?› and short ‹?›. sinilarly the Dative or

(se Vi. 1. 64 s. 264). anster. no, ror the stanivat rule toes not aply in cases or analviti ror the rive rules nentionet apove aply only to those reninine rorns thich ent in lonk a ant not to those rorns thich are supstitutes or such lonk entink tort. in ract, in the apove rules the tort ap shoult pe construet as conpountet or a + ap = ap ant ni + i = ni; that is those reninine torts in a ant i thich retain their a ant i in this state perore the ariles are atet ant not those torts thich to not ent in a ant i. ror the sane reason, the rorns ‹?› ant ‹?› are not to pe kovernet py these rules ror they ent in short ‹?› ant short ‹?›. sinilarly the tative or ati
s: 293. After द्वितीया and तृतीया the Dat. Abl. Gen. and Loc. Sg. may optionally get the augment स्याट् before which the आप् is shortened. As द्वितीयस्यै or द्वितीयायै; तृतीयस्यै or तृतीयायै; द्वितीयस्याः or द्वितीयायाः; तृतीयस्याः or तृतीयायाः; द्वितीयस्याम् or द्वितीयायाम्; तृतीयस्याम् or तृतीयायाम् The remaining forms are like those of रमा Now, we take up the declension of the word अम्बा According to VII. 3. 107. S. 267. the Voc. Sing is हे अम्ब So also हे अक्क, हे अल्ल The final आ of the word ending in simple ड, ल and क is not shortened. Thus हे अम्बाडे ; हे अम्बाले ; हे अम्बिके The declension of जरा is somewhat peculiar. Thus Nom. sg. जरा + सु = जरा ; Nom. Dual. जरा + औ = जरसौ ; जरा is replaced by जरस् (VII. 2. 101. S. 227) before the sûtra औङः शी (VII. 1. 18. S. 287) could be applied. In Gen: Pl: जरस् substitution takes place before the augment नुट् could be added; hence जरसाम् But the जरस् substitution is optional, so when there is no जरस् substitution and before consonantal affixes जरा is declined like रमा Some form the Nom. Dual as जरसी; their reason is that शी will replace औ even where जरस् substitution takes place and संनिपातपरिभाषा is not of universal application. The Paribhâshâ is as follows :— संनिपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य i. e. "That which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination." This is nowhere to be found. Ques. replacing may be considered as like ‹?› by the rule of ‹?› (I. 1. 56. S. 49), therefore the five rules mentioned above, namely, VII. 1. 18. S. 287, VII. 3. 105. S. 289, VII. 3. 113. S. 290; VII. 3. 114. S. 268; VII. 3. 116 S. 270, apply to ‹?›. Similarly those rules would apply also to नस् the substitute of नासिका; निश् the substitute of निशा, पृत् the substitute of पृतना 'an army'. (See VI. 1. 64 S. 2264). Answer. No, for the स्थानिवत् rule does not apply in cases of अनल्विधि For the five rules mentioned above apply only to those Feminine forms which end in long आ and not to those forms which are substitutes of such long ending word. In fact, in the above rules the word आप् should be construed as compounded of आ + आप् = आप् and ङी + ई = ङी; that is those Feminine words in आ and ई which retain their आ and ई in this state before the affixes are added and not those words which do not end in आ and ई. For the same reason, the forms ‹?› and ‹?› are not to be governed by these rules for they end in short ‹?› and short ‹?›. Similarly the Dative of अतिखट्व will be अतिखट्वाय Here also the augment याट् will not apply. नस् is substituted for नासिका in weak cases and is then declined as Acc. Pl. नसः; Instr. Sg. नसा &c., when this substitution does not take place नासिका is declined like रमा Similarly निशा is declined. But before the affixes भ्याम् &c. the श् is changed to ष by the following rule.

pk: 294. ror the rinal consonants or vraśc, bhrasj, sṛj, nṛj, yaj, rāj, and bhrāj, and ror the rinal Ca and sa, there is substituted sa berore jhal leter, or at the end or a word. Thus:— vrasc, Braswun, vrascanan, nulavruw Braswa Braswun Braswavyan Dananrw srj sraswa sraswun rajusrw nrj naswa narswun, narswavyan kansyaparinrw yaj yaswa yaswun yaswavyan upayaw raj sanraw svaraw, viraw, viBraw Thus nis + Byan = nis + Byan = niq + Byan = niqByan; niqBi By Vi. 3. 29. s. 131, there is an optional augnent Duw berore the Loc. Pl.; then this D is changed to d and q to w. This last substitution being considered as asidha because it is a ‹?› rule, the ‹?› and ‹?› are not changed to ‹?› and ‹?› as wil be required by Vārtika under Vi. 3. 28, s. 131. nor wil the rule Vi. 4. 42. s. 14. aply. Thus we get niwsu or niwtsu now apears the rolowing rule also ror aplication.
ck: 294. ror the rinal consonants or vraśc, phrasc, sṛc, nṛc, yac, rāc, ant phrāc, ant ror the rinal ca ant sa, there is supstitutet sa perore chal leter, or at the ent or a tort. thus:— vrasc, prastun, vrascanan, nulavrut prasta prastun prastavyan tananrt src srasta srastun racusrt nrc nasta narstun, narstavyan kansyaparinrt yac yasta yastun yastavyan upayat rac sanrat svarat, virat, viprat thus nis + pyan = nis + pyan = nit + pyan = nitpyan; nitpi py Vi. 3. 29. s. 131, there is an optional auknent tut perore the Loc. pl.; then this t is chanket to t ant t to t. this last supstitution peink consiteret as asitha pecause it is a ‹?› rule, the ‹?› ant ‹?› are not chanket to ‹?› ant ‹?› as til pe retuiret py Vārtika unter Vi. 3. 28, s. 131. nor til the rule Vi. 4. 42. s. 14. aply. thus te ket nitsu or nitsu not apears the rolotink rule also ror aplication.
s: 294. For the final consonants of vraśc, bhrasj, sṛj, mṛj, yaj, rāj, and bhrāj, and for the final छ and श, there is substituted ष before jhal letter, or at the end of a word. Thus:— व्रश्च्, भ्रष्टुम्, व्रश्चनम्, मूलव्रुट् भ्रष्टा भ्रष्टुम् भ्रष्टव्यम् धानामृट् सृज् स्रष्टा स्रष्टुम् रज्जुसृट् मृज् माष्ट मार्ष्टुम्, मार्ष्टव्यम् कांस्यपरिमृट् यज् यष्टा यष्टुम् यष्टव्यम् उपयट् राज् सम्राट् स्वराट्, विराट्, विभ्राट् Thus निश् + भ्याम् = निष् + भ्याम् = निड् + भ्याम् = निड्भ्याम्; निड्भिः By VIII. 3. 29. S. 131, there is an optional augment धुट् before the Loc. Pl.; then this ध् is changed to द् and ड् to ट्. This last substitution being considered as asiddha because it is a ‹?› rule, the ‹?› and ‹?› are not changed to ‹?› and ‹?› as will be required by Vārtika under VIII. 3. 28, S. 131. Nor will the rule VIII. 4. 42. S. 114. apply. Thus we get निट्सु or निट्त्सु Now appears the following rule also for application.

pk: 295. ka is substituted ror sa or Qa berore sa Thererore nis + su (Loc. Pl.) = nis + su = niq + su = nik + su = ‹?›. But the aplication or this rule would be wrong, ror the jas rule is considered as asidha ror the purposes or this rule. sone elplain the last sūtra by conrining it to rots only, they read the anuvṛti or Dato in that sūtra ron the previous sūtra, Vi. 2. 32 s. 325. acording to then, there wil be ‹?› when jas rule is aplied. Thus nijByan, niqBi in ract, acording to this opinion, there is no substitution or sa and so nis + Byan is changed to nij + Byan. Thererore, acording to then, the Loc. Pl. wil be nis + su = ‹?›. The j is not changed to k by Vi. 2. 30 s. 378, because the jas substitution is considered as asidha. Vārtika:—Berore the ariles or the ac. Pl. and the rest the words nansa, prtana and sanu are optionaly replaced by nans, prt and snu. Thererore ac. Pl. or prt wil be prta; instr. sg. prta; instr. Dual prdByan. in the other alternative and in the strong cases, nanely the rirst rive inrlectional cases prtana is declined like rana. The reninine gopa is declined like visvapa The reninine nati is declined like hari elcept in the rolowing cases:— The ac. Pl. is nati; there is no n because it is reninine. sinilarly the instr. sg. is natya and not natina because Vi. 3. 120. s. 24. does not aply to reninine nouns. Berore the nit ariles, nati is governed by the rolowing rule.
ck: 295. ka is supstitutet ror sa or ta perore sa thererore nis + su (Loc. pl.) = nis + su = nit + su = nik + su = ‹?›. put the aplication or this rule toult pe tronk, ror the cas rule is consiteret as asitha ror the purposes or this rule. sone elplain the last sūtra py conrinink it to rots only, they reat the anuvṛti or tato in that sūtra ron the previous sūtra, Vi. 2. 32 s. 325. acortink to then, there til pe ‹?› then cas rule is apliet. thus nicpyan, nitpi in ract, acortink to this opinion, there is no supstitution or sa ant so nis + pyan is chanket to nic + pyan. thererore, acortink to then, the Loc. pl. til pe nis + su = ‹?›. the c is not chanket to k py Vi. 2. 30 s. 378, pecause the cas supstitution is consiteret as asitha. Vārtika:—perore the ariles or the ac. pl. ant the rest the torts nansa, prtana ant sanu are optionaly replacet py nans, prt ant snu. thererore ac. pl. or prt til pe prta; instr. sk. prta; instr. tual prtpyan. in the other alternative ant in the stronk cases, nanely the rirst rive inrlectional cases prtana is teclinet like rana. the reninine kopa is teclinet like visvapa the reninine nati is teclinet like hari elcept in the rolotink cases:— the ac. pl. is nati; there is no n pecause it is reninine. sinilarly the instr. sk. is natya ant not natina pecause Vi. 3. 120. s. 24. toes not aply to reninine nouns. perore the nit ariles, nati is kovernet py the rolotink rule.
s: 295. क is substituted for ष or ढ before स Therefore निश् + सु (Loc. Pl.) = निष् + सु = निड् + सु = निक् + सु = ‹?›. But the application of this rule would be wrong, for the जश् rule is considered as asiddha for the purposes of this rule. Some explain the last Sūtra by confining it to roots only, they read the anuvṛtti of धातोः in that Sūtra from the previous Sūtra, VIII. 2. 32 S. 325. According to them, there will be ‹?› when जश् rule is applied. Thus निज्भ्याम्, निड्भिः In fact, according to this opinion, there is no substitution of ष and so निश् + भ्याम् is changed to निज् + भ्याम्. Therefore, according to them, the Loc. Pl. will be निश् + सु = ‹?›. The ज् is not changed to क् by VIII. 2. 30 S. 378, because the जश् substitution is considered as asiddha. Vārtika:—Before the affixes of the Acc. Pl. and the rest the words मांस, पृतना and सानु are optionally replaced by मांस्, पृत् and स्नु. Therefore Acc. Pl. of पृत् will be पृतः; Instr. Sg. पृता; Instr. Dual पृद्भ्याम्. In the other alternative and in the strong cases, namely the first five inflectional cases पृतना is declined like रमा. The Feminine गोपा is declined like विश्वपा The Feminine मतिः is declined like हरि except in the following cases:— The Acc. Pl. is मतीः; there is no न् because it is Feminine. Similarly the Instr. Sg. is मत्या and not मतिना because VII. 3. 120. S. 244. does not apply to Feminine nouns. Before the ङित् affixes, मति is governed by the following rule.

pk: 296. When a case-aril having an indicatory ṅ (ṅit) rolows, then reninine words ending in short i and u are optionaly terned nadī, as wel as reninine nouns in long ī and ū which adnit or iyaṅ and uvaṅ; but not so the word strī, which is always nadī. reninine words in long ī and ū have ben derined as nadī, words in short vowels can never be terned nadī, while even sone words in long vowels have also ben elcluded ron the scope or the derinition, ir they take iyaṅ and uvaṅ. The present sūtra declares an option in the case or al the above words, when a case-aril having an indicatory ṅ rolows. The case-ariles having an indicatory ṅ are the Dative, ablative, Genitive and Locative singulars. Thus we have:— Dative nataye or natyE, Denave or DenvE; sriye or sriyE; ablative and Genitive nate or natya, Deno or Denva; sriya or sriya; Locative natO or natyan, DenO or Denvan, sriyi or sriyan so also Bruve or BruvE &c. But strī is always striyE &c. When the word nati is treated as a nadī word, then the Loc. sg. requires O by Vi. 3. 18, s. 256. But this is prevented by the rolowing rule.
ck: 296. then a case-aril havink an inticatory ṅ (ṅit) rolots, then reninine torts entink in short i ant u are optionaly ternet natī, as tel as reninine nouns in lonk ī ant ū thich atnit or iyaṅ ant uvaṅ; put not so the tort strī, thich is altays natī. reninine torts in lonk ī ant ū have pen terinet as natī, torts in short votels can never pe ternet natī, thile even sone torts in lonk votels have also pen elclutet ron the scope or the terinition, ir they take iyaṅ ant uvaṅ. the present sūtra teclares an option in the case or al the apove torts, then a case-aril havink an inticatory ṅ rolots. the case-ariles havink an inticatory ṅ are the tative, aplative, kenitive ant Locative sinkulars. thus te have:— tative nataye or natyE, tenave or tenvE; sriye or sriyE; aplative ant kenitive nate or natya, teno or tenva; sriya or sriya; Locative natO or natyan, tenO or tenvan, sriyi or sriyan so also pruve or pruvE &c. put strī is altays striyE &c. then the tort nati is treatet as a natī tort, then the Loc. sk. retuires O py Vi. 3. 18, s. 256. put this is preventet py the rolotink rule.
s: 296. When a case-affix having an indicatory ṅ (ṅit) follows, then feminine words ending in short इ and उ are optionally termed Nadī, as well as feminine nouns in long ī and ū which admit of iyaṅ and uvaṅ; but not so the word strī, which is always Nadī. Feminine words in long ī and ū have been defined as nadī, words in short vowels can never be termed nadī, while even some words in long vowels have also been excluded from the scope of the definition, if they take iyaṅ and uvaṅ. The present sūtra declares an option in the case of all the above words, when a case-affix having an indicatory ṅ follows. The case-affixes having an indicatory ṅ are the Dative, Ablative, Genitive and Locative singulars. Thus we have:— Dative मतये or मत्यै, धेनवे or धेन्वै; श्रिये or श्रियै; Ablative and Genitive मतेः or मत्याः, धेनोः or धेन्वाः; श्रियः or श्रियाः; Locative मतौ or मत्याम्, धेनौ or धेन्वाम्, श्रियि or श्रियाम् So also भ्रुवे or भ्रुवै &c. But strī is always स्त्रियै &c. When the word मति is treated as a Nadī word, then the Loc. Sg. requires औ by VII. 3. 118, S. 256. But this is prevented by the following rule.

pk: 297. arter the reninine nadī words ending in i and u short, an is substituted ror the ni or the Loc. sg. When this rule does not aply, then it is treated as a ghi word and rule Vi. 3. 19 s. 247 aplies. Thus Loc. sg. is natyan or natO. The words sruti, snrti &c. are declined like nati now, we take up the declension or reninine nouns ending in r like tisr, and catasr the reninine or tri and catur which are rorned by the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 297. arter the reninine natī torts entink in i ant u short, an is supstitutet ror the ni or the Loc. sk. then this rule toes not aply, then it is treatet as a khi tort ant rule Vi. 3. 19 s. 247 aplies. thus Loc. sk. is natyan or natO. the torts sruti, snrti &c. are teclinet like nati not, te take up the teclension or reninine nouns entink in r like tisr, ant catasr the reninine or tri ant catur thich are rornet py the rolotink sūtra.
s: 297. After the Feminine nadī words ending in इ and उ short, आम् is substituted for the ङि of the Loc. Sg. When this rule does not apply, then it is treated as a ghi word and rule VII. 3. 119 S. 247 applies. Thus Loc. Sg. is मत्याम् or मतौ. The words श्रुति, स्मृति &c. are declined like मति Now, we take up the declension of feminine nouns ending in ॠ like तिसृ, and चतसृ the feminine of त्रि and चतुर् which are formed by the following Sūtra.

pk: 298. tisr is substituted ror tri and catasr ror catur in the reninine, when a case-ending rolows.
ck: 298. tisr is supstitutet ror tri ant catasr ror catur in the reninine, then a case-entink rolots.
s: 298. तिसृ is substituted for त्रि and चतसृ for चतुर् in the feminine, when a case-ending follows.

pk: 29. r is substituted ror the r or tisr and catasr berore case-ariles begining with a vowel. in the Genitive there is the augnent nuw under Vārtika Vi. 2. 24. s. 280. Thus tisr + nuw + an = tisr + nan. ere the sūtra Vi. 4. 3. s. 209 requires the lengthening or the r but it is prevented by the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 29. r is supstitutet ror the r or tisr ant catasr perore case-ariles pekinink tith a votel. in the kenitive there is the auknent nut unter Vārtika Vi. 2. 24. s. 280. thus tisr + nut + an = tisr + nan. ere the sūtra Vi. 4. 3. s. 209 retuires the lenkthenink or the r put it is preventet py the rolotink sūtra.
s: 299. र् is substituted for the ॠ of तिसृ and चतसृ before case-affixes beginning with a vowel. In the Genitive there is the augment नुट् under Vārtika VIII. 2. 24. S. 280. Thus तिसृ + नुट् + आम् = तिसृ + नाम्. Here the Sūtra VI. 4. 3. S. 209 requires the lengthening of the ॠ but it is prevented by the following Sūtra.

pk: 30. The rinals or tisr and catasr are not lengthened berore nan The Loc. Pl : is tisrsu. The word striyan qualiries tri and catur and not the word anga sten which is or course understod here. Thererore, though the anga nay be reninine, yet ir tri and catur rerer to nasculine or neuter nouns, the substitution wil not take place: as priyastrayosya or priyani trini va asya brahnanya priyatri a Brahnani to whon thre are beloved. dual. priyatriyO, Pl. priyatraya sinilarly priyacatvara, priyacatvarO, priyacatvara The word priyatri wil be declined like nati. The only distinction being that the genitive Pl. wil be priyatriyanan. sinilarly the substitution wil take place even where the anga rerers to a nasculine, or a neuter; when tri and catur rerer to a reninine ; as priyastisro brahnanyo sya brahnanasya - priyatisra brahnana (Vi. 1. 94 ) priyatisrO, priyatisra ir the conpound is analysed as priyastisro yasya tatkulan, nanely, ir the conpound rerers to a neuter word, then the rorn wil be priyatri. ere the non : and ac. case endings su and an are elided by Vi. 1. 23 s. 319 by using the word luk. Thererore, there being no pratyayalaksanan ( se i. 1. 63. s. 263 ), there wil be no tisr substitution. But ir the sûtra i. 1. 63. s. 263 be considered as not or universal aplication, then the tisr substitution wil take place and the non : and ac. singular wil be priyatisr. The non : and ac. Dual and Plural wil be rorned by the rolowing Vartika:— Vartika:—The guna or Vi. 3. 10 s 275 is debared in anticipation by Vi. 2. 10 s. 29 and thererore there wil be the augnent nun by Vi. 1. 73 s. 320. Thus the rorns are priyatisrni and priyatisrni. Berore the instrunental and other case-endings there wil be optionaly nun or the substitution, because the word nay be treated optionaly as neuter or nasculine. Thus priyatisra or priyatisrna &c. now we take up the declension or the reninine noun dvi. The d or dvi is replaced by a acording to sûtra Vi. 2. 102 s. 265 and it asunes the rorn dva. To this is aded the reninine aril wap and thus we get the rorn dve. it is always Dual and is declined as dve; dve; dvaByan; dvaByan; dvaByan; dvayo; dvayo now we take up the declension or the reninine noun gOri. its noninative : rorns are gOri; gOryO ; gOrya its Voc. is he gOri acording to Vi. 3. 107 s. 267. its Dat: wil be gOryE by Vi. 3. 12 s. 268 and Vi. 1. 90 s. 269. The reninine nouns or vani and nadi &c. are sinilarly declined. now we take up the declension or the ren: noun saKi. There arises

tve; tvapyan; tvapyan; tvapyan; tvayo; tvayo not te take up the teclension or the reninine noun kOri. its noninative : rorns are kOri; kOryO ; kOrya its Voc. is he kOri acortink to Vi. 3. 107 s. 267. its tat: til pe kOryE py Vi. 3. 12 s. 268 ant Vi. 1. 90 s. 269. the reninine nouns or vani ant nati &c. are sinilarly teclinet. not te take up the teclension or the ren: noun saki. there arises th
s: 300. The finals of तिसृ and चतसृ are not lengthened before नाम् The Loc. Pl : is तिसृषु. The word स्त्रियाम् qualifies त्रि and चतुर् and not the word अङ्ग 'stem' which is of course understood here. Therefore, though the anga may be feminine, yet if त्रि and चतुर् refer to Masculine or Neuter nouns, the substitution will not take place: as प्रियास्त्रयोऽस्याः or प्रियाणि त्रीणि वा अस्या ब्राह्मण्याः प्रियत्रिः 'a Brahmani to whom three are beloved.' dual. प्रियत्रियौ, Pl. प्रियत्रयः Similarly प्रियचत्वारः, प्रियचत्वारौ, प्रियचत्वारः The word प्रियत्रि will be declined like मति. The only distinction being that the genitive Pl. will be प्रियत्रियाणाम्. Similarly the substitution will take place even where the anga refers to a Masculine, or a Neuter; when त्रि and चतुर् refer to a Feminine ; as प्रियास्तिस्रो ब्राह्मण्यो ऽस्य ब्राह्मणस्य - प्रियतिस्रा ब्राह्मणः (VII. 1. 94 ) प्रियतिस्रौ, प्रियतिस्रः If the compound is analysed as प्रियास्तिस्रो यस्य तत्कुलं, namely, if the compound refers to a neuter word, then the form will be प्रियत्रि. Here the Nom : and Acc. case endings सु and अम् are elided by VII. 1. 23 S. 319 by using the word लुक्. Therefore, there being no प्रत्ययलक्षणं ( See I. 1. 63. S. 263 ), there will be no तिसृ substitution. But if the Sûtra I. 1. 63. S. 263 be considered as not of universal application, then the तिसृ substitution will take place and the Nom : and Acc. Singular will be प्रियतिसृ. The Nom : and Acc. Dual and Plural will be formed by the following Vartika:— Vartika:—The guna of VII. 3. 110 S 275 is debarred in anticipation by VII. 2. 100 S. 299 and therefore there will be the augment नुम् by VII. 1. 73 S. 320. Thus the forms are प्रियतिसृणी and प्रियतिसृणि. Before the Instrumental and other case-endings there will be optionally नुम् or the substitution, because the word may be treated optionally as Neuter or Masculine. Thus प्रियतिस्रा or प्रियतिसृणा &c. Now we take up the declension of the Feminine Noun द्वि. The द् of द्वि is replaced by अ according to Sûtra VII. 2. 102 S. 265 and it assumes the form द्व. To this is added the Feminine affix टाप् and thus we get the form द्वे. It is always Dual and is declined as द्वे; द्वे; द्वाभ्याम्; द्वाभ्याम्; द्वाभ्याम्; द्वयोः; द्वयोः Now we take up the declension of the Feminine Noun गौरी. Its Nominative : forms are गौरी; गौर्यौ ; गौर्यः Its Voc. is हे गौरि according to VII. 3. 107 S. 267. Its Dat: will be गौर्यै by VII. 3. 112 S. 268 and VI. 1. 90 S. 269. The Feminine Nouns of वाणी and नदी &c. are similarly declined. Now we take up the declension of the Fem: Noun सखी. There arises the doubt as to whether this word should take the affix ‹?› under Sûtra VII. 1. 93 S. 248 and the affix should be treated as णित् by VII. 1. 92. S. 253 on the maxim that "A Prâtipadika denotes, whenever it is employed in grammar, also such a crude form as is derived from it by the addition of an affix denoting gender." For the above rules only use the Pratipadika form सखि, and so according to this maxim, they may apply to the Noun सखी when it is Feminine. But this is not the case, however, when a Vibhakti is to be added, because then the above maxim is set aside by the following. Paribhasha:—"A Prâtipadika in a rule that teaches an operation which affects the Pratipadika before a case-termination after the Pratipadika, does not denote a crude form derived from the Pratipadika by the addition of an affix denoting gender." Thus Nom. forms of सखी are सखी सख्यौ सख्यः The rest of the declensions are like those of गौरी. Now we take up the declension of लक्ष्मी. As this word is not formed by the Feminine affix ङीप्, therefore the Nom: Singular affix will not be elided, because the rule of elision taught in VI. 1. 68 S. 252 applies only to those Feminine words which are formed by the Feminine affix ङी. The word लक्ष्मी is an Unâdi formed word. The long ई is not a Feminine affix. Thus Nom. Sing. is लक्ष्मीः The rest of the declensions are like those of गौरी. So are the words तरी, तन्त्री

pk: 301. iyan is substituted ror the i or stri berore an aril begining with a vowel. as striyO, striya in the ac : Dual and Pl : the rolowing rule gives option as regards the iyan adesa.
ck: 301. iyan is supstitutet ror the i or stri perore an aril pekinink tith a votel. as striyO, striya in the ac : tual ant pl : the rolotink rule kives option as rekarts the iyan atesa.
s: 301. इयङ् is substituted for the ई of स्त्री before an affix beginning with a vowel. As स्त्रियौ, स्त्रियः In the Acc : Dual and Pl : the following rule gives option as regards the इयङ् adesa.

pk: 302. Thus strinan The Loc rorns are striyan; striyo: ; strisu. now, we take up the declension or atistri, which neans "one who has surpased the wonan," its non, sing. is atistri ; Dual atistriyO. The augnent nun is aded to the ariles or the Dual and Plural by Vi. 1. 72 and 73 s 314 and 320 The instr: sing: is atistrina; Vi. 1. 73. in the dative and the rest, the neuter is optionaly treated like the nasculine acording to Vi. 1. 74 s. 321. s: 302. The substitution of इयङ् for the ई of stri is optional before the accusative endings अम् and शस् ( अस् ) Thus स्त्रियम् or स्त्रीम् ; स्त्रियः or स्त्री: The Instr : Sing is स्त्रिया ; Dat : Sing स्त्रियै. Abl: and Gen : Sing : स्त्रियाः ; Gen : Dual स्त्रियो: Gen : Pl is formed by the addition of नुट् to the exclusion of इयङ्, because नुट् is taught subsequently. Thus स्त्रीणाम् The Loc forms are स्त्रियाम्; स्त्रियो: ; स्त्रीषु. Now, we take up the declension of अतिस्त्रि, which means "one who has surpassed the woman," Its Nom, Sing. is अतिस्त्रिः ; Dual अतिस्त्रियौ. Verse :— The इयङ् substitution, being taught previously, is superseded by the following rules in the Masculine, because they are taught subsequently, viz. the rule of Guna (VII. 3. 109, S. 241; VII. 3. 111 S. 245.); the ना substitution in the Instr : (VII. 3. 120. S. 244 ) ; the औ substitution (VII. 3. 119 S. 247 ) and the augment नुट् (VII. 1. 54. S. 208) In the Neuter the शी being subsequent replaces the नुट्. Thus the rule 'अतिस्त्री' gives us the form अतिस्त्रयः The Voc forms are हे अतिस्त्रे ; हे अतिस्त्रियौ ; हे अतिस्त्रयः. The Acc forms are अतिस्त्रियम् or अतिस्त्रीम् ; अतिस्त्रियौ ; अतिस्त्रियः or अतिस्त्रीन्. The Instr. Sing is अतिस्त्रिणा. The Dat. Sing is अतिस्त्रये (with the guṇa, according to VII. 3. 111. S. 245). The Abl. Sing. is अतिस्त्रेः ; The genitive forms are अतिस्त्रेः, अतिस्त्रियोः, अतिस्त्रीणाम्. The Loc. Sing. is अतिस्त्रौ formed by अच्च घेः (VII. 3. 119. S. 247 ) The Loc. Dual is अतिस्त्रियोः. Verse :—The substitution taught above, is compulsory before the affixes of the Gen. and Loc. Duals (viz. ओस् ) also the Nom. and Acc. Duals (औ) and optionally before the Acc. Sing. and Pl. अम् and शस् and nowhere else when the स्त्री becomes the secondary member of a compound which denotes a Masculine. When the compound अतिस्त्री denotes a Neuter, then the declension is as follows :—Nom. and Acc forms are अतिस्त्रि; अतिस्त्रिणी; अतिस्त्रीणि. The augment नुम् is added to the affixes of the Dual and Plural by VII. 1. 72 and 73 S 314 and 320 The Instr: Sing: is अतिस्त्रिणा; VII. 1. 73. In the dative and the rest, the Neuter is optionally treated like the Masculine according to VII. 1. 74 S. 321. Thus the Dat : Sing : is अतिस्त्रये or अतिस्त्रिणे. The Abl: Sing : is अतिस्त्रेः or अतिस्त्रिणः and so also is Gen : Sing. The Gen and Loc : Dual अतिस्त्रियोः or अतिस्त्रिणोः &c. When the word is Feminine then it is declined almost like the Masculine with the following exceptions:—The Acc. Pl: is अतिस्त्रीः; Instr: Sing: अतिस्त्रिया. Before the case affixes, the rule of I. 4. 6 S. 296 applies and there is the option. The word स्त्री of the Sutra I. 4. 4. S. 303 which is read by anuvṛtti in the Sutra I. 4. 6. S. 296 is confined to that form of स्त्री which takes the substitution. Therefore the prohibition regarding the non inclusion of the word स्त्री in the Sutra I. 4. 6. S. 296 refers to that form of स्त्री which ends in long ई and not to short इ as in अतिस्त्रि. The result is that the rule I. 4. 6. S. 296 will apply to the word and it will be optionally treated as a Nadî word. Therefore, the Dat: Sing: is either अतिस्त्रियै (as a Nadî ) or अतिस्त्रये (as a ghi ) The Abl and Genitive Sing: forms are either अतिस्त्रियाः (as a Nadî ) or अतिस्त्रेः ( as a ghi ) The Genitive Pl: is अतिस्त्रीणाम् . The Loc : Sing : forms are either अतिस्त्रियाम् or अतिस्त्रौ —:0:— Now, we take up the declension of the Feminine Noun श्री. Its Nom; forms are श्रीः ; श्रियौ, श्रियः The Vocative is governed by the following rule :—

pk: 303. reninine words ending in î and û which adnit the substitute ( iyan ) iyaṅ and ( uvan ) uvaṅ ( Vi. 4. 7 ) are not caled nadî ; elcept the word strî, ( which is caled nadî notwithstanding its substituting iyaṅ ) s. 296. s: 303. Feminine words ending in î and û which admit the substitute ( इयङ् ) iyaṅ and ( उवङ् ) uvaṅ ( VI. 4. 77 ) are not called Nadî ; except the word strî, ( which is called nadî notwithstanding its substituting iyaṅ ) S. 296. The Vocative Singular is therefore हे श्रीः The Dative Sing is श्रियै or श्रिये ; Abl: Sing is श्रियाः or श्रियः by I. 4. 6. But in the Gen ; Pl : the following Sûtra applies :—

pk: 304. reninine words ending in î and û, though adniting iyaṅ and uvaṅ substitutes, are optionaly terned nadî, when the aril ân ( Gen Pl.) rolows, but not so the word strî, which is always nadî. sri + an = sr iyan + an = sriyan ; or sri + an (Vi. 1. 54.) = sri + nuw + an = srinan ; The Loc. sing. is sriyi or sriyan The word praDi is declined like laksni acording to the author or vrtikara and others, because it is taken to be a word which is always reninine ; and which by its own conotation is reninine without the help or any other word. But acording to Kaiyaṭa it is to be declined as a nasculine noun, because it does not denote any gender. When this word is analysed as prakrswa Di then it is to be declined like laksni The only peculiarities being in the ac : sing and Plural, where the rorns are praDyan and praDya The word suDi when analysed as susWuDiryasya "that wonan whose understanding is god" or when analysed as susWu Dyayati ya she who neditates wel, then it is declined as sri acording to Vṛti author. acording to others it is to be declined as a nasculine noun. But when it is analysed as a ‹?› Conpound susWu Di God inteligence it is always to be declined as a reninine noun like sri. The reninine noun granani renale head or a vilage is to be declined like the nasculine noun ‹?› ; because leadership or a vilage is, as a general rule, the duty or a nale person, and so the word in elceptional cases only denotes a renale, and then it nust have sone epithet used along with it to indicate that it rerers to a wonan. sinilarly, the word Kalapu a sweper aplies prinarily to a nale person though a wonan nay ocasionaly take up that work. Declension or reninines ending in u. The reninine noun Denu is declined like nati. We take up the declension or the reninine noun kroswu. in its declension, the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 304. reninine torts entink in î ant û, thoukh atnitink iyaṅ ant uvaṅ supstitutes, are optionaly ternet natî, then the aril ân ( ken pl.) rolots, put not so the tort strî, thich is altays natî. sri + an = sr iyan + an = sriyan ; or sri + an (Vi. 1. 54.) = sri + nut + an = srinan ; the Loc. sink. is sriyi or sriyan the tort prati is teclinet like laksni acortink to the author or vrtikara ant others, pecause it is taken to pe a tort thich is altays reninine ; ant thich py its otn conotation is reninine tithout the help or any other tort. put acortink to kaiyaṭa it is to pe teclinet as a nasculine noun, pecause it toes not tenote any kenter. then this tort is analyset as prakrsta ti then it is to pe teclinet like laksni the only peculiarities peink in the ac : sink ant plural, there the rorns are pratyan ant pratya the tort suti then analyset as sustutiryasya "that tonan those unterstantink is kot" or then analyset as sustu tyayati ya she tho netitates tel, then it is teclinet as sri acortink to Vṛti author. acortink to others it is to pe teclinet as a nasculine noun. put then it is analyset as a ‹?› conpount sustu ti kot intelikence it is altays to pe teclinet as a reninine noun like sri. the reninine noun kranani renale heat or a vilake is to pe teclinet like the nasculine noun ‹?› ; pecause leatership or a vilake is, as a keneral rule, the tuty or a nale person, ant so the tort in elceptional cases only tenotes a renale, ant then it nust have sone epithet uset alonk tith it to inticate that it rerers to a tonan. sinilarly, the tort kalapu a steper aplies prinarily to a nale person thoukh a tonan nay ocasionaly take up that tork. teclension or reninines entink in u. the reninine noun tenu is teclinet like nati. te take up the teclension or the reninine noun krostu. in its teclension, the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 304. Feminine words ending in î and û, though admitting iyaṅ and uvaṅ substitutes, are optionally termed Nadî, when the affix âm ( Gen Pl.) follows, but not so the word strî, which is always Nadî. श्री + आम् = श्र् इयङ् + आम् = श्रियाम् ; or श्री + आम् (VII. 1. 54.) = श्री + नुट् + आम् = श्रीणाम् ; The Loc. Sing. is श्रियि or श्रियाम् The word प्रधी is declined like लक्ष्मी according to the author of वृत्तिकार and others, because it is taken to be a word which is always Feminine ; and which by its own connotation is Feminine without the help of any other word. But according to Kaiyaṭa it is to be declined as a Masculine Noun, because it does not denote any gender. When this word is analysed as प्रकृष्टा धीः then it is to be declined like लक्ष्मी The only peculiarities being in the Acc : Sing and Plural, where the forms are प्रध्यम् and प्रध्यः The word सुधी when analysed as सुष्ठुधीर्यस्याः "that woman whose understanding is good" or when analysed as सुष्ठु ध्यायति या 'She who meditates well', then it is declined as श्री according to Vṛtti author. According to others it is to be declined as a Masculine Noun. But when it is analysed as a ‹?› Compound सुष्ठु धीः 'Good intelligence' it is always to be declined as a Feminine Noun like श्री. The Feminine Noun ग्रामणीः 'female head of a village' is to be declined like the Masculine Noun ‹?› ; because leadership of a village is, as a general rule, the duty of a male person, and so the word in exceptional cases only denotes a female, and then it must have some epithet used along with it to indicate that it refers to a woman. Similarly, the word खलपू 'a sweeper' applies primarily to a male person though a woman may occasionally take up that work. Declension of Feminines ending in u. The Feminine Noun धेनु is declined like मति. We take up the declension of the Feminine Noun क्रोष्टु. In its declension, the following rule applies :—

pk: 305. The word kroswu is treated as ir it ended in ṛ, in the reninine, berore al case-endings. and because kroswu is treated as ir it was ‹?›, the reninine wil be rorned by the aril ṅîp by iV. 1. 5. as given below :—
