s: 305. The word क्रोष्टु is treated as if it ended in ṛ, in the feminine, before all case-endings. And because क्रोष्टु is treated as if it was ‹?›, the feminine will be formed by the affix ṅîp by IV. 1. 5. as given below :—

pk: 306. The aril ṅîp is enployed, in rorning the reninine, arter the crude-rorns ending in ṛ or in n ; Thus kroswu becones kroswri and is declined as non : kroswri ; kroswryO ; kroswrya Declension or reninine nouns ending in û ; The reninine noun vaDu is declined like gOri ; Bu is declined like sri. its Voc. sing is he suBru ow then does the Bhaṭi use the Voc. sing as suBru in the rolowing pasage ha pita kvasi he suBru ? The Bhaṭi has nisaplied sûtra i. 2. 48 s. 656 which is not aplicable because suBru is not rorned by any reninine aril but by the aril ‹?› aded to the rot ‹?› (se uṇâdi i. 68). ir he has not aplied that rule, he night have aplied the sûtra Vi. 3. 107. s. 267 and so shortened the vowel in the Vocative. But ‹?› is not a nadi word, because or the prohibition i. 4. 4. s. 303 and so the rule or shortening wil not aply to it. The use by Kalidasa or the rorn ‹?› in the sentence ‹?› is also eroneous. The reninine noun Kalapu is to be declined like the nasculine noun Kalapu now we take up the declension or the reninine noun punarBu. By the Vartika, under Vi. 4. 84. s. 282, the ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› and thus the yan-substitution is prevented, and thererore the prohibition or the sutra i. 4. 4. s. 303 does not aply to punarBu which is declined like a nadi word. Thus the Voc. sing. is he punarBu. The ac. rorns are ‹?› ‹?› ‹?›. in rorning the Gen. Pl. the rolowing rule wil aply.
ck: 306. the aril ṅîp is enployet, in rornink the reninine, arter the crute-rorns entink in ṛ or in n ; thus krostu pecones krostri ant is teclinet as non : krostri ; krostryO ; krostrya teclension or reninine nouns entink in û ; the reninine noun vatu is teclinet like kOri ; pu is teclinet like sri. its Voc. sink is he supru ot then toes the phaṭi use the Voc. sink as supru in the rolotink pasake ha pita kvasi he supru ? the phaṭi has nisapliet sûtra i. 2. 48 s. 656 thich is not aplicaple pecause supru is not rornet py any reninine aril put py the aril ‹?› atet to the rot ‹?› (se uṇâti i. 68). ir he has not apliet that rule, he nikht have apliet the sûtra Vi. 3. 107. s. 267 ant so shortenet the votel in the Vocative. put ‹?› is not a nati tort, pecause or the prohipition i. 4. 4. s. 303 ant so the rule or shortenink til not aply to it. the use py kalitasa or the rorn ‹?› in the sentence ‹?› is also eroneous. the reninine noun kalapu is to pe teclinet like the nasculine noun kalapu not te take up the teclension or the reninine noun punarpu. py the Vartika, unter Vi. 4. 84. s. 282, the ‹?› is replacet py ‹?› ant thus the yan-supstitution is preventet, ant thererore the prohipition or the sutra i. 4. 4. s. 303 toes not aply to punarpu thich is teclinet like a nati tort. thus the Voc. sink. is he punarpu. the ac. rorns are ‹?› ‹?› ‹?›. in rornink the ken. pl. the rolotink rule til aply.
s: 306. The affix ṅîp is employed, in forming the feminine, after the crude-forms ending in ṛ or in n ; Thus क्रोष्टु becomes क्रोष्ट्री and is declined as Nom : क्रोष्ट्री ; क्रोष्ट्र्यौ ; क्रोष्ट्र्यः Declension of Feminine nouns ending in û ; The Feminine Noun वधू is declined like गौरी ; भू is declined like श्री. Its Voc. Sing is हे सुभ्रूः How then does the Bhaṭṭi use the Voc. Sing as सुभ्रु in the following passage 'हा पितः क्वासि हे सुभ्रु' ? The Bhaṭṭi has misapplied Sûtra I. 2. 48 S. 656 which is not applicable because सुभ्रू is not formed by any Feminine affix but by the affix ‹?› added to the root ‹?› (See Uṇâdi II. 68). If he has not applied that rule, he might have applied the Sûtra VII. 3. 107. S. 267 and so shortened the vowel in the Vocative. But ‹?› is not a Nadi word, because of the prohibition I. 4. 4. S. 303 and so the rule of shortening will not apply to it. The use by Kalidasa of the form ‹?› in the sentence ‹?› is also erroneous. The Feminine Noun खलपू is to be declined like the Masculine Noun खलपू Now we take up the declension of the Feminine Noun पुनर्भू. By the Vartika, under VI. 4. 84. S. 282, the ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› and thus the यण्-substitution is prevented, and therefore the prohibition of the Sutra I. 4. 4. S. 303 does not apply to पुनर्भू which is declined like a Nadi word. Thus the Voc. Sing. is हे पुनर्भु. The Acc. forms are ‹?› ‹?› ‹?›. In forming the Gen. Pl. the following rule will apply.

pk: ekajutarapadan yasya tasnin sanase purvapadasTaninitatparasya pratipadikantanunviBaktisTasya nasya nityan natvan syat aranBasanarTyanityatve sidDe punarnagrahanan spaswarTan yanan baDitva paratvanuw punarBunan varsaBu BekajatO nityastritvaBavat he varsaBu kEyawanate natantare tu he varsaBu punarBuvat nasi naso varsaBva varsaBve varsaBvO varsaBva svayanBu punvat 307. in a conpound, the second nenber or which is a nonosylable, there is n in the ron or n or the second nenber, provided that the n is at the end or a pratipadika, or is the augnent nuw, or ocurs in a vibhakti; and when the rirst nenber contains a cause or change. Telt: The na or na is repeated in this sûtra nerely ror the sake or distinctnes, and not to nake the sutra obligatory (as is the view or the author or the Kâsikâ). Because the sutra would be an obligatory rule even without it, because, the very ract that a separate sutra is conenced, shows that it is not an optional rule like the sûtras Vi. 4. 10 and 1. s. 1054. and 105. The augnent nuw is aded, because it is subsequently taught and supersedes the yan or the Vartika under Vi. 4. 84 s. 282. Thus punarBunan now, we take up the declension or the reninine noun varsaBu. When the word neans a rog, it is both a reninine and a nasculine and hence acording to the opinion or Kaiyata, the Voc. sing. wil be he varsaBu acording to others, the Voc. sing is he varsaBu acording to the Lelicographer nadava, varsaBu is reninine when denoting a rog or the herb caled Punarnava ; and it is nasculine when neaning a rog only, noun. The non : Dual and Pl: are varsaBvO : varsaBva The declension or the reninine noun svayanBu is like that or the nasc noun.
ck: ekacutarapatan yasya tasnin sanase purvapatastaninitatparasya pratipatikantanunvipaktistasya nasya nityan natvan syat aranpasanartyanityatve site punarnakrahanan spastartan yanan patitva paratvanut punarpunan varsapu pekacatO nityastritvapavat he varsapu kEyatanate natantare tu he varsapu punarpuvat nasi naso varsapva varsapve varsapvO varsapva svayanpu punvat 307. in a conpount, the secont nenper or thich is a nonosylaple, there is n in the ron or n or the secont nenper, provitet that the n is at the ent or a pratipatika, or is the auknent nut, or ocurs in a viphakti; ant then the rirst nenper contains a cause or chanke. telt: the na or na is repeatet in this sûtra nerely ror the sake or tistinctnes, ant not to nake the sutra oplikatory (as is the viet or the author or the kâsikâ). pecause the sutra toult pe an oplikatory rule even tithout it, pecause, the very ract that a separate sutra is conencet, shots that it is not an optional rule like the sûtras Vi. 4. 10 ant 1. s. 1054. ant 105. the auknent nut is atet, pecause it is supsetuently taukht ant supersetes the yan or the Vartika unter Vi. 4. 84 s. 282. thus punarpunan not, te take up the teclension or the reninine noun varsapu. then the tort neans a rok, it is poth a reninine ant a nasculine ant hence acortink to the opinion or kaiyata, the Voc. sink. til pe he varsapu acortink to others, the Voc. sink is he varsapu acortink to the Lelicokrapher natava, varsapu is reninine then tenotink a rok or the herp calet punarnava ; ant it is nasculine then neanink a rok only, noun. the non : tual ant pl: are varsapvO : varsapva the teclension or the reninine noun svayanpu is like that or the nasc noun.
s: एकाजुत्तरपदं यस्य तस्मिन् समासे पूर्वपदस्थान्निमित्तात्परस्य प्रातिपदिकान्तनुम्विभक्तिस्थस्य नस्य नित्यं णत्वं स्यात् आरम्भसामर्थ्यान्नित्यत्वे सिद्धे पुनर्णग्रहणं स्पष्टार्थम् यणं बाधित्वा परत्वान्नुट् पुनर्भूणाम् वर्षाभूः भेकजातौ नित्यस्त्रीत्वाभावात् हे वर्षाभूः कैयटमते मतान्तरे तु हे वर्षाभु पुनर्भूवत् ङसि ङसोः वर्षाभ्वा वर्षाभ्वे वर्षाभ्वौ वर्षाभ्वः स्वयम्भूः पुंवत् 307. In a compound, the second member of which is a monosyllable, there is ण् in the room of न् of the second member, provided that the न् is at the end of a pratipadika, or is the augment नुट्, or occurs in a vibhakti; and when the first member contains a cause of change. Text: The ण or न is repeated in this sûtra merely for the sake of distinctness, and not to make the sutra obligatory (as is the view of the author of the Kâsikâ). Because the sutra would be an obligatory rule even without it, because, the very fact that a separate sutra is commenced, shows that it is not an optional rule like the sûtras VIII. 4. 10 and 11. S. 1054. and 1055. The augment नुट् is added, because it is subsequently taught and supersedes the यण् of the Vartika under VI. 4. 84 S. 282. Thus पुनर्भूणाम् Now, we take up the declension of the Feminine Noun वर्षाभू. When the word means a frog, it is both a Feminine and a Masculine and hence according to the opinion of Kaiyata, the Voc. Sing. will be हे वर्षाभूः According to others, the Voc. Sing is हे वर्षाभु According to the Lexicographer Yadava, वर्षाभू is feminine when denoting a frog or the herb called Punarnava ; and it is masculine when meaning a frog only, Noun. The Nom : Dual and Pl: are वर्षाभ्वौ : वर्षाभ्वः The declension of the Feminine Noun स्वयंभू is like that of the Masc Noun.

pk: We take up the declension or the neuter noun jnana in rorning non : sing the rolowing rule aplies. 309. arter a neutral sten in a, an is substituted ror su and an the endings or the non. and ac. sing. Thus jnana + an = jnanan (se Vi. 1. 17. s. 194) in rorning the Voc. sg. the consonant only or the non : sg. is elided by Vi. 1. 69. s. 193. Thus he jnana ; i. e. the n or an is elided and not the a.
ck: te take up the teclension or the neuter noun cnana in rornink non : sink the rolotink rule aplies. 309. arter a neutral sten in a, an is supstitutet ror su ant an the entinks or the non. ant ac. sink. thus cnana + an = cnanan (se Vi. 1. 17. s. 194) in rornink the Voc. sk. the consonant only or the non : sk. is elitet py Vi. 1. 69. s. 193. thus he cnana ; i. e. the n or an is elitet ant not the a.
s: We take up the declension of the Neuter Noun ज्ञान In forming Nom : Sing the following rule applies. 309. After a Neutral stem in अ, अम् is substituted for सु and अम् the endings of the nom. and acc. sing. Thus ज्ञान + अम् = ज्ञानम् (See VI. 1. 117. S. 194) In forming the Voc. Sg. the consonant only of the Nom : Sg. is elided by VI. 1. 69. S. 193. Thus हे ज्ञान ; i. e. the म् of अम् is elided and not the अ.

pk: 310. arter a neutral sten, si is substituted ror the non. and ac. dual O and the base gets the designation or Bha. note:—By sutra i. 1. 43. s. 29 the ariles coning arter neuter bases are not sarva-nana sthâna, consequently the base berore such ariles is bha by i. 4. 18. s. 231 ir such aril begins with a Vowel, si is such an aril and thererore the base berore this aril is bha and hence the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 310. arter a neutral sten, si is supstitutet ror the non. ant ac. tual O ant the pase kets the tesiknation or pha. note:—py sutra i. 1. 43. s. 29 the ariles conink arter neuter pases are not sarva-nana sthâna, consetuently the pase perore such ariles is pha py i. 4. 18. s. 231 ir such aril pekins tith a Votel, si is such an aril ant thererore the pase perore this aril is pha ant hence the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 310. After a neutral stem, शी is substituted for the nom. and acc. dual औ and the base gets the designation of Bha. Note:—By Sutra I. 1. 43. S. 229 the affixes coming after Neuter bases are not Sarva-nama Sthâna, consequently the base before such affixes is bha by I. 4. 18. S. 231 if such affix begins with a Vowel, शी is such an affix and therefore the base before this affix is bha and hence the following rule applies.

pk: 31. The rinal i and a (both long and short), or a bha sten, are elided berore a Tadhita aril and berore the reninine aril i Thus jnana + si = jnan + i = jnani. But this is not the corect rorn. The elision or a is prevented by the rolowing Vartika :— Vart:—Prohibition nust be stated in the case or i (si), when it is the substitute or O (Vi. 1. 19), being the case aril or the non. and ac. dual in the neuter and or certain reninines in long a Berore this i, the preceding vowels, a and a are not elided. The sten berore this i is also bha by i. 4. 18 in the case or neuter nouns. Thus jnana + i = jnane it is owing to this Vartika, that we have inserted the word reninine in the translation or the sûtra. in rorning the non: and ac: Plurals, the rolowing rules aply
ck: 31. the rinal i ant a (poth lonk ant short), or a pha sten, are elitet perore a tathita aril ant perore the reninine aril i thus cnana + si = cnan + i = cnani. put this is not the corect rorn. the elision or a is preventet py the rolotink Vartika :— Vart:—prohipition nust pe statet in the case or i (si), then it is the supstitute or O (Vi. 1. 19), peink the case aril or the non. ant ac. tual in the neuter ant or certain reninines in lonk a perore this i, the precetink votels, a ant a are not elitet. the sten perore this i is also pha py i. 4. 18 in the case or neuter nouns. thus cnana + i = cnane it is otink to this Vartika, that te have insertet the tort reninine in the translation or the sûtra. in rornink the non: ant ac: plurals, the rolotink rules aply
s: 311. The final इ and अ (both long and short), of a bha stem, are elided before a Taddhita affix and before the feminine affix ई Thus ज्ञान + शी = ज्ञान् + ई = ज्ञानी. But this is not the correct form. The elision of अ is prevented by the following Vartika :— Vart:—Prohibition must be stated in the case of ई (शी), when it is the substitute of औ (VII. 1. 19), being the case affix of the nom. and acc. dual in the neuter and of certain feminines in long आ Before this ई, the preceding vowels, अ and आ are not elided. The stem before this ई is also bha by I. 4. 18 in the case of Neuter nouns. Thus ज्ञान + ई = ज्ञाने It is owing to this Vartika, that we have inserted the word 'feminine' in the translation of the sûtra. In forming the Nom: and Acc: Plurals, the following rules apply

pk: 312. arter a neutral sten, si is substituted ror the endings or the noninative and acusative Plural (jas and sas) Thus jnana + jas or sas = jnana + si. now, this gets the designation or sarvanâna sthâna as taught in the nelt sûtra and being so caled, the sûtra arter that aplies to it; by which a n is inserted.
ck: 312. arter a neutral sten, si is supstitutet ror the entinks or the noninative ant acusative plural (cas ant sas) thus cnana + cas or sas = cnana + si. not, this kets the tesiknation or sarvanâna sthâna as taukht in the nelt sûtra ant peink so calet, the sûtra arter that aplies to it; py thich a n is insertet.
s: 312. After a neutral stem, शि is substituted for the endings of the Nominative and Accusative Plural (जस् and शस्) Thus ज्ञान + जस् or शस् = ज्ञान + शि. Now, this gets the designation of Sarvanâma Sthâna as taught in the next Sûtra and being so called, the Sûtra after that applies to it; by which a न् is inserted.

pk: 313. The aril si (Vi. 1. 20) is caled sarvanânasthâna.
ck: 313. the aril si (Vi. 1. 20) is calet sarvanânasthâna.
s: 313. The affix शि (VII. 1. 20) is called sarvanâmasthâna.

pk: 314. The augnent nun is aded in the strong cases to a neuter sten ending in a consonant (other than a nasal or a senivowel), or ending in a vowel. Thus jnana + si = jnana + nun + si = jnana + n + i = jnana + ni = jnanani. The penultinate vowel is lengthened by Vi. 4. 8. s. 250. The ac: rorns are sinilar to those or the noninative. The rest are declined like those or rana Thus are to be declined the neuter nouns Dana, vana, Pala &c.
ck: 314. the auknent nun is atet in the stronk cases to a neuter sten entink in a consonant (other than a nasal or a senivotel), or entink in a votel. thus cnana + si = cnana + nun + si = cnana + n + i = cnana + ni = cnanani. the penultinate votel is lenkthenet py Vi. 4. 8. s. 250. the ac: rorns are sinilar to those or the noninative. the rest are teclinet like those or rana thus are to pe teclinet the neuter nouns tana, vana, pala &c.
s: 314. The augment नुम् is added in the strong cases to a Neuter stem ending in a consonant (other than a nasal or a semivowel), or ending in a vowel. Thus ज्ञान + शि = ज्ञान + नुम् + शि = ज्ञान + न् + इ = ज्ञान + नि = ज्ञानानि. The penultimate vowel is lengthened by VI. 4. 8. S. 250. The Acc: forms are similar to those of the Nominative. The rest are declined like those of राम Thus are to be declined the Neuter Nouns धन, वन, फल &c.

pk: now we take up the declension or the word katara. in its declension, the rolowing rule aplies. 315. adaq is substituted ror the non. and ac. singular endings su and an arter the rive Pronouns qatara &c. (i. e. the stens rorned with the ariles 1. qatara, and 2. qatana, and the stens 3. itara, 4. anya and 5. anyatara). note:—These are the rive pronouns, which in the list or sarvanânans are read together (se i. 1. 27. s. 213)—qatara, qatana, itara, anya and anyatara Thus katara + adaq = katarat (the a or katara elided by q): as katarat tisWati katarat pasya The rorce or this indicative leter qa in the aril adaq is to elide the rinal vowel by the rolowing sûtra.
ck: not te take up the teclension or the tort katara. in its teclension, the rolotink rule aplies. 315. atat is supstitutet ror the non. ant ac. sinkular entinks su ant an arter the rive pronouns tatara &c. (i. e. the stens rornet tith the ariles 1. tatara, ant 2. tatana, ant the stens 3. itara, 4. anya ant 5. anyatara). note:—these are the rive pronouns, thich in the list or sarvanânans are reat tokether (se i. 1. 27. s. 213)—tatara, tatana, itara, anya ant anyatara thus katara + atat = katarat (the a or katara elitet py t): as katarat tistati katarat pasya the rorce or this inticative leter ta in the aril atat is to elite the rinal votel py the rolotink sûtra.
s: Now we take up the declension of the word कतर. In its declension, the following rule applies. 315. अदड् is substituted for the Nom. and Acc. singular endings सु and अम् after the five Pronouns डतर &c. (i. e. the stems formed with the affixes 1. डतर, and 2. डतम, and the stems 3. इतर, 4. अन्य and 5. अन्यतर). Note:—These are the five pronouns, which in the list of Sarvanâmans are read together (See I. 1. 27. S. 213)—डतर, डतम, इतर, अन्य and अन्यतर Thus कतर + अदड् = कतरत् (the अ of katara elided by ड्): as कतरत् तिष्ठति कतरत् पश्य The force of this indicative letter ड in the affix अदड् is to elide the final vowel by the following Sûtra.

pk: 316. Berore an aril having an indicatory q, the last vowel, with the consonant, ir any, that rolows it, is elided in the case or a bha sten. Thus katara + su or an = katara + ad = katar + ad = katarad or katarat (d is optionaly changed to t by Vi. 4. 56. s. 206.) The non: and ac: Dual and Pl rorns are katare ; katarani. Why have we read the anuvriti or bha in this sutra ? Observe pancana note:—The anuvriti or bha is read into this sûtra ron Vi. 4. 129. s. 23, the word pancana is rorned by ading the aril qaw to the word pancan with the augnent naw (V. 2. 48 & 49 s. 1849 and 1850). Thus pancan + qaw. The aril qaw does not cause the elision or the an or pancan but the n is elided because it is rinal in a pada (se Vi. 2. 7. s. 236). Why do we nake the aril have an indicatory q? in order to prevent the lengthening or the vowel in the noninative singular : as katara + at = katarat by Vi. 1. 102. in the case or the acusative, ad being the substitute or an wil be sthanivat, and give us katarat by Vi. 1. 107 even without Why not nake the aril nerely ‹?› and not ‹?›; it would give a ‹?› &c. without the aplication or any rule or sandhi? The sinple ‹?› would not give us the Vocative ‹?›. The rinal ‹?› would have ben elided in the Vocative, as being an apṛkta. se however Vi. 1. 69. s. 193. ir in the sûtra Vi. 1. 69, there is the anuvṛiti or the word apṛkta then there is rault with regard to ‹?› (i.e. the vocative or nenbers in ‹?› wil not be elided, ‹?› wil be the rorn required and not ‹?›); ir however, the anuvṛiti or apṛkta ceases, there wil be anonaly with regard to pronouns &c (i.e. we shal not have the rorn ‹?› but ‹?›). Thererore, by reading the aril with an indicatory ‹?› i.e reading it as ‹?› we get out or this dilena, and so there is not the elision or ‹?› in ‹?› &c in the vocative, nor is there lengthening or the vowel (which would have ben the rorn had there ben no ‹?›). Thus the Voc: sing. is ‹?›. The ac. rorns are sinilar to those or the noninative. in the rest the declension is like that or the nasculine. The declension or katana, itara, anya and anyatara is like that or katara. Thus katanat itarat anyat and anyatarat The word anyatana rorns its non: and ac: sing anyatanan and not anyatanat Thererore it is a nistake to say sananyadisvanyatanatana Vartika:—Prohibition nust be stated with regard to the word ekatara although it is rorned with the aril ‹?›. Thus its non: sing is ekataran and not ekatarat. now, we take up the declension or the neuter noun ‹?›
ck: 316. perore an aril havink an inticatory t, the last votel, tith the consonant, ir any, that rolots it, is elitet in the case or a pha sten. thus katara + su or an = katara + at = katar + at = katarat or katarat (t is optionaly chanket to t py Vi. 4. 56. s. 206.) the non: ant ac: tual ant pl rorns are katare ; katarani. thy have te reat the anuvriti or pha in this sutra ? Opserve pancana note:—the anuvriti or pha is reat into this sûtra ron Vi. 4. 129. s. 23, the tort pancana is rornet py atink the aril tat to the tort pancan tith the auknent nat (V. 2. 48 & 49 s. 1849 ant 1850). thus pancan + tat. the aril tat toes not cause the elision or the an or pancan put the n is elitet pecause it is rinal in a pata (se Vi. 2. 7. s. 236). thy to te nake the aril have an inticatory t? in orter to prevent the lenkthenink or the votel in the noninative sinkular : as katara + at = katarat py Vi. 1. 102. in the case or the acusative, at peink the supstitute or an til pe sthanivat, ant kive us katarat py Vi. 1. 107 even tithout thy not nake the aril nerely ‹?› ant not ‹?›; it toult kive a ‹?› &c. tithout the aplication or any rule or santhi? s: 316. Before an affix having an indicatory ड्, the last vowel, with the consonant, if any, that follows it, is elided in the case of a bha stem. Thus कतर + सु or अम् = कतर + अद् = कतर् + अद् = कतरद् or कतरत् (द् is optionally changed to त् by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206.) The Nom: and Acc: Dual and Pl forms are कतरे ; कतराणि. Why have we read the anuvritti of bha in this Sutra ? Observe पञ्चमः Note:—The anuvritti of bha is read into this Sûtra from VI. 4. 129. S. 233, the word पञ्चम is formed by adding the affix डट् to the word पञ्चन् with the augment मट् (V. 2. 48 & 49 S. 1849 and 1850). Thus पञ्चन् + डट्. The affix डट् does not cause the elision of the अन् of पञ्चन् but the न् is elided because it is final in a pada (See VIII. 2. 7. S. 236). Why do we make the affix have an indicatory ड्? In order to prevent the lengthening of the vowel in the nominative singular : as कतर + अत् = कतरात् by VI. 1. 102. In the case of the accusative, अद् being the substitute of अम् will be sthanivat, and give us कतरत् by VI. 1. 107 even without Why not make the affix merely ‹?› and not ‹?›; it would give a ‹?› &c. without the application of any rule of Sandhi? The simple ‹?› would not give us the Vocative ‹?›. The final ‹?› would have been elided in the Vocative, as being an apṛkta. See however VI. 1. 69. S. 193. If in the Sûtra VI. 1. 69, there is the anuvṛitti of the word 'apṛkta' then there is fault with regard to ‹?› (i.e. the vocative of members in ‹?› will not be elided, ‹?› will be the form required and not ‹?›); if however, the anuvṛitti of apṛkta ceases, there will be anomaly with regard to pronouns &c (i.e. we shall not have the form ‹?› but ‹?›). Therefore, by reading the affix with an indicatory ‹?› i.e reading it as ‹?› we get out of this dilemma, and so there is not the elision of ‹?› in ‹?› &c in the vocative, nor is there lengthening of the vowel (which would have been the form had there been no ‹?›). Thus the Voc: Sing. is ‹?›. The Acc. forms are similar to those of the Nominative. In the rest the declension is like that of the Masculine. The declension of कतम, इतर, अन्य and अन्यतर is like that of कतर. Thus कतमत् इतरत् अन्यत् and अन्यतरत् The word अन्यतम forms its Nom: and Acc: Sing अन्यतमम् and not अन्यतमत् Therefore it is a mistake to say सामान्यादिष्वन्यतमत्तमः Vartika:—Prohibition must be stated with regard to the word एकतर although it is formed with the affix ‹?›. Thus its Nom: Sing is एकतरम् and not एकतरत्. Now, we take up the declension of the Neuter Noun ‹?› meaning 'one who does not decay' (‹?›). The ‹?› of जरा is shortened by I. 2. 48. S. 656. Thus we get the form अजर. Thus अजर + सु = अजर + अम् (VII. 1. 24. S. 309). At this stage Sûtra VII. 2. 101. S. 227 requires the substitution of जरस् in the place of जर, but this is prohibited by the maxim सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination. For अम् is added to अजर as it ended in अ and since अ has caused the production of अम्, this latter affix though beginning with a vowel will not cause जरस् to be substituted for जर. Thus Nom. Singular is अजरम् dual is—अजरसी or अजरे. In the case of Nom Plural there is affix शि, and when जरस् is substituted, then we have the augment नुम् (VII. 1. 72. S. 314) because शि is Sarvanâmasthâna. This must be added after the substitution has taken place, because जरस् substitution is taught by VII. 2. 101 S. 227. which is latter in order of the Ashtadhyayi than नुम् augment which is taught by VII. 1. 72 S. 314. Thus अजर + शि = जरस् + नुम् + अजरन्स् + शि. At this stage, applies the following Sûtra,

Or these luk elision is superseded by an or Vi. 1. 24 which is an elception to Vi. 1. 23; and in its turn an is replaced by the jaras or Vi. 2. 101. jaras being substituted ror jara, we have ajaras, now luk canot again apear and cause elision, as it has already lost the oportunity: and we are lert with an alone, and have ajarasan When there is no jaras substitution, the ac. sing. wil be ajaran The ac: Dual wil be ajarasi or ajare and Pl: ajaransi or ajarani The rest or the declensions is like those or the nasculine. note:—The rorn ajaransi is thus evolved: ajara + si. ere ir the nun augnent be aded rirst, it wil be a portion or the anga, and wil not be an intervention to anything which is to be aded or operated upon the anga. s: 317. In the strong cases with the exception of Vocative singular, the penultimate vowel is lengthened, in the case of a stem ending in स्, with a Nasal consonant preceding it, and of महत् That is, a stem ending in the conjunct consonant न्स्, elongates its penultimate vowel before the affixes of the first five cases. Thus अजरांसि. When जरस् substitution does not take place, the Nom. Pl. will be अजराणि. In the Acc: Sing:, we have अजर + अम्. Here three rules present themselves simultaneously; first luk-elision of the affix अम् by VII. 1. 23, (2) then the अम् substitution by VII. 1. 24, (3) and thirdly, जरस् for जर by VII. 2. 101. Of these लुक् elision is superseded by अम् of VII. 1. 24 which is an exception to VII. 1. 23; and in its turn अम् is replaced by the जरस् of VII. 2. 101. जरस् being substituted for जर, we have अजरस्, now luk cannot again appear and cause elision, as it has already lost the opportunity: and we are left with अम् alone, and have अजरसम् When there is no जरस् substitution, the Acc. Sing. will be अजरम् The Acc: Dual will be अजरसी or अजरे and Pl: अजरांसि or अजराणि The rest of the declensions is like those of the Masculine. Note:—The form अजरांसि is thus evolved: अजर + शि. Here if the नुम् augment be added first, it will be a portion of the anga, and will not be an intervention to anything which is to be added or operated upon the anga. But this augment will be an intervention with regard to जरा which is but a portion of the word अजर So that an operation applicable to जरा will not take effect, because of this intervention. And though tadantavidhi applies in these chapters (पदाधिकारे तस्य च तदन्तस्य च) yet the maxim is that the substitutes only replace those which are specifically exhibited in a rule (निर्दिश्यमानस्य आदेशा भवन्ति), therefore जरस् would not replace जरा which forms only a portion of a full word अजर Even if the substitution does take place, the नुम् would be found after the स् of जरस् Therefore, the substitution should be made first, because this is a subsequent rule; and having done so, the नुम् should be added afterwards under VII. 1. 72. The form अजरसम् is thus evolved. We have अजर + अम् Here on the maxim एकदेशविकृतस्य अनन्यत्वात्, we substitute जरस् for जर also, (for जर and जरा are considered as one). Then appears VII. 1. 23. ordaining the luk of अम् and VII. 1. 24. teaching अम् The latter rule is preferred for the reasons given above. Now, we take up the declension of पद्दन &c referred to in Sûtra VI. 1. 63. S. 228. The word हृदय is replaced by हृद्, उदक by उदन् and आस्य by आसन् and मांस् by मांस्. Thus in the weak cases (that is, Acc. Plural and onwards) the forms are हृन्ति, हृदा, हृद्भ्याम् &c; उदानि, उद्ना, उद्भ्याम् &c; आसानि, आसा, आसभ्याम् &c; मांसि, मांसा, मान्भ्याम्, &c. In fact, the word प्रभृति is used in the Sûtra VI. 1. 63. S. 228. in order to indicate method, so that not only the words mentioned in that sûtra, but other words also take such substituted forms before the weak cases. Therefore the author of Mahâbhâshya gives the example of 'मांस्पचन्या उखायाः'. Here there is not the elision of the final of the conjunct consonant स्. Note:—मांस्पचन्याः is thus formed. From the root पच् we form पचन with the affix ल्युट् in the sense of instrument and location, under Sûtra, III. 3. 93. S. 3271. meaning the vessel for cooking. To पचन is added the feminine affix ङीप्. मांसस्य पचनी मांस्पचनी. Here in forming the compound the genitive sign is elided by लुक् and the affix so elided leaves no trace behind by the Sûtra I. 1. 63. S. 263 and therefore मांस् would not have been substituted for मांस, but for the fact of our having explained the word प्रभृति in the sense प्रकार. By taking this compound under I. 4. 20. S. 3390 and taking it to be a bha, there is not संयोगान्तलोप. Moreover, if in the Sûtra VI. 1. 63. S. 228. the anuvṛitti of छन्दसि be read from the Sûtra VI. 1. 60 S. 3514, yet these words are formed in secular literature also. Because, in Sûtra VII. 4. 48. S. 442, the author of Mahâb

s: 321. A neuter stem ending in a vowel, except ‹?›, of which there exists an equivalent, uniform masculine, is treated like the masculine, in the opinion of Gâlava, before the vowel beginning affixes of the Instrumental and the cases that follow it. Thus the Dative Singular is either शुचये or शुचिने &c. The rest of the declensions is like those of वारि पीलु is the name of a tree and is of Masculine gender; its fruit called पीलु is of neuter gender. This last word has only one form. Thus the Dative Singular is पीलुने and not पीलवे This is because the word पीलु denoting 'fruit' has no corresponding Masculine word denoting fruit, for the corresponding Masculine पीलु refers to the tree, and not to the fruit; so this word पीलु cannot be said to be भाषितपुंस्कः -:0:- Now we take up the declension of the Noun दधि In the declension of this word the following rule applies :

Or eca vowels, ik is the substitute, when short is to be substituted. note:—This sûtra points out the hrasva substitutes or ec. We know there are short and long vowels in sanskrit, but properly speaking the ec vowels have no coresponding short vowels. Thererore, when, in any rule, ec vowels are told to be shortened, this sûtra declares that the short vowels or e and E, o and O, ror the purposes or the rule, wil be i and u respectively. Thus, i. 2. 47 declares:—“the short vowel is the substitute in the neuter or a crude rorn provided it ends in a vowel.” Thererore in conpounding ati + rE, the E nust be shortened. Properly speaking E has no short vowel coresponding to it, but by virtue or this sûtra, i suplies the place or such a short vowel, and we have atiri ‘eltravagant’; so nO, atinu ‘disenbarked or landed’, go, upagu ‘near a cow’. al avyayībhāva conpounds are neuter (i. 4. 18). Why do we say ‘or ec’? Because the short or other vowels wil not be ik. Thus the short or a is a: ati + Kawva = atiKawva ati + nala = atinala Why do we say ‘when short is to be substituted’? Because when pluta or prolated vowels are to be substituted ror ec, the ik wil not be the substitute. as devadata O Devadata ! 3 ta ! Thus non. and ac. rorns are pradyu, pradyuni, pradyuni. The instr. sing. is pradyuna etc. This word is not treated like a nasculine one because it has no coresponding nasculine rorn. ‘prari’ which is derived ron the rot ra to give with the preril pra. The i being changed to short i by the present sûtra, we get the rorn prari. it is declined as rolows:—non. and ac. rorns are prari, prarini, prarini. instr. sing. prarina. By the nalin ekadesa &c., that is “That which has undergone a change in regard to one or its parts, is by no neans in consequence or this change sonething else, than what it was berore the change had taken place,” the rule aplying to prari wil aply to prari also. ence the rule Vi. 2. 85. s. 286 wil aply to prari also. Thus rorns berore Byan and Bis wil be praraByan and praraBi, the augnent atva being aded by the Vartika &c. acording to nadhava, the Genitive Pl. wil be praranan, the augnent nuw being aded by the Vartika &c. But as a nater or ract, there is no atva berore nuw in acordance with the nalin sanipatalaksano viDir aninitan tadviGatasya, i. e. “That which is taught in a rule the aplication or which is
ck: not te take up the teclension or pratyo entink in o in neuter, the o is chanket to u in acortance tith the rolotink sûtra:— 323. Or eca votels, ik is the supstitute, then short is to pe supstitutet. note:—this sûtra points out the hrasva supstitutes or ec. te knot there are short ant lonk votels in sanskrit, put properly speakink the ec votels have no corespontink short votels. thererore, then, in any rule, ec votels are tolt to pe shortenet, this sûtra teclares that the short votels or e ant E, o ant O, ror the purposes or the rule, til pe i ant u respectively. thus, i. 2. 47 teclares:—“the short votel is the supstitute in the neuter or a crute rorn provitet it ents in a votel.” thererore in conpountink ati + rE, the E nust pe shortenet. properly speakink E has no short votel corespontink to it, put py virtue or this sûtra, i suplies the place or such a short votel, ant te have atiri ‘eltravakant’; so nO, atinu ‘tisenparket or lantet’, ko, upaku ‘near a cot’. al avyayīphāva conpounts are neuter (i. 4. 18). thy to te say ‘or ec’? s: Now we take up the declension of प्रद्यो ending in ओ In Neuter, the ओ is changed to उ in accordance with the following Sûtra:— 323. Of एच vowels, इक् is the substitute, when short is to be substituted. Note:—This sûtra points out the ह्रस्व substitutes of एच्. We know there are short and long vowels in Sanskrit, but properly speaking the एच् vowels have no corresponding short vowels. Therefore, when, in any rule, एच् vowels are told to be shortened, this sûtra declares that the short vowels of ए and ऐ, ओ and औ, for the purposes of the rule, will be इ and उ respectively. Thus, I. 2. 47 declares:—“the short vowel is the substitute in the neuter of a crude form provided it ends in a vowel.” Therefore in compounding अति + रै, the ऐ must be shortened. Properly speaking ऐ has no short vowel corresponding to it, but by virtue of this sûtra, इ supplies the place of such a short vowel, and we have अतिरि ‘extravagant’; so नौ, अतिनु ‘disembarked or landed’, गो, उपगु ‘near a cow’. All avyayībhāva compounds are neuter (II. 4. 18). Why do we say ‘of एच्’? Because the short of other vowels will not be इक्. Thus the short of आ is अ: अति + खट्वा = अतिखट्वः अति + माला = अतिमलः Why do we say ‘when short is to be substituted’? Because when प्लुत or prolated vowels are to be substituted for एच्, the इक् will not be the substitute. As देवदत्त O Devadatta ! ३ त ! Thus Nom. and Acc. forms are प्रद्यु, प्रद्युनी, प्रद्यूनि. The Instr. Sing. is प्रद्युना etc. This word is not treated like a Masculine one because it has no corresponding Masculine form. ‘प्ररी’ which is derived from the root रा to give with the prefix प्र. The ई being changed to short इ by the present Sûtra, we get the form प्ररि. It is declined as follows:—Nom. and Acc. forms are प्ररि, प्ररिणी, प्ररीणि. Instr. Sing. प्ररिणा. By the maxim एकदेश &c., that is “That which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means in consequence of this change something else, than what it was before the change had taken place,” the rule applying to प्ररी will apply to प्ररि also. Hence the rule VII. 2. 85. S. 286 will apply to प्ररि also. Thus forms before भ्याम् and भिस् will be प्रराभ्याम् and प्रराभिः, the augment आत्व being added by the Vartika &c. According to Madhava, the Genitive Pl. will be प्रराणाम्, the augment नुट् being added by the Vartika &c. But as a matter of fact, there is no आत्व before नुट् in accordance with the Maxim संनिपातलक्षणो विधिर् अनििमित्तं तद्विघातस्य, i. e. “That which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination.” That is to say this maxim does not apply and it is not of universal application, as we have already shown under Sutra VI. 4. 9 S. 209. Therefore the correct form is प्ररीणाम्. The word सुनु which is the shortened form of सु नौ meaning that which has a good boat, is declined in the Nom. and Acc. forms as सुनु, सुनुनी, सुनूनि. The Instr. and Dat. Singular forms are सुनुना, सुनवे respectively, &c. Here ends the declension of Neuter Nouns ending in Vowels.

pk: now, we take up the declension or the word lihu derived ron the rot liha ‘to taste,’ ‘to lick’ with the aril kvip The non. sing. is lihu + su The h is changed to Q by the rolowing rule. 324. Qa is substituted ror ha berore a jhal leter and at the end or a word. Thus lihu + su = lihu + 0 (The su is elided by halnya0 Vi. 1. 68 s. 252.) = lihu (The h is changed to Q because it is rinal in a pada) = liq (Vi. 2. 39 s. 84) or liw (Vi. 4. 56. s. 206). The non. Dual and Pl. are lihO, liha The ac. rorns are lihan, lihO, liha The instr. rorns are liha, liqByan, liqBi The Loc. Pl. is liwtsu (The Duw being optionaly aded by Vi. 3. 29. s. 131) or liwsu
ck: not, te take up the teclension or the tort lihu terivet ron the rot liha ‘to taste,’ ‘to lick’ tith the aril kvip the non. sink. is lihu + su the h is chanket to t py the rolotink rule. 324. ta is supstitutet ror ha perore a chal leter ant at the ent or a tort. thus lihu + su = lihu + 0 (the su is elitet py halnya0 Vi. 1. 68 s. 252.) = lihu (the h is chanket to t pecause it is rinal in a pata) = lit (Vi. 2. 39 s. 84) or lit (Vi. 4. 56. s. 206). the non. tual ant pl. are lihO, liha the ac. rorns are lihan, lihO, liha the instr. rorns are liha, litpyan, litpi the Loc. pl. is litsu (the tut peink optionaly atet py Vi. 3. 29. s. 131) or litsu
s: Now, we take up the declension of the word लिहू derived from the root लिह ‘to taste,’ ‘to lick’ with the affix क्विप् The Nom. Sing. is लिहू + सु The ह् is changed to ढ् by the following rule. 324. ढ is substituted for ह before a jhal letter and at the end of a word. Thus लिहू + सु = लिहू + ० (The सु is elided by हल्ङ्या० VI. 1. 68 S. 252.) = लिहू (The ह् is changed to ढ् because it is final in a pada) = लिड् (VIII. 2. 39 S. 84) or लिट् (VIII. 4. 56. S. 206). The Nom. Dual and Pl. are लिहौ, लिहः The Acc. forms are लिहम्, लिहौ, लिहः The Instr. forms are लिहा, लिड्भ्याम्, लिड्भिः The Loc. Pl. is लिट्त्सु (The धुट् being optionally added by VIII. 3. 29. S. 131) or लिट्सु

pk: 325. ✓ shiṭa, 326. ✓ siṭa, To slight, despise, disregard. Pre. — sewati, sewati Per. sisewa, sisewa i rut. sewita, sewita aor. asewot, asewit Caus. sewayati, sewayati aorist asisiwat, asisiwat Desi. sisewisati, sisewisati The sa is not changed to sa because or the restriction or Vi. 3. 61, § 2627. inten. sesiwyate, sesidyate
ck: 325. ✓ shiṭa, 326. ✓ siṭa, to slikht, tespise, tisrekart. pre. — setati, setati per. siseta, siseta i rut. setita, setita aor. asetot, asetit caus. setayati, setayati aorist asisitat, asisitat tesi. sisetisati, sisetisati the sa is not chanket to sa pecause or the restriction or Vi. 3. 61, § 2627. inten. sesityate, sesityate
s: 325. ✓ Shiṭa, 326. ✓ Siṭa, To slight, despise, disregard. Pre. — शेटति, सेटति Per. शिशेट, सिषेट I Fut. शेटिता, सेटिता Aor. अशेटोत्, असेटीत् Caus. शेटयति, सेटयति Aorist अशीशिटत्, असीसिटत् Desi. शिशेटिषति, सिसेटिषति The स is not changed to ष because of the restriction of VIII. 3. 61, § 2627. Inten. शेशिट्यते, सेसिद्यते

pk: 326. ror the leters ga, qa, da or ba in the begining or a nonosylable, and belonging to a rot, or a portion or it and which ends in Ja, Ba, Ga, Qa or Da, there is substituted Ga, Qa, Da or Ba respectively in that portion or it which begins with bas and ends with Jas berore sa or Dva, or at the end or a pada (word). in elplaining this sûtra, we have used the word avayava or a nenber or a portion. The rot itselr nay be or nore than one sylable, but ir there is any nenber in it, which satisries the requirenents or this sûtra, that is to say, which begins with ga, qa, da or ba and ends with Ja, Ba, Ga, Qa, Da, in other words, which begins with the third leter or the Varga, elcept ca and ends with the rourth leter or the Varga, then ror ga is substituted Ga, ror qa, Qa, ror da, Da, and ror ba, Ba. But had we elplained the sûtra by saying ekaco Dato, that is, or a rot which is nonosylabic and satisries the above qualirications then we could not have got the rorn garDak ron the denoninative rot gardaBayati. The word garDak is derived ron the rot gardaB by the aril kvip to the rot and the elision or ni ror gardaB The b is changed to B The anuvṛti or Jali ceases here and is not to be read in the sûtra. This had conenced ron Vi. 2. 26 or the ashṭâdhyâyî. By taking the leters sa and Dva in the sûtra, the substitution does not take place berore any other leter, such as in dugDan, dogDa ere d is not changed to D By aplying the nalin vyapadesivadBava, that is "an operation which arects sonething on acount or sone special designation which ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects likewise that which stands alone and to which thererore, just because the reasons ror it do not elist, that special designation does not atach;" the rule wil aply to sinple rots like to duh &c. also. Thererore duh + su = duh + 0 = duG + 0 = DuG = Dug or Duk The non: Dual and Pl: are duhO, duha in rorning the Loc: Pl: the present sûtra wil aply and we get the rorn Duksu (s being changed to sa by Vi. 3. 59. s. 212). in declining druh the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 326. ror the leters ka, ta, ta or pa in the pekinink or a nonosylaple, ant pelonkink to a rot, or a portion or it ant thich ents in ca, pa, ka, ta or ta, there is supstitutet ka, ta, ta or pa respectively in that portion or it thich pekins tith pas ant ents tith cas perore sa or tva, or at the ent or a pata (tort). in elplainink this sûtra, te have uset the tort avayava or a nenper or a portion. the rot itselr nay pe or nore than one sylaple, put ir there is any nenper in it, thich satisries the retuirenents or this sûtra, that is to say, thich pekins tith ka, ta, ta or pa ant ents tith ca, pa, ka, ta, ta, in other torts, thich pekins tith the thirt leter or the Varka, elcept ca ant ents tith the rourth leter or the Varka, then ror ka is supstitutet ka, ror ta, ta, ror ta, ta, ant ror pa, pa. put hat te elplainet the sûtra py sayink ekaco tato, that is, or a rot thich is nonosylapic ant satisries the apove tualirications then te coult not have kot the rorn kartak ron the tenoninative rot kartapayati. the tort kartak is terivet ron the rot kartap py the aril kvip to the rot ant the elision or ni ror kartap the p is chanket to p the anuvṛti or cali ceases here ant is not to pe reat in the sûtra. this hat conencet ron Vi. 2. 26 or the ashṭâthyâyî. py takink the leters sa ant tva in the sûtra, the supstitution toes not take place perore any other leter, such as in tuktan, tokta ere t is not chanket to t py aplyink the nalin vyapatesivatpava, that is "an operation thich arects sonethink on acount or sone special tesiknation thich ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects liketise that thich stants alone ant to thich thererore, cust pecause the reasons ror it to not elist, that special tesiknation toes not atach;" the rule til aply to sinple rots like to tuh &c. also. thererore tuh + su = tuh + 0 = tuk + 0 = tuk = tuk or tuk the non: tual ant pl: are tuhO, tuha in rornink the Loc: pl: the present sûtra til aply ant te ket the rorn tuksu (s peink chanket to sa py Vi. 3. 59. s. 212). in teclinink truh the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 326. For the letters ग, ड, द or ब in the beginning of a monosyllable, and belonging to a root, or a portion of it and which ends in झ, भ, घ, ढ or ध, there is substituted घ, ढ, ध or भ respectively in that portion of it which begins with बश् and ends with झष् before स or ध्व, or at the end of a pada (word). In explaining this sûtra, we have used the word अवयव or a member or a portion. The root itself may be of more than one syllable, but if there is any member in it, which satisfies the requirements of this sûtra, that is to say, which begins with ग, ड, द or ब and ends with झ, भ, घ, ढ, ध, in other words, which begins with the third letter of the Varga, except च and ends with the fourth letter of the Varga, then for ग is substituted घ, for ड, ढ, for द, ध, and for ब, भ. But had we explained the sûtra by saying एकाचो धातोः, that is, of a root which is monosyllabic and satisfies the above qualifications then we could not have got the form गर्धक् from the denominative root गर्दभयति. The word गर्धक् is derived from the root गर्दभ् by the affix क्विप् to the root and the elision of णि for गर्दभ् The ब् is changed to भ् The anuvṛtti of झलि ceases here and is not to be read in the sûtra. This had commenced from VIII. 2. 26 of the Ashṭâdhyâyî. By taking the letters स and ध्व in the sûtra, the substitution does not take place before any other letter, such as in दुग्धम्, दोग्धा Here द् is not changed to ध् By applying the maxim व्यपदेशिवद्भाव, that is "An operation which affects something on account of some special designation which for certain reasons attaches to the latter, affects likewise that which stands alone and to which therefore, just because the reasons for it do not exist, that special designation does not attach;" the rule will apply to simple roots like to दुह् &c. also. Therefore दुह् + सु = दुह् + ० = दुघ् + ० = धुघ् = धुग् or धुक् The Nom: Dual and Pl: are दुहौ, दुहः In forming the Loc: Pl: the present sûtra will apply and we get the form धुक्षु (स् being changed to ष by VIII. 3. 59. S. 212). In declining द्रुह् the following rule applies.

pk: 327. The ha or druh, nuh, snuh, and snih is optionaly changed to Ga berore a jhal leter or at the end or a word. The ha or these words is changed to Ga optionaly; in the other alternative it would be changed to Qa. Thus non: sing. is Druk or Drug or Drud or Druw. instrunental, Dative and ablative Dual is DrugByan or DruqByan. Locative Pl: is Druksu or Drutsu (Vi. 3. 29. s. 131) or Druwsu sinilar is the declension or nuha, snuh and snih —:o:— now, we take up the declension or visvavah. The non: rorns are visvavaw or visvavaq, visvavahO, visvavaha. ac: sing. and Dual are visvavahan, visvavahO in rorning the ac: Pl: the rule arter the rolowing aplies, because the base gets the designation or bha berore this aril; that is the seni-vowel va is changed to u This change is caled sanprasarana (sanprasâraṇa) or vocalisation, which is derined in the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 327. the ha or truh, nuh, snuh, ant snih is optionaly chanket to ka perore a chal leter or at the ent or a tort. the ha or these torts is chanket to ka optionaly; in the other alternative it toult pe chanket to ta. thus non: sink. is truk or truk or trut or trut. instrunental, tative ant aplative tual is trukpyan or trutpyan. Locative pl: is truksu or trutsu (Vi. 3. 29. s. 131) or trutsu sinilar is the teclension or nuha, snuh ant snih —:o:— not, te take up the teclension or visvavah. the non: rorns are visvavat or visvavat, visvavahO, visvavaha. ac: sink. ant tual are visvavahan, visvavahO in rornink the ac: pl: the rule arter the rolotink aplies, pecause the pase kets the tesiknation or pha perore this aril; that is the seni-votel va is chanket to u this chanke is calet sanprasarana (sanprasâraṇa) or vocalisation, thich is terinet in the rolotink sûtra.
s: 327. The ह of druh, muh, snuh, and snih is optionally changed to घ before a jhal letter or at the end of a word. The ह of these words is changed to घ optionally; in the other alternative it would be changed to ढ. Thus Nom: Sing. is ध्रुक् or ध्रुग् or ध्रुद् or ध्रुट्. Instrumental, Dative and Ablative Dual is ध्रुग्भ्याम् or ध्रुड्भ्याम्. Locative Pl: is ध्रुक्षु or ध्रुत्सु (VIII. 3. 29. S. 131) or ध्रुट्सु Similar is the declension of मुह, स्नुह् and स्निह् —:o:— Now, we take up the declension of विश्ववाह्. The Nom: forms are विश्ववाट् or विश्ववाड्, विश्ववाहौ, विश्ववाहः. Acc: Sing. and Dual are विश्ववाहम्, विश्ववाहौ In forming the Acc: Pl: the rule after the following applies, because the base gets the designation of 'bha' before this affix; that is the semi-vowel व is changed to उ This change is called संप्रसारण (Samprasâraṇa) or vocalisation, which is defined in the following sûtra.

pk: 328. The ik vowels which replace the senivowels yaṇ are caled sanprasâraṇa. note:— This derines the word sanprasâraṇa, or vocalisation. it is the nane given to the change or seni-vowels into vowels. The pratyâhâra ik includes the rour sinple vowels i, u, r and l, and their coresponding seni-vowels are y, v, r, and l included in the pratyâhâra yaṇ. The word sanprasâraṇa is properly the nane or the vowel which has replaced the seni-vowel. Thus the past participle or svap to slep, is rorned by ading the nishṭhâ aril kta (se sûtra 26). so that we have svap + ta. But there is a rule (Vi. 1. 15) by which there is sanprasâraṇa or the va or svap berore the ariles, and we have the rorn supta "slept". sinilarly ron vad—udita, yaj—iswan, vyaD—vidDa, grah—grhitan, pracC—prswan. The tern sanprasâraṇa is also enployed to designate the whole proces or the change or the seni-vowels as in Vi. 1. 13; Vi. 4. 131.
ck: 328. the ik votels thich replace the senivotels yaṇ are calet sanprasâraṇa. note:— this terines the tort sanprasâraṇa, or vocalisation. it is the nane kiven to the chanke or seni-votels into votels. the pratyâhâra ik inclutes the rour sinple votels i, u, r ant l, ant their corespontink seni-votels are y, v, r, ant l inclutet in the pratyâhâra yaṇ. the tort sanprasâraṇa is properly the nane or the votel thich has replacet the seni-votel. thus the past participle or svap to slep, is rornet py atink the nishṭhâ aril kta (se sûtra 26). so that te have svap + ta. put there is a rule (Vi. 1. 15) py thich there is sanprasâraṇa or the va or svap perore the ariles, ant te have the rorn supta "slept". sinilarly ron vat—utita, yac—istan, vyat—vita, krah—krhitan, prac—prstan. the tern sanprasâraṇa is also enployet to tesiknate the thole proces or the chanke or the seni-votels as in Vi. 1. 13; Vi. 4. 131.
s: 328. The ik vowels which replace the semivowels yaṇ are called samprasâraṇa. Note:— This defines the word samprasâraṇa, or vocalisation. It is the name given to the change of semi-vowels into vowels. The pratyâhâra ik includes the four simple vowels इ, उ, ऋ and ऌ, and their corresponding semi-vowels are य्, व्, र्, and ल् included in the pratyâhâra yaṇ. The word samprasâraṇa is properly the name of the vowel which has replaced the semi-vowel. Thus the past participle of स्वप् 'to sleep,' is formed by adding the nishṭhâ affix क्त (see sûtra 26). So that we have स्वप् + त. But there is a rule (VI. 1. 15) by which there is samprasâraṇa of the व of स्वप् before the affixes, and we have the form सुप्तः "slept". Similarly from वद्—उदितः, यज्—इष्टम्, व्यध्—विद्धः, ग्रह्—गृहीतम्, प्रच्छ्—पृष्टम्. The term samprasâraṇa is also employed to designate the whole process of the change of the semi-vowels as in VI. 1. 13; VI. 4. 131.

pk: 31. catura and anaquha get the acutely acented augnent a (an) arter the u in the strong cases. Thus anaquh + su = anaquah + su Then aplies the rolowing rule.
ck: 31. catura ant anatuha ket the acutely acentet auknent a (an) arter the u in the stronk cases. thus anatuh + su = anatuah + su then aplies the rolotink rule.
s: 331. चतुर and अनडुह get the acutely accented augment आ (आम्) after the उ in the strong cases. Thus अनडुह् + सु = अनडुआह् + सु Then applies the following rule.

pk: 32. anaquh gets the augnent nun berore the ending or the non. sg. (and Vocative). By the last anaquh gets the augnent a or a arter u in the strong cases, and a in Vocative singular (Vi. 1. 9) it thus becones anaqvah and anaqvah By the present sūtra nun is aded arter this a and a The case-ending is elided by Vi. 1. 68, and the rinal h by Vi. 2. 23. Thus we have anaqvan noninative singular ; and anaqvan in the Vocative singular. The augnents an and an (Vi. 1. 98, 9), do not supersede nun, nor are they superseded by nun The nun is speciricaly taught by this sūtra, the v is not changed to da by Vi. 2. 72 s 34. The rinal is not elided, because the elision or h by Vi. 2. 23. s 54 is not perceived by Vi. 2. 7. s. 236, requiring the elision or na because or the rule Vi. 2. 1. s 12. so the na is not elided. Thus the non : sing is anaqvan. in rorning the Voc : the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 32. anatuh kets the auknent nun perore the entink or the non. sk. (ant Vocative). py the last anatuh kets the auknent a or a arter u in the stronk cases, ant a in Vocative sinkular (Vi. 1. 9) it thus pecones anatvah ant anatvah py the present sūtra nun is atet arter this a ant a the case-entink is elitet py Vi. 1. 68, ant the rinal h py Vi. 2. 23. thus te have anatvan noninative sinkular ; ant anatvan in the Vocative sinkular. the auknents an ant an (Vi. 1. 98, 9), to not supersete nun, nor are they supersetet py nun the nun is speciricaly taukht py this sūtra, the v is not chanket to ta py Vi. 2. 72 s 34. the rinal is not elitet, pecause the elision or h py Vi. 2. 23. s 54 is not perceivet py Vi. 2. 7. s. 236, retuirink the elision or na pecause or the rule Vi. 2. 1. s 12. so the na is not elitet. thus the non : sink is anatvan. in rornink the Voc : the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 332. अनडुह् gets the augment नुम् before the ending of the Nom. Sg. (and Vocative). By the last अनडुह् gets the augment आ or अ after उ in the strong cases, and अ in Vocative Singular (VII. 1. 99) It thus becomes अनड्वाह् and अनड्वह् By the present sūtra नुम् is added after this आ and अ The case-ending is elided by VI. 1. 68, and the final ह् by VIII. 2. 23. Thus we have अनड्वान् Nominative Singular ; and अनड्वन् in the Vocative Singular. The augments आम् and अम् (VII. 1. 98, 99), do not supersede नुम्, nor are they superseded by नुम् The नुम् is specifically taught by this Sūtra, the व् is not changed to द by VIII. 2. 72 S 334. The final is not elided, because the elision of ह् by VIII. 2. 23. S 54 is not perceived by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236, requiring the elision of न because of the rule VIII. 2. 1. S 12. So the न is not elided. Thus the Nom : Sing is अनड्वान्. In forming the Voc : the following rule applies.

pk: 3. catur and anaquh get the augnent a arter the u in the Vocative singular. This debars the previous rule. as, he anaqvan, he anaqvahO, anaqvaha The instr : sing. is anaquha. Berore the ariles Byan, Bi &c, the h is changed to da by the rolowing rule.
ck: 3. catur ant anatuh ket the auknent a arter the u in the Vocative sinkular. this tepars the previous rule. as, he anatvan, he anatvahO, anatvaha the instr : sink. is anatuha. perore the ariles pyan, pi &c, the h is chanket to ta py the rolotink rule.
s: 333. चतुर् and अनडुह् get the augment अ after the उ in the Vocative Singular. This debars the previous rule. As, हे अनड्वन्, हे अनड्वाहौ, अनड्वाहः The Instr : Sing. is अनडुहा. Before the affixes भ्याम्, भिः &c, the ह् is changed to द by the following rule.

pk: 34. da is substituted ror the rinal or a word rorned with the aril vasu and ending in s and ror the rinal or sransu, Dvansu and anaquh at the end or a Pada (in the wider sense i. 4. 14, 17). Thus anaqudByan &c. Why do we say that the word rorned with the aril vasu nust end in s ? Observe vidvan. Why do we say rinal in a Pada? Observe srastan, Dvastan. now, we take up the declension or turasah. in its declension, the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 34. ta is supstitutet ror the rinal or a tort rornet tith the aril vasu ant entink in s ant ror the rinal or sransu, tvansu ant anatuh at the ent or a pata (in the titer sense i. 4. 14, 17). thus anatutpyan &c. thy to te say that the tort rornet tith the aril vasu nust ent in s ? Opserve vitvan. thy to te say rinal in a pata? Opserve srastan, tvastan. not, te take up the teclension or turasah. in its teclension, the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 334. द is substituted for the final of a word formed with the affix वसु and ending in स् and for the final of स्रंसु, ध्वंसु and अनडुह् at the end of a Pada (in the wider sense I. 4. 14, 17). Thus अनडुद्भ्याम् &c. Why do we say that the word formed with the affix वसु must end in स् ? Observe विद्वान्. Why do we say final in a Pada? Observe स्रस्तम्, ध्वस्तम्. Now, we take up the declension of तुरासाह्. In its declension, the following rule applies :—

pk: 35. sa is substituted ror the s in sah, when this ocurs in the rorn or saq (saq) Thus turasaw. saq is derived ron sah by the aril nvi (i. 2. 63 s 3409), there is vṛidhi or the penultinate, the h is changed to Qa (Vi. 2. 31) and the upapada is lengthened (Vi. 3. 137 s. 3539). note:—saqa sa would have ben enough, ror there is no other rorn saq elcept this derived ron sah : why then the word sahe is used in the sūtra ? There is another rorn saq not derived ron sah Thus saha qena vartate = saqa, tasya apatyan = saqi e in whose nane there is the leter qa is caled saqa ; as nrqa Why do we say in the rorn or saq ? The rule wil not aply when the rorn is sah, as jalasahan, turasahan Why do we say sa "ror the s" ? so that the a or saq nay not be changed to cerebral : the q is already cerebral. ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in h There is no nasculine noun ending in y though on the analogy or the noun kanala (se 340) we nay rorn toy neaning toyanacaksana and decline as toy, toyO, toya yet this y wil always be elided by the rule Vi. 1. 6 s. 373. We take up thererore, the declension or the nasculine nouns ending in v e.g. sudiv. in its declension, the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 35. sa is supstitutet ror the s in sah, then this ocurs in the rorn or sat (sat) thus turasat. sat is terivet ron sah py the aril nvi (i. 2. 63 s 3409), there is vṛithi or the penultinate, the h is chanket to ta (Vi. 2. 31) ant the upapata is lenkthenet (Vi. 3. 137 s. 3539). note:—sata sa toult have pen enoukh, ror there is no other rorn sat elcept this terivet ron sah : thy then the tort sahe is uset in the sūtra ? there is another rorn sat not terivet ron sah thus saha tena vartate = sata, tasya apatyan = sati e in those nane there is the leter ta is calet sata ; as nrta thy to te say in the rorn or sat ? the rule til not aply then the rorn is sah, as calasahan, turasahan thy to te say sa "ror the s" ? so that the a or sat nay not pe chanket to cerepral : the t is alreaty cerepral. ere ents the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in h there is no nasculine noun entink in y thoukh on the analoky or the noun kanala (se 340) te nay rorn toy neanink toyanacaksana ant tecline as toy, toyO, toya yet this y til altays pe elitet py the rule Vi. 1. 6 s. 373. te take up thererore, the teclension or the nasculine nouns entink in v e.k. sutiv. in its teclension, the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 335. ष is substituted for the स् in साह्, when this occurs in the form of साड् (षाड्) Thus तुराषाट्. साड् is derived from सह् by the affix ण्वि (III. 2. 63 S 3409), there is vṛiddhi of the penultimate, the ह् is changed to ढ (VIII. 2. 31) and the upapada is lengthened (VI. 3. 137 S. 3539). Note:—साडः सः would have been enough, for there is no other form साड् except this derived from सह् : why then the word सहेः is used in the sūtra ? There is another form साड् not derived from सह् Thus सह डेन वर्त्तते = सडः, तस्य अपत्यं = साडिः He in whose name there is the letter ड is called सड ; as मृड Why do we say 'in the form of साड्' ? The rule will not apply when the form is साह्, as जलासाहम्, तुरासाहम् Why do we say सः "for the स्" ? So that the आ of साड् may not be changed to cerebral : the ड् is already cerebral. Here ends the declension of Masculine nouns ending in ह् There is no masculine noun ending in य् though on the analogy of the Noun कमल (See 340) we may form तोय् meaning तोयमाचक्षाणः and decline as तोय्, तोयौ, तोयः yet this य् will always be elided by the rule VI. 1. 66 S. 373. We take up therefore, the declension of the Masculine nouns ending in व् e.g. सुदिव्. In its declension, the following rule applies :—

pk: 37. ror the rinal or the noninal-sten div, there is the substitution or u, when it is a Pada (i. 4. 14 &c). note:—The portion or the word angasya nust be read into this sûtra ron Vi. 1. 109. The word div is here a noninal-sten and not a verbal-rot. Thus ‹?›. We have said that div is here a prâtipadika and not a dhâtu, ror as a dhâtu it ought to have its servile leter (anubandha) and should have ben read as divun. in the case or its being used as a verb, there takes place the substitution or long u by Vi. 4. 19. in that case we shal have aksadyuByan, aksadyuBi The ut with a t shows that short u is neant, and debars (Vi. 4. 19). in the case or substitution the rorns wil be sudyuByan, sudyuBi The satva also cones because it is taught in a subsequent sûtra. Why do we say when it is a Pada? Observe sudivO, sudiva Thus instr: Dual and Pl. are sudyuByan, sudyuBi. ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in v. —:o:— Declension or nasculine nouns ending in r. We take up the declension or catur which is always Plural. its non: Pl. is catur + jas = catur + an + as (s. 31) = catvara its ac:, instr:, Dat. and abl: Pl: are catura, caturBi, caturBya, caturBya respectively. in rorning the Gen: Pl: the rolowing rule aplies:—
ck: 37. ror the rinal or the noninal-sten tiv, there is the supstitution or u, then it is a pata (i. 4. 14 &c). note:—the portion or the tort ankasya nust pe reat into this sûtra ron Vi. 1. 109. the tort tiv is here a noninal-sten ant not a verpal-rot. thus ‹?›. te have sait that tiv is here a prâtipatika ant not a thâtu, ror as a thâtu it oukht to have its servile leter (anupantha) ant shoult have pen reat as tivun. in the case or its peink uset as a verp, there takes place the supstitution or lonk u py Vi. 4. 19. in that case te shal have aksatyupyan, aksatyupi the ut tith a t shots that short u is neant, ant tepars (Vi. 4. 19). in the case or supstitution the rorns til pe sutyupyan, sutyupi the satva also cones pecause it is taukht in a supsetuent sûtra. thy to te say then it is a pata? Opserve sutivO, sutiva thus instr: tual ant pl. are sutyupyan, sutyupi. ere ents the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in v. —:o:— teclension or nasculine nouns entink in r. te take up the teclension or catur thich is altays plural. its non: pl. is catur + cas = catur + an + as (s. 31) = catvara its ac:, instr:, tat. ant apl: pl: are catura, caturpi, caturpya, caturpya respectively. in rornink the ken: pl: the rolotink rule aplies:—
s: 337. For the final of the nominal-stem दिव्, there is the substitution of उ, when it is a Pada (I. 4. 14 &c). Note:—The portion of the word अङ्गस्य must be read into this sûtra from VI. 1. 109. The word दिव् is here a nominal-stem and not a verbal-root. Thus ‹?›. We have said that दिव् is here a prâtipadika and not a dhâtu, for as a dhâtu it ought to have its servile letter (anubandha) and should have been read as दिवुँ. In the case of its being used as a verb, there takes place the substitution of long ऊ by VI. 4. 19. In that case we shall have अक्षद्यूभ्याम्, अक्षद्यूभिः The उत् with a त् shows that short उ is meant, and debars (VI. 4. 19). In the case of substitution the forms will be सुद्युभ्याम्, सुद्युभिः The षत्व also comes because it is taught in a subsequent sûtra. Why do we say 'when it is a Pada'? Observe सुदिवौ, सुदिवः Thus Instr: Dual and Pl. are सुद्युभ्याम्, सुद्युभिः. Here ends the declension of Masculine nouns ending in व्. —:o:— Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in र्. We take up the declension of चतुर् which is always Plural. Its Nom: Pl. is चतुर् + जस् = चतुर् + आम् + अस् (S. 331) = चत्वारः Its Acc:, Instr:, Dat. and Abl: Pl: are चतुरः, चतुर्भिः, चतुर्भ्यः, चतुर्भ्यः respectively. In forming the Gen: Pl: the following rule applies:—

pk: 38. The augnent nuw is aded berore the Genitive pl. ending an arter the nunerals caled shash, and arter catur Telt:—The n is changed to n by Vi. 4. 1. s. 235 and this is optionaly doubled by Vi. 4. 46. s. 59. as caturnan a nuneral ending in s is not shash, hence the speciric nention or catur note:—This rule aplies to conpounds ending with these nunerals, when these later are the principal nenber, as paranasanan, paranapancanan, paranacaturnan, but priyapancan, priyacaturan, where the nunerals are secondary (upasarjana). in rorning the Loc. Pl. the rolowing is held in abeyance, because the visarjaniya taught there aplies to that which is derived ron ru and not to every r.
ck: 38. the auknent nut is atet perore the kenitive pl. entink an arter the nunerals calet shash, ant arter catur telt:—the n is chanket to n py Vi. 4. 1. s. 235 ant this is optionaly touplet py Vi. 4. 46. s. 59. as caturnan a nuneral entink in s is not shash, hence the speciric nention or catur note:—this rule aplies to conpounts entink tith these nunerals, then these later are the principal nenper, as paranasanan, paranapancanan, paranacaturnan, put priyapancan, priyacaturan, there the nunerals are secontary (upasarcana). in rornink the Loc. pl. the rolotink is helt in apeyance, pecause the visarcaniya taukht there aplies to that thich is terivet ron ru ant not to every r.
s: 338. The augment नुट् is added before the Genitive pl. ending आम् after the Numerals called 'shash', and after चतुर् Text:—The न् is changed to ण् by VIII. 4. 1. S. 235 and this is optionally doubled by VIII. 4. 46. S. 59. As चतुर्णाम् A numeral ending in ष् is not 'shash', hence the specific mention of चतुर् Note:—This rule applies to compounds ending with these numerals, when these latter are the principal member, as परमषण्णाम्, परमपञ्चानाम्, परमचतुर्णाम्, but प्रियपञ्चाम्, प्रियचतुराम्, where the Numerals are secondary (upasarjana). In forming the Loc. Pl. the following is held in abeyance, because the विसर्जनीय taught there applies to that which is derived from रु and not to every र्.

s: 339. ✓ Biṭa (✓ Hiṭa), to swear, to curse, to shout, exclaim, to address harshly. Pre. बेटति, हेटति Per. बिबेट, बिहेट, बिबिटतुः, जिहिटतुः, बिबिदुः, शिहिदुः I Fut. बेटिता Aor. अबेटीत्, अहेटीत् Caus. बेटयति, हेटयति Desi. बिबेटिषति, बिबिटिषति, जिहिटिषति Inten. बेबिट्यते, जेहिट्यते यङ् लुक् बेविटीति, बेवेत्ति

pk: 340. There are not two in the ron or a sibilant (sar), when a vowel rolows. note:—The word na is to be read into the sûtra. This debars the aplication or rule Vi. 4. 46, s. 59. Thus karsati, varsati, prakarsa, aksadarsa Why do we say aci when a vowel rolows? Observe vrte Telt:—Thus catursu. now, we take up the declension or priyacatur which nay be declined in al nunbers (se note under s. 38). priyacatur + su = priyacatu + a + r + s (Vi. 1. 98. s. 31) = priyacatva. in the Voc: sing. instead or an there wil be an by Vi. 1. 9. s. 3. Thus he priyacatva The non: Dual and Pl: are priyacatvarO, priyacatvara. as catur here is a secondary nenber or a Conpound the augnent nuw required by Vi. 1. 5. s. 38 is not aded in the rornation or the Gen: Pl; Thus we have priyacaturan. But ir the conpound be not a Bahuvrihi, and catur be a principal nenber, then the Genitive Pl. wil be paranacaturnan ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in r. Declension or nasculine nouns ending in l. now we take up the declension or kanala. This is derived ron the noun kanalan or kanala by pasing through the curadigana under the rule tatkaroti tadacaswe, that is, when the sense is kanalan kanalan vacaksana that one speaks or Kanala or Kanalâ. Thus kanala + nic (or curadigana). To this we ad the aril kvip when the nic is elided by Vi. 4. 51. s. 2313. Thus we get kanala. its declension is non. kanala, kanalO, kanala. its Loc. Pl. kanalatsu. (The t being changed to l). ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in l. There is no noun ending in ‹?›. Thererore we take up the declension or nasculine nouns ending in n. in the declension or these nouns, the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 340. there are not to in the ron or a sipilant (sar), then a votel rolots. note:—the tort na is to pe reat into the sûtra. this tepars the aplication or rule Vi. 4. 46, s. 59. thus karsati, varsati, prakarsa, aksatarsa thy to te say aci then a votel rolots? Opserve vrte telt:—thus catursu. not, te take up the teclension or priyacatur thich nay pe teclinet in al nunpers (se note unter s. 38). priyacatur + su = priyacatu + a + r + s (Vi. 1. 98. s. 31) = priyacatva. in the Voc: sink. insteat or an there til pe an py Vi. 1. 9. s. 3. thus he priyacatva the non: tual ant pl: are priyacatvarO, priyacatvara. as catur here is a secontary nenper or a conpount the auknent nut retuiret py Vi. 1. 5. s. 38 is not atet in the rornation or the ken: pl; thus te have priyacaturan. put ir the conpount pe not a pahuvrihi, ant catur pe a principal nenper, then the kenitive pl. til pe paranacaturnan ere ents the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in r. teclension or nasculine nouns entink in l. not te take up the teclension or kanala. this is terivet ron the noun kanalan or kanala py pasink throukh the curatikana unter the rule tatkaroti tatacaste, that is, then the sense is kanalan kanalan vacaksana that one speaks or kanala or kanalâ. thus kanala + nic (or curatikana). to this te at the aril kvip then the nic is elitet py Vi. 4. 51. s. 2313. thus te ket kanala. its teclension is non. kanala, kanalO, kanala. its Loc. pl. kanalatsu. (the t peink chanket to l). ere ents the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in l. there is no noun entink in ‹?›. thererore te take up the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in n. in the teclension or these nouns, the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 340. There are not two in the room of a sibilant (शर्), when a vowel follows. Note:—The word न is to be read into the sûtra. This debars the application of rule VIII. 4. 46, S. 59. Thus कर्षति, वर्षति, प्राकर्षः, अक्षदर्शः Why do we say अचि 'when a vowel follows'? Observe वृत्ते Text:—Thus चतुर्षु. Now, we take up the declension of प्रियचतुर् which may be declined in all numbers (See Note under S. 338). प्रियचतुर् + सु = प्रियचतु + आ + र् + स् (VII. 1. 98. S. 331) = प्रियचत्वाः. In the Voc: Sing. instead of अम् there will be अन् by VII. 1. 99. S. 333. Thus हे प्रियचत्वः The Nom: Dual and Pl: are प्रियचत्वारौ, प्रियचत्वारः. As चतुर् here is a secondary member of a Compound the augment नुट् required by VII. 1. 55. S. 338 is not added in the formation of the Gen: Pl; Thus we have प्रियचतुराम्. But if the compound be not a Bahuvrihi, and चतुर् be a principal member, then the Genitive Pl. will be परमचतुर्णाम् Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in र्. Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ल्. Now we take up the declension of कमल. This is derived from the Noun कमलम् or कमला by passing through the चुरादिगण under the rule तत्करोति तदाचष्टे, that is, when the sense is कमलं कमलां वाऽऽचक्षाणः that one speaks of Kamala or Kamalâ. Thus कमल + णिच् (of चुरादिगण). To this we add the affix क्विप् when the णिच् is elided by VI. 4. 51. S. 2313. Thus we get कमल. Its declension is Nom. कमल, कमलौ, कमलाः. Its Loc. Pl. कमलत्सु. (The त् being changed to ल्). Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ल्. There is no noun ending in ‹?›. Therefore we take up the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in म्. In the declension of these nouns, the following rule applies.

pk: 341. n is substituted, at the end or a Pada, ror the rinal n or a rot. as prasan, this is rorned by ading kvip to the rot san The lengthening takes place by Vi. 4. 15. s. 256. The natva being considered as asidha is not elided by Vi. 2. 7. s. 236. The word padasya is understod here also. so we have prasanO, prasana where n is not at the end or a pada. The non: rorns are prasan, prasanO, prasana ; The instr: Dual is prasanByan, &c. —:o:— now, we take up the declension or kin sarvavat in its declension, the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 341. n is supstitutet, at the ent or a pata, ror the rinal n or a rot. as prasan, this is rornet py atink kvip to the rot san the lenkthenink takes place py Vi. 4. 15. s. 256. the natva peink consiteret as asitha is not elitet py Vi. 2. 7. s. 236. the tort patasya is unterstot here also. so te have prasanO, prasana there n is not at the ent or a pata. the non: rorns are prasan, prasanO, prasana ; the instr: tual is prasanpyan, &c. —:o:— not, te take up the teclension or kin sarvavat in its teclension, the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 341. न् is substituted, at the end of a Pada, for the final म् of a root. As प्रशान्, this is formed by adding क्विप् to the root शम् The lengthening takes place by VI. 4. 15. S. 2556. The नत्व being considered as asiddha is not elided by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236. The word पदस्य is understood here also. So we have प्रशामौ, प्रशामः where म् is not at the end of a pada. The Nom: forms are प्रशान्, प्रशामौ, प्रशामः ; The Instr: Dual is प्रशान्भ्याम्, &c. —:o:— Now, we take up the declension of किम् सर्ववत् In its declension, the following rule applies :—
