pk: 34. ay is substituted ror the id or idan in the non. sing. nasculine. as ayan The case ending is elided by Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. in other cases, sûtra Vi. 2. 102. s. 265. would aply and there wil be Para-rûpa (Vi. 1. 97. s. 191) and so wil asune the rorn ida at this stage, wil aply the rolowing rule.
ck: 34. ay is supstitutet ror the it or itan in the non. sink. nasculine. as ayan the case entink is elitet py Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. in other cases, sûtra Vi. 2. 102. s. 265. toult aply ant there til pe para-rûpa (Vi. 1. 97. s. 191) ant so til asune the rorn ita at this stake, til aply the rolotink rule.
s: 344. अय् is substituted for the इद् of इदम् in the Nom. Sing. masculine. As अयम् The case ending is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. In other cases, sûtra VII. 2. 102. S. 265. would apply and there will be Para-rûpa (VI. 1. 97. S. 191) and so will assume the form इद At this stage, will apply the following rule.

pk: 345. and na is substituted ror the d or idan berore a case-aril. as inO, ine, inan, inO, inan Thus idan + an = ida + an (Vi. 2. 102 s. 265.) = ina + an (Vi. 2. 109 s. 345) = inan (Vi. 1. 97, s. 191). it is a general rule that there is no Vocative case or tyadadi words. in rorning the instrunental and other cases, the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 345. ant na is supstitutet ror the t or itan perore a case-aril. as inO, ine, inan, inO, inan thus itan + an = ita + an (Vi. 2. 102 s. 265.) = ina + an (Vi. 2. 109 s. 345) = inan (Vi. 1. 97, s. 191). it is a keneral rule that there is no Vocative case or tyatati torts. in rornink the instrunental ant other cases, the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 345. And म is substituted for the द् of इदम् before a case-affix. As इमौ, इमे, इमम्, इमौ, इमान् Thus इदम् + अम् = इद + अम् (VII. 2. 102 S. 265.) = इम + अम् (VII. 2. 109 S. 345) = इमम् (VI. 1. 97, S. 191). It is a general rule that there is no Vocative case of त्यदादि words. In forming the Instrumental and other cases, the following rule applies.

pk: 346. ana is substituted ror the id or idan in the instrunental singular and the cases that rolow, provided that the augnent akach is not aded. as anena, anayo Why do we say "not when ka is aded by V. 3. 71"? Observe inakena, inakayo The word ap (api) in the sûtra is a pratyâhâra, rorned with the a or wa (ins. sg.), and p or sup (Loc. Pl.). Berore consonantal ariles, the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 346. ana is supstitutet ror the it or itan in the instrunental sinkular ant the cases that rolot, provitet that the auknent akach is not atet. as anena, anayo thy to te say "not then ka is atet py V. 3. 71"? Opserve inakena, inakayo the tort ap (api) in the sûtra is a pratyâhâra, rornet tith the a or ta (ins. sk.), ant p or sup (Loc. pl.). perore consonantal ariles, the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 346. अन is substituted for the इद् of इदम् in the Instrumental singular and the cases that follow, provided that the augment akach is not added. As अनेन, अनयोः Why do we say "not when क is added by V. 3. 71"? Observe इमकेन, इमकयोः The word आप् (आपि) in the sûtra is a pratyâhâra, formed with the आ of टा (Ins. Sg.), and प् of सुप् (Loc. Pl.). Before consonantal affixes, the following rule applies.

pk: 347. The id or idan is elided berore an âp case aril begining with a consonant, provided that the augnent akac is not aded. ere aplies the nalin—"The rule i. 1. 52. s. 42, by which a substitute should take the place or only the rinal leter or that which is elhibited in the genitive case, is not valid where what is elhibited in the genitive is neaningles, provided the rule teaching the substitution does not teach a change in a reduplicative sylable." aving elided id or idan, the only portion that renains now is n which is replaced by a Vi. 2. 102 s. 265. Thus we have only a lert. Thus a + Byan now Vi. 3. 102 s. 202 declares that a rinal a is lengthened berore a case aril begining with yan But the solitary a is initial and canot thererore be rinal and so it should not be lengthened. To renove this doubt, we have the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 347. the it or itan is elitet perore an âp case aril pekinink tith a consonant, provitet that the auknent akac is not atet. ere aplies the nalin—"the rule i. 1. 52. s. 42, py thich a supstitute shoult take the place or only the rinal leter or that thich is elhipitet in the kenitive case, is not valit there that is elhipitet in the kenitive is neaninkles, provitet the rule teachink the supstitution toes not teach a chanke in a retuplicative sylaple." avink elitet it or itan, the only portion that renains not is n thich is replacet py a Vi. 2. 102 s. 265. thus te have only a lert. thus a + pyan not Vi. 3. 102 s. 202 teclares that a rinal a is lenkthenet perore a case aril pekinink tith yan put the solitary a is initial ant canot thererore pe rinal ant so it shoult not pe lenkthenet. to renove this toupt, te have the rolotink sûtra.
s: 347. The इद् of इदम् is elided before an âp case affix beginning with a consonant, provided that the augment अकच् is not added. Here applies the maxim—"The rule I. 1. 52. S. 42, by which a substitute should take the place of only the final letter of that which is exhibited in the genitive case, is not valid where what is exhibited in the genitive is meaningless, provided the rule teaching the substitution does not teach a change in a reduplicative syllable." Having elided इद् of इदम्, the only portion that remains now is म् which is replaced by अ VII. 2. 102 S. 265. Thus we have only अ left. Thus अ + भ्याम् Now VII. 3. 102 S. 202 declares that a final अ is lengthened before a case affix beginning with यञ् But the solitary अ is initial and cannot therefore be final and so it should not be lengthened. To remove this doubt, we have the following Sûtra.

pk: 348. nuṇḍi, (also puḍi and suḍi) to shave; to shear, to crush; naitreya says sone say the rot is ‹?› in sone Dhātukoṣas it is given ‹?› Pre. nunqati, punqati noun: nunqa, nunqaka
ck: 348. nuṇḍi, (also puḍi ant suḍi) to shave; to shear, to crush; naitreya says sone say the rot is ‹?› in sone thātukoṣas it is kiven ‹?› pre. nuntati, puntati noun: nunta, nuntaka
s: 348. Muṇḍi, (also puḍi and suḍi) to shave; to shear, to crush; Maitreya says 'Some say the root is ‹?›' In some Dhātukoṣas it is given ‹?› Pre. मुण्डति, पुण्डति Noun: मुण्डः, मुण्डकः

pk: 349. This substitution or Es (required by Vi. 1. 9 s. 203) does not take place arter idan and adas, elcept when they end in ka Thus a + Bi = eBi (Vi. 3. 103 s. 205). The dative rorns are thus rorned:—a + ne = asnE (Vi. 1. 14 s. 215); a + Byan = aByan; a + Bya = eBya The abl:, Gen: and Loc: rorns are as rolow:—asnat, (Vi. 1. 15 s. 216); aByan, eBya; asya (Vi. 1. 12. s. 201); anayo (Vi. 3. 104 s. 207 and Vi. 2. 12. s. 346); esan (Vi. 1. 52. s. 217); asnin (Vi. 1. 15. s. 216); esu (Vi. 3. 59 s. 212). When akac is aded the rorns are as rolows:—non: ayakan, inako, inake; ac: inakan, inako, inakan; instr: inakena, inakaByan, inake By the rolowing rule, when idan is used in the second clause or a sentence rerering to a nan already nentioned in the rirst clause, the rorn is direrent in the instr: and other cases.
ck: 349. this supstitution or Es (retuiret py Vi. 1. 9 s. 203) toes not take place arter itan ant atas, elcept then they ent in ka thus a + pi = epi (Vi. 3. 103 s. 205). the tative rorns are thus rornet:—a + ne = asnE (Vi. 1. 14 s. 215); a + pyan = apyan; a + pya = epya the apl:, ken: ant Loc: rorns are as rolot:—asnat, (Vi. 1. 15 s. 216); apyan, epya; asya (Vi. 1. 12. s. 201); anayo (Vi. 3. 104 s. 207 ant Vi. 2. 12. s. 346); esan (Vi. 1. 52. s. 217); asnin (Vi. 1. 15. s. 216); esu (Vi. 3. 59 s. 212). then akac is atet the rorns are as rolots:—non: ayakan, inako, inake; ac: inakan, inako, inakan; instr: inakena, inakapyan, inake py the rolotink rule, then itan is uset in the secont clause or a sentence rererink to a nan alreaty nentionet in the rirst clause, the rorn is tirerent in the instr: ant other cases.
s: 349. This substitution of ऐस् (required by VII. 1. 9 S. 203) does not take place after इदम् and अदस्, except when they end in क Thus अ + भिः = एभिः (VII. 3. 103 S. 205). The dative forms are thus formed:—अ + ङे = अस्मै (VII. 1. 14 S. 215); अ + भ्याम् = आभ्याम्; अ + भ्यः = एभ्यः The Abl:, Gen: and Loc: forms are as follow:—अस्मात्, (VII. 1. 15 S. 216); आभ्याम्, एभ्यः; अस्य (VII. 1. 12. S. 201); अनयोः (VII. 3. 104 S. 207 and VII. 2. 112. S. 346); एषाम् (VII. 1. 52. S. 217); अस्मिन् (VII. 1. 15. S. 216); एषु (VIII. 3. 59 S. 212). When अकच् is added the forms are as follows:—Nom: अयकम्, इमको, इमके; Acc: इमकम्, इमको, इमकान्; Instr: इमकेन, इमकाभ्याम्, इमकेः By the following rule, when इदम् is used in the second clause of a sentence referring to a man already mentioned in the first clause, the form is different in the Instr: and other cases.

pk: 350. in the ron or idan this, in case or its re-enploynent in a subsequent nenber or the sane sentence and rerering to the sane thing (anvâdeśa) there is the substitution or as which is anudâta i. e., gravely acented, when the third case-aril and the rest rolow. note:—The word anvadesa neans literaly saying (âdeśa) arter (anu) or arter-say or re-enploynent. as (actualy a) replaces idan in al cases elcept the noninative and the acusative, when anvâdeśa or repetition is inplied. a replaces the whole or idan by i. 1. 5 s. 45. and not only the rinal. Telt:—The substitute as wil replace idan, even when the later takes the aril akac (V. 3. 71.)
ck: 350. in the ron or itan this, in case or its re-enploynent in a supsetuent nenper or the sane sentence ant rererink to the sane think (anvâteśa) there is the supstitution or as thich is anutâta i. e., kravely acentet, then the thirt case-aril ant the rest rolot. note:—the tort anvatesa neans literaly sayink (âteśa) arter (anu) or arter-say or re-enploynent. as (actualy a) replaces itan in al cases elcept the noninative ant the acusative, then anvâteśa or repetition is inpliet. a replaces the thole or itan py i. 1. 5 s. 45. ant not only the rinal. telt:—the supstitute as til replace itan, even then the later takes the aril akac (V. 3. 71.)
s: 350. In the room of idam 'this,' in case of its re-employment in a subsequent member of the same sentence and referring to the same thing (anvâdeśa) there is the substitution of अश् which is anudâtta i. e., gravely accented, when the third case-affix and the rest follow. Note:—The word अन्वादेश means literally saying (âdeśa) 'after' (anu) or after-say or re-employment. अश् (actually अ) replaces इदम् in all cases except the nominative and the accusative, when anvâdeśa or repetition is implied. अ replaces the whole of इदम् by I. 1. 55 S. 45. and not only the final. Text:—The substitute अश् will replace इदम्, even when the latter takes the affix अकच् (V. 3. 71.)

pk: 351. ✓ Vaṭi, to divide; to share. This is not round here in the sidhānta. Pre. vanwati
ck: 351. ✓ Vaṭi, to tivite; to share. this is not rount here in the sithānta. pre. vantati
s: 351. ✓ Vaṭi, to divide; to share. This is not found here in the Siddhānta. Pre. वण्टति

pk: 352. (But such n) is not elided in the Locative and Vocative singular. This debars the elision or n, which otherwise would have taken place by the sûtra Vi. 2. 7. s. 236. The elanples or non-elision or n, in the Locative singular are to be round in the Vedas. as parane vyonan (nig. i. 164. 39). ere the sign or the Locative, nanely, (ni) is elided by Vi. 1. 39 s. 3561. in the Vocative singular the n is not elided; as he rajan, he taksan The very ract or the prohibition or the elision or n, as contained in this aphorisn, indicates by inplication (jñâpaka), that a word does get the designation or pada, though an aril has ben elided arter it by using luk, yet such elided aril does sonetines produce its erect in spite or i. 1. 63. s. 263. Vart:— Prohibition or the prohibition nust be stated, when the Locative word is rolowed by another word in a conpound. That is, when a conpound is a Locative Tatpurusha, the n is elided: as, carnani tila asya = carnatila, brahnani nisWa asya = brahnanisWa The non : Dual and Pl : are rajanO ; rajana The ac. sing and Dual are rajanan ; rajanO The ac: Pl. is thus rorned:—rajan + sas ere rajan gets the designation or bha by i. 4. 18. s. 231. and thererore the a or rajan is elided by Vi. 4. 134 s. 234. and the n is changed to n by Vi. 4. 40. s. 1. The elision or a is not sthanivat, because it is so prohibited in sûtra Vi. 2. 1. s. 12. nor can the elision be considered asidha on acount or its being bahiranga. There are two aspects under which sanjna or technical terns, and Paribhâshâs nay be viewed in Paninis Granar. One is yaTodesapaksa and the other is karyakalapaksa. The rorner i e yaTodesan sanjnapariBasan neans that "sanjnas and Paribhashas renain where they are taught ;" and the later, i. e. karyakalan sanjnapariBasan neans that "sanjnâs and Paribhashâs are atracted by, or unite with, the rules that enjoin certain operations, provided that sanjnâs ocur or are valid in those rules, and provided the Paribhashâs concern then." ere we take the rirst alternative and the change or n into n being asidha in the view or the rule i. 1. 94. s. 38., there is no antaranga-hod and so the Paribhasha which declares that "antaranga is stronger than bahiranga" rinds no scope ror aplication. Thererore j and n conbining rorn jna. Thus we get the ac. Pl. rajna; inst. sing is rajna sinilarly parane vyonan ere vyonan is in the Locative case. vyonan + ni = vyonan + 0 (Vi. 1. 39, s. 3561) ere the aril is elided by using the word luk, and thererore
ck: 352. (put such n) is not elitet in the Locative ant Vocative sinkular. this tepars the elision or n, thich othertise toult have taken place py the sûtra Vi. 2. 7. s. 236. the elanples or non-elision or n, in the Locative sinkular are to pe rount in the Vetas. as parane vyonan (nik. i. 164. 39). ere the sikn or the Locative, nanely, (ni) is elitet py Vi. 1. 39 s. 3561. in the Vocative sinkular the n is not elitet; as he racan, he taksan the very ract or the prohipition or the elision or n, as containet in this aphorisn, inticates py inplication (cñâpaka), that a tort toes ket the tesiknation or pata, thoukh an aril has pen elitet arter it py usink luk, yet such elitet aril toes sonetines protuce its erect in spite or i. 1. 63. s. 263. Vart:— prohipition or the prohipition nust pe statet, then the Locative tort is rolotet py another tort in a conpount. that is, then a conpount is a Locative tatpurusha, the n is elitet: as, carnani tila asya = carnatila, prahnani nista asya = prahnanista the non : tual ant pl : are racanO ; racana the ac. sink ant tual are racanan ; racanO the ac: pl. is thus rornet:—racan + sas ere racan kets the tesiknation or pha py i. 4. 18. s. 231. ant thererore the a or racan is elitet py Vi. 4. 134 s. 234. ant the n is chanket to n py Vi. 4. 40. s. 1. the elision or a is not sthanivat, pecause it is so prohipitet in sûtra Vi. 2. 1. s. 12. nor can the elision pe consiteret asitha on acount or its peink pahiranka. there are to aspects unter thich sancna or technical terns, ant pariphâshâs nay pe vietet in paninis kranar. s: 352. (But such न्) is not elided in the Locative and Vocative Singular. This debars the elision of न्, which otherwise would have taken place by the sûtra VIII. 2. 7. S. 236. The examples of non-elision of न्, in the Locative singular are to be found in the Vedas. As परमे व्योमन् (Rig. I. 164. 39). Here the sign of the Locative, namely, (ङि) is elided by VII. 1. 39 S. 3561. In the Vocative singular the न् is not elided; as हे राजन्, हे तक्षन् The very fact of the prohibition of the elision of न्, as contained in this aphorism, indicates by implication (jñâpaka), that a word does get the designation of pada, though an affix has been elided after it by using लुक्, yet such elided affix does sometimes produce its effect in spite of I. 1. 63. S. 263. Vart:— Prohibition of the prohibition must be stated, when the Locative word is followed by another word in a compound. That is, when a compound is a Locative Tatpurusha, the न् is elided: as, चर्माणि तिला अस्य = चर्मतिलः, ब्रह्मणि निष्ठा अस्य = ब्रह्मनिष्ठः The Nom : Dual and Pl : are राजानौ ; राजानः The Acc. Sing and Dual are राजानम् ; राजानौ The Acc: Pl. is thus formed:—राजन् + शस् Here राजन् gets the designation of bha by I. 4. 18. S. 231. and therefore the अ of राजन् is elided by VI. 4. 134 S. 234. and the न् is changed to ञ् by VIII. 4. 40. S. 111. The elision of अ is not Sthanivat, because it is so prohibited in Sûtra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12. Nor can the elision be considered asiddha on account of its being bahiranga. There are two aspects under which संज्ञा or technical terms, and Paribhâshâs may be viewed in Panini's Grammar. One is यथोद्देशपक्ष and the other is कार्यकालपक्ष. The former i e यथोद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् means that "Samjnas and Paribhashas remain where they are taught ;" and the latter, i. e. कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् means that "Samjnâs and Paribhashâs are attracted by, or unite with, the rules that enjoin certain operations, provided that Samjnâs occur or are valid in those rules, and provided the Paribhashâs concern them." Here we take the first alternative and the change of न् into ञ् being asiddha in the view of the rule I. 1. 94. S. 38., there is no antaranga-hood and so the Paribhasha which declares that "antaranga is stronger than bahiranga" finds no scope for application. Therefore ज् and ञ् combining form ज्ञ. Thus we get the Acc. Pl. राज्ञः; Inst. Sing is राज्ञा Similarly परमे व्योमन् Here व्योमन् is in the Locative case. व्योमन् + ङि = व्योमन् + 0 (VII. 1. 39, S. 3561) Here the affix is elided by using the word लुक्, and therefore there will be no pratyaya-lakshana (I. 1. 63 S. 263). The result would be that the word व्योमन् would not get the designation of पद (सुप्तिङन्तं पदं) because it has no सुप् after it, so the rule (VIII. 2. 7. S. 236) will not hold good, and therefore there will be no elision of न् of व्योमन्. But in that case the present Sûtra would have been useless. But the very fact that this sûtra is made, indicates that the rule न लुमता is not nitya, and so, there will be pratyayalakshana. That being the case, the word becomes पद, and so rule VIII. 2. 7 would have applied to it, but for this Sûtra. Although ‹?› excludes and debars ‹?›, but in this case it has been superseded by the former. Now we take up the formation of Acc. pl. Thus राजन् + शस् = राज् + 0 + न् + शस् (अल्लोपोऽनः) Here the zero will be sthânivat (by अचः परस्मिन् I. 1. 57 S. 50) That being the case, न् will not be changed to ञ् and so we could not get the form राज्ञः But the lopâdeśa is not sthânivat, because of the vârttika पूर्वत्रासिद्धे न स्थानिवत् (See Mahâbhâshya I. 1. 58 and Siddhânta VIII. 4. 1) If it be said that the lopa rule is Bahiranga, because it takes place on account of the affix which is outside; and the change of न् into ञ् is inside it, or antaranga; and therefore the lopa will be asiddha with regard to ञ्, then we reply that there is no relation of Antaranga and Bahiranga here. The Paribhâshâ &c. is derived from the Jñâpaka of वाह ऊठ् (VI. 4. 132 S. 329) which

pk: 354. Or a rot ending in r or v, the penultinate i or u is lengthened, berore a consonantal begining aril. Or a rot entink in r or v, the penultinate i or u is lenkthenet, perore a consonantal pekinink aril. the lenkthenink takes place here, the elision or ‹?› is not consiteret here as sthānivat pecause or the prohipition in i. 1. 58 s. 57 tith rekart to tirkaviti ant so v pecones penultinate. nor is this elision py Vi. 4. 134. s. 234. a pahiraṅka ant thererore asitha, ror the purposes or this rule thich is an antaraṅka, ror the reasons alreaty kiven apove unter Vi. 2. 8. s. 352. thus ac : pl : is pratitivya instr: sk. pratitivya &c. -:0:- not te take up the teclension or yacvan its non: rorns are yacva, yacvanO, yacvana put in pha cases there til not pe the elision or a or nan pecause or the rolotink prohipition.
s: 354. Of a root ending in र् or व्, the penultimate इ or उ is lengthened, before a consonantal beginning affix. The lengthening takes place here, the elision of ‹?› is not considered here as sthānivat because of the prohibition in I. 1. 58 S. 57 with regard to दीर्घविधिः and so व् becomes penultimate. s: 355. The अ in अन् is not elided when the Bha stem ends in a consonant preceding व् or मन् Thus Acc : Pl : यज्वनः Instr: Sing and dual यज्वना, यज्वभ्याम् &c. Similar is the declension of ब्रह्मन् Nom. ब्रह्मा, ब्रह्माणौ, ब्रह्माणः, Acc. ब्रह्माणम्, ब्रह्माणौ, ब्रह्मणः; Ins. ब्रह्मणा, ब्रह्मभ्याम्, ब्रह्मभिः -:0:- Now, we take up the declension of वृत्रहन् In its declension the following rule applies :—

pk: 356. The penultinate vowel is lengthened only berore the aril si ( noninative and acusative Pl. ), when the sten ends in in, or han, or pusan or aryanan and nowhere else. To this prohibition is the elception contained in the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 356. the penultinate votel is lenkthenet only perore the aril si ( noninative ant acusative pl. ), then the sten ents in in, or han, or pusan or aryanan ant nothere else. to this prohipition is the elception containet in the rolotink sūtra.
s: 356. The penultimate vowel is lengthened only before the affix शि ( Nominative and Accusative Pl. ), when the stem ends in इन्, or हन्, or पूषन् or अर्यमन् and nowhere else. To this prohibition is the exception contained in the following sūtra.

pk: 357. The penultinate vowels or a sten ending in in, han, pusan or aryanan are lengthened berore the aril su or the noninative singular, but not in Vocative singular. Thus vrtraha The n is elided by Vi. 2. 7. s. 236, and the case-aril by Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. in the Vocative singular we have he vrtrahan The na is changed to na by Vi. 4. 12 s. 307. Thus we get the rolowing rorns n. D. vrtrahanO ; n. Pl : vrtrahana, ac: sg and Dual : vrtrahanan and vrtrahanO respectively. in ac : Pl : the a or han is elided by Vi. 4. 134 s. 234 and the h is changed to gutural by the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 357. the penultinate votels or a sten entink in in, han, pusan or aryanan are lenkthenet perore the aril su or the noninative sinkular, put not in Vocative sinkular. thus vrtraha the n is elitet py Vi. 2. 7. s. 236, ant the case-aril py Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. in the Vocative sinkular te have he vrtrahan the na is chanket to na py Vi. 4. 12 s. 307. thus te ket the rolotink rorns n. t. vrtrahanO ; n. pl : vrtrahana, ac: sk ant tual : vrtrahanan ant vrtrahanO respectively. in ac : pl : the a or han is elitet py Vi. 4. 134 s. 234 ant the h is chanket to kutural py the rolotink sūtra.
s: 357. The penultimate vowels of a stem ending in इन्, हन्, पूषन् or अर्यमन् are lengthened before the affix सु of the Nominative Singular, but not in Vocative Singular. Thus वृत्रहा The न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236, and the case-affix by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. In the Vocative singular we have हे वृत्रहन् The न is changed to ण by VIII. 4. 12 S. 307. Thus we get the following forms N. D. वृत्रहणौ ; N. Pl : वृत्रहणः, Acc: Sg and Dual : वृत्रहणम् and वृत्रहणौ respectively. In Acc : Pl : the अ of हन् is elided by VI. 4. 134 S. 234 and the ह् is changed to guttural by the following Sūtra.

pk: 358. a gutural is substituted ror the h in han berore an aril having an indicatory n, or n and berore n The nelt sūtra hanteratpurvasya is divided by the author into two parts, vis., rirst, hante and then atpurvasya
ck: 358. a kutural is supstitutet ror the h in han perore an aril havink an inticatory n, or n ant perore n the nelt sūtra hanteratpurvasya is tivitet py the author into to parts, vis., rirst, hante ant then atpurvasya

pk: 359. The na, in the rot han, is changed to na, when the verb is preceded by a preposition conpetent to cause the change. as prahanyat This requires the n or vrtrahan to be changed to na But to this the second halr or the above sūtra nakes an elception,
ck: 359. the na, in the rot han, is chanket to na, then the verp is precetet py a preposition conpetent to cause the chanke. as prahanyat this retuires the n or vrtrahan to pe chanket to na put to this the secont halr or the apove sūtra nakes an elception,

pk: 360. tr is diversely substituted ror the rinal or naGavan. r or tr is it. and thus we get naGavat. ere aplies the nelt sūtra, showing the rorce or this indicatory,
ck: 360. tr is tiversely supstitutet ror the rinal or nakavan. r or tr is it. ant thus te ket nakavat. ere aplies the nelt sūtra, shotink the rorce or this inticatory,
s: 360. तृ is diversely substituted for the final of मघवन्. ऋ of तृ is इत्. And thus we get मघवत्. Here applies the next Sūtra, showing the force of this indicatory,

pk: 361. Whatever has an indicatory u, r and l, (with the elception or a rot), and the sten anc, (nancati) get the augnent nun in the strong cases. Thus non : sing. is naGavan. The penultinate a is lengthened by Vi. 4. 14. s. 425. The aril is elided by Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. and the t is elided by Vi. 2. 23. s. 54. The rorn being naGavanta, the elision or t takes place by the Tripadi rule sanyogantasya lopa Vi. 2. 23. s. 54. and thererore this elision is not perceived by the dirGa rule or the silth Bok or Panini (i.e. Vi. 4. 14. s. 425). The a or vant thererore not being penultinate wil not be lengthened, as it is not lengthened in Verbal nouns like ‹?› &c, where also the elision or t is held to be asidha. Why do we lengthen it in the case or naGavan ? Because or the word bahulan in the last sutra Vi. 4. 128 s. 360. as this word naGavan requires the help or bahula to give us the proper rorn, the author or nahābhashya has erected the rornation or naGavan by the unadi i. 159, and he has also asuned that the aril natup wil erect the sane rorn when aded to naGa in secular literature, and thererore he has in his conentary stated that the sūtra naGava bahulan is a redundancy. The author or Bhati Kavya also uses the rorn in secular literature as:— ‹?› "That naghavan eats rearlesly the sacriricial orerings in the sacririces." The non : Dual and Pl. wil be naGavantO, naGavanta The Voc : sing wil be he naGavan The ac. rorns are naGavantan, naGavantO, naGavata instr: rorns are naGavata, naGavadByan &c. When tr is not substituted ror the rinal n or naGavan, then the non : sing is naGava Vartika:—in the Chandas, the ariles ini and vanip are aded to nouns in the sense or natup (se sūtra V. 2. 12. s. 3498). Thererore ir the word naGavan be rorned with vanip aded to naGa then the word naGavan wil have acute acent on the nidle in the Chandas alone, but in the secular literature it has acute acent on the rinal also. This is the direrence, as naGavan. The non : Dual and Pl. are naGavanO, naGavana in the sarvanānasthāna ariles, naGavan, without tr is declined like rajan. Thus n. D. naGavanO, n. Pl. naGavana; ac. s. D. are naGavanan and naGavanO. in rorning the ac. Pl, the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 361. thatever has an inticatory u, r ant l, (tith the elception or a rot), ant the sten anc, (nancati) ket the auknent nun in the stronk cases. thus non : sink. is nakavan. the penultinate a is lenkthenet py Vi. 4. 14. s. 425. the aril is elitet py Vi. 1. 68. s. 252. ant the t is elitet py Vi. 2. 23. s. 54. the rorn peink nakavanta, the elision or t takes place py the tripati rule sanyokantasya lopa Vi. 2. 23. s. 54. ant thererore this elision is not perceivet py the tirka rule or the silth pok or panini (i.e. Vi. 4. 14. s. 425). the a or vant thererore not peink penultinate til not pe lenkthenet, as it is not lenkthenet in Verpal nouns like ‹?› &c, there also the elision or t is helt to pe asitha. thy to te lenkthen it in the case or nakavan ? pecause or the tort pahulan in the last sutra Vi. 4. 128 s. 360. as this tort nakavan retuires the help or pahula to kive us the proper rorn, the author or nahāphashya has erectet the rornation or nakavan py the unati i. 159, ant he has also asunet that the aril natup til erect the sane rorn then atet to naka in secular literature, ant thererore he has in his conentary statet that the sūtra nakava pahulan is a retuntancy. the author or phati kavya also uses the rorn in secular literature as:— ‹?› "that nakhavan eats rearlesly the sacriricial orerinks in the sacririces." the non : tual ant pl. til pe nakavantO, nakavanta the Voc : sink til pe he nakavan the ac. rorns are nakavantan, nakavantO, nakavata instr: rorns are nakavata, nakavatpyan &c. then tr is not supstitutet ror the rinal n or nakavan, then the non : sink is nakava Vartika:—in the chantas, the ariles ini ant vanip are atet to nouns in the sense or natup (se sūtra V. 2. 12. s. 3498). thererore ir the tort nakavan pe rornet tith vanip atet to naka then the tort nakavan til have acute acent on the nitle in the chantas alone, put in the secular literature it has acute acent on the rinal also. this is the tirerence, as nakavan. the non : tual ant pl. are nakavanO, nakavana in the sarvanānasthāna ariles, nakavan, tithout tr is teclinet like racan. thus n. t. nakavanO, n. pl. nakavana; ac. s. t. are nakavanan ant nakavanO. in rornink the ac. pl, the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 361. Whatever has an indicatory उ, ऋ and ऌ, (with the exception of a root), and the stem अञ्च्, (मञ्चति) get the augment नुम् in the strong cases. Thus Nom : Sing. is मघवान्. The penultimate अ is lengthened by VI. 4. 14. S. 425. The affix is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. and the त् is elided by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54. The form being मघवन्त, the elision of त् takes place by the Tripadi rule संयोगान्तस्य लोपः VIII. 2. 23. S. 54. and therefore this elision is not perceived by the दीर्घ rule of the Sixth Book of Panini (i.e. VI. 4. 14. S. 425). The a of वन्त् therefore not being penultimate will not be lengthened, as it is not lengthened in Verbal Nouns like ‹?› &c, where also the elision of त् is held to be asiddha. Why do we lengthen it in the case of मघवन् ? Because of the word बहुलं in the last Sutra VI. 4. 128 S. 360. As this word मघवान् requires the help of बहुल to give us the proper form, the author of Mahābhashya has effected the formation of मघवान् by the Unadi I. 159, and he has also assumed that the affix मतुप् will effect the same form when added to मघ in secular literature, and therefore he has in his commentary stated that the Sūtra मघवा बहुलं is a redundancy. The author of Bhatti Kavya also uses the form in secular literature as:— ‹?› "That Maghavan eats fearlessly the sacrificial offerings in the sacrifices." The Nom : Dual and Pl. will be मघवन्तौ, मघवन्तः The Voc : Sing will be हे मघवन् The Acc. forms are मघवन्तम्, मघवन्तौ, मघवतः Instr: forms are मघवता, मघवद्भ्याम् &c. When तृ is not substituted for the final न् of मघवन्, then the Nom : Sing is मघवा Vartika:—In the Chhandas, the affixes इनि and वनिप् are added to nouns in the sense of मतुप् (See Sūtra V. 2. 122. S. 3498). Therefore if the word मघवन् be formed with वनिप् added to मघ then the word मघवन् will have acute accent on the middle in the Chhandas alone, but in the secular literature it has acute accent on the final also. This is the difference, as मघवन्. The Nom : Dual and Pl. are मघवानौ, मघवानः In the Sarvanāmasthāna affixes, मघवन्, without तृ is declined like राजन्. Thus N. D. मघवानौ, N. Pl. मघवानः; Acc. S. D. are मघवानम् and मघवानौ. In forming the Acc. Pl, the following rule applies :—

pk: 362. The va or svan, yuvan and naGavan when ending in an becones vocalised, but not berore a Tadhita aril. Thus naGavan + sas = naG u an + sas = naG un + sas (a and u becone u by Vi. 1. 108. s. 30) = naGona + sas (a and u becone o by Vi. 1. 87. s. 69) = naGona Why do we say when ending in an? Observe ac : Pl : naGavata when the noun is naGavat and not naGavan in this case the instr : sg. is naGavata The reninine rorn or naGavat is naGavati Why do we say not berore a Tadhita aril? Observe naGavanan The instr : sg. and Dual or naGavan are naGona, naGavadByan &c. sinilar is the declension or svan Thus suna (ac. Pl.), suna (instr : s.), svaByan (instr : Dual) &c. now we take up the declension or yuvan yuvan + sas = yu + u + n + sas ere the ya or yuvan would also require to be vocalised. But this is prevented by the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 362. the va or svan, yuvan ant nakavan then entink in an pecones vocaliset, put not perore a tathita aril. thus nakavan + sas = nak u an + sas = nak un + sas (a ant u pecone u py Vi. 1. 108. s. 30) = nakona + sas (a ant u pecone o py Vi. 1. 87. s. 69) = nakona thy to te say then entink in an? Opserve ac : pl : nakavata then the noun is nakavat ant not nakavan in this case the instr : sk. is nakavata the reninine rorn or nakavat is nakavati thy to te say not perore a tathita aril? Opserve nakavanan the instr : sk. ant tual or nakavan are nakona, nakavatpyan &c. sinilar is the teclension or svan thus suna (ac. pl.), suna (instr : s.), svapyan (instr : tual) &c. not te take up the teclension or yuvan yuvan + sas = yu + u + n + sas ere the ya or yuvan toult also retuire to pe vocaliset. put this is preventet py the rolotink sūtra.
s: 362. The व of श्वन्, युवन् and मघवन् when ending in अन् becomes vocalised, but not before a Taddhita affix. Thus मघवन् + शस् = मघ् उ अन् + शस् = मघ् उन् + शस् (अ and उ become उ by VI. 1. 108. S. 330) = मघोन + शस् (अ and उ become ओ by VI. 1. 87. S. 69) = मघोनः Why do we say 'when ending in अन्'? Observe Acc : Pl : मघवतः when the noun is मघवत् and not मघवन् In this case the Instr : Sg. is मघवता The feminine form of मघवत् is मघवती Why do we say 'not before a Taddhita affix'? Observe माघवनम् The Instr : Sg. and Dual of मघवन् are मघोना, मघवद्भ्याम् &c. Similar is the declension of श्वन् Thus शुनः (Acc. Pl.), शुना (Instr : S.), श्वभ्याम् (Instr : Dual) &c. Now we take up the declension of युवन् युवन् + शस् = यु + उ + न् + शस् Here the य of युवन् would also require to be vocalised. But this is prevented by the following Sūtra.

s: 363. ✓ Satha, to cheat, and also 'to hurt,' 'to feel pain.' Pre. शठति Per. शशाठ, शेठतुः, शेठुः I Fut. शठिता Aorist अशाठीत्, अशठीत् Caus. शाठयति Desi. शिशाठिषति Inten. शाशठ्यते Yaṅ luk, शाशठीति, ‹?›

pk: 364. sutha, to be inpeded or hindered. Pre. soWati, sunWati Per. susoWa, susunWa i rut. soWita, sunWita aorist asoWit, asunWit Caus. soWayati, sunWayati Desi. susoWisati, susunWisati inten. ‹?›

s: 364. Sutha, to be impeded or hindered. Pre. शोठति, शुण्ठति Per. शुशोठ, शुशुण्ठ I Fut. शोठिता, शुण्ठिता Aorist अशोठीत्, अशुण्ठीत् Caus. शोठयति, शुण्ठयति Desi. शुशोठिषति, शुशुण्ठिषति Inten. ‹?›

pk: 365. at ( a ) is substituted ror the rinal or pathin, nathin and ṛbhukshin, berore the ending su (or the non. sg.). Though the sthānin here is a nasal (i. e. n), yet the substitute a is not to be nasalised by the rule or nearnes (i. 1. 50. 39) but to be pronounced purely, ror the at or the sûtra is realy a + at, indicating that pure a is to be taken and not the nasal an
ck: 365. at ( a ) is supstitutet ror the rinal or pathin, nathin ant ṛphukshin, perore the entink su (or the non. sk.). thoukh the sthānin here is a nasal (i. e. n), yet the supstitute a is not to pe nasaliset py the rule or nearnes (i. 1. 50. 39) put to pe pronouncet purely, ror the at or the sûtra is realy a + at, inticatink that pure a is to pe taken ant not the nasal an
s: 365. आत् ( आ ) is substituted for the final of 'pathin', 'mathin' and 'ṛbhukshin', before the ending सु (of the Nom. Sg.). Though the sthānin here is a nasal (i. e. न्), yet the substitute आ is not to be nasalised by the rule of nearness (I. 1. 50. 39) but to be pronounced purely, for the आत् of the sûtra is really आ + आत्, indicating that pure आ is to be taken and not the nasal आँ

pk: 36. at is substituted ror the i or pathin, nathin and ṛbhukshin, in the strong cases. note:—Though the anuvṛiti or at was here, the separate nention or at is ror the sake or Vi. 4. 98 s. 354 by which in the case or rBuksin we have two rorns, rBuksanan and rBuksanan
ck: 36. at is supstitutet ror the i or pathin, nathin ant ṛphukshin, in the stronk cases. note:—thoukh the anuvṛiti or at tas here, the separate nention or at is ror the sake or Vi. 4. 98 s. 354 py thich in the case or rpuksin te have to rorns, rpuksanan ant rpuksanan
s: 366. अत् is substituted for the इ of 'pathin', 'mathin' and 'ṛbhukshin', in the strong cases. Note:—Though the anuvṛitti of आत् was here, the separate mention of अत् is for the sake of VI. 4. 98 S. 354 by which in the case of ऋभुक्षिन् we have two forms, ऋभुक्षाणम् and ऋभुक्षणम्

pk: 368. The last vowel, with the consonant that rolows it, is droped in pathin, nathin, and ṛbhukshin, berore an aril begining with a vowel or ya (berore which the sten is caled Bha i. 4. 18). as paTa, paTa, paTe, naTa, naTa, naTe, rBuksa, rBuksa, rBukse in the reninine the aril nip wil be aded by iV. 1. 5. as paTin + nip, and the in is elided berore the aril nip by the present sûtra. Thus supaTi nagari, and rBuksi sena. in the neuter, there is no lengthening or Vi. 1. 85. s. 365. because the aril is elided by using the word luk (Vi. 1. 23. s. 319) and thererore the aril su leaves no trace behind by i. 1. 63. s. 263. Thus supaTi vanan. Thus supaTin + su = supaTin + 0 = supaTi (The rinal n is elided by Vi. 2. 7, s. 236). in the Vocative sing. or the neuter noun supaTin, the elision or n is optional, acording to the rolowing Vārtika:— Vārtika:—in the Voc. singular or the neuter nouns, the elision or rinal n is optional. Thus he supaTin or he supaTi. The short i or supaTi is not guṇated (as it is guṇated in he hare) because or the prohibition contained in Vi. 2. 2, s. 353 by which the elision or n is asidha in the case or case-endings. in the non: Dual, the base being bha, the wi portion or paTin is elided berore the Dual aril si. Thus supaTi in the non: Pl. (si) which is a sarvanānasthāna aril (i. 1. 42. s. 313) there is no elision and the rules Vi. 1. 86 and 87 s. 36 and 367 aply and so we get the rorn supanTani The ac: rorns are the sane as the noninative ones, as supaTi, supaTi, supanTani The instr: sing and Dual are supaTa, supaTiByan The Dative sing: is supaTe &c. now, we take up the declension or pancan. it is a saw word by the rolowing derinition.
ck: 368. the last votel, tith the consonant that rolots it, is tropet in pathin, nathin, ant ṛphukshin, perore an aril pekinink tith a votel or ya (perore thich the sten is calet pha i. 4. 18). as pata, pata, pate, nata, nata, nate, rpuksa, rpuksa, rpukse in the reninine the aril nip til pe atet py iV. 1. 5. as patin + nip, ant the in is elitet perore the aril nip py the present sûtra. thus supati nakari, ant rpuksi sena. in the neuter, there is no lenkthenink or Vi. 1. 85. s. 365. pecause the aril is elitet py usink the tort luk (Vi. 1. 23. s. 319) ant thererore the aril su leaves no trace pehint py i. 1. 63. s. 263. thus supati vanan. thus supatin + su = supatin + 0 = supati (the rinal n is elitet py Vi. 2. 7, s. 236). in the Vocative sink. or the neuter noun supatin, the elision or n is optional, acortink to the rolotink Vārtika:— Vārtika:—in the Voc. sinkular or the neuter nouns, the elision or rinal n is optional. thus he supatin or he supati. the short i or supati is not kuṇatet (as it is kuṇatet in he hare) pecause or the prohipition containet in Vi. 2. 2, s. 353 py thich the elision or n is asitha in the case or case-entinks. in the non: tual, the pase peink pha, the ti portion or patin is elitet perore the tual aril si. thus supati in the non: pl. (si) thich is a sarvanānasthāna aril (i. 1. 42. s. 313) there is no elision ant the rules Vi. 1. 86 ant 87 s. 36 ant 367 aply ant so te ket the rorn supantani the ac: rorns are the sane as the noninative ones, as supati, supati, supantani the instr: sink ant tual are supata, supatipyan the tative sink: is supate &c. not, te take up the teclension or pancan. it is a sat tort py the rolotink terinition.
s: 368. The last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, is dropped in pathin, mathin, and ṛbhukshin, before an affix beginning with a vowel or य (before which the stem is called Bha I. 4. 18). As पथः, पथा, पथे, मथः, मथा, मथे, ऋभुक्षः, ऋभुक्षा, ऋभुक्षे In the Feminine the affix ङीप् will be added by IV. 1. 5. as पथिन् + ङीप्, and the इन् is elided before the affix ङीप् by the present Sûtra. Thus सुपथी नगरी, and ऋभुक्षी सेना. In the Neuter, there is no lengthening of VII. 1. 85. S. 365. because the affix is elided by using the word लुक् (VII. 1. 23. S. 319) and therefore the affix सु leaves no trace behind by I. 1. 63. S. 263. Thus सुपथि वनम्. Thus सुपथिन् + सु = सुपथिन् + 0 = सुपथि (The final न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7, S. 236). In the Vocative Sing. of the Neuter Noun सुपथिन्, the elision of न् is optional, according to the following Vārtika:— Vārtika:—In the Voc. Singular of the Neuter nouns, the elision of final न् is optional. Thus हे सुपथिन् or हे सुपथि. The short इ of सुपथि is not guṇated (as it is guṇated in हे हरे) because of the prohibition contained in VIII. 2. 2, S. 353 by which the elision of न् is asiddha in the case of case-endings. In the Nom: Dual, the base being bha, the टि portion of पथिन् is elided before the Dual affix शी. Thus सुपथी In the Nom: Pl. (शि) which is a Sarvanāmasthāna affix (I. 1. 42. S. 313) there is no elision and the rules VII. 1. 86 and 87 S. 366 and 367 apply and so we get the form सुपन्थानि The Acc: forms are the same as the Nominative ones, as सुपथि, सुपथी, सुपन्थानि The Instr: Sing and Dual are सुपथा, सुपथिभ्याम् The Dative Sing: is सुपथे &c. Now, we take up the declension of पञ्चन्. It is a षट् word by the following definition.

pk: 369. The saṅkhyās having s or n as their rinal are caled ṣaṭ. it is one or the peculiarities or saw words that they lose their noninative and acusative plural terninations (Vi. 1. 2. s. 261). Thus panca, panca Why do we say sanKya Observe viprusa and panana note:—This sûtra derines the tern saw which is a subdivision or the larger group saṅkhyā. Those saṅkhyās which end in s or n are caled saw The word saṅkhyā is understod in this sûtra, because the word saw is in the reninine gender, showing that it qualiries saṅkhyā which is also reninine. The nunerals that end in s or n are sil, nanely pancan rive, sas sil, saptan seven, aswan eight, navan nine, dasan ten. The word anta in the sûtra shows that the leters s and n nust be aupadeśika i. e., nust belong to the words as originaly enunciated and not aded arterwards as aril &c. Thus in satani hundreds, sahasrani thousands, aswanan or eights the n is not radical, but an augnent, and thererore they are not saw and the noninative and acusative plural terninations are not elided; as satan + i = satani &c. in rorning non: Pl: or sata we have sata + si. Then we ad nun by Vi. 1. 72. s. 314. Thus we get satani. ere the word sata is a saṅkhyā and ends in n. Why should not this si be elided by Vi. 1. 2. s. 261? This si is not elided by the nalin sanipatapariBasa ror the nalin, se Vi. 1. 13. s. 204. Because it was the presence or si that caused the insertion or nun and now this n canot cause the destruction or its originator. Thus we get satani sahasrani is also sinilarly rorned. The instr, Dative and abl: plurals are pancaBi, pancaBya, pancaBya respectively. The augnent nuw is aded by Vi. 1. 5. s. 38 in rorning the Gen. Pl: Then the rolowing sûtra cones into operation.
ck: 369. the saṅkhyās havink s or n as their rinal are calet ṣaṭ. it is one or the peculiarities or sat torts that they lose their noninative ant acusative plural terninations (Vi. 1. 2. s. 261). thus panca, panca thy to te say sankya Opserve viprusa ant panana note:—this sûtra terines the tern sat thich is a suptivision or the larker kroup saṅkhyā. those saṅkhyās thich ent in s or n are calet sat the tort saṅkhyā is unterstot in this sûtra, pecause the tort sat is in the reninine kenter, shotink that it tualiries saṅkhyā thich is also reninine. the nunerals that ent in s or n are sil, nanely pancan rive, sas sil, saptan seven, astan eikht, navan nine, tasan ten. the tort anta in the sûtra shots that the leters s ant n nust pe aupateśika i. e., nust pelonk to the torts as orikinaly enunciatet ant not atet artertarts as aril &c. thus in satani huntrets, sahasrani thousants, astanan or eikhts the n is not ratical, put an auknent, ant thererore they are not sat ant the noninative ant acusative plural terninations are not elitet; as satan + i = satani &c. in rornink non: pl: or sata te have sata + si. then te at nun py Vi. 1. 72. s. 314. thus te ket satani. ere the tort sata is a saṅkhyā ant ents in n. thy shoult not this si pe elitet py Vi. 1. 2. s. 261? this si is not elitet py the nalin sanipataparipasa ror the nalin, se Vi. 1. 13. s. 204. pecause it tas the presence or si that causet the insertion or nun ant not this n canot cause the testruction or its orikinator. thus te ket satani sahasrani is also sinilarly rornet. the instr, tative ant apl: plurals are pancapi, pancapya, pancapya respectively. the auknent nut is atet py Vi. 1. 5. s. 38 in rornink the ken. pl: then the rolotink sûtra cones into operation.
s: 369. The Saṅkhyās having ष् or न् as their final are called ṣaṭ. It is one of the peculiarities of षट् words that they lose their nominative and accusative plural terminations (VII. 1. 22. S. 261). Thus पञ्च, पञ्च Why do we say संख्या Observe विप्रुषः and पामानः Note:—This sûtra defines the term षट् which is a subdivision of the larger group saṅkhyā. Those Saṅkhyās which end in ष् or न् are called षट् The word saṅkhyā is understood in this sûtra, because the word षट् is in the feminine gender, showing that it qualifies saṅkhyā which is also feminine. The numerals that end in ष् or न् are six, namely पञ्चन् 'five', षष् 'six', सप्तन् 'seven', अष्टन् 'eight', नवन् 'nine', दशन् 'ten'. The word अन्तः in the sûtra shows that the letters ष् and न् must be aupadeśika i. e., must belong to the words as originally enunciated and not added afterwards as affix &c. Thus in शतानि 'hundreds', सहस्राणि 'thousands', अष्टानाम् 'of eights' the न् is not radical, but an augment, and therefore they are not षट् and the nominative and accusative plural terminations are not elided; as शतान् + इ = शतानि &c. In forming Nom: Pl: of शत we have शत + शि. Then we add नुम् by VII. 1. 72. S. 314. Thus we get शतानि. Here the word शत is a saṅkhyā and ends in न्. Why should not this शि be elided by VII. 1. 22. S. 261? This शि is not elided by the maxim संनिपातपरिभाषा For the maxim, see VII. 1. 13. S. 204. Because it was the presence of शि that caused the insertion of नुम् and now this न् cannot cause the destruction of its originator. Thus we get शतानि सहस्राणि is also similarly formed. The Instr, Dative and Abl: plurals are पञ्चभिः, पञ्चभ्यः, पञ्चभ्यः respectively. The augment नुट् is added by VII. 1. 55. S. 338 in forming the Gen. Pl: Then the following sûtra comes into operation.

pk: 370. in a sten ending in n, the preceding vowel is lengthened berore the aril nan Thus pancan + nan (Vi. 1. 5, s. 38) = pancan + nan (Vi. 4. 7, s. 370) = pancanan (n being elided by Vi. 2. 7, s. 236). The Loc. Pl. is pancasu sinilar is the declension or paranapanca Thus n. Pl. paranapanca, Gen. Pl. is paranapancanan When panca is a secondary nenber or a conpound, there is neither luk or sûtra Vi. 1. 2, s. 261, nor the nuw augnent or Vi. 1. 5, s. 38. Thus priyapancan is declined as non. priyapanca, priyapancanO, priyapancana; ac. priyapancanan sinilar is the declension or saptan, navan and dasan in the declension or aswan the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 370. in a sten entink in n, the precetink votel is lenkthenet perore the aril nan thus pancan + nan (Vi. 1. 5, s. 38) = pancan + nan (Vi. 4. 7, s. 370) = pancanan (n peink elitet py Vi. 2. 7, s. 236). the Loc. pl. is pancasu sinilar is the teclension or paranapanca thus n. pl. paranapanca, ken. pl. is paranapancanan then panca is a secontary nenper or a conpount, there is neither luk or sûtra Vi. 1. 2, s. 261, nor the nut auknent or Vi. 1. 5, s. 38. thus priyapancan is teclinet as non. priyapanca, priyapancanO, priyapancana; ac. priyapancanan sinilar is the teclension or saptan, navan ant tasan in the teclension or astan the rolotink rules aply.
s: 370. In a stem ending in न्, the preceding vowel is lengthened before the affix नाम् Thus पञ्चन् + नाम् (VII. 1. 55, S. 338) = पञ्चान् + नाम् (VI. 4. 7, S. 370) = पञ्चानाम् (न् being elided by VIII. 2. 7, S. 236). The Loc. Pl. is पञ्चसु Similar is the declension of परमपञ्च Thus N. Pl. परमपञ्च, Gen. Pl. is परमपञ्चानाम् When पञ्च is a secondary member of a compound, there is neither लुक् of Sûtra VII. 1. 22, S. 261, nor the नुट् augment of VII. 1. 55, S. 338. Thus प्रियपञ्चन् is declined as Nom. प्रियपञ्चा, प्रियपञ्चानौ, प्रियपञ्चानः; Acc. प्रियपञ्चानम् Similar is the declension of सप्तन्, नवन् and दशन् In the declension of अष्टन् the following rules apply.

pk: 372. Kada, to be harsh or severe; to be hard or rough. Pre. kaqati Per. cakaqa i rut. kaqita aorist akaqit Caus. kaqayati Desi. cikaqisati inten. cakaqyate cakaqiti or ‹?› noun:— ‹?› conpound or kas + an The thre rots cuqa, aqa and kaqa have a d as penultinate. Thererore with the aril kvip the rorns would be cut, aw and kat respectively.

s: 372. Kadda, to be harsh or severe; to be hard or rough. s: 375. There is elision of the affix ‹?› when reduced to the single letter ‹?› Note:—The affix ‹?› includes ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› &c. In all these, the real affix is ‹?›, which being an apṛkta (I. 2. 41 S. 251), is elided. Thus ‹?›, ‹?› (III. 2. 87 S. 2998). Here the affix क्विप् is elided. So also घृतस्पृक्, तैलस्पृक् (III. 2. 58 S. 432). Here the affix ‹?› is elided. So also अर्धभाक्, पादभाक्, तुरीभाक् (III. 2. 62 S. 2976). Here the affix ‹?› is elided. Why do we say "of an apṛkta—an affix consisting of a single letter"? Observe ‹?› formed by the affix ‹?› (‹?› being the real affix ‹?›); so also ‹?› formed by ‹?›, see Uṇādi Sûtras IV. 53, 44. No root can become a noun unless some kṛt affix is added to it (see I. 2. 45 and 46); hence the necessity of these imaginary affixes, in order to raise certain roots bodily, without any change, to the rank of nouns—from Dhâtu to a Prâtipadika the way lies only through an affix. And though these imaginary affixes are after all totally elided, yet by I. 1. 62, they leave their characteristic mark behind, namely, the derivative word becomes a nominal stem &c. Thus ‹?› words are adverbs (Gati) and Indeclinables. The word ‹?› being a ‹?› word gets the designation of Prâtipadika by I. 2. 46 S. 179 and therefore we add to it the case affixes ‹?› &c. Thus ‹?› + ‹?› At this stage comes the following sûtra for application. N. S.

Thus non. rorns are suyuk or suyug, suyujO, suyuja in the sûtra Vi. 1. 71, s. 376, the rot is elhibited as yuje showing that that rot or the Dhâtupâṭha should be taken which ends in i, vis., the rot yujin the 7th rot or the ruDadi clas. s: 378. A Guttural is substituted for a Palatal, before a jhal letter or at the end of a word. This requires the change of ज् to a guttural i.e. of क class. The कुत्व ordained by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377 is asiddha or not perceived by the present Sûtra, which is antecedent to VIII. 2. 62. S. 377 in the order of enunciation by Pâṇini. In the case of ‹?› and ‹?›, the ‹?› is not changed to a letter of the ‹?› class even when we take words to be formed by the affix ‹?› under Sûtra VIII. 2. 62 S. 377. The reason for this we shall explain under Sûtra VIII. 2. 68. S. 443 in declining the Neuter noun. Thus Nom. forms are सुयुक् or सुयुग्, सुयुजौ, सुयुजः In the Sûtra VII. 1. 71, S. 376, the root is exhibited as युजेः showing that that root of the Dhâtupâṭha should be taken which ends in इ, viz., the root युजिँ the 7th root of the रुधादि class. Therefore it does not apply to the root युज the 10th root of the दिवादि class and is Âtmanepadî. In the latter case, the form will be युक्. Now we take up the declension of खन्. It is derived from खज् ‘to move' and 'to feel done up' by adding the affix ‹?› The ‹?› of ‹?› is elided because it is ‹?›, leaving behind ‹?› to which the augment ‹?› is added by VII. 1. 58. S. 2262. Thus we get ‹?›. Then ‹?› is elided by VIII. 2. 23 S. 54. In the N. S. the affix सु is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. Thus the N. S. remains as खन्. The N. Dual and Pl. are खञ्जौ and खञ्जः &c. Now we take up the declension of राज्. By VIII. 2. 36. S. 294, the ज् of राज् is changed to ष. Then the ष is changed to ड by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84, and VIII. 4. 56. S. 206. Then ड is changed to ट. Thus we get N. S. राट् or राड्. The N. D. and Pl. are राजौ, राजः Loc. Pl. is राट्सु or राड्सु. Similarly is declined विभ्राज्. So also देवेज्. Its Nom. forms are देवेद् or देवेड्, देवेजौ, देवेजः The Nom. forms of विश्वसृज् are विश्वसृद् or विश्वसृड्, विश्वसृजौ, विश्वसृजः With regard to ‹?› and ‹?› there is not gutturalisation as will be further explained under Sûtra VIII. 2. 68. S. 443. The N. S. of परिमृज् is परिमृट् The word विभ्राज् given above is formed from that root which belongs to फणादि subdivision of भ्वादि gaṇa, i.e. the root डुभ्राज् 'to shine' भ्वादि 875, and not the root भ्राज् number 20 of the भ्वादि where it is exhibited भ्राजृ दीप्तौ. This we do, because the root भ्राज् is read along with root राज् in the subdivision; and as the VIII. 2. 36. S. 294. mentions भ्राज् and राज् together, the भ्राज् here should be taken as the भ्राज् of the फणादि class, where also both are enunciated together and not the other which is shown along with ‹?› and ‹?› (Dhâtupâṭha I. 193, 194 and 195). In the case of this भ्राज् there will be कुत्व and not षत्व. Thus N. S. is विभ्राक् or विभ्राग्. Instr. D. विभ्राग्भ्याम् &c. Vârtika:—When व्रज् is preceded by upapada परि there comes the affix क्विप् and the ‹?› is lengthened and ज् is changed to ष when it is final in a Pada. Thus N. S. of परिव्राज् is परिव्राट् which means one who has gone out leaving every thing. The N. Dual and Pl are परिव्राजौ and परित्राजः respectively.

pk: now, we take up the declension or visvaraj. in its declension, the rolowing rule aplies :- 379. The rinal vowel or visva is lengthened berore vasu and raw (the rorn asuned by raj). Thus visvavasu, i.e. one whose wealth is the whole universe. The rule aplies to the raw rorn or raj in the noninative singular, and not when it retains its own rorn as visvarajO, visvaraja The raw is taken in the sûtra only as an ilustration or its Padânta rorn. it does not nean that the rorn visvaraq is not valid. Thus n. s. has both rorns, i.e. visvaraw and visvaraq.
ck: not, te take up the teclension or visvarac. in its teclension, the rolotink rule aplies :- 379. the rinal votel or visva is lenkthenet perore vasu ant rat (the rorn asunet py rac). thus visvavasu, i.e. one those tealth is the thole universe. the rule aplies to the rat rorn or rac in the noninative sinkular, ant not then it retains its otn rorn as visvaracO, visvaraca the rat is taken in the sûtra only as an ilustration or its patânta rorn. it toes not nean that the rorn visvarat is not valit. thus n. s. has poth rorns, i.e. visvarat ant visvarat.
s: Now, we take up the declension of विश्वराज्. In its declension, the following rule applies :-- 379. The final vowel of विश्व is lengthened before वसु and राट् (the form assumed by राज्). Thus विश्वावसुः, i.e. one whose wealth is the whole universe. The rule applies to the राट् form of राज् in the Nominative singular, and not when it retains its own form as विश्वराजौ, विश्वराजः The राट् is taken in the Sûtra only as an illustration of its Padânta form. It does not mean that the form विश्वाराड् is not valid. Thus N. S. has both forms, i.e. विश्वाराट् and विश्वाराड्.

s: Then the rule after the following applies, to understand which the following rule is necessary. 383. The substitutions taught hereafter upto VII. 2. 98 take effect with regard to the portions of युष्मद् and अस्मद् upto म् ie the substitutes replace युष्म and अस्म This is an Adhikâra Sûtra and exerts governing influence on all the seven subsequent sûtras in the order of Ashțâdhyâyî.

pk: 385. in the renaining cases where (a or ya is not substituted by Vi. 2. 8. and 89. s. 387, 392.) there is elision or the rinal or yushnad and asnad. Thus yusnad + su = yusnad + an (Vi. 1. 28. s. 342) = tvad (Vi. 2. 94. s. 384) + an = tva + an (d is elided by the present sûtra) = tvan (by Vi. 1. 97. s. 191, and Vi. 1. 107. s. 194). sinilarly, the n. s. or asnad is ahan Why is not wap aded in the reninine in tvan stri ahan stri? ror tva + an and aha + an the pûrvarûpa rule ordained by Vi. 1. 97. s. 191 and Vi. 1. 107. s. 194, though subsequent, is arter al bahiranga, and would be set aside by the antaranga rule ordaining wap to be aded to tva and aha? True. But yusnad and asnad have no genders, and thererore they have no reninine rorns and consequently would not give ocasion to the adition or the aril wap. Or, in order to avoid al this diriculty about wap, sone would elide the ad (or renaining portion) or yusnad and asnad under this sûtra. They argue that by the previous sûtra Vi. 2. 91. s. 383 the portions yushn and asn, nanely the portions upto na or yusnad and asnad are replaced by substitutes. The portion that renains (sesa) is ad, and it is this ad which is to be elided. acording to their view, the word sesa does not rerer to the vibhakti or case aril, but the rorce or Locative in sese is that or a genitive, neaning “or the renaining” and to point out the particular sthânî which is to be replaced. Thererore in yusnad and asnad, the yusn and as portions have ben already operated upon by other rules, the d that renains is a portion. in this view, the sûtra should be translated as "in the renaining cases (i. e. where a is not substituted as by Vi. 2. 8. s. 387, nor ya as by Vi. 2. 89. s. 392) there is elision or the renaining (ad) portion (i. 1. 64. s. 79) or these two (yusnad and asnad)". in the reninine, there is one nore point to be considered even in the light or the second elplanation. in yusnad + an = tva + ad + an ir we rolow the ordinary rule or ‹?› the ad should be elided rirst by sese lopa; then should aply the rule or ato gune ir at al. Then the rorn wil be tva + an ere tva ends with a, and so would require wap in the reninine, and the sane diriculty again recurs. To clear up this point, we state that the rule or elision (sese lopa) is bahiranga, because its ericient cause lies outside in the aril an, while the ato gune rule is antaranga, because the ocasion ror its aplication or the ericient cause is within the very rorn tva + ad. Thererore
ck: 385. in the renainink cases there (a or ya is not supstitutet py Vi. 2. 8. ant 89. s. 387, 392.) there is elision or the rinal or yushnat ant asnat. thus yusnat + su = yusnat + an (Vi. 1. 28. s. 342) = tvat (Vi. 2. 94. s. 384) + an = tva + an (t is elitet py the present sûtra) = tvan (py Vi. 1. 97. s. 191, ant Vi. 1. 107. s. 194). sinilarly, the n. s. or asnat is ahan thy is not tap atet in the reninine in tvan stri ahan stri? ror tva + an ant aha + an the pûrvarûpa rule ortainet py Vi. 1. 97. s. 191 ant Vi. 1. 107. s. 194, thoukh supsetuent, is arter al pahiranka, ant toult pe set asite py the antaranka rule ortainink tap to pe atet to tva ant aha? true. put yusnat ant asnat have no kenters, ant thererore they have no reninine rorns ant consetuently toult not kive ocasion to the atition or the aril tap. Or, in orter to avoit al this tiriculty apout tap, sone toult elite the at (or renainink portion) or yusnat ant asnat unter this sûtra. they arkue that py the previous sûtra Vi. 2. 91. s. 383 the portions yushn ant asn, nanely the portions upto na or yusnat ant asnat are replacet py supstitutes. the portion that renains (sesa) is at, ant it is this at thich is to pe elitet. acortink to their viet, the tort sesa toes not rerer to the viphakti or case aril, put the rorce or Locative in sese is that or a kenitive, neanink “or the renainink” ant to point out the particular sthânî thich is to pe replacet. thererore in yusnat ant asnat, the yusn ant as portions have pen alreaty operatet upon py other rules, the t that renains is a portion. in this viet, the sûtra shoult pe translatet as "in the renainink cases (i. e. there a is not supstitutet as py Vi. 2. 8. s. 387, nor ya as py Vi. 2. 89. s. 392) there is elision or the renainink (at) portion (i. 1. 64. s. 79) or these to (yusnat ant asnat)". in the reninine, there is one nore point to pe consiteret even in the likht or the secont elplanation. in yusnat + an = tva + at + an ir te rolot the ortinary rule or ‹?› the at shoult pe elitet rirst py sese lopa; then shoult aply the rule or ato kune ir at al. then the rorn til pe tva + an ere tva ents tith a, ant so toult retuire tap in the reninine, ant the sane tiriculty akain recurs. to clear up this point, te state that the rule or elision (sese lopa) is pahiranka, pecause its ericient cause lies outsite in the aril an, thile the ato kune rule is antaranka, pecause the ocasion ror its aplication or the ericient cause is tithin the very rorn tva + at. thererore ato
s: 385. In the remaining cases where (आ or य is not substituted by VII. 2. 88. and 89. S. 387, 392.) there is elision of the final of yushmad and asmad. Thus युष्मद् + सु = युष्मद् + अम् (VII. 1. 28. S. 342) = त्वद् (VII. 2. 94. S. 384) + अम् = त्व + अम् (द् is elided by the present sûtra) = त्वम् (by VI. 1. 97. S. 191, and VI. 1. 107. S. 194). Similarly, the N. S. of अस्मद् is अहम् Why is not टाप् added in the feminine in 'त्वं स्त्री' 'अहं स्त्री'? For त्व + अम् and अह + अम् the pûrvarûpa rule ordained by VI. 1. 97. S. 191 and VI. 1. 107. S. 194, though subsequent, is after all bahiranga, and would be set aside by the antaranga rule ordaining टाप् to be added to त्व and अह? True. But युष्मद् and अस्मद् have no genders, and therefore they have no feminine forms and consequently would not give occasion to the addition of the affix टाप्. Or, in order to avoid all this difficulty about टाप्, some would elide the अद् (or remaining portion) of युष्मद् and अस्मद् under this sûtra. They argue that by the previous sûtra VII. 2. 91. S. 383 the portions 'yushm' and 'asm', namely the portions upto म of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are replaced by substitutes. The portion that remains (शेष) is अद्, and it is this अद् which is to be elided. According to their view, the word शेष does not refer to the vibhakti or case affix, but the force of Locative in शेषे is that of a genitive, meaning “of the remaining” and to point out the particular sthânî which is to be replaced. Therefore in युष्मद् and अस्मद्, the युष्म् and अस् portions have been already operated upon by other rules, the द् that remains is a portion. In this view, the Sûtra should be translated as "in the remaining cases (i. e. where आ is not substituted as by VII. 2. 88. S. 387, nor य as by VII. 2. 89. S. 392) there is elision of the remaining (अद्) portion (I. 1. 64. S. 79) of these two (युष्मद् and अस्मद्)". In the feminine, there is one more point to be considered even in the light of the second explanation. In युष्मद् + अम् = त्व + अद् + अम् if we follow the ordinary rule of ‹?› the अद् should be elided first by शेषे लोपः; then should apply the rule of अतो गुणे if at all. Then the form will be त्व + अम् Here त्व ends with अ, and so would require टाप् in the feminine, and the same difficulty again recurs. To clear up this point, we state that the rule of elision (शेषे लोपः) is bahiranga, because its efficient cause lies outside in the affix अम्, while the अतो गुणे rule is antaranga, because the occasion for its application or the efficient cause is within the very form त्व + अद्. Therefore अतो गुणे will apply first, we get त्वद् + अम्. Then शेषे लोपः produces its effect i. e. अद् is elided, and we get त्व् + अम् As there is no अ in त्व्, it would not require टाप् Thus we get त्वम् in the feminine also. So also परमत्वम्, परमाहम्, अतित्वम् and अत्यहम्. In forming the N. Dual, the following rules apply.

pk: 386. yuva is substituted ror yusn and ava ror asn, when the bases thenselves denote duality.
ck: 386. yuva is supstitutet ror yusn ant ava ror asn, then the pases thenselves tenote tuality.
s: 386. युव is substituted for युष्म् and आव for अस्म्, when the bases themselves denote duality.

pk: 387. a is substituted ror the rinal or yusnad and asnad berore the ending or the non. Du. in the spoken language. as yuvan, avan it would have ben beter had the sûtra ben enunciated as “Oni” only. Why in the “spoken language”? Observe yuvan vastrani pivasa vasaTe in the Veda, so also avan Why upto na? Observe yuvakan, avakan The ka (V. 3. 71. s. 2026), is not replaced. sinilarly Vi. 2. 97. s. 389 teaches that tva and na replace yushnad and asnad in the singular; by the sûtra Vi. 2. 91. s. 383 yushn and asn are only replaced. Thus tvaya, naya the ad portion renains ror which ya is substituted by Vi. 2. 89. s. 392. ad the whole ben replaced, then the a or tva and na would have ben replaced by ya (Vi. 2. 89. s. 392), and given us undesired rorns like tya and nya sinilarly the rorns yuvakaByan and avakaByan would not have ben evolved. in rorning the n. Pl. the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 387. a is supstitutet ror the rinal or yusnat ant asnat perore the entink or the non. tu. in the spoken lankuake. as yuvan, avan it toult have pen peter hat the sûtra pen enunciatet as “Oni” only. thy in the “spoken lankuake”? Opserve yuvan vastrani pivasa vasate in the Veta, so also avan thy upto na? Opserve yuvakan, avakan the ka (V. 3. 71. s. 2026), is not replacet. sinilarly Vi. 2. 97. s. 389 teaches that tva ant na replace yushnat ant asnat in the sinkular; py the sûtra Vi. 2. 91. s. 383 yushn ant asn are only replacet. thus tvaya, naya the at portion renains ror thich ya is supstitutet py Vi. 2. 89. s. 392. at the thole pen replacet, then the a or tva ant na toult have pen replacet py ya (Vi. 2. 89. s. 392), ant kiven us untesiret rorns like tya ant nya sinilarly the rorns yuvakapyan ant avakapyan toult not have pen evolvet. in rornink the n. pl. the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 387. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before the ending of the Nom. Du. in the spoken language. As युवाम्, आवाम् It would have been better had the Sûtra been enunciated as “औङि” only. Why in the “spoken language”? Observe युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे in the Veda, so also आवाम् Why 'upto म'? Observe युवकाम्, आवकाम् The क (V. 3. 71. S. 2026), is not replaced. Similarly VII. 2. 97. S. 389 teaches that त्व and म replace 'yushmad' and 'asmad' in the singular; by the sûtra VII. 2. 91. S. 383 'yushm' and 'asm' are only replaced. Thus त्वया, मया the अद् portion remains for which य is substituted by VII. 2. 89. S. 392. Had the whole been replaced, then the अ of त्व and म would have been replaced by य (VII. 2. 89. S. 392), and given us undesired forms like त्या and म्या Similarly the forms युवकाभ्याम् and आवकाभ्याम् would not have been evolved. In forming the N. Pl. the following rule applies.

s: 392. ✓ Kepri, 393. ✓ Gepri, 394. ✓ Glepri, to tremble, and to move. By the force of च, both the senses of trembling and moving are taken. This is done by yoga-vibhāga according to Swāmī. According to Maitreya, the sense of trembling would be understood by context even without च. His meaning is that these roots could well have been read with चेप, but they are not done, because traditionally they are read separately. The ✓ Glep is repeated because it has a different meaning here. Pre. केपते Per. चिकेपे I Fut. केपिता Bene. केपिषीष्ट Aorist अकेपिष्ट Caus. केपयति (I. 3. 87 S. 2753). Desi. चिकेपिषते Inten. चेकेप्यते

pk: 393. a is substituted ror the rinal or yusnad and asnad berore a case-ending, begining with a consonant, when it is not a substitute. The substitute case-endings are given in Vi. 1. 27-3. s. 39 &c. Thus yuvaByan, avaByan, yusnaBi, asnaBi
ck: 393. a is supstitutet ror the rinal or yusnat ant asnat perore a case-entink, pekinink tith a consonant, then it is not a supstitute. the supstitute case-entinks are kiven in Vi. 1. 27-3. s. 39 &c. thus yuvapyan, avapyan, yusnapi, asnapi
s: 393. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before a case-ending, beginning with a consonant, when it is not a substitute. The substitute case-endings are given in VII. 1. 27-33. S. 399 &c. Thus युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम्, युष्माभिः, अस्माभिः

pk: 394. in the Dative singular tuBya is substituted ror yusna and nahya ror asna The aril an is substituted ror ne by Vi. 1. 28. s. 382 the tu is elided by Vi. 2. 90. s. 385. Thus tuByan, nahyan, paranatuByan, parananahyan, atituByan, atinahyan, yuvaByan, avaByan
ck: 394. in the tative sinkular tupya is supstitutet ror yusna ant nahya ror asna the aril an is supstitutet ror ne py Vi. 1. 28. s. 382 the tu is elitet py Vi. 2. 90. s. 385. thus tupyan, nahyan, paranatupyan, parananahyan, atitupyan, atinahyan, yuvapyan, avapyan
s: 394. In the Dative Singular तुभ्य is substituted for युष्म and मह्य for अस्म The affix अम् is substituted for ङे by VII. 1. 28. S. 382 the तू is elided by VII. 2. 90. S. 385. Thus तुभ्यम्, मह्यम्, परमतुभ्यम्, परममह्यम्, अतितुभ्यम्, अतिमह्यम्, युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम्

pk:
404. ror the Genitive, Dative and acusative Dual or yushnad and asnad are substituted van and nO respectively, when a word precedes it and ir it does not stand at the begining or a rot or a verse, and these substitutes are anudâta.

al the thre sûtras padasya, padat and anudatan sarvanapadadO are aplicable here.

ote:—These two van and nO cone in the Dual only, because other substitutes have ben taught ror the singular and Plural in the two subsequent sûtras.
ck:
404. ror the kenitive, tative ant acusative tual or yushnat ant asnat are supstitutet van ant nO respectively, then a tort precetes it ant ir it toes not stant at the pekinink or a rot or a verse, ant these supstitutes are anutâta.

al the thre sûtras patasya, patat ant anutatan sarvanapatatO are aplicaple here.

ote:—these to van ant nO cone in the tual only, pecause other supstitutes have pen taukht ror the sinkular ant plural in the to supsetuent sûtras.
s:
404. For the Genitive, Dative and Accusative Dual of yushmad and asmad are substituted वाम् and नौ respectively, when a word precedes it and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta.

All the three sûtras पदस्य, पदात् and अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ are applicable here.

Note:—These two वाम् and नौ come in the Dual only, because other substitutes have been taught for the Singular and Plural in the two subsequent sûtras.

pk: 405. ror (the Genitive, Dative, and acusative) plural or yushnad and asnad are substituted vas and nas respectively, (when a word precedes, and ir it does not stand at the begining or a rot or a verse, and these substitutes are anudâta).\n\nThis sûtra debars the substitutes van and nO taught in the previous sûtra.
ck: 405. ror (the kenitive, tative, ant acusative) plural or yushnat ant asnat are supstitutet vas ant nas respectively, (then a tort precetes, ant ir it toes not stant at the pekinink or a rot or a verse, ant these supstitutes are anutâta).\n\nthis sûtra tepars the supstitutes van ant nO taukht in the previous sûtra.
s: 405. For (the Genitive, Dative, and Accusative) plural of yushmad and asmad are substituted वस् and नस् respectively, (when a word precedes, and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta).\n\nThis Sûtra debars the substitutes वाम् and नौ taught in the previous Sûtra.

pk: 406. ror the Genitive and Dative singular (or yushnad and asnad are substituted) te and ne respectively, (when a word precedes and ir it does not stand at the begining or a rot or a verse and these are anudâta).
ck: 406. ror the kenitive ant tative sinkular (or yushnat ant asnat are supstitutet) te ant ne respectively, (then a tort precetes ant ir it toes not stant at the pekinink or a rot or a verse ant these are anutâta).
s: 406. For the Genitive and Dative Singular (of yushmad and asmad are substituted) ते and मे respectively, (when a word precedes and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse and these are anudâtta).
