pk: 409. The above substitutions do not take place also in conection with verbs having the sense or "seing" when physical seing is not denoted, but "knowing" is neant.\n\note:—The word pasyarTa is equivalent to darsanarTa, and darsana neans knowledge, i. e. verbs denoting to know. alocana neans perception obtained through sight i. e. physical seing oposed to netaphorical "seing" or "knowing". The substitutions or tva and na &c. ror yusnad and asnad do not take place when these pronouns are enployed in conection with verbs denoting seing (netaphoricaly) but not loking (physicaly). Thus taTa tvan saniksate Baktastava rupan Dyayati Why do we say when not neaning to lok? Observe Baktastva pasyati caksusa ishti :—With regard to verbs or "seing" the rule should aply even where the conection is not direct : as, Baktastava rupan Dyayati
ck: 409. the apove supstitutions to not take place also in conection tith verps havink the sense or "seink" then physical seink is not tenotet, put "knotink" is neant.\n\note:—the tort pasyarta is etuivalent to tarsanarta, ant tarsana neans knotletke, i. e. verps tenotink to knot. alocana neans perception optainet throukh sikht i. e. physical seink oposet to netaphorical "seink" or "knotink". the supstitutions or tva ant na &c. ror yusnat ant asnat to not take place then these pronouns are enployet in conection tith verps tenotink seink (netaphoricaly) put not lokink (physicaly). thus tata tvan saniksate paktastava rupan tyayati thy to te say then not neanink to lok? Opserve paktastva pasyati caksusa ishti :—tith rekart to verps or "seink" the rule shoult aply even there the conection is not tirect : as, paktastava rupan tyayati
s: 409. The above substitutions do not take place also in connection with verbs having the sense of "seeing" when physical seeing is not denoted, but "knowing" is meant.\n\nNote:—The word पश्यार्थाः is equivalent to दर्शनार्थाः, and दर्शन means 'knowledge', i. e. verbs denoting 'to know'. आलोचन means perception obtained through sight i. e. physical 'seeing' opposed to metaphorical "seeing" or "knowing". The substitutions of त्वा and मा &c. for युष्मद् and अस्मद् do not take place when these pronouns are employed in connection with verbs denoting 'seeing' (metaphorically) but not 'looking' (physically). Thus तथा त्वां समीक्षते भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति Why do we say when not meaning 'to look'? Observe भक्तस्त्वा पश्यति चक्षुषा Ishti :—With regard to verbs of "Seeing" the rule should apply even where the connection is not direct : as, भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति

pk: 410. When the pronoun rolows arter a noninative which itselr is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions nay take place optionaly even in anvâdesa. Thus Baktastvanapyahan tena haristvan trayate sa nan ere the alternative rorns tva and na are adnisible. We have already said that yusnad and asnad substitutions do not take place when they are in the begining or a pada. To this, however, there is an elception, when the rirst word is a Vocative, technicaly caled anantrita which is derined in the nelt sutra, then also though yusnad and asnad nay not realy be in the begining or a pada, yet the substitutions wil not take place by the sûtra arter nelt.
ck: 410. then the pronoun rolots arter a noninative thich itselr is precetet py another tort, then the apove supstitutions nay take place optionaly even in anvâtesa. thus paktastvanapyahan tena haristvan trayate sa nan ere the alternative rorns tva ant na are atnisiple. te have alreaty sait that yusnat ant asnat supstitutions to not take place then they are in the pekinink or a pata. to this, hotever, there is an elception, then the rirst tort is a Vocative, technicaly calet anantrita thich is terinet in the nelt sutra, then also thoukh yusnat ant asnat nay not realy pe in the pekinink or a pata, yet the supstitutions til not take place py the sûtra arter nelt.
s: 410. When the pronoun follows after a Nominative which itself is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions may take place optionally even in anvâdesa. Thus भक्तस्त्वमप्यहं तेन हरिस्त्वां त्रायते स माम् Here the alternative forms त्वा and मा are admissible. We have already said that युष्मद् and अस्मद् substitutions do not take place when they are in the beginning of a pada. To this, however, there is an exception, when the first word is a Vocative, technically called आमन्त्रित which is defined in the next sutra, then also though युष्मद् and अस्मद् may not really be in the beginning of a pada, yet the substitutions will not take place by the sûtra after next.

pk: 412. a preceding Vocative is considered as non-elistent, (ror the purposes or the acent or the rolowing word, and the enclitic rorns or yusnad and asnad) Thus agne ! tava deva ! asnanpahi agne ! naya agne ! indra ! varuna ! ere tava and asnan canot get the shorter rorn, though they are not at the begining or a henistich, because they are preceded by the anantrita words agne and deva sinilarly in agne naya the verb naya does not becone acentles as it would otherwise have becone by Vi. 1. 28. s. 3935. in agne ! indra ! varuna ! the rule Vi. 1. 19 s. 3654 does not aply. note:—such a Vocative is treated as ir not at al elisting, it is sinply ignored. The operation which its presence otherwise would have caused does not take place, and that operation takes place which would have taken place had it not elisted. What are the particular purposes served by considering it as non-elistent? They are (1) the absence or the acent-les-nes or the subsequent Vocative which the rirst, taken as a pada, would have caused under Vi. 1. 19. s. 3654. as devadata ! yajnadata ! ere the rirst Vocative devadata does not cause the second Vocative to lose its acent, but it renains rirst acute by Vi. 1. 198. s. 3653. (2) The acent-les-nes or the verb required by Vi. 1. 28 s. 3935 is prevented : as, devadata pacasi (3) The substitution or the shorter rorns or yusnad and asnad, required by Vi. 1. 20-28 s. 404 &c. is prevented, as devadata tava (not te) grana svan, devadata nana (not ne) grana (4) The aplication or Vi. 1. 37. s. 394 takes place, in spite or the intervention or the Vocative betwen the Particle and the verb; such intervention is not considered as taking away anything ron the inediatenes (vyavaDana) or the Particle ron the verb : as, aho devadata pacasi (5) ror the purposes or Vi. 1. 47, s. 3954 though a Vocative nay precede, the later is stil considered as non-elistent and Vi. 1. 47 aplies, as devadata jatu pacasi (6) so also in the case or Vi. 1. 49, s. 3956 as aho devadata pacasi, aho devadata jalpasi, no option is alowed here by Vi. 1. 50. s. 3957. in sarvada raksa deva na although the word deva is non-elistent, yet taking raksa as a preceding word, na is used. in inan ne gange yanune sarasvati sutudri the rirst Vocative gange is considered as non-elistent with regard to ne, and, thererore, yanune is considered as rolowing inediately arter the pada ne and thus yanune becones anudâta, not because or gange, but because or ne. in other words, the intervention or the
ck: 412. a precetink Vocative is consiteret as non-elistent, (ror the purposes or the acent or the rolotink tort, ant the enclitic rorns or yusnat ant asnat) thus akne ! tava teva ! asnanpahi akne ! naya akne ! intra ! varuna ! ere tava ant asnan canot ket the shorter rorn, thoukh they are not at the pekinink or a henistich, pecause they are precetet py the anantrita torts akne ant teva sinilarly in akne naya the verp naya toes not pecone acentles as it toult othertise have pecone py Vi. 1. 28. s. 3935. in akne ! intra ! varuna ! the rule Vi. 1. 19 s. 3654 toes not aply. note:—such a Vocative is treatet as ir not at al elistink, it is sinply iknoret. the operation thich its presence othertise toult have causet toes not take place, ant that operation takes place thich toult have taken place hat it not elistet. that are the particular purposes servet py consiterink it as non-elistent? they are (1) the apsence or the acent-les-nes or the supsetuent Vocative thich the rirst, taken as a pata, toult have causet unter Vi. 1. 19. s. 3654. as tevatata ! yacnatata ! ere the rirst Vocative tevatata toes not cause the secont Vocative to lose its acent, put it renains rirst acute py Vi. 1. 198. s. 3653. (2) the acent-les-nes or the verp retuiret py Vi. 1. 28 s. 3935 is preventet : as, tevatata pacasi (3) the supstitution or the shorter rorns or yusnat ant asnat, retuiret py Vi. 1. 20-28 s. 404 &c. is preventet, as tevatata tava (not te) krana svan, tevatata nana (not ne) krana (4) the aplication or Vi. 1. 37. s. 394 takes place, in spite or the intervention or the Vocative peten the particle ant the verp; such intervention is not consiteret as takink atay anythink ron the inetiatenes (vyavatana) or the particle ron the verp : as, aho tevatata pacasi (5) ror the purposes or Vi. 1. 47, s. 3954 thoukh a Vocative nay precete, the later is stil consiteret as non-elistent ant Vi. 1. 47 aplies, as tevatata catu pacasi (6) so also in the case or Vi. 1. 49, s. 3956 as aho tevatata pacasi, aho tevatata calpasi, no option is alotet here py Vi. 1. 50. s. 3957. in sarvata raksa teva na althoukh the tort teva is non-elistent, yet takink raksa as a precetink tort, na is uset. in inan ne kanke yanune sarasvati sututri the rirst Vocative kanke is consiteret as non-elistent tith rekart to ne, ant, thererore, yanune is consiteret as rolotink inetiately arter the pata ne ant thus yanune pecones anutâta, not pecause or kanke, put pecause or ne. in other torts, the intervention or the Vocatives
s: 412. A preceding Vocative is considered as non-existent, (for the purposes of the accent of the following word, and the enclitic forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्) Thus अग्ने ! तव देव ! अस्मान्पाहि अग्ने ! नय अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! Here तव and अस्मान् cannot get the shorter form, though they are not at the beginning of a hemistich, because they are preceded by the आमन्त्रित words अग्ने and देव Similarly in अग्ने नय the verb नय does not become accentless as it would otherwise have become by VIII. 1. 28. S. 3935. In अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! the rule VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654 does not apply. Note:—Such a Vocative is treated as if not at all existing, it is simply ignored. The operation which its presence otherwise would have caused does not take place, and that operation takes place which would have taken place had it not existed. What are the particular purposes served by considering it as non-existent? They are (1) the absence of the accent-less-ness of the subsequent Vocative which the first, taken as a पद, would have caused under VIII. 1. 19. S. 3654. As देवदत्त ! यज्ञदत्त ! Here the first Vocative देवदत्त does not cause the second Vocative to lose its accent, but it remains first acute by VI. 1. 198. S. 3653. (2) The accent-less-ness of the verb required by VIII. 1. 28 S. 3935 is prevented : as, देवदत्त पचसि (3) The substitution of the shorter forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्, required by VIII. 1. 20-28 S. 404 &c. is prevented, as देवदत्त तव (not ते) ग्रामः स्वम्, देवदत्त मम (not मे) ग्रामः (4) The application of VIII. 1. 37. S. 3944 takes place, in spite of the intervention of the Vocative between the Particle and the verb; such intervention is not considered as taking away anything from the immediateness (व्यवधान) of the Particle from the verb : as, अहो देवदत्त पचसि (5) For the purposes of VIII. 1. 47, S. 3954 though a Vocative may precede, the latter is still considered as non-existent and VIII. 1. 47 applies, as देवदत्त जातु पचसि (6) So also in the case of VIII. 1. 49, S. 3956 as अहो देवदत्त पचसि, अहो देवदत्त जल्पसि, no option is allowed here by VIII. 1. 50. S. 3957. In 'सर्वदा रक्ष देव नः' although the word देव is non-existent, yet taking रक्ष as a preceding word, नः is used. In इमं मे गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि the first Vocative गङ्गे is considered as non-existent with regard to मे, and, therefore, यमुने is considered as following immediately after the pada मे and thus यमुने becomes anudâtta, not because of गङ्गे, but because of मे. In other words, the intervention of the Vocatives does not stop the action of मे. This nighâta or accentlessness is heard in Pada-Pâtha only, i. e. when the words are read separately, and not in Sanhitâ-reading. In Sanhitâ there will be eka-sruti of I. 2. 39 S. 3668.

pk: 413. a preceding Vocative, when it conveys a general idea, is not to be considered as ir non-elistent, ror the purposes or the subsequent Vocative, which stands in aposition with the rorner. Thus hare dayalo na pahi "O ari ! O nercirul! protect us." agne tejasvin "O agni! O powerul!" ere dayalo is al anudâta by Vi. 1. 19 s. 3654, because it is preceded by a word, though that word is Vocative. note:—Why do we say sananyavacanan which is a generic word? The rule wil not aply when the Vocatives are synonyns. Thus ‹?› al these Vocatives are synonyns or saraswati, and hence al retain their acent or the Vocative (Vi. 1. 198). acording to Padananjari the reading given in Taitirîya Br. is :— ‹?› sananyavacanan neans a generic tern. When the rirst is a generic tern, and the second is a speciric tern, (visesavacana) qualirying the rirst, and both are in the singular nunber, there the present rule wil aply. This sutra prevents the operation or the last sûtra in the particular case when the two Vocatives are in aposition, and the second qualiries the rirst. Thus agne grhapate, nanavaka jawilakaDyapaka The rirst vocative being considered as elisting, the second vocative loses its acent. Why do we say the vocative subsequent? Observe devadata pacasi here the verb does not lose its acent. Why do we say standing in aposition or sananaDikaranye? Observe devadata panqita yajnadata, here the word panqita qualiries yajnadata, and is not in aposition with devadata, and hence it retains its acent. Then aplies sûtra Vi. 1. 74. s. 365 which ror the sake or convenience we repeat here. 413 (ka) viBasitan visesavacane 8 1 74 atra Basyan bahuvacananiti vaksyaniti bahuvacanantan visesyan sananaDikarane anantrite visesane pare avidyananavadva yuyan praBava deva saranya yusnan Baje vo Baje iti va ihanvadesepi vEkalpika adesa supat supada supadO supada supadan supadO 413. a. When the preceding Vocative is in the plural nunber, it is optionaly considered as non-elistent, ir the subsequent Vocative, in aposition with it, is a speciric tern. ere the author or the nahabhashya states :— "The word bahuvachanan should be aded to the sûtra to conplete the sense." That is the sûtra should run as viBasitan visesavacane bahuvacanan We have thererore translated the sûtra with this enendation or Patanjali. Thus yuyan praBava, deva saranya yusnan Baje or vo Baje ere even in anvâdesa there is optional substitution or va ror yusnan now, we take up the declension or supad. in the strong, i. e. in the
ck: 413. a precetink Vocative, then it conveys a keneral itea, is not to pe consiteret as ir non-elistent, ror the purposes or the supsetuent Vocative, thich stants in aposition tith the rorner. thus hare tayalo na pahi "O ari ! O nercirul! protect us." akne tecasvin "O akni! O poterul!" ere tayalo is al anutâta py Vi. 1. 19 s. 3654, pecause it is precetet py a tort, thoukh that tort is Vocative. note:—thy to te say sananyavacanan thich is a keneric tort? the rule til not aply then the Vocatives are synonyns. thus ‹?› al these Vocatives are synonyns or sarastati, ant hence al retain their acent or the Vocative (Vi. 1. 198). acortink to patanancari the reatink kiven in taitirîya pr. is :— ‹?› sananyavacanan neans a keneric tern. then the rirst is a keneric tern, ant the secont is a speciric tern, (visesavacana) tualiryink the rirst, ant poth are in the sinkular nunper, there the present rule til aply. this sutra prevents the operation or the last sûtra in the particular case then the to Vocatives are in aposition, ant the secont tualiries the rirst. thus akne krhapate, nanavaka catilakatyapaka the rirst vocative peink consiteret as elistink, the secont vocative loses its acent. thy to te say the vocative supsetuent? Opserve tevatata pacasi here the verp toes not lose its acent. thy to te say stantink in aposition or sananatikaranye? Opserve tevatata pantita yacnatata, here the tort pantita tualiries yacnatata, ant is not in aposition tith tevatata, ant hence it retains its acent. then aplies sûtra Vi. 1. 74. s. 365 thich ror the sake or convenience te repeat here. 413 (ka) vipasitan visesavacane 8 1 74 atra pasyan pahuvacananiti vaksyaniti pahuvacanantan visesyan sananatikarane anantrite visesane pare avityananavatva yuyan prapava teva saranya yusnan pace vo pace iti va ihanvatesepi vEkalpika atesa supat supata supatO supata supatan supatO 413. a. then the precetink Vocative is in the plural nunper, it is optionaly consiteret as non-elistent, ir the supsetuent Vocative, in aposition tith it, is a speciric tern. ere the author or the nahaphashya states :— "the tort pahuvachanan shoult pe atet to the sûtra to conplete the sense." that is the sûtra shoult run as vipasitan visesavacane pahuvacanan te have thererore translatet the sûtra tith this enentation or patancali. thus yuyan prapava, teva saranya yusnan pace or vo pace ere even in anvâtesa there is optional supstitution or va ror yusnan not, te take up the teclension or supat. in the stronk, i. e. in the rirs
s: 413. A preceding Vocative, when it conveys a general idea, is not to be considered as if non-existent, for the purposes of the subsequent Vocative, which stands in apposition with the former. Thus हरे दयालो नः पाहि "O Hari ! O Merciful! protect us." अग्ने तेजस्विन् "O Agni! O powerful!" Here दयालो is all anudâtta by VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654, because it is preceded by a word, though that word is Vocative. Note:—Why do we say सामान्यवचनम् 'which is a generic word'? The rule will not apply when the Vocatives are synonyms. Thus ‹?› All these Vocatives are synonyms of Saraswati, and hence all retain their accent of the Vocative (VI. 1. 198). According to Padamanjari the reading given in Taittirîya Br. is :— ‹?› सामान्यवचनम् means 'a generic term'. When the first is a generic term, and the second is a specific term, (विशेषवचन) qualifying the first, and both are in the singular number, there the present rule will apply. This sutra prevents the operation of the last sûtra in the particular case when the two Vocatives are in apposition, and the second qualifies the first. Thus अग्ने गृहपते, माणवक जटिलकाध्यापक The first vocative being considered as existing, the second vocative loses its accent. Why do we say 'the vocative subsequent'? Observe देवदत्त पचसि here the verb does not lose its accent. Why do we say 'standing in apposition or सामानाधिकरण्ये'? Observe देवदत्त पण्डित यज्ञदत्त, here the word पण्डित qualifies यज्ञदत्त, and is not in apposition with देवदत्त, and hence it retains its accent. Then applies Sûtra VIII. 1. 74. S. 3655 which for the sake of convenience we repeat here. ४१३ (क) विभाषितं विशेषवचने ८ १ ७४ अत्र भाष्यम् बहुवचनमिति वक्ष्यामीति बहुवचनान्तं विशेष्यं समानाधिकरणे आमन्त्रिते विशेषणे परे अविद्यमानवद्वा यूयं प्रभवः देवाः शरण्याः युष्मान् भजे वो भजे इति वा इहान्वादेशेऽपि वैकल्पिका आदेशाः सुपात् सुपाद सुपादौ सुपादः सुपादम् सुपादौ 413. A. When the preceding Vocative is in the plural number, it is optionally considered as non-existent, if the subsequent Vocative, in apposition with it, is a specific term. Here the author of the Mahabhashya states :— "The word bahuvachanam should be added to the sûtra to complete the sense." That is the sûtra should run as विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् We have therefore translated the sûtra with this emendation of Patanjali. Thus यूयं प्रभवः, देवाः शरण्याः युष्मान् भजे or वो भजे Here even in anvâdesa there is optional substitution of वः for युष्मान् Now, we take up the declension of सुपाद्. In the strong, i. e. in the first five cases it is declined as :— Sing. Dual. Pl. Nom : सुपात् or सुपाद, सुपादौ सुपादः Ac. सुपादम्, सुपादौ. In the formation of the Acc. Pl. and the rest, the following rule applies.

pk: 414. ror pad is substituted pad when the rorner is Bha. note:—The substitute replaces the whole rorn pad and not only the rinal, on the nalin nirdisyananasyadesa Bavanti "substitutes take the place or that which is actualy enunciated in a rule." Thus the ac. Pl. is supada instr: sing and Dual are supada, supadByan &c. now we take up the declension or agninaT neaning kindling rire. it is declined as: non. sing. agninat or agninad Dual agninaTO Pl. agninaTa instr: Dual is agninadByan &c. ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in Ta. Declension or nasculine nouns ending in c. now we take up the declension or pranc. acording to sūtra i. 2. 59. s. 373, the aril kvin is enployed arter the verb anc to nake it a Prātipadika, berore the case terninations. Thus having got the noun pranc, in its declension, the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 414. ror pat is supstitutet pat then the rorner is pha. note:—the supstitute replaces the thole rorn pat ant not only the rinal, on the nalin nirtisyananasyatesa pavanti "supstitutes take the place or that thich is actualy enunciatet in a rule." thus the ac. pl. is supata instr: sink ant tual are supata, supatpyan &c. not te take up the teclension or akninat neanink kintlink rire. it is teclinet as: non. sink. akninat or akninat tual akninatO pl. akninata instr: tual is akninatpyan &c. ere ents the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in ta. teclension or nasculine nouns entink in c. not te take up the teclension or pranc. acortink to sūtra i. 2. 59. s. 373, the aril kvin is enployet arter the verp anc to nake it a prātipatika, perore the case terninations. thus havink kot the noun pranc, in its teclension, the rolotink rules aply.
s: 414. For पाद् is substituted पद् when the former is Bha. Note:—The substitute replaces the whole form पाद् and not only the final, on the maxim निर्दिश्यमानस्यादेशा भवन्ति "substitutes take the place of that which is actually enunciated in a rule." Thus the Acc. Pl. is सुपदः Instr: Sing and Dual are सुपदा, सुपाद्भ्याम् &c. Now we take up the declension of अग्निमथ् meaning 'kindling fire'. It is declined as: Nom. Sing. अग्निमत् or अग्निमद् Dual अग्निमथौ Pl. अग्निमथः Instr: Dual is अग्निमद्भ्याम् &c. Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in थ. Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in च्. Now we take up the declension of प्राञ्च्. According to Sūtra III. 2. 59. S. 373, the affix क्विन् is employed after the verb अञ्च् to make it a Prātipadika, before the case terminations. Thus having got the noun प्राञ्च्, in its declension, the following rules apply.

pk: 415. in a rot-sten ending in a consonant preceded by n,—this na not being aded to the rot owing to its having an indicatory i (Vi. 1. 58)—the na is elided when an aril having an indicatory ka or n rolows. By sūtra Vi. 1. 70. s. 361, the sten anc gets the augnent nun in the strong cases. Then by Vi. 2. 23. s. 54, the last consonant is droped. By Vi. 2. 62. s. 37, which says that a sten rorned with the aril kvin substitutes at the end or a word, a gutural ror the rinal consonant we get the n. s. as pran thus:— pranc + su = prac (Vi. 4. 24 s. 415) + su = pra + n (Vi. 1. 70. s. 361) + c + su = pran c + 0 (su is elided by Vi. 1. 68 s. 252) = pran c = pran (c being elided by Vi. 2. 23. s. 54) = pran (n turned to n by Vi. 2. 62. s. 37). The n. Dual &c. are rorned by changing the na into anuswāra, and then the anuswāra into n by Vi. 4. 58. s. 124. Thus prancO pranca ac. prancan, prancO. in rorning the ac. Pl. &c. the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 415. in a rot-sten entink in a consonant precetet py n,—this na not peink atet to the rot otink to its havink an inticatory i (Vi. 1. 58)—the na is elitet then an aril havink an inticatory ka or n rolots. py sūtra Vi. 1. 70. s. 361, the sten anc kets the auknent nun in the stronk cases. then py Vi. 2. 23. s. 54, the last consonant is tropet. py Vi. 2. 62. s. 37, thich says that a sten rornet tith the aril kvin supstitutes at the ent or a tort, a kutural ror the rinal consonant te ket the n. s. as pran thus:— pranc + su = prac (Vi. 4. 24 s. 415) + su = pra + n (Vi. 1. 70. s. 361) + c + su = pran c + 0 (su is elitet py Vi. 1. 68 s. 252) = pran c = pran (c peink elitet py Vi. 2. 23. s. 54) = pran (n turnet to n py Vi. 2. 62. s. 37). the n. tual &c. are rornet py chankink the na into anustāra, ant then the anustāra into n py Vi. 4. 58. s. 124. thus prancO pranca ac. prancan, prancO. in rornink the ac. pl. &c. the rolotink rules aply.
s: 415. In a root-stem ending in a consonant preceded by न्,—this न not being added to the root owing to its having an indicatory इ (VII. 1. 58)—the न is elided when an affix having an indicatory क or ङ् follows. By Sūtra VII. 1. 70. S. 361, the stem अञ्च् gets the augment नुम् in the strong cases. Then by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54, the last consonant is dropped. By VIII. 2. 62. S. 377, which says that 'a stem formed with the affix क्विन् substitutes at the end of a word, a guttural for the final consonant' we get the N. S. as प्राङ् thus:— प्राञ्च् + सु = प्राच् (VI. 4. 24 S. 415) + सु = प्रा + न् (VII. 1. 70. S. 361) + च् + सु = प्रान् च् + ० (सु is elided by VI. 1. 68 S. 252) = प्रान् च् = प्रान् (च् being elided by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54) = प्राङ् (न् turned to ङ् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377). The N. Dual &c. are formed by changing the न into anuswāra, and then the anuswāra into ञ् by VIII. 4. 58. S. 124. Thus प्राञ्चौ प्राञ्चः Acc. प्राञ्चम्, प्राञ्चौ. In forming the Acc. Pl. &c. the following rules apply.

pk: 416. The a or ac (when anc loses its nasal,) is elided at the end or a Bha sten. The lengthening or the rirst nenber takes place by Vi. 3. 138: s. 417.
ck: 416. the a or ac (then anc loses its nasal,) is elitet at the ent or a pha sten. the lenkthenink or the rirst nenper takes place py Vi. 3. 138: s. 417.
s: 416. The अ of अच् (when अञ्च् loses its nasal,) is elided at the end of a Bha stem. The lengthening of the first member takes place by VI. 3. 138: S. 417.

pk: 417. The rinal vowel or the preceding nenber is lengthened berore aca, when it asunes the rorn ca, having lost its nasal and the vowel a Thus ac: Pl is praca; instr: sing or Dual are praca, pragByan &c. now we take up the declension or pratyanc in strong cases, it is declined as pratyan, pratyancO, pratyanca pratyancan, pratyancO, in weak cases, a is elided by Vi. 4. 138 s. 416, and though this lopa is a bahiraṅga proces, while the yaṇ or senivowel sandhi is an antaraṅga proces, yet this lopa is not considered asidha ror the purposes or this sandhi. This proceds on the nalin akrtavyuha &c. se under sūtra i. 3. 1 s. 46. Thus ac: Pl: is pratica, instr: sing is pratica &c. prati + anc + sas = prati + c + as ere two sūtras sinultaneously apear ror aplication, vis. iko yanaci and aca now iko yanaci is antaraṅga, because the ericient cause a or anc is inside that or sas; and the ericient cause sas by which a or anc would be elided is outside; thererore yaṇ ādeśa should take place rirst, thus prati + a + sas = praty + ac + sas arter this a should be elided as praty + c + as This however gives us no rorn, and so relying on the nalin akrtavyuha &c. the antaraṅga yaṇ substitution is set aside. now, we take up the declension or anc as conpounded with the pronoun adas neaning anun ancati Thus we have adas + anc + kvin ere aplies the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 417. the rinal votel or the precetink nenper is lenkthenet perore aca, then it asunes the rorn ca, havink lost its nasal ant the votel a thus ac: pl is praca; instr: sink or tual are praca, prakpyan &c. not te take up the teclension or pratyanc in stronk cases, it is teclinet as pratyan, pratyancO, pratyanca pratyancan, pratyancO, in teak cases, a is elitet py Vi. 4. 138 s. 416, ant thoukh this lopa is a pahiraṅka proces, thile the yaṇ or senivotel santhi is an antaraṅka proces, yet this lopa is not consiteret asitha ror the purposes or this santhi. this procets on the nalin akrtavyuha &c. se unter sūtra i. 3. 1 s. 46. thus ac: pl: is pratica, instr: sink is pratica &c. prati + anc + sas = prati + c + as ere to sūtras sinultaneously apear ror aplication, vis. iko yanaci ant aca not iko yanaci is antaraṅka, pecause the ericient cause a or anc is insite that or sas; ant the ericient cause sas py thich a or anc toult pe elitet is outsite; thererore yaṇ āteśa shoult take place rirst, thus prati + a + sas = praty + ac + sas arter this a shoult pe elitet as praty + c + as this hotever kives us no rorn, ant so relyink on the nalin akrtavyuha &c. the antaraṅka yaṇ supstitution is set asite. not, te take up the teclension or anc as conpountet tith the pronoun atas neanink anun ancati thus te have atas + anc + kvin ere aplies the rolotink sūtra.
s: 417. The final vowel of the preceding member is lengthened before अच, when it assumes the form च, having lost its nasal and the vowel अ Thus Acc: Pl is प्राचः; Instr: Sing or Dual are प्राचा, प्राग्भ्याम् &c. Now we take up the declension of प्रत्यञ्च् In strong cases, it is declined as प्रत्यङ्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, प्रत्यञ्चः प्रत्यञ्चम्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, in weak cases, अ is elided by VI. 4. 138 S. 416, and though this lopa is a bahiraṅga process, while the yaṇ or semivowel Sandhi is an antaraṅga process, yet this lopa is not considered asiddha for the purposes of this sandhi. This proceeds on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. See under Sūtra I. 3. 11 S. 46. Thus Acc: Pl: is प्रतीचः, Instr: Sing is प्रतीचा &c. प्रति + अञ्च् + शस् = प्रति + च् + अस् Here two sūtras simultaneously appear for application, viz. इको यणचि and अचः Now इको यणचि is antaraṅga, because the efficient cause अ of अञ्च् is inside that of शस्; and the efficient cause शस् by which अ of अञ्च् would be elided is outside; therefore yaṇ ādeśa should take place first, thus प्रति + अ + शस् = प्रत्य् + अच् + शस् After this अ should be elided as प्रत्य् + च् + अस् This however gives us no form, and so relying on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. the antaraṅga yaṇ substitution is set aside. Now, we take up the declension of अञ्च् as compounded with the pronoun अदस् meaning अमुम् अञ्चति Thus we have अदस् + अञ्च् + क्विन् Here applies the following sūtra.

pk: 418. in the ron or the last vowel, with the consonant that rolows it, or a Pronoun and or the words visvak and deva, is substituted adri, when anc has no visible aril rolowing it. Thus adas + anc = adadri + anc = adady + anc. at this stage, aplies the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 418. in the ron or the last votel, tith the consonant that rolots it, or a pronoun ant or the torts visvak ant teva, is supstitutet atri, then anc has no visiple aril rolotink it. thus atas + anc = atatri + anc = ataty + anc. at this stake, aplies the rolotink sūtra.
s: 418. In the room of the last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, of a Pronoun and of the words विष्वक् and देव, is substituted अद्रि, when अञ्च् has no visible affix following it. Thus अदस् + अञ्च् = अदद्रि + अञ्च् = अदद्य् + अञ्च्. At this stage, applies the following sūtra.

pk: 419. When the pronoun adas does not end in s, then there is substituted u or u ror the vowel arter d, and n ror d The short u in the sūtra is a sanāhāra dvandva conpound including both the short u and long u. By the rule or antartana i. 1. 50 s. 39, the short vowel and the consonant rolowing it wil be replaced by the short u; and the long vowel with the consonant rolowing it wil be replaced by the long ū. Thus adady + anc = anunudy + anc : the rirst d and a are changed to n and u, and the second d and y are also changed to n and u; so the declension is:— non. sing. anunuyan Dual anunuyancO Pl. anunuyanca ac. sing. anunuyancan Dual anunuyancO Pl. anunuca ins. sing. anunuca Dual anunuyagByan &c. &c. The nutva being considered as asidha, there is no sandhi in in æg, ror the sandhi rule is contained in the silth Bok or Panini, while this g substitute is ordained in the Tripadi portion or ashtadhyayi. ence the sutra Vi. 2. 1. s. 12 aplies. sone, by aplying the rolowing nalin, get the rorn Paribhasha "When a nodirication is ordained with regard to sonething which is not rinal, the operation takes place on that only which is in prolinity to the rinal." The second clas aply this nalin and nake g change only ror which stands in prolinity to the rinal. There is a third rorn, which is obtained by elplaining the ase in the sutra as na seryasya soyanasi, tatra sakarasya nakara kriyate "The word ase in the sutra is a Bahuvrihi, and neans that in which as is substituted ror ‹?›" The sutra is thus conrined to the rorn derived by changing the d into n by Vi. 2. 102. and not to any other. Thus there are thre views with regard to the aplication or the present sutra:— (1) the d or adas, and or adri are both changed to n by the present sutra; (2) the rirst is not changed, but only the second; (3) none is changed. Thus we have (1) anunuyan (Vi. 1. 70, Vi. 1. 68, Vi. 2. 23 and 62), anunuyancO, anunuyanca (2) secondly, adanuyan, adanuyancO, adanuyanca (3) Lastly adriryan, adriyancO, adriyanca The above verse sunarises this: Verse:—sone ordain that n should cone separately ror both adas and adri, as there is double d (in se sutra Vi. 2. 80 and Vi. 4. 90 s. 264); others would have n only ror the last portion which stands in prolinity to the rinal, (i.e. ror adri); while a third clas would have n nowhere, because they elplain ase or the sutra by conrining it to Tyadadi Vi. 2. 102." note:—Thus udan = visvak. This rorn is thus evolved. anc + kvin = anc + 0 = anc + nun (Vi. 1. 70).

s: 419. When the pronoun अदस् does not end in स्, then there is substituted उ or ऊ for the vowel after द्, and म् for द् The short u in the sūtra is a samāhāra dvandva compound including both the short u and long ऊ. By the rule of antartama I. 1. 50 S. 39, the short vowel and the consonant following it will be replaced by the short u; and the long vowel with the consonant following it will be replaced by the long ū. Thus अदद्य् + अञ्च् = अमुमुद्य् + अञ्च् : the first द् and अ are changed to म् and उ, and the second द् and य् are also changed to म् and उ; so the declension is:— Nom. Sing. अमुमुयङ् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुयञ्चः Acc. Sing. अमुमुयञ्चम् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुचः Ins. Sing. अमुमुचा Dual अमुमुयग्भ्याम् &c. &c. The mutva being considered as asiddha, there is no sandhi in in æg, for the Sandhi rule is contained in the Sixth Book of Panini, while this g substitute is ordained in the Tripadi portion of Ashtadhyayi. Hence the Sutra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12 applies. Some, by applying the following maxim, get the form Paribhasha "When a modification is ordained with regard to something which is not final, the operation takes place on that only which is in proximity to the final." The second class apply this maxim and make g change only for which stands in proximity to the final. There is a third form, which is obtained by explaining the असेः in the Sutra as मः सेर्यस्य सोऽयमसिः, तत्र सकारस्य मकारः क्रियते "The word असेः in the sutra is a Bahuvrihi, and means that in which अस् is substituted for ‹?›" The sutra is thus confined to the form derived by changing the द् into म् by VII. 2. 102. and not to any other. Thus there are three views with regard to the application of the present sutra:— (1) the d of adas, and of adri are both changed to m by the present sutra; (2) the first is not changed, but only the second; (3) none is changed. Thus we have (1) अमूमुयङ् (VII. 1. 70, VI. 1. 68, VIII. 2. 23 and 62), अमूमुयञ्चौ, अमूमुयञ्चः (2) Secondly, अदमुयङ्, अदमुयञ्चौ, अदमुयञ्चः (3) Lastly अद्रिर्यङ्, अद्रियञ्चौ, अद्रियञ्चः The above verse summarises this: Verse:—Some ordain that m should come separately for both adas and adri, as there is double d (in see sutra VIII. 2. 80 and VII. 4. 90 S. 2644); others would have m only for the last portion which stands in proximity to the final, (i.e. for adri); while a third class would have m nowhere, because they explain असेः of the sutra by confining it to Tyadadi VII. 2. 102." Note:—Thus उदङ् = विष्वक्. This form is thus evolved. अञ्च् + क्विन् = अञ्च् + ० = अञ्च् + नुम् (VII. 1. 70). Then there is elision of the final conjunct consonant, then the final dental is changed to guttural because of the क्विन् affix (VIII. 2. 62), i.e. च् is changed to क् and we have ‹?› which with ङि, gives the above form. प्राङ्, प्रत्यङ्, उदङ् प्राची and प्रतीची (VI. 3. 95) have acute on the final irregularly (nipatana) in order to prevent the krit-accent, and when ई is changed into य् the following vowel becomes svarita (VIII. 2. 4). Observe अश्वाव्री—अश्वमञ्चति, the अ of अञ्च् is elided by VI. 4. 138. Why 'when an affix follows'? Observe प्राची The न् is totally elided by VI. 4. 24, feminine ङीप् being added by IV. 1. 6 Vart. The अ is elided by VI. 4. 138, and the final of प्र is lengthened by VI. 3. 138. Why do we say of क्विन् and अनप्रत्यये? Observe अञ्चनम् Another reading of the sutra is अनवप्रत्यये (नावप्रत्यये) It would give the same result, the meaning then being when no affix follows. The word अनप्रत्यये or अनवप्रत्यये indicates by implication that in other places where simply a verb is mentioned, it means a word-form beginning with that verb which ends with some affix. For had अनप्रत्यये not been used, then the rule would have applied not only when anch followed, but when anchana ending in ल्युट् also followed. The maxim धातुग्रहणे तदादिविधिरिष्यते is illustrated in अयस्कृते and अयस्कारः; for VIII. 3. 46 teaches that visarga is changed into स् when कृ follows. There the कृ denotes not only the root कृ but a

(aninasnangrahanesvarTavatapyanarTakena ca tadantaviDin prayojayanti) The word atu in the sûtra indicates whatever ends in atu whether when rirst enunciated (upadesa), such as vatu, ktavatu &c. or which asunes the rorn atu in granatical inrlection, such as qavatu, which in upadesa ends in atu, but becones atu in prayoga or aplication. in Vocative singular we have he gonan, he supaya, this rule not aplying there. Even in the case or Denoninative rots, the lengthening wil take place. The prohibition or aDatu in this sûtra aplies to original rots and not to derivative rots ron nouns. Thus — "e wishes to have cows." The aril kyac is aded to gonat in rorning the derivative rot by i. 1. 8. or i. 1. 10. with the rorce or "wishing" or "behaving." The rot is gonatya. it is a derivative rot, and so it does not ral within the prohibition or this sûtra. now gonaty + kvip = gonat (a is droped by Vi. 4. 48, and y by Vi. 4. 50). "One wishing to have cows." ere ends with at (which was part or the original aril natup aded to go) and here we wil have lengthening as wel as nun The nun wil be aded ror the rolowing reason:— in the sûtra ugidacan Vi. 1. 70. s. 361 the rot ancu is taken ror the sake
ck: 425. in the noninative sinkular (tith the elception or the Vocative sinkular) the penultinate votel is lenkthenet in a sten entink in atu, ant as then the consonant (as) toes not pelonk to a rot. the nun (n) is atet to the apove py Vi. 1. 70, arter the elonkation has taken place, ror ir atet perore elonkation, the votel no lonker peink penultinate, til not pe lenkthenet at al. this is pecause or the rorce or this sûtra, thich thoukh precetent in the orter or enunciation in paninis ashtathyayi, ant thererore oukht to have pen supersetet py the supsetuent ant nitya sutra (Vi. 1. 70 s. 361) ortainink nun, yet is not so. thus its teclension is noninative sinkular tinan tual tinantO plural tinanta Vocative he tinan perore the teak case terninations, it is teclinet like nahat. note:—as :— as supaya, suyasa, susrota thy to te say not pelonkink to a thātu? Opserve pintakrasa there s pelonks to the rot kras (pintan krasate), so also carnava (carna vaste) the as havink no sikniricance as an aril &c. is also inclutet here, on the strenkth or the nalin "thenever an or in or as or nan, then they are taukht in kranar tenote py i. 1. 72, sonethink that ents tith these, there they represent these conpination or leters, poth in so rar as they poses, ant also in so rar as they are voit or a neanink". (aninasnankrahanesvartavatapyanartakena ca tatantavitin prayocayanti) the tort atu in the sûtra inticates thatever ents in atu thether then rirst enunciatet (upatesa), such as vatu, ktavatu &c. or thich asunes the rorn atu in kranatical inrlection, such as tavatu, thich in upatesa ents in atu, put pecones atu in prayoka or aplication. in Vocative sinkular te have he konan, he supaya, this rule not aplyink there. "One tishink to have cots." ere ents tith at (thich tas part or the orikinal aril natup atet to ko) ant here te til have lenkthenink as tel as nun the nun til pe atet ror the rolotink reason:— in the sûtra ukitacan Vi. 1. 70. s. 361 the rot ancu is taken ror the sake
s: 425. In the Nominative Singular (with the exception of the Vocative Singular) the penultimate vowel is lengthened in a stem ending in अतु, and अस् when the consonant (अस्) does not belong to a root. The नुम् (न्) is added to the above by VII. 1. 70, after the elongation has taken place, for if added before elongation, the vowel no longer being penultimate, will not be lengthened at all. This is because of the force of this sûtra, which though precedent in the order of enunciation in Panini's Ashtadhyayi, and therefore ought to have been superseded by the subsequent and nitya sutra (VII. 1. 70 S. 361) ordaining नुम्, yet is not so. Thus its declension is Nominative Singular धीमान् Dual धीमन्तौ Plural धीमन्तः Vocative हे धीमन् Before the weak case terminations, it is declined like महत्. Note:—अस् :— as सुपयाः, सुयशाः, सुश्रोताः Why do we say 'not belonging to a dhātu'? Observe पिण्डग्रसः where स् belongs to the root ग्रस् (पिण्डं ग्रसते), so also चर्मवः (चर्म वस्ते) The अस् having no significance as an affix &c. is also included here, on the strength of the maxim "whenever अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are taught in Grammar denote by I. 1. 72, something that ends with these, there they represent these combination of letters, both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of a meaning". (अनिन्नस्मन्ग्रहणेष्वर्थवताऽप्यनर्थकेन च तदन्तविधिं प्रयोजयन्ति) The word अतु in the sûtra indicates whatever ends in अतु whether when first enunciated (उपदेश), such as वतु, क्तवतु &c. or which assumes the form अतु in grammatical inflection, such as डवतु, which in upadesa ends in अतु, but becomes अतु in प्रयोग or application. In Vocative singular we have हे गोमन्, हे सुपयः, this rule not applying there. Even in the case of Denominative roots, the lengthening will take place. The prohibition of अधातु in this sûtra applies to original roots and not to derivative roots from nouns. Thus — "He wishes to have cows." The affix क्यच् is added to गोमत् in forming the derivative root by III. 1. 8. or III. 1. 10. with the force of "wishing" or "behaving." The root is गोमत्य. It is a derivative root, and so it does not fall within the prohibition of this sûtra. Now गोमत्य् + क्विप् = गोमत् (अ is dropped by VI. 4. 48, and य् by VI. 4. 50). "One wishing to have cows." Here ends with अत् (which was part of the original affix मतुप् added to गो) and here we will have lengthening as well as नुम् The नुम् will be added for the following reason:— In the sûtra उगिदचां VII. 1. 70. S. 361 the root अञ्चु is taken for the sake of niyama or restriction, that is, the operations dependent upon ugit, when applied to roots, will apply to the root añchu only, and not to any other root having an ugit. Thus in स्रंसु and ध्वंसु there is no ugit operation. Therefore, we could have easily inferred that no other root except अञ्चु would take नुम् under that sutra. The specific mention of अधातुः in that sutra would have become redundant. But the fact, that Panini has mentioned अधातुः in that sutra, indicates that by धातु is meant the original root and not a derivative root. Thus we have Singular गोमान् Dual गोमन्तौ Plural गोमन्तः "One who wishes to be possessed of cows." Now we take up the declension of भवत् not derived from भू, but from भा meaning 'to shine'. (see Unâdi sutra I. 63) with the affix डवतु Thus भा + डवतु = भवत् (the आ is elided by VI. 4. 143 and I. 4. 18 because the affix has an indicatory ड). It is declined as Nominative Singular भवान् Dual भवन्तौ Plural भवन्तः &c. But when it is derived from the root भू with the affix शतृ, as it does not then end with the affix अतु, the penultimate is not lengthened. Thus in this case, the Nominative Singular is भवन्. Now, we take up the declension of ‹?› formed from the root ‹?› with the affix ‹?›. The root is reduplicated. The reduplication is technically called अभ्यस्त as defined below, and because it is अभ्यस्त, it does not get the augment नुम्, for the sûtra after next prohibits it.

pk: 427. The Participial-aril satun (at-anta), does not take the augnent nun arter a reduplicate sten. Thus, dadat, dadata note:—This is an elception to Vi. 1. 70, and aplies or course to sarvanânasthâna or strong cases. The nun is to be read into this sûtra, ron Vi. 1. 70; ror the negation or this sûtra canot aply to i taught in the preceding sûtra ror i is never ordained arter śatṛ: thererore, though several other operations intervene, yet nun is to be read here. now, we take up the declension or jaksat, rorned with the aril satun aded to the rot jaks. its declension is governed by the rolowing sûtra:—
ck: 427. the participial-aril satun (at-anta), toes not take the auknent nun arter a retuplicate sten. thus, tatat, tatata note:—this is an elception to Vi. 1. 70, ant aplies or course to sarvanânasthâna or stronk cases. the nun is to pe reat into this sûtra, ron Vi. 1. 70; ror the nekation or this sûtra canot aply to i taukht in the precetink sûtra ror i is never ortainet arter śatṛ: thererore, thoukh several other operations intervene, yet nun is to pe reat here. not, te take up the teclension or caksat, rornet tith the aril satun atet to the rot caks. its teclension is kovernet py the rolotink sûtra:—
s: 427. The Participial-affix शतुँ (अत्-अन्त), does not take the augment नुम् after a reduplicate stem. Thus, ददत्, ददतः Note:—This is an exception to VII. 1. 70, and applies of course to sarvanâmasthâna or strong cases. The नुम् is to be read into this sûtra, from VII. 1. 70; for the negation of this sûtra cannot apply to ई taught in the preceding sûtra for ई is never ordained after śatṛ: therefore, though several other operations intervene, yet नुम् is to be read here. Now, we take up the declension of जक्षत्, formed with the affix शतुँ added to the root जक्ष्. Its declension is governed by the following Sûtra:—

pk: 428. so also the sil rots, with jakshi itselr as the seventh, are caled abhyasta. note:—The word abhyasta is understod here. The verb jakshi and the sil verbs that rolow it in the Dhatupatha, in al seven verbs, get this designation. These are jaksa, jagr, daridra, cakas, sas, diDi and vevi (Panini has overloked vevi and nentions only the rirst sil.) By geting the designation or abhyasta, the participles derived ron these verbs are declined like dadat Thus jaksat or jaksad (n. s.); jaksatO (n. Dual); jaksata (n. Plural). sinilar is the declension or jagrt, daridrat, sasat, cakasat diDi and vevi though elhibited in the Dhâtupâṭha as diDin and vevin with an indicatory n and thererore, they ought to be atnanepadi by i. 3. 12. s. 2158, yet they are parasnEpadi because or the Vaidic iregularities. These rorn their noninative singulars as diDyat and vevyat. ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in t. Declension or nasculine nouns ending in p. now we take up the declension or gup which is rorned ron the curadi rot gup with the aril kvip. The an or the curadi clas is optionaly elided by i. 1. 31. s. 2305. it is declined as: non: gup or gub, gupO, gupa; instr: Dual gubByan &c. ere ends the declension or nasculine nouns ending in p. Declension or nasculine nouns ending in sa. now, we take up the declension or tadrs rorned acording to the rolowing sûtra:—
ck: 428. so also the sil rots, tith cakshi itselr as the seventh, are calet aphyasta. note:—the tort aphyasta is unterstot here. the verp cakshi ant the sil verps that rolot it in the thatupatha, in al seven verps, ket this tesiknation. these are caksa, cakr, taritra, cakas, sas, titi ant vevi (panini has overloket vevi ant nentions only the rirst sil.) py ketink the tesiknation or aphyasta, the participles terivet ron these verps are teclinet like tatat thus caksat or caksat (n. s.); caksatO (n. tual); caksata (n. plural). sinilar is the teclension or cakrt, taritrat, sasat, cakasat titi ant vevi thoukh elhipitet in the thâtupâṭha as titin ant vevin tith an inticatory n ant thererore, they oukht to pe atnanepati py i. 3. 12. s. 2158, yet they are parasnEpati pecause or the Vaitic irekularities. these rorn their noninative sinkulars as tityat ant vevyat. ere ents the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in t. teclension or nasculine nouns entink in p. not te take up the teclension or kup thich is rornet ron the curati rot kup tith the aril kvip. the an or the curati clas is optionaly elitet py i. 1. 31. s. 2305. it is teclinet as: non: kup or kup, kupO, kupa; instr: tual kupyan &c. ere ents the teclension or nasculine nouns entink in p. teclension or nasculine nouns entink in sa. not, te take up the teclension or tatrs rornet acortink to the rolotink sûtra:—
s: 428. So also the six roots, with jakshi itself as the seventh, are called abhyasta. Note:—The word abhyasta is understood here. The verb jakshi and the six verbs that follow it in the Dhatupatha, in all seven verbs, get this designation. These are जक्ष, जागृ, दरिद्रा, चकास्, शास्, दीधी and वेवी (Panini has overlooked वेवी and mentions only the first six.) By getting the designation of Abhyasta, the participles derived from these verbs are declined like ददत् Thus जक्षत् or जक्षद् (N. S.); जक्षतौ (N. Dual); जक्षतः (N. Plural). Similar is the declension of जागृत्, दरिद्रत्, शासत्, चकासत् दीधी and वेवी though exhibited in the Dhâtupâṭha as दीधीङ् and वेवीङ् with an indicatory ङ् and therefore, they ought to be आत्मनेपदी by I. 3. 12. S. 2158, yet they are परस्मैपदी because of the Vaidic irregularities. These form their Nominative Singulars as दीध्यत् and वेव्यत्. Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in त्. Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्. Now we take up the declension of गुप् which is formed from the चुरादि root गुप् with the affix क्विप्. The आम् of the चुरादि class is optionally elided by III. 1. 31. S. 2305. It is declined as: Nom: गुप् or गुब्, गुपौ, गुपः; Instr: Dual गुब्भ्याम् &c. Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्. Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in श. Now, we take up the declension of तादृश् formed according to the following Sûtra:—

pk: 429. The aril kan as wel as kvin cones arter the verb drs ‘to se’ when it is in conbination with tyad &c. which precede it, and when it does not signiry perception. note:—The rorce or ca is that the kvin also cones under sinilar circunstances. tyad &c. are pronouns, ror a list or which se i. 1. 27. Thus tadrs
ck: 429. the aril kan as tel as kvin cones arter the verp trs ‘to se’ then it is in conpination tith tyat &c. thich precete it, ant then it toes not sikniry perception. note:—the rorce or ca is that the kvin also cones unter sinilar circunstances. tyat &c. are pronouns, ror a list or thich se i. 1. 27. thus tatrs
s: 429. The affix कञ् as well as क्विन् comes after the verb दृश् ‘to see’ when it is in combination with त्यद् &c. which precede it, and when it does not signify perception. Note:—The force of 'च' is that the क्विन् also comes under similar circumstances. त्यद् &c. are pronouns, for a list of which see I. 1. 27. Thus तादृश्

pk: 430. a is substituted ror the rinal or the Pronouns (i. 1. 27) berore these words drg, drs and the aril vatu Thus tad + drs + kvin (by the present sûtra) = ta + drk (the s is changed to k by Vi. 2. 62. s. 37). This is not perceived (asidDa) ror the purposes or change by Vi. 2. 36, s. 294. Thus we have tadrs = tadrs = tadrq (Vi. 2. 39. s. 84) = tadrg (Vi. 2. 62. s. 37) = tadrk (optionaly by Vi. 4. 56. s. 206). Thus non. rorns are tadrk or tadrg, tadrsO, tadrsa. acording to the opinion or Kaiyaṭa and aradata &c. the rorn would be tadrK but never tadrg, in the alternative when it is not tadrk. Because they aply the kutva rule as an apavâda to vrasca rule and by kutva they get Ka in the place or sa (se Padananjarî p. 953): and Ka wil never becone g by Vi. 2. 39. s. 84; because Ka obtained by kvinpratyayasya ku Vi. 2. 62. is asidha or not perceived by the jastva rule Vi. 2. 39. s. 84. Or we nay say that Ka is not asidha ror Panini hinselr has changed K into g in the word digadi (se iV. 4. 54. s. 1429). now, we take up the declension or visu. This is rorned by the aril kvip aded to the rot vis to enter. The s is changed to s by Vi. 2. 36, s. 294. which is changed to q by Vi. 2. 39. s. 84. and optionaly to w by Vi. 4. 56. s. 206. Thus it is declined as: sing. Dual. Pl. non. viw or viq visO visa ac. visan visO visa &c. &c. now, we take up the declension or nas. in its declension, the rolowing rule aplies.
ck: 430. a is supstitutet ror the rinal or the pronouns (i. 1. 27) perore these torts trk, trs ant the aril vatu thus tat + trs + kvin (py the present sûtra) = ta + trk (the s is chanket to k py Vi. 2. 62. s. 37). this is not perceivet (asita) ror the purposes or chanke py Vi. 2. 36, s. 294. thus te have tatrs = tatrs = tatrt (Vi. 2. 39. s. 84) = tatrk (Vi. 2. 62. s. 37) = tatrk (optionaly py Vi. 4. 56. s. 206). thus non. rorns are tatrk or tatrk, tatrsO, tatrsa. acortink to the opinion or kaiyaṭa ant aratata &c. the rorn toult pe tatrk put never tatrk, in the alternative then it is not tatrk. pecause they aply the kutva rule as an apavâta to vrasca rule ant py kutva they ket ka in the place or sa (se patanancarî p. 953): ant ka til never pecone k py Vi. 2. 39. s. 84; pecause ka optainet py kvinpratyayasya ku Vi. 2. 62. is asitha or not perceivet py the castva rule Vi. 2. 39. s. 84. Or te nay say that ka is not asitha ror panini hinselr has chanket k into k in the tort tikati (se iV. 4. 54. s. 1429). not, te take up the teclension or visu. this is rornet py the aril kvip atet to the rot vis to enter. the s is chanket to s py Vi. 2. 36, s. 294. thich is chanket to t py Vi. 2. 39. s. 84. ant optionaly to t py Vi. 4. 56. s. 206. thus it is teclinet as: sink. tual. pl. non. vit or vit visO visa ac. visan visO visa &c. &c. not, te take up the teclension or nas. in its teclension, the rolotink rule aplies.
s: 430. आ is substituted for the final of the Pronouns (I. 1. 27) before these words दृग्, दृश् and the affix वतु Thus तद् + दृश् + क्विन् (by the present sûtra) = ता + दृक् (the श् is changed to क् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377). This is not perceived (असिद्ध) for the purposes of change by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. Thus we have तादृश् = तादृष् = तादृड् (VIII. 2. 39. S. 84) = तादृग् (VIII. 2. 62. S. 377) = तादृक् (optionally by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206). Thus Nom. forms are तादृक् or तादृग्, तादृशौ, तादृशः. According to the opinion of Kaiyaṭa and Haradatta &c. the form would be तादृख् but never तादृग्, in the alternative when it is not तादृक्. Because they apply the कुत्व rule as an apavâda to व्रश्च rule and by कुत्व they get ख in the place of श (See Padamanjarî p. 953): and ख will never become ग् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84; because ख obtained by क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः VIII. 2. 62. is asiddha or not perceived by the जश्त्व rule VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. Or we may say that ख is not asiddha for Panini himself has changed ख् into ग् in the word दिगादि (See IV. 4. 54. S. 1429). Now, we take up the declension of विशू. This is formed by the affix क्विप् added to the root विश् 'to enter'. The श् is changed to ष् by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. which is changed to ड् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. and optionally to ट् by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206. Thus it is declined as: Sing. Dual. Pl. Nom. विट् or विड् विशौ विशः Acc. विशम् विशौ विशः &c. &c. Now, we take up the declension of नश्. In its declension, the following rule applies.

pk: 431. The rinal or nas at the end or a word is optionaly changed to a gutural. note:—ere the rot nas has taken kvin in denoting condition or state; by considering it as belonging to sanpadadi clas. Thus there are rour rorns in the noninative singular nanely:—nak or nag or naw or naq noninative Dual and Plural are nasO, nasa. instr: Dual is nagByan and naqByan &c. now, we take up the declension or Grtasprs. its declension is governed by the rolowing rule:—
ck: 431. the rinal or nas at the ent or a tort is optionaly chanket to a kutural. note:—ere the rot nas has taken kvin in tenotink contition or state; py consiterink it as pelonkink to sanpatati clas. thus there are rour rorns in the noninative sinkular nanely:—nak or nak or nat or nat noninative tual ant plural are nasO, nasa. instr: tual is nakpyan ant natpyan &c. not, te take up the teclension or krtasprs. its teclension is kovernet py the rolotink rule:—
s: 431. The final of नश् at the end of a word is optionally changed to a guttural. Note:—Here the root नश् has taken क्विन् in denoting 'condition or state'; by considering it as belonging to संपदादि class. Thus there are four forms in the Nominative Singular namely:—नक् or नग् or नट् or नड् Nominative Dual and Plural are नशौ, नशः. Instr: Dual is नग्भ्याम् and नड्भ्याम् &c. Now, we take up the declension of घृतस्पृश्. Its declension is governed by the following rule:—

pk: 432. √ tunpa, To injure, to hurt. Pre. tunpati Per. tutunpa i rut. tunpita i rut. tunpisyati inperative tunpatu inper. atunpat Pot. tunpet Bene. tupyat aorist atunpit Condi. atunpisyat Caus. tunpayati aorist atitunpat Desi. tutunpisati inten. totunpyate yan-luk totonpiti or totarnpiti

pk: Declension or nasculines ending in s. We take up the declension or pipaWis (neaning wishing to read). it is derived ron the rot pipaWis with the aril kvip. The a or sa is elided by Vi. 4. 48. s. 2308. The s was changed to s by Vi. 3. 39. s. 153. But this is not perceived by the sūtra requiring the substitution or s into run ror it is precedent in the order or enuneration in Pāṇinis ashṭādhyāyī, (Vi. 2. 6. s. 162). Thus pipaWis + su = pipaWis + 0 (by Vi. 1. 68. s. 252). now pipaWis gets the nane or a pada though the aril su is elided arter it (i. 1. 62. s. 262). Thererore the s which is realy s becones run. Thus pipaWis becones pipaWir. at this stage aplies the rolowing sūtra. 43. a penultinate ik is lengthened, when the rinal r or v or a rot can stand at the end or a Pada. Thus pipaWir becones pipaWi. The noninative Dual and Plural are pipaWisO and pipaWisa. The inst: Dual is pipaWirByan. in rorning the Locative Plural the sūtra Vi. 3. 36 s. 151 as wel as the rolowing cones into operation.
ck: teclension or nasculines entink in s. te take up the teclension or pipatis (neanink tishink to reat). it is terivet ron the rot pipatis tith the aril kvip. the a or sa is elitet py Vi. 4. 48. s. 2308. the s tas chanket to s py Vi. 3. 39. s. 153. put this is not perceivet py the sūtra retuirink the supstitution or s into run ror it is precetent in the orter or enuneration in pāṇinis ashṭāthyāyī, (Vi. 2. 6. s. 162). thus pipatis + su = pipatis + 0 (py Vi. 1. 68. s. 252). not pipatis kets the nane or a pata thoukh the aril su is elitet arter it (i. 1. 62. s. 262). thererore the s thich is realy s pecones run. thus pipatis pecones pipatir. at this stake aplies the rolotink sūtra. 43. a penultinate ik is lenkthenet, then the rinal r or v or a rot can stant at the ent or a pata. thus pipatir pecones pipati. the noninative tual ant plural are pipatisO ant pipatisa. the inst: tual is pipatirpyan. in rornink the Locative plural the sūtra Vi. 3. 36 s. 151 as tel as the rolotink cones into operation.
s: Declension of Masculines ending in स्. We take up the declension of पिपठिस् (meaning 'wishing to read'). It is derived from the root पिपठिस् with the affix क्विप्. The अ of स is elided by VI. 4. 48. S. 2308. The स् was changed to ष् by VIII. 3. 39. S. 153. But this is not perceived by the Sūtra requiring the substitution of स् into रुँ for it is precedent in the order of enumeration in Pāṇini's Ashṭādhyāyī, (VIII. 2. 66. S. 162). Thus पिपठिष् + सु = पिपठिष् + ० (by VI. 1. 68. S. 252). Now पिपठिष् gets the name of a pada though the affix सु is elided after it (I. 1. 62. S. 262). Therefore the ष् which is really स् becomes रुँ. Thus पिपठिष् becomes पिपठिर्. At this stage applies the following Sūtra. 433. A penultimate ik is lengthened, when the final r or v of a root can stand at the end of a Pada. Thus पिपठिर् becomes पिपठीः. The Nominative Dual and Plural are पिपठिषौ and पिपठिषः. The Inst: Dual is पिपठीर्भ्याम्. In forming the Locative Plural the sūtra VIII. 3. 36 S. 151 as well as the following comes into operation.

s: 436. असुङ् ( अस् ) is substituted for the final of पुंस् when the sarvanāmasthāna affixes are to be added. The उ in असुङ् is for the sake of pronunciation and not to indicate that नुम् should be added under VII. 1. 70 S. 361 because the नुम् will be added in strong cases by the very fact that the word पुंस् is formed from पा ( to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178 ) and as the affix डुम्सुन् is an उगित् affix, it will produce its effect under VII. 1. 70 by causing नुम् pari passu as it does in causing ङीप् to be added to in the feminine, in forming बहुपुंसी, by the sūtra उगितश्च ( IV. 1. 6 S. 455 ) Thus it is declined as follows:-- Singular. Dual. Plural. Nom. पुमान् पुमांसौ पुमांसः Voc. हे पुमन् Acc. पुंसः Inst. पुंसा पुंभ्याम् पुम्भिः Loc. पुंसु Kāśikā:-- The word is derived from पा (to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178), the न् being changed to anusvāra. So when ‹?› of पुंस् is replaced by असुङ् we get the form पुमस्, the उ of असुङ् indicates that नुम् should be added in the strong cases after म ( VII. 1. 70 ), so we have पुमान्, पुमांसौ, पुमांसः This substitution must take place in its incipient stage before the affixes are added, (अङ्गस्य) : otherwise the accent will be wrong. The compounds have acute on the final, (VI. 1. 223 ), therefore, परमपुंस् has acute on पुं, and in the Nominative Singular the acute will remain on पु, but it is intended that it should be on मा, thus परमपुमान् The simple word पुंस्, of course, has accent on पु. Now, we take up the declension of उशनस्. By VII. 1. 94. S. 276, अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Nom. Sing: Thus Nom. forms are उशना, उशनसौ, उशनसः In forming the Voc: Sing: the following Vārtika will apply :— Vārt :— अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Voc. S. also, as an alternative, the final न् not being elided (See VIII. 2. 8). Otherwise we have three forms in the Vocative Singular: as हे उशनन्, हे उशन, and हे उशनः The Instr Dual is उशनोभ्याम् &c. Now, we take up the declension of अनेहस् meaning 'time'. Singular. Dual. Plural. Nom. अनेहा अनेहसौ अनेहसः Voc. हे अनेहः Instr. अनेहोभ्याम् &c. Now, we take up the declension of वेधस् meaning 'the Creator'. Singular. Dual. Plural. Nom. वेधाः वेधसौ वेधसः Voc. हे वेधः Instr. वेधोभ्याम् &c. Now, we take up the declension of सुवस् meaning 'one who wears well'. Here वस् belongs to a root and so in the Nom: S. its vowel is not lengthened because of the prohibition of अधातु in VI. 4. 14. S. 425. Hence its Nom forms are सुवः, सुवसौ, सुवसः Now we take up the declension of पिण्डग्रस् and पिण्डग्रसस् The verbs ग्रस् and ग्रसु mean 'to swallow'; the Nominative singular forms of these are पिण्डग्रः and पिण्डग्रसः meaning 'a lump eater'. Now, we take up the declension of अदस्. In its declension the following rules apply :--

pk: 438. √ trunpha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. trunPati Per. tutrunPa i rut. trunPita aorist atrunPit Caus. trunPayati Desi. tutrunPisati inten. totrunPyate note:—The nasal in the above rots is not elided in the Perect because the ariles are here aded to a rot ending in a conjunct consonant, and they are not kit (i. 2. 5. s. 242). Thererore we have the rorns tutunpa &c. ror the rule or elision or nasal (Vi. 4. 24. s. 415) aplies to kit or ṅit ariles. in the Benedictive, the ariles being kit by i. 4. 104 s. 216, there is elision or the nasal (Vi. 4. 24. s. 415). Thus tupyat ron tunpa When preceded by pra the rot tunpa ads a sibilant in its begining, because or the rolowing vārtika to be round in the Pāraskarādi clas (Vi. 1. 157 s. 1071):— Gaṇa Vārtika:—The augnent suw is aded to the rot tunpa when preceded by the preposition pra provided the agent or the notion is a cow. Thus prastunpati gO (prastunpati iti pravrte suw Padanañjarī.) since the rot is elhibited in the above Vārtika as prastunpati with sitap, thererore when this rot is conjugated in yan-luk the sibilant is not aded (Vi. 2. 10 s. 2646). Thus pratotunpiti

s: 438. √ trumpha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुम्फति Per. तुत्रुम्फ I Fut. त्रुम्फिता Aorist अत्रुम्फीत् Caus. त्रुम्फयति Desi. तुत्रुम्फिषति Inten. तोत्रुम्फ्यते Note:—The nasal in the above roots is not elided in the Perfect because the affixes are here added to a root ending in a conjunct consonant, and they are not kit (I. 2. 5. S. 2242). Therefore we have the forms तुतुम्प &c. For the rule of elision of nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415) applies to kit or ṅit affixes. In the Benedictive, the affixes being kit by III. 4. 104 S. 2216, there is elision of the nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415). Thus तुप्यात् from तुम्प When preceded by प्र the root तुम्प adds a sibilant in its beginning, because of the following vārtika to be found in the Pāraskarādi class (VI. 1. 157 S. 1071):— Gaṇa Vārtika:—The augment सुट् is added to the root तुम्प when preceded by the preposition प्र provided the agent of the notion is a cow. Thus प्रस्तुम्पति गौः (प्रस्तुम्पति इति प्रवृत्ते सुट् Padamañjarī.) Since the root is exhibited in the above Vārtika as प्रस्तुम्पति with शितप्, therefore when this root is conjugated in यङ्-लुक् the sibilant is not added (VII. 2. 10 S. 2646). Thus प्रतोतुम्पीति

pk: 458. The aril qap is enployed in the reninine, arter a noninal-sten ending with the word pâd, when the word denotes a verse or the nig-veda. This debars ‹?›. Thus dvipada rk a nik verse consisting or two quarter verses, sinilarly ekapada rk or tripada rk, or catuspada rk 458 a. The reninine ariles are not enployed arter the stens caled saw (i. 1. 24 s. 369), and svasr &c. This prohibits al reninine ariles that would otherwise have presented thenselves. Thus, panca the rive Brāhnaṇī ladies. so also sapta, nava, dasa &c. are reninine as wel as nasculine. note:—in panca, though the n or pancan is elided, yet the elided n is asidha ror the purposes or saw and the word pancan though not ending in n wil get the designation saw by i. 1. 24 s. 369, because the elided n is asidha by Vi. 2. 2. s. 358 and so there is no aril arter panca by the present sûtra. sanjnaviDi—as panca brahnanya, dasa brahnanya The elision or n being asidha, the words panca and dasa are stil caled shash, though they no longer end in n. Being caled saw (snanta saw i. 1. 24), they do not take ariles in the reninine (iV. 1. 10 s. 308). acording to the Vartikakâra, there is no necesity or using the word sanjna in the sutra Vi. 2. 2. s. 230 (sanjnagrahananarTakyan ca taninitatvalopasya), because the elision or n is caused by reason or its having such a designation (as saw). Thus without its having the nane or saw there would be no elision or jas and sas, without such elision there is no pada sanjñâ or these words, and unles these words get Pada designation, there can be no elision or n by Vi. 2. 7, s. 36. The shash designation, however, would not be retained by these words arter taking plural ariles, when reninine ariles are to be aded to then, but ror this sûtra. The pancan and dasan ending in n would require nip in the reninine, which is however prohibited, ror when jas and sas are elided, the words end in a and require wap ror their reninine, which is also prohibited, because, by the present sutra the word stil retains its designation or saw. ow can this be the purpose or this sûtra? There are two views as to derinitions (sanjna), the one is that a particular nane is given to a thing once ror al prior to any operations; and operations are perorned arterwards upon it, as ocasions arise. This view is enbodied in the nalin yaTadesan sanjnapariBasan ‘sanjñās and Paribhāshās renain where they are taught.’ The other view is that the sanjñâ sûtra is to be read with every particular operative sûtra,

s: 458. The affix डाप् is employed in the feminine, after a Nominal-stem ending with the word 'pâd', when the word denotes a verse of the Rig-veda. This debars ‹?›. Thus द्विपदा ऋक् 'a Rik verse consisting of two quarter verses', similarly एकपदा ऋक् or त्रिपदा ऋक्, or चतुष्पदा ऋक् 458 A. The feminine affixes are not employed after the stems called 'षट्' (I. 1. 24 S. 369), and स्वसृ &c. This prohibits all feminine affixes that would otherwise have presented themselves. Thus, पञ्च 'the five Brāhmaṇī ladies'. So also सप्त, नव, दश &c. are feminine as well as masculine. Note:—In पञ्च, though the न् of पञ्चन् is elided, yet the elided न् is asiddha for the purposes of षट् and the word पञ्चन् though not ending in न् will get the designation षट् by I. 1. 24 S. 369, because the elided न् is asiddha by VIII. 2. 2. S. 358 and so there is no affix after पञ्च by the present Sûtra. संज्ञाविधिः—As पञ्च ब्राह्मण्याः, दश ब्राह्मण्याः The elision of न् being asiddha, the words पञ्च and दश are still called shash, though they no longer end in न्. Being called षट् (ष्णान्ता षट् I. 1. 24), they do not take affixes in the feminine (IV. 1. 10 S. 308). According to the Vartikakâra, there is no necessity of using the word संज्ञा in the sutra VIII. 2. 2. S. 2330 (संज्ञाग्रहणानर्थक्यं च तन्निमित्तत्वाल्लोपस्य), because the elision of न् is caused by reason of its having such a designation (as षट्). Thus without its having the name of षट् there would be no elision of जस् and शस्, without such elision there is no pada sanjñâ of these words, and unless these words get Pada designation, there can be no elision of न् by VIII. 2. 7, S. 366. The shash designation, however, would not be retained by these words after taking plural affixes, when feminine affixes are to be added to them, but for this sûtra. The पञ्चन् and दशन् ending in न् would require ङीप् in the feminine, which is however prohibited, for when जस् and शस् are elided, the words end in अ and require टाप् for their feminine, which is also prohibited, because, by the present sutra the word still retains its designation of षट्. How can this be the purpose of this sûtra? There are two views as to definitions (संज्ञा), the one is that a particular name is given to a thing once for all prior to any operations; and operations are performed afterwards upon it, as occasions arise. This view is embodied in the maxim यथाद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् ‘Sanjñās and Paribhāshās remain where they are taught.’ The other view is that the sanjñâ sûtra is to be read with every particular operative sûtra, and the sanjñâ given to the word afresh, with every new operation. In other words, the sanjñâ sûtra becomes identified with a vidhi sûtra, every time that a rule is to be applied. This is embodied in the maxim कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् ‘Sanjñās and Paribhāshās are attracted by or unite with the rules that enjoin particular operations’. In the first view, the sanjñâ will be good throughout, both for the purposes of eliding जस् and शस् and for prohibiting टाप्. Hence this sûtra is not necessary in that view. But in the other view, the sûtra is necessary. For if the view be taken that a sanjñâ is to be applied with regard to each operation, then that sanjñâ which had taken effect for the purposes of eliding जस् and शस्, will no longer hold good for the purposes of preventing the application of the feminine affix. Hence, the word संज्ञा is taken in this sûtra, to prevent the application of the second view.

pk: 459. The aril nip is not enployed arter a noninal-sten ending in the sylable nan. Thus sinan is both nasculine and reninine, declined as sina, sinanO &c.
ck: 459. the aril nip is not enployet arter a noninal-sten entink in the sylaple nan. thus sinan is poth nasculine ant reninine, teclinet as sina, sinanO &c.
s: 459. The affix ङीप् is not employed after a Nominal-stem ending in the syllable मन्. Thus सीमन् is both masculine and feminine, declined as सीमा, सीमानौ &c.

pk: 460. The aril nip is not enployed to denote the reninine, arter a Bahuvrîhi conpound ending in an This rerers to those Bahuvrîhi conpounds, in which the penultinate a is not elided. Or the Bahuvrîhi conpounds which lose their penultinate a, it is optional to enploy this aril or not; as it wil be taught in iV. 1. 28. s. 462. Thus bahuyajvan is or both genders and is declined as nasculine, n. s. bahuyajva, n. d. bahuyajvanO &c. The penultinate a or bahuyajvan is not elided because or the prohibition or nalopa &c. (Vi. 4. 137 s. 35).
ck: 460. the aril nip is not enployet to tenote the reninine, arter a pahuvrîhi conpount entink in an this rerers to those pahuvrîhi conpounts, in thich the penultinate a is not elitet. Or the pahuvrîhi conpounts thich lose their penultinate a, it is optional to enploy this aril or not; as it til pe taukht in iV. 1. 28. s. 462. thus pahuyacvan is or poth kenters ant is teclinet as nasculine, n. s. pahuyacva, n. t. pahuyacvanO &c. the penultinate a or pahuyacvan is not elitet pecause or the prohipition or nalopa &c. (Vi. 4. 137 s. 35).
s: 460. The affix ङीप् is not employed to denote the feminine, after a Bahuvrîhi compound ending in अन् This refers to those Bahuvrîhi compounds, in which the penultimate अ is not elided. Of the Bahuvrîhi compounds which lose their penultimate अ, it is optional to employ this affix or not; as it will be taught in IV. 1. 28. S. 462. Thus बहुयज्वन् is of both genders and is declined as masculine, N. s. बहुयज्वा, N. d. बहुयज्वानौ &c. The penultimate अ of बहुयज्वन् is not elided because of the prohibition of नलोप &c. (VI. 4. 137 S. 355).

pk: 461. The aril qap cones optionaly arter both vis. the noninal-sten ending in nan, and a Bahuvrîhi conpound ending in an, as nentioned in the preceding two sûtras. Or the aril qap, the leter q indicates that the aril is to be aded arter the elision or the wi (i. 1. 64 s. 79) or the base. Thus danan + qap = dan + a = dana This being an optional rule we have 1. dana, d. dane or dananO, 2. dana or danana; sinilarly with sina, as, sina, sine or sinanO, sina or sinana so also in Bahuvrîhi conpounds ending in an as:— bahuraja, bahuraje or bahurajanO, bahuraja or bahurajana bahutaksa, bahutakse or bahutaksanO, bahutaksa or bahutaksana bahuyajva, bahuyajve or bahuyajvanO, bahuyajva or bahuyajvana Why do we say optionaly? so that the option nay aply to sûtra iV. 1. 7 s. 456 also; i. e. when a prâtipadika ending in van, which can be regarded as ending in an, in a Bahuvrîhi conpound, then the change or na into r and the aplication or nip are optional: we nay aply the aril qap instead. as:—bahuDiva or bahuDivari; bahupiva or bahupivari By iV. 1. 5, s. 306 prâtipadikas ending in nan would have taken the aril nip, inasnuch as they end in n; but the present sûtra prohibits that. Thus danan a string is both neuter and reninine; and is declined as rolows:— 1s. dana, d. danani, pl. danani sinilarly pana, panani, panani The word danan is never nasculine acording to anarakoṣa.
ck: 461. the aril tap cones optionaly arter poth vis. the noninal-sten entink in nan, ant a pahuvrîhi conpount entink in an, as nentionet in the precetink to sûtras. Or the aril tap, the leter t inticates that the aril is to pe atet arter the elision or the ti (i. 1. 64 s. 79) or the pase. thus tanan + tap = tan + a = tana this peink an optional rule te have 1. tana, t. tane or tananO, 2. tana or tanana; sinilarly tith sina, as, sina, sine or sinanO, sina or sinana so also in pahuvrîhi conpounts entink in an as:— pahuraca, pahurace or pahuracanO, pahuraca or pahuracana pahutaksa, pahutakse or pahutaksanO, pahutaksa or pahutaksana pahuyacva, pahuyacve or pahuyacvanO, pahuyacva or pahuyacvana thy to te say optionaly? so that the option nay aply to sûtra iV. 1. 7 s. 456 also; i. e. then a prâtipatika entink in van, thich can pe rekartet as entink in an, in a pahuvrîhi conpount, then the chanke or na into r ant the aplication or nip are optional: te nay aply the aril tap insteat. as:—pahutiva or pahutivari; pahupiva or pahupivari py iV. 1. 5, s. 306 prâtipatikas entink in nan toult have taken the aril nip, inasnuch as they ent in n; put the present sûtra prohipits that. thus tanan a strink is poth neuter ant reninine; ant is teclinet as rolots:— 1s. tana, t. tanani, pl. tanani sinilarly pana, panani, panani the tort tanan is never nasculine acortink to anarakoṣa.
s: 461. The affix डाप् comes optionally after both viz. the Nominal-stem ending in मन्, and a Bahuvrîhi compound ending in अन्, as mentioned in the preceding two Sûtras. Of the affix डाप्, the letter ड् indicates that the affix is to be added after the elision of the टि (I. 1. 64 S. 79) of the base. Thus दामन् + डाप् = दाम् + आ = दामा This being an optional rule we have 1. दामा, d. दामे or दामानौ, 2. दामाः or दामानः; similarly with सीमा, as, सीमा, सीमे or सीमानौ, सीमाः or सीमानः So also in Bahuvrîhi compounds ending in अन् As:— बहुराजा, बहुराजे or बहुराजानौ, बहुराजाः or बहुराजानः बहुतक्षा, बहुतक्षे or बहुतक्षाणौ, बहुतक्षाः or बहुतक्षाणः बहुयज्वा, बहुयज्वे or बहुयज्वानौ, बहुयज्वाः or बहुयज्वानः Why do we say 'optionally'? So that the option may apply to sûtra IV. 1. 7 S. 456 also; i. e. when a prâtipadika ending in वन्, which can be regarded as ending in अन्, in a Bahuvrîhi compound, then the change of न into र् and the application of ङीप् are optional: we may apply the affix डाप् instead. As:—बहुधीवा or बहुधीवरी; बहुपीवा or बहुपीवरी By IV. 1. 5, S. 306 prâtipadikas ending in मन् would have taken the affix ङीप्, inasmuch as they end in न्; but the present sûtra prohibits that. Thus दामन् 'a string' is both neuter and feminine; and is declined as follows:— 1s. दामा, d. दामानी, pl. दामानि Similarly पामा, पामानी, पामानि The word दामन् is never masculine according to Amarakoṣa.

pk: 462. The aril nip optionaly cones arter that Bahuvrîhi conpound, which ending in the sylable an loses its penultinate a Thus bahurajan is a Bahuvrîhi conpound ending in an; in aplying nip, it loses its penultinate a by Vi. 4. 134 s. 234, (alopona there is elision or penultinate a or an when a bha aril rolows). Thus bahurajni having nany kings. in the alternative, when nip is not aded, we nay ad the aril qap by iV. 1. 13. s. 461. Thus bahuraja, bahuraje, bahuraja Or we nay aply the prohibition contained in iV. 1. 12 s. 460 and have bahuraja, bahurajanO, bahurajana note:—When the penultinate is not elided we canot aply the aril nip at al; in cases or such conpounds there are only two rorns or the reninine noun as suparva, suparve, suparva or suparva, suparvanO, suparvana That is to say we aply iV. 1. 13 and 12 only; ror in the case or suparvan &c rule Vi. 4. 137 s. 35 prevents the elision or the penultinate n; sanyogasananantat, there is not elision or the a or Can when it cones arter a conjunct consonant ending in ‹?› or ‹?›) in rorning the reninines or words ending in ‹?› the aril wil be aded arter the change or ‹?› to ‹?› by the rolowing sûtra.
