s: 462. The affix ङीप् optionally comes after that Bahuvrîhi compound, which ending in the syllable अन् loses its penultimate अ Thus बहुराजन् is a Bahuvrîhi compound ending in अन्; in applying ङीप्, it loses its penultimate अ by VI. 4. 134 S. 234, (अल्लोपोऽनः there is elision of penultimate अ of अन् when a bha affix follows). Thus बहुराज्ञी 'having many kings'. In the alternative, when ङीप् is not added, we may add the affix डाप् by IV. 1. 13. S. 461. Thus बहुराजा, बहुराजे, बहुराजाः Or we may apply the prohibition contained in IV. 1. 12 S. 460 and have बहुराजा, बहुराजानौ, बहुराजानः Note:—When the penultimate is not elided we cannot apply the affix ङीप् at all; in cases of such compounds there are only two forms of the feminine noun as सुपर्वा, सुपर्वे, सुपर्वाः or सुपर्वा, सुपर्वाणौ, सुपर्वाणः That is to say we apply IV. 1. 13 and 12 only; for in the case of सुपर्वन् &c rule VI. 4. 137 S. 355 prevents the elision of the penultimate न्; संयोगासननन्तात्, there is not elision of the अ of छन् when it comes after a conjunct consonant ending in ‹?› or ‹?›) In forming the feminines of words ending in ‹?› the affix will be added after the change of ‹?› to ‹?› by the following Sûtra.

pk: 463. i is substituted ror the a which stands berore the k belonging to an aril, when the reninine-ending ap rolows, provided that, it does not cone arter a case-aril (i. e. when such a word in k does not stand at the end or a Bahuvrîhi). That which stands in an aril is caled pratyayasTa i. e. k nust be the part or the aril. The a is changed into i in the reninine in ap. as sarvika, karika, &c. Why do we say ata? The k nust be preceded by short a, thererore, not here nOka. Why do we say belonging to an aril? The k nust belong to the aril thererore, not in saka ron saknotiti saka The sTa in pratyayasTa is ror the sake or distinctnes, there is no aril which is only k Why do we say provided that the reninine aril does not cone arter a case aril? Observe bahava parivrajaka asyan nagaryan = bahuparivrajaka nagari ere ap cones arter the noun parivrajaka which ends in a case-aril, and hence the a or karaka is not changed to i. The case aril is elided by i. 4. 71, s. 650 and it stil elerts its inrluence by i. 1. 62 s. 272. Why do we say arter asupa? The rule aplies to asup, thererore, not to nan. Why do we say "which stands berore"? The i is substituted ror the a which precedes (purvasya) k, and not the a which rolows k, as kawuka, nuwuka Why do we say short a? Observe raka. Why do we say when ap rolows? k should be rolowed by ap, se karaka. The substitution takes place when ap rolows, thererore, not in karakan. The word ap qualiries k. s: 463. इ is substituted for the अ which stands before the क् belonging to an affix, when the Feminine-ending आप् follows, provided that, it does not come after a case-affix (i. e. when such a word in क् does not stand at the end of a Bahuvrîhi). That which stands in an affix is called प्रत्ययस्थ i. e. क् must be the part of the affix. The अ is changed into इ in the feminine in आप्. As सर्विका, कारिका, &c. Why do we say अतः? The क् must be preceded by short अ, therefore, not here नौका. Why do we say belonging to an affix? The क् must belong to the affix therefore, not in शका from शक्नोतीति शका The स्थ in प्रत्ययस्थ is for the sake of distinctness, there is no affix which is only क् Why do we say 'provided that the feminine affix does not come after a case affix'? Observe बहवः परिव्राजका अस्यां नगर्याम् = बहुपरिव्राजका नगरी Here आप् comes after the noun परिव्राजक which ends in a case-affix, and hence the अ of कारक is not changed to इ. The case affix is elided by II. 4. 71, S. 650 and it still exerts its influence by I. 1. 62 S. 272. Why do we say after असुपः? The rule applies to असुप्, therefore, not to नञ्. Why do we say "which stands before"? The इ is substituted for the अ which precedes (पूर्वस्य) क्, and not the अ which follows क्, as कटुका, मुटुका Why do we say short अ? Observe राका. Why do we say when आप् follows? क् should be followed by आप्, see कारकः. The substitution takes place when आप् follows, therefore, not in कारकम्. The word आप् qualifies क्. Vårt :— मामक and नरक should be enumerated, for the क् of these is not part of the affix as मामिका, नरिका Here ‹?› is substituted for ‹?› before the affix अण् (IV. 3. 3. S. 1372), to which आप् is then added. The word मामक takes long ‹?› in the feminine only when it is a Name or in the Vedas (IV. 1. 30 S. 488) therefore though it ends in ‹?›, it does not take ङीप् (IV. 1. 15 S. 470) but टाप् (IV. 1. 4 S. 454), नरान् कायति = नरक formed with the affix क (III. 2. 3 S. 2915). Vårt :— The rule applies to the words ending in त्यक् (IV. 2. 98) and त्यप्, (IV. 2. 104 S. 1324) in spite of the prohibition in VII. 3. 46. S. 2915. As दाक्षिणात्यिका, ऐहत्यिका Note :— The word in the sûtra is कात् the fifth case of क ending in अ If then this be the condition, that the affix must end in ka क and not in k क्, then the rule will not apply to एतिका Because here the augment is अकच् (अक् with क् : the final अ in अक is for euphony only, and not a portion of the affix, as we find in भिन्धकि, छिन्धकि, रुन्धकि The word कात् therefore, is construed to mean ending in the consonant क्

pk: 464. The i is not substituted ror the a or ya and ta, with the augnent ka, when the reninine ap rolows. as yaka, saka; yakan, takan note :— The ya and sa sinply stand ror yad and tad, and the prohibition is not conrined to the noninative case only, as the rorns ya and sa nay lead one to think. yatado would have ben a beter sûtra. The prohibition aplies in every case, as yakanaDinahe, tan pacanahe Or yakan yakanaDinahe (i. e. kasan gaTan va), and takan takanpacanahe (i. e. osaDin sakinin va) Vårt :— Prohibition with regard to the aril tyak (V. 3. 34 s. 1983) should be stated also :— as aDityaka, upatyaka Vårt :— so also in the aril vun used in benediction as jivatad jivaka and Bavatat Bavaka. se i. 1. 150. s. 2912. note :— The reninine or pavaka &c. in the Veda does not take i ror a as hiranyavarna sucaya pavaka, yasu lonaka kaksaka &c. But pavika, alonika in secular literature. Vårt :— so also when the second nenber is elided in a conpound : as devaka, yajnaka, the second nenber data is elided, the ruler rorns being devadatika, yajnadatika (anajadO viBasa lopo vaktavya ) se V. 3. 83 Vart s. 2035. Vårt :— ksipaka &c. should be enunerated in this prohibition as ksipaka, Druvaka, putraka, cawaka, kanyaka Vårt :— taraka is rorned when it neans stars, but tarika a naid-servant ron tarayati Vårt :— varnaka is rorned when it neans a nantle or nask, but varnika an elpounder : as varnika Baguri lokayate Bhaguri is a conentary or Lokayata. Vårt :— vartaka a bird acording to the Eastern granarians, but vartika acording to the northern authorities. Why do we say when neaning a bird? Observe vartika Kari lokayatasya Vårt :— aswaka when neaning a pitrdevatya cerenony, but aswika Kari The cerenony related to Pitridevata is caled Pitridaivatya, the aril is yat The rorner is derived ron the rot as with aril takan (asnanti brahnana asyan ), the other is derived ron the nuneral aswan by the aril kan (V. 1. 2 s. 1687). Vårt :— Optionaly sutaka, putraka and vrndaraka, the other rorns are sutika, putrika, and vrndarika note :— The word veti or this vartika should be analysed as va a iti and not veti; and it neans that a is optionaly substituted ror the vowel that precedes ka Thererore in putrika the short i which is not the a or this sûtra, but or nin or putri shortened to i, this is replaced by a. in other elanples i is replaced by a
ck: 464. the i is not supstitutet ror the a or ya ant ta, tith the auknent ka, then the reninine ap rolots. as yaka, saka; yakan, takan note :— the ya ant sa sinply stant ror yat ant tat, ant the prohipition is not conrinet to the noninative case only, as the rorns ya ant sa nay leat one to think. yatato toult have pen a peter sûtra. the prohipition aplies in every case, as yakanatinahe, tan pacanahe Or yakan yakanatinahe (i. e. kasan katan va), ant takan takanpacanahe (i. e. osatin sakinin va) Vårt :— prohipition tith rekart to the aril tyak (V. 3. 34 s. 1983) shoult pe statet also :— as atityaka, upatyaka Vårt :— so also in the aril vun uset in penetiction as civatat civaka ant pavatat pavaka. se i. 1. 150. s. 2912. note :— the reninine or pavaka &c. in the Veta toes not take i ror a as hiranyavarna sucaya pavaka, yasu lonaka kaksaka &c. put pavika, alonika in secular literature. Vårt :— so also then the secont nenper is elitet in a conpount : as tevaka, yacnaka, the secont nenper tata is elitet, the ruler rorns peink tevatatika, yacnatatika (anacatO vipasa lopo vaktavya ) se V. 3. 83 Vart s. 2035. Vårt :— ksipaka &c. shoult pe enuneratet in this prohipition as ksipaka, truvaka, putraka, cataka, kanyaka Vårt :— taraka is rornet then it neans stars, put tarika a nait-servant ron tarayati Vårt :— varnaka is rornet then it neans a nantle or nask, put varnika an elpounter : as varnika pakuri lokayate phakuri is a conentary or Lokayata. Vårt :— vartaka a pirt acortink to the Eastern kranarians, put vartika acortink to the northern authorities. thy to te say then neanink a pirt? Opserve vartika kari lokayatasya Vårt :— astaka then neanink a pitrtevatya cerenony, put astika kari the cerenony relatet to pitritevata is calet pitritaivatya, the aril is yat the rorner is terivet ron the rot as tith aril takan (asnanti prahnana asyan ), the other is terivet ron the nuneral astan py the aril kan (V. 1. 2 s. 1687). Vårt :— Optionaly sutaka, putraka ant vrntaraka, the other rorns are sutika, putrika, ant vrntarika note :— the tort veti or this vartika shoult pe analyset as va a iti ant not veti; ant it neans that a is optionaly supstitutet ror the votel that precetes ka thererore in putrika the short i thich is not the a or this sûtra, put or nin or putri shortenet to i, this is replacet py a. in other elanples i is replacet py a
s: 464. The इ is not substituted for the अ of य and त, with the augment क, when the feminine आप् follows. As यका, सका; यकाम्, तकाम् Note :— The या and सा simply stand for यद् and तद्, and the prohibition is not confined to the nominative case only, as the forms या and सा may lead one to think. यत्तदोः would have been a better sûtra. The prohibition applies in every case, as यकामधीमहे, तां पचामहे Or यकां यकामधीमहे (i. e. कशां गाथां वा), and तकां तकाम्पचामहे (i. e. ओषधीं शाकिनीं वा) Vårt :— Prohibition with regard to the affix त्यक् (V. 3. 34 S. 1983) should be stated also :— As अधित्यका, उपत्यका Vårt :— So also in the affix वुन् used in benediction as जीवताद् जीवका and भवतात् भवका. See III. 1. 150. S. 2912. Note :— The feminine of पावक &c. in the Veda does not take इ for अ As हिरण्यवर्णाः शुचयः पावकाः, यासु लोमकाः कक्षकाः &c. But पाविकाः, अलोमिकाः in secular literature. Vårt :— So also when the second member is elided in a compound : as देवका, यज्ञका, the second member दत्त is elided, the fuller forms being देवदत्तिका, यज्ञदत्तिका (अनजादौ विभाषा लोपो वक्तव्यः ) See V. 3. 83 Vart S. 2035. Vårt :— क्षिपका &c. should be enumerated in this prohibition as क्षिपका, ध्रुवका, पुत्रका, चटका, कन्यका Vårt :— तारका is formed when it means 'stars', but तारिका 'a maid-servant' from तारयति Vårt :— वर्णका is formed when it means 'a mantle or mask', but वर्णिका 'an expounder' : as वर्णिका भागुरी लोकायते 'Bhaguri is a commentary of Lokayata'. Vårt :— वर्तका 'a bird' according to the Eastern grammarians, but वर्तिका according to the Northern authorities. Why do we say 'when meaning a bird'? Observe वर्तिका खारी लोकायतस्य Vårt :— अष्टका when meaning a पितृदेवत्य ceremony, but अष्टिका खारी The ceremony related to Pitridevata is called Pitridaivatya, the affix is यत् The former is derived from the root अश् with affix तकन् (अश्नन्ति ब्राह्मणा अस्याम् ), the other is derived from the numeral अष्टन् by the affix कन् (V. 1. 22 S. 1687). Vårt :— Optionally सूतका, पुत्रका and वृन्दारका, the other forms are सूतिका, पुत्रिका, and वृन्दारिका Note :— The word वेति of this vartika should be analysed as वा अ इति and not वेति; and it means that अ is optionally substituted for the vowel that precedes क Therefore in पुत्रिका the short इ which is not the अ of this sûtra, but of ङीन् of पुत्री shortened to इ, this is replaced by अ. In other examples इ is replaced by अ

pk: 465. acording to the opinion or northern granarians, i is not substituted ror that a which is obtained by shortening the long a or the reninine (under Vi. 4. 13 s. 834 berore the aril ka ), which is preceded by a y or a k The nention or northern granarians nakes this an optional rule. as aryaka or aryika, cawakaka or cawakika Why do we say or long a? Observe sankasye Bava sankasyika The word sankasya is rorned ron sankasa by the aril nya (sankase nirvrtan) Then is aded the aril vun (iV. 2. 121 s. 1345). ere there is no shortening or a long a, and hence no option is alowed. Why do we say preceded by y or ka? Observe asvika only (ron asva) Why do we say the a or the reninine aril? The word purvaya is elhibited in the reninine, in order to indicate that the rule aplies when the reninine aril ap is shortened to a Thererore not here ‹?› ron ‹?› ( suBan yati ) so also ‹?› ron Badraya where a is part or the rot ya ( se i. 2. 74 s. 318 ). Vârt :—Prohibition nust be stated or the y and v being rinals or a rot. When the y or v preceding this â, is the rinal or the rot, the prohibition contained in the sûtra, does not aply : as sunayika, supakika

s: 465. According to the opinion of Northern grammarians, इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the long आ of the feminine (under VII. 4. 13 S. 834 before the affix क ), which is preceded by a य् or a क् The mention of 'northern grammarians' makes this an optional rule. As आर्यका or आर्यिका, चटकका or चटकिका Why do we say 'of long आ'? Observe सांकाश्ये भवा सांकाश्यिका The word सांकाश्य is formed from संकाश by the affix ण्य (संकाशे निर्वृत्तम्) Then is added the affix वुञ् (IV. 2. 121 S. 1345). Here there is no shortening of a long आ, and hence no option is allowed. Why do we say preceded by य् or क? Observe अश्विका only (from अश्वा) Why do we say the आ of the Feminine affix? The word पूर्वायाः is exhibited in the feminine, in order to indicate that the rule applies when the feminine affix आप् is shortened to अ Therefore not here ‹?› from ‹?› ( शुभं याति ) So also ‹?› from भद्रया where आ is part of the root या ( see III. 2. 74 S. 3118 ). Vârt :—Prohibition must be stated of the y and v being finals of a root. When the y or v preceding this â, is the final of the root, the prohibition contained in the sûtra, does not apply : as सुनयिका, सुपाकिका

pk: 46. acording to the opinion or northern granarians, i is not substituted ror that a which is obtained by shortening the a (berore ka by Vi. 4. 13 s. 834), or Bastra, esa, aja, jna, dva (Vi. 2. 102 s. 265 ), and sva ; even not then, when the negative particle precedes then. The word Bastrajajnadvasvan or the sûtra has no case aril, but we nust interpret it as having the genitive case aril elided arter it; the word nanpurvananapi is used in the sûtra nerely ror the sake or clearnes, ror even without these words, the rule would have aplied, when the negative particle preceded ; because as we have already shown, the rule or tadanta vidhi aplies here. The word Bastra is nentioned in the sûtra to indicate that the rule would aply to it even then when it is an upasarjana. When it is not an upasarjana, the rorn would be evolved by the nelt sûtra. note :—Bastra is a word which has no coresponding nasculine rorn and as such, by the rolowing rule Vi. 3. 48 it would not have taken i ; its special nention here indicates that it should be the secondary nenber or the conpound here as avidyanana Bastra yasya - aBastra, the Dininutive or which is aBastraka or aBastrika ere rirst the a is shortened, as it is a secondary nenber ( upasarjana ), then when the Bahuvrîhi is nade, the reninine aril wap is aded to this aBasitapunska word, then this a is shortened berore ka by Vi. 4. 13. This short a (Vi. 4. 13 ) does not cone in the ron or the a which is ordained to cone arter a word having no coresponding nasculine. But or the two words esa and dva, the adition or i would be prohibited, when they are preceded by another word; because in a conpound the elided case aril is considered to be present, and thererore the prohibition or asupa or sûtra Vi. 3. 4 s. 463 would have aplied to these. Thus anesaka, paranesaka, advake, paranadvake note :—The nention or these two words in the sûtra ron this point or view, would be rather redundant, while in the case or the other rour words, Bastra, aja, jna, and sva, there would be itva, by the option alowed by this sûtra, even when they are the last nenbers in a conpound and in spite or the prohibition or asupa By this proces or elinination, we cone to the conclusion stated above, that the words nanpurvananapi qualiry sva only. ror this word alone is anbiguous. ror when sva is a sarvanâna neaning ones own, i. e., when it is not an upasarjana, then it is capable or taking akac by V. 3. 71. s. 2026. Thus sva+akac a + a = svaka ere the a berore ka
ck: 46. acortink to the opinion or northern kranarians, i is not supstitutet ror that a thich is optainet py shortenink the a (perore ka py Vi. 4. 13 s. 834), or pastra, esa, aca, cna, tva (Vi. 2. 102 s. 265 ), ant sva ; even not then, then the nekative particle precetes then. the tort pastracacnatvasvan or the sûtra has no case aril, put te nust interpret it as havink the kenitive case aril elitet arter it; the tort nanpurvananapi is uset in the sûtra nerely ror the sake or clearnes, ror even tithout these torts, the rule toult have apliet, then the nekative particle precetet ; s: 466. According to the opinion of Northern grammarians, इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the आ (before क by VII. 4. 13 S. 834), of भस्त्रा, एषा, अजा, ज्ञा, द्वा (VII. 2. 102 S. 265 ), and स्वा ; even not then, when the negative particle precedes them. The word भस्त्राजाज्ञाद्वास्वाम् of the Sûtra has no case affix, but we must interpret it as having the genitive case affix elided after it; the word नञ्पूर्वाणामपि is used in the Sûtra merely for the sake of clearness, for even without these words, the rule would have applied, when the negative particle preceded ; because as we have already shown, the rule of tadanta vidhi applies here. The word भस्त्रा is mentioned in the Sûtra to indicate that the rule would apply to it even then when it is an upasarjana. When it is not an upasarjana, the form would be evolved by the next Sûtra. Note :—भस्त्रा is a word which has no corresponding masculine form and as such, by the following rule VII. 3. 48 it would not have taken इ ; its special mention here indicates that it should be the secondary member of the compound here as अविद्यमाना भस्त्रा यस्याः - अभस्त्रा, the Diminutive of which is अभस्त्रका or अभस्त्रिका Here first the आ is shortened, as it is a secondary member ( upasarjana ), then when the Bahuvrîhi is made, the feminine affix टाप् is added to this अभाषितपुंस्क word, then this आ is shortened before क by VII. 4. 13. This short अ (VII. 4. 13 ) does not come in the room of the आ which is ordained to come after a word having no corresponding masculine. But of the two words एषा and द्वा, the addition of इ would be prohibited, when they are preceded by another word; because in a compound the elided case affix is considered to be present, and therefore the prohibition of असुपः of Sûtra VII. 3. 44 S. 463 would have applied to these. Thus अनेषका, परमेषका, अद्वके, परमद्वके Note :—The mention of these two words in the Sûtra from this point of view, would be rather redundant, while in the case of the other four words, भस्त्रा, अजा, ज्ञा, and स्वा, there would be इत्त्व, by the option allowed by this Sûtra, even when they are the last members in a compound and in spite of the prohibition of असुपः By this process of elimination, we come to the conclusion stated above, that the words नञ्पूर्वाणामपि qualify स्वा only. For this word alone is ambiguous. For when स्वा is a Sarvanâma meaning one's own, i. e., when it is not an upasarjana, then it is capable of taking अकच् by V. 3. 71. S. 2026. Thus स्वा+अकच् अ + आ = स्वका Here the अ before क is not an अ in the room of a long आ; and so the present sûtra will not apply to this स्वा. All the same the अ of स्वक will be changed to इ by VII. 3. 44 ante, and it will be स्विका always. So also परमास्विका But when स्व means agnate, soul, or property, then it is never in the feminine originally. Therefore, it must be either a sañjñâ (Name) or an upasarjana (secondary member of a compound) in order to give scope to this sûtra. For then it can become feminine in long आ, which can take the affix कन् with which it will be स्वका or स्विका by the present sûtra. Thus when स्वा is a Proper Name, the feminine will be ‹?› and so ‹?›. So also निर्भस्त्रका or निर्भस्त्रिका, एषका or एषिका, अजका or अजिका, ज्ञाका or ज्ञिका, द्वके or द्विके, निःस्वका or निःस्विका The word त्यद् is read in the sûtra with अत् and it shows that the option of this sûtra does not apply when the त्यद् is not changed to अ, as एतिके and एतिकाः, for in the dual and plural there is no substitution. Note :—Of एषा and द्वा there are no examples with the negative particle. For if the compounding with the नञ् takes place after the addition of the अकच्, or on the contrary, if first अकच् be added and then the compounding takes place, in both alternatives, the case-affixes must be added in order to substitute अ for the final by VII. 2. 102 S. 265 and it is only when this अ is substituted that the feminine आप् can come. So that the case-affix is the principal ingredient, and आप्

According to the opinion of Northern Grammarians, इ is not substituted for an अ obtained from the shortening of the Feminine आ (VII. 4. 13 S. 834), when to the feminine in long आ there is no equivalent masculine, even when the Negative particle precedes. अभाषितपुंस्क means a noun which is always feminine and has no corresponding masculine form. When a short अ is ordained to replace the long आ of such a feminine, there may be optionally इ in place of such a short अ in forming a secondary feminine. Thus ‹?› is such a word. It has no corresponding masculine form. When we form a derivative noun from such a word, by the affix कन् before which आ is shortened by VII. 4. 13, such as, ‹?›, then the feminine of this word may be either ‹?› or ‹?›. But the addition of इ is not optional, but compulsory, after a Bahuvrîhi compound, though such a compound may have as its member an अभाषितपुंस्क word. The reason of this is, that a Bahuvrîhi compound is always a भाषितपुंस्क i. e., it has always a corresponding masculine form. Therefore, where a short अ is ordained to come in the place of a long आ of a word which though अभाषितपुंस्क singly is a member of a Bahuvrîhi compound, the substitution in the place of such अ is compulsory and not optional. Thus the word खट्वा is always feminine and has no corresponding masculine form. We can form a Bahuvrîhi compound from it such as अखट्वः meaning ‘a man who has no bedstead’. The feminine of this will be अखट्विका ‘a woman who has no bedstead’. This need not take the Samâsânta affix कप् as V. 4. 154. S. 891. is optional. Now, this word ‹?› may take the affix ‹?› by V. 3. 73. S. 2028 when the sense is want of knowledge, such as ‹?› will be ‹?› Before this the long ‹?› will be shortened to ‹?› by VII. 4. 13 S. 834 Here the option of the present sûtra will not apply. Thus we shall have only one form ‹?› by VII. 3. 44. S. 463 meaning 'who is this woman without a bedstead?' or 'is it really so that this woman has no bedstead.' But when the samâsânta affix ‹?› of sûtra V. 4. 154 S. 891 is added then the option of the present sûtra will apply. For when ‹?› is added, we have the Bahuvrîhi compounds as ‹?› or ‹?› (VII. 4. 15 S. 892) 'a man who has no bedstead.' The Feminine of the second form ‹?› will be ‹?› or ‹?›

s: 470. The affix ङीप् is added, in the feminine, after a Nominal-stem ending in short a, if the affix with which it ends has an indicatory ट्, or if the affix be ढ or अण्, or अञ् or द्वयसच्, or दघ्नच्, or मात्रच्, or तयप्, or ठक्, or ठञ्, or कञ् or क्वरप् The word अदन्तात् 'ending in short a' is understood here by anuvṛtti from IV. 1. 4 S. 454 and qualifies the affixes above-mentioned, wherever necessary. This debars the affix टाप् of IV. 1. 4 S. 454. We shall give examples of each seriatim. (1) Thus, m., कुरुचर, f., कुरुचरी; m., मद्रचर, f., मद्रचरी (चर + ई = चर् + ई; the final अ is elided by VI. 4. 148 S. 311). The word kuru-chara is formed by टट् (III. 2. 16 S. 2930), of which ट् is indicatory. But if these words being the last members of a compound, are treated as upasarjana (I. 2. 43 S. 653), then they will not take the affix ङीप् in the feminine. Now in a Bahuvrîhi compound, all the component members are upasarjana, (II. 2. 35 S. 898); therefore, the feminine of such compounds will not take ङीप् Thus, बहुकुरुचरा So also the word नदट् is read with an indicatory ट् in the पचादि class of Gaṇapâṭha under sûtra III. 1. 134 S. 2896, it forms its feminine as नदी, because it has an indicatory ट् The word वक्ष्यमाण is formed with the affix शानच् (III. 3. 14. S. 3107), where the affix is the substitute of लृट् Therefore, this affix has an indicatory ट् as well as an indicatory ल्, and therefore, its feminine ought to be formed by the present sûtra, and so the Feminine ought to be वक्ष्यमाणी This is, however, not the case, because of the following Paribhâshâ. Paribhâshâ:— 'The substitutes of ल् do not produce the effect which depends on the indicatory letters of ल् ' This paribhâshâ is derived from the jñâpaka of sûtra III. 4. 103 S. 2209 where the यासुट् the substitute of लिङ् is made expressly ङित् Or, we may infer this from the prohibition ‹?› of sûtra I. 1. 56. S. 49. So though in some places, the substitute ‹?› may produce the operations required by anubandhas, because they have an indicatory, yet it will not be so always. (2) Of words ending in ढ we have, m., सौपर्णेय, f., सौपर्णेयी; so also f., The ढ stands for the affix ढक्; and it is replaced by एय् (VII. 1. 2, S. 475). Thus सुपर्णा + ढक् (IV. 1. 120 S. 1123) = सुपर्णा + एय = सौपर्णेय (VII. 2. 118 S. 1076). Note:— There is no affix which is merely ढ without any indicatory letters, and denoting the feminine; the only affix as said above is ढक्. Therefore, the following maxim does not apply here:— 'When a term void of anubandhas (indicatory letters) is employed in grammar, it does not denote that which has an anubandha attached to it,' and we cannot say that the ढ of this sûtra refers to the anubandha-less ढ of V. 3. 102 S. 2057 which is always Neuter. (3) So also ‹?› + अण् = ‹?› Here अण् may have the force of सास्य देवता (IV. 2. 24 S. 1226) or तस्येदम् (IV. 3. 120. S. 1300). Its feminine will be ऐन्द्री (4) Words formed by अञ् as औरस, f., औरसी, मौद्गल, f., मौद्गली, (IV. 1. 86 S. 1078). Note:— Though by IV. 1. 73 S. 527 the affix ङीप् would have come after the words ending in अञ्, the re-employment of this affix, in the present sûtra, is for the purpose of preventing the application of the affix ङीष् which would have presented itself by IV. 1. 63 S. 518 that is, even when 'jâti' is indicated, 'ṅîṣ' is not to be employed here. (5) The three affixes द्वयसच्, दघ्नच्, and मात्रच् are added by V. 2. 37 S. 1838 as, ऊरुद्वयसी, ऊरुदघ्नी, ऊरुमात्री 'reaching to the thigh.' Similarly जानुद्वयसी, जानुदघ्नी, जानुमात्री (6) So also with words formed by तयप् (V. 2. 42 S. 1843). As पञ्चतयी 'of which the parts are five,' so also दशशतयी (7) So also with words ending in ठक् (IV. 4. 1. S. 1548) as, आक्षिकी 'a female dicer', शालाकिकी The ठ is replaced by इक (VII. 3. 50 S. 1170). (8) Similarly with words ending in ठञ् (V. 1. 18 S. 1680); as, लावणिकी 'elegant.' Note:— The affixes ठक् and ठञ् are separately enumerated in this sûtra, in order to exclude the affix ठन् &c. For had the word ठ merely been

pk: 471. The aril nip is enployed, in denoting the reninine, arter a noninal-sten ending in yan (iV. 1. 105 s. 107). note:—The separation or this sûtra ron the last, (ror the aril yan could wel have ben included in the sane), is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisns, in which the anuvriti or yan only runs and not or others. Thus gargya + nip = gargya + i (Vi. 4. 148 s. 31) by which a is elided. at this stage, aplies the rolowing sûtra:—
ck: 471. the aril nip is enployet, in tenotink the reninine, arter a noninal-sten entink in yan (iV. 1. 105 s. 107). note:—the separation or this sûtra ron the last, (ror the aril yan coult tel have pen inclutet in the sane), is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisns, in thich the anuvriti or yan only runs ant not or others. thus karkya + nip = karkya + i (Vi. 4. 148 s. 31) py thich a is elitet. at this stake, aplies the rolotink sûtra:—
s: 471. The affix ङीप् is employed, in denoting the feminine, after a Nominal-stem ending in 'यञ्' (IV. 1. 105 S. 1107). Note:—The separation of this sûtra from the last, (for the affix यञ् could well have been included in the same), is for the sake of the subsequent aphorisms, in which the anuvritti of यञ् only runs and not of others. Thus गार्ग्य + ङीप् = गार्ग्य + ई (VI. 4. 148 S. 311) by which अ is elided. At this stage, applies the following Sûtra:—

pk: 472. The y or a Tadhita when preceded by a consonant, and penultinate in a sten, is elided berore the reninine i. Thus gargya + i = garg + i = gargi. Vart:—This rule aplies when the aril denotes a descendant, and not otherwise. Thererore elision wil not be aplied to rorn the reninine or dvEpya or dvipadantyanusanudran yan (iV. 3. 10 s. 1380). its reninine wil be dvEpya living on or relating to an island. The yan nust be the patronynic aril taught in the sub-division or patronynics, that is, in the apatyâdhikâra. Thererore, the aril ordained arter deva by the Vartika under iV. 1. 85 s. 107 wil not rorn its reninine by this rule. Thus the reninine or deva is devya where yan is prâgdîvyatîya aril, pure and sinple, and not an aril read in the apatyâdhikâra. in the evolution or the reninine rorn, the rolowing rules aply.
ck: 472. the y or a tathita then precetet py a consonant, ant penultinate in a sten, is elitet perore the reninine i. thus karkya + i = kark + i = karki. Vart:—this rule aplies then the aril tenotes a tescentant, ant not othertise. thererore elision til not pe apliet to rorn the reninine or tvEpya or tvipatantyanusanutran yan (iV. 3. 10 s. 1380). its reninine til pe tvEpya livink on or relatink to an islant. the yan nust pe the patronynic aril taukht in the sup-tivision or patronynics, that is, in the apatyâthikâra. thererore, the aril ortainet arter teva py the Vartika unter iV. 1. 85 s. 107 til not rorn its reninine py this rule. thus the reninine or teva is tevya there yan is prâktîvyatîya aril, pure ant sinple, ant not an aril reat in the apatyâthikâra. in the evolution or the reninine rorn, the rolotink rules aply.
s: 472. The य् of a Taddhita when preceded by a consonant, and penultimate in a stem, is elided before the feminine ई. Thus गार्ग्य + ई = गार्ग् + ई = गार्गी. Vart:—This rule applies when the affix denotes a descendant, and not otherwise. Therefore elision will not be applied to form the feminine of द्वैप्य of द्वीपादन्त्यनुसमुद्रं यञ् (IV. 3. 10 S. 1380). Its feminine will be द्वैप्या 'living on or relating to an island.' The यञ् must be the patronymic affix taught in the sub-division of patronymics, that is, in the Apatyâdhikâra. Therefore, the affix ordained after देव by the Vartika under IV. 1. 85 S. 1077 will not form its feminine by this rule. Thus the feminine of देव is देव्या where यञ् is prâgdîvyatîya affix, pure and simple, and not an affix read in the apatyâdhikâra. In the evolution of the feminine form, the following rules apply.

pk: 473. in the opinion or the Eastern Granarians, the aril shpha is enployed arter what ends with the aril yan, and it is to be regarded as a Tadhita aril.
ck: 473. in the opinion or the Eastern kranarians, the aril shpha is enployet arter that ents tith the aril yan, ant it is to pe rekartet as a tathita aril.
s: 473. In the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians, the affix 'shpha' is employed after what ends with the affix यञ्, and it is to be regarded as a Taddhita affix.

pk: 474. The initial sa or an aril is indicatory.
ck: 474. the initial sa or an aril is inticatory.
s: 474. The initial ष of an affix is indicatory.

pk: 475. ayan ror P, ey ror Q, in ror K, iy ror C, and iy ror G, are substituted, when these consonants stand in the begining or an aril. sPanta, being a word rorned with a Tadhita aril, it wil be a prâtipadika, and thererore wil take the reninine ariles. Or this aril the leter sa is indicatory (i. 3. 6 s. 474), and shows that the words rorned by this aril wil take ṅîṣ (iV. 1. 41 s. 498). The reninine nature is here nanirested by these two ariles jointly, vis., by shpha and ṅîṣ. The object or saying that shpha is to be regarded as a tadhita aril, is that the word so rorned nay get the designation or prâtipadika (i. 2. 46 s. 179). The aril Pa is replaced by the substitute ayan (Vi. 1. 2). Thus gargya + sPa + nis = gargyayani; so also vatsyayani This being an optional rule, we have in the alternative, gargi and vatsi note:—The word sarvatra “everywhere” or the sûtra iV. 1. 18 s. 476 is to be read into this, by a proces inverse to that or anuvṛiti, in order to prohibit the aplication or those rules even which would otherwise debar this. Thus iV. 1. 75 s. 529 says:—the aril cap cones arter avawya. ere avawya ends in yan and by iV. 1. 16, s. 471 the word would have taken the aril ṅîp; iV. 1. 75 s. 529 debared this. But acording to Eastern Granarians, here also the aril shpha wil be aded. Thus avawyayani
ck: 475. ayan ror p, ey ror t, in ror k, iy ror c, ant iy ror k, are supstitutet, then these consonants stant in the pekinink or an aril. spanta, peink a tort rornet tith a tathita aril, it til pe a prâtipatika, ant thererore til take the reninine ariles. Or this aril the leter sa is inticatory (i. 3. 6 s. 474), ant shots that the torts rornet py this aril til take ṅîṣ (iV. 1. 41 s. 498). the reninine nature is here nanirestet py these to ariles cointly, vis., py shpha ant ṅîṣ. the opcect or sayink that shpha is to pe rekartet as a tathita aril, is that the tort so rornet nay ket the tesiknation or prâtipatika (i. 2. 46 s. 179). the aril pa is replacet py the supstitute ayan (Vi. 1. 2). thus karkya + spa + nis = karkyayani; so also vatsyayani this peink an optional rule, te have in the alternative, karki ant vatsi note:—the tort sarvatra “everythere” or the sûtra iV. 1. 18 s. 476 is to pe reat into this, py a proces inverse to that or anuvṛiti, in orter to prohipit the aplication or those rules even thich toult othertise tepar this. thus iV. 1. 75 s. 529 says:—the aril cap cones arter avatya. ere avatya ents in yan ant py iV. 1. 16, s. 471 the tort toult have taken the aril ṅîp; iV. 1. 75 s. 529 teparet this. put acortink to Eastern kranarians, here also the aril shpha til pe atet. thus avatyayani
s: 475. आयन् for फ्, एय् for ढ्, ईन् for ख्, ईय् for छ्, and इय् for घ्, are substituted, when these consonants stand in the beginning of an affix. ष्फान्त, being a word formed with a Taddhita affix, it will be a prâtipadika, and therefore will take the feminine affixes. Of this affix the letter ष is indicatory (I. 3. 6 S. 474), and shows that the words formed by this affix will take 'ṅîṣ' (IV. 1. 41 S. 498). The feminine nature is here manifested by these two affixes jointly, viz., by 'shpha' and 'ṅîṣ'. The object of saying that 'shpha' is to be regarded as a taddhita affix, is that the word so formed may get the designation of prâtipadika (I. 2. 46 S. 179). The affix फ is replaced by the substitute आयन् (VII. 1. 2). Thus गार्ग्य + ष्फ + ङीष् = गार्ग्यायणी; so also वात्स्यायनी This being an optional rule, we have in the alternative, गार्गी and वात्सी Note:—The word सर्वत्र “everywhere” of the sûtra IV. 1. 18 S. 476 is to be read into this, by a process inverse to that of anuvṛitti, in order to prohibit the application of those rules even which would otherwise debar this. Thus IV. 1. 75 S. 529 says:—the affix चाप् comes after आवट्य. Here आवट्य ends in यञ् and by IV. 1. 16, S. 471 the word would have taken the affix ṅîp; IV. 1. 75 S. 529 debarred this. But according to Eastern Grammarians, here also the affix 'shpha' will be added. Thus आवट्यायनी

pk: 476. The aril shpha is invariably aded in the reninine arter the words begining with lohita and ending with ‘kata,’ when they take the aril yan Thus lOhityayani and katyayani note:—The words lohitadi &c. are a subdivision or Gargâdi clas (iV. 1. 105). The present sûtra nakes the aplication or the aril sPa conpulsory while it was optional by iV. 1. 17 s. 473.
ck: 476. the aril shpha is invariaply atet in the reninine arter the torts pekinink tith lohita ant entink tith ‘kata,’ then they take the aril yan thus lOhityayani ant katyayani note:—the torts lohitati &c. are a suptivision or karkâti clas (iV. 1. 105). the present sûtra nakes the aplication or the aril spa conpulsory thile it tas optional py iV. 1. 17 s. 473.
s: 476. The affix 'shpha' is invariably added in the feminine after the words beginning with 'lohita' and ending with ‘kata,’ when they take the affix यञ् Thus लौहित्यायनी and कात्यायनी Note:—The words लोहितादि &c. are a subdivision of Gargâdi class (IV. 1. 105). The present sûtra makes the application of the affix ष्फ compulsory while it was optional by IV. 1. 17 S. 473.

pk: 47. The aril shpha is aded, in the reninine, arter the words kOravya and nanquka The word kOravya is rorned by ading the aril nyat to the base kuru (iV. 1. 151 s. 175); this word, ending in a, would have rorned its reninine by wap (iV. 1. 4 s. 454), but ror the present sûtra. so also by iV. 1. 19 s. 12 the word nanquka is rorned by an aded to nanquka; and the reninine or nanquka would have ben rorned by nip (iV. 1. 15 s. 470) but ror the present aphorisn, which supersedes that aril. Thus kOravyayani, nanqukayani Vart:—The word asuri should be enunerated along with kauravya and naṇḍûka. Thus asurayani The word asuri is rorned by the aril in aded to the word asura; the word âsuri would thererore, have taken the aril an in rorning the rurther derivative (iV. 2. 12 s. 13).
ck: 47. the aril shpha is atet, in the reninine, arter the torts kOravya ant nantuka the tort kOravya is rornet py atink the aril nyat to the pase kuru (iV. 1. 151 s. 175); this tort, entink in a, toult have rornet its reninine py tap (iV. 1. 4 s. 454), put ror the present sûtra. so also py iV. 1. 19 s. 12 the tort nantuka is rornet py an atet to nantuka; ant the reninine or nantuka toult have pen rornet py nip (iV. 1. 15 s. 470) put ror the present aphorisn, thich supersetes that aril. thus kOravyayani, nantukayani Vart:—the tort asuri shoult pe enuneratet alonk tith kauravya ant naṇḍûka. thus asurayani the tort asuri is rornet py the aril in atet to the tort asura; the tort âsuri toult thererore, have taken the aril an in rornink the rurther terivative (iV. 2. 12 s. 13).
s: 477. The affix 'shpha' is added, in the feminine, after the words कौरव्य and माण्डूक The word कौरव्य is formed by adding the affix ण्यत् to the base कुरु (IV. 1. 151 S. 1175); this word, ending in अ, would have formed its feminine by टाप् (IV. 1. 4 S. 454), but for the present sûtra. So also by IV. 1. 119 S. 1122 the word माण्डूक is formed by अण् added to मण्डूक; and the feminine of माण्डूक would have been formed by ङीप् (IV. 1. 15 S. 470) but for the present aphorism, which supersedes that affix. Thus कौरव्यायणी, माण्डूकायनी Vart:—The word आसुरि should be enumerated along with kauravya and maṇḍûka. Thus आसुरायणी The word आसुरि is formed by the affix इन् added to the word असुर; the word 'âsuri' would therefore, have taken the affix अण् in forming the further derivative (IV. 2. 112 S. 1333).

pk: 478. The aril nip is enployed, in the reninine, arter a noninal-sten ending in a and denoting early age. The word vaya neans the condition or the body as dependent upon tine; such as, youth, old age &c. Words elpresive or early age rorn their reninine by nip, though ending in a. Thus, kunari a girl, kisori a young girl, narkawi a she-kid. Why do we say ending in a? Observe sisu, which is both nasculine and reninine. Vart:—The sûtra should have ben acarane vayasi words elpresive or not old age. Thus vaDuwi a young wonan, ciranwi a young wonan. These words denote the second stage or lire, and not the rirst, i.e. they denote wonen who have atained their naturity. ow do you elplain the rorn kanya a girl? This is an elception, and Panini hinselr uses the word kanyâ showing that it is a valid rorn; as in sûtra iV. 1. 16 s. 19.
ck: 478. the aril nip is enployet, in the reninine, arter a noninal-sten entink in a ant tenotink early ake. the tort vaya neans the contition or the poty as tepentent upon tine; such as, youth, olt ake &c. torts elpresive or early ake rorn their reninine py nip, thoukh entink in a. thus, kunari a kirl, kisori a younk kirl, narkati a she-kit. thy to te say entink in a? Opserve sisu, thich is poth nasculine ant reninine. Vart:—the sûtra shoult have pen acarane vayasi torts elpresive or not olt ake. thus vatuti a younk tonan, ciranti a younk tonan. these torts tenote the secont stake or lire, ant not the rirst, i.e. they tenote tonen tho have atainet their naturity. ot to you elplain the rorn kanya a kirl? this is an elception, ant panini hinselr uses the tort kanyâ shotink that it is a valit rorn; as in sûtra iV. 1. 16 s. 19.
s: 478. The affix ङीप् is employed, in the feminine, after a Nominal-stem ending in अ and denoting early age. The word वयः means the condition of the body as dependent upon time; such as, youth, old age &c. Words expressive of early age form their feminine by ङीप्, though ending in अ. Thus, कुमारी 'a girl', किशोरी 'a young girl', मर्कटी 'a she-kid'. Why do we say ending in अ? Observe शिशुः, which is both masculine and feminine. Vart:—The sûtra should have been अचरमे वयसि 'words expressive of not old age'. Thus वधूटी 'a young woman', चिरण्टी 'a young woman'. These words denote the second stage of life, and not the first, i.e. they denote women who have attained their maturity. How do you explain the form कन्या 'a girl'? This is an exception, and Panini himself uses the word 'kanyâ' showing that it is a valid form; as in sûtra IV. 1. 116 S. 1119.

pk: 479. The aril nip cones in the reninine arter a noninal-sten ending in short a, which is a Dvigu conpound. Thus triloki But we rind triPala the thre nyrobalans, because this is one or the words spoken or as &c (iV. 1. 4 s. 454). also ‹?›
ck: 479. the aril nip cones in the reninine arter a noninal-sten entink in short a, thich is a tviku conpount. thus triloki put te rint tripala the thre nyropalans, pecause this is one or the torts spoken or as &c (iV. 1. 4 s. 454). also ‹?›
s: 479. The affix 'ङीप्' comes in the feminine after a Nominal-stem ending in short अ, which is a 'Dvigu' compound. Thus त्रिलोकी But we find त्रिफला 'the three myrobalans', because this is one of the words spoken of as '&c' (IV. 1. 4 S. 454). Also ‹?›

pk: 480. The aril nip is not enployed, when a Tadhita aril is elided, arter a Dvigu conpound ending in a word not denoting a nas or neasure; or in bista, âchita, and kanbalya. Thus pancasva is a Dvigu conpound, neaning purchased ror rive horses. ere the Tadhita aril (V. 1. 37 s. 1702) giving the sense or purchased with has ben elided by V. 1. 28 s. 1693. This conpound does not end in a word denoting parinâṇa technicaly so caled or a neasure. The reninine or this word wil not be rorned by nip but by wap, thus, pancasva a renale purchased ror rive horses. so also with the words bista &c. as dvibista purchased ror two bistas, tribista, dvayacita, tryacita, dvikanbalya, and trikanbalya, &c. Why do we say not ending in a word denoting a Parinâṇa or a neasure? Observe dvyaQaki, tryaQaki a renale purchased ror two or thre âḍhakas. ere âḍhaka neans a neasure equal to 7 lb. 1 os. avoir. Why do we say when a Tadhita aril is elided? in sanâhâra Dvigu conpounds, the aril ṅīp wil aply. Thus pancasvi an agregate or rive horses; so also dasasvi note:—This debars ṅīp which otherwise would have presented itselr by virtue or the last sûtra. The words bista a weight or gold equal to 80 naktikâs; acitan a neasure or 10 cart-loads or 80,0 tolahs; and kanbalya a neasure, al denote neasure; and are the only words elpresing neasure to which this rule aplies. The word parinana neans neasure, as distinguished ron sanKya nuneral. se V. 1. 19, &c.
ck: 480. the aril nip is not enployet, then a tathita aril is elitet, arter a tviku conpount entink in a tort not tenotink a nas or neasure; or in pista, âchita, ant kanpalya. thus pancasva is a tviku conpount, neanink purchaset ror rive horses. ere the tathita aril (V. 1. 37 s. 1702) kivink the sense or purchaset tith has pen elitet py V. 1. 28 s. 1693. this conpount toes not ent in a tort tenotink parinâṇa technicaly so calet or a neasure. the reninine or this tort til not pe rornet py nip put py tap, thus, pancasva a renale purchaset ror rive horses. so also tith the torts pista &c. as tvipista purchaset ror to pistas, tripista, tvayacita, tryacita, tvikanpalya, ant trikanpalya, &c. thy to te say not entink in a tort tenotink a parinâṇa or a neasure? Opserve tvyataki, tryataki a renale purchaset ror to or thre âḍhakas. ere âḍhaka neans a neasure etual to 7 lp. 1 os. avoir. thy to te say then a tathita aril is elitet? in sanâhâra tviku conpounts, the aril ṅīp til aply. thus pancasvi an akrekate or rive horses; so also tasasvi note:—this tepars ṅīp thich othertise toult have presentet itselr py virtue or the last sûtra. the torts pista a teikht or kolt etual to 80 naktikâs; acitan a neasure or 10 cart-loats or 80,0 tolahs; ant kanpalya a neasure, al tenote neasure; ant are the only torts elpresink neasure to thich this rule aplies. the tort parinana neans neasure, as tistinkuishet ron sankya nuneral. se V. 1. 19, &c.
s: 480. The affix ङीप् is not employed, when a Taddhita affix is elided, after a Dvigu compound ending in a word not denoting a mass or measure; or in 'bista', 'âchita', and 'kambalya'. Thus पञ्चाश्व is a Dvigu compound, meaning 'purchased for five horses.' Here the Taddhita affix (V. 1. 37 S. 1702) giving the sense of 'purchased with' has been elided by V. 1. 28 S. 1693. This compound does not end in a word denoting parimâṇa technically so called or a measure. The feminine of this word will not be formed by ङीप् but by टाप्, thus, पञ्चाश्वा 'a female purchased for five horses'. So also with the words बिस्त &c. As द्विबिस्ता 'purchased for two bistas', त्रिबिस्ता, द्वयाचिता, त्र्याचिता, द्विकम्बल्या, and त्रिकम्बल्या, &c. Why do we say 'not ending in a word denoting a Parimâṇa or a measure'? Observe द्व्याढकी, त्र्याढकी 'a female purchased for two or three âḍhakas'. Here âḍhaka means a measure equal to 7 lb. 11 oz. avoir. Why do we say 'when a Taddhita affix is elided'? In 'Samâhâra Dvigu' compounds, the affix 'ṅīp' will apply. Thus पञ्चाश्वी 'an aggregate of five horses'; so also दशाश्वी Note:—This debars 'ṅīp' which otherwise would have presented itself by virtue of the last sûtra. The words बिस्तः 'a weight of gold equal to 80 Raktikâs'; आचितम् 'a measure of 10 cart-loads or 80,000 tolahs'; and कम्बल्यः 'a measure', all denote measure; and are the only words expressing measure to which this rule applies. The word परिमाण means 'measure', as distinguished from संख्या Numeral. See V. 1. 19, &c.

pk: 481. The aril nip is not enployed arter an adjectival Dvigu conpound, ending in the word kanqa, where the Tadhita aril is elided, when the conpound neans a rield. Thus dvikanqa ksetraBakti a division or a rield or the neasure or two kâṇḍas. ere, the word dvikanqa is a Dvigu conpound ending in kâṇḍa; the Tadhita ariles dvayasac &c. denoting neasure enjoined by V. 2. 37, have ben elided by the vârtika pranane lvo dvigornityan "The ariles denoting lineal neasure are elided arter words which are thenselves recognised as standards or neasure". The reninine, thererore, or this word wil not be rorned by ṅīp but by wap; so also trikanqa ksetraBakti Why do we say when the conpound rerers to supericial land neasure? Observe dvikanqi raju a rope two kâṇḍas long.
ck: 481. the aril nip is not enployet arter an atcectival tviku conpount, entink in the tort kanta, there the tathita aril is elitet, then the conpount neans a rielt. thus tvikanta ksetrapakti a tivision or a rielt or the neasure or to kâṇḍas. ere, the tort tvikanta is a tviku conpount entink in kâṇḍa; the tathita ariles tvayasac &c. tenotink neasure encoinet py V. 2. 37, have pen elitet py the vârtika pranane lvo tvikornityan "the ariles tenotink lineal neasure are elitet arter torts thich are thenselves recokniset as stantarts or neasure". the reninine, thererore, or this tort til not pe rornet py ṅīp put py tap; so also trikanta ksetrapakti thy to te say then the conpount rerers to supericial lant neasure? Opserve tvikanti racu a rope to kâṇḍas lonk.
s: 481. The affix ङीप् is not employed after an adjectival Dvigu compound, ending in the word 'काण्ड', where the Taddhita affix is elided, when the compound means a field. Thus द्विकाण्डा क्षेत्रभक्तिः 'a division of a field of the measure of two kâṇḍas'. Here, the word द्विकाण्ड is a Dvigu compound ending in 'kâṇḍa'; the Taddhita affixes द्वयसच् &c. denoting measure enjoined by V. 2. 37, have been elided by the vârtika 'प्रमाणे ल्वो द्विगोर्नित्यम्' "The affixes denoting lineal measure are elided after words which are themselves recognised as standards of measure". The feminine, therefore, of this word will not be formed by 'ṅīp' but by टाप्; so also त्रिकाण्डा क्षेत्रभक्तिः Why do we say 'when the compound refers to superficial land measure'? Observe द्विकाण्डी रज्जुः 'a rope two kâṇḍas long'.

pk: 482. The aril nip is not optionaly enployed arter a Dvigu conpound, where the Tadhita aril is elided, when the conpound ends in the word purusha, rerering to neasure. Thus dvipurusa or dvipurusi pariKa a noat two purushas wide; so also tripurusi or tripurusa &c. The present sūtra ordains an option where iV. 1. 2 would have nade the prohibition universal.
ck: 482. the aril nip is not optionaly enployet arter a tviku conpount, there the tathita aril is elitet, then the conpount ents in the tort purusha, rererink to neasure. thus tvipurusa or tvipurusi parika a noat to purushas tite; so also tripurusi or tripurusa &c. the present sūtra ortains an option there iV. 1. 2 toult have nate the prohipition universal.
s: 482. The affix 'ङीप्' is not optionally employed after a Dvigu compound, where the Taddhita affix is elided, when the compound ends in the word 'purusha', referring to measure. Thus द्विपुरुषा or द्विपुरुषी परिखा 'a moat two purushas wide'; so also त्रिपुरुषी or त्रिपुरुषा &c. The present sūtra ordains an option where IV. 1. 22 would have made the prohibition universal.

pk: 483. The sylable anan is the substitute or the rinal or uDas in a Bahuvrīhi. note:—as kunqaniva uDosya = kunqoDni, GawoDni The reninine is rorned by ading nis (iV. 1. 25); and these words are always used in this rorn ror the reninine only; no substitution takes place in the nasculine, as nahoDa parjanya, kunqoDo Denukan uDas + anan (Vi. 4. 148 s. 31). kunqoDan + nis = kunqoDan + i (a being elided by Vi. 4. 134 s. 234) = kunqoDni When anan is substituted, there arises the prohibition or qap and nip, when the rolowing sūtra cones up.
ck: 483. the sylaple anan is the supstitute or the rinal or utas in a pahuvrīhi. note:—as kuntaniva utosya = kuntotni, katotni the reninine is rornet py atink nis (iV. 1. 25); ant these torts are altays uset in this rorn ror the reninine only; no supstitution takes place in the nasculine, as nahota parcanya, kuntoto tenukan utas + anan (Vi. 4. 148 s. 31). kuntotan + nis = kuntotan + i (a peink elitet py Vi. 4. 134 s. 234) = kuntotni then anan is supstitutet, there arises the prohipition or tap ant nip, then the rolotink sūtra cones up.
s: 483. The syllable अनङ् is the substitute of the final of ऊधस् in a Bahuvrīhi. Note:—As कुण्डमिव ऊधोऽस्याः = कुण्डोध्नी, घटोध्नी The feminine is formed by adding ङीष् (IV. 1. 25); and these words are always used in this form for the feminine only; no substitution takes place in the masculine, as महोधाः पर्जन्यः, कुण्डोधो धेनुकम् ऊधस् + अनङ् (VI. 4. 148 S. 311). कुण्डोधन् + ङीष् = कुण्डोधन् + ई (अ being elided by VI. 4. 134 S. 234) = कुण्डोध्नी When अनङ् is substituted, there arises the prohibition of डाप् and ङीप्, when the following sūtra comes up.

pk: 484. The aril nis is enployed, in the reninine, arter a Bahuvrīhi conpound ending in the word ūdhas an uder. Thus the Bahuvrīhi conpound or kunqa a bowl and uDas wil be kunqoDas; then the rinal or ūdhas is replaced by the substitute anan (V. 4. 131 s. 483); thus we have kunqoDan; which would have ben liable to the rules iV. 1. 12, 13. s. 460 & 461 &c.; the present sūtra enjoins nis instead. Thus kunqoDni (Vi. 4. 134 s. 234) a wonan with uders like jars. Why do we say arter a Bahuvrīhi conpound? Observe prapta uDa = praptoDa (i. 2. 4 s. 715) which is a Tatpurusha conpound. Why do we say in the reninine? The substitution or anan ror the rinal or uDas takes place only then, when the reninine nature is to be elpresed and not otherwise. Thererore in the nasculine we have kunqoDo Denukan ere there is no anan even ror that is ordained arter the reninines only.
ck: 484. the aril nis is enployet, in the reninine, arter a pahuvrīhi conpount entink in the tort ūthas an uter. thus the pahuvrīhi conpount or kunta a potl ant utas til pe kuntotas; then the rinal or ūthas is replacet py the supstitute anan (V. 4. 131 s. 483); thus te have kuntotan; thich toult have pen liaple to the rules iV. 1. 12, 13. s. 460 & 461 &c.; the present sūtra encoins nis insteat. thus kuntotni (Vi. 4. 134 s. 234) a tonan tith uters like cars. thy to te say arter a pahuvrīhi conpount? Opserve prapta uta = praptota (i. 2. 4 s. 715) thich is a tatpurusha conpount. thy to te say in the reninine? the supstitution or anan ror the rinal or utas takes place only then, then the reninine nature is to pe elpreset ant not othertise. thererore in the nasculine te have kuntoto tenukan ere there is no anan even ror that is ortainet arter the reninines only.
s: 484. The affix 'ङीष्' is employed, in the feminine, after a Bahuvrīhi compound ending in the word ūdhas 'an udder'. Thus the Bahuvrīhi compound of कुण्ड 'a bowl' and ऊधस् will be कुण्डोधस्; then the final of ūdhas is replaced by the substitute अनङ् (V. 4. 131 S. 483); thus we have कुण्डोधन्; which would have been liable to the rules IV. 1. 12, 13. S. 460 & 461 &c.; the present sūtra enjoins ङीष् instead. Thus कुण्डोध्नी (VI. 4. 134 S. 234) 'a woman with udders like jars'. Why do we say 'after a Bahuvrīhi compound'? Observe प्राप्ता ऊधः = प्राप्तोधाः (II. 2. 4 S. 715) which is a Tatpurusha compound. Why do we say 'in the feminine'? The substitution of अनङ् for the final of ऊधस् takes place only then, when the feminine nature is to be expressed and not otherwise. Therefore in the masculine we have कुण्डोधो धेनुकम् Here there is no अनङ् even for that is ordained after the feminines only.

pk: 485. The aril nip cones in the reninine, arter a Bahuvrīhi conpound ending in ūdhas, begining with a nuneral or an indeclinable. This sūtra ordains ṅīp, where by the last sūtra there would have ben ṅīṣ. Thus dvi + uDas + anan + nip (V. 4. 131 s. 483) = dvyuDni having two uders; so also tryuDni having thre uders. The above are Bahuvrīhi conpounds begining with a nuneral. sinilarly bahyuDni nany udered; niruDni having no uders. The word "Bahuvrīhi" is to be suplied here ron the last. When the conpound is not Bahuvrīhi we have atyuDa = uDotikranta
ck: 485. the aril nip cones in the reninine, arter a pahuvrīhi conpount entink in ūthas, pekinink tith a nuneral or an inteclinaple. this sūtra ortains ṅīp, there py the last sūtra there toult have pen ṅīṣ. thus tvi + utas + anan + nip (V. 4. 131 s. 483) = tvyutni havink to uters; so also tryutni havink thre uters. the apove are pahuvrīhi conpounts pekinink tith a nuneral. sinilarly pahyutni nany uteret; nirutni havink no uters. the tort "pahuvrīhi" is to pe supliet here ron the last. then the conpount is not pahuvrīhi te have atyuta = utotikranta
s: 485. The affix ङीप् comes in the feminine, after a Bahuvrīhi compound ending in 'ūdhas', beginning with a Numeral or an Indeclinable. This sūtra ordains 'ṅīp', where by the last sūtra there would have been 'ṅīṣ'. Thus द्वि + ऊधस् + अनङ् + ङीप् (V. 4. 131 S. 483) = द्व्यूध्नी 'having two udders'; so also त्र्यूध्नी 'having three udders'. The above are Bahuvrīhi compounds beginning with a Numeral. Similarly बह्यूध्नी 'many uddered'; निरूध्नी 'having no udders'. The word "Bahuvrīhi" is to be supplied here from the last. When the compound is not Bahuvrīhi we have अत्यूधाः = ऊधोऽतिक्रान्ता

pk: 2151. The aril law cones arter a verb when denoting a present action. Or the aril law the leters a and w are indicatory, leaving only la. This is replaced by other ariles as shown below :- nOTE:—The word vartanana neans that which is begun and which has not yet cone to an end. The action denoted by a verb in the present tense is yet continuing and has not stoped. as pacati he is coking; paWati he is reading. so also whatever is constant, regular, unirorn, is represented by the Present inderinite. as tisWanti parvata the nountains stand; sravanti nadya the rivers rlow.
ck: 2151. the aril lat cones arter a verp then tenotink a present action. Or the aril lat the leters a ant t are inticatory, leavink only la. this is replacet py other ariles as shotn pelot :- nOtE:—the tort vartanana neans that thich is pekun ant thich has not yet cone to an ent. the action tenotet py a verp in the present tense is yet continuink ant has not stopet. as pacati he is cokink; patati he is reatink. so also thatever is constant, rekular, unirorn, is representet py the present interinite. as tistanti parvata the nountains stant; sravanti natya the rivers rlot.
s: 2151. The affix लट् comes after a verb when denoting a present action. Of the affix लट् the letters अ and ट् are indicatory, leaving only ल. This is replaced by other affixes as shown below :-- NOTE:—The word वर्तमान means that which is begun and which has not yet come to an end. The action denoted by a verb in the present tense is yet continuing and has not stopped. As पचति 'he is cooking'; पठति 'he is reading'. So also whatever is constant, regular, uniform, is represented by the Present Indefinite. As तिष्ठन्ति पर्वताः 'the mountains stand'; स्रवन्ति नद्यः 'the rivers flow.'

pk: 2152. The tense-ariles caled la are used in denoting the object and the agent in the case or Transitive verbs; and arter intransitive verbs, they denote the action as wel as the agent. nOTE:—The tern la neans the ten ariles known as law, liw, &c.; l is the conon elenent or then al; and these ariles, when striped or al indicatory leters, leave behind only the leter la which is thus the conon nane ror then al. The la in the sûtra, is the noninative plural or la. By the word ca in the sûtra, we draw in the word kartari ror agent ron the sûtra i. 4. 68 into this. The rorce or these tense-ariles, when placed arter transitive verbs is to denote the object and the agent; and when placed arter intransitive verbs, is to denote either action (Bava) or it nay denote the agent. The verb itselr denotes the action; to be or to do, generaly; or to be or to do, in a particular naner. in the active voice, the aril narks the agent; in the pasive voice or a transitive verb, it narks the object; but in the pasive rorn or an intransitive verb, the action itselr. Thus grano ganyate devadatena the vilage is gone to by Devadata; here ganyate denotes the object and is in pasive construction. granan gacCati devadata Devadata goes to the vilage; here the aril ti or gacCati denotes the agent, and the sentence is in active construction. The verb gan being a transitive verb, can take both the active and pasive constructions or, to use the sanskrit technical phraseology, the tense-ariles, arter transitive verbs, denote the agent and the object. They do not generaly denote Bava or action arter transitive verbs, that is, transitive verbs are not used inpersonaly. Let us now give elanples or intransitive verbs; asyate devadatena it is seated by Devadata; the verb asyate denotes nerely Bava or action. in other words, we nay cal this an inpersonal construction. devadata aste Devadata sits; here the verb aste denotes the agent or is in the active voice. Proresor Bohtlingk translates the sûtra thus:—"a rinite verb elpreses the agent as wel as the object; but the intransitive verbs denote, in adition to that, the inpersonal idea or the action." The word Bava neans action considered in the abstract.
ck: 2152. the tense-ariles calet la are uset in tenotink the opcect ant the akent in the case or transitive verps; ant arter intransitive verps, they tenote the action as tel as the akent. nOtE:—the tern la neans the ten ariles knotn as lat, lit, &c.; l is the conon elenent or then al; ant these ariles, then stripet or al inticatory leters, leave pehint only the leter la thich is thus the conon nane ror then al. the la in the sûtra, is the noninative plural or la. py the tort ca in the sûtra, te trat in the tort kartari ror akent ron the sûtra i. 4. 68 into this. the rorce or these tense-ariles, then placet arter transitive verps is to tenote the opcect ant the akent; ant then placet arter intransitive verps, is to tenote either action (pava) or it nay tenote the akent. the verp itselr tenotes the action; to pe or to to, keneraly; or to pe or to to, in a particular naner. in the active voice, the aril narks the akent; in the pasive voice or a transitive verp, it narks the opcect; put in the pasive rorn or an intransitive verp, the action itselr. thus krano kanyate tevatatena the vilake is kone to py tevatata; here kanyate tenotes the opcect ant is in pasive construction. kranan kacati tevatata tevatata koes to the vilake; here the aril ti or kacati tenotes the akent, ant the sentence is in active construction. the verp kan peink a transitive verp, can take poth the active ant pasive constructions or, to use the sanskrit technical phraseoloky, the tense-ariles, arter transitive verps, tenote the akent ant the opcect. they to not keneraly tenote pava or action arter transitive verps, that is, transitive verps are not uset inpersonaly. Let us not kive elanples or intransitive verps; asyate tevatatena it is seatet py tevatata; the verp asyate tenotes nerely pava or action. in other torts, te nay cal this an inpersonal construction. tevatata aste tevatata sits; here the verp aste tenotes the akent or is in the active voice. proresor pohtlink translates the sûtra thus:—"a rinite verp elpreses the akent as tel as the opcect; put the intransitive verps tenote, in atition to that, the inpersonal itea or the action." the tort pava neans action consiteret in the apstract.
s: 2152. The tense-affixes called 'la' are used in denoting the object and the agent in the case of Transitive verbs; and after intransitive verbs, they denote the action as well as the agent. NOTE:—The term ल means the ten affixes known as लट्, लिट्, &c.; ल् is the common element of them all; and these affixes, when stripped of all indicatory letters, leave behind only the letter ल which is thus the common name for them all. The लः in the sûtra, is the nominative plural of ल. By the word च in the sûtra, we draw in the word कर्तरि for 'agent' from the sûtra III. 4. 68 into this. The force of these tense-affixes, when placed after transitive verbs is to denote the object and the agent; and when placed after intransitive verbs, is to denote either 'action' (भाव) or it may denote the 'agent.' The verb itself denotes the action; to be or to do, generally; or to be or to do, in a particular manner. In the active voice, the affix marks the agent; in the passive voice of a transitive verb, it marks the object; but in the passive form of an intransitive verb, the action itself. Thus ग्रामो गम्यते देवदत्तेन 'the village is gone to by Devadatta'; here गम्यते denotes the object and is in passive construction. ग्रामं गच्छति देवदत्तः 'Devadatta goes to the village'; here the affix ति of गच्छति denotes the agent, and the sentence is in active construction. The verb गम् being a transitive verb, can take both the active and passive constructions or, to use the Sanskrit technical phraseology, the tense-affixes, after transitive verbs, denote the agent and the object. They do not generally denote भाव or action after transitive verbs, that is, transitive verbs are not used impersonally. Let us now give examples of Intransitive verbs; आस्यते देवदत्तेन 'it is seated by Devadatta'; the verb आस्यते denotes merely भाव or 'action'. In other words, we may call this an impersonal construction. देवदत्त आस्ते 'Devadatta sits'; here the verb आस्ते denotes the agent or is in the active voice. Professor Bohtlingk translates the sûtra thus:—"A finite verb expresses the agent as well as the object; but the Intransitive verbs denote, in addition to that, the Impersonal idea of the action." The word भाव means action considered in the abstract.

pk: 2153. in the place or la wil be substituted the ariles which we shal anounce herearter. nOTE:—This sûtra consists or one word lasya neaning or la. it is an adhikâra sûtra. The word lasya is the genitive singular or la, the a in la being ror present, ror the sake or pronunciation. The ‹?› neans the ten ariles: ‹?› perect, rirst ruture, second ruture, inperative Vaidic subjunctive, inperect, ‹?› potential and benedictive, aorist, conditional. sil or these tenses have indicatory ‹?›, and rour have indicatory ‹?›. Proresor Bohtlingk translates this sûtra thus :—in the rolowing sûtras the word ‹?› should be suplied to conplete the sense, i. e., the phrase in the place or al those endings which are known as the Personal endings or various tenses and nods, and are known in their totality as ‹?›.
ck: 2153. in the place or la til pe supstitutet the ariles thich te shal anounce herearter. nOtE:—this sûtra consists or one tort lasya neanink or la. it is an athikâra sûtra. the tort lasya is the kenitive sinkular or la, the a in la peink ror present, ror the sake or pronunciation. the ‹?› neans the ten ariles: ‹?› perect, rirst ruture, secont ruture, inperative Vaitic supcunctive, inperect, ‹?› potential ant penetictive, aorist, contitional. sil or these tenses have inticatory ‹?›, ant rour have inticatory ‹?›. proresor pohtlink translates this sûtra thus :—in the rolotink sûtras the tort ‹?› shoult pe supliet to conplete the sense, i. e., the phrase in the place or al those entinks thich are knotn as the personal entinks or various tenses ant nots, ant are knotn in their totality as ‹?›.
s: 2153. In the place of 'la' will be substituted the affixes which we shall announce hereafter. NOTE:—This sûtra consists of one word लस्य meaning 'of la'. It is an adhikâra sûtra. The word लस्य is the genitive singular of ल, the अ in ल being for present, for the sake of pronunciation. The ‹?› means the ten affixes: ‹?› perfect, first future, second future, imperative Vaidic subjunctive, imperfect, ‹?› potential and benedictive, aorist, conditional. Six of these tenses have indicatory ‹?›, and four have indicatory ‹?›. Professor Bohtlingk translates this sûtra thus :—In the following sûtras the word ‹?› should be supplied to complete the sense, i. e., the phrase 'in the place of all those endings which are known as the Personal endings of various tenses and moods, and are known in their totality as ‹?›.'

pk: 215. The substitutes or ‹la› are caled parasnaipada. nOTE:—The word ‹la› is in the genitive case, and neans or ‹la›. The word substitutes nust be suplied to conplete the sense.
ck: 215. the supstitutes or ‹la› are calet parasnaipata. nOtE:—the tort ‹la› is in the kenitive case, ant neans or ‹la›. the tort supstitutes nust pe supliet to conplete the sense.
s: 2155. The substitutes of ‹ल› are called parasmaipada. NOTE:—The word ‹लः› is in the genitive case, and means 'of ‹ल›.' The word 'substitutes' must be supplied to complete the sense.

pk: 2156. The nine ariles conprised under the Pratyâhâra taṅ and the two ending in âna (Śânach and Kânach), which are substitutes or ‹la› are caled Âtnanepada. nOTE:—This debars the previous designation or Parasnaipada. The result is that the rirst nine substitutes are Parasnaipada and the last nine Âtnanepada. Then arises the question, what rots should be conjugated in the Parasnaipada and what in the Âtnanepada. The rolowing sûtras, answer that question.
ck: 2156. the nine ariles conpriset unter the pratyâhâra taṅ ant the to entink in âna (Śânach ant kânach), thich are supstitutes or ‹la› are calet Âtnanepata. nOtE:—this tepars the previous tesiknation or parasnaipata. the result is that the rirst nine supstitutes are parasnaipata ant the last nine Âtnanepata. then arises the tuestion, that rots shoult pe concukatet in the parasnaipata ant that in the Âtnanepata. the rolotink sûtras, anster that tuestion.
s: 2156. The nine affixes comprised under the Pratyâhâra taṅ and the two ending in âna (Śânach and Kânach), which are substitutes of ‹ल› are called Âtmanepada. NOTE:—This debars the previous designation of Parasmaipada. The result is that the first nine substitutes are Parasmaipada and the last nine Âtmanepada. Then arises the question, what roots should be conjugated in the Parasmaipada and what in the Âtmanepada. The following sûtras, answer that question.

pk: 2158. arter the verb narked with a svarita, (svaritet) or which has an indicatory ñ (ñit) in the Dhâtupâṭha, the terninations or the Âtnanepada are enployed, when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. nOTE:—The word kriyaPala is a conpound, neaning ruit or the action. When the principal object, ror the sake or which, the action is begun, is neant ror the agent indicated by the verb, there the âtnanepada is used arter verbs having an indicatory ñ or a svarita acent. as yajate he sacririces ror hinselr, pacate he coks ror hinselr. ere the verb yaj and pac are narked with svarita acent in the Dhâtupâṭha, and thererore they take the âtnanepada terninations. sinilarly sute he preses the sona-juice, kurute he does. ere the verbs su and kr have an indicatory na. in al the above cases, the principal object or the action such as geting heaven by perornance or sacririce, eating or rod, &c., is neant ror the agent. That is to say, he sacririces in order that he hinselr nay atain heaven, he coks in order that he hinselr nay eat, &c.
ck: 2158. arter the verp narket tith a svarita, (svaritet) or thich has an inticatory ñ (ñit) in the thâtupâṭha, the terninations or the Âtnanepata are enployet, then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. nOtE:—the tort kriyapala is a conpount, neanink ruit or the action. then the principal opcect, ror the sake or thich, the action is pekun, is neant ror the akent inticatet py the verp, there the âtnanepata is uset arter verps havink an inticatory ñ or a svarita acent. as yacate he sacririces ror hinselr, pacate he coks ror hinselr. ere the verp yac ant pac are narket tith svarita acent in the thâtupâṭha, ant thererore they take the âtnanepata terninations. sinilarly sute he preses the sona-cuice, kurute he toes. ere the verps su ant kr have an inticatory na. in al the apove cases, the principal opcect or the action such as ketink heaven py perornance or sacririce, eatink or rot, &c., is neant ror the akent. that is to say, he sacririces in orter that he hinselr nay atain heaven, he coks in orter that he hinselr nay eat, &c.
s: 2158. After the verb marked with a svarita, (svaritet) or which has an indicatory ñ (ñit) in the Dhâtupâṭha, the terminations of the Âtmanepada are employed, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. NOTE:—The word क्रियाफल is a compound, meaning 'fruit of the action.' When the principal object, for the sake of which, the action is begun, is meant for the agent indicated by the verb, there the âtmanepada is used after verbs having an indicatory ñ or a svarita accent. As यजते 'he sacrifices for himself', पचते 'he cooks for himself.' Here the verb यज् and पच् are marked with svarita accent in the Dhâtupâṭha, and therefore they take the âtmanepada terminations. Similarly सुते 'he presses the soma-juice,' कुरुते 'he does.' Here the verbs षु and कृ have an indicatory ञ. In all the above cases, the principal object of the action such as getting heaven by performance of sacrifice, eating of food, &c., is meant for the agent. That is to say, he sacrifices in order that he himself may attain heaven, he cooks in order that he himself may eat, &c.

pk: 2162. When the pronoun yushnad, "thou" understod, and also when the sane elpresed, is the atendant word in agrenent with the verb, then there is the verbal ternination caled the nidle (2nd person). nOTE:—This derines the 2nd person or conjugational ariles. as tvan pacasi thou cokest or pacasi; yuvan pacaTa or pacaTa you two are coking; yuyan pacaTa or pacaTa you cok.
ck: 2162. then the pronoun yushnat, "thou" unterstot, ant also then the sane elpreset, is the atentant tort in akrenent tith the verp, then there is the verpal ternination calet the nitle (2nt person). nOtE:—this terines the 2nt person or concukational ariles. as tvan pacasi thou cokest or pacasi; yuvan pacata or pacata you to are cokink; yuyan pacata or pacata you cok.
s: 2162. When the pronoun yushmad, "thou" understood, and also when the same expressed, is the attendant word in agreement with the verb, then there is the verbal termination called the Middle (2nd person). NOTE:—This defines the 2nd person of conjugational affixes. As त्वं पचसि thou cookest or पचसि; युवां पचथः or पचथः you two are cooking; यूयं पचथ or पचथ you cook.

pk: 2165. in the other cases, nanely, where, "thou" or "i" are not the atendant words in agrenent with the verb, there is the verbal ternination caled the lowest (or 3rd person). nOTE: as ‹?› he coks, ‹?› they two cok, ‹?› they cok. now we take up the conjugation or the verb "to be" when the agent is neant, i. e., in the active Voice. Thus Bu + tip. now aply the rolowing rules :—
ck: 2165. in the other cases, nanely, there, "thou" or "i" are not the atentant torts in akrenent tith the verp, there is the verpal ternination calet the lotest (or 3rt person). nOtE: as ‹?› he coks, ‹?› they to cok, ‹?› they cok. not te take up the concukation or the verp "to pe" then the akent is neant, i. e., in the active Voice. thus pu + tip. not aply the rolotink rules :—
s: 2165. In the other cases, namely, where, "thou" or "I" are not the attendant words in agreement with the verb, there is the verbal termination called the lowest (or 3rd person). NOTE: As ‹?› he cooks, ‹?› they two cook, ‹?› they cook. Now we take up the conjugation of the verb "to be" when the agent is meant, i. e., in the Active Voice. Thus भू + तिप्. Now apply the following rules :—

pk: 216. al personal endings (i. 4. 78, s. 2154) and al ariles with an indicatory s are caled sârvadhâtuka. nOTE: Or course, this aplies to the ariles which have ben already treated berore, nanely, the ariles which relate to verbal rots and not to Tadhita ariles, &c. Thus, ‹?›; ‹?› and ‹?› are elceptions. [‹?›].
ck: 216. al personal entinks (i. 4. 78, s. 2154) ant al ariles tith an inticatory s are calet sârvathâtuka. nOtE: Or course, this aplies to the ariles thich have pen alreaty treatet perore, nanely, the ariles thich relate to verpal rots ant not to tathita ariles, &c. thus, ‹?›; ‹?› ant ‹?› are elceptions. [‹?›].
s: 2166. All personal endings (III. 4. 78, S. 2154) and all affixes with an indicatory श् are called 'sârvadhâtuka.' NOTE: Of course, this applies to the affixes which have been already treated before, namely, the affixes which relate to verbal roots and not to Taddhita affixes, &c. Thus, ‹?›; ‹?› and ‹?› are exceptions. [‹?›].

pk: 2167. The aril sap cones arter a rot, when a sârvadhâtuka rolows signirying the agent. nOTE: in active voice, sap is enployed in the conjugational tenses. This aril, which is technicaly caled a vikarana cones arter rots or the Bvadi clas and conpound rots rorned by san &c. (i. 1. 32). The indicatory s nakes it a sârvadhâtuka aril by i. 4. 13, s. 216, the p indicates that the vowel has anudâta acent (i. 1. 4, s. 3709). as Bu + sap + tip. The s and p are indicatory, the real aril is a.
ck: 2167. the aril sap cones arter a rot, then a sârvathâtuka rolots sikniryink the akent. nOtE: in active voice, sap is enployet in the concukational tenses. this aril, thich is technicaly calet a vikarana cones arter rots or the pvati clas ant conpount rots rornet py san &c. (i. 1. 32). the inticatory s nakes it a sârvathâtuka aril py i. 4. 13, s. 216, the p inticates that the votel has anutâta acent (i. 1. 4, s. 3709). as pu + sap + tip. the s ant p are inticatory, the real aril is a.
s: 2167. The affix शप् comes after a root, when a sârvadhâtuka follows signifying the agent. NOTE: In active voice, शप् is employed in the conjugational tenses. This affix, which is technically called a विकरण comes after roots of the भ्वादि class and compound roots formed by सन् &c. (III. 1. 32). The indicatory श् makes it a sârvadhâtuka affix by III. 4. 113, S. 2166, the प् indicates that the vowel has anudâtta accent (III. 1. 4, S. 3709). As भू + शप् + तिप्. The श् and प् are indicatory, the real affix is अ.

pk: 2168. The Guṇa is substituted ror the rinal ik (i, u, r, lr) vowel or a sten berore the ariles caled sârvadhâtuka and ârdhadhâtuka (i. 4. 13, s. 216, &c.) [Those that are not sârvadhâtuka are ârdhadhâtuka]. nOTE: Thus Bu + tip = Bu + sap + tip = Bo + a + ti = Bav + a + ti = Bavati sinilarly Bu + tas = Bavata The word ik is read in the sûtra, ron i. 1. 3, s. 34. in rorning the 3rd Pers. Pl. Bu + Ji, the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 2168. the kuṇa is supstitutet ror the rinal ik (i, u, r, lr) votel or a sten perore the ariles calet sârvathâtuka ant ârthathâtuka (i. 4. 13, s. 216, &c.) [those that are not sârvathâtuka are ârthathâtuka]. nOtE: thus pu + tip = pu + sap + tip = po + a + ti = pav + a + ti = pavati sinilarly pu + tas = pavata the tort ik is reat in the sûtra, ron i. 1. 3, s. 34. in rornink the 3rt pers. pl. pu + ci, the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 2168. The Guṇa is substituted for the final इक् (इ, उ, ऋ, लृ) vowel of a stem before the affixes called sârvadhâtuka and ârdhadhâtuka (III. 4. 113, S. 2166, &c.) [Those that are not sârvadhâtuka are ârdhadhâtuka]. NOTE: Thus भू + तिप् = भू + शप् + तिप् = भो + अ + ति = भव् + अ + ति = भवति Similarly भू + तस् = भवतः The word इक् is read in the sûtra, from I. 1. 3, S. 34. In forming the 3rd Pers. Pl. भू + झि, the following rule applies :—

pk: 2169. ant is substituted ror the J or an aril. nOTE:—Thererore Bu + Ji = Bu + sap + anti = Bo + a + anti = Bavanti sinilarly Bavasi, BavaTa, BavaTa in rorning the 1st Pers. sing. Bu + sap + nip = Bo + a + ni = Bav + a + ni ere the rolowing rule aplies :—
ck: 2169. ant is supstitutet ror the c or an aril. nOtE:—thererore pu + ci = pu + sap + anti = po + a + anti = pavanti sinilarly pavasi, pavata, pavata in rornink the 1st pers. sink. pu + sap + nip = po + a + ni = pav + a + ni ere the rolotink rule aplies :—
s: 2169. अन्त् is substituted for the झ् of an affix. NOTE:—Therefore भू + झि = भू + शप् + अन्ति = भो + अ + अन्ति = भवन्ति Similarly भवसि, भवथः, भवथ In forming the 1st Pers. Sing. भू + शप् + मिप् = भो + अ + मि = भव् + अ + मि Here the following rule applies :—

pk: 2170.
