The long is substituted ror the rinal a or a Tense-sten, berore a sârvadhâtuka aril begining with v or n (lit. a consonant or yan pratyâhâra). nOTE:—Thus Bava + ni = Bavani sinilarly Bavava, and Bavana Thus the whole conjugation is :— law Present Tense. singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person Bavani i becone Bavava We two becone Bavana We becone 2nd Person Bavasi Thou beconest BavaTa nou two becone BavaTa nou becone 3rd Person Bavati e becones Bavata They two becone Bavanti They becone. We have already nentioned in sûtra i. 4. 106, s. 2163, that in joke, the 1st Person, nay be used with the rorce or 2nd Person. Thus ehi nanye odanan Boksyase, Bukta sotiTiBi "Cone here, thou thinkest i shal take rod; but it is eaten already by the guest." ere "i think" neans "thou thinkest" and "thou shalt eat" is equal to "Boksye" "i shal eat." sinilarly in the other elanples given above. in the above sutra i. 4. 106, s. 2163, the phrase nanyakarnani &c., is understod ron the previous sûtra. Thererore, when the verb is not in the 2nd person, this construction is not alowed, even though joke be neant. as ehi Bo nanyate Bavan odanan Boksye &c.! Cone respected sir! (jocularly), your honor thinks "i shal eat rice," &c. Why do we say "in joke"? The proper person should be used, when sinple asertion is intended. Thus ehi nanyase odanan Boksya iti Bukta sotiTiBi "Cone, thou thinkest i shal eat rice—but it has ben eaten by the guest." nOTE:—This coresponds with the Direct and indirect naration or the English Granar. sanskrit does not adnit or indirect naration, elcept in the above elanples. now we take up the liw Thus Bu + liw. The rorce or liw is to denote the Past tine, as shown in the rolowing :—
ck: 2170. the lonk is supstitutet ror the rinal a or a tense-sten, perore a sârvathâtuka aril pekinink tith v or n (lit. a consonant or yan pratyâhâra). nOtE:—thus pava + ni = pavani sinilarly pavava, ant pavana thus the thole concukation is :— lat present tense. sinkular. tual. plural. 1st person pavani i pecone pavava te to pecone pavana te pecone 2nt person pavasi thou peconest pavata nou to pecone pavata nou pecone 3rt person pavati e pecones pavata they to pecone pavanti they pecone. te have alreaty nentionet in sûtra i. 4. 106, s. 2163, that in coke, the 1st person, nay pe uset tith the rorce or 2nt person. thus ehi nanye otanan poksyase, pukta sotitipi "cone here, thou thinkest i shal take rot; put it is eaten alreaty py the kuest." ere "i think" neans "thou thinkest" ant "thou shalt eat" is etual to "poksye" "i shal eat." sinilarly in the other elanples kiven apove. in the apove sutra i. 4. 106, s. 2163, the phrase nanyakarnani &c., is unterstot ron the previous sûtra. thererore, then the verp is not in the 2nt person, this construction is not alotet, even thoukh coke pe neant. as ehi po nanyate pavan otanan poksye &c.! cone respectet sir! (cocularly), your honor thinks "i shal eat rice," &c. thy to te say "in coke"? the proper person shoult pe uset, then sinple asertion is intentet. thus ehi nanyase otanan poksya iti pukta sotitipi "cone, thou thinkest i shal eat rice—put it has pen eaten py the kuest." nOtE:—this coresponts tith the tirect ant intirect naration or the Enklish kranar. sanskrit toes not atnit or intirect naration, elcept in the apove elanples. not te take up the lit thus pu + lit. the rorce or lit is to tenote the past tine, as shotn in the rolotink :—
s: 2170. The long is substituted for the final अ of a Tense-stem, before a Sârvadhâtuka affix beginning with व् or म् (lit. a consonant of यञ् pratyâhâra). NOTE:—Thus भव + मि = भवामि Similarly भवावः, and भवामः Thus the whole conjugation is :— लट् Present Tense. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person भवामि I become भवावः We two become भवामः We become 2nd Person भवसि Thou becomest भवथः You two become भवथ You become 3rd Person भवति He becomes भवतः They two become भवन्ति They become. We have already mentioned in sûtra I. 4. 106, S. 2163, that in joke, the 1st Person, may be used with the force of 2nd Person. Thus एहि मन्ये ओदनं भोक्ष्यसे, भुक्तः सोऽतिथिभिः "Come here, thou thinkest 'I shall take food'; but it is eaten already by the guest." Here "I think" means "thou thinkest" and "thou shalt eat" is equal to "भोक्ष्ये" "I shall eat." Similarly in the other examples given above. In the above sutra I. 4. 106, S. 2163, the phrase मन्यकर्मणि &c., is understood from the previous sûtra. Therefore, when the verb is not in the 2nd person, this construction is not allowed, even though joke be meant. As एहि भो मन्यते भवान् ओदनं भोक्ष्ये &c.! Come respected Sir! (jocularly), your honor thinks "I shall eat rice," &c. Why do we say "in joke"? The proper person should be used, when simple assertion is intended. Thus एहि मन्यसे ओदनं भोक्ष्य इति भुक्तः सोऽतिथिभिः "Come, thou thinkest 'I shall eat rice'—but it has been eaten by the guest." NOTE:—This corresponds with the Direct and Indirect narration of the English Grammar. Sanskrit does not admit of Indirect narration, except in the above examples. Now we take up the लिट् Thus भू + लिट्. The force of लिट् is to denote the Past time, as shown in the following :—

pk: 2171. The aril liw cones arter a verb, in the sense or the past, berore the conencenent or the curent day, and unperceived by the narator. nOTE: The word unperceived qualiries the words past and non-curent day understod in this aphorisn. This liw is replaced by tip &c. are these ariles sârvadhâtuka or Ârdhadhâtuka? By the general rule i. 4. 13, s. 216, they would have ben sârvadhâtuka, but ror the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 2171. the aril lit cones arter a verp, in the sense or the past, perore the conencenent or the curent tay, ant unperceivet py the narator. nOtE: the tort unperceivet tualiries the torts past ant non-curent tay unterstot in this aphorisn. this lit is replacet py tip &c. are these ariles sârvathâtuka or Ârthathâtuka? py the keneral rule i. 4. 13, s. 216, they toult have pen sârvathâtuka, put ror the rolotink sûtra.
s: 2171. The affix लिट् comes after a verb, in the sense of the past, before the commencement of the current day, and unperceived by the narrator. NOTE: The word 'unperceived' qualifies the words 'past' and 'non-current day' understood in this aphorism. This लिट् is replaced by तिप् &c. Are these affixes Sârvadhâtuka or Ârdhadhâtuka? By the general rule III. 4. 113, S. 2166, they would have been Sârvadhâtuka, but for the following sûtra.

pk: 2172. The personal endings or the Perect are also caled ârdhadhâtuka. nOTE:—The substitutes or ‹liw› get the designation or Ârdhadhâtuka, and not that or sârvadhâtuka. Thererore, they do not take the vikaraṇa or the node-aril &c. rurther on, even the ‹tip› &c. are replaced by the rolowing:—
ck: 2172. the personal entinks or the perect are also calet ârthathâtuka. nOtE:—the supstitutes or ‹lit› ket the tesiknation or Ârthathâtuka, ant not that or sârvathâtuka. thererore, they to not take the vikaraṇa or the note-aril &c. rurther on, even the ‹tip› &c. are replacet py the rolotink:—
s: 2172. The personal endings of the Perfect are also called 'ârdhadhâtuka.' NOTE:—The substitutes of ‹लिट्› get the designation of Ârdhadhâtuka, and not that of Sârvadhâtuka. Therefore, they do not take the vikaraṇa or the Mode-affix &c. Further on, even the ‹तिप्› &c. are replaced by the following:—

pk: 2173. in the ron or the Parasnaipada ariles, the rolowing are substituted in the Perect Tense :— sing. Dual. Plural. 3rd Pers. ṇal (‹nal›) atus (‹atus›) us (‹us›) 2nd Pers. thal (‹Tal›) athus (‹aTus›) a (‹a›) 1st Pers. ṇal (‹nal›) va (‹va›) na (‹na›) nOTE:—The indicatory ‹l› in ‹nal› is ror the sake or acent (Vi. 1. 193, s. 3676). The indicatory ‹n› in ‹nal› is ror the sake or causing ‹vrdDi› (Vi. 2. 25, s. 3065). Thus papaca, pecatu, pecu, peciTa or papakTa, pecaTu, peca, papaca or papaca; peciva, pecina ror the nine substitutes ror ‹tip› &c. or ‹liw› there are ‹nal› &c. instead. Thus ‹Bu + l = Bu + nal›. Then aplies the rolowing rule :—
ck: 2173. in the ron or the parasnaipata ariles, the rolotink are supstitutet in the perect tense :— sink. tual. plural. 3rt pers. ṇal (‹nal›) atus (‹atus›) us (‹us›) 2nt pers. thal (‹tal›) athus (‹atus›) a (‹a›) 1st pers. ṇal (‹nal›) va (‹va›) na (‹na›) nOtE:—the inticatory ‹l› in ‹nal› is ror the sake or acent (Vi. 1. 193, s. 3676). the inticatory ‹n› in ‹nal› is ror the sake or causink ‹vrti› (Vi. 2. 25, s. 3065). thus papaca, pecatu, pecu, pecita or papakta, pecatu, peca, papaca or papaca; peciva, pecina ror the nine supstitutes ror ‹tip› &c. or ‹lit› there are ‹nal› &c. insteat. thus ‹pu + l = pu + nal›. then aplies the rolotink rule :—
s: 2173. In the room of the Parasmaipada affixes, the following are substituted in the Perfect Tense :— Sing. Dual. Plural. 3rd Pers. ṇal (‹णल्›) atus (‹अतुस्›) us (‹उस्›) 2nd Pers. thal (‹थल्›) athus (‹अथुस्›) a (‹अ›) 1st Pers. ṇal (‹णल्›) va (‹व›) ma (‹म›) NOTE:—The indicatory ‹ल्› in ‹णल्› is for the sake of accent (VI. 1. 193, S. 3676). The indicatory ‹ण्› in ‹णल्› is for the sake of causing ‹वृद्धि› (VII. 2. 25, S. 3065). Thus पपाच, पेचतुः, पेचुः, पेचिथ or पपक्थ, पेचथुः, पेच, पपाच or पपच; पेचिव, पेचिम For the nine substitutes for ‹तिप्› &c. of ‹लिट्› there are ‹णल्› &c. instead. Thus ‹भू + ल् = भू + णल्›. Then applies the following rule :—

pk: 2174. ‹Bu› gets the augnent ‹vuk› (v) berore the tense-ariles or the aorist and the Perect, when begining with a vowel. nOTE:—This being a nitya rule, supersedes or debars the Guṇa ordained by ‹sarvaDatukarDaDatukayo› (Vi. 3. 84, s. 2168) and Vṛidhi ordained by ‹aco niti› (Vi. 2. 15, s. 254). That is to say, the indicatory ‹n› or ‹nal› does not cause Vṛidhi berore ‹vuk› takes place. Thus ‹Bu + v + a = Buv + a›. now aply the rolowing rules :—
ck: 2174. ‹pu› kets the auknent ‹vuk› (v) perore the tense-ariles or the aorist ant the perect, then pekinink tith a votel. nOtE:—this peink a nitya rule, supersetes or tepars the kuṇa ortainet py ‹sarvatatukartatatukayo› (Vi. 3. 84, s. 2168) ant Vṛithi ortainet py ‹aco niti› (Vi. 2. 15, s. 254). that is to say, the inticatory ‹n› or ‹nal› toes not cause Vṛithi perore ‹vuk› takes place. thus ‹pu + v + a = puv + a›. not aply the rolotink rules :—
s: 2174. ‹भू› gets the augment ‹वुक्› (व्) before the tense-affixes of the Aorist and the Perfect, when beginning with a vowel. NOTE:—This being a nitya rule, supersedes or debars the Guṇa ordained by ‹सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः› (VII. 3. 84, S. 2168) and Vṛiddhi ordained by ‹अचो ञ्णिति› (VII. 2. 115, S. 254). That is to say, the indicatory ‹ण्› of ‹णल्› does not cause Vṛiddhi before ‹वुक्› takes place. Thus ‹भू + व् + अ = भूव् + अ›. Now apply the following rules :—

pk: 2175. in the ron or the rirst portion, containing a single vowel, there are two. nOTE:—up to sûtra Vi. 1. 12 inclusive it is to be understod that ror the rirst sylable two are to be nade, i.e., the rirst sylable is to be reduplicated. This is an adhikâra sûtra: al the thre words vis., ‹ekaca›, ‹dve› and ‹praTanasya› are to be read in the subsequent sûtras up to Vi. 1. 12, berore the rule or sanprasâraṇa begins. Thus sûtra Vi. 1. 8 says "when ‹liw› rolows, or an unreduplicated verbal rot." The sense or this sûtra is inconplete, unles we suply the thre words or this sûtra, when it wil read thus: "when ‹liw› rolows there are two in the ron or the rirst portion, containing a single vowel or an unreduplicated verbal rot."
ck: 2175. in the ron or the rirst portion, containink a sinkle votel, there are to. nOtE:—up to sûtra Vi. 1. 12 inclusive it is to pe unterstot that ror the rirst sylaple to are to pe nate, i.e., the rirst sylaple is to pe retuplicatet. this is an athikâra sûtra: al the thre torts vis., ‹ekaca›, ‹tve› ant ‹pratanasya› are to pe reat in the supsetuent sûtras up to Vi. 1. 12, perore the rule or sanprasâraṇa pekins. thus sûtra Vi. 1. 8 says "then ‹lit› rolots, or an unretuplicatet verpal rot." the sense or this sûtra is inconplete, unles te suply the thre torts or this sûtra, then it til reat thus: "then ‹lit› rolots there are to in the ron or the rirst portion, containink a sinkle votel or an unretuplicatet verpal rot."
s: 2175. In the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel, there are two. NOTE:—Up to Sûtra VI. 1. 12 inclusive it is to be understood that for the first syllable two are to be made, i.e., the first syllable is to be reduplicated. This is an adhikâra sûtra: all the three words viz., ‹एकाचः›, ‹द्वे› and ‹प्रथमस्य› are to be read in the subsequent sûtras up to VI. 1. 12, before the rule of Samprasâraṇa begins. Thus Sûtra VI. 1. 8 says "when ‹लिट्› follows, of an unreduplicated verbal root." The sense of this sûtra is incomplete, unless we supply the three words of this sûtra, when it will read thus: "when ‹लिट्› follows there are two in the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel of an unreduplicated verbal root."

pk: 217. When the tense-ariles or the Perect rolow, there is reduplication or the rot, which is not already reduplicated. nOTE:—The reduplication is either or the rirst sylable or or the second sylable acording as the rot begins with a consonant or a vowel. Thus ‹Buv + a› = ‹Buv + Buv + a›. now aplies the rolowing sûtra by which the rirst is caled abhyâsa.
ck: 217. then the tense-ariles or the perect rolot, there is retuplication or the rot, thich is not alreaty retuplicatet. nOtE:—the retuplication is either or the rirst sylaple or or the secont sylaple acortink as the rot pekins tith a consonant or a votel. thus ‹puv + a› = ‹puv + puv + a›. not aplies the rolotink sûtra py thich the rirst is calet aphyâsa.
s: 2177. When the tense-affixes of the Perfect follow, there is reduplication of the root, which is not already reduplicated. NOTE:—The reduplication is either of the first syllable or of the second syllable according as the root begins with a consonant or a vowel. Thus ‹भूव् + अ› = ‹भूव् + भूव् + अ›. Now applies the following sûtra by which the first is called Abhyâsa.

pk: 2178. The rirst or the two is caled the abhyâsa or the neduplicate. nOTE:—The word ‹dve› in the noninative case is understod here, but ror the purposes or this sûtra it is taken in the Genitive case i.e., ‹dvayo praTana› "the rirst or the two" ordained above. The word abhyâsa ocurs in sûtras i. 1. 6, Vi. 1. 7 &c. Thus or ‹Buv + Buv + a›, the rirst is caled abhyâsa, and thererore the nelt rule aplies to it.
ck: 2178. the rirst or the to is calet the aphyâsa or the netuplicate. nOtE:—the tort ‹tve› in the noninative case is unterstot here, put ror the purposes or this sûtra it is taken in the kenitive case i.e., ‹tvayo pratana› "the rirst or the to" ortainet apove. the tort aphyâsa ocurs in sûtras i. 1. 6, Vi. 1. 7 &c. thus or ‹puv + puv + a›, the rirst is calet aphyâsa, ant thererore the nelt rule aplies to it.
s: 2178. The first of the two is called the Abhyâsa or the Reduplicate. NOTE:—The word ‹द्वे› in the nominative case is understood here, but for the purposes of this sûtra it is taken in the Genitive case i.e., ‹द्वयोः प्रथमः› "the first of the two" ordained above. The word Abhyâsa occurs in sûtras III. 1. 6, VI. 1. 7 &c. Thus of ‹भूव् + भूव् + अ›, the first is called Abhyâsa, and therefore the next rule applies to it.

pk: 2179. Or the consonants or the reduplicate, only the rirst is retained, the renainders are droped. nOTE:—Thus or ‹Buv Buv + a›, the ‹v› is elided, and we get ‹Bu Buv + a›. Then aplies the rolowing rules :—
ck: 2179. Or the consonants or the retuplicate, only the rirst is retainet, the renainters are tropet. nOtE:—thus or ‹puv puv + a›, the ‹v› is elitet, ant te ket ‹pu puv + a›. then aplies the rolotink rules :—
s: 2179. Of the consonants of the reduplicate, only the first is retained, the remainders are dropped. NOTE:—Thus of ‹भूव् भूव् + अ›, the ‹व्› is elided, and we get ‹भू भूव् + अ›. Then applies the following rules :—

pk: 2180. a short is substituted ror the long vowel or the reduplicate. nOTE:—But in the case or Bu, this rule is superseded by the nelt rule. Or we nay aply this rule and get ‹Bu Buv + a›, and then aply the nelt.
ck: 2180. a short is supstitutet ror the lonk votel or the retuplicate. nOtE:—put in the case or pu, this rule is supersetet py the nelt rule. Or te nay aply this rule ant ket ‹pu puv + a›, ant then aply the nelt.
s: 2180. A short is substituted for the long vowel of the reduplicate. NOTE:—But in the case of भू, this rule is superseded by the next rule. Or we may apply this rule and get ‹भु भूव् + अ›, and then apply the next.

pk: 2181. ‹a› is substituted ror the vowel or the reduplicate or Bu in the Perect. nOTE:—as baBuva, baBuvatu, baBuvu, baBuve Why do we say in the Perect? Observe buBusati and boBuyate The word Bavate is shown in the sûtra in the active Voice, thererore the rule wil not aply to Pasive and nerlelive rorns; as anubuBuve kanbalo devadatena This opinion or Kâśikâ, however, is not endorsed by later Granarians. Thus ‹Bu Buv + a› = ‹Ba Buv + a›. Then aplies the rolowing :—
ck: 2181. ‹a› is supstitutet ror the votel or the retuplicate or pu in the perect. nOtE:—as papuva, papuvatu, papuvu, papuve thy to te say in the perect? Opserve pupusati ant popuyate the tort pavate is shotn in the sûtra in the active Voice, thererore the rule til not aply to pasive ant nerlelive rorns; as anupupuve kanpalo tevatatena this opinion or kâśikâ, hotever, is not entorset py later kranarians. thus ‹pu puv + a› = ‹pa puv + a›. then aplies the rolotink :—
s: 2181. ‹अ› is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate of भू in the Perfect. NOTE:—As बभूव, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः, बभूवे Why do we say 'in the Perfect'? Observe बुभूषति and बोभूयते The word भवतेः is shown in the sûtra in the Active Voice, therefore the rule will not apply to Passive and Reflexive forms; as अनुबुभूवे कम्बलो देवदत्तेन This opinion of Kâśikâ, however, is not endorsed by later Grammarians. Thus ‹भु भूव् + अ› = ‹भ भूव् + अ›. Then applies the following :—

pk: 2182. The car is also the substitute or Jal leters ocuring in a reduplicate sylable, as wel as jas nOTE:—in a reduplicate sylable, a sonant non-aspirate (‹jas›) as wel as a surd non-aspirate (‹car›) is the substitute or a nute leter. By aplying the rule or nearest in place (i. 1. 50, s. 39), we rind that sonant non-aspirate (‹jas›) is the substitute or al sonants ‹Jas› and ‹car› is the substitute or al surds. in other words al aspirate leters becone non-aspirate. The word ‹jas› has ben drawn into the sûtra by the word ‹ca› also. The leters are replaced by ‹?› wil renain unchanged, and so also an original ‹?› because or the rule or nearnes or place. That is to say:— ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› which is ‹?› leters, and ‹?› by ‹?› But an original ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› not ‹?› but by ‹?› Thus ‹?› Then the rolowing doubt arises. The augnent ‹?› was aded by Vi. 4. 8, s. 2174; and the rule Vi. 4. 7, s. 271 requires ‹?› augnent, and by the rolowing rule is asidha, and so why should we not have ‹?› also.
ck: 2182. the car is also the supstitute or cal leters ocurink in a retuplicate sylaple, as tel as cas nOtE:—in a retuplicate sylaple, a sonant non-aspirate (‹cas›) as tel as a surt non-aspirate (‹car›) is the supstitute or a nute leter. py aplyink the rule or nearest in place (i. 1. 50, s. 39), te rint that sonant non-aspirate (‹cas›) is the supstitute or al sonants ‹cas› ant ‹car› is the supstitute or al surts. in other torts al aspirate leters pecone non-aspirate. the tort ‹cas› has pen tratn into the sûtra py the tort ‹ca› also. the leters are replacet py ‹?› til renain unchanket, ant so also an orikinal ‹?› pecause or the rule or nearnes or place. that is to say:— ‹?› is replacet py ‹?› thich is ‹?› leters, ant ‹?› py ‹?› put an orikinal ‹?› is replacet py ‹?› not ‹?› put py ‹?› thus ‹?› then the rolotink toupt arises. the auknent ‹?› tas atet py Vi. 4. 8, s. 2174; ant the rule Vi. 4. 7, s. 271 retuires ‹?› auknent, ant py the rolotink rule is asitha, ant so thy shoult te not have ‹?› also.
s: 2182. The चर् is also the substitute of झल् letters occurring in a reduplicate syllable, as well as जश् NOTE:—In a reduplicate syllable, a sonant non-aspirate (‹जश्›) as well as a surd non-aspirate (‹चर्›) is the substitute of a Mute letter. By applying the rule of 'nearest in place' (I. 1. 50, S. 39), we find that sonant non-aspirate (‹जश्›) is the substitute of all sonants ‹झश्› and ‹चर्› is the substitute of all surds. In other words all aspirate letters become non-aspirate. The word ‹जश्› has been drawn into the sûtra by the word ‹च› 'also.' The letters are replaced by ‹?› will remain unchanged, and so also an original ‹?› because of the rule of nearness of place. That is to say:— ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› which is ‹?› letters, and ‹?› by ‹?› But an original ‹?› is replaced by ‹?› not ‹?› but by ‹?› Thus ‹?› Then the following doubt arises. The augment ‹?› was added by VI. 4. 88, S. 2174; and the rule VI. 4. 77, S. 271 requires ‹?› augment, and by the following rule is asiddha, and so why should we not have ‹?› also.

pk: 2183. The change, which a sten wil undergo by the aplication or any or the rules ron this sûtra up to Vi. 4. 129, is to be considered as not to have taken erect, when we have to aply any other rule or this very section Vi. 4. 23 to 129. nOTE:—ron this sûtra (which is the 2nd sûtra or the rourth chapter or the silth adhyâya or Pânini) up to the end or the rourth Chapter are taught the rules caled ‹?›. When two rules or this Âbhîya section sinultaneously apear ror aplication in one and the sane place, both are aplied, one being considered as non-elistent ror the purposes or the other. Thererore, ‹?› being non-elistent, there wil be ‹?›, the result or which wil be, that in ‹?›, the long ‹?› wil be shortened. But this is prevented by the rolowing Vârtika:— Vârt:—The augnents vuk (Vi. 4. 8), and yuw (Vi. 4. 68) should however be considered as not asidha, and rule Vi. 4. 7 teaching uvan and Vi. 4. 82 teaching ‹?› substitution should not be aplied sinultaneously with then. Thus Bu—baBuva, baBuvatu, baBuvu with vuk, and upadidiye, upadidiyaTe, upadidivire, with yuw or Vi. 4. 68. in the case or Bu, when vuk is aded, there is not the adition or uvan, and in the case or din, when yuw is aded, there is not ‹?› The a in aBat has the rorce or linit inclusive, so that, the asidha rule aplies to the sutras governed by Ba. ror ruler elplanation or this inportant sutra, se ny ashtadhyayi. now we take up, 2nd Per sing. baBuva + Tal ere aplies the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 2183. the chanke, thich a sten til unterko py the aplication or any or the rules ron this sûtra up to Vi. 4. 129, is to pe consiteret as not to have taken erect, then te have to aply any other rule or this very section Vi. 4. 23 to 129. nOtE:—ron this sûtra (thich is the 2nt sûtra or the rourth chapter or the silth athyâya or pânini) up to the ent or the rourth chapter are taukht the rules calet ‹?›. then to rules or this Âphîya section sinultaneously apear ror aplication in one ant the sane place, poth are apliet, one peink consiteret as non-elistent ror the purposes or the other. thererore, ‹?› peink non-elistent, there til pe ‹?›, the result or thich til pe, that in ‹?›, the lonk ‹?› til pe shortenet. put this is preventet py the rolotink Vârtika:— Vârt:—the auknents vuk (Vi. 4. 8), ant yut (Vi. 4. 68) shoult hotever pe consiteret as not asitha, ant rule Vi. 4. 7 teachink uvan ant Vi. 4. 82 teachink ‹?› supstitution shoult not pe apliet sinultaneously tith then. thus pu—papuva, papuvatu, papuvu tith vuk, ant upatitiye, upatitiyate, upatitivire, tith yut or Vi. 4. 68. in the case or pu, then vuk is atet, there is not the atition or uvan, ant in the case or tin, then yut is atet, there is not ‹?› the a in apat has the rorce or linit inclusive, so that, the asitha rule aplies to the sutras kovernet py pa. ror ruler elplanation or this inportant sutra, se ny ashtathyayi. not te take up, 2nt per sink. papuva + tal ere aplies the rolotink sûtra.
s: 2183. The change, which a stem will undergo by the application of any of the rules from this sûtra up to VI. 4. 129, is to be considered as not to have taken effect, when we have to apply any other rule of this very section VI. 4. 23 to 129. NOTE:—From this sûtra (which is the 22nd sûtra of the fourth chapter of the sixth Adhyâya of Pânini) up to the end of the Fourth Chapter are taught the rules called ‹?›. When two rules of this Âbhîya section simultaneously appear for application in one and the same place, both are applied, one being considered as non-existent for the purposes of the other. Therefore, ‹?› being non-existent, there will be ‹?›, the result of which will be, that in ‹?›, the long ‹?› will be shortened. But this is prevented by the following Vârtika:— Vârt:—The augments वुक् (VI. 4. 88), and युट् (VI. 4. 68) should however be considered as not asiddha, and rule VI. 4. 77 teaching उवङ् and VI. 4. 82 teaching ‹?› substitution should not be applied simultaneously with them. Thus भू—बभूव, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः with वुक्, and उपदिदीये, उपदिदीयाथे, उपदिदीविरे, with युट् of VI. 4. 68. In the case of भू, when वुक् is added, there is not the addition of उवङ्, and in the case of दीङ्, when युट् is added, there is not ‹?› The आ in आभात् has the force of limit inclusive, so that, the asiddha rule applies to the sutras governed by भ. For fuller explanation of this important sutra, see my Ashtadhyayi. Now we take up, 2nd Per Sing. बभूव + थल् Here applies the following sûtra.

pk: 2184. an ârdhadhâtuka aril (i. 4. 14 &c) begining with a consonant (elcept ya), gets the augnent iw (in these rules). Thus baBuva + Ta = baBuva + i + Ta = baBuviTa so also baBuvaTu, baBuva, baBuviva, baBuvina ror Perect. 3rd Person: sing. baBuva, Dual baBuvatu, Plural baBuvu 2nd Person: sing. baBuviTa, Dual baBuvaTu, Plural baBuva 1st Person: sing. baBuva, Dual baBuviva, Plural baBuvina now we take up the conjugation or Bu in luw rirst ruture. The rorce or luw is given in the nelt sûtra. Thus Bu + luw
ck: 2184. an ârthathâtuka aril (i. 4. 14 &c) pekinink tith a consonant (elcept ya), kets the auknent it (in these rules). thus papuva + ta = papuva + i + ta = papuvita so also papuvatu, papuva, papuviva, papuvina ror perect. 3rt person: sink. papuva, tual papuvatu, plural papuvu 2nt person: sink. papuvita, tual papuvatu, plural papuva 1st person: sink. papuva, tual papuviva, plural papuvina not te take up the concukation or pu in lut rirst ruture. the rorce or lut is kiven in the nelt sûtra. thus pu + lut
s: 2184. An ârdhadhâtuka affix (III. 4. 114 &c) beginning with a consonant (except य), gets the augment इट् (in these rules). Thus बभूव + थ = बभूव + इ + थ = बभूविथ So also बभूवथुः, बभूव, बभूविव, बभूविम for Perfect. 3rd Person: Sing. बभूव, Dual बभूवतुः, Plural बभूवुः 2nd Person: Sing. बभूविथ, Dual बभूवथुः, Plural बभूव 1st Person: Sing. बभूव, Dual बभूविव, Plural बभूविम Now we take up the conjugation of भू in लुट् First Future. The force of लुट् is given in the next sûtra. Thus भू + लुट्

pk: 2186. When lr and luw rolow, then sya and tasi are respectively the node ariles or a verbal rot. nOTE:—lr is the conon elpresion ror lrw and lrn rorned by rejecting their special anubandhas, and neans thererore the 2nd ruture and the conditional tenses. luw is the 1st ruture also caled the Periphrastic ruture. The i or tasi is indicatory to show that the penultinate nasal or the rot is not to be droped berore this; as nan to think, nanta ‘he wil think.’ This debars the node-ariles sap &c. Thus Bu + tasi + tip The p or tip is indicatory. The node-aril is ârdhadhâtuka.
ck: 2186. then lr ant lut rolot, then sya ant tasi are respectively the note ariles or a verpal rot. nOtE:—lr is the conon elpresion ror lrt ant lrn rornet py recectink their special anupanthas, ant neans thererore the 2nt ruture ant the contitional tenses. lut is the 1st ruture also calet the periphrastic ruture. the i or tasi is inticatory to shot that the penultinate nasal or the rot is not to pe tropet perore this; as nan to think, nanta ‘he til think.’ this tepars the note-ariles sap &c. thus pu + tasi + tip the p or tip is inticatory. the note-aril is ârthathâtuka.
s: 2186. When लृ and लुट् follow, then स्य and तासि are respectively the Mode affixes of a verbal root. NOTE:—लृ is the common expression for लृट् and लृङ् formed by rejecting their special anubandhas, and means therefore the 2nd Future and the conditional tenses. लुट् is the 1st Future also called the Periphrastic Future. The इ of तासि is indicatory to show that the penultimate nasal of the root is not to be dropped before this; as मन् 'to think,' मन्ता ‘he will think.’ This debars the Mode-affixes शप् &c. Thus भू + तासि + तिप् The प् of तिप् is indicatory. The mode-affix is ârdhadhâtuka.

pk: 2187. The renainder i. e., the ariles other than tiṅ, and those with an indicatory ś subjoined to a verbal rot, are caled ârdhadhâtuka. nOTE:—The node-ariles sya and tasi are thererore ârdhadhâtuka, and so get the augnent iw Thus Bu + iw + tas + tip Then rurther the conjugational ariles ti, tas, Ji are replaced by qa, rO, ras, acording to the rolowing sûtra:—
ck: 2187. the renainter i. e., the ariles other than tiṅ, ant those tith an inticatory ś supcoinet to a verpal rot, are calet ârthathâtuka. nOtE:—the note-ariles sya ant tasi are thererore ârthathâtuka, ant so ket the auknent it thus pu + it + tas + tip then rurther the concukational ariles ti, tas, ci are replacet py ta, rO, ras, acortink to the rolotink sûtra:—
s: 2187. The remainder i. e., the affixes other than 'tiṅ', and those with an indicatory 'ś' subjoined to a verbal root, are called 'ârdhadhâtuka'. NOTE:—The Mode-affixes स्य and तासि are therefore ârdhadhâtuka, and so get the augment इट् Thus भू + इट् + तास् + तिप् Then further the conjugational affixes ति, तस्, झि are replaced by डा, रौ, रस्, according to the following sûtra:—

pk: 218. qa, rO, and ras are substituted respectively in the ron or the thre-ariles or the third person or luw (rirst-ruture), both in the Parasnaipada and the Âtnanepada. nOTE:—as the anubandha qa in qa nust produce sone erect, it causes the elision or the wi portion or the aril though the base is not Bha. Thus Bu + i + tas + ti = Bu + i + ta + qa (a). Then aplies the rolowing sûtra:—
ck: 218. ta, rO, ant ras are supstitutet respectively in the ron or the thre-ariles or the thirt person or lut (rirst-ruture), poth in the parasnaipata ant the Âtnanepata. nOtE:—as the anupantha ta in ta nust protuce sone erect, it causes the elision or the ti portion or the aril thoukh the pase is not pha. thus pu + i + tas + ti = pu + i + ta + ta (a). then aplies the rolotink sûtra:—
s: 2188. डा, रौ, and रस् are substituted respectively in the room of the three-affixes of the third person of लुट् (First-future), both in the Parasmaipada and the Âtmanepada. NOTE:—As the anubandha ड in डा must produce some effect, it causes the elision of the टि portion of the affix though the base is not Bha. Thus भू + इ + तास् + ति = भू + इ + ता + डा (आ). Then applies the following sûtra:—

pk: 2189. Guṇa is substituted berore a sârvadhâtuka or an ârdhadhâtuka aril, ror the vowels or the Causative stens which take the augnent puk (Vi. 3. 36), and ror the vowel or a sten which has a penultinate short vowel. Thus ‹?› = Bavita + a Then the question arises, should not the present sutra aply in the case the or ‹?› i. e. should not the ‹?› be gunated to ‹?› berore the vowel sârvadhâtuka ti. ror ‹?› is a sten which has a penultinate short vowel ‹?›; and an ‹?› leter; though the vikaraṇa is aded betwen ‹?› and ‹?› One nay prina racie reply, no, because betwen the ‹?› or the aṅga and the change-producing ti, there are thre leters ‹?› etc and there being a vyavadhâna or intervention, they prevent the rorce or ti pasing through then to ‹?› This, however, is not the case, because or the rolowing nalin. “That which canot but be an intervention, though it do intervene, is not considered an intervention, because the rule nust have its scope.” The word ‹?› neans “not non-intervention,” i. e. which nust necesarily intervene. such an absolutely necesary intervention is not to be considered an intervention. Thererore, ir there is only one intervention, the rule wil aply. Thus in the case or ‹?› + ti, there are thre leters intervening betwen ‹?› and ti i. e., to say, ‹?› and ‹?›; and so the guṇa rule does not aply. But in the case or ‹?› only one leter intervenes, and so there ought to be guṇa. But here the rolowing aplies :—
ck: 2189. kuṇa is supstitutet perore a sârvathâtuka or an ârthathâtuka aril, ror the votels or the causative stens thich take the auknent puk (Vi. 3. 36), ant ror the votel or a sten thich has a penultinate short votel. thus ‹?› = pavita + a then the tuestion arises, shoult not the present sutra aply in the case the or ‹?› i. e. shoult not the ‹?› pe kunatet to ‹?› perore the votel sârvathâtuka ti. ror ‹?› is a sten thich has a penultinate short votel ‹?›; ant an ‹?› leter; thoukh the vikaraṇa is atet peten ‹?› ant ‹?› One nay prina racie reply, no, pecause peten the ‹?› or the aṅka ant the chanke-protucink ti, there are thre leters ‹?› etc ant there peink a vyavathâna or intervention, they prevent the rorce or ti pasink throukh then to ‹?› this, hotever, is not the case, pecause or the rolotink nalin. “that thich canot put pe an intervention, thoukh it to intervene, is not consiteret an intervention, pecause the rule nust have its scope.” the tort ‹?› neans “not non-intervention,” i. e. thich nust necesarily intervene. such an apsolutely necesary intervention is not to pe consiteret an intervention. thererore, ir there is only one intervention, the rule til aply. thus in the case or ‹?› + ti, there are thre leters intervenink peten ‹?› ant ti i. e., to say, ‹?› ant ‹?›; ant so the kuṇa rule toes not aply. put in the case or ‹?› only one leter intervenes, ant so there oukht to pe kuṇa. put here the rolotink aplies :—
s: 2189. Guṇa is substituted before a sârvadhâtuka or an ârdhadhâtuka affix, for the vowels of the Causative stems which take the augment पुक् (VII. 3. 36), and for the vowel of a stem which has a penultimate short vowel. Thus ‹?› = भविता + आ Then the question arises, should not the present sutra apply in the case the of ‹?› i. e. should not the ‹?› be gunated to ‹?› before the vowel Sârvadhâtuka ति. For ‹?› is a stem which has a penultimate short vowel ‹?›; and an ‹?› letter; though the vikaraṇa is added between ‹?› and ‹?› One may prima facie reply, no, because between the ‹?› of the aṅga and the change-producing ति, there are three letters ‹?› etc and there being a vyavadhâna or intervention, they prevent the force of ति passing through them to ‹?› This, however, is not the case, because of the following maxim. “That which cannot but be an intervention, though it do intervene, is not considered an intervention, because the rule must have its scope.” The word ‹?› means “not non-intervention,” i. e. which must necessarily intervene. Such an absolutely necessary intervention is not to be considered an intervention. Therefore, if there is only one intervention, the rule will apply. Thus in the case of ‹?› + ति, there are three letters intervening between ‹?› and ति i. e., to say, ‹?› and ‹?›; and so the guṇa rule does not apply. But in the case of ‹?› only one letter intervenes, and so there ought to be guṇa. But here the following applies :—

pk: 2190. The guṇa and vṛidhi substitutions, which would otherwise have presented thenselves, do not however, cone, in the place or the vowels or didhî to shine, and vevî to go, and or the augnent caled ‹?›. nOTE:—Thererore, there is no guṇation or the ‹?› or ‹?› berore ‹?›. so we get Bavita in 3rd Pers. Dual, we have ‹?› + ‹?› + ‹?› + ‹?›. Then aplies the rule arter the rolowing:—

s: 2197. तातङ् is optionally substituted for the affixes तु and हि of the Imperative, when benediction is meant. The substitute तातङ् consists of more than one letter and therefore replaces the whole of तु and हि and not only their final उ or इ. This is by sûtra I. 1. 55 S. 45. But here an objector says, "the substitute तातङ् has an indicatory ङ् and therefore by the sûtra I. 1. 53 S. 43; it will replace only the final, though it consists of more than one letter, just as the substitute ‹?› (VI. 3. 25) replaces only the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद्; or just as the substitute replaces the final of roots only. For the sûtra ङिच्च (I. 1. 53) is an apavada or exception in anticipation to अनेकाल् शित् सर्वस्य (I. 1. 55)." To this we reply "True; but the sûtra ङिच्च (I. 1. 53) has its scope in affixes like अम्, वस् &c. where ङ् has no other force or indicatory power. But in the case of तातङ् the indicatory ङ् finds its scope in preventing guna and vriddhi (I. 1. 5), and in effecting vocalisation (VI. 1. 16) &c. So the sutra I. 1. 53 applies there only where the indicatory ङ् has no other purpose. In the case of तातङ् it seemed to apply with exhausted force, but that little is also set aside by the subsequent sutra अनेकाल् &c. I. 1. 55. For in the case of तातङ्, the general rule I. 1. 55 and the exceptional rule ङिच्च I. 1. 53 are of equal force, and therefore the maxim विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम् will apply, and the subsequent sutra I. 1. 55 will supersede ङिच्च I. 1. 53. Therefore तातङ् replaces the whole affix. Thus भवतात् "May he be prosperous." Note:—The affix तातङ् being a substitute of हि, is like हि, and, therefore, rules propounded with regard to हि, will apply to तातङ् also. Thus VI. 4. 105 says that after stems ending in short अ, the हि is elided: therefore, after such words तातङ् should also be elided. Therefore we cannot get the form भवतात् say for भिन्तात्. This objection, however, is futile; for, in the sutra अतो हेः (VI. 4. 105), there is the anuvritti of हि from sutra VI. 4. 101 (हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिः). So that अतो हेः should be construed as meaning "there is the elision of हि when it is of the form हि, and not when it assumes the form तातङ्". The object of ङ् in तातङ् is, as we have said above, for the sake of preventing Guna and Vriddhi. It should not be said that the object of ङ् in तातङ् is for the sake of ‹?› by the application of sutra ङिच्च (I. 1. 53), just as the substitutes &c. (VII. 1. 93 and 94) apply to the finals. For by so doing, तातङ् would replace only the उ of तु and the इ of हि, which is not desired. And the case of तातङ् is to be distinguished from आङ्, for in आङ् the ङ् has no other object but to prevent sarvâdesa; but in तातङ् we see that ङ् has another object, namely, the prevention of Guna and Vṛiddhi and having thus found scope, the तातङ् substitute will be governed by the general rule अनेकाल्शित् सर्वस्य (I. 1. 55.)

pk: 2198. The personal endings or the inperative are as those or the inperect. This is an atidesa sutra; as in the lan there are the ariles tan, tan, ta and na, so also in the low—pacatan, pacatan, pacata, pacava, pacana Q. ir low is like lan, why have we not the augnent at, aw, or the substitution or jus ror Ji (se i. 4. 1) in the case or low also? a. The sa or sutra i. 4. 83 is understod in this sutra also, so that the analogy betwen low and lan is a linited analogy and does not nake al the rules which are aplicable to lan equaly aplicable to low also. nOTE:—The inperative being treated as the inperect we have the rolowing substitutions.
ck: 2198. the personal entinks or the inperative are as those or the inperect. this is an atitesa sutra; as in the lan there are the ariles tan, tan, ta ant na, so also in the lot—pacatan, pacatan, pacata, pacava, pacana t. ir lot is like lan, thy have te not the auknent at, at, or the supstitution or cus ror ci (se i. 4. 1) in the case or lot also? a. the sa or sutra i. 4. 83 is unterstot in this sutra also, so that the analoky peten lot ant lan is a linitet analoky ant toes not nake al the rules thich are aplicaple to lan etualy aplicaple to lot also. nOtE:—the inperative peink treatet as the inperect te have the rolotink supstitutions.
s: 2198. The personal endings of the Imperative are as those of the Imperfect. This is an अतिदेश sutra; as in the लङ् there are the affixes तां, तम्, त and म, so also in the लोट्—पचताम्, पचतम्, पचत, पचाव, पचाम Q. If लोट् is like लङ्, why have we not the augment अत्, अट्, or the substitution of जुस् for झि (see III. 4. 111) in the case of लोट् also? A. The सः of sutra III. 4. 83 is understood in this sutra also, so that the analogy between लोट् and लङ् is a limited analogy and does not make all the rules which are applicable to लङ् equally applicable to लोट् also. NOTE:—The Imperative being treated as the Imperfect we have the following substitutions.

pk: 208. The aril Liṅ cones arter a verb, when the agent either conands, invites, pernits, politely elpreses a wish, asks questions, or prays. The word viDi neans conanding or directing a subordinate such as a servant, &c.; ninantranan neans giving invitation such as inviting a daughters son in Śrādha reast, &c.; anantranan neans elpresing pernision to do as one likes; aDiswa neans to politely elpres a wish; sanprasna neans a question; and prarTana neans a prayer. The sūtra would have ben beter worded had Pāṇini said pravartanayan lin, instead or using the above rour words which elpres direrent aspects or pravartanā or pronpting one to act. The enploynent or these rour words separately in the sūtra is nerely an anplirication. Thus Bu + lin = Bu + a + ti = Bav + a + ti note:—This elcludes al other tense-ariles. Thus:— (1) ‹?› let hin nake the nat; ‹?› you cone to the vilage; (2 and 3) ‹?› you wil or nay dine here; ‹?› here you wil or nay sit; (4) ‹?› we wish that you should condescend to initiate this boy; (5) ‹?› sir, what shal i learn, the Granar or the Logic? (6) ‹?› this is ny prayer that i should learn Granar.

s: 2208. The affix 'Liṅ' comes after a verb, when the agent either commands, invites, permits, politely expresses a wish, asks questions, or prays. The word विधिः means 'commanding or directing a subordinate such as a servant, &c.'; निमन्त्रणं means 'giving invitation' such as inviting a daughter's son in Śrāddha feast, &c.; आमन्त्रणं means 'expressing permission to do as one likes'; अधीष्टः means 'to politely express a wish'; संप्रश्नः means 'a question'; and प्रार्थना means 'a prayer.' The sūtra would have been better worded had Pāṇini said प्रवर्त्तनायां लिङ्, instead of using the above four words which express different aspects of pravartanā or prompting one to act. The employment of these four words separately in the sūtra is merely an amplification. Thus भू + लिङ् = भू + अ + ति = भव् + अ + ति Note:—This excludes all other tense-affixes. Thus:— (1) ‹?› 'let him make the mat'; ‹?› 'you come to the village'; (2 and 3) ‹?› 'you will or may dine here'; ‹?› 'here you will or may sit'; (4) ‹?› 'we wish that you should condescend to initiate this boy'; (5) ‹?› 'Sir, what shall I learn, the Grammar or the Logic'? (6) ‹?› 'this is my prayer that I should learn Grammar.'

pk: 209. When the Parasnaipada ariles or the Potential rolow, then yāsuṭ acutely acented, is their augnent, and the ternination is regarded as having an indicatory ṅ. s: 2209. When the Parasmaipada affixes of the Potential follow, then 'yāsuṭ' acutely accented, is their augment, and the termination is regarded as having an indicatory 'ṅ'. This debars सीयुट्; the उद् of यासुट् is indicatory; the real augment is यास्. All augments being anudātta, the present sūtra, therefore, especially uses the word udātta, to show that this augment is an exception to the general rule. Though लिङ् has an indicatory ङ, and therefore by the rule I. 1. 56, its substitutes would also be regarded as having an indicatory ङ, the repetition of the word ङित् in this sūtra, shows the existence of the paribhāshā “that the ङ belonging to लिङ् does not influence its substitutes;” in other words, the substitutes of ‹?›, are not to be regarded as having an indicatory ङ (‹?›). Or it indicates that the prohibition of अनल्विध of sūtra I. 1. 56 does sometime apply to the letters of an anubandha, in other words, the operations required by a particular anubandha letter do not sometimes take place, when the affix having that anubandha-letter is replaced by another which has it not. This we further infer from the employment of the anubandha ‹?› in the substitute which replaces the लिङ् affix ‹?› (see III. 1. 83). The substitute could have been very well enunciated as ‹?›, for replacing a लिङ् affix, it would have been ‹?› by virtue of ‹?› (I. 1. 56). In the Potential, the ‹?› of ‹?› is elided by VII. 2. 79. So we get the forms ‹?›, and by applying III. 4. 108 and VI. 1. 96, ‹?›. For the Benedictive लिङ् the sūtra III. 4. 116. S. 2216, applies. Thus ‹?› Then applies the following.

s: 2211. In the sârvadhâtuka Liṅ (i. e. Potential), the स which is not final (i. e. the स् of the augments यास् and सीयुट्), is elided. What is the स which is not final? The स् of the augments, यास् and सीयुट्. Thus both स्'s are elided. The स् of सीयुट् is heard in the Benedictive; and better still in the âtmanepada. Thus भू+शप्+या+त्

pk: 212. arter a Present sten ending in short a, iy is substituted ror the sârvadhâtuka ya (i. e., the augnent or the Potential). Thus Bu+sap+yas + t = Bava+yas + t = Bava+iy+t The a+i becone guṇa and the y is elided by Vi. 1. 6. s. 873. (lopo vyorvali) Thus we have Bavet nOTE:—The objector nay say, the rorn Bavet wil be so by the elision or a under Vi. 4. 48, (ato lopa) and so there is no necesity or reading the anuvṛti or sârvadhâtuka in this sûtra; ror when a is elided by Vi. 4. 48, in the case or ârdhadhâtuka ya the present rule canot aply, as there is no base lert which ends in a. To this we reply, this is not a god reason: ror then in the case or cikirset and also, the rule (Vi. 3. 101) would aply, and the a would require to be lengthened. But that is not so. The ract is that the present sûtra debars rule Vi. 3. 101. Thererore, as this substitute debars the lengthening or Vi. 3. 101, so it would debar the lopa or Vi. 4. 48. Thererore, ir the anuvṛti or sârvadhâtuka be not read into this sûtra, the substitute iy would aply to ârdhadhâtuka also, and the lopa-elision Vi. 4. 48, would not help, as that would be superseded by this special rule. Thererore the anuvṛti or "sârvadhâtuka" should be read into this sûtra. TElT:—The above is stated on general grounds. But ir the nalin naDyepavada purvan viDin baDante notaran (apavâdas that are surounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavâda operations; supersede only those rules that precede, not those that rolow then) be aplied here, then the present sûtra would supersede only the preceding sûtra Vi. 4. 48, and not the rolowing sûtra Vi. 3. 101 which would not be superseded by the present sûtra. in this view also, the lopa alone being superseded, and not the dīrgha, there would have ben lengthening in Bavet &c. by the subsequent sûtra, hence the anuvṛti or sârvadhâtuka nust be read into this sûtra. so also 3rd Dual. Bavetan Then 3rd Pl. Bava+ya+us

s: 2212. After a Present stem ending in short अ, इय् is substituted for the sârvadhâtuka या (i. e., the augment of the Potential). Thus भू+शप्+यास् + त् = भव+यास् + त् = भव+इय्+त् The अ+इ become guṇa and the य् is elided by VI. 1. 66. S. 873. (लोपो व्योर्वलि) Thus we have भवेत् NOTE:—The objector may say, the form भवेत् will be so by the elision of अ under VI. 4. 48, (अतो लोपः) and so there is no necessity of reading the anuvṛtti of sârvadhâtuka in this sûtra; for when अ is elided by VI. 4. 48, in the case of ârdhadhâtuka या the present rule cannot apply, as there is no base left which ends in अ. To this we reply, this is not a good reason: for then in the case of चिकीर्षेत् and also, the rule (VII. 3. 101) would apply, and the अ would require to be lengthened. But that is not so. The fact is that the present sûtra debars rule VII. 3. 101. Therefore, as this substitute debars the lengthening of VII. 3. 101, so it would debar the lopa of VI. 4. 48. Therefore, if the anuvṛtti of sârvadhâtuka be not read into this sûtra, the substitute इय् would apply to ârdhadhâtuka also, and the lopa-elision VI. 4. 48, would not help, as that would be superseded by this special rule. Therefore the anuvṛtti of "sârvadhâtuka" should be read into this sûtra. TEXT:—The above is stated on general grounds. But if the maxim मध्येऽपवादाः पूर्वान् विधीन् बाधन्ते नोत्तरान् (Apavâdas that are surrounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavâda operations; supersede only those rules that precede, not those that follow them) be applied here, then the present sûtra would supersede only the preceding sûtra VI. 4. 48, and not the following sûtra VII. 3. 101 which would not be superseded by the present sûtra. In this view also, the lopa alone being superseded, and not the dīrgha, there would have been lengthening in भवेत् &c. by the subsequent sûtra, hence the anuvṛtti of 'sârvadhâtuka' must be read into this sûtra. So also 3rd Dual. भवेताम् Then 3rd Pl. भव+या+उस्

s: 2213. In the Potential and Benedictive, 'jus' is the substitute of 'jhi', the ending of the first person plural Parasmaipada. This debars अन्त् (VII. 1. 3). The ज् is इत् or indicatory. Thus da+an+Ji (the Ji or i. 4. 108) (i. 4. 7) + jus (i. 4. 10) = ada+us = adu a+ya+Ji+ya+us (Vi. 4. 1): The usa is also the substitute or Ji in liw (Perect) se i. 4. 82. Thus pra+usta=prosta, pra+usita=prosita nost likely this word has ben read here ror the sake or the subsequent sûtra or because usa sylable is taken here and not nerely the aril ror here usa cones arter the a, and thererore there should be the single substitute or the rorn or the second and ato yeya wil rind no scope here, ror there is no ya and the rorn would be Bavoyu To this there are two replies. rirst acording to Eastern Granarians who interpret ato yeya "arter a sten in a, the ya or yasuw is replaced by iy". in this view, the s being elided by Vi. 2. 79, we have iya+us, and here the sûtra ato yeya nust aply rirst and then the present sûtra, because Vi. 2. 80, is a subsequent sûtra to the present in the order or Pāṇini; and because it is a nitya rule, because it wil aply whether the conbination required by Vi. 1. 96, has taken place or not. But in the present case, there is no ocasion ror its operation, because the whole ya is replaced by iy acording to our interpretation. s: 2214. For the अ or आ (not standing at the end of a Pada or full word) + उ of उस the Tense affix the second vowel is the single substitute. NOTE:—The आत् is understood here. This debars the guṇa taught in VI. 1. 87. Thus भिक्षा+उ=भिक्षु, हिंसा+उ=हिंसु, (उ of उस) अदुः All these are examples of उस. Thus दा+आङ्+झि (the झि of III. 4. 108) (II. 4. 77) + जुस् (III. 4. 110) = अदा+उस् = अदुः अ+या+झि+या+उस् (VI. 4. 111): The उस is also the substitute of झि in लिट् (Perfect) see III. 4. 82. When the preceding vowel is not अ or आ, this rule does not apply. Thus the 3rd per. pl. of the Perfect of बिभी is:—बिभ्युः So also from भी we have बिभी + उस् = बिभ्युः The word अपदान्तात् 'not being final in a Pada' does strictly speaking, serve no good purpose in this sûtra. For the affix can never be added to a Pada, it must always be added to a stem, that has not yet risen to the rank of a Pada. If, however, उस be taken as the syllable उस (whether an affix or part of an affix or not), then the limitation of अपदान्तात् becomes valid. Thus प्र+उस्त=प्रोस्त, प्र+उषित=प्रोषित Most likely this word has been read here for the sake of the subsequent sûtra or because उस syllable is taken here and not merely the affix For here उस comes after the आ, and therefore there should be the single substitute of the form of the second and अतो येयः will find no scope here, for there is no या and the form would be भवोयुः To this there are two replies. First according to Eastern Grammarians who interpret अतो येयः "After a stem in अ, the या of यासुट् is replaced by इय्". In this view, the स् being elided by VII. 2. 79, we have इया+उस्, and here the sûtra अतो येयः must apply first and then the present sûtra, because VII. 2. 80, is a subsequent sûtra to the present in the order of Pāṇini; and because it is a nitya rule, because it will apply whether the combination required by VI. 1. 96, has taken place or not. Thus we get भव + इया + उ = भवेयुः For if the pararūpa sandhi takes place first, then भव+या+उ becomes भवोस्, and so there is no occasion for the application of अतो येयः, for there is no या to be replaced, and so there is no इय् and we get भवोयुः The other view is, that the pararūpa sandhi of the present sûtra is antaraṅga, because the operation ordained by it is inside that of VII. 2. 80: and therefore it ought to apply first. But in the present case, there is no occasion for its operation, because the whole या is replaced by इय् according to our interpretation. Thus the sûtra अतो येयः is an apavâda to the rule requiring the elision of स् taught by the sûtra VII. 2. 79. Thus we get भव+इय्+स्+उस्, and here there is no preceding अ, and so the present sûtra cannot apply. The word इयः in the sûtra is formed by इय्+स्; and is exhibited without any case-termination. Others say, the word is इयः the sixth case of इ formed on the analogy of सख्युः by the elision of य् (VI. 4. 140). Then भव+इय्+उस् = भव+इ+उस् (VIII. 3. 19) after this elision, there ordinarily would take place no sandhi as this elision is considered asiddha (VIII. 2. 1) for the purposes of VI. 1. 87. Contrary to this general rule, however, the sandhi takes place here and we have ‹?› by VI. 1. 87. The ‹?› in ‹?› is for the sake of pronunciation only. The real substitute is ‹?› Some read the sûtra as ‹?› so that the sthânin is ‹?› and not ‹?›, and ‹?› is a genitive compound. POTENTIAL or विधिलिङ् 3rd Person. s: 2219. The affix 'Luṅ' comes after a verb when the word 'mâṅ' is used in connection with it. This sets aside all other tense affixes. As मा कार्षीत् 'let him not do', मा हार्षीत् 'let him not take'. How have we then the Imperative and the Future tenses in the following sentence instead of the Aorist ? मा भवतु तस्य पापं मा भविष्यति This sentence is against good usage. Or, we may explain it by saying that there is another मा which has not the indicatory ṅ ; and with that मा, other tenses may be used. The augment अ is elided after the prohibitive particle मा, by VI. 4. 71.

s: 2225. A single consonantal sârvadhâtuka affix gets the augment ईट् after 'to be' and after the Aorist character सिच् when the ‹?› of अस् and सिच् are not elided. The सिच् plus अस् have become a Samâhâra Dvandva compound, declined in the Ablative Singular. The ‹?› of सिच् has not become ‹?› and then ‹?› is considered here as a Bha base by Sûtra-license. The words of this sûtra require a little explanation. It consists of four words 1. अस्ति (an Indeclinable meaning "when present") 2. सिच्, 3. अप्रुक्ते, 4. ‹?›. The सिच् has become ‹?› a Samâhâra Dvandva compound meaning "the Mode-affix सिच् and the root to be". In forming the compound, the word सिच् is not treated as a Pada, but as a Bha; and so the ‹?› is not changed to ‹?› or ‹?› i. e., the compound is not ‹?›, as in वाग्रथौ This is a Sûtra license. The word अस्ति is an Indeclinable meaning "when present"; i. e., when अस् and सिच् are present as सिच् and अस् without the elision of ‹?› Then this ‹?› is compounded with सिच् as a Karmadhâraya compound, and we have ‹?› Then this compound takes the Ablative affix and so we have ‹?› But this Ablative ending is elided as a Sûtra-anomaly and we have ‹?› literally meaning "after sich and as, when existing (as such)". This sutra however does not apply here, because सिच् is non-existent. Therefore we have, अभूत्, अभूताम् &c. As आसीत्, आसीः ; अवादीत्, अवादीः Why do we say consonantal? Observe ‹?›. Why do we say a single-consonant affix? Observe ‹?› and अभूताम् Vârt:— Prohibition of the sthânivad-bhâva must be stated when ‹?› is substituted for ‹?› (III. 4. 84), and ‹?› for अस् (II. 4. 52), before the augment ‹?› Therefore not here ‹?› and ‹?› The word ‹?› is thus formed. ‹?› NOTE:— This round about explanation of Bhattoji Dikshit is for the following reason:— According to Ancient Grammarians the word अस्तिसिच् is a Samâhâra Dvandva of asti and sich, meaning "the verb अस् and the affix सिच्". And the Ablative singular of asti-sich is asti-sichas meaning "after the verb as and the affix sich." But the compound asti-sich will require the Samâsânta ‹?› (V. 4. 106) and the word would be asti-sicha, a vowel-ending prâtipadika. If it be said that the Samâsânta is anitya, then there is this difficulty that सिच् should be placed first in forming the compound, i. e., we should have सिजस्ति because सिच् consists of fewer letters than अस्ति (अल्पाच्तरम् II. 2. 34). If it be said that this rule is also anitya, because Pânini himself violates it in the sûtra ‹?› (IV. 4. 118), where samudra is placed first and not abhra; even then when ‹?› is changed to ‹?› in the example ‹?›, this sûtra will apply, because ‹?› is considered as sthânivat to ‹?› And similarly in ‹?› and ‹?› the elided सिच् will be sthânivat and so there will be ‹?› To prevent all these difficulties, Bhattoji has given the above explanation. s: 2227. When सिच् is elided, then the झि is not changed to जुस् except when the stem ends in long आ The Present Sûtra says that after verbs in which सिच् has been elided, जुस् does not replace झि in the case of any other verb than that which ends in long आ; it is thus a niyama rule. But where the सिच् is not elided, there, of course, जुस् does come. pk: 29. Where there is a reason ror ariling Lin, the aril Lrin is enployed in the ruture tense, when the non-conpletion or the action is to be understod. The words in denoting ruture tine are understod here. The reasons ror ariling lin are such, as, cause and erect &c. nentioned in sûtra i. 3. 156 and 157 &c. The lrn is caled the conditional tense. "it cones in the conditional sentences in which the non-perornance or the action is inplied; or where the ralsity or the antecedent is inplied as a nater or ract. it usualy coresponds to the English pluperect conditional, and nust, in sanskrit, be used in both the antecedent and the consequent clauses". Thus suvrswiscedaBavisyat tada suBiksanaBavisyat "ir there had ben god rain, then there would have ben plenty or rod; or ir there were to be god rain then there would be plenty or rod". it is inplied that there was not god rain, nor consequent plenty: or that the ocurence or god rain is dubious, and the desirable consequence equaly so. so also here, daksinena cedyasyan na sakawan paryaBavisyat ir he were to go by the right side, the cariage would not be upset; yadi kanalakaran vyahasyan na sakawan paryaBavisyat ir he were to cal Kanalaka (which he wil not), the cariage would not be upset; naBojyata Bavan Grtena yadi natsanipan aganisyat you would eat rod with clariried buter, ir you (were to) cone to ne (but you wil not cone). al these sentences rerer to ruture tine. The non-upseting is a ruture contingency and is an erect, the cause or which is the caling or Kanalaka. The speaker—having aprehended the cause and erect, and having also learned ron other sources that such an erect wil not take place, that is to say, that Kanalaka wil not be caled, and the cariage wil be upset—has enployed this conditional tense to elpres his idea. The whole sentence yadi kanalakaran vyahasyan &c. realy gives this sense:—That both actions, the caling and the non-upseting, which are subjects or a ruture tine, and which are related as cause and erect, wil not be conpleted; that neither Kanalaka wil be caled, nor the inpending rate averted ron the cariage. The sûtra nay also be thus rendered acording to Proresor Böhtlingk:—in conditional sentence, which would require a Potential acording to i. 3. 156 the conditional tense is used, ir the sense is that or ruture tine, when the action is not conplete. Thus Bu + lrn = Bu + l + tip (i. 1. 3. s. 2186.) = a + Bu + sya + ti = a + Bo + sya + ti = a + Bav + i + sya + ti = aBavisyat singular. Dual.
