s: 2229. Where there is a reason for affixing 'Lin,' the affix 'Lrin' is employed in the Future tense, when the non-completion of the action is to be understood. The words 'in denoting future time' are understood here. The reasons for affixing लिङ् are such, as, cause and effect &c. mentioned in sûtra III. 3. 156 and 157 &c. The लृङ् is called the conditional tense. "It comes in the conditional sentences in which the non-performance of the action is implied; or where the falsity of the antecedent is implied as a matter of fact. It usually corresponds to the English pluperfect conditional, and must, in Sanskrit, be used in both the antecedent and the consequent clauses". Thus सुवृष्टिश्चेदभविष्यत् तदा सुभिक्षमभविष्यत् "if there had been good rain, then there would have been plenty of food; or if there were to be good rain then there would be plenty of food". It is implied that there was not good rain, nor consequent plenty: or that the occurrence of good rain is dubious, and the desirable consequence equally so. So also here, दक्षिणेन चेद्यास्यन् न शकटं पर्य्याभविष्यत् 'if he were to go by the right side, the carriage would not be upset'; यदि कमलकरं व्यहास्यन् न शकटं पर्य्याभविष्यत् 'if he were to call Kamalaka (which he will not), the carriage would not be upset'; नाभोज्यत भवान् घृतेन यदि मत्समीपम् आगमिष्यत् 'you would eat food with clarified butter, if you (were to) come to me (but you will not come).' All these sentences refer to future time. The non-upsetting is a future contingency and is an effect, the cause of which is the calling of Kamalaka. The speaker—having apprehended the cause and effect, and having also learned from other sources that such an effect will not take place, that is to say, that Kamalaka will not be called, and the carriage will be upset—has employed this conditional tense to express his idea. The whole sentence यदि कमलकरं व्यहास्यन् &c. really gives this sense:—That both actions, 'the calling' and 'the non-upsetting', which are subjects of a future time, and which are related as cause and effect, will not be completed; that neither Kamalaka will be called, nor the impending fate averted from the carriage. The sûtra may also be thus rendered according to Professor Böhtlingk:—In conditional sentence, which would require a Potential according to III. 3. 156 the conditional tense is used, if the sense is that of Future time, when the action is not complete. Thus भू + लृङ् = भू + ल् + तिप् (III. 1. 33. S. 2186.) = अ + भू + स्य + ति = अ + भो + स्य + ति = अ + भव् + इ + ष्य + ति = अभविष्यत् Singular. Dual. Plural. Third person. अभविष्यत् अभविष्यताम् अभविष्यन् Second person. अभविष्यः अभविष्यतम् अभविष्यत First person. अभविष्यम् अभविष्याव अभविष्याम Thus we have conjugated भू in all the लकारs except the Vedic लेट् The author now gives some rules about the adding of Prepositions to the verbs and the changes of meaning and conjugation which such addition induces. The first question is, where are those prepositions to be placed. In English they are generally placed after the verb; in the Vedas they are placed any where in the sentence; but Panini restricts the use in Classical Sanskrit by the following :—

pk: 230. The particles caled gati and upasarga are to be enployed berore the verbal rot: (that is to say, they are preriles). The word te has ben enployed to include the tern upasarga also. The list or prepositions has already ben given in the sûtra upasarga kriyayoge (i. 4. 59 and 60; s. 2 and 23). Thus pra + Bavani (inperative 1st Pers. sing.). ere aplies the rolowing sûtra.
ck: 230. the particles calet kati ant upasarka are to pe enployet perore the verpal rot: (that is to say, they are preriles). the tort te has pen enployet to inclute the tern upasarka also. the list or prepositions has alreaty pen kiven in the sûtra upasarka kriyayoke (i. 4. 59 ant 60; s. 2 ant 23). thus pra + pavani (inperative 1st pers. sink.). ere aplies the rolotink sûtra.
s: 2230. The particles called gati and upasarga are to be employed before the verbal root: (that is to say, they are prefixes). The word ते has been employed to include the term उपसर्ग also. The list of prepositions has already been given in the sûtra उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे (I. 4. 59 and 60; S. 22 and 23). Thus प्र + भवानि (Imperative 1st Pers. Sing.). Here applies the following sûtra.

pk: 231. The na or ani, the aril or the inperative, 1st Person, is changed into na, when it rolows a leter conpetent to cause such a change, standing in an upasarga. The word ani is the 1st person singular ternination or the inperative. Thus praBavani. sinilarly "Let us cultivate or sow." note:—Why do we say or the inperative? Observe pravapani patrani. ere ani is the neuter plural ternination, and the word neans prakirnani vrihyadini yesu tani. acording to Padananjari, the enploynent or the word low in the sûtra is redundant. ror without it also ani would have neant the inperative aril, and not the neuter ternination, on the nalin or arTavadgrahane &c. noreover in the noun pravapani, pra is not an upasarga at al, on the nalin yat kriyayukta pradaya tan prati gatyupasargasanjne Bavata Vart:— The upasarga dur is not to be treated as an upasarga, when satva or natva is to be erected. That is to say, the r or dur does not cause the subsequent s or n to be changed to s and n, respectively. Thus dusTiti, durBavani Vart:— The indeclinable word antar should be treated as an upasarga ror the aplication or (1) a viDi nanely the ariling or a by i. 3. 106. s. 3283. atascopasarge, as antar + Da + a = antarDa, (2) kiviDi nanely the aplication or ki by upasarge Go ki (i. 3. 92. s. 3270), as antar + Da + ki = antarDi (3) natva viDi as antarBavani
ck: 231. the na or ani, the aril or the inperative, 1st person, is chanket into na, then it rolots a leter conpetent to cause such a chanke, stantink in an upasarka. the tort ani is the 1st person sinkular ternination or the inperative. thus prapavani. sinilarly "Let us cultivate or sot." note:—thy to te say or the inperative? Opserve pravapani patrani. ere ani is the neuter plural ternination, ant the tort neans prakirnani vrihyatini yesu tani. acortink to patanancari, the enploynent or the tort lot in the sûtra is retuntant. ror tithout it also ani toult have neant the inperative aril, ant not the neuter ternination, on the nalin or artavatkrahane &c. noreover in the noun pravapani, pra is not an upasarka at al, on the nalin yat kriyayukta prataya tan prati katyupasarkasancne pavata Vart:— the upasarka tur is not to pe treatet as an upasarka, then satva or natva is to pe erectet. that is to say, the r or tur toes not cause the supsetuent s or n to pe chanket to s ant n, respectively. thus tustiti, turpavani Vart:— the inteclinaple tort antar shoult pe treatet as an upasarka ror the aplication or (1) a viti nanely the arilink or a py i. 3. 106. s. 3283. atascopasarke, as antar + ta + a = antarta, (2) kiviti nanely the aplication or ki py upasarke ko ki (i. 3. 92. s. 3270), as antar + ta + ki = antarti (3) natva viti as antarpavani
s: 2231. The न of आनि, the affix of the Imperative, 1st Person, is changed into ण, when it follows a letter competent to cause such a change, standing in an Upasarga. The word आनि is the 1st person singular termination of the Imperative. Thus प्रभवाणि. Similarly "Let us cultivate or sow." Note:—Why do we say 'of the Imperative'? Observe प्रवपाणि पात्राणि. Here आनि is the neuter plural termination, and the word means प्रकीर्णानि व्रीह्यादीनि येषु तानि. According to Padamanjari, the employment of the word लोट् in the sûtra is redundant. For without it also आनि would have meant the Imperative affix, and not the Neuter termination, on the maxim of अर्थवद्ग्रहणे &c. Moreover in the noun प्रवपाणि, प्र is not an upasarga at all, on the maxim यत् क्रियायुक्ताः प्रादयः तं प्रति गत्युपसर्गसंज्ञे भवतः Vart:— The Upasarga दुर् is not to be treated as an upasarga, when षत्व or णत्व is to be effected. That is to say, the र् of दुर् does not cause the subsequent स् or न् to be changed to ष् and ण्, respectively. Thus दुःस्थितिः, दुर्भवानि Vart:— The Indeclinable word अन्तर् should be treated as an upasarga for the application of (1) अ विधिः namely the affixing of अ by III. 3. 106. S. 3283. आतश्चोपसर्गे, as अन्तर् + धा + अ = अन्तर्धा, (2) किविधिः namely the application of कि by उपसर्गे घोः किः (III. 3. 92. S. 3270), as अन्तर् + धा + कि = अन्तर्धिः (3) णत्व विधि as अन्तर्भवाणि

pk: 232. in the renaining verbs, optionaly the na or ni is replaced by na, when it is preceded by an upasarga conpetent to cause the change; provided that, in the original enunciation, the verb has not an initial ka or Ka, nor ends with sa The words ne and upasargat are understod in the sûtra. The word sese neans verbs other than those nentioned in Vi. 4. 17 s. 285 nanely, other than gada, nada &c. Thus praniBavati or praniBavati, praniBinati or praniBinati Why do we say akaKadO "not begining with ka or Ka"? Observe praniKanati, pranikasati ere there is no change. Why do we say aBavanta: “not ending in ‹?›” ? Observe ‹?› Why do we say "in original enunciation"? so that the prohibition nay aply to rorns like pranicakara, pranicaKada, pratiseDayati (Vi. 2. 41 s. 295). ere, &c., do not begin with ‹?› or ‹?› nor does ‹?› end with ‹?› but with ‹?› (Vi. 2. 41) but in the Dhâtupâṭha the verb ‹?› and ‹?› begin with ‹?› and ‹?› and ‹?› ends with ‹?›, and hence the rule wil not aply. so also in ‹?› and ‹?› ron the rot ‹?› ere though the verb now ends with ‹?› by Vi. 2. 36, s. 295, yet in the original enunciation or Dhâtupâṭha, it ends with ‹?›. an objector nay say "what is the necesity or using the word optionaly in the sutra, when the present sûtra is governed by the word sanhitayan (Vi. 3. 14 s. 1035). so where there is no sanhitâ, there wil be no ‹?› change ; and as upasargas are not conpounded with the verb berore which they are placed, there is no conpulsory sanhitâ." To this we reply "no. The sanhitâ is conpulsory, even though the upasarga nay not be conpounded with the rot as here." The rolowing verse nentions this :— Verse. The sanhitâ is conpulsory (1) in a Pada (conplete word), (2) in a dhâtu (verb) preceded by an upasarga; and (3) in conpounds (sanâsa). But the sanhitâ is optional betwen the words or a sentence. The rot ‹?› neans “to be” in the Dhâtupâṭha, and "to increase" &c. al these neanings are nerely ilustrative. ror we rind in the elanple ‹?› "By sacririce eaven is produced or atained," that the rot has the neaning or to produce. so every rot has nany neanings. The upasargas when aded to a rot, do not give it a new neaning, but linit the particular neaning. in other words, out or nany neanings that a rot poseses, a particular neaning is speciried by the enploynent or a particular upasarga. Thus ‹?› "e conquers," anuBavati "e elperiences", aBiBavati "e dereats", ‹?› "it is posible", ‹?› "e is overpowered", udBavati "it springs rorth", pariBavati "e
ck: 232. in the renainink verps, optionaly the na or ni is replacet py na, then it is precetet py an upasarka conpetent to cause the chanke; provitet that, in the orikinal enunciation, the verp has not an initial ka or ka, nor ents tith sa the torts ne ant upasarkat are unterstot in the sûtra. the tort sese neans verps other than those nentionet in Vi. 4. 17 s. 285 nanely, other than kata, nata &c. thus pranipavati or pranipavati, pranipinati or pranipinati thy to te say akakatO "not pekinink tith ka or ka"? Opserve pranikanati, pranikasati ere there is no chanke. thy to te say apavanta: “not entink in ‹?›” ? Opserve ‹?› thy to te say "in orikinal enunciation"? so that the prohipition nay aply to rorns like pranicakara, pranicakata, pratisetayati (Vi. 2. 41 s. 295). ere, &c., to not pekin tith ‹?› or ‹?› nor toes ‹?› ent tith ‹?› put tith ‹?› (Vi. 2. 41) put in the thâtupâṭha the verp ‹?› ant ‹?› pekin tith ‹?› ant ‹?› ant ‹?› ents tith ‹?›, ant hence the rule til not aply. so also in ‹?› ant ‹?› ron the rot ‹?› ere thoukh the verp not ents tith ‹?› py Vi. 2. 36, s. 295, yet in the orikinal enunciation or thâtupâṭha, it ents tith ‹?›. an opcector nay say "that is the necesity or usink the tort optionaly in the sutra, then the present sûtra is kovernet py the tort sanhitayan (Vi. 3. 14 s. 1035). so there there is no sanhitâ, there til pe no ‹?› chanke ; ant as upasarkas are not conpountet tith the verp perore thich they are placet, there is no conpulsory sanhitâ." to this te reply "no. the sanhitâ is conpulsory, even thoukh the upasarka nay not pe conpountet tith the rot as here." the rolotink verse nentions this :— Verse. the sanhitâ is conpulsory (1) in a pata (conplete tort), (2) in a thâtu (verp) precetet py an upasarka; ant (3) in conpounts (sanâsa). put the sanhitâ is optional peten the torts or a sentence. the rot ‹?› neans “to pe” in the thâtupâṭha, ant "to increase" &c. al these neaninks are nerely ilustrative. ror te rint in the elanple ‹?› "py sacririce eaven is protucet or atainet," that the rot has the neanink or to protuce. so every rot has nany neaninks. the upasarkas then atet to a rot, to not kive it a net neanink, put linit the particular neanink. in other torts, out or nany neaninks that a rot poseses, a particular neanink is speciriet py the enploynent or a particular upasarka. thus ‹?› "e contuers," anupavati "e elperiences", apipavati "e tereats", ‹?› "it is posiple", ‹?› "e is overpoteret", utpavati "it sprinks rorth", paripavati "e suptu
s: 2232. In the remaining verbs, optionally the न of नि is replaced by ण, when it is preceded by an upasarga competent to cause the change; provided that, in the original enunciation, the verb has not an initial क or ख, nor ends with ष The words नेः and उपसर्गात् are understood in the sûtra. The word शेषे means verbs other than those mentioned in VIII. 4. 17 S. 2285 namely, other than गद, नद &c. Thus प्रणिभवति or प्रनिभवति, प्रणिभिनत्ति or प्रनिभिनत्ति Why do we say अकखादौ "not beginning with क or ख"? Observe प्रनिखनति, प्रनिकषति Here there is no change. Why do we say अभवान्त: “not ending in ‹?›” ? Observe ‹?› Why do we say "in original enunciation"? So that the prohibition may apply to forms like प्रणिचकार, प्रणिचखाद, प्रतिषेधयति (VIII. 2. 41 S. 295). Here, &c., do not begin with ‹?› or ‹?› nor does ‹?› end with ‹?› but with ‹?› (VIII. 2. 41) but in the Dhâtupâṭha the verb ‹?› and ‹?› begin with ‹?› and ‹?› and ‹?› ends with ‹?›, and hence the rule will not apply. So also in ‹?› and ‹?› from the root ‹?› Here though the verb now ends with ‹?› by VIII. 2. 36, S. 295, yet in the original enunciation or Dhâtupâṭha, it ends with ‹?›. An objector may say "what is the necessity of using the word optionally in the sutra, when the present sûtra is governed by the word संहितायाम् (VI. 3. 114 S. 1035). So where there is no samhitâ, there will be no ‹?› change ; And as upasargas are not compounded with the verb before which they are placed, there is no compulsory samhitâ." To this we reply "No. The samhitâ is compulsory, even though the upasarga may not be compounded with the root as here." The following verse mentions this :— Verse. The Samhitâ is compulsory (1) in a Pada (complete word), (2) in a dhâtu (verb) preceded by an upasarga; and (3) in compounds (Samâsa). But the Samhitâ is optional between the words of a sentence. The root ‹?› means “to be” in the Dhâtupâṭha, and "to increase" &c. All these meanings are merely illustrative. For we find in the example ‹?› "By sacrifice Heaven is produced or attained," that the root has the meaning of 'to produce.' So every root has many meanings. The upasargas when added to a root, do not give it a new meaning, but limit the particular meaning. In other words, out of many meanings that a root possesses, a particular meaning is specified by the employment of a particular upasarga. Thus ‹?› "He conquers," अनुभवति "He experiences", अभिभवति "He defeats", ‹?› "It is possible", ‹?› "He is overpowered", उद्भवति "It springs forth", परिभवति "He subdues." Therefore we have the following verse: By an upasarga the sense of the root is forcibly modified, such as the root ‹?› "to lose", in प्रहार means “a blow”, आहार “food”, संहार “destruction”, विहार “sport”, परिहार “avoidance”. Here ends the conjugation of the Parasmaipada root भू

pk: aTnanEPaDa. now we take up the conjugation or the rot eDr "to increase." The thirty-sil rots begining with eDa and ending with ‹?› are anudateta. That is, the rinal ‹?› in eDa &c. has anudata acent and is indicatory or it. rirst we conjugate it in law Present Tense, 3rd Pers. sing. Thus eD + ta = eD + sap + ta = eD + a + ta ere aplies the rolowing sutra :— 23. The substitute e replaces the last vowel, with the consonant that rolows it, or the atnanepada substitutes or that ‘la’ which has an indicatory w. Thus eD + ta = eD + t + e = eDate The 3rd Pers. Dual is eD + atan now aply the rolowing sutras :—
ck: atnanEpata. not te take up the concukation or the rot etr "to increase." the thirty-sil rots pekinink tith eta ant entink tith ‹?› are anutateta. that is, the rinal ‹?› in eta &c. has anutata acent ant is inticatory or it. rirst te concukate it in lat present tense, 3rt pers. sink. thus et + ta = et + sap + ta = et + a + ta ere aplies the rolotink sutra :— 23. the supstitute e replaces the last votel, tith the consonant that rolots it, or the atnanepata supstitutes or that ‘la’ thich has an inticatory t. thus et + ta = et + t + e = etate the 3rt pers. tual is et + atan not aply the rolotink sutras :—
s: ATMANEPADA. Now we take up the conjugation of the root एधृ "to increase." The thirty-six roots beginning with एध and ending with ‹?› are Anudatteta. That is, the final ‹?› in एध &c. has anudatta accent and is indicatory or इत्. First we conjugate it in लट् Present Tense, 3rd Pers. sing. Thus एध् + त = एध् + शप् + त = एध् + अ + त Here applies the following sutra :— 2233. The substitute ए replaces the last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, of the 'Atmanepada' substitutes of that ‘la’ which has an indicatory 'ट्'. Thus एध् + त = एध् + त् + ए = एधते The 3rd Pers. Dual is एध् + आताम् Now apply the following sutras :—

pk: 234. a sârvadhâtuka (i. 4. 13 s. 216) aril not having an indicatory p is like nit The aril atan is thererore nit, and consequently the rolowing sûtra aplies.
ck: 234. a sârvathâtuka (i. 4. 13 s. 216) aril not havink an inticatory p is like nit the aril atan is thererore nit, ant consetuently the rolotink sûtra aplies.
s: 2234. A Sârvadhâtuka (III. 4. 113 S. 2166) affix not having an indicatory प् is like ङित् The affix आताम् is therefore ङित्, and consequently the following sûtra applies.

pk: 235. ror the a being a portion or a sarvadhatuka Personal ending which is nit (i.e. ate, aTe, atan and aTan), coning arter a verbal sten ending in short a, there is substituted iy Thus eD + atan = eD + a + iy + tan = eD + itan (lopo vyorvali Vi. 1. 6 s. 873) = eDetan = eDete so also eDante The 2nd Pers. sing. is eD + Tas. now aplies the rolowing sûtra :—
ck: 235. ror the a peink a portion or a sarvathatuka personal entink thich is nit (i.e. ate, ate, atan ant atan), conink arter a verpal sten entink in short a, there is supstitutet iy thus et + atan = et + a + iy + tan = et + itan (lopo vyorvali Vi. 1. 6 s. 873) = etetan = etete so also etante the 2nt pers. sink. is et + tas. not aplies the rolotink sûtra :—
s: 2235. For the आ being a portion of a Sarvadhatuka Personal ending which is ङित् (i.e. आते, आथे, आताम् and आथाम्), coming after a verbal stem ending in short अ, there is substituted इय् Thus एध् + आताम् = एध् + अ + इय् + ताम् = एध् + इताम् (लोपो व्योर्वलि VI. 1. 66 S. 873) = एधेताम् = एधेते So also एधन्ते The 2nd Pers. Sing. is एध् + थास्. Now applies the following sûtra :—

pk: 236. The word se is the substitute or thas in those tenses that have an indicatory w. Thus eD + sap + Tas = eD + a + se = eDase sinilarly eDeTe, eDaDve The 1st Pers. sing. is eD + iw = eD + a + e (i. 4. 79 s. 23) = eDe (Vi. 1. 97 s. 191). so also eDavahe, eDanahe Conjugation or eD to increase in law Present Tense. 3rd Person. singular eDate Dual eDete Plural eDante 2nd Person. singular eDase Dual eDeTe Plural eDaDve 1st Person. singular eDe Dual eDavahe Plural eDanahe
ck: 236. the tort se is the supstitute or thas in those tenses that have an inticatory t. thus et + sap + tas = et + a + se = etase sinilarly etete, etatve the 1st pers. sink. is et + it = et + a + e (i. 4. 79 s. 23) = ete (Vi. 1. 97 s. 191). so also etavahe, etanahe concukation or et to increase in lat present tense. 3rt person. sinkular etate tual etete plural etante 2nt person. sinkular etase tual etete plural etatve 1st person. sinkular ete tual etavahe plural etanahe
s: 2236. The word 'se' is the substitute of 'thas' in those tenses that have an indicatory 'ट्'. Thus एध् + शप् + थास् = एध् + अ + से = एधसे Similarly एधेथे, एधध्वे The 1st Pers. Sing. is एध् + इट् = एध् + अ + ए (III. 4. 79 S. 2233) = एधे (VI. 1. 97 S. 191). So also एधावहे, एधामहे Conjugation of एध् 'to increase' in लट् Present Tense. 3rd Person. Singular एधते Dual एधेते Plural एधन्ते 2nd Person. Singular एधसे Dual एधेथे Plural एधध्वे 1st Person. Singular एधे Dual एधावहे Plural एधामहे

pk: liw Perect Tense. in liw we have eD + ta. ere aplies the rolowing :— 237. The aril an is used when liw rolows, arter a rot begining with a vowel (elcept a or a) and which has a heavy vowel, but not arter the rot rcC to go. The n or an is not it or indicatory. This we inrer ron an being taught with regard to the rots kas and as in sutra kaspratyayadananantre liwi (i. 1. 35 s. 2308) and dayayasasca (i. 1. 37 s. 2324). ir n were indicatory, then kas + an = ka + n + a + s = kas ; sinilarly as + an would have renained as; ror the rorce or indicatory n is to place the aril arter the penultinate vowel. so there would have ben no ned or teaching an arter kas and as rots, as it can produce no change in then. The ract, that it is so taught, leads to the conclusion (jñâpaka) that n is not indicatory. Thus eD + ta = eDan + ta now aplies the rolowing sutra.

s: लिट् Perfect Tense. In लिट् we have एध् + त. Here applies the following :— 2237. The affix आम् is used when लिट् follows, after a root beginning with a vowel (except अ or आ) and which has a heavy vowel, but not after the root ऋच्छ् 'to go'. The म् of आम् is not इत् or indicatory. This we infer from आम् being taught with regard to the roots कास् and आस् in sutra कास्प्रत्ययादाममन्त्रे लिटि (III. 1. 35 S. 2308) and दयायासश्च (III. 1. 37 S. 2324). If म् were indicatory, then कास् + आम् = का + म् + आ + स् = कास् ; similarly आस् + आम् would have remained आस्; for the force of indicatory म् is to place the affix after the penultimate vowel. So there would have been no need of teaching आम् after कास् and आस् roots, as it can produce no change in them. The fact, that it is so taught, leads to the conclusion (jñâpaka) that म् is not indicatory. Thus एध् + त = एधाम् + त Now applies the following sutra.

s: 2239. After a verb which ends with आम्, the verb 'to do' is annexed, when लिट् follows. After the verbs formed by taking the आम् augment, the perfect tense of कृञ् is added, to form their Perfect. The word कृञ् includes also the verbs भू and अस्. This we infer from the next sûtra आम्प्रत्ययवत्कृञोऽनुप्रयोगस्य (I. 3. 63 § 2240) from the fact that root कृञ् is specifically mentioned in it as an anuprayoga or auxiliary verb. For the sûtra I. 3. 63 is confined to कृञ् anuprayoga, implying thereby that there are other anuprayoga verbs also which are not governed by that sûtra I. 3. 63. In fact, the word कृञ् of the present sûtra is a Pratyâhâra or a formula, formed with the कृ of the sûtra भूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे संपद्यकर्तरि च्विः (V. 4. 50) and the ञ् of the sûtra कृञः सातिदाचिष्वलोपः (V. 4. 58), and thus, as a pratyâhâra कृञ् means and includes कृ, भू and अस् also. The roots कृ, भू and अस् denote action in general, while the bases in आम् such as कास् denote a particular action; and hence when the auxiliary कृ, भू or अस् is combined with आम् ending base, the two senses, namely the general sense of the auxiliary and the particular sense of the आम् ending verb, coalesce into one and give one full indivisible sense. Thus the syntactical connection is indissoluble or abheda-anvaya. Therefore, though the root संपद् is included in the Pratyâhâra कृञ् (for that pratyâhâra extends over eight sûtras V. 4. 50 to V. 4. 58 and संपद् is in sûtra V. 4. 53) yet that root is not applicable here, because it does not denote mere action and so can never form an abheda-anvaya with the main verb. Now the auxiliary कृञ् because it has an indicatory ञ् would take the affixes of the Parasmaipada when the fruit of the action accrues to another, by force of I. 3. 72; but it is prevented by the following.

s: 2240. When the principal verb that takes the affix आम् is Âtmanepadî, then the verb कृञ् when subjoined thereto as an auxiliary, will similarly be Âtmanepadî, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. This sûtra applies where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The question is what conjugation, parasmai or âtmanepada, do the auxiliaries take, in forming the periphrastic perfect? This sûtra supplies the answer. The auxiliary कृ follows the conjugation of its principal, the other auxiliaries do not. Thus the root एध् (to increase, prosper) is âtmanepadî, therefore in forming the periphrastic perfect, the verb कृ will be also in the âtmanepada. But the other auxiliaries भू and अस् retain their own peculiar conjugation and are not influenced by the conjugation of their principal. Thus एधांबभूव, एधामास. The word âm-pratyaya of the sûtra is a Bahuvrîhi, in which the force is that of atadguṇa-saṃvijñâna. That is, the root without the affix आम् is meant here, and not along with or qualified by the actual presence of आम्: it means 'that after which the affix आम् comes.' Of the verb kriñ, when subjoined to another as an auxiliary, the termination is that of the âtmanepada, like the verb that takes the affix आम् Note:—If this sûtra enjoined a rule of injunction (vidhi), then there would be the termination of the âtmanepada even in examples like ‹?› and ‹?› where the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. This is no valid objection to the present sûtra. It is to be interpreted in both ways, that is, both as a vidhi (a general injunction) and a niyama (a restrictive injunction). How is that to be done? Because the word "pûrvavat" of the immediately preceding Ashțâdhyâyî sûtra is to be read in the present aphorism also and thus there are two sentences. That is, there is âtmanepada of the auxiliary, when the Primary verb is âtmanepadî, but not the contrary. Thus चकास् (to appear with great splendour) is originally parasmaipadî and the auxiliary after it will be parasmaipada even when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, as चकासाञ्चकार (he appeared with great splendour). The second explanation, in that case, will be for the sake of establishing a niyama or restrictive rule. It has already been said above, that the auxiliary verbs कृ, भू and अस् are used in forming the periphrastic perfect. This is done by force of the aphorism III. 1. 40 § 2239 कृञ्चानुप्रयुज्यते लिटि, meaning, the verb kriñ is annexed in the perfect tense, to verbs that take आम्. In this sûtra (III. 1. 40) the word kriñ is a pratyâhâra, implying the verbs भू and अस्. It might be asked how is this pratyâhâra formed? The word kri is taken from the fourth word of sûtra V. 4. 50, भूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे &c. and the letter ñ is taken from sûtra V. 4. 58 कृञः सातिदाचिष्वलोपः &c. This is the way in which the commentators explain, how not only the verb kriñ is used as an auxiliary in forming the periphrastic perfect, but also the verbs भू and अस्. These three verbs denoting absolute action, unmodified by any especial condition, have in all languages been fixed upon as the best auxiliaries. It must, however, be noted that the word kriñ in this sûtra is not used as a pratyâhâra and consequently does not include the verbs भू and अस्. Therefore कृ requires here Âtmanepada termination. Thus एधाम् + कृ + त Now applies the following :—

s: 2246. The augment इट् is not added to that Ârdhadhâtuka affix, though beginning with a consonant except य, when it is joined to a root, which in the Grammatical system of Instruction (i.e. in the Dhâtupâṭha) is of one syllable, and is without accent (anudâtta). The word upadeśe qualifies both words ekâc, and anudâtta. Why do we say "which is monosyllabic?" So that the present rule should not apply to the same root when it is Intensive, with the affix यङ् elided. The Intensive of every verb is included in the enunciation of its root; and as a general rule, all the sûtras specified for the simple root, will apply to the Intensive also, with certain exceptions, as contained in the following:— शितपा शपानुबन्धेन निर्दिष्टं यद्गणेन च यदेकाच् ग्रहणं चैव पञ्चैतानि न यङ्लुकि "These five sorts of operations will not apply to Intensive-yaṅ-luk forms: 1. When the simple root is exhibited in the sûtra with श्तिप् as भू in VII. 4. 73 is shown as भवति In the Intensive, the perfect will be बोभवाञ्चकार and not भवाञ्चकार. 2. Where the root is exhibited with श as the root ‹?› in VII. 2. 49 is shown as ‹?›. There is ‹?› after the Desiderative of simple root, but not in Intensive. 3. When a simple root is exhibited with an anubandha, as शीङ् VII. 1. 6. 4. Where a gaṇa is mentioned in a rule, as श्यन् is taught after Divâdi-roots (III. 1. 69). It will apply to simple roots of Divâdi gaṇa, and not to their Intensive. 5. Lastly, where the word एकाच् is used in a sûtra. As VII. 2. 10. That rule will apply to एकाच् simple roots and not to their Intensives. This we infer because the word ekâc is used in the present sûtra. For had not this been the meaning, then there was no necessity of using the word "eka" in the sûtra, for the word अचः Abl. singular, by itself alone would have denoted one vowel; but by the additional use of the word "eka," the roots consisting of more than one vowel are excluded. Therefore, since we find that the last statement in the above verse (‹?› &c.) is supported by the inference to be drawn from the present sutra, we may conclude that the other four statements of the above verse are also authoritative and approved by Panini. See also sûtra II. 2. 19. Therefore the substitute root vadha (II. 4. 42) is not affected by the present rule; for though the root which replaces vadha in Dhatupatha is taught (upadesa) with one vowel, yet its substitute vadha is taught (upadesa) in the sutra II. 4. 42 with two vowels, hence it is not ekach: and so it gets the augment and we have vadhitum. But the prohibition applies to han as hantum and not hanitum. The anudatta roots will be shown later on by giving a list of them. Thus एधाम् + च + कृ + आ = एधाञ्चक्रे, and so also एधाञ्चक्राते The 2nd Pers. Pl. is एधाम् + चकृ + ध्वे Here applies the next sûtra.

s: 2247. The cerebral sound ‹?› is substituted in the room of the ध of षीध्वम्, and of the Personal-endings of the Aorist and the Perfect, after a stem ending in इण् (a vowel other than अ). Therefore एधाम् + चकृ + ध्वे = एधाञ्चकृढ्वे एधाञ्चक्रे एधाञ्चक्राते एधाञ्चक्रिरे Similarly the perfect of एध् may be formed by the auxiliary भू as well as by अस्. But in the case of भू and अस्, though the Principal Verb is atmanepadi, the auxiliaries will be conjugated as Parasmaipadi. Thus एधाञ्चकार and एधामास &c. First person singular is एधाञ्चक्रे. Now the perfect of अस् is formed by replacing अस् by भू; but here it is not so replaced, because then the rule about अस् being an auxiliary would be useless; as भू is already taught. Had it not been so, then instead of saying कृञ् चानुप्रयुज्यते &c., Panini would have used कृस चानुप्रयुज्यते or कृभूषानुप्रयुज्यते &c. But the fact that he uses the Pratyahara कृञ् shows that अस् must be conjugated as a distinct form, and not replaced by भू. Therefore though the Perfect of the Principal Verb is atmanepadi, yet the perfect of the Auxiliary Verb अस् is in parasmaipada. In other words, the forms आसाञ्चक्रे &c., can never stand alone, but must be used as auxiliaries. How is then अस् to be conjugated in the perfect? See below.

s: 2254. आट् acutely accented is the augment of a verbal stem beginning with a vowel, in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional. This debars the augment अट् Thus आट् + एध् + त = ऐधत The vṛiddhi is by VI. 1. 90. S. 262. लङ् or Imperfect. Singular. Dual. pk: 25. The personal endings or the Potential and the Benedictive take the augnent sīyuṭ. The w or siyuw is indicatory and shows that this augnent is to be placed berore the ariles (i. 1. 46 s. 38.) The u is ror the sake or pronunciation; this rule aplies to the Ātnanepada ariles. in the Potential, the sa or the augnent is elided by Vi. 2. 79. s. 21. and the y also, berore a personal-ending begining with a consonant, is droped acording to Vi. 1. 6. s. 873. in the Benedictive, the augnent retains its rul rorn, only so rar as it is not governed by Vi. 1. 6. Thus eD + siyuw + ta = eD + siy + ta = eD + iy + ta (Vi. 2. 79. s. 21.) = eD + i + ta (Vi. 1. 6. s. 873) = eDeta so also eDeyatan The 3rd Person Plural is rorned by the rolowing.
ck: 25. the personal entinks or the potential ant the penetictive take the auknent sīyuṭ. the t or siyut is inticatory ant shots that this auknent is to pe placet perore the ariles (i. 1. 46 s. 38.) the u is ror the sake or pronunciation; this rule aplies to the Ātnanepata ariles. in the potential, the sa or the auknent is elitet py Vi. 2. 79. s. 21. ant the y also, perore a personal-entink pekinink tith a consonant, is tropet acortink to Vi. 1. 6. s. 873. in the penetictive, the auknent retains its rul rorn, only so rar as it is not kovernet py Vi. 1. 6. thus et + siyut + ta = et + siy + ta = et + iy + ta (Vi. 2. 79. s. 21.) = et + i + ta (Vi. 1. 6. s. 873) = eteta so also eteyatan the 3rt person plural is rornet py the rolotink.
s: 2255. The personal endings of the Potential and the Benedictive take the augment 'sīyuṭ'. The ट् of सीयुट् is indicatory and shows that this augment is to be placed before the affixes (I. 1. 46 S. 38.) The उ is for the sake of pronunciation; this rule applies to the Ātmanepada affixes. In the Potential, the स of the augment is elided by VII. 2. 79. S. 2211. and the य् also, before a personal-ending beginning with a consonant, is dropped according to VI. 1. 66. S. 873. In the Benedictive, the augment retains its full form, only so far as it is not governed by VI. 1. 66. Thus एध् + सीयुट् + त = एध् + सीय् + त = एध् + ईय् + त (VII. 2. 79. S. 2211.) = एध् + ई + त (VI. 1. 66. S. 873) = एधेत So also एधेयाताम् The 3rd Person Plural is formed by the following.

pk: 256. The aril ran is the substitute or jha in the Liṅ (Potential and Benedictive). ck: 256. the aril ran is the supstitute or cha in the Liṅ (potential ant penetictive). the ca in other places, is replacet keneraly py anta (Vi. 1. 3. s. 2169.) put in lin, it is replacet py ran thus et + iy + ran = eteran so also 2nt person sinkular &c. are eteta, eteyatan, etetvan the 1st person sinkular is rornet py the rolotink.
s: 2256. The affix 'ran' is the substitute of 'jha' in the 'Liṅ' (Potential and Benedictive). The झ in other places, is replaced generally by अन्त (VII. 1. 3. S. 2169.) but in लिङ्, it is replaced by रन् Thus एध् + ईय् + रन् = एधेरन् So also 2nd Person singular &c. are एधेथाः, एधेयाथाम्, एधेध्वम् The 1st Person singular is formed by the following.

s: 2258. अत् is always substituted for the झ in the Atmanepada, when it is not preceded by a verbal stem ending in अ Thus ऐधिषत The 2nd Person sing. is ऐधिष्ठाः, Dual ऐधिषाथाम् In the Plural the ध of ध्वम् may be changed to ढ by applying VIII. 3. 78. S. 2247. Thus ऐधिढ्वम्. But some take the ‹?› of VIII. 3. 78. S. 2247 as not including the augment इट् and in that view the ध remains unchanged. Thus, ऐधिध्वम् By doubling ध, and ढ we get sixteen forms. Thus ऐधिध्वम्, ऐधिढ्वम् &c. -: 0 :- लुङ् or AORIST. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person ऐधिषि ऐधिष्वहि ऐधिष्महि 2nd Person ऐधिष्ठाः ऐधिषाथाम् ऐधिध्वम् or ऐधिढ्वम् 3rd Person ऐधिष्ट ऐधिषाताम् ऐधिषत लृङ् or Conditional. The Conditional presents no irregularities, and is similar to the Second Future. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person ऐधिष्ये ऐधिष्यावहि ऐधिष्यामहि 2nd Person ऐधिष्यथाः ऐधिष्येथाम् ऐधिष्यध्वम् 3rd Person ऐधिष्यत ऐधिष्येताम् ऐधिष्यन्त Here ends the conjugation of एध् in the Atmanepada. The rule of intermediate I It has been already taught before, that as a general rule the augment इट् is added to all affixes which begin with a consonant except (VII. 2. 85. S. 2184.) The roots that require this in their conjugation are Udâtta roots. It is desirable to collect together all roots which are anudatta and do not take this intermediate इ The following is a list of such roots :- 1. The root श्विति (श्वित्) should be included in this list, according to the opinion of Chandra and Durga. So also it is to be seen in the Bhashya. But Vyaghrabhuti has not read this root in Anit list. s: 2261. ए is substituted for अ, of a verbal stem standing between two simple consonants, the stem not having any different letter substituted in the reduplicate, when the ending थल् of the Perfect having the augment इट् follows, and thereby, the reduplicate is elided. By the phrase "no other consonant has been substituted" is meant "no other dissimilar in form consonant has been substituted". This we learn from the implication (jñâpaka) of sûtra VI. 4. 126 where exception is made in the case of ‹?› and ‹?›. Therefore, where the substitute is a different letter, then the reduplicate becomes âdeśâdi: otherwise not. If the form of the letter is not changed in the reduplicate, by substitution, then such substitution will not make the stem âdeśâdi. Thus by VIII. 4. 54, a letter (ग्, घ्, ड्, etc.) is substituted for a consonant (other than a nasal and a semi-vowel) in the reduplicate. Thus in the reduplicate is ‹?›, the first is also a substitute, for the substitute of ‹?› will be ‹?›. Such substitutes, however, are not meant here. Here, therefore, there will be the elision of the reduplicate and the ए substitution. Thus Similarly द + दध् + ए = देधे So also, 3. d. देधाते ; 3. p. देधिरे ; देधिषे, देथे, देधिवहे So also रेजतुः, रेजुः, येनतुः, येनुः, पेचतुः, पेचुः, देभतुः, देभुः Why 'for short अ'? Observe दिदिवतुः, दिदिवुः the इ is not replaced. Why do we say 'short अ'? Observe रासतुः, रासुः... Why do we say 'standing between two simple consonants'? Observe तस्तरतुः, तस्तरुः. Some say this example is not appropriate, for by I. 2. 5, the Perfect affixes are not कित् here, as they come after a conjunct consonant. The following is then more appropriate: सस्मरतुः ; and शशमतुः (Bhu. 586). Why do we say 'which has no substitute consonant in the reduplicate'? Observe चकाणतुः, चकाणुः, जघ्नतुः, जघ्नुः, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः The substitution referred to here must be caused by the affixes of the Perfect, therefore, the rule will apply to ‹?› and ‹?› though ‹?› and ‹?› are the roots, and ‹?› and ‹?› are changed to ‹?› and ‹?›. The substitution of a consonant or a consonant in the reduplicate, should not be here considered asiddha (VIII. 2. 54, read with VIII. 2. 1.). That substitution will be considered a substitution for the purposes of this sûtra and will make the stem, as is indicated by the special exception made in favor of ‹?› and ‹?› in sûtra VI. 4. 122. 8 दध लट् — दधते, दधेते, दधन्ते ; दधसे ; दधावहे, दधामहे लिट् — देधे, देधाते, देधिरे ; देधिषे ; देथे, देधिवहे लुट् — दधिता, दधितारौ, दधितारः लृट् — दधिष्यते लोट् — दधताम्, दधस्व, दधै लङ्—अदधत, अदधाताम्, अदधन्त ; अदधथाः, अदध्वम् अदधावहि विधिलिङ्—दधीत, दधीयाताम्, दधीध्वम्, दधीवहि आशीर्लिङ्—दधिषीष्ट अददिष्ट, अदधिषाताम् ; अददिष्टः, अददिषि लृङ्—अददिष्यत 9. स्कुदि “to jump, to raise or lift.” The i in स्कुदि is indicatory and by the following न् is inserted. Note :—According to Tarangini, the root means, 1. आप्लवनम्, or 2. उत्प्लवनम् or 3. उदयनम् According to Bhoja, it means उद्धरणम् also.

ck: 262. n is atet arter the votel or the rot, in a rot thich has an inticatory i in the thatupatha. thus skunta + sap + te = skuntate, skuntase, skunte perect :—puskunte, puskuntase, puskuntatve lut—skuntita lrt—skuntisyate lot—skuntatan lan—askuntata vitilin—skunteta asirlin—skuntisista lun—askuntista lrn—askuntisyata 10. viti “to pecone thite.” it is an intransitive verp. thus pres. vintate ; per. vivinte 1. vati “to salute, to praise, to torship.” pres. vantate, per. vavante ; lut vantita &c. note :—prahvatipurvapasanan is apivatanan noun vanta = pucaka 12. pati “to tel a kot nets, to pe rortunate, to pe klat, to honor, to shine.” pres. pantate, per. papante, lut—pantita &c. note:—noun patra “auspicious,” patra “shavink.” 13. nati to praise, to recoice, pe klat, to pe trunk, or pe prout, to slep or pe lasy, to shine, to nove (slotly), nate to pe lankuit, ant caye to pe victorious. it is intransitive elcept then neanink to praise or to nove. pres. nantate, per. nanante lut nantita nouns :—nantatu ; nantana, nanti, nanta 14. spati “to throp, viprate.” it is intransitive. pres. spantate, per. paspante (Vi. 4. 61 §. 259); lut spantita nouns :—spanta, spantana 15. kliti “to krieve, lanent.” this is a transitive verp. pres. klintate cEtran he lanents ror chaitra. per. ciklinte 16. nuta “to recoice.” pres. notate per. nunute no kuna pecause or (i. 2. 5). notate, notase, note lit—nunute, nunutate, nunutise, nunutitve lut—notita lrt—notisyate lot—notatan lan—anotata vitilin—noteta asirlin—notisista lun—anotista lrn—anotisyata nouns :—notana ; nota ; notira ; notanana ; nota 17. tata to kive, present. pres. tatate, per. tete — put this is a tronk rorn, as the rolotink sutra aplies.
s: 2262. न् is added after the vowel of the root, in a root which has an indicatory इ in the Dhatupatha. Thus स्कुन्द + शप् + ते = स्कुन्दते, स्कुन्दसे, स्कुन्दे Perfect :—पुस्कुन्दे, पुस्कुन्दषे, पुस्कुन्दध्वे लुट्—स्कुन्दिता लृट्—स्कुन्दिष्यते लोट्—स्कुन्दताम् लङ्—अस्कुन्दत विधिलिङ्—स्कुन्देत आशीर्लिङ्—स्कुन्दिषीष्ट लुङ्—अस्कुन्दिष्ट लृङ्—अस्कुन्दिष्यत 10. विदि “to become white.” It is an Intransitive verb. Thus Pres. विन्दते ; Per. विविन्दे 11. वदि “to salute, to praise, to worship.” Pres. वन्दते, Per. ववन्दे ; लुट् वन्दिता &c. Note :—प्रह्वतिपूर्वभाषणं is अभिवादनम् Noun वन्दः = पूजकः 12. भदि “to tell a good news, to be fortunate, to be glad, to honor, to shine.” Pres. भन्दते, Per. बभन्दे, लुट्—भन्दिता &c. Note:—Noun भद्र “auspicious,” भद्रा “shaving.” 13. नदि 'to praise, to rejoice, be glad, to be drunk, or be proud, to sleep or be lazy, to shine, to move (slowly),' मदे 'to be languid,' and जये 'to be victorious.' It is Intransitive except when meaning 'to praise' or 'to move.' Pres. नन्दते, Per. ननन्दे लुट् नन्दिता Nouns :—नन्दथुः ; नन्दनः, नन्दी, नन्दा 14. स्पदि “to throb, vibrate.” It is Intransitive. Pres. स्पन्दते, Per. पस्पन्दे (VII. 4. 61 §. 2259); लुट् स्पन्दिता Nouns :—स्पन्दः, स्पन्दनः 15. क्लिदि “to grieve, lament.” This is a Transitive verb. Per. चिक्लिन्दे 16. मुद “to rejoice.” Pres. मोदते Per. मुमुदे No guna because of (I. 2. 5). मोदते, मोदसे, मोदे लिट्—मुमुदे, मुमुदाते, मुमुदिषे, मुमुदिध्वे लुट्—मोदिता लृट्—मोदिष्यते लोट्—मोदताम् लङ्—अमोदत विधिलिङ्—मोदेत आशीर्लिङ्—मोदिषीष्ट लुङ्—अमोदिष्ट लृङ्—अमोदिष्यत Nouns :—मोदनः ; मोदः ; मोदिरः ; मोदमानः ; मोदा 17. दद 'to give, present.' Pres. ददते, Per. देदे — But this is a wrong form, as the following sutra applies.

pk: 263. e is not substituted ror the a or sas, dad, or or rots begining with v, or or such verbal stens in which the a results through the substitution or Guna, though the ariles or the Perect being kit or nit rolow, or the set Tal, nor is the reduplicate elided. s: 2263. ए is not substituted for the अ of शस्, दद्, or of roots beginning with व्, or of such verbal stems in which the अ results through the substitution of Guna, though the affixes of the Perfect being कित् or ङित् follow, or the set थल्, nor is the reduplicate elided. Thus (विशशसतुः, विशशसुः, विशशसिथ) दददे, दददाते, दददिरे लट् ददते, ददेते, ददन्ते लिट्—दददे, दददाते, दददिरे, दददिषे लुट् ददिता लृट् ददिष्यते लोट् ददताम् लङ् अददत विधिलिङ् ददेत आशीर्लिङ् ददिषीष्ट लुङ् अददिष्ट लृङ् अददिष्यत (Of roots beginning with व् :— ववनतुः, ववतुः, ववनिथ Of roots where अ is the result of guna, विववरतुः, विववरुः, विववरिथ, लुलविथ, पोपथिथ गुणशब्देन निर्वृत्तस्यात एवेह ग्रहणान्न तु सवर्णदीर्घे कृत आकारस्य चायमकार इति रत्वं प्रतिषिध्यते ) The अ of Guna may result either from the guna of ऋ changed to अर्, or of उ changed to ओ again changed to अव् as—लव 18. ष्वद, 19 ष्वर्द “to taste, to be liked, be sweet, be pleasant to the taste; to sweeten.” This root is Transitive when meaning “to experience” i. e. to taste, and it is Intransitive when meaning “liking” i. e. to be liked. According to Kshiraswami it means “to choose.” Transitive; as स्वदतेऽन्नम् 'he tastes food' It is Parasmaipadi here as a Vaidic Irregularity. Intransitive, as स्वदते सर्पिर्देवदत्ताय “curd is pleasant to the taste of Devadatta.” It is conjugated regularly. The initial ष् in ष्वद् is changed to स् by the following :—

pk: 264. There is the substitution or s in the ron or the s, being the initial or a verbal rot as enunciated in the Dhatupatha. Thererore svad is changed to svad, and this is not again changed to s, because or the prohibition or sutra Vi. 3. 1. §. 2128. Thus anusvadate liw :—tasvade sinilarly svardate, tasvarde Generaly the rot svada is preceded by the upasarga a, as asvadate ‹?› 20. urda to neasure, to play. By rorce or ca and, this rot also neans to taste. acording to sanati, the word nana does not nean neasure but ror hapines, and “to be cherul or easy.” Thus urda + sap + te ere aplies the rolowing sutra.
ck: 264. there is the supstitution or s in the ron or the s, peink the initial or a verpal rot as enunciatet in the thatupatha. thererore svat is chanket to svat, ant this is not akain chanket to s, pecause or the prohipition or sutra Vi. 3. 1. §. 2128. thus anusvatate lit :—tasvate sinilarly svartate, tasvarte keneraly the rot svata is precetet py the upasarka a, as asvatate ‹?› 20. urta to neasure, to play. py rorce or ca ant, this rot also neans to taste. acortink to sanati, the tort nana toes not nean neasure put ror hapines, ant “to pe cherul or easy.” thus urta + sap + te ere aplies the rolotink sutra.
s: 2264. There is the substitution of स् in the room of the ष्, being the initial of a verbal root as enunciated in the Dhatupatha. Therefore ष्वद् is changed to स्वद्, and this is not again changed to ष्, because of the prohibition of sutra VIII. 3. 111. §. 2128. Thus अनुस्वदते लिट् :—तस्वदे Similarly स्वर्दते, तस्वर्दे Generally the root स्वद is preceded by the upasarga आ, as आस्वदते ‹?› 20. ऊर्द 'to measure, to play.' By force of च 'and,' this root also means 'to taste.' According to Sanmati, the word मान does not mean 'measure' but for happiness, and “to be cheerful or easy.” Thus ऊर्द + शप् + ते Here applies the following sutra.

pk: 265. The short i or u or a rot is lengthened, when the verb has r or v as its penultinate leter, and is rolowed by a consonant. * The anuvriti or dirGa is curent ron the preceding ashtadhyayi sutra. The rot nust end in a consonant, and nust have r or v as preceding such consonant, ror the aplication or this rule. Thererore the u is lengthened. Thus we have. urdate ; liw :—urdancakre luw urdita lrw urdisyate low urdatan lan—Ordata viDilin—urdeta asirlin—urdisiswa lun—Ordiswa lrn—Ordisyata 21. kurda, 2. Kurda, 23. gurda, 24. guda in Kaiyata, Purushakara and naitreya the rot ‹?› is not round. in sanati, anogha, Vistara and Chandra al the rirst thre rots are given. in Charaka ‹?› is taken as one word neaning re. But acording to naitreya and Kasyapa, ‹?› is a separate rot. so al the rour rots nean "to play." Thus kurdate, cakurde ; Kurdate ; gurdate ; gudate, jugude in ruture the words law &c. wil orten be onited. it is to be understod that the words are aranged in that order. as, 1. kurdate, 2. cakurde ; 3. kurdita, 4. kurdisyate ; 5. kurdatan ; 6. akurdata, 7. kurdeta, 8. kurdisiswa, 9. akurdiswa, 10. akurdisyata 25. sudan "to rlow, eruse, pour out, distil." it is an intransitive verb in these senses. When neaning to strike, hurt, wound, kil, destroy, it is Transitive, as rorned by Gan or i. 1. 134. s. 2896. The causative has the aditional sense or "to cok, dres, season, prepare." as sudayati (sanskaroti) so also ahoratrani nasto viliswan sudantu (= draQan kurvantu) Thus sudate, Per. susude, luw = sudita noun suda: "a cok, a noras." nOTE:—Why do we say initial in the preceding sutra 264? Observe— karsati, krsati Why have these rots ben elhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial sa, when ror al practical purposes this sa is to be replaced by sa, would it not have ben easier to spel at once these words with a sa? This apears cunbersone no doubt, but the speling or the rots with sa is ror the sake or brevity. Certain rots change their sa into sa when preceded by certain leters: those rots which thus change their leter ror sa have ben at once taught with an initial sa, and thus by Vi. 3. 59 their sa is changed to sa. Thus ron sic instead or ‹?› we have ‹?› This rot is elhibited in the Dhatupatha with a sa, and thus we know that the sa nust be changed to sa. The short इ or उ of a root is lengthened, when the verb has र् or व् as its penultimate letter, and is followed by a consonant. * The anuvritti of दीर्घः is current from the preceding Ashtadhyayi sutra. It is an Intransitive verb in these senses. When meaning 'to strike, hurt, wound, kill, destroy,' it is Transitive, as formed by घञ् of III. 1. 134. S. 2896. The causative has the additional sense of "to cook, dress, season, prepare." As सूदयति (संस्करोति) So also अहोरात्राणि नस्तो विलिष्टं सूदन्तु (= द्राढं कुर्वन्तु) Thus सूदते, Per. सुषूदे, लुट् = सूदिता Noun सूद: "a cook, a morass." NOTE:—Why do we say 'initial' in the preceding sutra 2264? Observe— कर्षति, कृषति Why have these roots been exhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial ष, when for all practical purposes this ष is to be replaced by स, would it not have been easier to spell at once these words with a स? This appears cumbersome no doubt, but the spelling of the roots with ष is for the sake of brevity. Certain roots change their स into ष when preceded by certain letters: those roots which thus change their letter for ष have been at once taught with an initial ष, and thus by VIII. 3. 59 their स is changed to ष. Thus from षिच् instead of ‹?› we have ‹?› This root is exhibited in the Dhatupatha with a ष, and thus we know that the स must be changed to ष. Otherwise a list of such roots would have to be separately given. One must refer to the Dhatupatha for a list of the roots beginning with ष ; As a general rule, however, all monosyllabic roots beginning with a स and followed by a vowel or a dental letter have been taught in the Dhatupatha as beginning with an initial ष, as well as the following roots, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, and ‹?› though followed by ‹?› or ‹?›. The following roots though followed by a vowel or dental are not taught with an initial ष viz. ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› The "dental" here means the dental pure and simple. i. e. त, थ, द, ध, न and not dento-labial व This we infer from the inclusion of स्वद &c. in the list, which are followed by व Had व been included in the terms "dental" there was no necessity of teaching स्वद &c. separately. s: 2266. The s is dropped after the augment iṭ, if after this s the augment īṭ follows. Thus āt + iṣ + s + īt = āt + i + 0 + īt. Now this s is elided by VIII. 2. 28 (the present sūtra) of the Tripādī (the last three sections or Pādas of the Aṣṭādhyāyī). This elision would, therefore, be asiddha for the purposes of ekādeśa (VI. 1. 101 S. 85), and we could not combine the i of iṣ with the long ī as the zero intervenes. So the form would be ‹?› as in case of sūtra VIII. 3. 19 S. 67; for VIII. 2. 1 S. 12 applies. To prevent this anomaly, we have the following vārtika:— Vārt:— When ekādeśa is to be done, the elision of sic is to be considered siddha or valid. As आतीत् Here the sic is elided by ईटि (VIII. 2. 28). This elision is considered valid or siddha, and thus we have dīrgha single substitution of ī for i + 0 + ī in āt + i + 0 + īt = आतीत् This elision of s takes place when it is situated between iṣ on one side and īṭ on the other. When there is not īṭ following, there is no elision. आतीष्टाम्, अतिषुः The above examples आतीत्, आतीष्टाम् and अतिषुः may be either with or without a. The question is what is the true form of the Aorist without the augment a; is it अतीत् or आतीत्? According to the next sūtra it might have been आतीत्, but that sūtra is set aside by the sūtra following it.
