Pre. nanTati Per. nananTa, nananTiTa i rut. nanTina i rut. nanTisyati inp. ananTat inper. ananTat Pot. nanyet Bene. naTyat in the Benedictive, the n or nanTa is elided, because the aril yasuw is kit by i. 4. 104 s. 216; and because it is kit it causes the elision or n by Vi. 4. 24 s. 415. ad the rot ben read as naTi, there would have ben no elision or the nasal. in ract, there is such a rot also, as given below. se not 47. aor. ananTit Cond. ananyisyat Pasive naDyate Causative nanDayati aor. anananTat Desiderative ninanTisati inten. nanaTyate nan luk nananTiti or nananti inperect ananan Gerund naTitva or nanDitva nouns:—nanTa, nanTani This rot takes two acusatives, as suDan ksiraniDin naTnati 4 √ Kuthi, 45 √ Puthi, 46 √ Luthi, 47 √ nathi, to hurt, to surer pain, to injure, to strike, to kil, to be arlicted, to crush, to
ck: 269. an is optionaly the supstitute or cli arter that rot thich has an inticatory ir, then the parasnaipata terninations are enployet. nOtE:—thus ron citir (cit) to tivite, te terive, acitat, or tith sic acEtsit put te have acita in the atnanepata. so ron pitir—apitat, or apEtsit sinilarly cyutir, has its aorist either as acyotit, or acyutat, tith an aril. 40. √ chyutir, to sprinkle, to tet. pre.—scyotati per. cuscyota cyotati cucyoti i rut. scyotita i rut. scyotisyati inp. ascyotat pot. scyotet pene. scyutyat aorist acyutat, or acyotit pas. scyutyate caus. scyotayati aor. acuscyotat tesi. cuscyotisati or cuscyutisati inten. coscyutyate nan luk coscyotiti or coscyoti past part. pas. scyutita or scyotita ker. scyotitva 41. √ schyutir, to trickle, ose, elute, rlot; to shet, pour out, tiruse, scater. pre. scyotati per. cuscyota &c. like cyut aor. acyutat, tith an, or acyotit sone reat this rot tithout s, nanely as cyutir then the concukation til pe cyotati &c. as in natuscyutan krtaniva suputan nOtE:—the thole portion ir is inticatory, ant not i ant r separately. they can pe nate separately also py upatesecanunasika it (i. 3. 2. s. 3); thich til nake i inticatory; ant py halantyan (i. 3. 3. s. 1) thich til nake r inticatory. this is tone actualy py nathava in his thatuvriti. put the opcection to it is that ir r pe taken separately as inticatory, then there shoult pe an insertion or nasal py itito nun tato (Vi. 1. 58. s. ‹?›). 42. [pasane to shine]. sinilarly shoult pe concukatet the rot ‹?› this rot is not kiven in the sithanta. 43. nantha, to churn, to akitate, shake, stir rount or up, to crush, to krint totn, opres, arlict, testroy, kil. pre. nantati per. nananta, nanantita i rut. nantina i rut. nantisyati inp. anantat inper. anantat pot. nanyet pene. natyat in the penetictive, the n or nanta is elitet, pecause the aril yasut is kit py i. 4. 104 s. 216; ant pecause it is kit it causes the elision or n py Vi. 4. 24 s. 415. at the rot pen reat as nati, there toult have pen no elision or the nasal. in ract, there is such a rot also, as kiven pelot. se not 47. aor. anantit cont. ananyisyat pasive natyate causative nantayati aor. ananantat tesiterative ninantisati inten. nanatyate nan luk nanantiti or nananti inperect ananan kerunt natitva or nantitva nouns:—nanta, nantani this rot takes to acusatives, as sutan ksiranitin natnati 4 √ kuthi, 45 √ puthi, 46 √ Luthi, 47 √ nathi, to hurt, to surer pain, to incure, to strike, to kil, to pe arlictet, to crush, to krin
s: 2269. अङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि after that root which has an indicatory इर्, when the Parasmaipada terminations are employed. NOTE:—Thus from छिदिर् (छिद्) 'to divide,' we derive, अच्छिदत्, or with सिच् अच्छैत्सीत् But we have अच्छित्त in the Atmanepada. So from भिदिर्—अभिदत्, or अभैत्सीत् Similarly च्युतिर्, has its Aorist either as अच्योतीत्, or अच्युतत्, with अङ् affix. 40. √ Chyutir, to sprinkle, to wet. Pre.—श्च्योतति Per. चुश्च्योत च्योतति चुच्योति I Fut. श्च्योतिता II Fut. श्च्योतिष्यति Imp. अश्च्योतत् Pot. श्च्योतेत् Bene. श्च्युत्यात् Aorist अच्युतत्, or अच्योतीत् Pass. श्च्युत्यते Caus. श्च्योतयति Aor. अचुश्च्योतत् Desi. चुश्च्योतिषति or चुश्च्युतिषति Inten. चोश्च्युत्यते Yan luk चोश्च्योतीति or चोश्च्योत्ति Past Part. Pass. श्च्युतितः or श्च्योतितः Ger. श्च्योतित्वा 41. √ Schyutir, 'to trickle, ooze, exude, flow;' 'to shed, pour out, diffuse, scatter.' Pre. श्च्योतति Per. चुश्च्योत &c. like च्युत् Aor. अच्युतत्, with अङ्, or अच्योतीत् Some read this root without स्, namely as च्युतिर् Then the conjugation will be च्योतति &c. As in मधुश्च्युतं घृतमिव सुपूतम् NOTE:—The whole portion इर् is indicatory, and not इ and र् separately. They can be made separately also by उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् (I. 3. 2. S. 3); which will make इ indicatory; and by हलन्त्यम् (I. 3. 3. S. 1) which will make र् indicatory. This is done actually by Madhava in his Dhatuvritti. But the objection to it is that if र् be taken separately as indicatory, then there should be an insertion of nasal by इदितो नुम् धातोः (VII. 1. 58. S. ‹?›). 42. [भासने 'to shine']. Similarly should be conjugated the root ‹?› This root is not given in the Siddhanta. 43. Mantha, 'to churn,' to agitate, shake, stir round or up, to crush, to grind down, oppress, afflict, destroy, kill. Pre. मन्थति Per. ममन्थ, ममन्थिथ I Fut. मन्थिना II Fut. मन्थिष्यति Imp. अमन्थत् Imper. अमन्थत् Pot. मन्येत् Bene. मथ्यात् In the Benedictive, the n of मन्थ is elided, because the affix यासुट् is कित् by III. 4. 104 S. 2216; and because it is कित् it causes the elision of न् by VI. 4. 24 S. 415. Had the root been read as मथि, there would have been no elision of the nasal. In fact, there is such a root also, as given below. See Root 47. Aor. अमन्थीत् Cond. अमन्यिष्यत् Passive मध्यते Causative मन्धयति Aor. अममन्थत् Desiderative मिमन्थिषति Inten. मामथ्यते Yan luk मामन्थीति or मामन्ति Imperfect अमामन् Gerund मथित्वा or मन्धित्वा Nouns:—मन्थः, मन्थनी This root takes two accusatives, as सुधां क्षीरनिधिं मथ्नाति 44 √ Kuthi, 45 √ Puthi, 46 √ Luthi, 47 √ Mathi, 'to hurt, to suffer pain, to injure, to strike, to kill, to be afflicted, to crush, to grind down, to oppress.' Pre. कुन्थति Per. चुकुन्थ &c. like मन्थ as given above. In the Benedictive (आशीर्लिङ्) however, there will be no elision of the nasal. As कुन्ध्यात् ; पुन्ध्यात् &c. Similarly लुन्थति, पुन्थति and मन्थति Both roots मथि and मन्थ are read here, according to Saumata. Kshiraswami reads it समन्थे and not मथि even here, and gives the example मन्थ्नाति All these roots mean 'to injure.' As शत्रुमभिकुन्थति, मारयति 48. √ Shidha, 'to go, to ward, to drive.' Some read this with an indicatory short उ The initial ष् is changed to स् by धात्वादेः षः सः (VI. 1. 64 S. 2264). Pre. सेधति Per. सिषेध, सिषिधिथ; सिषेधिथ I Fut. सेधिता II Fut. सेधिष्यति Imp. असेधत् Pot. सेधेत् Ben. सिध्यात् Aor. असेधीत् Cond. असेधिष्यत् Passive सिध्यते Causative Pre. सेधयति, Aor. असीषिधत् Desiderative सिषिधिषति or सिषेधिषति Intensive सेषिध्यते Yan luk सेषेधीति or सेषेत्ति Gerund सेधित्वा or सिधित्वा Nouns सेधः 'a kind of tree,' सिद्धम् and सिद्धयन्तः When an upasarga like नि is added we have नि+सेधति The question arises should स् be changed to ष after नि ? The Sutra VIII. 3. 111, S. 2125 requires that there should be no substitution, since सेधति is the beginning of a Pada. To this, however, the following sutra makes an exception. That sutra (VIII. 3. 65) and the five sutras that follow it in the order of Ashtadhyayi are given together here once for all, to show when स्

pk: 270. sa is substituted ror sa, arter an alterant i and u or an upasarga in the rolowing verbs: su (sunoti), su (suvati), so (syati Vi. 3. 71), stu (stOti Vi. 3. 89), stuB (stoBate), sTa, senaya (Denoninative), siD (seDati), sic, sanj and svanj Thus susoti susava, prasusava syati, aBisyati stu, aBiswOti stuB, aBiswoBate sTa, aBisWasyati senaya, aBisenayati seDa, aBiseDati, pariseDati, paryaseDat sic, aBisincati sanj, aBisajati svanj, parisvajate nOTE:—The rot siD is elhibited in the sutra as seDa with vikarana, thus debaring siDu—siDyati
ck: 270. sa is supstitutet ror sa, arter an alterant i ant u or an upasarka in the rolotink verps: su (sunoti), su (suvati), so (syati Vi. 3. 71), stu (stOti Vi. 3. 89), stup (stopate), sta, senaya (tenoninative), sit (setati), sic, sanc ant svanc thus susoti susava, prasusava syati, apisyati stu, apistOti stup, apistopate sta, apistasyati senaya, apisenayati seta, apisetati, parisetati, paryasetat sic, apisincati sanc, apisacati svanc, parisvacate nOtE:—the rot sit is elhipitet in the sutra as seta tith vikarana, thus teparink situ—sityati
s: 2270. ष is substituted for स, after an alterant इ and उ of an upasarga in the following verbs: षु (सुनोति), सू (सुवति), सो (स्यति VII. 3. 71), स्तु (स्तौति VII. 3. 89), स्तुभ् (स्तोभते), स्था, सेनय (Denominative), सिध् (सेधति), सिच्, सञ्ज् and स्वञ्ज् Thus सुषोति सुषाव, प्रसुषाव स्यति, अभिष्यति स्तु, अभिष्टौति स्तुभ्, अभिष्टोभते स्था, अभिष्ठास्यति सेनय, अभिषेणयति सेध, अभिषेधति, परिषेधति, पर्यषेधत् सिच्, अभिषिञ्चति सञ्ज्, अभिषजति स्वञ्ज्, परिष्वजते NOTE:—The root सिध् is exhibited in the sutra as सेध with vikarana, thus debarring षिधु—सिध्यति

pk: 271. The sa or svaska is changed to sa arter an upasarga having an i or u, but not arter prati Thus parisyaskati, pranisyaskati, nisasvaska, susvaska The second s renains unchanged in the Perect by Vi. 3. 18. Why do we say but not arter prati ? Observe pratisvaskati
ck: 271. the sa or svaska is chanket to sa arter an upasarka havink an i or u, put not arter prati thus parisyaskati, pranisyaskati, nisasvaska, susvaska the secont s renains unchanket in the perect py Vi. 3. 18. thy to te say put not arter prati ? Opserve pratisvaskati
s: 2271. The स of ष्वष्क is changed to ष after an Upasarga having an इ or उ, but not after प्रति Thus परिष्यष्कति, प्रणिष्यष्कति, निषष्वाष्क, सुष्वष्क The second ष् remains unchanged in the Perfect by VIII. 3. 118. Why do we say 'but not after प्रति' ? Observe प्रतिष्वष्कति

pk: 272. The s or stanBa (read in sutra i. 1. 82 s. 25.) is changed into sa arter an upasarga, having an i or u. Thus aBiswanBati pariswanBati The word aprate or the last sûtra is not to be read here. ence we have rorns like:— pratiswanBati ‹?› ‹?› The present sûtra is nade a separate rule, when it could wel have ben included in the inediately preceding one, as sadistanBo ror two reasons. rirst that the anuvriti or stanBa alone should run into the nelt sûtra. secondly that it should not be restricted by the word aprate pratiswanBana
ck: 272. the s or stanpa (reat in sutra i. 1. 82 s. 25.) is chanket into sa arter an upasarka, havink an i or u. thus apistanpati paristanpati the tort aprate or the last sûtra is not to pe reat here. ence te have rorns like:— pratistanpati ‹?› ‹?› the present sûtra is nate a separate rule, then it coult tel have pen inclutet in the inetiately precetink one, as satistanpo ror to reasons. rirst that the anuvriti or stanpa alone shoult run into the nelt sûtra. secontly that it shoult not pe restrictet py the tort aprate pratistanpana
s: 2272. The s of स्तम्भ (read in sutra III. 1. 82 S. 2555.) is changed into ष after an upasarga, having an i or u. Thus अभिष्टम्भाति परिष्टम्भाति The word अप्रतेः of the last sûtra is not to be read here. Hence we have forms like:— प्रतिष्टम्भाति ‹?› ‹?› The present sûtra is made a separate rule, when it could well have been included in the immediately preceding one, as सदिस्तम्भोः for two reasons. First that the anuvritti of स्तम्भ alone should run into the next sûtra. Secondly that it should not be restricted by the word अप्रतेः प्रतिष्टम्भनः

pk: 273. The s or stanBa is changed into sa arter the preposition ava in the sense or suport and contiguity. note:—The word alanbana neans suport, reruge, that upon which anything depends or leans, avidura neans the state or not being dura or rar or, i.e. to be contiguous. Thus avaswaByaste e renains leaning upon a star &c., avaswaBya tisWati so also in the sense or to be near, as avaswabDa sena the arny near at hand, ‹?› se V. 2. 13. avaswaByaste—nitva san sanipe caste
ck: 273. the s or stanpa is chanket into sa arter the preposition ava in the sense or suport ant contikuity. note:—the tort alanpana neans suport, reruke, that upon thich anythink tepents or leans, avitura neans the state or not peink tura or rar or, i.e. to pe contikuous. thus avastapyaste e renains leanink upon a star &c., avastapya tistati so also in the sense or to pe near, as avastapta sena the arny near at hant, ‹?› se V. 2. 13. avastapyaste—nitva san sanipe caste
s: 2273. The स् of स्तम्भ is changed into ष after the preposition अव in the sense of 'support' and 'contiguity.' Note:—The word 'आलम्बन' means 'support, refuge, that upon which anything depends or leans,' 'अविदूर' means 'the state of not being दूर or far off, i.e. to be contiguous.' Thus अवष्टभ्यास्ते 'He remains leaning upon a staff &c.,' अवष्टभ्य तिष्ठति So also in the sense of to be near, as अवष्टब्धा सेना 'the army near at hand,' ‹?› See V. 2. 13. अवष्टभ्यास्ते—मित्वा सन् समीपे चास्ते

pk: 274. The sa is substituted ror the sa or svan, arter vi and ava, when the sense is to snack while eating. Thus viswanati, viswanati, viswanayate, avaswanati, avaswanati, avaswanayate That is, he nakes sound while eating, he eats with a snack.
ck: 274. the sa is supstitutet ror the sa or svan, arter vi ant ava, then the sense is to snack thile eatink. thus vistanati, vistanati, vistanayate, avastanati, avastanati, avastanayate that is, he nakes sount thile eatink, he eats tith a snack.
s: 2274. The ष is substituted for the स of स्वन्, after वि and अव, when the sense is 'to smack while eating.' Thus विष्टनति, विष्टणति, विष्टनायते, अवष्टनति, अवष्टणति, अवष्टनायते That is, he makes sound while eating, he eats with a smack.

pk: 275. [sa] is substituted ror the sa or sev, sita, saya, sivu, saha, the augnent suw, stu and svanj, arter the prepositions pari, ni, and vi. Thus niseDati The rot sevr to serve belongs to the Bhvâdi clas. The sita is the Past Participle or sin banDane, and saya is the noun derived ron the sane rot with the aril ac; sivu is a Divâdi rot. note:—The rot sita or this rule is an inportant landnark. al rots enunerated in the sutras Vi. 3. 65 to Vi. 3. 70 change their sa to sa even when the augnent aw intervenes, but not so the rot sita and those that rolow it. This is taught in the nelt sûtra.
ck: 275. [sa] is supstitutet ror the sa or sev, sita, saya, sivu, saha, the auknent sut, stu ant svanc, arter the prepositions pari, ni, ant vi. thus nisetati the rot sevr to serve pelonks to the phvâti clas. the sita is the past participle or sin pantane, ant saya is the noun terivet ron the sane rot tith the aril ac; sivu is a tivâti rot. note:—the rot sita or this rule is an inportant lantnark. al rots enuneratet in the sutras Vi. 3. 65 to Vi. 3. 70 chanke their sa to sa even then the auknent at intervenes, put not so the rot sita ant those that rolot it. this is taukht in the nelt sûtra.
s: 2275. [ष] is substituted for the स of सेव्, सित, सय, सिवु, सह, the augment सुट्, स्तु and स्वञ्ज्, after the prepositions परि, नि, and वि. Thus निषेधति The root षेवृ 'to serve' belongs to the Bhvâdi class. The सित is the Past Participle of षिञ् बन्धने, and सय is the noun derived from the same root with the affix अच्; सिवु is a Divâdi root. Note:—The root सित of this rule is an important landmark. All roots enumerated in the sutras VIII. 3. 65 to VIII. 3. 70 change their स to ष even when the augment अट् intervenes, but not so the root सित and those that follow it. This is taught in the next sûtra.

pk: 276. (The substitution or sa, ror s, as taught hereinberore wil take place) ror al rots up to sita elclusive in Vi. 3. 70 even when the augnent aw intervenes (betwen the sa and the alterant leter). This sûtra governs al the rirten rots given in the preceding sutras ron Vi. 3. 65. Thus with the augnent aw we have nyaseDat in the inperect, nyaseDit in the aorist and nyaseDisyat in the Conditional.
ck: 276. (the supstitution or sa, ror s, as taukht hereinperore til take place) ror al rots up to sita elclusive in Vi. 3. 70 even then the auknent at intervenes (peten the sa ant the alterant leter). this sûtra koverns al the rirten rots kiven in the precetink sutras ron Vi. 3. 65. thus tith the auknent at te have nyasetat in the inperect, nyasetit in the aorist ant nyasetisyat in the contitional.
s: 2276. (The substitution of ष, for स्, as taught hereinbefore will take place) for all roots up to सित exclusive in VIII. 3. 70 even when the augment अट् intervenes (between the स and the alterant letter). This sûtra governs all the fifteen roots given in the preceding sutras from VIII. 3. 65. Thus with the augment अट् we have न्यषेधत् in the Imperfect, न्यषेधीत् in the Aorist and न्यषेधिष्यत् in the Conditional.

pk: 27. in sya &c. up to sita elclusive (Vi. 3. 65 to Vi. 3. 70), this sa substitution takes place then also, when the reduplicate intervenes, and the sa or the reduplicate is also changed to sa. Thus siseDa, sisiDatu in the Perect.
ck: 27. in sya &c. up to sita elclusive (Vi. 3. 65 to Vi. 3. 70), this sa supstitution takes place then also, then the retuplicate intervenes, ant the sa or the retuplicate is also chanket to sa. thus siseta, sisitatu in the perect.
s: 2277. In स्या &c. up to सित exclusive (VIII. 3. 65 to VIII. 3. 70), this ष substitution takes place then also, when the reduplicate intervenes, and the स of the reduplicate is also changed to ष. Thus सिषेध, सिषिधतुः in the Perfect.

pk: 278. The s or the verb seDa is not changed to sa when the neaning is that or noving. This is an elception to Vi. 3. 65 s. 270. Thus gangan viseDati siDu 49 sastre nangalye ca sastran sasanan 49. Şhidha, To ordain, conand, instruct, to turn out wel or auspiciously. sastra neans conand, rule. This rot has an indicatory long u, the rorce or which is given in the nelt sûtra. it is conjugated like the preceding rot ‹?› no. 48 elcept in so rar as the erect or the indicatory u nakes the change. luw—seDita lrw—seDisyati in the 2nd Person Dual we have sisiDaTu with the augnent iw aded to Tus. But this augnent is optional, owing to the rot having an indicatory u as given below.
ck: 278. the s or the verp seta is not chanket to sa then the neanink is that or novink. this is an elception to Vi. 3. 65 s. 270. thus kankan visetati situ 49 sastre nankalye ca sastran sasanan 49. Şhitha, to ortain, conant, instruct, to turn out tel or auspiciously. sastra neans conant, rule. this rot has an inticatory lonk u, the rorce or thich is kiven in the nelt sûtra. it is concukatet like the precetink rot ‹?› no. 48 elcept in so rar as the erect or the inticatory u nakes the chanke. lut—setita lrt—setisyati in the 2nt person tual te have sisitatu tith the auknent it atet to tus. put this auknent is optional, otink to the rot havink an inticatory u as kiven pelot.
s: 2278. The स् of the verb षेध is not changed to ष when the meaning is that of moving. This is an exception to VIII. 3. 65 S. 2270. Thus गङ्गां विसेधति षिधू ४९ शास्त्रे माङ्गल्ये च शास्त्रं शासनम् 49. Şhidha, 'To ordain, command, instruct,' 'to turn out well or auspiciously'. शास्त्र means command, rule. This root has an indicatory long ऊ, the force of which is given in the next sûtra. It is conjugated like the preceding root ‹?› No. 48 except in so far as the effect of the indicatory ऊ makes the change. लुट्—सेधिता लृट्—सेधिष्यति In the 2nd Person Dual we have सिषिधथुः with the augment इट् added to थुस्. But this augment is optional, owing to the root having an indicatory ऊ as given below.

pk: 279. a Valâdi-Ârdhadhâtuka aril optionaly takes iṭ arter svṛi, arter the two rots sû (sûti and sûyati), arter dhûñ and arter a rot which has an indicatory long û. Thus siseD + Ta now aplies the nelt sûtra.
ck: 279. a Valâti-Ârthathâtuka aril optionaly takes iṭ arter svṛi, arter the to rots sû (sûti ant sûyati), arter thûñ ant arter a rot thich has an inticatory lonk û. thus siset + ta not aplies the nelt sûtra.
s: 2279. A Valâdi-Ârdhadhâtuka affix optionally takes 'iṭ' after svṛi, after the two roots 'sû' (sûti and sûyati), after 'dhûñ' and after a root which has an indicatory long 'û'. Thus सिषेध् + थ Now applies the next sûtra.

pk: 280. Dha is substituted ror ta or tha coning arter jha, bha, gha, ḍha or dha (jhash), but not arter the rot dhâ (dadh). note:—Thus ron laB, we have labDa, labDun, labDavyan, alabDa, alapsata Thus siseD + Ta = siseD + Da = sisedDa The other rorn is siseDiTa sisiDatu or sisiDyatu luw—seDita or sodDa lrw—seDisyati or setsyati low—seDatu lun—asEtsit in the 3rd Person Dual we have aseD + s + tan now aplies the nelt sûtra, which causes the elision or s
ck: 280. tha is supstitutet ror ta or tha conink arter cha, pha, kha, ḍha or tha (chash), put not arter the rot thâ (tath). note:—thus ron lap, te have lapta, laptun, laptavyan, alapta, alapsata thus siset + ta = siset + ta = siseta the other rorn is sisetita sisitatu or sisityatu lut—setita or sota lrt—setisyati or setsyati lot—setatu lun—asEtsit in the 3rt person tual te have aset + s + tan not aplies the nelt sûtra, thich causes the elision or s
s: 2280. 'Dha' is substituted for 'ta' or 'tha' coming after 'jha', 'bha', 'gha', 'ḍha' or 'dha' (jhash), but not after the root dhâ (dadh). Note:—Thus from लभ्, we have लब्धा, लब्धुम्, लब्धव्यम्, अलब्ध, अलप्सत Thus सिषेध् + थ = सिषेध् + ध = सिषेद्ध The other form is सिषेधिथ सिषिधतुः or सिषिध्यतुः लुट्—सेधिता or सोद्धा लृट्—सेधिष्यति or सेत्स्यति लोट्—सेधतु लुङ्—असैत्सीत् In the 3rd Person Dual we have असेध् + स् + ताम् Now applies the next sûtra, which causes the elision of स्

pk: 281. The s is elided when it is preceded by a jhal consonant (any consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals), and is rolowed by an aril begining with a jhal consonant. Thus aseD + s + tan = asedDan Thererore the rul conjugation in aorist is:— singular Dual Plural. Third Person asetsit asedDan asetsu second Person asetsi asedDan asedDa rirst Person asetsan asetsva asetsna second rorn. Third Person aseDit aseDiswan aseDisu second Person aseDi aseDiswan aseDiswa rirst Person aseDisan aseDisva aseDisna The Desiderative is siseDisati 50. to eat. The ‹?› is indicatory. 51. The rorce or the indicatory ‹?› is that we have no shortening or the penultinate in ‹?› Desiderative : ciKadisati intensive : caKadyate naṅ-luk caKaditi or ‹?› Causative : Kadayati Past Participle Kadita noun Kadaka 51. Kad to be steady, rirn, to strike, hurt, kil. By the rorce or the word and, it neans to eat also. it is intransitive when neaning to be rirn, — law—Kadati liw—caKada ere we have caused the Vṛidhi or the a or Kad by the rolowing sūtra.
ck: 281. the s is elitet then it is precetet py a chal consonant (any consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals), ant is rolotet py an aril pekinink tith a chal consonant. thus aset + s + tan = asetan thererore the rul concukation in aorist is:— sinkular tual plural. thirt person asetsit asetan asetsu secont person asetsi asetan aseta rirst person asetsan asetsva asetsna secont rorn. thirt person asetit asetistan asetisu secont person aseti asetistan asetista rirst person asetisan asetisva asetisna the tesiterative is sisetisati 50. to eat. the ‹?› is inticatory. 51. the rorce or the inticatory ‹?› is that te have no shortenink or the penultinate in ‹?› tesiterative : cikatisati intensive : cakatyate naṅ-luk cakatiti or ‹?› causative : katayati past participle katita noun kataka 51. kat to pe steaty, rirn, to strike, hurt, kil. py the rorce or the tort ant, it neans to eat also. it is intransitive then neanink to pe rirn, — lat—katati lit—cakata ere te have causet the Vṛithi or the a or kat py the rolotink sūtra.
s: 2281. The 's' is elided when it is preceded by a jhal consonant (any consonant except semi-vowels and nasals), and is followed by an affix beginning with a jhal consonant. Thus असेध् + स् + ताम् = असेद्धाम् Therefore the full conjugation in Aorist is:— Singular Dual Plural. Third Person असेत्सीत् असेद्धाम् असेत्सुः Second Person असेत्सीः असेद्धम् असेद्ध First Person असेत्सम् असेत्स्व असेत्स्म Second Form. Third Person असेधीत् असेधिष्टाम् असेधिषुः Second Person असेधीः असेधिष्टम् असेधिष्ट First Person असेधिषम् असेधिष्व असेधिष्म The Desiderative is सिषेधिषति 50. 'to eat. The ‹?› is indicatory. 51. The force of the indicatory ‹?› is that we have no shortening of the penultimate in ‹?› Desiderative : चिखादिषति Intensive : चाखाद्यते Yaṅ-luk चाखादीति or ‹?› Causative : खादयति Past Participle खादितः Noun खादकः 51. खद् 'to be steady, firm,' 'to strike, hurt, kill.' By the force of the word 'and,' it means 'to eat' also. It is Intransitive when meaning 'to be firm,' — लट्—खदति लिट्—चखाद Here we have caused the Vṛiddhi of the अ of खद् by the following sūtra.

pk: 282. in a sten ending in a consonant with an a inediately preceding it, the Vṛidhi is substituted ror such a when an aril having an indicatory ñ or ṇ rolows. Thererore Kad + nal = caKada in the rirst Person singular, however, this Vṛidhi is optional by the nelt sūtra.
ck: 282. in a sten entink in a consonant tith an a inetiately precetink it, the Vṛithi is supstitutet ror such a then an aril havink an inticatory ñ or ṇ rolots. thererore kat + nal = cakata in the rirst person sinkular, hotever, this Vṛithi is optional py the nelt sūtra.
s: 2282. In a stem ending in a consonant with an 'a' immediately preceding it, the Vṛiddhi is substituted for such 'a' when an affix having an indicatory 'ñ' or 'ṇ' follows. Therefore खद् + णल् = चखाद In the First Person singular, however, this Vṛiddhi is optional by the next sūtra.

pk: 283. The ending or the rirst Person singular in the Perect optionaly acts as ṇit. The Vṛidhi is optional, as caKada or caKada The other Tenses are conjugated like Kada in the aorist (lun) there are two rorns caused by the rolowing :—
ck: 283. the entink or the rirst person sinkular in the perect optionaly acts as ṇit. the Vṛithi is optional, as cakata or cakata the other tenses are concukatet like kata in the aorist (lun) there are to rorns causet py the rolotink :—
s: 2283. The ending of the First Person Singular in the Perfect optionally acts as ṇit. The Vṛiddhi is optional, as चखाद or चखद The other Tenses are conjugated like खाद In the Aorist (लुङ्) there are two forms caused by the following :—

pk: 284. Berore an iṭ begining s-aorist or the Parasnaipada, the short a or the rot gets optionaly Vṛidhi, when the sten begins with a consonant, and the a is prosodialy short by being rolowed by a sinple consonant. Thus aKadit or aKadit Causative : Kadayati intensive asaKadyate nouns : Kadi 52. bada (b) to be steady, rirn. The ba is the labial b, and not va or v. liw—babada, bedatu, bediTa, babada or babada lun—abadit or abadit its conjugation is like Kada in the Perect we have ‹?› as the rot in reduplication retains ba without any change. so there is etva as wel as the reduplication elision. nouns :— badaran, badari naitreya reads this rot as banda e rorns bedatu by eliding na, and then etva and elision or reduplication. This is incorect, acording to nādhava : because the rot being sanyoganta (ending in a conjunct consonant) like anc &c., the endings or the perect are not kit There is another rot ‹?› given rurther on. 53. gada to speak. law—gadati liw—jagada luw—gadita &c. like Kada But in pra+ni+gadati, we have the rolowing.
ck: 284. perore an iṭ pekinink s-aorist or the parasnaipata, the short a or the rot kets optionaly Vṛithi, then the sten pekins tith a consonant, ant the a is prosotialy short py peink rolotet py a sinple consonant. thus akatit or akatit causative : katayati intensive asakatyate nouns : kati 52. pata (p) to pe steaty, rirn. the pa is the lapial p, ant not va or v. lit—papata, petatu, petita, papata or papata lun—apatit or apatit its concukation is like kata in the perect te have ‹?› as the rot in retuplication retains pa tithout any chanke. so there is etva as tel as the retuplication elision. nouns :— pataran, patari naitreya reats this rot as panta e rorns petatu py elitink na, ant then etva ant elision or retuplication. this is incorect, acortink to nāthava : pecause the rot peink sanyokanta (entink in a concunct consonant) like anc &c., the entinks or the perect are not kit there is another rot ‹?› kiven rurther on. 53. kata to speak. lat—katati lit—cakata lut—katita &c. like kata put in pra+ni+katati, te have the rolotink.
s: 2284. Before an 'iṭ' beginning 's'-Aorist of the Parasmaipada, the short 'a' of the root gets optionally Vṛiddhi, when the stem begins with a consonant, and the 'a' is prosodially short by being followed by a simple consonant. Thus अखादीत् or अखदीत् Causative : खादयति Intensive अशाखाद्यते Nouns : खादिः 52. बद (ब्) 'to be steady, firm.' The ब is the labial b, and not व or v. लिट्—बबाद, बेदतुः, बेदिथ, बबाद or बबद लुङ्—अबादीत् or अबदीत् Its conjugation is like खाद In the Perfect we have ‹?› as the root in reduplication retains ब without any change. So there is एत्त्व as well as the reduplication elision. Nouns :— बदरं, बदरी Maitreya reads this root as बन्द He forms बेदतुः by eliding न, and then एत्त्व and elision of reduplication. This is incorrect, according to Mādhava : because the root being संयोगान्त (ending in a conjunct consonant) like अञ्च् &c., the endings of the perfect are not कित् There is another root ‹?› given further on. 53. गद 'to speak.' लट्—गदति लिट्—जगाद लुट्—गदिता &c. like खाद But in प्र+नि+गदति, we have the following.

pk: 285. The ṇ is the substitute or n or the preril ni rolowing a cause ror such change standing in an upasarga, when these verbs rolow, nanely, 1. gad to speak, 2. nad to be hapy, 3. pat to ral, 4. pad to go, 5. the sil ghu verbs, 6. nā to neasure, 7. sho to destroy, 8. han to kil, 9. yā to go, 10. vā to blow, 1. drā to rle, 12. psā to eat, 13. vap to weave, 14. vah to bear, 15. śan to be tranquil, 16. chi to colect and 17. dih to anoint. Thus 1. gad, pranigadati 2. nad, praninadati 3. pat, pranipatati 4. pad, pranipadyate 5. The sil rots caled ghu. pranidadati, pranidaDati, pranideti, pranidyati, praniDayati, praniDayati 6. nan, pranininite nen, praninayate iṣhṭi :—By the word na in the sūtra, both verbs nan and nen are to be taken and not the rots so or ni or na nane, ror they also take the rorn na by Vi. 1. 50. 7. syati, pranisyati 8. hanti, pranihanti 9. yati, praniyati 10. vati, pranivati 1. drati, pranidrati 12. psati, pranipsati The last rive rots belong to the adādi clas. 13. vapati, pranivapati 14. vahati, pranivahati 15. sanyati, pranisanyati (Vi. 3. 74). 16. cinoti, pranicinoti 17. degDi, pranidegDi iṣhṭi :—The above change takes place even when the augnent aw intervenes, as pranyagadat, praninadat The rot syati &c., are elhibited in their conjugated rorn in the sūtra, in order to indicate that the rule does not aply to yaṅ-luk rorn or these rots (Vi. 4. 85). Thererore not here :—praniKagaditi, praninanaditi, pranileQiti &c. Thus jagadatu liw—jagadatu &c. noun :—gada, nigada, nigada 54. rada To split, rend, scratch, gnaw, dig. Vilekhana neans division or breaking. law—radati liw—rarada, redatu, rediTa &c., like the preceding. noun :—rada 5. nada To uter inarticulate sound. The rot is elhibited with an initial na This nasal is changed to n by the rolowing.

Vilekhana neans tivision or preakink. lat—ratati lit—rarata, retatu, retita &c., like the precetink. noun :—rata 5. nata to uter inarticulate sount. the rot is elhipitet tith an initial na this nasal is chanket to n py the rolotink.
s: 2285. The 'ṇ' is the substitute of 'n' of the prefix 'ni' following a cause for such change standing in an upasarga, when these verbs follow, namely, 1. gad 'to speak,' 2. nad 'to be happy,' 3. pat 'to fall,' 4. pad 'to go,' 5. the six ghu verbs, 6. mā 'to measure,' 7. sho 'to destroy,' 8. han 'to kill,' 9. yā 'to go,' 10. vā 'to blow,' 11. drā 'to flee,' 12. psā 'to eat,' 13. vap 'to weave,' 14. vah 'to bear,' 15. śam 'to be tranquil,' 16. chi 'to collect' and 17. dih 'to anoint.' Thus 1. गद्, प्रणिगदति 2. नद्, प्रणिनदति 3. पत्, प्रणिपतति 4. पद्, प्रणिपद्यते 5. The six roots called ghu. प्रणिददाति, प्रणिदधाति, प्रणिदेति, प्रणिद्यति, प्रणिधयति, प्रणिधायति 6. माङ्, प्रणिमिमीते मेङ्, प्रणिमयते Iṣhṭi :—By the word मा in the sūtra, both verbs माङ् and मेङ् are to be taken and not the roots सो or मि or मा माने, for they also take the form मा by VI. 1. 50. 7. स्यति, प्रणिष्यति 8. हन्ति, प्रणिहन्ति 9. याति, प्राणियाति 10. वाति, प्रणिवाति 11. द्राति, प्रणिद्राति 12. प्साति, प्रणिप्साति The last five roots belong to the Adādi class. 13. वपति, प्रणिवपति 14. वहति, प्रणिवहति 15. शाम्यति, प्राणिशाम्यति (VII. 3. 74). 16. चिनोति, प्रणिचिनोति 17. देग्धि, प्रणिदेग्धि Iṣhṭi :—The above change takes place even when the augment अट् intervenes, as प्राण्यगदत्, प्राणिनदत् The root स्यति &c., are exhibited in their conjugated form in the sūtra, in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to yaṅ-luk form of these roots (VII. 4. 85). Therefore not here :—प्रनिखागदीति, प्रनिमामदीति, प्रनिलेढीति &c. Thus जगदतुः लिट्—जगदतुः &c. Noun :—गदः, निगदः, निगादः 54. रद 'To split, rend, scratch, gnaw, dig.' Vilekhana means 'division' or 'breaking.' लट्—रदति लिट्—रराद, रेदतुः, रेदिथ &c., like the preceding. Noun :—रदः 55. णद 'To utter inarticulate sound.' The root is exhibited with an initial ण This nasal is changed to n by the following.

pk: 286. There is the substitution or n ror the initial ṇ or the rot in the Dhātupāṭha. al rots begining with n should be understod to have ben so taught with the elception or the rolowing eight rots narda, nawi, naTa, naDr, nanda, naka, nr and nrt note :—The rots narda sabda (i. 57) and narda avasyandane (l. 12) belong to the Bhvādi and Churādi clas respectively. The rot nawa nrtO (i. 818) belonging to the ghaṭādi (Vi. 4. 92, s. 2568) is not to be taken; as the rot is elhibited with a long ā as nāṭi in the above verse, while the ghaṭādi naṭ being nit is incapable or asuning the lengthened rorn nāṭi in the Causative by Vi. 4. 92, s. 2568. Thererore that naṭ should be taken which can asune the rorn nāṭi. note :—The rots naT and naD to beg &c. have already ben nentioned berore. ‹?› are the other rots. acording to sone the rot ‹?› is to be read as ‹?›; and so also the rots ‹?› as ‹?›. Only rive rots are thus lert, which begin with na in the Dhātupāṭha, nanely narda, naw, naw, naTa and ‹?› Conjugation or nada to sound, resound, thunder. law—nadati liw—nanada, nedatu, nedu nediTa, nedaTu, neda, nanada or nanada, nediva, nedina luw—nadita lrw—nadisyati lew—nadisati, naditi low—nadatu, anadat viDilin—nadet lun—anadit or anadit When preceded by an upasarga, the na is changed to na by the rolowing :—
ck: 286. there is the supstitution or n ror the initial ṇ or the rot in the thātupāṭha. al rots pekinink tith n shoult pe unterstot to have pen so taukht tith the elception or the rolotink eikht rots narta, nati, nata, natr, nanta, naka, nr ant nrt note :—the rots narta sapta (i. 57) ant narta avasyantane (l. 12) pelonk to the phvāti ant churāti clas respectively. the rot nata nrtO (i. 818) pelonkink to the khaṭāti (Vi. 4. 92, s. 2568) is not to pe taken; as the rot is elhipitet tith a lonk ā as nāṭi in the apove verse, thile the khaṭāti naṭ peink nit is incapaple or asunink the lenkthenet rorn nāṭi in the causative py Vi. 4. 92, s. 2568. thererore that naṭ shoult pe taken thich can asune the rorn nāṭi. note :—the rots nat ant nat to pek &c. have alreaty pen nentionet perore. ‹?› are the other rots. acortink to sone the rot ‹?› is to pe reat as ‹?›; ant so also the rots ‹?› as ‹?›. Only rive rots are thus lert, thich pekin tith na in the thātupāṭha, nanely narta, nat, nat, nata ant ‹?› concukation or nata to sount, resount, thunter. lat—natati lit—nanata, netatu, netu netita, netatu, neta, nanata or nanata, netiva, netina lut—natita lrt—natisyati let—natisati, natiti lot—natatu, anatat vitilin—natet lun—anatit or anatit then precetet py an upasarka, the na is chanket to na py the rolotink :—
s: 2286. There is the substitution of 'n' for the initial 'ṇ' of the root in the Dhātupāṭha. All roots beginning with n should be understood to have been so taught with the exception of the following eight roots नर्द, नाटि, नाथ, नाधृ, नन्द, नक्क, नॄ and नृत् Note :—The roots नर्द शब्द (I. 57) and नर्द अवस्यन्दने (X. 12) belong to the Bhvādi and Churādi class respectively. s: 2290. इयङ् and उवङ् are substituted for the इ and उ of a reduplicate, before a non-homogenous vowel. Therefore उ+ओख+अ = उव्+ओख+अ = उवोख When by Guṇa, the root assumes the form ओख्, it becomes a heavy vowelled root : and the Perfect ought to be formed by the addition of आम् periphrastically by III. 1. 36 S. 2237 but this is not so because of the maxim संनिपात &c. ("that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination." See VII. 1. 9 S. 203). Here उ was changed to ओ by the presence of णल्; and if आम् be added, it will cause the elision of its progenitor अच् by II. 4. 81 S. 2238 which the maxim prevents. The dual is formed thus उख+उख+अतुस् = उ+उख+अतुस् = ऊखतुः The Plural is ऊखुः The affixes being कित्, there is no guṇa, and consequently no उवङ् substitution, as the vowels are now homogenous. This single substitute long ऊ (उ+उ=ऊ) may be considered as the final of the first or the beginning of the second (VI. 1. 85. S. 75). Considering it as final of the first, namely, as the long of the reduplicate (abhyāsa), it requires to be shortened by VII. 4. 59. S. 2180. [But because the rule of shortening depends upon abhyāsa alone and is therefore antaraṅga, while the savarṇa-lengthening is Bahiraṅga ; as it depends upon two, namely the precedent and the subsequent letters— the maxim "नाजानन्तर्ये बहिष्ट्वप्रक्लृप्तिः" applies (see Vol I. p. 30) : and so it is not shortened. Or]. Pass. Part. कुचितः कुचितवान् Gerund कुचित्वा Similarly is conjugated kruñcha, as क्रुञ्चति &c. S. 3325). अञ्चु २०३ गतिपूजनयोः अच्यात् गतौ तु नलोपः पूजायां तु अञ्च्यात् 203. √ Añchu 'to go,' 'to worship.' लट्—अञ्चति लिट्—आनञ्च लुट्—अञ्चिता आशीर्लिंङ्—अच्यात्, अञ्च्यात् The nasal is elided when the sense is 'to go' (VI. 4. 30 S. 424). And, optionally aṅ is the substitute of cli after It is not shortened, because it had already been once shortened before, and "an operation once performed on a stem &c., is not repeated again"—is the maxim that would apply. Note:—When was the first u shortened? It was shortened by VII. 4. 59, S. 2180 as soon as was reduplicated to उ + उ But it was already short, how could it be shortened? Ans. Rules of grammar act like clouds (which rain both on sea and on land though raining on sea is useless). The rule of ह्रस्वः S. 2180 therefore substitutes a short in the place of the already existing short उ. Thus उ + उख + अतुः = उ + उख + अतुः (VII. 4. 59 S. 2180) = But why should Rule S. 2180 apply first and not the rule of lengthening? In other words, why should we not make उ + उख = ऊख first and then apply the rule of shortening? The rule of shortening being a rule applicable to anga (or stem) is stronger than the rule of lengthening (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः) on the maxim: Paribhasha: A rule relating to a stem (anga) is stronger than a rule relating to letters. Therefore, the ह्रस्वः (S. 2180) applies first. Another reason for its applying first is that it is subsequent in order to the rule of lengthening. Thus उ + उ + ख् + अतुः = उ + उख + अतुः (S. 2180 short for short उ) = ऊखतुः (lengthening). Similarly कख् : कखतुः Similarly may be conjugated the other roots given above. Thus उंखति लिट्—उरुंखाञ्चकार आशीर्लिङ्—उख्यात् लुट्—उंखिता Des. उउंखिषिषति वखति ववाख, ववखतुः वखिता, 133. उखि उंखति लिट्—उरुंखाञ्चकार Caus. उंखयति Aor. औजिंखत् 134. वख वखति ववाख, ववखतुः वखिता, लुट्—अवाचीत् or अवाखीत् 135. वखि वंखति 137. मखि मंखति 138. मख मखति ममाख मखिता Similarly चख् gives us : लट्—चखति, लिट्—चचाख, चचखतुः. pk: ajervityayanadesa syadarDaDatukavisaye Gananapan ca varjayitva vivaya vivyatu vivyu atra vakarasya halparatvat upaDayan ca (245) iti dirGe prapte— aca parasnin— (50) iti sTanivadBavenacparatvan na ca na padanta— (51) iti pratiseDe prapte— svaradirGayalopesu lopajadesa eva na sTanivat ityukte na pratiseDa ekaca upadesenudatat (265) iti dirGe prapte— iqadavarDaDatuke vesyate 292. vi is the substitute or the verb aj to drive, lead, when an Ārdhadhātuka aril rolows, with the elception or the ariles Gan (i. 3. 18) and ap (i. 3. 69). ishti:—The substitution is optional berore ârdhadhâtukas begining with a leter or Pratyâhâra val (al consonants elcept y). as ‹?› in viyatuḥ and viyuḥ the ‹?› is changed to ‹?› berore atuḥ and us. The equation now stands thus viy + atuḥ. ere the rot has a penultinate leter ya which is rolowed by a consonant; thererore the i or viy ought to be lengthened by Vi. 2. 78 s. 265. But it is not so, because the y, substitute ror ‹?›, is considered sthânivat to ‹?›, by i. 1. 51, s. 50, ror the purposes or s. 265. y being as ‹?›, the penultinate is not considered to be rolowed by a consonant but by a vowel, and hence s. 265 canot aply. Obj.:—But the rule Vi. 2. 78, s. 265 is a dīrgha-vidhi, as it ordains lengthening and thererore the substitute or ‹?› wil not be sthânivat by i. 1. 51. s. 50; because that rule nust be read with the proviso or i. 1. 58 s. 51 which declares inter alia that ror the purposes or dīrgha-vidhi the âdeśa is not sthânivat, so there ought to be lengthening or viy. ans:—The rolowing vârtika nakes a counter-elception to that rule or s. 51. Vârt:—ror the aplication or the rules or acent (svara-vidhi), or the rules or lengthening (dīrgha-vidhi) or the rule or the elision or ya (ya-lopa-vidhi), the lopa-substitute only or a vowel is to be considered as not sthânivat, and not any other substitute. ere the substitute is y and not lopa; and so is considered sthânivat to ‹?›. in rorning the second Person singular, we have aj + thal = vi + â + thal = ‹?›. now aplies the prohibition or s. 246 debaring the augnent iw. But the rolowing sûtra nakes an elception.
ck: acervityayanatesa syatartatatukavisaye kananapan ca varcayitva vivaya vivyatu vivyu atra vakarasya halparatvat upatayan ca (245) iti tirke prapte— aca parasnin— (50) iti stanivatpavenacparatvan na ca na patanta— (51) iti pratisete prapte— svaratirkayalopesu lopacatesa eva na stanivat ityukte na pratiseta ekaca upatesenutatat (265) iti tirke prapte— itatavartatatuke vesyate 292. vi is the supstitute or the verp ac to trive, leat, then an Ārthathātuka aril rolots, tith the elception or the ariles kan (i. 3. 18) ant ap (i. 3. 69). ishti:—the supstitution is optional perore ârthathâtukas pekinink tith a leter or pratyâhâra val (al consonants elcept y). as ‹?› in viyatuḥ ant viyuḥ the ‹?› is chanket to ‹?› perore atuḥ ant us. the etuation not stants thus viy + atuḥ. ere the rot has a penultinate leter ya thich is rolotet py a consonant; thererore the i or viy oukht to pe lenkthenet py Vi. 2. 78 s. 265. put it is not so, pecause the y, supstitute ror ‹?›, is consiteret sthânivat to ‹?›, py i. 1. 51, s. 50, ror the purposes or s. 265. y peink as ‹?›, the penultinate is not consiteret to pe rolotet py a consonant put py a votel, ant hence s. 265 canot aply. Opc.:—put the rule Vi. 2. 78, s. 265 is a tīrkha-vithi, as it ortains lenkthenink ant thererore the supstitute or ‹?› til not pe sthânivat py i. 1. 51. s. 50; pecause that rule nust pe reat tith the proviso or i. 1. 58 s. 51 thich teclares inter alia that ror the purposes or tīrkha-vithi the âteśa is not sthânivat, so there oukht to pe lenkthenink or viy. ans:—the rolotink vârtika nakes a counter-elception to that rule or s. 51. s: अजेर्वीत्ययमादेशः स्यादार्धधातुकविषये घञमपं च वर्जयित्वा विवाय विव्यतुः विव्युः अत्र वकारस्य हल्परत्वात् 'उपधायां च' (२२४५) इति दीर्घे प्राप्ते— 'अचः परस्मिन्—' (५०) इति स्थानिवद्भावेनाच्परत्वम् न च 'न पदान्त—' (५१) इति प्रतिषेधे प्राप्ते— 'स्वरदीर्घयलोपेषु लोपाजादेश एव न स्थानिवत्' इत्युक्तेः न प्रतिषेधः 'एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्' (२२६५) इति दीर्घे प्राप्ते— 'इडादावर्धधातुके वेष्यते' 2292. वी is the substitute of the verb अज् 'to drive, lead,' when an Ārdhadhātuka affix follows, with the exception of the affixes घञ् (III. 3. 18) and अप् (III. 3. 69). Ishti:—The substitution is optional before ârdhadhâtukas beginning with a letter of Pratyâhâra val (all consonants except y). As ‹?› In viyatuḥ and viyuḥ the ‹?› is changed to ‹?› before atuḥ and us. The equation now stands thus viy + atuḥ. Here the root has a penultimate letter य which is followed by a consonant; therefore the i of viy ought to be lengthened by VIII. 2. 78 S. 2265. But it is not so, because the y, substitute for ‹?›, is considered sthânivat to ‹?›, by I. 1. 51, S. 50, for the purposes of S. 2265. y being as ‹?›, the penultimate is not considered to be followed by a consonant but by a vowel, and hence S. 2265 cannot apply. Obj.:—But the rule VIII. 2. 78, S. 2265 is a dīrgha-vidhi, as it ordains lengthening and therefore the substitute of ‹?› will not be sthânivat by I. 1. 51. S. 50; because that rule must be read with the proviso of I. 1. 58 S. 51 which declares inter alia that for the purposes of dīrgha-vidhi the âdeśa is not sthânivat, so there ought to be lengthening of viy. Ans:—The following vârttika makes a counter-exception to that rule of S. 51. Vârt:—For the application of the rules of accent (svara-vidhi), or the rules of lengthening (dīrgha-vidhi) or the rule of the elision of ya (ya-lopa-vidhi), the lopa-substitute only of a vowel is to be considered as not sthânivat, and not any other substitute. Here the substitute is y and not lopa; and so is considered sthânivat to ‹?›. In forming the Second Person Singular, we have aj + thal = vi + â + thal = ‹?›. Now applies the prohibition of S. 2246 debarring the augment इट्. But the following sûtra makes an exception.

pk: 293. The Personal endings or the Perect do not get the augnent iw arter kr, sr, Br, vr, stu, dru, sru, sru The rour rots, kr, sr, Br, and vr are taken in order to nake a restriction with regard to then. Every prohibition or iw augnent whether depending on any particular rinal, or depending on any particular aril, ir that prohibition is to aply to the Perect, then it aplies only to the rour rots kṛ &c. nentioned here, and not to other rots. as regards the renaining rour rots stu, dru, sru, and sru, the present sûtra prohibits the iw which would have cone berore the aril Tal by the rule or Bhâradvâja (Vi. 2. 63 s. 296) and the iw which would have cone berore the ariles va or na &c. by the present rule or Krâdi (i.e., the ariles va, na, nahin and nahin); note:—Thus kr—cakre, cakrivahe; cakrnahe; Bu—baBuva, baBuviva &c. ‹?› These rots with the elception or ‹?› are aniṭ by Vi. 2. 10 s. 243; their special nention here is ror the sake or niyana, nanely these rots alone are aniṭ in the Perect, other rots are al seṭ in the Perect. Thus ‹?› al anudâta rots or the Dhâtupâṭha are to be understod, by this rule, to get iw. The aril Tal or the Perect gets iw arter Bu, as the iregular rorn baBuviTa in Vi. 2. 64, indicates that in the Vedic it does not get iw arter Bu, but in the clasical literature it does. By Vi. 2. 63, s. 296 the Tal would have got iw arter dru and sru; that also is prohibited by the present sûtra. as tuswoTa, dudroTa, susroTa, susroTa Vârt:—iw is aded when kr takes the suw augnent: as sancaskariTa, sancaskarina The sûtra Vi. 2. 63, s. 296 aplies here also, as sanskariTa
ck: 293. the personal entinks or the perect to not ket the auknent it arter kr, sr, pr, vr, stu, tru, sru, sru the rour rots, kr, sr, pr, ant vr are taken in orter to nake a restriction tith rekart to then. Every prohipition or it auknent thether tepentink on any particular rinal, or tepentink on any particular aril, ir that prohipition is to aply to the perect, then it aplies only to the rour rots kṛ &c. nentionet here, ant not to other rots. as rekarts the renainink rour rots stu, tru, sru, ant sru, the present sûtra prohipits the it thich toult have cone perore the aril tal py the rule or phâratvâca (Vi. 2. 63 s. 296) ant the it thich toult have cone perore the ariles va or na &c. py the present rule or krâti (i.e., the ariles va, na, nahin ant nahin); note:—thus kr—cakre, cakrivahe; cakrnahe; pu—papuva, papuviva &c. ‹?› these rots tith the elception or ‹?› are aniṭ py Vi. 2. 10 s. 243; their special nention here is ror the sake or niyana, nanely these rots alone are aniṭ in the perect, other rots are al seṭ in the perect. thus ‹?› al anutâta rots or the thâtupâṭha are to pe unterstot, py this rule, to ket it. the aril tal or the perect kets it arter pu, as the irekular rorn papuvita in Vi. 2. 64, inticates that in the Vetic it toes not ket it arter pu, put in the clasical literature it toes. py Vi. 2. 63, s. 296 the tal toult have kot it arter tru ant sru; that also is prohipitet py the present sûtra. as tustota, tutrota, susrota, susrota Vârt:—it is atet then kr takes the sut auknent: as sancaskarita, sancaskarina the sûtra Vi. 2. 63, s. 296 aplies here also, as sanskarita
s: 2293. The Personal endings of the Perfect do not get the augment इट् after कृ, सृ, भृ, वृ, स्तु, द्रु, स्रु, श्रु The four roots, कृ, सृ, भृ, and वृ are taken in order to make a restriction with regard to them. Every prohibition of इट् augment whether depending on any particular final, or depending on any particular affix, if that prohibition is to apply to the Perfect, then it applies only to the four roots kṛ &c. mentioned here, and not to other roots. As regards the remaining four roots स्तु, द्रु, स्रु, and श्रु, the present sûtra prohibits the इट् which would have come before the affix थल् by the rule of Bhâradvâja (VII. 2. 63 S. 2296) and the इट् which would have come before the affixes व or म &c. by the present rule of Krâdi (i.e., the affixes व, म, महिङ् and महिङ्); Note:—Thus कृ—चक्रे, चक्रिवहे; चकृमहे; भू—बभूव, बभूविव &c. ‹?› These roots with the exception of ‹?› are Aniṭ by VII. 2. 10 S. 2243; their special mention here is for the sake of niyama, namely these roots alone are aniṭ in the Perfect, other roots are all Seṭ in the Perfect. Thus ‹?› All anudâtta roots of the Dhâtupâṭha are to be understood, by this rule, to get इट्. The affix थल् of the Perfect gets इट् after भू, as the irregular form बभूविथ in VII. 2. 64, indicates that in the Vedic it does not get इट् after भू, but in the classical literature it does. By VII. 2. 63, S. 2296 the थल् would have got इट् after द्रु and स्रु; that also is prohibited by the present sûtra. As तुष्टोथ, दुद्रोथ, सुस्रोथ, शुश्रोथ Vârt:—इट् is added when कृ takes the सुट् augment: as संचस्करिथ, संचस्करिम The sûtra VII. 2. 63, S. 2296 applies here also, as संस्करिथ

pk: 294. arter a rot, which in the Dhâtupâṭha, ends in a vowel, and arter which the rirst rut. aril tâsi is always devoid or the augnent iw; (arter such a rot) Tal the personal ending or the Perect, like tâsi, does not also get the augnent iw

s: 2295. After a root which possesses a short 'a' as its root vowel in the original enunciation (the Dhâtupâṭha), and after which the First Fut. affix तासि is always devoid of the augment इट्, थल् the Personal ending of the Perfect, like तासि, does not get the augment इट्

pk: 296. in the opinion or Bharadvaja, it is only arter a rot which ends in a short r, and arter which the rirst rut. tasi is always devoid or the augnent iw that Tal also, like tasi, does not take the augnent iw. Thererore, the other ariles do take iw. On this there is the rolowing verse (saṅgraha), which suns up the last thre sûtras:— That rot which ends in a vowel, or which has a short a in the Dhâtupâṭha, and which is aniṭ berore tas aril, is optionaly sew berore Tal aril. But ir such rot ends in short r, then it is invariably aniṭ berore Tal aril. nots other than kr &c. are sew in the Perect. One should not, however, think that the rour rots stu, dru, sru and sru wil also be optionaly aniṭ in Tal as they are not ṛi-ending rots. The rule nade by Bharadvâja renoves the prohibition with regard to the adition or iw nade by the two inediately preceding sûtras s. 294 and 295 : and not the iw or s. 293. This is on the nalin a rule, nay it enjoin or rorbid anything, either enjoins or rorbids only that which is nearest to it in sone other rule. (se Vol i. 203) Thererore vi + a + aj + Ta = vivajiTa or vivyajiTa or vivyajiTa in rorning the aorist, the rolowing sûtra aplies.
ck: 296. in the opinion or pharatvaca, it is only arter a rot thich ents in a short r, ant arter thich the rirst rut. tasi is altays tevoit or the auknent it that tal also, like tasi, toes not take the auknent it. thererore, the other ariles to take it. On this there is the rolotink verse (saṅkraha), thich suns up the last thre sûtras:— that rot thich ents in a votel, or thich has a short a in the thâtupâṭha, ant thich is aniṭ perore tas aril, is optionaly set perore tal aril. put ir such rot ents in short r, then it is invariaply aniṭ perore tal aril. nots other than kr &c. are set in the perect. One shoult not, hotever, think that the rour rots stu, tru, sru ant sru til also pe optionaly aniṭ in tal as they are not ṛi-entink rots. the rule nate py pharatvâca renoves the prohipition tith rekart to the atition or it nate py the to inetiately precetink sûtras s. 294 ant 295 : ant not the it or s. 293. this is on the nalin a rule, nay it encoin or rorpit anythink, either encoins or rorpits only that thich is nearest to it in sone other rule. (se Vol i. 203) thererore vi + a + ac + ta = vivacita or vivyacita or vivyacita in rornink the aorist, the rolotink sûtra aplies.
s: 2296. In the opinion of Bharadvaja, it is only after a root which ends in a short ऋ, and after which the First Fut. तासि is always devoid of the augment इट् that थल् also, like तासि, does not take the augment इट्. Therefore, the other affixes do take इट्. On this there is the following verse (saṅgraha), which sums up the last three sûtras:— That root which ends in a vowel, or which has a short अ in the Dhâtupâṭha, and which is aniṭ before तास् affix, is optionally सेट् before थल् affix. But if such root ends in short ऋ, then it is invariably aniṭ before थल् affix. Roots other than कृ &c. are सेट् in the Perfect. One should not, however, think that the four roots स्तु, द्रु, स्रु and श्रु will also be optionally aniṭ in थल् as they are not ṛi-ending roots. The rule made by Bharadvâja removes the prohibition with regard to the addition of इट् made by the two immediately preceding sûtras S. 2294 and 2295 : and not the इट् of S. 2293. This is on the maxim 'a rule, may it enjoin or forbid anything, either enjoins or forbids only that which is nearest to it in some other rule.' (see Vol I. 203) Therefore वि + अ + आज् + थ = विवजिथ or विव्यजिथ or विव्याजिथ In forming the Aorist, the following sûtra applies.

The Conditional is अवैष्यत् or आजिष्यत् तेज २४९ पालने तेजति 249. √ Teja, 'to protect.' लट्—तेजति लिट्—सितेज लुट्—तेजिता Noun:—तेजः खज २५० मन्थे खजति 250. √ Khaja, 'to churn', 'to stir.' लट्—खजति लिट्—चखाज लुट्—खजिता लुङ्—अखासीत्, ‹?› Noun:—खलाकः कज २५१ मदे 251. √ Kaja, 'to be drunk.' The Vṛiddhi of the vowel of the following stems does not take place before the इट्-augmented s-Aorist in the Parasmaipada ; namely—the stems ending in ह्, म् or य्, the roots क्षण, श्वस् and जागृ, a stem formed with णि, the root श्वि, and the roots having an indicatory ॠ in the Dhâtupâṭha. s: 2306. आम् is the affix of the verb कास् 'to cough,' and of those roots that are formed by affixes (i. e. the derivative verbs), when लिट् follows, except in the Mantra. NOTE:— This forms the Periphrastic Perfect. The perfect of कास् will be कासाम्, after which the terminations of the Perfect are all elided (II. 4. 81) and instead, the perfect tense of the auxiliary verb कृ or भू or अस् is added. As कासाञ्चक्रे 'he coughed'; चोरयाञ्चकार 'he stole.' So also ‹?›. This rule however does not apply to the Vedas; as Rig Veda I. 79. 2. Vârt:— This rule only applies where the root is polysyllabic consisting of more than one vowel; as चुलुम्पाञ्चकार, दरिद्राञ्चकार The force of this vartika is that even of non-derivative roots, the Perfect will be formed periphrastically if the root consists of more than one syllable. In fact, the vârtika would substitute the word anekâchaḥ in the room of pratyayât. The sutra would then run thus: "kâsânekâcha âm amantre liṭi": "आम् is added to the root kâs and to roots of more than one syllable in the Perfect; but not in the Vedas."

s: 2307. From this upto VI. 4. 68 inclusive, is always to be supplied "before an affix called ârdhadhâtuka (III. 4. 114 &c)." NOTE:— This is an adhikâra sûtra and extends upto VI. 4. 69 (exclusive). In all the sûtras upto VI. 4. 68 should be supplied the phrase "before an affix called ârdhadhâtuka." Thus VI. 4. 48 teaches "the अ standing at the end of a verbal stem is elided." To complete the sense we should add: "before an ârdhadhâtuka affix." Thus the final अ of the verbal stem चिकीर्ष is elided before the ârdhadhâtuka affix तृच्, as चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्; but the final is not elided before a sârvadhâtuka affix, as the अ of भू in भवति, भवतः. The luk-elision of शप् after roots of अदादि class, implies that there is never lopa of अकार. Kârikâ:— लोपो यलोपोऽथ णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् आल्लोप ईत्वमेत्वं च चिण्वद्भावश्च सेधुटि The following purposes are served by this sutra, i. e. an ârdhadhâtuka affix causes the following special changes: (1) अलोपः—The elision of अ of a stem, as shown above, in चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्. (2) यलोपश्च The elision of य by VI. 4. 49, 50: as बेभिदिता, बेभिदितुम्, बेभिदितव्यम् from the intensive stem. Before Sârvadhâtuka, we have बेभिद्यते, चेच्छिद्यते (3) णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् The elision of णि by VI. 4. 51, as कारणा, हारणा, पाच्यते (पाचि + यक् + ते = पाच + य + ते), पाक्यते In Sârvadhâtuka, पाचयति, याजयति, कारयति, हारयति (4) आल्लोपः—the elision of आकार, VI. 4. 64: पपतुः, पपुः, ववतुः, वपुः In Sârvadhâtuka, यान्ति, वान्ति (5) ईत्वम्—The substitution of long ई for आकार in some roots, VI. 4. 65: as दीयेताम्, दीयेरन्; in Sârvadhâtuka प्रदाताम्, प्रधाताम् (6) एत्वम्—The substitution of ए for आकार, VI. 4. 68; as म्लेयात्, ग्लेयात्; in Sârvadhâtuka, स्नायात्, ग्लायात् This is confined to the Precative (âśîrliṅ). (7) चिण्वद्भावश्च सेधुटि—The treatment of the Precative like Aorist Passive in चिण् by VI. 4. 62, as कारिषीष्ट, हारिषीष्ट In Sârvadhâtuka क्रियेत, ह्रियेत

s: 2308. The अ standing at the end of a stem is elided before an Ârdhadhâtuka affix. NOTE:— Thus चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम् and चिकीर्षितव्यम्, from the Desiderative stem चिकीर्ष So also धिनुतः and कृणुतः from the roots धिन्व् and कृण्व्; thus धिन्व् + उ (III. 1. 80) = धिन् + अ + उ (III. 1. 80) = धिन् + उ (अ being elided before the ârdhadhâtuka उ) = धिनु, the 3rd Personal dual of it is धिनुतः The addition of अ by III. 1. 80 and its subsequent elision by the present sûtra, may appear a redundancy, but the elided अ being sthânivat, prevents guṇa of धि So also कृणुतः See sûtra III. 1. 80. s: 2311. अय् is substituted for the णि of णिङ्, before the affixes आम्, अन्त, आलु, आय्य, इत्स्नु, and ष्णुक Note:—Thus कारयाञ्चकार, हारयाञ्चकार, मण्डयन्तः मण्डयन्तः (formed by the Jhac affix झ = अन्त; added to the roots मण्ड and मन्त्र) धातु पहयालुः आय्य—उपायाय्यः सहायाय्यः इत्स्नुः—स्तनयित्स्नुः ष्णुक—पोषयिष्णुकः Note:—This sūtra could have been well dispensed with for the affix णि would take guṇa ए which will be changed to अय् by the rules of Sandhi, before these affixes. The substitution of अय् for णि is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra VI. 4. 56, § 2336 however, because there णि could not be changed to अय् by any sandhi-rules. The णि is always changed to अय्; therefore the अय् substitution of the present sūtra would have been redundant, but it is taught here in order to supersede the elision declared hereafter in VI. 4. 51, § 2313. Thus कामयां ‹?› The addition of आय being optional (III. 1. 31, § 2305) we have the alternative form चकमे also. The Future forms are:—कामयिता or कमिता कामयिष्यते or कमिष्यते In forming the Aorist, the following sūtra applies.

s: 2312. pk: 2313. The ni or the verbal sten rorned with the aril ni, is elided berore an ârdhadhâtuka aril which does not take the augnent iw nOTE:— This debars the seni-vowel y, the guṇa, vṛidhi and the long substitutions. The elision or (ni) supersedes al the above rive rules or iyaṅ, yaṇ, guṇa, vṛidhi and lengthening. Q. s: 2313. The णि of the verbal stem formed with the affix णि, is elided before an ârdhadhâtuka affix which does not take the augment इट् NOTE:— This debars the semi-vowel य्, the guṇa, vṛiddhi and the long substitutions. Thus अशशमत्, अशीशमत्, आटिटत्, कारणा, हारणा, कारकः, हारकः, कार्यते, हार्यते and कारयिता (see VII. 4. 1 for the shortening of the stem of the Aorists in these). Why do we say 'not having the augment इट्'? Observe कारयिता and हारयिता The sûtra VI. 4. 82, S. 272 (a semi-vowel is substituted for the final इ or ई of a root before a vowel-beginning affix &c.) being subsequent in order of Ashṭâdhyâyî would debar the present sûtra and prevent the elision of णि and cause य् to be substituted instead. This however is prevented by the following. Vârtika:— The rule ordaining the elision of णि (S. 2313) and that teaching the elision of अ (VI. 4. 48, S. 2308) take effect even to the supersession of the subsequent rules ordaining इयङ् (VI. 4. 78, S. 2290), or semi-vowel (VI. 4. 82, S. 272), or guṇa, (VII. 3. 84, S. 2168 &c.) or vṛiddhi, (VII. 2. 115, S. 254), or lengthening. NOTE:— The elision of अ supersedes only the two rules of vṛiddhi, lengthening and not the others. The elision of (णि) supersedes all the above five rules of iyaṅ, yaṇ, guṇa, vṛiddhi and lengthening. Q. There is no necessity for this vârtika with regard to णि, for if the five rules mentioned above were not to be superseded by णि-elision, then this rule will find no scope anywhere. And as scope must be given to every rule, the present sûtra inferentially and necessarily supersedes the above rules. Ans. The vârtika is not unnecessary. The णि elision finds its unrestricted scope before the ârdhadhâtuka affixes like क्तिन् (III. 3. 174, S. 3313). Thus from शमि we have शान्तिः, from √ तमि तन्तिः. The intermediate इट् is prevented there by VII. 2. 9, S. 3163. Hence if this vârtika were not taught, the णि would be elided only before the ârdhadhâtuka kṛit affix क्तिन् and no where else. As a matter of fact, the force of the word अनिटि in the sûtra is that the rule of the elision of णि applies to all ârdhadhâtuka affixes, and not only to a single affix क्तिन्. NOTE:— Had the present sûtra not superseded इयङ् &c., then it would have been more proper to draft it as णेः only without the word अनिटि For the sûtra with the anuvṛitti of आर्धधातुके read into it, would apply to the affix क्तिन्, only after the rules yaṇ &c. had restricted its scope. So there would be no necessity of adding अनिटि. The very fact that the word अनिटि is added shows that the sûtra has for its scope all ârdhadhâtuka affixes, and therefore it is an exception by anticipation to the rules of iyaṅ &c. Thus, इयङ् is superseded in अशिश्रियत्. It is a चङ् Aorist. There is no scope for guṇa here, as चङ् is ङित् and yaṇ of sûtra VI. 4. 82, S. 272 has also no scope, as the इ (णि) in श्रि is preceded by a conjunct consonant. The only rule left that would have applied to this णि is इयङ्. The present vârtika debars इयङ् but causes the elision of इ (णि) Similarly यण् (semivowel) substitution is superseded in आटिटत् Guṇa is superseded in अशशमत् and vṛiddhi in कारकः and lengthening in कार्यते Now applies the following. Thus ‹?›

s: 2314. A short is substituted for the vowel, standing in a penultimate position, in the णि-formed stem; when the affix चङ् (of the Reduplicate Aorist) follows. Thus ‹?› (VI. 4. 51, S. 2313) = ‹?› (VII. 4. 1, S. 2314). Now applies the following sûtra which causes reduplication.

pk: 2315. Or a non-reduplicate rot there is reduplication when the aril can or the aorist rolows. Dr. Balantyne translates it this:— "When can rolows, there are two in the ron or the rirst portion, containing a single vowel, or an unreduplicated rot; but the reduplication is or the second portion or a rot that begins with a vowel." The rirst sylable is reduplicated ir the rirst portion or the rot begins with a consonant; the second sylable is reduplicated ir the rirst portion begins with a vowel. Thus ‹?› now aplies the rolowing atideśa sûtra.
ck: 2315. Or a non-retuplicate rot there is retuplication then the aril can or the aorist rolots. tr. palantyne translates it this:— "then can rolots, there are to in the ron or the rirst portion, containink a sinkle votel, or an unretuplicatet rot; put the retuplication is or the secont portion or a rot that pekins tith a votel." the rirst sylaple is retuplicatet ir the rirst portion or the rot pekins tith a consonant; the secont sylaple is retuplicatet ir the rirst portion pekins tith a votel. thus ‹?› not aplies the rolotink atiteśa sûtra.
s: 2315. Of a non-reduplicate root there is reduplication when the affix चङ् of the Aorist follows. Dr. Ballantyne translates it this:— "When चङ् follows, there are two in the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel, of an unreduplicated root; but the reduplication is of the second portion of a root that begins with a vowel." The first syllable is reduplicated if the first portion of the root begins with a consonant; the second syllable is reduplicated if the first portion begins with a vowel. s: 2316. In the reduplicated Aorist of the णि-stems, the reduplicate adapts itself to that of the Desiderative, when the vowel of the root is light, and the root has not lost its end-vowel before the णि affix. The word चङ्परे is a Bahuvrîhi compound and therefore it means णि. This word णि so qualified, as well as the word अङ्गस्य should both be twice employed in this sûtra, in order to give the full meaning. We explain therefore the sûtra thus:— "that णि which is followed by that affix which gives the designation of अङ्ग to the root"—this is one portion. The next part is—"a short vowel which follows such णि, and the abhyâsa of the aṅga which follows such short vowel of that abhyâsa, the operations are like those of the Desiderative, before the णि, when no अक्-vowel is elided." Or the word अङ्गस्य is not repeated. Then the sûtra would mean 'that aṅga which stands before that णि which is followed by चङ्; the abhyâsa of such an aṅga, when followed by a short vowel,—on that abhyâsa, the operations are like those of the Desiderative &c.' NOTE:— Dr. Ballantyne has translated this sûtra as follows:— "Let the effect be like as if सन् (III. 1. 7, S. 2608) had followed, on the reduplicate, if followed by a light vowel of an inflective base to which णि followed by चङ् is affixed provided there is not the elision of any letter in the pratyâhâra अक् occasioned by the affixing of णि (as, for example under the provisions of VI. 4. 48, S. 2308)." NOTE:— The words of this sûtra require a little detailed explanation. The word सन्वत् means "like unto सन् or Desiderative"; i. e. as the Desiderative is treated, so should the चङ् Aorist of the णि stems. The words लघुनि and चङ्परे are both in the Locative case, but not in apposition with each other, but refer to different objects. लघुनि means 'when a light vowel follows,' namely that reduplicate which is followed by the light root-vowel. The operations to be performed on such a reduplicate, in the चङ् Aorist, after the णि, are the same, as on the reduplicate of the Desiderative, अनग्लोपे "provided that a simple vowel of the Pratyâhâra अक् has not been elided." We read the word णि into this sûtra, because there can be no other root which will form a चङ् Aorist. णि stems form such Aorist, (III. 1. 48), as well as the simple roots श्रि, द्रु and स्रु. The word चङ्परे is a Bahuvrîhi and qualifies the word णि understood: that stem which is followed by चङ्; therefore, it refers to the णि stem, and not to the simple roots śri, dru and sru. The light vowel, therefore, refers to the light vowel of the णि-stem before चङ्. The word अनग्लोपे is in apposition with चङ्परे Thus कम् + णिच्, (III. 1. 30) = चकाम् + णिच् + अत् (III. 1. 48) = अकाम् + अत् (VI. 4. 51) = अकमत् (VII. 4. 1) = अचकम् + अत् (VI. 1. 11). Then applies the next sûtra. NOTE:— Thus VII. 4. 79 teaches the substitution of ‹?› for ‹?› in the reduplicate of the Desiderative. The same substitution will take place in the reduplicate of the Aorist: as ‹?› Thus by VII. 4. 80, is substituted for the ‹?› of the reduplicate in the Desiderative, the same will be the case in the reduplicate of the Aorist, as प्रपोपवत् and अलीलवत्, and अजीजवत् Thus by VII. 4. 81, ‹?› is optionally substituted for उ in the Desiderative reduplicate of सु &c., the same will hold good in the Aorist-reduplicate, as ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?› Why do we say 'having a light vowel' ? Observe प्रततक्षत्, अजागरत् By sûtra III. 1. 48 : 2313 the roots श्वि, ‹?› and सु also form चङ् aorist. The sanvadbhâva however does not take place with regard to these roots: because these roots do not get the designation of अङ्ग before चङ् The rule is therefore confined to णि-roots, for these are the roots which get the designation अङ्ग before the affix चङ् Moreover the reduplicate must be that of the ‹?›, which can be of णि-roots only.

s: 2318. In the reduplicative syllable, a prosodially short vowel is lengthened in the Reduplicated Aorist of the णि-stem when the vowel of the root is light, and the root has not lost its end-vowel before the Causative णि Therefore अचिकम् + अत = अचीकमत The affix णि being optional, when it is not added, then applies the following vārtika:—"The aorist of Kam is formed by चङ् even when it does not take णि". As there is absence of णि, so we have neither lengthening nor sanvadbhâva. Thus अचकमत NOTE:—In Grammar there are two opinions as regards rules of definition (संज्ञा); one is expressed by the maxim कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् and the other by यथोद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् The first means that a rule defining a term (i.e. a saṁjñā rule) or giving a maxim of interpretation (paribhâshâ) manifests itself at the time of application. Whenever an occasion arises to apply such rule, it appears there anew. The other means that the saṁjñās and paribhâshâs remain where they have been originally taught, and do not appear anew each time when a particular operation is to be performed. They exert their influence from the place where they are, and do not require to be recited afresh each time that an operation is to be performed. Now the abhyâsa is defined in the sûtra पूर्वेऽभ्यासः (VI. 1. 4. S. 2178) and the word abhyâsa occurs in the sûtra 2316. In both views of the function of a definition, the sûtras पूर्वेऽभ्यासः and सन्यल्लघुनि &c., will become one sentence. But in the first view of kâryakâla paksha the one-sentence will be of different padas or words; in the second view the one-sentence will be of different sentences. Mâdhava favours the view of kâryakâla paksha with regard to the sûtra 2316: which opinion the author has summarised in the following two verses :— Verse 1. "According to Mâdhava, the rules of lengthening (2318) and sanvadbhâva (2316) apply there only where the kâryakâla function of a rule of definition being taken as valid, the aṅga or inflective base is reduplicated: and not where there are many-syllabled stems." NOTE:—The sense is that in the sûtras 2316 and 2318 there is the anuvṛitti of the words aṅgasya and abhyâsasya. Here the designation of abhyâsa (reduplicate) will be given to the first portion of the doublet aṅga. Therefore the lengthening (2318) and sanvadbhâva (2316) will take place in that abhyâsa only which is the abhyâsa of an aṅga—that is where an aṅga has been reiterated, there the first portion will get the designation of abhyâsa for the purposes of the application of 2316 and 2318. As अचिकमत and अचीकमत Verse 2. "But in the roots चकस्, अर्थापय and ‹?› &c. there is no reduplication of an aṅga but only a portion of an aṅga is reduplicated. Therefore the two rules 2316 and 2318 are confined to monosyllabic roots." NOTE:—Thus we have अचकासत्, आर्तिधपत् and और्णुनवत् without the application of S. 2316 and 2318. Here the whole aṅga chakâs &c. has not been reduplicated, but only a part of it, namely the first consonant in the case of chakâs and the second consonant in the case of vowel-beginning roots. The result is that it is only in monosyllabic roots that the whole of aṅga is reduplicated, and not only a part of it (for there can be no such part), and consequently the dîrgha and sanvadbhâva apply to monosyllabic roots. Moreover, in this view (kâryakâla paksha), the word ekâchaḥ in the sûtra ekâcho dve prathamasya (VI. 1. 1. S. 2175), qualifies the word aṅgasya understood therein. Obj. Let it be so, that the dîrgha and sanvadbhâva rules apply to the reduplicate of monosyllabic roots only. Then stretching this argument further the other rules that apply to reduplicates will also be restricted in their scope such as the rules of shortening (VII. 4. 59 S. 2180), retention of first consonant (VII. 4. 60. S. 2179) and substitution of a palatal (VII. 4. 62. S. 2245), &c. and these will not apply to polysyllabic roots. Verses 3 and 4. pk: 2321. The aril syan is optionaly enployed in the active voice berore a sarvadhatuka aril arter the rolowing verbs ; Bras to shine, Blas to shine, Bran to whirl, kran to walk, klan to be sad, tras to rear, truw to cut, and las to desire. note:—Thus Brasate or Brasyate he shines ; Blasate or Blasyate, he shines, Branati or Branyati he whirls ; kranati or kranyati he walks ; klanati or klanyati he is sad. so also trasyati or trasati ; truwyati or truwati ; lasyati or lasati Thus kran + sap + ti or kran + syan + ti now aplies the rolowing sutra.
ck: 2321. the aril syan is optionaly enployet in the active voice perore a sarvathatuka aril arter the rolotink verps ; pras to shine, plas to shine, pran to thirl, kran to talk, klan to pe sat, tras to rear, trut to cut, ant las to tesire. note:—thus prasate or prasyate he shines ; plasate or plasyate, he shines, pranati or pranyati he thirls ; kranati or kranyati he talks ; klanati or klanyati he is sat. so also trasyati or trasati ; trutyati or trutati ; lasyati or lasati thus kran + sap + ti or kran + syan + ti not aplies the rolotink sutra.
s: 2321. The affix श्यन् is optionally employed in the active voice before a sarvadhatuka affix after the following verbs ; भ्राश् 'to shine,' भ्लाश् 'to shine,' भ्रम् 'to whirl,' क्रम् 'to walk,' क्लम् 'to be sad,' त्रस् 'to fear,' त्रुट् 'to cut,' and लष् 'to desire.' Note:—Thus भ्राशते or भ्राश्यते 'he shines' ; भ्लाशते or भ्लाश्यते, 'he shines,' भ्रमति or भ्राम्यति 'he whirls' ; क्रामति or क्राम्यति 'he walks' ; क्लामति or क्लाम्यति 'he is sad.' So also त्रस्यति or त्रसति ; त्रुट्यति or त्रुटति ; लष्यति or लषति Thus क्रम् + शप् + ति or क्रम् + श्यन् + ति Now applies the following sutra.

pk: 232. The long is substituted in kran, berore a sit aril, in the Parasnaipada. as kranati, kranata, krananti or kranyati &c. Per. cakrana inperative kranyatu or kranatu &c. Why in the Parasnaipada ? Observe akranate aditya ow do you elplain the lengthening in utkrana and sankrana ( inperative 2nd Per. sg.) ror when hi is elided by luk, (Vi. 4. 105 ) then by i. 1. 63. the aril being droped by a l-elision, it would produce no erect and so there ought to have ben no lengthening ? This is no valid objection. The prohibition or i. 1. 63, aplies to the anga sten arter which the aril is elided. ere kran is not a sten or anga with regard to hi, but it is a sten with regard to sap as kran + sap + hi Thererore, though hi is elided, the lengthening wil take place by i. 1. 62, (pratyayalaksanan)
ck: 232. the lonk is supstitutet in kran, perore a sit aril, in the parasnaipata. as kranati, kranata, krananti or kranyati &c. per. cakrana inperative kranyatu or kranatu &c. thy in the parasnaipata ? Opserve akranate atitya ot to you elplain the lenkthenink in utkrana ant sankrana ( inperative 2nt per. sk.) ror then hi is elitet py luk, (Vi. 4. 105 ) then py i. 1. 63. the aril peink tropet py a l-elision, it toult protuce no erect ant so there oukht to have pen no lenkthenink ? this is no valit opcection. the prohipition or i. 1. 63, aplies to the anka sten arter thich the aril is elitet. ere kran is not a sten or anka tith rekart to hi, put it is a sten tith rekart to sap as kran + sap + hi thererore, thoukh hi is elitet, the lenkthenink til take place py i. 1. 62, (pratyayalaksanan)
s: 2322. The long is substituted in क्रम्, before a शित् affix, in the Parasmaipada. As क्रामति, क्रामतः, क्रामन्ति or क्राम्यति &c. Per. चक्राम Imperative क्राम्यतु or क्रामतु &c. Why in the Parasmaipada ? Observe आक्रमते आदित्यः How do you explain the lengthening in उत्क्राम and संक्राम ( Imperative 2nd Per. Sg.) For when हि is elided by लुक्, (VI. 4. 105 ) then by I. 1. 63. the affix being dropped by a l-elision, it would produce no effect and so there ought to have been no lengthening ? This is no valid objection. The prohibition of I. 1. 63, applies to the अङ्ग stem after which the affix is elided. Here क्रम् is not a stem or anga with regard to हि, but it is a stem with regard to शप् as क्रम् + शप् + हि Therefore, though हि is elided, the lengthening will take place by I. 1. 62, (प्रत्ययलक्षणम्)

pk: 2323. The augnent iw is aded to ardhadhatuka valadi ariles arter sru and kran, only then when they do not ocasion the taking or the Personal endings or the atnanepada. The restriction is that when the rots thenselves ocasion atnanepada ariles, then they do not take iw, otherwise they wil. Thus akranit 502. Kranu, To walk, step. s: 2323. The augment इट् is added to ardhadhatuka valadi affixes after स्रु and क्रम्, only then when they do not occasion the taking of the Personal endings of the Atmanepada. The roots स्रु and क्रम्, are udatta, and will get इट् augment naturally, the sutra makes a restriction or niyama. The restriction is that when the roots themselves occasion atmanepada affixes, then they do not take इट्, otherwise they will. Thus अक्रमीत् 502. Kramu, To walk, step. pk: 2326. l is substituted ror the r or a Preposition, when ay rolows. Thus palayate, playate The s, or the Prepositions dur and nir, is changed to r, but this is not changed to l, because it is asidha thus we have the rorns nirayate, durayate But there is a preposition nili also, the r or which is changed to l, as nilayate se Vi. 2. 46. so also there is a Preposition dur which rorns dulayate The word pratyaya is not rorned ron prati + ay but ron prati + in ir the rot ay is atnanepadi why is it conjugated as Parasnaipadi in the rolowing line or nagha :—"udayati vitatordhva rasni rajau." ? The word udayati is not rorned by ud+√ay but ron ud + √ i ; the √ i is obtained by the analysis or kawo as we have already shown. se kawo no. 342. Or the rolowing nalin aplies : nalin : The atnanepada, which a rot nay take because it is enunciated in the Dhatupatha as anudateta is not or universal aplication. This nalin we inrer ron the jnapaka or caksin which is shown with an indicatory n. This rot is or adadi clas no. 7. it is read as anudatet. it would have ben conjugated in the atnanepada by the nere ract or its being caled anudatet, the rurther ading or n shows that the anudatet atnanepada is not universaly valid. in the Perect or √ aya, the rule Vi. 4. 126 s. 263 aplies, because the rot begins with a va and so we have vavaye and not yeye. But peye, neye, ceye, teye pranayate and neye 503. aya, to go.
